title: Ferroptotic stress-guided glutathione dynamics profiling identifies melatonin priming as a potential mesenchymal stem cell strategy for asthma therapy
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) show therapeutic potential for inflammatory diseases; however, their efficacy is often compromised during ex vivo expansion. Here, melatonin (MT) is identified as a safe and effective priming agent enhancing MSC functionality through intracellular glutathione dynamics. Using MitoFreSHtracer, a real-time quantitative monitoring platform is developed for live MSCs under ferroptotic stress. Multiple parameters based on the fluorescence ratio mean, heterogeneity, and ferroptotic stress resistance capacity are used. Dynamic assessment of MSC heterogeneity related to ex vivo expansion and accurate key functional capacity predictions are established in MSC batches and tissue sources. High-throughput screening of 39 flavonoids and 7 antioxidants identifies MT as a pharmacopeia-compliant priming agent with superior redox-enhancing capacity. MT priming robustly activates CREB1–NRF2 and JAK–STAT3–PD-L1 pathways, leading to the enhanced clonogenicity, migration, angiogenesis, anti-inflammation, and immunosuppressive properties. Transcriptomic analysis revealed molecular signatures associated with immune modulation and tissue regeneration. MT-primed MSCs significantly alleviate Th2-mediated inflammation and improves lung engraftment in allergic asthma mice. A deep learning-based convolutional neural network for automated bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis provides objective and efficient inflammatory cell profiling. Overall, an integrated approach involving MT advances the development of high-quality MSC-based therapies for asthma and other inflammatory diseases.

title: Enhancing electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia on diatomic Salen-COFs: Integrated density functional theory and machine learning studies

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习由DFT描述符预测Salen-COF双原子催化剂NO吸附能，研究电催化制氨。

verified_metadata.title: Enhancing electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia on diatomic Salen-COFs: Integrated density functional theory and machine learning studies
verified_metadata.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction has emerged as a highly promising and environmentally friendly approach for ammonia synthesis. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were systematically performed to explore the catalytic performance of MM-Salen-COF-based diatomic catalysts in the nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR). A total of 21 transition metals (TMs) from 3d to 5d (TM = V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Nb, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Ta, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au) were screened via a three-step computational approach. Subsequently, ten heteronuclear MM'-Salen-COFs catalysts were further designed by combining promising homonuclear catalysts. The performance indicators, including structural stability and catalytic activity, were thoroughly assessed and compared. Notably, heteronuclear Cu/Ag, Cu/Cr and Ag/Cr catalysts exhibited comparable or even superior performance relative to their homonuclear counterparts. Furthermore, a machine learning (ML) model was employed to predict NO adsorption energies using computationally derived descriptors. This combined DFT and ML approach provides valuable insights for rational NORR catalyst design, opening pathways toward novel diatomic catalyst development.

title: Photonic crystal-plasmonic nanoantenna coupling biosensor for AI assisted protein biomarker detection

ai4s_review.rationale: 优化UNet从光子晶体等离子体生物传感图像定量蛋白质标志物浓度。

verified_metadata.title: Photonic crystal-plasmonic nanoantenna coupling biosensor for AI assisted protein biomarker detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Photonic crystal (PC) biosensors have been widely used in protein detection, leveraging their cost-effectiveness and operational simplicity. However, they confront challenges in balancing detection sensitivity and analysis speed. In this paper, an intelligent biosensing platform integrating a PC-plasmonic nanoantenna (PC-PN) coupling system with an optimized UNet model was constructed. By precisely tuning the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) properties of Au@Ag-Au core-shell nanoparticles, efficient coupling with the intrinsic resonance of PC is achieved. Angle-resolved spectroscopy (ARS) was employed to acquire multi-dimensional spectral datasets in 10 s, replacing conventional single-point reflectance spectral measurements that require 1–2 h. An optimized UNet model, featuring hierarchical feature fusion and anti-noise convolutional layers, was designed to establish a regression model for target protein concentration. Using interleukin-6 (IL-6) as target protein, the system exhibits linear detection over the range of 5–100 pg/mL, with a detection limit as low as 5 pg/mL. Notably, the entire detection process, from biosensing interface identification to AI-driven concentration prediction, can be completed within 15 min, which satisfies the requirements of both high sensitivity and rapid PC-based sensing.

title: Simultaneous optimization of reactor design and operating conditions using geometry-aware physics-informed neural network

ai4s_review.rationale: 几何感知物理信息神经网络联合优化反应器形状与运行条件，无需预先CFD样本。

verified_metadata.title: Simultaneous optimization of reactor design and operating conditions using geometry-aware physics-informed neural network
verified_metadata.abstract: Although design of reactor geometry is a crucial task, most existing optimization studies have considered only operating parameters on a fixed geometry, due to the high computational cost of computational fluid dynamics (CFD). To address this, we present an inverse-design framework that does not require CFD data by incorporating a geometry-aware learning concept into a physics-informed neural network (PINN), which can generalize flow fields across any arbitrary geometry. The PINN predicted velocity profiles with a relative root-mean-squared error (RMSE) below 4 % across six geometries. Additionally, a compartment model was employed to efficiently couple the velocity profiles with chemical reactions, and the PINN-based compartment model successfully reproduced ethylene distribution in a polymerization reactor within 3 min at a given blade design. To further leverage this, we jointly optimized the blade geometry and operating parameters to produce a desired molecular weight distribution (MWD). The optimized blade design and condition achieved an MWD matching the target, with an R2 of 0.994. It does not require CFD data for training and is generally applicable to any non-ideal reactor design problems, confirming the potential of generalizable PINNs as a practical tool for reactor geometry optimization without repeated CFD simulations.

title: Machine learning-assisted the directed evolution of descriptor for Mg-CO2 batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 梯度提升学习MgCO3吸附机理的关键描述符，指导镁二氧化碳电池催化剂设计。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted the directed evolution of descriptor for Mg-CO2 batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: Mg-CO₂ batteries are promising for energy conversion and CO₂ fixation, but designing optimal single-atom catalysts (SACs) is challenging due to the lack of effective descriptors for complex chemical microenvironments. We developed a machine learning (ML) approach to uncover MgCO₃ adsorption mechanisms and identify key controlling factors. Using gradient boosting regression (GBR), we successfully identified a concise and universal descriptor ϕ″ through feature cleaning and importance analysis. This descriptor enables rapid, accurate evaluation of adsorption energies across diverse coordination environments, advancing catalyst design for Mg-CO₂ batteries. In general, the mathematical expression of ϕ″ can be viewed as the digital fingerprint for SACs with specific coordination environments. We anticipate that such a robustness and transferability descriptor ϕ″ can be extended and applied to other fields of catalytic science.

title: Intelligent high-energy molecules design for solid propellants via interpretable machine learning and latent space optimization

ai4s_review.rationale: 变分自编码与贝叶斯优化在潜空间生成高能分子，并结合可解释性能模型设计推进剂。

verified_metadata.title: Intelligent high-energy molecules design for solid propellants via interpretable machine learning and latent space optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: Intelligently designing molecules based on composite material properties is the ideal goal across many areas of materials science. For solid propellants, where high-energy molecules critically affect performance, property-driven molecular design is highly desirable but remains unrealized. To this end, we present an AI workflow that integrates property prediction, feature attribution, and generative modeling to enable interpretable molecular design for high-energy solid propellants. A curated dataset of over 16,000 molecules supports both accurate multi-target prediction models and a generative framework. The predictor attains high accuracy for Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) system formulations (R2 ≥ 0.996) and generalizes to Glycidyl Azide Polymer (GAP) and NitrateEster Plasticized PolyetherPropellant (NEPE) systems (R2 ≥ 0.970). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlights oxygen balance (OBCO > −10 %) and nitrogen content (35–45 wt%) as key factors. Guided by these insights, latent space optimization using a Junction Tree Variational Autoencoder and Bayesian optimization yields over 200 novel high-energy molecules with predicted Isp above 265 s. This work demonstrates an interpretable pipeline for accelerating high-energy molecules discovery and propellant formulation design.

title: Transformer-based framework for configuration-agnostic Li-ion battery SoH estimation by exploring novel health indicators

ai4s_review.rationale: 多目标Transformer学习跨电池配置的健康指标并估计锂电池健康状态。

verified_metadata.title: Transformer-based framework for configuration-agnostic Li-ion battery SoH estimation by exploring novel health indicators
verified_metadata.abstract: With continuous advancements in Li-ion battery technology, it has become imperative to develop battery health assessment with general applicability. In particular, the batteries can satisfy a range of energy demands for diverse end products, which has motivated previous studies to develop State of Health (SoH) frameworks across various configurations. However, to achieve general applicability, a SoH estimator was required to train separately for each battery configuration, leading to substantial inefficiency. Hence, in this paper, we propose BADA (By capturing Attention in a transformer, assessing state of lithium-ion batteries with Distinguished health indicators Applicable to various configurations). This novel approach explores the five most significant health indicators (HIs) and leverages them to enable configuration-agnostic health diagnostics without additional training on different configurations. It further employs a multi-objective transformer with key HIs, achieving effective performance in SoH estimation while exhibiting limited effectiveness in battery configurations classification, which in turn helps ensure reliable assessment across different battery configuration units. BADA, constructed with dominant HIs and transformer encoders, demonstrated its general applicability. Notably, this transformer-based framework showed an RMSE of 1.90×10−2 for a 7P module despite being trained on single cells with an RMSE of 1.33×10−2. Accordingly, this transformer-based framework is expected to significantly enhance the general applicability of configuration-agnostic battery health estimation through transfer learning, effectively addressing all potential scenarios encountered under real-world usage.

title: Accurate prediction and screening of Ni-based bimetallic catalysts for hydrogen production from biogas reforming: An interpretable machine learning study

ai4s_review.rationale: 随机森林与多层感知器结合DFT筛选生物气重整制氢Ni双金属催化剂。

verified_metadata.title: Accurate prediction and screening of Ni-based bimetallic catalysts for hydrogen production from biogas reforming: An interpretable machine learning study
verified_metadata.abstract: Catalytic reforming of biogas provides an environmentally sustainable pathway for hydrogen production, wherein Ni-based bimetallic catalysts play a crucial role. Nonetheless, rapid and cost-efficient screening of such catalysts remains a significant challenge. In this study, machine learning methods, specifically random forest (RF) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models, were employed for preliminary catalyst screening. The catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability were evaluated jointly by predicting CH4 conversion, CO2 conversion, H2/CO ratio, and the change of CH4 conversion in extended testing periods. The RF model exhibited superior predictive accuracy (R2 > 0.9, RMSE ≤5.01) across all performance metrics compared to the MLP model. Through integrated interpretative approaches, the optimal characteristics of Ni-based bimetallic catalysts and operational parameters influencing catalytic performance were elucidated. Catalyst stability was found to be strongly dependent on catalyst properties with smaller Ni particle sizes (< 7 nm) and lower specific surface areas (< 225 m2/g) contributing positively to stability. Additionally, temperature and weight hourly space velocity (WHSV) significantly impacted CH4 conversion, with maximum conversion observed at temperatures above 725 °C and WHSV below 132 L·g−1·h−1. Importantly, the doping metals in the Ni-based bimetallic catalysts were screened based on ML models, revealing that alkaline-earth and lanthanide dopants exhibited promising performance at low temperatures, whereas fifth- and sixth-period transition metal promoters had advantages at elevated temperatures.

title: Multi-staged machine learning-driven investigation of biomass-derived hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries: Connecting precursor, structure, and performance

ai4s_review.rationale: 多阶段机器学习联结生物质前驱体、硬碳结构和钠离子电池电化学性能。

verified_metadata.title: Multi-staged machine learning-driven investigation of biomass-derived hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries: Connecting precursor, structure, and performance
verified_metadata.abstract: Biomass-derived hard carbon is a low-cost, sustainable anode candidate for sodium-ion batteries, yet the structural evolution mechanisms governing its performance remain unclear. A novel two-step predictive approach was developed and compared with the conventional one-step model. This approach not only slightly improved the prediction accuracy for electrochemical performance, but also established interpretable correlations between input features and electrochemical performance outputs, and further enabled the prediction and analysis of rate performance indicators. The framework first uses biomass three-component ratios and thermal parameters to infer key structural descriptors (SSA, d002, ID/IG, La, Lc), which are then combined with current density to predict electrochemical performance. The target space extends beyond experimental capacity (QM,E) and initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), encompassing rate-related parameters (QM,F, τ, n) and long-cycle capacity (QM,100) within a unified interpretable model. Trained on an expanded dataset covering diverse biomass compositions and carbonization conditions, the model captures both kinetic and durability behaviors across a wide compositional space. SHAP and PDP analyses reveal that moderate disorder (ID/IG ∼ 1.5–1.8), narrow interlayer spacing (∼0.37–0.38 nm), and lateral domain sizes of 3.5–5.0 nm synergistically enhance reversible capacity, while their kinetic response reflects a trade-off rather than optimal rate capability—a behavior instead observed at smaller or larger lateral domain sizes. These capacity-favorable structures are typically achieved using cellulose-rich precursors with tuned hemicellulose and lignin content under optimized carbonization protocols. This study offers mechanistic insights and practical guidance for designing high-performance hard carbon anodes in sodium-ion batteries.

title: Machine learning-enabled advanced oxidation processes: Catalytic active site engineering, oxidation pathway regulation, and reaction condition optimization

ai4s_review.rationale: 实质综述机器学习预测活性位点和活性物种、调控高级氧化污染降解路径及反应条件。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-enabled advanced oxidation processes: Catalytic active site engineering, oxidation pathway regulation, and reaction condition optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a pivotal tool for predicting and optimizing the performance of advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), which are widely applied for degrading persistent organic pollutants. Notwithstanding, a systematic summary of ML-based applications in AOPs remains lacking. To address this gap, this review presents a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements in ML utilization within AOPs, focusing on methodologies, mechanisms, and practical case studies. Additionally, a parameter importance analysis was performed to assess key factors in AOPs, with specific emphasis on catalyst site construction, oxidation pathway regulation, and reaction condition optimization, which are thoroughly analyzed. For catalytic site construction, ML overcomes limitations of univariate experiments by demystifying the “black-box” of biochar active site formation, revealing that higher heating values and pyrolysis temperature are dominant factors governing the generation of carbon- and nitrogen-containing sites. Regarding oxidation pathway regulation, ML accurately establishes the complex nonlinear relationship between catalyst structure and 1O2 generation in biochar/peroxymonosulfate system, pinpointing the optimal catalyst structure to enhance 1O2 performance. In terms of reaction condition optimization, ML employs high-throughput screening of pollutant molecular descriptors to determine degradation mechanisms mediated by SO4•-, •OH, and O3, and unveils optimal reaction conditions by establishing complex relationships among key parameters. This review delineates critical predictive capabilities of ML in AOPs, demonstrating how ML enables high-throughput catalyst fabrication and targeted oxidation pathway modulation through predictions of active sites and reactive species, while consolidating data-driven optimization strategies for AOPs. The findings herein provide valuable guidance for the intelligent development of AOPs.

title: Large language models for automated data extraction and inverse design of copolymers with targeted glass transition temperatures

ai4s_review.rationale: 大语言模型从文献抽取共聚物数据并训练性能模型，反向设计目标玻璃化温度共聚物。

verified_metadata.title: Large language models for automated data extraction and inverse design of copolymers with targeted glass transition temperatures
verified_metadata.abstract: The design of copolymers with tailored thermal properties is crucial for advanced applications in aerospace, the automotive industry, and electronics. However, the development of data-driven models for this task is severely hampered by the scarcity of structured, high-quality datasets, as copolymer data remains buried in the unstructured text of scientific literature. Here, we demonstrate a large language model (LLM)-powered pipeline to overcome this data bottleneck and enable the inverse design of novel copolymers. We developed a method to accurately extract copolymer names and their thermal properties (glass transition temperature, Tg, and melting temperature, Tm) from 393 research articles, achieving a high extraction accuracy (F1 score = 0.7834) and constructing a curated dataset of 1195 entries. This LLM-generated dataset was used to train machine learning models that rival the performance of models built on manually curated data. Our forward prediction models achieved R2 values of 0.791 and 0.845 for Tg and Tm, respectively, on an independent manually labeled test set. Critically, we deployed an inverse model for de novo design, generating 2052 novel, valid copolymer structures targeting high Tg, which exhibited a 189.5 % increase in average predicted Tg. The thermal properties of eight selected AI-generated copolymers were validated with molecular dynamics simulations, confirming their predicted performance with a mean relative error of 4.17 %. This work establishes LLMs as a powerful and reliable tool for automating scientific data extraction, effectively bridging the data gap in materials science and paving the way for accelerated discovery of high-performance polymers.

title: Machine learning-assisted oxide semiconductor sensor array for accurate discrimination of alcohol gases

ai4s_review.rationale: 比较KNN、SVM等机器学习识别氧化物传感阵列中的醇类气体，研究传感器物理检测性能。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted oxide semiconductor sensor array for accurate discrimination of alcohol gases
verified_metadata.abstract: The growing alcoholic beverage market and stringent quality control standards have heightened the demand for precise detection technologies for alcohol components. Traditional metal oxide semiconductors (MOS) sensors face significant challenges in terms of selectivity and cross-sensitivity, which seriously hinder the accurate discrimination of alcohol components. Herein, we developed an electronic nose system utilizing a sensor array composed of In2O3, ZnO, and In2O3/ZnO heterojunction sensors, all of which have demonstrated high sensitivity and stability in the detection of alcoholic gases. To facilitate effective gas differentiation and classification, four machine learning algorithms, including K-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), Gaussian naive Bayes (GNB), and logistic regression (LR), were employed and compared. Through parameter optimization via grid search and cross-validation, we achieved classification accuracies of 91 % for KNN and SVM, 87 % for GNB, and 89 % for LR for single gases. Notably, the E-nose demonstrated a remarkable 94.12 % accuracy in recognizing mixed gas samples containing ethanol and methanol/n-butanol, highlighting its potential for rapid detection of alcohol volatiles.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning–assisted amphiphilic metal–organic framework–based hydrogel sensor for visual and wireless ammonia monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of gas sensors with ultrahigh sensitivity and selectivity is crucial for public safety, environmental protection, and early warning of hazardous leaks. However, achieving real–time, portable, and reusable sensing platforms with distinct visual responses remains a key challenge. Herein, we report a deep learning–assisted sensing strategy that integrates multifunctional metal–organic framework (MOF)–based hydrogels with artificial intelligence (AI) for visual ammonia (NH₃) monitoring. Gemini surfactant–modified zirconium metal–organic framework hydrogels (GS6–ZrMOF@gel and GS10–ZrMOF@gel) were engineered, combining the high porosity of MOFs, amphiphilic surfactant functionality, and the mechanical robustness of hydrogels (tensile strength ≈ 1.52 MPa; toughness ≈ 4.48 MJ m−3). Notably, GS10–ZrMOF@gel exhibits sub–ppm sensitivity toward ammonia vapor (limit of detection ≈0.27 ppm) alongside excellent selectivity and recyclability. The sensing mechanism was systematically elucidated through combined experimental investigations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Furthermore, deep learning–enabled image analysis allowed direct visualization and accurate classification of ammonia concentrations, achieving 100% recognition accuracy. As a proof of concept, a wireless alarm system integrating the sensing hydrogels with AI algorithms was successfully demonstrated for real–time gas–leakage monitoring. This work establishes a universal strategy for real–time visual gas detection by coupling multifunctional materials with intelligent data analytics, and highlights its strong potential for environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and healthcare applications.

title: Autonomous in silico optimization framework for high-performance micromixers
abstract: Effective mixing at the microscale is essential for lab-on-a-chip systems, yet designing micromixers that achieve both high mixing efficiency and low pressure drop remains challenging and resource-intensive. Here, we introduce an autonomous in silico framework for designing obstacle-based micromixers through integrating 3D geometry generation, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and a multi-objective artificial intelligence optimization algorithm within a fully automated close-loop workflow. A constraint-aware NSGA-II variant is used, incorporating a repair operator to ensure design feasibility. Experimentally validated against hyperspectral imaging-based mixing characterization and pressure-drop measurements, the framework eliminates manual trial-and-error workload and alleviates researchers from the tedious tasks of navigating across 3D modeling, CFD simulations, and optimization algorithms, reducing optimization time by 48% compared to the conventional simulation-assisted approach. By autonomously screening hundreds of designs, it identifies Pareto-optimal micromixers and generates an extensive database that supports inverse design and reveals the mixing structure-performance relationship, facilitating the establishment of general design guidelines. The framework is generally applicable to a wide range of passive micromixers. • An autonomous in silico framework reduces micromixer optimization time by 48%. • A hyperspectral-assisted microfluidic platform is developed for experimental validation. • The resulting dataset enables inverse design and derivation of design guidelines. • Stretching interfaces and reducing vortices improve obstacle micromixer performance at low Re .

verified_metadata.title: AI-assisted modeling and optimization of large-scale ethylene production by catalytic oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane in a shell-and-tube multi-tubular reactor
verified_metadata.abstract: The present study is devoted to the development of a methodology based on artificial intelligence to model and optimize a novel process for efficient ethylene production on a large scale. To this end, a wall-cooled multi-tubular reactor for the catalytic oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane that benefits from MoVTeNbO catalysts was modeled and optimized with different plans of artificial neural networks (ANNs). A mathematical model was then employed to generate a large database (1440 runs at varied process conditions) for this process. Having screened with a relevancy analysis, the dataset was then utilized to analyze different ANN designs based on single-layer perceptron (SLP) and single-layer cascade feed-forward (SLCFF) modes and different training functions. These designs were compared with radial basis function (RBF) as well. The impacts of train function (Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno Quasi-Newton (trainbfg) and Levenberg-Marquardt (trainlm)) and hidden layer size were also monitored rigorously. Although the RBF ANN failed to describe this system, the SLP and SLCFF plans could represent the outputs precisely. Based on a robust statistical analysis of the errors, as well as kernel density and histogram analyses, it was proven that the calculations of SLP and SLCFF ANN models were reliable. The model composed of SLP-trainbfg with 20 neurons in the hidden layer was selected as the most accurate and fastest one, which was then combined with a multi-objective genetic algorithm method to search for the optimum operating conditions of the system in terms of higher feed conversion and ethylene generation with lower carbon oxide release. The observations signified that the process working under optimum conditions produces a considerable amount of ethylene at moderate temperature and pressure while releasing small quantities of carbon oxides.

verified_metadata.title: AI–DFT-DNN-guided dopant–ligand engineering of MOF-derived chemiresistors for ppb-level 2,5-Dimethylpyrazine detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Pollination by bees underpins agriculture and ecosystem health but is increasingly threatened by American foulbrood (AFB) caused by Paenibacillus larvae. Conventional AFB diagnostics are slow and costly, underscoring the need for portable sensors targeting the key biomarker 2,5-dimethylpyrazine (2,5-DMP). Here, natural language processing is applied to mine a large corpus of scholarly literature. A domain-adaptive SensBERT model evaluates 514,088 bimetallic ion–organic ligand combinations for gas sensing, with similarity scores near unity indicating high applicability. Integrated analysis of application context, physicochemical traits, and MOFs performance identifies three optimal systems: Sm(III)/Sn(II) with 3,3′,3″-((1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl)tris(azanediyl))tribenzoic_acid (H3TATAB); In(III)/Zn(II) with 4-(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)benzoic_acid (H2TZBA); and Tm(III)/Sn(II) with furan-2,5-dicarboxylic_acid (FDCA). Sm/Sn–H3TATAB exhibits superior sensitivity and selectivity toward 2,5-DMP. After plasma conversion, the derived metal oxides retain highly specific 2,5-DMP recognition with excellent response consistency and stability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations model adsorption of multiple AFB-related VOCs at the atomic scale, revealing a uniquely strong binding preference for 2,5-DMP; coupling DFT-generated data with a deep neural network further clarifies the sensing mechanism. The resulting sensor achieves a detection limit of 20 ppb for 2,5-DMP, with a response of 2.7 at 20 ppb. This work establishes a synergistic paradigm that integrates deep learning, first-principles computation, and experimental validation to deliver a high-performance, non-invasive platform for rapid AFB detection, highlighting the promise of cross-disciplinary strategies for environmental monitoring and agricultural biosecurity.

title: Comprehensive study on the competitive mechanisms of oxidation and nitriding reactions in ferrosilicon alloys under high-temperature air condition: reaction mechanism, product properties, and kinetics
abstract: As a key additive in steelmaking, ferrosilicon alloy significantly improved steel performance through deoxidation and nitrogen control during refining. However, the competitive reaction mechanism between oxidation and nitriding of ferrosilicon alloy in the high-temperature air environment post molten steel tapping remained unclear. This study conducted a systematic investigation via a combination of experiments, kinetic analysis, and density functional theory (DFT) simulations: high-temperature air experiments were performed to reveal the evolution law of the alloy's physicochemical properties during reaction; the reaction mechanism was evaluated by integrating kinetic analysis and product characterization; a DFT-based adsorption model was established to clarify the competitive mechanism at the microscopic level. The results demonstrate that after reacting in an air atmosphere, ferrosilicon alloy forms a reaction layer characterized by a layered structure, surface collapse, and cracks. For samples with particle size 0.075–0.1 mm reacted at 1673.15 K for 120 min, shows that silicon-related compounds consist of 2 wt% Si 3 N 4 and 52 wt% SiO 2 , while iron-related compounds comprise 1 wt% Fe 4 N and 9 wt% Fe 2 O 3 . In the kinetic analysis, the one-dimensional diffusion model exhibits the best fitting performance, suggesting that the reaction is significantly influenced by the diffusion rate of gas molecules. Using this model, the apparent activation energies for Group S, Group M, and Group L are calculated to be 105.75 kJ∙mol −1 , 119.63 kJ∙mol −1 , and 127.54 kJ∙mol −1 , respectively. Furthermore, the co-adsorption model reveals that the average adsorption energies of Si(111) and β -FeSi 2 (220) are −8.047 eV and −5.142 eV, respectively. Additionally, the significant change in the bond length of O 2 and the negligible change in the bond length of N 2 further confirm that the oxidation reaction dominates the entire reaction process. • The reaction products of ferrosilicon alloys in an air environment are primarily layered oxides. • It is verified that the optimal kinetic fitting model for the reaction of ferrosilicon alloy in an air atmosphere is a one-dimensional diffusion model. • It was verified that the co-adsorption effect of O 2 and N 2 in Si(111) was stronger than that of β -FeSi 2 (220). • During co-adsorption, O 2 exhibits significantly greater bond length and average charge transfer than N 2 .

verified_metadata.title: AIEgen-regulated metal-organic framework enabled machine learning-assisted lateral flow immunoassay sensor for intelligent diagnosis of P. aeruginosa
verified_metadata.abstract: Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA), as a portable point-of-care testing (POCT) platform, shows significant potential for applications in clinical diagnostics. However, conventional LFIA sensors typically suffer from low sensitivity, which greatly limits their application in trace analyte detection. In this study, we developed a machine learning (ML)-assisted LFIA platform based on metal-AIEgen frameworks (MAFs) for ultrasensitive and intelligent detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa). By regulating the carboxyl density and arm rigidity of the AIE ligand, the synthesized MAF-1 exhibited outstanding luminescent performance and excellent biocompatibility. After integrating it into the LFIA system, the resulting MAF-1-LFIA achieved a detection limit (LOD) of 10 CFU/mL, with sensitivity enhanced by approximately 100-fold, 100-fold, and 10-fold compared with gold nanoparticles-based LFIA (AuNPs-LFIA), time-resolved fluorescent microsphere-based LFIA (TRFM-LFIA) and Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA), respectively. In addition, the MAF-1-LFIA has been successfully applied to the detection of P. aeruginosa in tap water and milk samples, with a recovery rate ranging from 98.23% to 106.82% and a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.11% to 8.34%, demonstrating excellent accuracy and practicality. Furthermore, the incorporation of ML algorithms enabled efficient classification and precise quantification of the detection signals, with a classification accuracy of 100% and a concentration prediction accuracy of 99.04%. In summary, this work proposes a promising strategy that integrates MAFs materials with artificial intelligence for high-performance detection in complex biological matrices, paving the way for the development of next-generation intelligent POCT biosensors.

title: Multivariate optimization and inverse design of multiphase reactive systems via deep learning and 3D CFD–PBM simulations
abstract: This work presents a deep learning-driven framework for multivariate optimization, focusing on the identification of precipitation kinetics parameters in a complex three-dimensional (3D) Computational Fluid Dynamics-Population Balance Model (CFD-PBM) model describing Mg(OH)2 precipitation in T- and Y-mixer static reactors. A numerical dataset was first generated using the CFD-PBM model to train an inverse design neural network (mirror model), which takes characteristic particle dimensions ([[EQUATION]]) as input and predicts the corresponding kinetic parameters ([[EQUATION]]) as output. Experimental particle size distributions (PSD) from the T-mixer were then provided to the trained mirror model to predict the kinetic parameter vector. The predicted parameters were subsequently validated by comparing the CFD-PBM outputs with experimental PSD from the Y-mixer configuration. The framework demonstrates excellent generalization, accurately reproducing PSD for conditions not included in the training set. Moreover, the same numerical dataset was also employed to train a surrogate CFD-PBM model which takes kinetic parameters ([[EQUATION]]) as input and returns characteristic particle dimensions ([[EQUATION]]) as output. The surrogate CFD-PBM model was subsequently used to perform a sensitivity analysis of the kinetic parameters. Minor deviations are observed in the estimation of the smallest ([[EQUATION]]) and largest ([[EQUATION]]) particle size fractions, consistent with physical aggregation and collision mechanisms. A key outcome of this study is that the proposed framework enables, for the first time, the use of fully 3D CFD–PBM simulations equipped with a rigorously calibrated kinetic model, without requiring empirical simplifications or iterative fitting procedures. This significantly enhances the predictive capability of 3D CFD–PBM models in nonlinear reactive systems, providing a computationally efficient and generalizable tool for kinetic parameter identification in precipitation and crystallization processes.

title: Reduced-order modeling of particle-fluid flows with heat transfer via a curriculum learning approach
abstract: Reduced-order models (ROM) exhibit promising potential for accelerating large-scale numerical simulations. Many studies have developed ROMs of particle-fluid flow systems, but those that also include heat transfer phenomena have only been used to forecast temperatures over time. In this work, we developed non-intrusive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based ROMs for forecasting and parametrizing the fluid and particle temperatures in a cooling fluidized bed. A physics-based full-order model (FOM) of the fluidized bed is set up using the coupled computational fluid dynamics and discrete element method (CFD-DEM) and an interphase heat transfer model. Afterward, snapshots of the FOM are decomposed into modes and coefficients via Lanczos-based POD. The number of modes in the ROMs are determined via energy truncation, while the coefficients are predicted by long-short term memory (LSTM) and Bahdanau attention-based neural networks via recursive single-step forecasting in both temporal and parametric spaces. Neural network training is accomplished via a curriculum learning approach, and ablation tests showed that this is necessary for learning the nonlinear characteristics of the high-order modal coefficients associated with particle-fluid dynamics. The results show that both the time forecasting and parametric ROMs can accurately predict temperature fluctuations and macroscopic particle-fluid dynamics while reducing computational costs by several orders of magnitude compared to the FOM. The POD-based ROM in this work is the first to parametrize the temperatures from a CFD-DEM simulation, which is a substantial contribution to the modeling and simulation of heat transfer systems for chemical engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: Reduced-order modeling of particle-fluid flows with heat transfer via a curriculum learning approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Reduced-order models (ROM) exhibit promising potential for accelerating large-scale numerical simulations. Many studies have developed ROMs of particle-fluid flow systems, but those that also include heat transfer phenomena have only been used to forecast temperatures over time. In this work, we developed non-intrusive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based ROMs for forecasting and parametrizing the fluid and particle temperatures in a cooling fluidized bed. A physics-based full-order model (FOM) of the fluidized bed is set up using the coupled computational fluid dynamics and discrete element method (CFD-DEM) and an interphase heat transfer model. Afterward, snapshots of the FOM are decomposed into modes and coefficients via Lanczos-based POD. The number of modes in the ROMs are determined via energy truncation, while the coefficients are predicted by long-short term memory (LSTM) and Bahdanau attention-based neural networks via recursive single-step forecasting in both temporal and parametric spaces. Neural network training is accomplished via a curriculum learning approach, and ablation tests showed that this is necessary for learning the nonlinear characteristics of the high-order modal coefficients associated with particle-fluid dynamics. The results show that both the time forecasting and parametric ROMs can accurately predict temperature fluctuations and macroscopic particle-fluid dynamics while reducing computational costs by several orders of magnitude compared to the FOM. The POD-based ROM in this work is the first to parametrize the temperatures from a CFD-DEM simulation, which is a substantial contribution to the modeling and simulation of heat transfer systems for chemical engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: Design of three-dimensional SERS-active biopolymer platform: Towards highly sensitive molecular detection and artificial intelligence-enhanced multi-biomarker diagnosis
verified_metadata.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) nanoengineered surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates enable ultrasensitive molecular detection by amplifying localized electromagnetic fields. To overcome the complexity and limitation associated with fabricating 3D SERS substrates, a facile and cost-effective 3D SERS platform was designed by coupling silver (Ag) nanoparticles with a polycaprolactone–chitosan (PCL–CHT) biopolymer matrix. The hybrid nanostructure generates densely distributed electromagnetic hotspots, expands the Raman-active region, and effectively minimizes the impact of laser defocusing during measurement. The optimized Ag@PCL-CHT substrate exhibits a strong analytical enhancement factor of 1010, enabling trace-level detection of methylene blue (MB) down to picomolar concentrations. Furthermore, to address reproducibility and complex data interpretation issues commonly faced in biomedical sensing, an artificial intelligence-assisted multi-diagnostic model was integrated with the 3D substrate. The unique nanoarchitecture ensures consistent and reliable SERS responses from diverse biofluids, including sweat, urine, and serum, enabling simultaneous monitoring of creatinine, uric acid and pH. This multiplex sensing platform minimizes dependence on multiple single-analyte tests and provides a holistic evaluation of metabolic states. The proposed strategy demonstrates a controllable and scalable route for constructing highly sensitive and reproducible SERS sensors, advancing the practical deployment of 3D SERS technology for point-of-care diagnostics and personalized health monitoring.

title: A semantic framework for chemical process digitalisation using ontologies
abstract: Digitalisation holds promise for the transformation of modern chemical processes into intelligent manufacturing systems that are responsive to dynamic market demands and sustainability goals. To achieve interconnection of physical installations with their digital twins, we developed a semantic framework which enables systematic knowledge management and effective utilisation of plant data, serving as a backbone of intelligent manufacturing. Our approach leverages ontologies and agents built on a knowledge graph infrastructure to host the deployment of both first-principles and artificial intelligence (AI) models of chemical processes. Additional ontologies were designed for connecting models with industrial plants. We present an end-to-end demonstration of the knowledge graph-based digital twin system and illustrate this technology with a use case of anomaly detection in an industrial pilot plant for nanomaterials synthesis. The implementation includes data acquisition, secure communication protocols, cloud-hosted data storage, dedicated AI workflows, and a user interface with version control for both ontologies and models. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the semantic framework in managing chemical process knowledge, linking plants to first-principles and data-driven models, and enabling the execution of complex AI-driven workflows.

verified_metadata.title: Design of green multifunctional mesoporous nanosheets for trace biomarker detection, AI-enhanced pollutant discrimination, and synergistic catalytic degradation
verified_metadata.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework nanosheets (MONs) with nanozyme activity hold great promise, yet their scalable and eco-friendly synthesis remains challenging. Herein, bioinspired Cu-MON was synthesized via a rapid one-step coordination self-assembly of expired phloroglucinol drugs with Cu2+ in water at room temperature enabling high-value recycling of expired pharmaceutical waste. Cu-MON exhibits excellent laccase-like and peroxidase-like activities, significantly outperforming natural enzymes and other Cu-based nanozymes in catalytic efficiency, kinetics, and stability. Its superior performance stems from the ultrathin mesoporous structure, high copper content, and engineered defects, which enhance the adsorption and activation of substrates. Density functional theory calculations demonstrated the key role of coordination shell regulation in reducing the energy barrier and promoting electron transfer. Notably, this work reveals the synergistic effect of Metal-Ligand-Substrate, involving not only the CuII-CuI redox cycle but also the simultaneous coordination and electron transfer between the redox-active functional groups of ligands and the metal sites/substrates. Leveraging its laccase-like behavior and differential responses, a machine learning-enabled, smartphone-integrated colorimetric sensor array was developed for on-site discrimination of structurally similar phenolic contaminants. Unlike traditional “detection-only” platforms, our system integrates “sense and kill” functionality, further enabling efficient contaminant removal. Moreover, a novel degradation-polymerization dual-removal pathway for tetracycline antibiotics was discovered, ensuring near-complete removal and detoxification. Finally, a peroxidase-driven dual-mode ratiometric fluorescence-colorimetric sensor was constructed for dopamine detection in biological fluids, with cross-validation ensuring high reliability and accuracy. This “One-MON-Three-Functions” strategy provides a new perspective for designing next-generation multifunctional nanozymes for pollutant monitoring, environmental remediation, and biosensing.

verified_metadata.title: UV–visible Auto-Reactometry enabled parallel screening for accelerating chemical synthesis development with LLM
verified_metadata.abstract: Photochemical reactions are highly sensitive to parameters such as light intensity, wavelength, irradiation time, and moisture content. The lack of precise control and real-time monitoring often makes these reactions difficult to reproduce and purify, prompting many researchers to favour non-photochemical alternatives. To overcome these limitations, we present the UV–Visible Auto-Reactometry (UVAR) platform an AI-integrated, continuous flow microfluidic system designed for autonomous optimization and acceleration of photochemical synthesis. Leveraging large language models (LLMs) for dynamic planning and real-time parameter control, UVAR enables precise, reproducible, and efficient screening of reaction conditions. The platform demonstrated broad applicability across four key photochemical transformations: cross-coupling, rearrangement, cycloaddition, and isomerization, successfully synthesizing 36 structurally diverse molecules, including the late-stage functionalization of the Apixaban (APX) active pharmaceutical ingredient (API).

verified_metadata.title: Enhanced metal-organic framework-driven deep learning-assisted magnetic crystal paper aptsensor for two-step sensitization and in-situ detection of pathogenic bacteria
verified_metadata.abstract: In-situ quantitative techniques for pathogens across diverse scenarios can transform detection from a retrospective “laboratory tool” into a proactive “field decision-making tool,” which is crucial for precise early warning of pathogens. Herein, we developed an enhanced metal-organic framework (MOF) by anchoring dual single atoms (DSAs) Co-Cu onto an MOF carrier (Co/Cu@EnMOF). Low-cost aptamer-functionalized Co/Cu@EnMOF enabled specific bacterial recognition. In addition to increasing the sensitivity of the sensing signal through DSAs anchoring of the MOF structure, the anti-interference capability against the food matrix was also achieved by using targeted magnetic nanoflowers that increase the binding sites for target bacteria. Addressing the main issue restricting sensing sensitivity, the two-step sensitization technology has comprehensively enhanced the signal for E. coli O157:H7 and the anti-interference ability in food, enabling rapid early warning of trace pathogens. To achieve portable bioanalysis, we engineered a novel crystalline sensing carrier by immobilizing the chromogenic substrate o-Phenylenediamine (OPD) onto cellulose paper matrices. Under the catalytic action of Co/Cu@EnMOF, OPD is oxidized to generate a product that exhibits both color change and fluorescence emission, enabling dual-mode signal output. The newly developed multi-signal integrated reading device enables sensitive in-situ detection and, when combined with deep learning, can accurately read RGB values. The proposed smart crystal paper sensor enables dual-mode in-situ quantitative detection, with detection limits of 38.73 and 97.72 cfu/mL for colorimetric and fluorescence modes, respectively. It demonstrates excellent performance when applied to complex food matrices, offering a new approach for in-situ monitoring and early warning of pathogens.

title: Machine learning assisted optical biosensing of bacteria on a monolayer MoS2 platform
abstract: Bacterial infections continue to impact billions of lives worldwide. Current detection methods are struggling to provide both rapid and accurate bacterial detection. Therefore, innovative approaches to rapid disease detection are urgently required. Recently, there has been much interest in the space of 2D material-based sensing. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as suitable biosensor candidates, due to their unique properties. These materials are relatively easy to make, non-toxic and have distinct charge characteristics. This study explores the integration of Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) into a monoclonal antibody (mAb) functionalized biosensor which successfully detects methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) using both Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy. 2D nanoflakes of MoS 2 were deposited onto a Silicon oxide (SiO 2 ) substrate via chemical vapour deposition (CVD). The resulting MoS 2 chips were functionalised with F598, a mAb that binds to the polysaccharide poly -N- acetyl-glucosamine (PNAG) found in various microbes, including many diverse species of bacteria. MRSA was incubated onto the MoS 2 chips for 30 min, before rinsing with phosphate buffered saline (PBS), then PL and Raman spectroscopy were performed on the samples. Our results show accurate and rapid detection of MRSA using both PL and Raman spectroscopy, based on spectral changes that occur because of bacterial adhesion onto the chip surfaces. Machine learning was then utilized in a convolutional neural network (CNN) to distinguish between the different classes of spectra (controls and MRSA). Using a CNN an accuracy of 86% and 96% was found for the Raman and PL data, respectively. Thus, with a platform of MoS 2 nanoflakes, generalized detection of PNAG-expressing bacteria (in this case MRSA) using spectroscopic techniques is successful. As this platform's detection is based on the antibody used, the platform can be modified to detect various species of bacteria by using different monoclonal antibodies. • Antibody-functionalised monolayer MoS₂ enables rapid, label-free MRSA detection. • Raman and photoluminescence spectroscopy reveal clear optical signatures of bacterial adhesion. • Convolutional neural network achieves 86–96% classification accuracy from spectra. • Platform adaptable for diverse PNAG-expressing bacteria via antibody substitution.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence for energetic materials: design on the levels of molecule, crystal and composite
verified_metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the design of energetic materials (EMs), which are essential in military, aerospace, and industrial applications. From the molecular, crystal, and composite perspectives, this article highlights how machine learning models enable property and performance prediction in high-throughput virtual screening, offering density functional theory-level accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. Meanwhile, generative models, as a new paradigm in the AI era, enable target-driven design of molecules and crystals. Despite much progress, challenges remain in data scarcity, insufficient interpretability, and limited cross-scale integration. Advances in the quantity and quality of data, interpretable and physics-informed models, multiscale frameworks, and EMs-specific foundation models will pave the way toward a data-driven and efficient paradigm for the discovery of next-generation EMs.

verified_metadata.title: Highly sensitive colorimetric 3D covalent organic framework sensors with artificial intelligence analysis enabled early detection of plant diseases
verified_metadata.abstract: The biosynthesis of volatile organic compound (VOC) signaling is essential for plant adaptation under disease stress. However, the efficient identification of VOCs remains a significant challenge. In this study, we engineered a biomimetic colorimetric sensor array by integrating stimulus-responsive dyes into a highly porous three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF), which is coupled with artificial intelligence analysis. These 3D COF@dye sensors exhibit high surface areas and interconnected large channels, facilitating highly sensitive colorimetric sensing of VOCs. The resultant platform demonstrated markedly enhanced sensitivity towards target VOCs, with detection limits ranging from 0.081 to 0.95 ppm. Furthermore, AI-assisted information fusion and perceptual analysis considerably improved the accuracy of VOC sensing processes, enabling direct visualization and classification of VOCs with ≥95% accuracy within 24 h of inoculation. This design, which leverages molecular recognition capabilities, amplifies host-guest interactions, thereby facilitating the differentiation of VOCs by their polarity, size, and shape. The platform effectively distinguished VOCs emitted by Botrytis cinerea, Alternaria solani, and Phytophthora infestans. Our findings provide a generalizable platform of intelligent, nano-enabled sensors for precision agriculture and non-invasive plant health monitoring.

title: Superstructure optimization with embedded neural networks for sustainable aviation fuel production
abstract: This study presents a multi-objective optimization framework for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production, integrating artificial neural networks (ANNs) within a mixed-integer quadratically constrained programming (MIQCP) formulation. By embedding data-driven surrogate models into the mathematical optimization structure, the proposed methodology addresses key limitations of conventional superstructure-based approaches, enabling simultaneous optimization of discrete process choices and continuous operating parameters. The framework captures variable input and output stream compositions, facilitating the joint optimization of target product composition and system design. Application to Fischer–Tropsch (FT) kerosene production demonstrates that cost-minimizing configurations under unconstrained CO 2 emissions are dominated by the fossil-based autothermal reforming (ATR) route. Imposing carbon emission constraints necessitates the integration of biomass gasification and direct air capture coupled with carbon sequestration (DAC-CS), resulting in substantially reduced net emissions but higher production costs. At the zero-emission limit, hybrid configurations combining ATR and biomass gasification achieve the lowest costs ( ∼ 2.38 $/kg kerosene ), followed closely by biomass gasification-only ( ∼ 2.43 $/kg), both of which outperform the ATR-only pathway with DAC-CS ( ∼ 2.65 $/kg). In contrast, DAC-only systems relying exclusively on atmospheric CO 2 and water electrolysis are prohibitively expensive ( ∼ 10.8 $/kg). The results highlight the critical role of the embedded ANNs: optimal process conditions, such as FT reactor pressure and gasification temperature, adapt to changing circumstances, consistently outperforming fixed setups and achieving up to 20 % cost savings.

verified_metadata.title: Revealing the key factors of synergistic transport of microplastics and heavy metals in groundwater: Batch experiments, density functional theory calculations, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning modeling
verified_metadata.abstract: Environmental contamination by microplastics (MPs) and heavy metals (HMs) has raised global concerns due to their potential ecological risks, but the mechanisms underpinning synergistic migrations of these two pollutants remain unclear. To achieve this purpose, batch experiments, laboratory column experiments, microscopic characterization, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and interpretable machine learning (ML) were integrated to investigate the adsorption and co-migration of fresh and UV-aged polypropylene (PP) and polyethylene (PE) with respect to their interactions with copper ions (Cu2+) and cadmium ions (Cd2+). The results showed that aging significantly improved the adsorption performance of MPs. For aged PP, the equilibrium adsorption capacity for Cu2+ reached 1.31 mg/g, indicating a 50% increase compared with fresh PP, while that for Cd2+ was 0.624 mg/g, representing an increase of nearly 20%. Moreover, aged MPs significantly promoted the migration of HMs, with aged-PP increasing the Cu2+ recovery rate by 8.28% compared with that without aged PP. DFT calculations indicated that the adsorption energy of Cu2+ with PE (−2.26 eV) was stronger than that of Cd2+ (−1.73 eV). MD simulations confirmed that electrostatic interaction was the main binding driving force. Among various ML models, the CatBoost model (R2 = 0.85, RMSE = 0.217) performs the best. By integrating molecular-scale simulations (DFT/MD), batch and column experiments, and ML-based feature attribution, this multi-scale framework linked local HM–MP binding mechanisms to macroscopic co-migration processes in saturated porous media, overcoming the fragmentation and biases inherent to conventional studies that rely on a single technique, thus providing a mechanistic framework that may help evaluate MP-facilitated HM transport under controlled groundwater-relevant conditions.

title: Formation-consumption neural networks for efficient chemical kinetics modeling
abstract: Reaction kinetics lie at the center of reactive systems engineering, yet discovering them from data and incorporating them into predictive simulations remain time-consuming tasks that slow down model-based process design and control. To address this challenge, we introduce the Exponential Scaling Formation Consumption Neural Network (+/- ExpNet), a physics-inspired neural network architecture that can learn kinetics directly from integral reactor data and easily integrates with computational fluid dynamics to accelerate multiscale reactive simulations. The +/- ExpNet models latent formation and consumption rates which are subtracted to compute source terms, and enforces atom conservation as a hard constraint by exploiting the principles of elementary reaction kinetics. Using two catalytic and one non-catalytic test case we demonstrate that this relatively simple approach represents source terms with surprising accuracy, in most cases en par with previous approaches that require significantly more specific knowledge of the reaction system. Further, we employ the +/- ExpNet to extract kinetics for the direct DME synthesis using integral reactor data from literature. In doing so, we simultaneously derive kinetic models for both catalysts in this dual-catalyst system, without having to specify the global reactions occurring on the two catalysts or any thermodynamic constraints. This demonstrates that the +/- ExpNet provides a general and interpretable framework for automated kinetic modeling and efficient multiscale reactive simulations. Its simplicity makes it easy to integrate into big data frameworks and high-throughput experimentation, offering a path to make accurate kinetic models more widely accessible across catalysis, combustion, and other data-rich chemical disciplines.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-powered high-throughput designing and screening of electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia
verified_metadata.abstract: The technology of ammonia production via electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) offers a sustainable solution for addressing nitrate pollution in water bodies and recovering nitrogen resources. Among this technology, the design and selection of efficient catalysts are the key to achieving high selectivity and stable nitrogen conversion in NO3RR. This study employed machine learning (ML)-powered density functional theory (DFT) to develop a strategy for designing NO3RR catalysts based on geometric-electronic-adsorption properties. The stability and activity of 282 single-atom catalysts (SACs) with high carbon‑nitrogen stoichiometric ratios of CxN3 (M-CxN3, M-X-CxN3, X = Cl, Br, I) are evaluated. Four high-performance catalysts are screened, among which Ru-Cl-C₇N₃ exhibits the optimal catalytic activity (limiting potential = −0.38 V). This study further extracts 15 key characteristic parameters of four categories through data mining and constructs eight ML prediction models. It is found that Random Forest Regression has the best predictive performance for the NO3RR activity of SACs (test set: R2 = 0.923). The DFT-ML collaborative prediction framework not only significantly provides an effective strategy for designing NO3RR catalysts, but also offers certain guidance for the rational design of materials and resource recovery in sustainable energy technologies.

title: Agentic AI framework for accelerated catalyst design in biomass valorization via small language models and automated machine learning

verified_metadata.title: Agentic AI framework for accelerated catalyst design in biomass valorization via small language models and automated machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Biomass valorization is a critical pathway toward sustainable energy and resource utilization; however, catalyst design for biomass refining remains challenging due to the chemical diversity of feedstocks, coupled reaction parameters, and the coexistence of structured numerical data and unstructured textual knowledge dispersed across the literature. These complexities impose substantial manual effort in prescreening catalytic pathways and hinder rapid catalyst discovery. In this work, we propose an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework that integrates small language models (SLMs) for contextual text interpretation with automated machine learning (AutoML) for quantitative performance prediction. The framework autonomously extracts domain-relevant knowledge from unstructured experimental reports, links qualitative insights to structured datasets, and performs predictive screening of catalytic pathways with minimal human intervention. By bridging unstructured textual information and numerical modeling, the system accelerates the catalyst design cycle while maintaining interpretability and data security through local deployment. Multiple SLM architectures were systematically benchmarked with respect to domain specificity, response efficiency, and feature identification accuracy, leading to the selection of a lightweight model suitable for laboratory-scale deployment. The agentic workflow enables iterative database updates without retraining large models and supports seamless adaptation to domain-specific datasets. Experimental validation using biomass-derived deoxygenation reactions suggests that the proposed framework shows promising potential for guiding catalyst screening and pathway selection. This study establishes a practical agentic AI approach for accelerating biomass catalyst discovery by unifying contextual reasoning and numerical prediction within a single autonomous workflow. The framework is readily extensible to other catalysis and chemical engineering applications where unstructured knowledge and limited datasets constrain conventional machine learning approaches.

title: Knowledge-driven machine learning models for prediction of critical outputs in atmospheric and pressurized trickle-bed reactors for ex-situ biomethanation
abstract: Trickle bed reactors (TBRs) represent a promising strategy for ex-situ biomethanation and biomethane production with high methane content. The influence of operating parameters has been extensively studied across both laboratory and pilot scale TBRs to optimize critical outputs/key performance indicators such as methane purity, methane production rate (MPR), and hydrogen (H 2 ) transfer. In this study, machine learning (ML) techniques have evolved into an effective approach for studying the interactions among operating parameters and their effect on TBR performance, enabling more accurate prediction and optimization under both atmospheric and pressurized conditions. Ten ML regression models were employed to predict key parameters in the two identical TBRs operating at atmospheric and pressurized conditions. The results indicate that RF, XGBoost, and kNN outperform the other models, achieving R 2 > 0 . 95. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was then applied to identify optimal operating conditions for the TBRs with the predicted models. Data from external pilot-plant TBRs were used to validate the ML regression models with the unseen data from the external pilot scale TBRs. Interestingly, while RF and XGBoost exhibit the best overall performance, kNN and ANN provide more accurate predictions for individual data points from the external pilot-scale TBRs. • Machine learning modelling workflow was created for biological methanation in Trickle Bed Reactors. • Certain models were able to confidently predict the methane purity at the exit of the reactor, the methane production rate, and the hydrogen transfer rate. • Explainability of the models was ascertained through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values. • Optimized operating conditions were estimated through Particle Swarm Optimization of the ML models. • The model was experimentally validated with data coming from other similar biogas upgrade systems, solidifying its universal applicability.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning and multi−scale descriptor frameworks for accelerated discovery of CO2 electrocatalysts
verified_metadata.abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction is central to sustainable fuel and chemical production, facilitating the conversion of greenhouse gases into valuable products. Progress in this field is hindered by complex reaction pathways, competing intermediates, and a high−dimensional design space, posing challenges for mechanistic understanding and material selection. Modern catalyst design increasingly relies on systematic, principle−driven approaches that link physicochemical properties to catalytic performance. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful data−centric methodology, accelerating discovery and revealing hidden patterns in extensive catalyst datasets. This review examines the role of machine learning in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, emphasizing descriptor frameworks that connect catalyst structure with reactivity and selectivity. It considers key sources of CO2RR − related data−computed, measured, or literature−based−and analyzes strategies for constructing and validating electronic and thermodynamic descriptors. By highlighting case studies, we illustrate how machine learning models predict performance trends and screen catalysts across diverse composition spaces, offering mechanistic insights overlooked by traditional methods. We prioritize the reliability and interpretability of descriptor−based models to guide researchers in effectively utilizing machine learning in CO2RR and reshaping rational electrocatalyst discovery principles.

verified_metadata.title: Techno-economic optimization and cycle schedule analysis of poly-bed VPSA process for CO2 capture from natural gas combustion emissions using parallel Bayesian optimization with ANN ensembles
verified_metadata.abstract: Vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) processes stand out among CO2 capture technologies for their low energy requirement, environmental sustainability, and operational flexibility. Most existing VPSA-based CO2 capture studies have focused on coal-fired flue gas (~15% CO2). However, the ongoing shift toward natural gas-fired power plants, which emit flue gas with lower CO2 concentrations (< 10% CO2), highlights the need for systems optimized for dilute CO2 streams. Moreover, previous studies have largely been limited to small-scale systems with simplified cycle configurations, restricting their industrial applicability. This study optimizes the operating conditions and cycle configurations of industrial-scale poly-bed VPSA processes for CO2 capture by introducing a novel parallel batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework utilizing artificial neural network ensembles. The optimization considered three objectives of CO2 purity, recovery, and total annualized cost (TAC), with a focus on the role of pressure equalization (PE) steps in minimizing energy consumption during desorption. A pronounced trade-off was found: adding PE steps enhances CO2 purity and recovery and lowers energy consumption, but raises TAC. Notably, the optimization results indicated that incorporating three or more PE steps was essential for achieving optimal performance. Global sensitivity and techno-economic analyses were conducted to identify key variables and to examine the effects of PE steps, CO2 emission penalties, and electricity prices. To rationalize the need for PE steps, a net CO2 recovery was introduced to consider both process-level CO2 recovery and indirect CO2 emissions associated with energy consumption. This study provides a comprehensive optimization framework that balances energy efficiency, cost, and separation performance, contributing to the sustainable design of next-generation VPSA systems for low-concentration CO2 flue gas.

title: Integrated techno-economic and structure-property assessment of continuous TEMPO-mediated oxidation for cellulose nanofiber production
abstract: The transition towards sustainable materials manufacturing demands scalable and economically viable processes for producing cellulose nanofibers (CNFs). TEMPO-mediated oxidation is among the most efficient routes for generating carboxylated fibers, yet its industrial application remains constrained by chemical costs and the challenge of shifting from batch to continuous operation. In this work, TEMPO-mediated oxidation of bleached eucalyptus kraft pulp for CNF production was performed in a continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) to assess how residence time affects CNF properties and process economics, through integrated experimentation, reaction-kinetics modeling and techno-economic assessment (TEA). Short residence times generated under-oxidized fibers, whereas excessive exposure led to partial degradation, indicating an optimal residence time of 90 min. TEA under two scenarios, fixed production rate and fixed reactor volume, showed that operating at 90 min offers the most cost-effective balance between CNF quality and processing costs. Finally, an AI-assisted TEA framework (predictive R 2 > 0.99) allowed a 10,000-run Monte Carlo Simulation, yielding a 90% confidence interval for the Minimum Selling Price of $4.46/kg - $9.78/kg, considering catalyst recovery. Overall, this study establishes a process-level framework by providing an understanding of the relation between the residence times in a CSTR with final CNF properties, indispensable for implementing industrial production and application of these nanomaterials. By integrating the experimental structure-property maps with the TEA, an ideal operating window was identified, that balances CNF performance with reaction cost, and quantitatively identified production scale (≈90% importance) and catalyst cost (≈5% importance) as the dominant drivers of economic viability. • Continuous TEMPO-oxidation of fibers proof of concept for scale up • Best conditions for optimal residence time were identified. • ML-augmented TEA identifies feature importance. • Monte Carlo simulation showed economic potential for speciality applications.

verified_metadata.title: Active learning-driven multi-objective design of high-entropy alloy catalysts for saline water electrolysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Saline water electrolysis has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable hydrogen production due to the abundance of seawater resources. However, commercialization is hindered by reliance on precious-metal catalysts and the difficulty of maintaining selective reaction pathways under saline conditions. Here, we introduce a high-entropy alloy (HEA) catalyst design strategy enabled by an active learning, multi-objective framework that simultaneously optimizes activity, selectivity, and cost. By combining Gaussian process regression with the expected improvement acquisition, we efficiently explore the vast compositional space of HEAs using only a limited number of density functional theory calculations, achieving high predictive accuracy at ∼1.2% of the computational cost of full-space exploration. Computational results reveal distinct optimal compositions for seawater electrolysis. Cu-rich HEA compositions at the anode maximize oxygen evolution reaction activity while effectively suppressing the competing chlorine evolution reaction, providing a cost-effective alternative to conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. In addition, Ni-rich compositions exhibit hydrogen evolution reaction activity comparable to that of pure Pt while significantly reducing precious-metal content at the cathode. Overall, this active learning-driven, multi-objective protocol accelerates HEA discovery for seawater electrolysis and is readily transferable to other electrochemical energy-conversion and catalyst-design problems requiring simultaneous optimization of multiple competing objectives.

verified_metadata.title: Inverse design of water-stable MOFs for CO2 capture from wet flue gas via AI-based descriptor engineering and theoretical investigation using DFT
verified_metadata.abstract: Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture from wet flue gas face critical challenges, such as competitive H2O adsorption and humidity-induced structural degradation. This study presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based descriptor engineering for inverse design framework integrating the Cascaded Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CasTGAN) and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to accelerate the discovery of high-performance water-stable MOFs. Analysis of the CoRE MOF 2019 dataset using correlation and mutual information methods identified pore confinement parameters (pore volume and largest cavity diameter) and framework electronegativity (metallic percentage and weighted electronegativity) as critical selectivity determinants under humid conditions. CasTGAN demonstrated superior synthetic data quality and enabled realistic MOF descriptor engineering, achieving a Fréchet inception distance of 0.017, which was lower than that of conventional GAN (1.384). Moreover, TabPFN achieved exceptional predictive accuracy (R2 of 0.959 and 0.943 for CO2/H2O and CO2/N2 selectivity, respectively), outperforming other AI models. SHAP-based explainable AI validated key descriptor contributions and guided systematic screening to identify five promising candidates: OKAYEG, OHIHET, QOKCID, QUXRIM, and ZERQOE. Density functional theory confirmed the preference of OKAYEG and QOKCID on CO2 binding (−39.48 kJ/mol and − 42.08 kJ/mol) over competing H2O (+3.82 kJ/mol and + 4.2 kJ/mol) and N2 (−30.12 kJ/mol and − 25.17 kJ/mol). This study showed that a lack of open metal sites, small pore size, and unique structural orientation enhance the CO2 uptake capacity of OKAYEG over H2O and N2. This integrated computational pipeline offers a transformative approach for the rational design of water-stable MOFs under realistic industrial flue gas conditions.

title: Electrochemical construction of Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF substrate for machine learning-assisted SERS analysis of volatile organic compounds

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习分析MOF-SERS挥发有机物光谱，区别模拟呼气中结直肠癌标志物。

verified_metadata.title: Electrochemical construction of Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF substrate for machine learning-assisted SERS analysis of volatile organic compounds
verified_metadata.abstract: Plasmonic MOF materials offer a promising solution to the low affinity of volatile organic compounds (VOC) toward conventional pure-metal surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates. However, the widely adopted bottom-up synthesis approaches often suffer from the irregular aggregation of metal nanostructures, impairing signal reproducibility, and the formation of flexible MOF with ligand defects, compromising selectivity. Here, we report a purely electrochemical top-down strategy to fabricate a Turing-patterned plasmonic MOF SERS substrate, in which the electrochemically sculptured Turing-patterned Ag enables highly reproducible Raman signal amplification, while the subsequently current-grown rigid ZIF-8 layer—with restricted ligand dynamics—selectively enriches volatile organic compounds via hierarchical porosity and non-covalent interactions. Notably, the Turing-patterned Ag@ZIF-8 enables instantaneous readout of the molar ratios of chloroform, benzene, and benzaldehyde in the gaseous mixtures solely by their Raman intensity ratios. By integrating spectral collection via portable Raman spectrometers with machine learning-assisted spectral analysis, we can readily distinguish colorectal cancer-related VOC profiles from healthy ones in simulated breath samples with an accuracy up to 94.0%. This work presents a novel practical approach for constructing low-cost, high-performance plasmonic MOF SERS substrates, advancing point-of-care diagnostics by leveraging SERS technique and artificial intelligence.
