title: Modeling of crystallization processes using physics-informed neural networks and in-situ image analysis

ai4s_review.rationale: 计算机视觉晶体分割与物理信息神经网络结合，从实验图像学习结晶动力学。

verified_metadata.title: Modeling of crystallization processes using physics-informed neural networks and in-situ image analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate determination of crystal size distribution (CSD) and kinetics is crucial for understanding and controlling crystallization. This study presents a hybrid framework integrating a crystal segmentation model (CSM) with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The CSM, based on a YOLO instance-segmentation backbone, converts raw process images into structured CSDs and distinguishes crystals from bubbles. These CSDs and process variables are then input into a PINN that embeds the population balance equation (PBE) as soft constraints to predict CSD evolution and infer growth and nucleation kinetics directly from experimental visuals. Across multiple cooling runs, the framework accurately reconstructs full CSDs and extracts interpretable kinetic parameters. The results demonstrate that computer vision can serve as a virtual sensor providing high-quality data for PINNs, enabling physically consistent learning from experiments and advancing crystallization process modeling and control.

title: Engineered ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core–shell nanozymes enable ultrasensitive Cas12a-mediated miRNA biosensing for machine learning-aided gastric cancer diagnosis

verified_metadata.title: Engineered ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core–shell nanozymes enable ultrasensitive Cas12a-mediated miRNA biosensing for machine learning-aided gastric cancer diagnosis
verified_metadata.abstract: Circulating miRNAs (e.g., miR-155 and miR-21) hold great potential as biomarkers for gastric cancer (GC) diagnosis, yet their extremely low abundance in body fluids and high sequence homology pose substantial challenges for clinical applications. Herein, an ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensing platform has been developed for precise detection of GC-associated miRNAs based on engineered core-shell nanozymes and a cascade enzymatic amplification strategy. Specifically, a miRNA-initiated SDA enabled CRISPR/Cas12a amplification strategy (miSCAS) was designed to achieve automatic signal amplification in a single-tube setup. Subsequently, the activated Cas12a cleaved the sensing-interface hairpin probes, thereby exposing the phosphate groups. Simultaneously, the ZrFe-MOF@PtSn core-shell nanozymes were synthesized by in situ growth of a ZrFe-MOF shell onto the PtSn core. This engineered architecture not only endows the nanozyme with stronger catalytic activity but also utilizes the Zr element in the ZrFe-MOF shell to form Zr-O-P bonds with the phosphate groups exposed by the probe, thereby achieving efficient amplification cascade integration of nanozyme catalysis and miSCAS. Benefiting from the synergistic signal enhancement of ZrFe-MOF@PtSn nanozymes and miSCAS, the developed biosensing method achieved an attomolar-level limit of detection (1.349 aM for miR-155 and 1.428 aM for miR-21) and demonstrated high agreement with the gold standard RT-qPCR (R2 > 0.96) in clinical sample validation. Crucially, the integration of a Lasso machine learning model enabled intelligent classification, significantly improving the accuracy of the biosensor in diagnosing GC based on dual-target current response values to 98%. This work deeply integrated nanozyme catalysis, Cas12a-based cascade amplification, and machine learning to construct a universal miRNA biosensing system, which provided a translational strategy for the precise diagnosis of GC.

title: Interpretable machine learning guides rational design of dual-site catalysts for synergistic aerobic oxidation of benzylamine

ai4s_review.rationale: 可解释XGBoost解码描述符与苄胺有氧氧化性能关系，指导双位点催化剂设计。

verified_metadata.title: Interpretable machine learning guides rational design of dual-site catalysts for synergistic aerobic oxidation of benzylamine
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient heterogeneous catalysts play a pivotal role in the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine to imine. However, conventional “trial-and-error” approaches for catalyst development are often cost-prohibitive and labor-intensive. The advent of interpretable machine learning (ML) offers a transformative solution, enabling the accelerated discovery and rational design of high-performance catalysts. Herein, we developed an interpretable XGBoost model to decode the relationship between feature descriptors and catalytic performance. Leveraging this model, we rapidly pinpointed optimal catalyst compositions with exceptional activity. Guided by these insights, we synthesized a cost-effective dual-site catalyst, FeNP-FeSA@NC-800, which demonstrated outstanding performance with complete conversion of benzylamine and 98% selectivity for imine under mild conditions (90 °C, 8 h). Moreover, the catalyst exhibited broad substrate compatibility and excellent recyclability. Control experiments and theoretical calculations revealed that the synergistic interplay between dual active sites is key to the enhanced catalytic efficiency. Specifically, the coexisting Fe nanoparticles (FeNP) effectively modulated the d-band center of Fe single atoms (FeSA), optimizing the adsorption capacity for oxygen and benzylamine, thereby accelerating the aerobic oxidation of benzylamine.

verified_metadata.title: An integrated self-powered platform featuring acid responsive MOF probes for machine learning based early warning of lung cancer
verified_metadata.abstract: The early and precise diagnosis of lung cancer is crucial for improving patient prognosis. This study constructs an integrated cluster based on bioinformatic design and matrix-derived energy supply for building in vitro and in vivo detection models. Through bioinformatic analysis, the highly expressed miRNA-21 in lung cancer is identified as a key biomarker. A metal-organic framework (MOF) is employed to encapsulate natural enzymes, leveraging its acid-responsive properties for controlled enzyme release. The material surface is modified with an aptamer specifically targeting miRNA-21, enabling the cluster to actively seek out and bind to the target. Innovatively, the system utilizes glucose in clinical body fluids as an endogenous fuel, converting chemical energy into electrical energy through enzyme-catalyzed redox reactions to achieve self-powering operation, thereby driving electrochemical signal output. Simultaneously, the fluorophore-modified aptamer enables synchronous fluorescence signal output, making it suitable for different clinical detection scenarios. Finally, the collected signal data are integrated with a machine learning algorithm to construct a early-warning model for lung cancer. This work establishes a streamlined pipeline from biomarker discovery to predictive clinical analysis.

title: Nanostructured composite E-nose for selective exhaled nitric oxide detection and machine learning-assisted respiratory disease diagnosis

verified_metadata.title: Nanostructured composite E-nose for selective exhaled nitric oxide detection and machine learning-assisted respiratory disease diagnosis
verified_metadata.abstract: Detection of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) in exhaled breath is essential for monitoring respiratory diseases. Despite significant progress in NO sensing, achieving sub- parts-per-billion (ppb) detection in complex environments remains challenging. Here, we introduce a highly sensitive and selective NO sensor composed of gallium nitride nanowires (GaN-NWs) coated with zinc oxide (ZnO) and cadmium sulfide (CdS) nanoparticles (CZ-GaN-NWs). The integration of ZnO and CdS onto GaN-NWs strategically enhances sensing performance through interfacial charge transfer and surface redox reactions, leading to resistance modulation upon NO adsorption. The optimized C2Z2-GaN-NWs sensor demonstrates a 3.96-fold increase in response compared to bare GaN-NWs. It offers exceptional sensitivity with a detection limit of 2 ppb and a high signal-to-noise ratio in highly humid exhaled breath, surpassing the performance of current state-of-the-art NO sensors. Sensor arrays are further employed to enable pattern recognition capable of discriminating between simulated biomarkers and controlled breath. Validated through exhaled breath analysis, the sensor successfully distinguishes between healthy individuals and those with respiratory diseases. Moreover, advanced machine learning models accurately predict NO concentrations and classify disease stages. The proposed e-nose breath sensor offers a reliable, non-invasive solution for the early diagnosis and monitoring of respiratory diseases.

title: Design of dual-atom catalysts for CO2 reduction to C2 products: From synergistic mechanisms to machine learning guidance

verified_metadata.title: Design of dual-atom catalysts for CO2 reduction to C2 products: From synergistic mechanisms to machine learning guidance
verified_metadata.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have garnered significant attention due to their maximized atomic utilization and intrinsic catalytic activity. However, their application—particularly in multi-electron pathways—is often constrained by low metal loading and the geometric isolation of active sites. In contrast, dual-atom catalysts (DACs) offer a compelling solution by enhancing site density and fostering neighboring synergistic effects. These proximal sites provide a versatile platform for breaking scaling relations, rendering DACs an ideal strategy for facilitating CC coupling. Here, we comprehensively review the design and application of DACs for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to C2 products. We first elucidate the reaction mechanisms, contrasting the “single-site dilemma” of SACs with the synergistic advantages of DACs. Furthermore, we examine the critical role of machine learning (ML) in accelerating catalyst discovery, highlighting its capability to efficiently navigate the vast compositional space for rational design. Finally, we summarize existing challenges and outline future directions for bridging the gap between laboratory-scale research and industrial applications.

title: Data-driven inverse design for magnesium hydroxide precipitation: Coupling CFD–PBM with deep learning to control hexagonal platelets morphology formation and particle size distribution
abstract: Magnesium hydroxide precipitation is a key industrial process whose outcome strongly depends on operating conditions, hydrodynamics, and supersaturation dynamics, ultimately affecting particle morphology and particle size distribution (PSD). In this work, a mechanistic and data-driven inverse design framework is proposed by coupling Computational Fluid Dynamics and Population Balance Modelling (CFD-PBM) with deep learning techniques to identify precipitation kinetics and predict particle characteristics under different semi-batch feeding strategies. A neural-network-based surrogate model is employed to infer kinetic parameters governing nucleation, growth, and agglomeration directly from experimentally measured characteristic particle sizes, drastically reducing the computational burden associated with traditional optimization loops. The identified kinetic parameters are shown to be transferable across operating conditions and reactor configurations, enabling accurate predictions without re-calibration. The proposed CFD-PBM model successfully captures the effect of supersaturation generation rate on particle morphology, distinguishing between globular primary particles formed under rapid supersaturation buildup and hexagonal platelet-like structures obtained under slower supersaturation conditions. Shape effects are accounted for through morphology-dependent shape factors, demonstrating that particle shape primarily influences the quantitative magnitude of characteristic sizes while preserving qualitative trends. Model predictions are in good agreement with experimental data within the observed variability. Overall, this study provides a robust and computationally efficient framework for the mechanistic interpretation of magnesium hydroxide precipitation, offering new opportunities for morphology and PSD control through the integration of CFD-PBM modelling and advanced machine learning techniques.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-driven MOF-on-MOF luminescent array for multiplexed biomarker recognition in depression diagnostics and information anticounterfeiting
verified_metadata.abstract: The global burden of depression urgently requires precision diagnostics capable of overcoming the high misdiagnosis rate associated with symptom-based assessments. Concurrent recognition of interrelated biomarkers in body fluid is capable of improving diagnostic accuracy but remains technically challenging. However, it is remains technically challenging due to the structural similarity between the targets and their susceptibility to interference from complex matrices. To address these limitations, a machine learning (ML)-driven MOF-on-MOF (metal-organic framework) intelligent luminescent array was developed. This array leverages programmable heteroepitaxial growth to architecturally integrate distinct luminescent MOFs into a single hierarchical structure. This design enables precise spatial confinement of tunable emission centers, facilitating effective multi-channel signal generation. The multi-luminescent centers combine its multiple signal generation capabilities to convert spectral response datasets into interpretable diagnostic outputs of four biomarkers of depression via ML algorithms. This array sensor not only demonstrated low detection limits for the biomarkers but also realized nearly 100% accuracy for recognition of biomarkers, highlighting its potential for both sensitive detection and selective identification of biomarkers in serum and urine samples. The applicability of this sensor platform can also be extended to fingerprint and security code for anticounterfeiting. The integration of programmable MOF heterostructures with multi-channel signal emphasizing the critical role of multi-biomarker profiling in enhancing diagnostic accuracy and enabling personalized therapeutic monitoring.

title: Unraveling the early-stage hydration mechanism of tricalcium silicate via machine learning potentials

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习势能分子动力学研究硅酸三钙早期水化反应，解释水泥化学机理。

verified_metadata.title: Unraveling the early-stage hydration mechanism of tricalcium silicate via machine learning potentials
verified_metadata.abstract: Portland cement (PC), the most widely used construction material globally, requires a deep understanding of its hydration mechanisms to improve its performance, with tricalcium silicates (C3S) playing a central role in determining its fundamental properties. Due to the limitations of experimental methods and the slow, inaccurate nature of traditional molecular dynamics, it is challenging to characterize reactions occurring over large temporal and spatial scales. To overcome these challenges, we used a high-precision and efficient neuroevolution potential (NEP-MLP). For the first time, we achieved atomistic-scale early-stage dynamic simulations of the complete C3S hydration process, improving computational efficiency by seven orders of magnitude compared to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Our findings show that hydration begins with surface hydroxylation, followed by inward proton transfer, calcium dissolution through two coordination mechanisms, and the formation of calcium hydroxide (CH) clusters. Calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) gel formation occurs through both low-energy and high-energy pathways, with matrix pitting effects enhancing deep-layer reaction kinetics. This study establishes a new paradigm for cement science by bridging the atomic and engineering scales. This paradigm shift, which integrates data and physics, not only advances the field toward predictive development but also provides a foundation for designing durable, low-carbon cementitious materials for century-scale projects.

title: From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence
abstract: Nucleic acid aptamers are emerging as powerful “chemical antibodies,” namely synthetic oligonucleotide ligands that emulate antibody-like molecular recognition while retaining the programmability and scalability of chemical synthesis, for precision medicine. Yet their clinical translation has been historically bottlenecked by the stochastic nature of classical discovery methods like SELEX. This trial-and-error paradigm is labor-intensive and often fails to identify binders with optimal therapeutic properties. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is currently driving a fundamental paradigm shift from empirical screening to rational engineering. This review synthesizes the rapid evolution of this landscape, framing High-Throughput SELEX not merely as a selection tool, but as a critical data engine fueling computational discovery. We categorize current AI frameworks into two distinct paradigms: predictive architectures that decipher complex sequence-structure-function rules from noisy datasets, and generative models (e.g., VAEs, diffusion models, and inverse folding) that enable the de novo design of binders targeting specific geometries. Furthermore, we highlight translational breakthroughs in AI-designed biosensors and chemically optimized therapeutics. Finally, we discuss current challenges in data sparsity and interpretability, outlining a roadmap toward closed-loop ecosystems, that is, iterative design–test–refine workflows in which computational design, experimental validation, and model updating are continuously linked, to accelerate the development of next-generation molecular tools.

ai4s_review.rationale: 结合DFT与机器学习筛选黑磷负载单原子催化剂，研究锂硫电池电子调控机制。

verified_metadata.title: Unveiling the electronic regulation mechanism via a combined DFT-machine learning strategy to screen high performance single-atom catalysts on black phosphorus monolayer for LiS batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: Lithium‑sulfur batteries (LiS), despite their high theoretical energy density, suffer from polysulfide shuttling and sluggish redox kinetics. Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer a promising route to address these issues, but their development is impeded by both the vast chemical space and insufficient understanding of how local electronic structure controls interfacial processes. Herein, a synergistic computational strategy integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML) is presented to efficiently screen and design high performance SACs, using transition metal atoms anchored on black phosphorus monolayer (TM-BP) as a model system. The combined approach identifies Ti-BP, V-BP and ML-predicted Hf-BP as exceptional electrocatalysts with optimal polysulfide binding and accelerated kinetics. The underlying catalytic mechanism is further deciphered through systematic electronic structure analysis, revealing that d-p orbital hybridization plays a critical role in regulating adsorption behavior and charge transfer. Furthermore, a unique “aggregation-donation-feedback” interfacial electron transfer mechanism is proposed, which clearly elucidates the complete electronic process of Li2S on the catalyst surface, from adsorption and activation to eventual decomposition, thereby explaining the origin of catalytic activity at the quantum mechanical level. By employing the SISSO algorithm, an interpretable, low-dimensional descriptor is derived that quantitatively correlates the Li2S decomposition barrier with intrinsic properties of the metal centers, establishing a generalizable principle for catalyst design. This work establishes an efficient DFT-ML synergistic screening framework, which not only accelerates the discovery of single-atom electrocatalysts but also provides a rational design pathway for high performance cathode hosts in LiS batteries.

title: Stability-aware, transferable discovery of metal-organic frameworks for selective adsorption of C6 alkane isomers by machine learning

verified_metadata.title: Stability-aware, transferable discovery of metal-organic frameworks for selective adsorption of C6 alkane isomers by machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Separation of C6 alkane isomers is a key yet energy-intensive step in petroleum refining because they exhibit highly similar physicochemical properties. Here we develop a stability-aware, transferable discovery workflow to identify metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) capable of shape-selective (SS) or inverse shape-selective (IS) adsorption of C6 isomer mixtures comprising n-hexane (n-hex), 2-methylpentane (2mp), and 2,3-dimethylbutane (23dmb). We first perform computational screening on the CoRE-MOF-2024 database with 14,500 MOFs and reveal distinct SS/IS schemes governed by pore confinement and cavity-guest matching. To translate separation performance into practical viability, we then shortlist MOFs with thermal, activation and mechanical stabilities. Guided by these screening results, we train high-fidelity machine learning (ML) classifiers that achieve receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ≥ 0.90 and robust accuracy (0.88–0.91), enabling rapid prioritization beyond the screened set. For the more extensive and diverse ARC-MOF database with 270,000 MOFs, we identify two experimentally actionable candidates that surpass training-set benchmarks, achieving TSN(SS) = 15.17 and TSN(IS) = 2.57. This study establishes a generalizable, stability-aware ML paradigm for accelerating the digital discovery of deployable MOFs for challenging hydrocarbon separations and other industrially important applications.

title: Advances in methane sensor development: From fundamentals to field deployment and future perspective
abstract: Methane plays a dual role in modern society, serving as a valuable energy resource while also being a major contributor to climate change and a serious safety hazard due to its explosivity. As a result, the ability to reliably detect and quantify methane is critical across a wide range of sectors, including mining, oil and gas, agriculture, and waste management. Over the past decades, a diverse array of methane sensing technologies has been developed to address these needs, spanning laboratory-scale devices, field-deployable sensors, and large-area monitoring platforms. This review examines these technologies from a practical, application-driven perspective, covering their underlying sensing principles, material systems, performance characteristics, and typical deployment contexts. Point sensors such as catalytic pellistors, non-dispersive infrared sensors, and chemiresistive devices remain central to localized safety monitoring and leak detection, where fast response and robust operation are essential. At larger spatial scales, mobile and fixed open-path optical techniques enable real-time monitoring of methane over distances ranging from tens of meters to several kilometres, while airborne and satellite-based hyperspectral imaging now plays an increasingly important role in identifying large emission sources and validating regional and global emission inventories. Rather than viewing these approaches in isolation, this review frames methane detection as a complementary, multi-scale sensing hierarchy, in which different technologies address distinct but interconnected monitoring challenges. Particular attention is given to the trade-offs that currently limit widespread deployment, including selectivity, long-term stability, environmental interference, and cost. Finally, emerging trends in sensor integration, data fusion, and the coupling of sensing platforms with Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure and AI-based analytics are discussed as key enablers for scalable, real-time methane monitoring and more effective emission mitigation strategies.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning and process simulation-enabled discovery of high-performance MOFs for CO2/CH4 separation: An integrated molecular-to-process screening framework
verified_metadata.abstract: Identifying suitable materials for industrial gas separation from a vast pool of candidates and performing preliminary process-level assessment of their separation potential remain challenging and time-consuming tasks. This study proposes a new end-to-end ultrafast screening framework for identifying optimal metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2/CH4 separation processes, using deep learning-based MOF property prediction. The proposed framework integrates molecular-level and process-level MOF screening evaluations. In the molecular-level, prescreening of the MOFs was conducted considering the physical descriptors of the MOF structures. Then, a lattice constant-hybridized graph neural network (GNN) was developed to predict CO2 and CH4 adsorption uptakes by combining global structural information with local atomic representations, overcoming the limited receptive field of standard GNN. The predicted uptakes enable pressure swing adsorption (PSA) process simulations to determine process-level metrics, including CH4 recovery and CO2 working capacity. The framework was applied to experimentally reported MOFs across three industrial scenarios with varying methane concentrations: landfill gas, biogas and coalbed methane. The proposed framework identified promising optimal MOF solutions for each application to enhance separation efficiency, including 290 for landfill gas, 42 for biogas, and 33 for coalbed methane. Structural analysis of top-performing MOFs provides recommended property ranges including pore limiting diameter of 5.12 ± 1.50 Å and volumetric surface area of 1183 ± 551 m2/cm3 that can guide adsorbent design. The techno-economic analysis demonstrates that the identified MOF-based PSA reduces separation cost by up to 51% and improves energy efficiency by up to 28% compared to conventional separation processes. This proposed screening framework provides a fast tool for narrowing large MOF databases to a manageable set of promising candidates, linking molecular-level prediction with process-level and techno-economic screening indicators that can guide subsequent rigorous evaluation.

verified_metadata.title: Synergizing machine learning and self-assembly to hypercrosslinked polymers-based carbon nanotubes for supercapacitors
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid carbon-neutral industrialization has significantly increased the demand for high-performance supercapacitors. Porous carbon materials have received great attention for their tunable structures and hierarchical porosity, which can be optimized to enhance capacitance. However, further research is needed to elucidate the relationship between pore size, morphology, doping ratio, and performance for practical energy storage applications. To address this challenge, we propose an effective strategy that combines theoretical predictions with in-situ self-assembly of hypercrosslinked polymers (HCPs) to design optimal electrode materials. Machine learning identifies key features of carbon materials, while density functional theory calculations confirm the strong K+ adsorption energy (−0.33 eV) from heteroatom incorporation. Guided by these insights, nitrogen, sulfur, and oxygen-doped HCPs with tubular morphology are synthesized via the Friedel-Crafts reaction to meet the identified criteria. Further pyrolysis forms a heteroatom-enriched porous carbon nanotube with a hierarchical structure. It exhibits exceptional performance, achieving a high capacitance of 812.43 F g−1 at 0.3 A g−1 in a 6 M KOH solution, along with remarkable cycling stability, retaining 99.84% of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1. This work provides a robust strategy for the rational design of porous carbon for energy storage, leveraging advanced theoretical predictions and assembly techniques.

title: Normal/inverse sandwich structure series-engineered layer-dependent double-atom catalysts featuring bridge-bonded dual‑oxygen ligands for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis: Machine learning-based layer-rich extended exploration and constant-potential frontier orbital analysis

verified_metadata.title: Normal/inverse sandwich structure series-engineered layer-dependent double-atom catalysts featuring bridge-bonded dual‑oxygen ligands for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis: Machine learning-based layer-rich extended exploration and constant-potential frontier orbital analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: The urgent demand for efficient bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts motivates innovative structural designs beyond conventional planar configurations. We propose a vertically stacked dual‑oxygen-bridged bilayer architecture (TMN4-2O-TMN4@C16N3) where oxygen ligands mediate interlayer charge transfer to optimize d-band and tailor adsorption of oxygen intermediates. By integrating density functional theory (DFT) with machine learning (ML), we screened 256 bilayer configurations, identifying exceptional bifunctional catalysts such as CoN4-2O-MoN4@C16N3 (ηOER = 0.49 V, ηORR = 0.36 V), outperforming IrO2/Pt benchmarks. ML predictions achieve high accuracy with mean absolute errors of 0.09 V (OER) and 0.11 V (ORR) against independent DFT validation. Crucially, constant-potential frontier orbital analysis revealed electrode-potential-driven Fermi level shifts and orbital rehybridization, decoding dynamic adsorption mechanisms beyond neutral DFT. Extension of the machine learning framework to 768 single-layer, trilayer, and quadlayer configurations enabled high-throughput exploration of expanded structural space (ultimately extending to 1024 layer-dependent configurations), with predictions rigorously validated by independent DFT calculations. While single-layer TMN4@C16N3 suffers from high OER/ORR overpotentials due to strong oxygen intermediate binding and resultant energy barriers, the trilayer structure achieves significantly lower overpotentials through optimized pathways; performance gains saturate at quadlayers as catalytic behavior becomes governed by adjacent-layer electronic coupling and diversified charge transfer pathways, highlighting the diminishing returns and critical layer-interaction synergy in layer-dependent catalyst design. This work establishes a scalable DFT-ML workflow for accelerating the discovery of oxygen-bridged electrocatalysts across diverse architectures, with the descriptor-based ML framework readily extendable to cost-effective TM combinations for practical applications.

title: A layered approach to secure the safety and therapeutic efficacy of hiPSC-derived functionalized neuronal tissueoid for repair after complete spinal cord lnjury in rats
abstract: The functional integration of donor neurons with host neural pathways is a critical treatment for spinal cord injury (SCl). We constructed human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neuronal tissueoids (Ntoids) transfected with thymidine kinase (TK) to transplant donor neurons into SCl rats. Ntoids were produced after 28-days culture in a 3-dimensional gelatin sponge scaffold and possessed neuronal cells with synaptic transmission and neural network property in vitro. Ganciclovir, a TK substrate, depleted proliferative cells in Ntoids without affecting neuronal tissueoid formation, leaving non-mitotic and functionalized neuronal cells for transplantation. Ntoid-treated SCl rats achieved significantly better functional recovery in paralyzed hindlimbs and improved electrophysiological performance. Eight weeks after transplantation, remarkable surviving of donor cells suffused the entire injury/graft site and did not present discernible long-distance cell migration, leading to intensive innervation of the injury/graft site. Ntoids possessed cholinergic hiPSC-derived neurons that survived at the injury/graft site, successfully integrating with regenerating nerve fibers and neurons via synapse-like contacts. Some donor cells differentiated into astrocytes and formed a chimeric blood/spinal cord barrier with the host's vascular epithelium. Ntoids represent a structural and functional neuronal relay to restore functionality in paralyzed limbs. These findings support the safety and efficacy of the transplantation of mature neuronal tissue with safety-regulatory mechanisms to treat SCI and provide a framework for future clinical application using tissue-engineered Ntoid.

verified_metadata.title: Estimating dense-packed zone height in liquid–liquid separation: A physics-informed neural network approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Separating liquid–liquid dispersions in gravity settlers is critical in chemical, pharmaceutical, and recycling processes. The dense-packed zone height is an important performance and safety indicator but it is often expensive and impractical to measure due to optical limitations. We propose a framework to estimate phase heights by combining a PINN model with readily available volume flow measurements, without requiring phase height measurements during deployment. To this end, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) is first pretrained on synthetic data and physics equations derived from a low-fidelity (approximate) mechanistic model to reduce the need for extensive experimental data. While the mechanistic model is used to generate synthetic training data, only volume balance equations are used in the PINN, as incorporating droplet coalescence and sedimentation submodels would be computationally prohibitive. The pretrained PINN is then fine-tuned with scarce experimental phase height and flow-rate data to capture the actual dynamics of the separator. We then deploy the differentiable PINN as a predictive model in an Extended Kalman Filter inspired state estimation framework, enabling the phase heights to be tracked and updated using flow-rate measurements only. We first test the two-stage trained PINN by forward simulation from a known initial state against the mechanistic model and a non-pretrained PINN. We then evaluate phase height estimation performance with the filter, comparing the two-stage trained PINN with a two-stage trained purely data-driven neural network. All model types are trained and evaluated using ensembles to account for model parameter uncertainty. In all evaluations, the two-stage trained PINN yields the most accurate phase-height estimates.

title: Machine learning integrated spirulina peptide hydrogel microneedle patches for spatiotemporal sensing mercury in marine matrices
abstract: Protein-based functional hydrogels have attracted wide attention due to their biocompatibility, tunable structures, and functional diversity. We developed a novel spirulina peptide–functionalized hydrogel (SPP), integrating the intrinsic fluorescence of natural peptides with a highly hydrated, mechanically flexible polymer network. Spirulina peptides were embedded into a dual-network hydrogel, preserving fluorescence while maintaining high hydration and mechanical performance. Acting as both Hg²⁺-selective fluorescent probes and structural components, the SPP exhibits pronounced fluorescence quenching upon Hg²⁺ exposure, enabling sensitive detection with a linear range of 50–150 μg/L and a detection limit of 4.3 μg/L. Engineered into microneedle arrays, the developed hydrogel showed enhanced adhesion and interfacial adaptability on soft, curved, and moist surfaces. Meanwhile, fluorescence signals can be rapidly digitized via smartphone and analyzed with convolutional neural networks, achieving up to 97.73% quantification accuracy under complex interfaces. This study presents a versatile strategy for efficiently incorporating natural protein functionalities into hydrogel networks, offering a promising platform for biointerface materials and intelligent protein-based functional systems.

title: Optimizing aromatics yield-selectivity trade-off in zeolite-catalyzed biomass fast pyrolysis using machine learning
abstract: Catalytic fast pyrolysis of biomass to aromatic hydrocarbons is an attractive valorization technology to produce high-value chemicals and biofuels. However, process optimization to produce desired products remains challenging due to reaction complexity. Herein, we present a data-driven approach to address this issue. A literature dataset of ZSM-5-based catalysts, including promoted and unpromoted systems is compiled, resulting in 254 datapoints and subjected to data-mining. A random forest model with uncertainty quantification is devised to predict the aromatic hydrocarbon yield, and benzene, toluene, and xylene (BTX) selectivity. The models achieved comparable performance ( R 2 > 0.80) and feature-importance analysis identified feedstock composition, catalyst total acidity, catalyst-to-biomass ratio, and space velocity as key drivers of performance metrics. Given the inherent trade-off between aromatic yield and BTX selectivities, an optimization framework was devised to screen over 20,000 promoted-zeolite and reaction condition combinations, uncovering Cu, Ga, Sn, and Zr promoted-ZSM-5 as Pareto-optimal catalysts. Lastly, motivated by challenges encountered during data collection and model limitations in out-of-box predictions, we urge the community to report biomass fast pyrolysis protocols in standardized manner, and provide effective guidelines for the cause. Our study provides a predictive toolkit to identify promising catalytic systems and optimize biomass fast pyrolysis performance while improving machine readability.

title: Single atom anchored covalent organic framework assisted with machine learning for high-throughput pesticides discrimination

ai4s_review.rationale: 多层感知器解析COF-Hemin传感响应，鉴别水体单组分及多组分农药污染。

verified_metadata.title: Single atom anchored covalent organic framework assisted with machine learning for high-throughput pesticides discrimination
verified_metadata.abstract: The excessive use of modern pesticides poses significant risks to the environment and human health, yet their high-throughput discrimination in complex samples remains challenging. In this study, we report a functional material of single atom anchored covalent organic frameworks (COFs) based on self-assembly of COFs and iron porphyrin (COFs–Hemin) that has atomic Fe-N catalytic site, exhibiting highly efficient oxidase-like (OXD-like) and peroxidase-like (POD-like) activities and enabling efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation without external energy input. COFs–Hemin with desired functional groups and nanozyme activity is employed to construct a colorimetric sensor array that successfully classifies five representative pesticides in fresh apple samples with high-throughput capability. Furthermore, integrating with a machine learning algorithm of multilayer perceptron (MLP) model that can discriminate mono-component and multicomponent mixtures of multiple pesticides, COFs–Hemin demonstrates excellent performance in surface water samples with a 95.7% classification accuracy and area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.93 across all pesticide categories. The strategy that integrates single atom anchored COFs and machine learning delivers a reliable tool for high-throughput discrimination of multiple pesticides in environmental monitoring and food safety.

title: Unifying CO2 diffusion mechanisms in diamine-functionalized metal–organic frameworks via quantum-accurate machine learning dynamics
abstract: Diamine-functionalized M2(dobpdc) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) (dobpdc4- = 4,4'-dioxidobiphenyl-3,3'-dicarboxylate; M = Mg, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) exhibit exceptional CO2 capture, yet their CO2 diffusion behavior has remained difficult to rationalize across pore sizes, loadings, and functionalization. Here we resolve this gap by combining diffusion measurements with quantum-accurate machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) to establish a unified, loading-dependent mechanism for CO2 transport in Mg2(dobpdc) MOFs. Our MLPs reproduce density functional theory energetics and forces, enabling converged diffusion coefficients and microscopic trajectories. By comparing Mg2(dobdc), Mg2(dobpdc), and Mg2(dotpdc), we show that at low uptake CO2 is transiently trapped near open Mg sites, producing suppressed diffusivity in both MLP-MD simulations and diffusion measurements. With increasing uptake, the progressive saturation of these strong adsorption sites screens their trapping potential, leading to a rise in diffusion coefficients for Mg2(dobpdc) and Mg2(dotpdc), quantitatively consistent with experiments. Diamine functionalization further accelerates CO2 transport by limiting access to open Mg sites and introducing cooperative CO2–diamine interactions. Finally, the same MLPs accurately predict CO2 adsorption isotherms via grand canonical Monte Carlo. Together, the experimentally validated MLP-MD framework reveals how pore size and diamine functionalization synergistically govern CO2 diffusion, providing design rules for high-capacity MOFs with improved mass transport.

title: Ba- and Mg-promoted Ni/g-C3N4 for efficient CO2 methanation using in-house data machine learning
abstract: Methanation is one of the solutions for decreasing carbon emissions and synthetic green fuels production, being a potentially large-scale option for CO 2 utilization. However, thermodynamics in conventional reaction conditions limit the CO 2 conversion. In this work, alkaline-earth-metal modified nickel nanoparticles supported on graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) were tested in a fixed-bed reactor, being a compelling route for atmospheric CO 2 methanation. The use of g-C 3 N 4 as a support offers a more sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional oxide materials, while maintaining competitive catalytic performance with lower Ni loading and milder activation conditions. The catalysts were synthesized using two synthesis approaches: pre-incorporation and co-impregnation with Ni and Ba or Mg into the g-C₃N₄ lattice. The catalysts were characterised using N 2 physisorption, XRD, H 2 -TPR, CO 2 -TPD, TPR, Raman and XPS. The catalyst, where first incorporating the alkaline-earth metal into the g-C 3 N 4 support (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Mg), exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a 17-fold increase in CO 2 conversion (from 3 to 51%) and a substantial enhancement in CH 4 selectivity (from 13 to 94%) compared to the undoped catalyst at 325 °C. The Mg-promoted catalyst has better-dispersed Ni nanoparticles, stronger metal-support interaction, greater proportion of metallic Ni species and more moderate basic sites than Ni/g-C 3 N 4 . Mg incorporation also creates Lewis basic sites and increases overall CO 2 adsorption sites on the eg-C 3 N 4 support. The linked Mg dopant and eg-C 3 N 4 synergy drives high activity and stability for low-temperature CO 2 methanation. The catalyst prepared by pre-incorporating the alkaline-earth Ba into the g-C 3 N 4 (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Ba) exhibits degraded textural properties and basicity. The presence of barium promotes the stabilization of ferromagnetic Ni clusters. However, the intense signals from Ni + single sites justify the catalyst's performance. Overall, the increased surface nitrogen concentration and the higher proportion of metallic Ni species are clearly beneficial for CO₂ activation and hydrogenation, underscoring their pivotal role in enhancing catalytic activity. In summary, these results highlight the crucial role of promoter choice in CO₂ hydrogenation catalysts, with Mg or Ba-doped Ni/g-C₃N₄ presenting an effective route for methane synthesis. An in-house dataset (71 CO 2 methanation runs) was used to train a Random Forest model to predict CH 4 yield from six controllable descriptors. The model ranked temperature, metal identity, and support-promoter loading as the main drivers and, through surrogate-based screening, identified an optimum at 350 °C over Ni/g-C 3 N 4 promoted with Mg on the support (CSP = 1.0 mmol) without a metal promoter.

verified_metadata.title: Dual-objective protein language model for discovery of non-hemolytic antimicrobial peptides from the bee-melectin sequence space
verified_metadata.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are the natural defense molecules of the innate immune system, and have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics owing to their broad-spectrum activity and low resistance potential. However, their clinical translation is hindered by proteolytic degradation and slow discovery pipelines. To address this, we developed a ProtBERT-based dual-objective machine learning (ML) framework and applied it to a constrained library of 20,000 peptide variants (6–12 residues) derived from the 18-residue bee-venom AMP, Melectin. The model was trained on curated datasets (∼25,000) to simultaneously screen for high antimicrobial potency and minimal hemolytic toxicity. This targeted approach identified 16 hit candidates, from which two lead peptides emerged, each containing at least four mutations relative to known sequences. The optimized peptides exhibited potent activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, while demonstrating negligible hemolysis. The D-enantiomer of the lead peptide demonstrated efficacy against drug-resistant strains within serum-rich media. In 3D-spheroid infection models, the peptides demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity, reflecting the promise of host-defense peptides and ML-guided strategies for scalable AMP discovery.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-assisted intelligent fluorescence sensor incorporating perovskite quantum dots with dual-recognition imprinting polymers for ultrasensitive and high-selectivity kanamycin detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Kanamycin (KANA) overuse threatens public health, necessitating precise and portable detection approaches. To address this challenge, a ratiometric fluorescence sensor (TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb) was innovatively developed for ultrasensitive and selective detection of KANA. This sensor integrated oriented molecular imprinting on TB-Eu-MOFs with in-situ encapsulation of CsPbBr₃-Rb perovskite quantum dots. High-affinity imprinting layer featuring covalent/non-covalent dual-recognition sites boosted the precise identification of TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb to KANA. Thanks to synergistic dual-mechanism of dynamic quenching and electron transfer, water-resistant CsPbBr₃-Rb (520 nm) underwent pronounced fluorescence quenching upon exposure to KANA, boosting sensitivity. Conversely, the red fluorescence (620 nm) of TB-Eu-MOFs remained unaffected. Given inherent merits, TB-Eu-MOFs@MIPs@CsPbBr₃-Rb demonstrated exceptional suitability for ratiometric fluorescence profiling of KANA, featuring a linear range of 0.075–24.000 μg/mL, a detection limit of 22.5 ng/mL, a superior imprinting factor (6.66), ultra-fast response (2 min), attractive green-yellow-pale pink-red transformation, and satisfactory recoveries (90.00–98.43%). Intriguingly, by integrating a deep learning-driven smartphone device, the proposed sensor achieved on-site identification, concentration classification, and quantitative assay of KANA, demonstrating commendable precision and desirable recoveries (90.47–109.85%) in tap water, milk, and chicken. Accordingly, the deep learning-driven fluorescence sensor exhibited portability, feasibility, high selectivity, and sensitivity, offering a powerful tool for on-site food safety and environmental monitoring with high practicality.

verified_metadata.title: Elucidating the dual role of fulvic acid in Cu2+ adsorption on Mn-modified algal biochar through density functional theory and machine learning analyses
verified_metadata.abstract: Cu2+ contamination in aquatic environments poses serious ecological and health risks, requiring efficient, sustainable remediation strategies. In this study, Mn-modified algal biochar was prepared and used as a model adsorbent to elucidate fulvic-acid (FA)-mediated Cu2+ adsorption in a ternary system. Characterization analyses revealed that Mn modification substantially increased the specific surface area, mesopore volume, and oxygen-containing surface functional groups, thereby enhancing Cu2+ affinity. Batch experiments demonstrated a pronounced FA “dual effect”: at a low concentration of 10 mg·L−1, FA markedly enhanced Cu2+ adsorption capacity up to 211.6 mg·g−1 through ternary surface complexation and increased negative surface charge, whereas a higher concentration of 20 mg·L−1 inhibited adsorption through competitive complexation in solution and surface-site blockage. Kinetic and isotherm analyses indicated dominant chemisorption, best described by the pseudo-second-order and Langmuir models, respectively. Density functional theory calculations clarified the microscopic mechanism, supporting preferential Cu2+ anchoring by MnO and carboxyl sites on the biochar followed by FA bridging to form stable ternary complexes. An extreme gradient boosting machine-learning model achieved strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.941 on the test set), with FA concentration and pH identified as the most influential factors. The major contribution of this work is not only the observation of FA concentration-dependent behavior, but also the identification of a DFT-supported Cu-bridged ternary complexation pathway and the ML-based quantification of key environmental controls. These findings provide mechanistic insights into FA-mediated Cu2+ adsorption and support Mn-modified algal biochar as a promising, sustainable adsorbent for heavy-metal remediation in surface water.

title: A fully adaptive automated system for nanoparticle washing enabled by vision and language AI
abstract: Self-driving laboratories are reshaping materials discovery by combining automated experimentation with AI-driven decision-making. However, the lack of automation in key preprocessing steps such as nanoparticle (NP) washing, remains a major barrier to achieving full experimental autonomy. Effective automation of NP washing requires visual adaptivity to detect subtle changes in the appearance of dispersions or precipitates, and cognitive adaptivity, to handle failure cases like incomplete sedimentation or phase separation. These demands make NP washing uniquely challenging despite its apparent simplicity. We introduce a fully integrated NP washing platform that combines computer vision with a large language model (LLM) to enable intelligent, end-to-end preprocessing in self-driving labs. The system employs YOLACT for real-time robotic manipulation and latent mask R-CNN for uncertainty-aware image segmentation, achieving 100% task success across 60 trials and accurately processing 45 diverse precipitate images. A retrieval-augmented LLM autonomously generates and continuously refines washing protocols based on cognitive feedback from failure detection. The platform was validated on NiFe layered double hydroxides, IrRu nanoparticles, and CdSe/CdS quantum dots. Electrochemical and photoluminescence analyses demonstrated that the automated washing achieves a quality comparable to manual processing. This work represents a critical step toward fully autonomous, closed-loop experimentation by bridging synthesis and characterization through intelligent preprocessing.

A retrieval-augmented LLM autonomously generates and continuously refines washing protocols based on cognitive feedback from failure detection. The platform was validated on NiFe layered double hydroxides, IrRu nanoparticles, and CdSe/CdS quantum dots. Electrochemical and photoluminescence analyses demonstrated that the automated washing achieves a quality comparable to manual processing. This work represents a critical step toward fully autonomous, closed-loop experimentation by bridging synthesis and characterization through intelligent preprocessing.

title: Dual-enhancement strategy for high-performance multimodal hydrogel sensors in deep learning-assisted speech recognition systems
abstract: Conductive hydrogels under large deformation often suffer from stress concentration and pronounced hysteresis, compromising their mechanical integrity and sensing reliability. Here, we propose a dual-reinforcement strategy to develop a multimodal hydrogel sensor based on amphiphilic polymer chains and MXene nanosheets. The reinforced hydrophobic micelles integrate hydrophobic association, triple hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to mitigate stress concentration and hysteresis, while MXene introduces nanoscale confinement and strong interfacial interactions, enhancing elastic recovery and reducing energy dissipation. The resulting hydrogel exhibits excellent stretchability (>1000% elongation), high toughness (2.75 MJ m-3), low hysteresis (4.1% at 400% strain), an ultralow detection limit (0.1%), and stable sensitivity (GF = 1.16) over a wide strain range (0.1-500%) with outstanding fatigue resistance (10,000 cycles). It also enables multimodal sensing of deformation and temperature (TCR=-2.13%°C-1), and can monitor environmental perturbations such as wind and hail impact. Combined with a deep learning framework, the sensor achieves 97% recognition accuracy for language-related inputs. Moreover, its intrinsic biodegradability reduces environmental impact. These features highlight its promise for healthcare monitoring, AI interfaces, and electronic skin systems.

title: Deep learning-driven strategies for the de novo design of membrane-targeting narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-driven strategies for the de novo design of membrane-targeting narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides
verified_metadata.abstract: As the global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis continues to escalate, narrow-spectrum antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have emerged as an important direction in precision anti-infective research. However, current AMPs design strategies remain largely focused on the optimization of broad-spectrum activity, and a systematic framework centered on pathogen-specific membrane interfaces is still lacking. This review focuses on deep learning (DL)-driven de novo design of membrane-interface-centered, or membrane-targeting, narrow-spectrum AMPs. It first delineates the conceptual boundaries among selectivity, targeting, specificity, and narrow-spectrum activity, and systematically summarizes exploitable differences at the cellular membrane level. It then further discusses how membrane-associated differences can be translated into programmable constraints within DL models, on the basis of which four major design routes are summarized. Subsequently, a multi-objective evaluation framework is established, and the workflow for AMPs validation across four distinct levels is outlined. Ultimately, in view of the current state of the field and its future development, targeted questions and methodological recommendations are proposed, with the aim of providing a clearer theoretical framework and methodological reference for more advanced AMPs design.

verified_metadata.title: Crystal field splitting energy mediated d-band center regulation in transition metal for enhancing plasma/persulfate degradation of metronidazole: Experiments, theoretical calculation and machine learning study
verified_metadata.abstract: Modulating the d-band center of transition metals by doping engineering is an efficient strategy to enhance their catalytic efficiency. However, there remains a lack of systematic theoretical explanation for how doping engineering modulates the d-band center and activates antibonding orbitals at the electronic structure scale. Herein, using α-Fe2O3 (αFO) as a model transition metal, machine learning, density functional theory calculations and experimental characterization were integrated to elucidate the doping induced d-band center shifts. The results reveal that dopants modulated the crystal field splitting energy of transition metals, which in turn tailors the d-band center, thereby enhancing the catalyst's ability to activate the antibonding orbitals of reactive species. This mechanism rationalized the efficient degradation of metronidazole observed in the Cu-αFO/DBD/persulfate process. Furthermore, to elucidate the degradation mechanism at the molecular level, this study investigated the structure-activity relationship, specifically how the molecular structure of the pollutants and the catalytic system influence the degradation efficiency. The data revealed the correlation between molecular properties (e.g., dipole moment and energy of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) and degradation kinetics. The proposed d-band center modulation and antibonding orbital activation mechanism provides both a theoretical foundation and a practical pathway for the rational design of high performance transition metal catalysts.

title: Machine learning-optimized coarse-grained simulations reveal multicomponent solvent-regulated phase separation for precise control of porous polymers
abstract: Precise control of pore structures in porous polymers is critical for optimizing their functional performance. Although third solvent-assisted phase separation has been experimentally demonstrated to promote pore interconnectivity and structural tunability, the molecular mechanisms governing this process remain largely unresolved. Here, we develop a machine learning-assisted dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) force fields that bridges all-atom-level accuracy and coarse-grained efficiency through data-driven force field generation. By training on structural descriptors derived from all-atom simulations, the optimized DPD force fields reliably reproduce intermolecular interactions in multicomponent solvent systems. Applying this optimized force field to polylactic acid ternary solvent systems, we reveal how the third solvent modulates phase separation behavior and propose a quantitative solvent-selection principle based on polarity and interaction energy. Experimental validation confirms the predictive capability of the model in guiding pore morphology control. Together, these results provide molecular-level insights and a practical framework for multicomponent solvent engineering, offering a pathway toward the rational fabrication advanced porous polymer materials with precisely controllable structures.

verified_metadata.title: Precision detection of early-stage liver fibrosis in MASLD via physics-informed interfacial impedance sensing of procollagen type I C-terminal peptide
verified_metadata.abstract: Early-stage liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains difficult to identify because conventional indirect fibrosis indices inadequately reflect active fibrogenesis. Procollagen type I C-terminal peptide (PICP), released during extracellular processing of type I procollagen, directly reflects collagen synthesis and provides a mechanistically relevant biomarker for fibrosis activity. Here, we present a fibrosis electrochemical impedance spectroscopy platform (FIB-EIS), a label-free impedance immunosensor for direct quantification of PICP in human plasma. The sensing interface was engineered on a gold nanoparticle–modified screen-printed carbon electrode to provide stable antibody immobilization and controlled interfacial charge transport. Upon specific PICP binding, formation of a dielectric biolayer perturbed double-layer capacitance and charge-transfer kinetics, producing a concentration-dependent increase in charge-transfer resistance. To suppress matrix-driven interfacial fouling in plasma, a Tween-20–assisted interfacial control strategy was introduced, selectively removing weakly adsorbed plasma constituents and stabilizing a reproducible dual-time-constant impedance response. This enabled mechanistically interpretable equivalent-circuit analysis by separating double-layer and biomolecular capacitive contributions under complex plasma conditions. Under optimized conditions, FIB-EIS achieved picogram-level sensitivity with a detection limit of 0.81 pg mL−1 and high selectivity against abundant plasma proteins, including procollagen type III N-terminal peptide. Because plasma dilution shifts clinically relevant PICP concentrations into the pg mL−1 regime, this sensitivity supports early-stage fibrosis discrimination. Clinical validation across biopsy-staged fibrosis (F0–F4) demonstrated 95.24% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These results establish FIB-EIS as a physics-informed and clinically translatable platform for minimally invasive fibrosis activity assessment and longitudinal MASLD monitoring.

verified_metadata.title: Synthesis of highly active binary alloy acidic oxygen evolution catalysts assisted by machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is promising for green hydrogen production, but its oxygen evolution reaction (OER) suffers from high overpotential and catalyst corrosion. While transition metal alloys exhibit excellent catalytic activity, traditional experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations are inefficient for exploring the vast binary alloy space. Machine learning enables rapid prediction and optimization by mining DFT data to map material properties with catalytic performance. Herein, this study integrates machine learning methods, including ABR, GBR, and other ensemble models, with DFT calculations to rapidly screen of acidic OER catalysts based on binary transition metal systems. Based on model predictions, we utilize electrodeposition and Joule heating techniques to synthesize FeRu alloy in a short period of time and perform experimental validation. The as-synthesized FeRu alloy exhibits exceptional bifunctional activity, requiring ultralow overpotentials of 171 mV (OER) and 47 mV (hydrogen evolution reaction) to achieve 10 mA cm−2 in acidic media. This catalyst reaches a current density of 1 A cm−2 at only 1.65 V in PEMWE. DFT calculations confirm that alloying optimizes electronic structure and reduces the rate-determining step (RDS) energy barrier, providing theoretical support for its excellent activity and stability. This work establishes a closed-loop framework that integrates data mining with experimental validation to shorten catalyst research and development cycles. It provides an efficient approach for screening and optimizing high-performance acidic PEMWE catalysts and facilitates the industrialization of green hydrogen production via PEMWE.

title: Machine learning-assisted modeling of tandem catalytic polymerization for tailoring comb-branched polyolefin elastomers

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习构建串联催化聚合动力学模型，调节梳状支化聚烯烃弹性体链结构。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted modeling of tandem catalytic polymerization for tailoring comb-branched polyolefin elastomers
verified_metadata.abstract: Polyolefin elastomers are widely utilized due to their unique combination of thermoplastic processability and rubber-like elasticity. Among them, comb-branched polyolefin elastomers (CPOEs) synthesized via tandem catalytic polymerization (TCP) of ethylene and α-olefin feature amorphous backbones with long polyethylene (PE) side chains, enabling elevated melting temperatures even at high α-olefin incorporation. Because TCP integrates ethylene homopolymerization with terpolymerization of ethylene, 1-octene, and PE macromonomers (PEMs), kinetic modeling is essential for tailoring CPOE chain structures while simultaneously controlling PEM incorporation and residual content. Herein, a kinetic model based on the method of moments was developed, with an orthogonalization algorithm employed to reduce the number of parameters requiring estimation. Direct coupling of the kinetic model with differential evolution (DE) optimization using a conventional ODE solver proved computationally intensive for parameter estimations. A large-scale training dataset was generated from the kinetic model with parameter ranges aligned to literature values and experimental observations, substantially reducing the need for expensive experimental data. The ML-assisted model was validated against experimental results. Systematic analyses of catalyst concentrations, 1-octene concentration, and polymerization times elucidated their impacts on CPOE chain structure, providing mechanistic insights for CPOE design. Overall, this study demonstrates a practical ML-assisted strategy for kinetic modeling of complex polymerization systems and provides a powerful tool for rational CPOE chain structure engineering and data-driven polymer product development.

title: Molecular characterization and chlorination reactivity of microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter revealed by ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and machine learning

ai4s_review.rationale: XGBoost由超高分辨质谱分子描述符预测微塑料溶出有机物氯化反应性。

verified_metadata.title: Molecular characterization and chlorination reactivity of microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter revealed by ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Microplastics-derived dissolved organic matter (MPs-DOM) comprises a chemically heterogeneous pool of dissolved organic compounds released during the environmental degradation of microplastics. Despite growing interest in the environmental implications of MPs-DOM, its molecular composition and reactivity are still poorly characterized. In this study, Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) was employed to characterize MPs-DOM released from polystyrene (PS), polyamide (PA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), as well as their transformation products formed during chlorination, and a reactivity prediction model was developed based on reaction networks. The results showed that all microplastics released MPs-DOM under dark conditions, while UV irradiation altered MPs surface functional groups and the molecular composition of the released MPs-DOM, leading to differences in chlorination reactivity between the dark and UV conditions. CHO dominated DOM derived from PS and PBAT, whereas PA-DOM was relatively enriched in CHNO compounds, indicating that MPs-DOM exhibited high molecular complexity and source dependent characteristics. Both aging and chlorination induced pronounced molecular transformations, leading to a significant increase in O/C ratios. The reaction network analysis linked 111 chlorine-containing DBP molecules to 127 precursors, including 122 polymer-specific precursors, with 63, 23, and 35 detected in PS, PA, and PBAT, respectively. A machine learning model based on extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) successfully identified double bond equivalent (DBE) and nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC) as the primary molecular features associated with highly reactive MPs-DOM, achieving an overall prediction accuracy of 73.53%. This work provides a molecular-level understanding of the composition, formation mechanisms, and chlorination behavior of MPs-DOM, improving our understanding of the environmental behavior and potential risks associated with MPs-DOM.

title: Bioinspired hierarchically structured liquid metal-composited eutectogel for energy conversion and intelligent perception
abstract: Inspired by the hierarchical structure of brain’s blood vessels and neural networks, which enables synergistic trade-offs among multiple properties, we developed a structural biomimetic strategy to create liquid metal (LM)-initiated polymerizable deep eutectic solvents (PDES) eutectogels. In this design, the polymerizable hydrogen bond donor forms polymer chains that mimic vascular walls and provide mechanical support, while the hydrogen bond acceptor enables ion transport for signal transmission, analogous to neurotransmitter-mediated communication. LM acts as a ”growth factor” to induce the formation of a biomimetic hierarchical network in PDES-based eutectogels. Specifically, LM introduces ionic coordination bonds to construct a hierarchical supramolecular network, while simultaneously serving as a conductive filler to establish an ion-electron conductive network, with interfacial modification promoting the dissociation of hydrogen bond acceptors. Consequently, the resulting eutectogels achieve a balanced combination of mechanical strength, ultrastretchability ((451.8 kPa, 1106%) ~substantially outperforming LM-free PDES eutectogels), high elasticity (energy dissipation rate <15% within 500% strain), and excellent ionic conductivity (~31.19 mS cm-1). This strategy effectively overcomes the practical application limitations of PDES eutectogels arising from their insufficient mechanical performance and low ionic conductivity. Furthermore, based on this platform, a ”dynamic-static” self-powered system enables low-grade heat and mechanical energy conversion into electricity while serving as a supercapacitor (SC) electrolyte for energy storage. Integrated with a convolutional neural network (CNN), the PDES-LM20 eutectogel enabled multi-channel gesture recognition with 99.5% accuracy for ten gestures. This work bridges structural biomimicry and functional synergy, advancing integrated gel platforms for energy conversion, storage, and intelligent perception.

title: “Tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors: Decoupling, anti-interference, and applications
abstract: Conventional flexible strain sensors can only detect mechanical deformation, which limits their ability to perceive multiple physical stimuli in complex scenarios such as health monitoring and human–robot interaction. To overcome this limitation, ”tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors that integrate strain sensing with other modalities (e.g., pressure, temperature, humidity, magnetic field, and bioelectricity) have emerged as a promising solution. This review provides a systematic overview of recent progress in these sensors, with an emphasis on decoupling strategies and anti‐interference methodologies. According to the output signal type and decoupling principle, existing devices are classified into four categories: single‐output, multi‐output, structurally/spatially separated, and algorithm‐assisted decoupling. Single‐output sensors exploit polarity, temporal, or amplitude differences for signal separation under constrained conditions. Multi‐output sensors achieve inherent crosstalk freedom via heterogeneous signals (e.g., electro‐optical, resistance‐voltage). Structural/spatial separation physically isolates sensing units through modulus modulation or modular design. Algorithm‐assisted decoupling employs frequency‐domain filtering, matrix algebra, and data‐driven models (e.g., LSTM, CNN) to reconstruct individual physical quantities from mixed signals. Key anti‐interference strategies, including intrinsically insensitive materials, encapsulation layers, and temporal/scenario separation, are also discussed. The applications of these sensors have expanded from limb motion monitoring to sports rehabilitation, simultaneous respiration‐behavior tracking, human‐machine interaction, and structural health monitoring. Finally, future directions are outlined, focusing on intrinsically decoupling materials, edge intelligence, and multimodal fusion for robotics and embodied intelligence. This review offers a comprehensive framework that guides the design of next‐generation intelligent multimodal sensors.

ai4s_review.rationale: 可解释机器学习结合分子动力学及实验，预测PFAS在腐殖质吸附能并解释环境归趋。

verified_metadata.title: Structure-resolved adsorption of PFAS on humic substances: A combined study of molecular dynamics, explainable machine learning, and experiments
verified_metadata.abstract: Understanding the adsorption behavior of PFAS on humic substances (HS) is critical for predicting their environmental fate and developing effective remediation strategies. Here, we integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, experimental characterization, and explainable machine learning (XAI) to resolve PFAS interactions with HS at the molecular level. Based on 410 PFAS structures, MD-derived adsorption energies reveal a clear structure-dependent adsorption trend, with a strong negative correlation (Pearson's |r| > 0.72) between molecular weight and adsorption energy magnitude. Machine learning models show robust predictive performance (R2 > 0.88), enabling accurate adsorption-energy prediction across structurally diverse PFAS. SHAP analysis reveals that PFAS adsorption onto HS is governed by a synergistic interplay of multiple molecular descriptors rather than any single molecular property. Molar refractivity, Kappa3, Number of hydrogen bond acceptors, and molecular weight emerge as the most influential descriptors, highlighting the coupled roles of electronic polarizability, molecular topology, conformational adaptability, and size in controlling adsorption. In contrast, descriptors associated with polarity and hydration tendency are more closely linked to migration behavior. Adsorption experiments and complementary spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations consistently confirmed stronger fluorine accumulation and greater compaction of the HS matrix induced by long-chain PFAS. Overall, the results converge on a unified molecular picture in which larger, more polarizable, and structurally adaptable PFAS are preferentially retained, whereas smaller and more hydration-favored PFAS remain comparatively mobile. This work provides a physics-informed and interpretable framework for predicting PFAS transport in heterogeneous organic environments.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted screening of efficient homogeneous catalysts for the aerobic reaction of aromatic hydrocarbons
verified_metadata.abstract: The ligand modification of the catalyst is a promising strategy to enhance the yields of the aerobic reaction of aromatic hydrocarbons. The approach of machine learning incorporating high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations successfully achieves the efficient screening and design of catalysts. In this work, the impact of ligands on catalyst activity was investigated. The results reveal how ligands influence the catalyst's properties and structure, which subsequently affects its reaction activity. A unique descriptor, φ, which is the ratio of nonpolar and surface area, was identified using ML for predicting yields and efficiently capturing catalytic activity trends for a variety of ligands (R2 = 0.999, error < 1%). The optimal catalyst, Cat II (cobalt bis(2-ethylhexanoate)), was selected by ML, which exhibits the highest yield (22.81 mol%). The kinetic model achieves great predictive ability for the variation in compound concentration under different conditions. The strategy incorporates ML, experimentation, and reaction kinetics, offering significant insights into catalyst screening, modifications, aerobic reaction, and modeling of aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: ELEVATE-LNP: Empty lipid nanoparticle enabled validation and AI-guided therapeutic evaluation for efficient formulation optimization for mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as a leading platform for mRNA delivery, particularly following the success of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines. However, identifying effective LNP formulations remains time-consuming because of the large and complex multicomponent formulation space. Here, we present ELEVATE-LNP an Empty-LNP-Enabled Validation and AI-Guided Therapeutic Evaluation platform by integrating a high-throughput parallelized microfluidic preparation with physicochemical characterization and machine learning for mid-stream and downstream LNP formulation optimization when ionizable lipids are shortlisted. A broad formulation space comprising four ionizable lipids, different helper lipids, lipid ratios, and process conditions was first screened using empty LNPs to identify formulations with desirable particle size and polydispersity index (PDI). Machine-learning analysis was then used to determine the formulation and process parameters associated with empty-LNP properties. Selected candidates were subsequently evaluated following mRNA encapsulation by assessing particle size, PDI, encapsulation efficiency, cell viability, and transfection performance. The results revealed lipid-dependent relationships between formulation parameters and the physicochemical properties of empty LNPs. Six features were strongly associated with particle size, while eleven features contributed to variations in PDI. GFP expression in CFBE cells demonstrated that SM-102-based LNPs achieved higher transfection efficiency than CKK-E12-based formulations. In a separate CFTR mRNA evaluation, DOPC-containing LNPs produced higher CFTR protein expression than their DSPC-containing counterparts. By integrating empty-LNP prescreening with subsequent payload-based validation, the ELEVATE-LNP workflow reduces the number of candidates and the amount of nucleic acid required for functional testing. The platform therefore provides a practical approach for narrowing lipid-ratio and formulation-condition spaces within preselected ionizable lipid systems.

verified_metadata.title: AI-driven de novo protein design coupled with high-throughput screening: Challenges and opportunities
verified_metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming protein engineering from an empirical discipline into a predictive and data-driven paradigm, accelerating the development of next-generation biocatalysts. Nevertheless, a significant gap remains because generative models can propose candidate proteins far more rapidly than laboratories can experimentally them, and computational novelty does not guarantee the performance under most of the process conditions. This review examines recent advances in AI-assisted protein engineering, highlighting how generative models, protein language models, and structure-prediction frameworks are reshaping enzyme discovery, design, and optimization. The evolution from conventional rational design and directed evolution to modern data-centric workflows built on the Design–Build–Test–Learn (DBTL) cycle is explored. Major AI architectures, such as transformers, diffusion models, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks, are evaluated for their ability to generate novel protein structures and functional sequences. Most importantly, we summarize machine learning approaches for predicting enzyme activity, substrate specificity, catalytic efficiency, thermostability, solubility, and functional annotation, which facilitate candidate prioritization and reduce the experimental burden. Reported predictive performance reaches an R2 of 0.69 for turnover number and a Pearson coefficient of 0.84 for stability change, while computational triage eliminates 50% to 80% of the design pool before synthesis. Because sequence-function relationships are inherently nonlinear, a single metric optimization is unreliable. We therefore discuss current limitations, arising from data scarcity, model interpretability, cross-family transferability, developability, and the lack of standardized benchmarks. Future perspectives are provided on integrating multimodal biological data, foundation models, and autonomous experimentation to enable scalable biocatalyst development and accelerate the transition toward AI-driven sustainable biomanufacturing.
