verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed surrogate modeling and optimization of Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites for microwave absorbers
verified_metadata.abstract: Achieving thin, target-specific microwave absorbers remains challenging because absorber performance is governed by the coupled interplay among complex permittivity, complex permeability, and thickness, while the direct linkage between target absorption behavior, electromagnetic-property spectra, and realizable material compositions is often limited. Here, we present a physics-informed optimization framework based on Zn–Co substituted Ba–W ferrite/CNT/TPU composites, in which magnetic and dielectric responses can be tuned in a decoupled manner. Co substitution in Ba–W ferrite selectively shifts the magnetic-loss frequency through anisotropy-controlled ferromagnetic resonance, whereas CNT loading independently modulates the dielectric response without significantly perturbing the magnetic behavior. Exploiting this decoupled tunability, complex permittivity and permeability were modeled separately using Kramers–Kronig-consistent spectral representations, namely a hybrid Cole–Cole model and a Gaussian–Dawson master-curve model, and then integrated into a differential-evolution-based optimization loop. This framework transformed discrete experimental datasets into a physically constrained continuous composition space, enabling continuous prediction of composition-dependent electromagnetic properties and target-specific optimization of absorber composition and thickness. As representative demonstrations, a 1.9 mm-thick absorber achieved full X-band absorption below −10 dB, whereas a 1.5 mm-thick absorber achieved nearly full Ku-band absorption below −10 dB with a measured −20 dB EAB of 3.76 GHz. Both absorbers were fabricated as 12 × 12 cm specimens and successfully validated by free-space RL measurements. This study provides an integrated framework that connects absorber performance, electromagnetic-property prediction, and material composition within a physically grounded optimization scheme.

title: A mechanistic study on the concentration-dependent pyrolysis behavior of 3D cross-linked epoxy/TPP networks via ReaxFF-MD
abstract: The local flame-retardant (FR) chemistry of polymer composites involves complex atomic-level synergistic effects that are difficult to characterize experimentally. Here, we combined reactive force field molecular dynamics (ReaxFF-MD) simulations with thermogravimetry-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy-gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (TG-FTIR-GCMS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) experiments to elucidate the concentration-dependent FR mechanism of triphenyl phosphate (TPP) in a cross-linked epoxy resin (EP) network. The ReaxFF-MD simulations quantitatively reproduced the experimental activation energies (Ea) within 5% error across TPP loadings of 0–50% and captured the non-monotonic Ea trend, which peaks at 10% TPP (243 kJ/mol experimentally; 233 kJ/mol simulated). Atomic-level reaction pathway analysis revealed that TPP decomposes via O P bond scission to release C₆H₅O• radicals; these radicals abstract hydrogen to form phenol—the primary gas-phase dilution agent—while the phosphorus-containing fragments form P-O-C linkages that bridge carbon fragments into a protective char layer in the condensed phase. These findings indicate that an optimal FR loading exists beyond which thermal stability degrades, and the identified pathways provide molecular-level targets for rational FR design. The validated ReaxFF-MD framework offers a predictive simulation platform that can serve future machine learning (ML)-accelerated FR discovery.

title: Unveiling the structural basis of Adeno-associated virus CNS tropism via geometric protein language modeling
abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid engineering enables tissue-selective gene delivery; however, identifying variants with enhanced central nervous system (CNS) tropism remains challenging. Notwithstanding the success of directed evolution approaches, it often faces practical limitations, including the substantial loss of library diversity during cloning and packaging, production biases that confound functional selection, and difficulties in assessing production fitness independently of tissue tropism. Moreover, this process requires extensive animal experimentation and iterative selection cycles, making it resource-intensive and time-consuming. Here, we developed a machine learning framework that simultaneously predicts both capsid production fitness and tissue-specific enrichment, providing capsid-residue-level biological interpretation that could be used rationally to identify CNS-targeting AAV variants. We performed in vivo directed evolution of AAV9 by replacing residues at the surface-exposed loops of VR-IV and VR-VIII, subjecting libraries to two rounds of systemic selection in mice, and quantifying tissue-specific enrichment across multiple CNS and peripheral tissues. Meanwhile, by integrating protein-language model embeddings and AlphaFold-derived structural features into attention-based neural networks, our framework achieved high predictive accuracy while providing residue-level biological interpretation. Structural validation confirmed a significant correlation between the predicted binding affinity and CNS enrichment. Moreover, this study demonstrates that high-performing tissue-targeting variants possess residues enriched in glycine, serine, and arginine, exhibiting broader charged surfaces, larger hydrophobic patches, and greater solvent accessibility. This computational framework enables capsid residue-level biological interpretation based on experimental data, which could potentially improve variant selection accuracy and reduce experimental time and animal use, establishing a foundation for rational identification of CNS-targeting variants in future studies.

title: Machine learning-assisted descriptor screening of high-entropy alloy-based catalysts for CO2 methanation
abstract: Carbon dioxide hydrogenation provides a route for converting CO 2 into methane (CH 4 ), but the large compositional space of high-entropy alloy (HEA)-based catalysts complicates empirical catalyst selection. In this study a literature-derived dataset of 251 observations was analysed using machine learning to evaluate composition-derived atomic and electronic descriptors together with surface, synthesis, and reaction variables. XGBR achieved random-split test R 2 values of 0.95 for CO 2 conversion and 0.91 for CH 4 selectivity, whereas intrinsic-descriptor-only models achieved R 2 values of 0.37 and 0.69, respectively, showing that full-model performance arises from combined catalyst and process information. SHAP and partial-dependence analyses identified reaction temperature and composition-derived descriptors including weighted Pauling electronegativity (EN), weighted atomic radius (R), and ΔR as influential model features. Weighted Pauling EN above approximately 1.2, smaller weighted atomic radii (R), and low ΔR were associated with favourable model predictions within the present dataset. These relationships are interpreted as empirical screening trends rather than direct mechanistic thresholds. NSGA-II and fuzzy logic analysis defined descriptor space screening regions, and more than 205 million five-element compositions were enumerated, of which 4,811,467, or 2.35%, satisfied the property window criteria. Experimental assessment showed lower apparent activation energies than Ni/Al 2 O 3 for several HEA-based formulations, with AlCdMgCoNi achieving 45 kJ mol −1 compared with 75 kJ mol −1 for the reference. However, the synthesized catalysts were multiphase, CH 4 selectivity remained below 60% at atmospheric pressure, and selectivity predictions transferred poorly to the experimental systems. These limitations indicate that surface-sensitive descriptors and descriptors capturing the local chemical environment are required for selectivity-focused catalyst design. Therefore, the framework is supported primarily as an activity-oriented screening and property-space narrowing approach.

title: Framework-organic symbiotic multilayer composites with artificial musculoskeletal architecture for high-performance thermal management and shape-memory flexible electronics
abstract: Bioinspired approaches based on soft biological tissues have driven major advances in artificial materials for applications. Many natural tissues, particularly muscles, exhibit anisotropic mechanical behavior and efficient energy dissipation. Here, we present a new strategy that transforms conventional composites into microscale artificial musculoskeletal systems. This is achieved by redefining inorganic nanosheets (PCNC-M) from passive reinforcing components to active structural frameworks, and by elevating the organic polymer from a simple matrix to a multifunctional, dynamic adhesive, and responsive medium. Through synergistic, physically guided co-assembly, pre-stretching drives the ordered alignment of PCNC-M nanosheets, while, poly (propylene carbonate) (PPC) acts as a dynamic adhesive, energy dissipating matrix, and multifunctional thermal and electrical regulator. The resulting multilayer composites exhibit a high tensile strength of 35.7 MPa, an in-plane thermal conductivity of 7.2 W/mK, and exceptional electrical insulation of 2.5 × 10¹⁵ Ω·cm. When applied to high-power LED modules, smartphone CPUs, and control transformers, the material achieves temperature reductions of 19.1,12.4, and 16.0°C, respectively. It also displays pronounced shape-memory behavior, with shape fixity (Rf) and shape recovery (Rr) ratios of 90.3% and 92.4%, respectively. Notably, after 120 days of soil burial, the composite achieves a degradation rate of 43.7%. This strategy transcends the conventional passive filler-matrix paradigm, enabling a dynamic artificial musculoskeletal system for next-generation thermal management in flexible and high-power devices.

verified_metadata.title: AI-accelerated discovery of a high-entropy garnet electrolyte with a flattened Li-ion energy landscape for practical solid-state batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: The vast compositional space of high-entropy materials makes the discovery of superior solid electrolytes extremely challenging. Here, we introduce a hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework that synergistically combines unsupervised learning with crystal graph convolutional neural networks (CGCNN) in a dual-stage screening architecture. This approach navigates >1800 potential Zr-site doped Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) compositions, first partitioning them into 21 distinct groups via unsupervised clustering, then focusing on a high-potential group (G19) for precise CGCNN prediction of band gaps and Li+ diffusion barriers. This AI-identified optimal high-entropy electrolyte, Li7La3Zr0.4Cr0.4Mo0.4Sn0.4Ta0.4O12 (HE-LLZO), would otherwise require years of trial-and-error. Entropy stabilization lowers the synthesis temperature to 920 °C and suppresses detrimental Li2CO3/LiOH surface formation. Bond valence site energy (BVSE) calculations, supported by solid-state NMR and geometric phase analysis, reveal that the high-entropy configuration introduces moderate lattice distortion (dσ = 0.104 Å) and significantly flattens the 3D Li+ migration energy landscape, reducing the macroscopic diffusion barrier from 1.060 eV (pristine LLZO) to 0.777 eV. Consequently, HE-LLZO achieves a high ionic conductivity of 1.05 × 10−3 S cm−1, a low activation energy of 0.287 eV, and an expanded electrochemical window of 4.81 V. All-solid-state cells with Ta-doped NCM811 cathodes retain 92.5% capacity after 250 cycles, and flexible pouch cells (NCM90|SE|Li-alloy) deliver 200.1 mAh g−1 with 86% retention after 200 cycles, demonstrating practical viability. This work establishes a generalizable, AI-guided paradigm for accelerating the discovery of high-entropy solid electrolyte toward high-energy-density batteries.

title: Bowl-shaped conductive filler enabled low-modulus conductive ionic elastomer for conformal and efficient near-field electromagnetic shielding
abstract: Lightweight and conformable electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are highly desirable for wearable communication and embodied artificial intelligence. However, simultaneously achieving extremely high electrical conductivity and low modulus in conductive elastomers remains a significant challenge. Herein, a novel bowl-shaped silver-coated expanded polymer beads (Ag@EBs) incorporated polyvinyl alcohol/phytic acid (PVA/PhA) conductive ionic elastomer with silver/ion dual conductive network structure is fabricated for conformal and highly efficient near-field (NF) EMI shielding. The bowl-shaped Ag@EBs, featuring an open-ended architecture, enable dense in-plane stacking to form the primary conductive network and can readily deform with the soft PVA/PhA ionic elastomer matrix. Meanwhile, H⁺ ions released from the PhA moieties serve as a synergistic ionic conductive pathway, reducing the contact resistance between adjacent Ag@EBs and thereby stabilizing the conductive network. As a result, the prepared composite film exhibited a rather low modulus of only 299 kPa and an exceptional EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 92.6 dB at the thickness of only ~200 μm. Notably, the dual-conductive network also ensured the stable conductivity of the elastomer even under large deformation, with only a negligible decrease at a tensile strain of ~200%. Owing to its soft and robustly conductive characteristics, the film exhibits excellent conformability to complex surfaces and achieves a remarkable near-field EMI shielding effectiveness (NF-SE) of -53.28 dB, comparable to that of copper foil shields. Our work provides a new strategy for designing conformable EMI shielding materials which are highly promising for conferring reliable NF shielding to stretchable and wearable electronics

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy for designing all-organic polyimide dielectrics with deep traps and wide-temperature-range
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of high-power electronics demands polymer dielectrics with high thermal stability and dielectric performance. However, most materials suffer performance degradation in harsh environments due to increased electrical conductivity. Herein, a physics-informed data-driven topology-supported precursor screening strategy was proposed to design quasi-branched polyimides (QbPIs) with enhanced energy density (Ue) and charge-discharge efficiency (η) at elevated temperatures. By constructing automated screening workflow, key descriptors involving HOMO-LUMO gap (Gap) and dielectric constant (εr) were sufficiently evaluated to form multi-parameter ranking framework, in which melamine was identified as the optimal topological center for constructing QbPIs with tunable topological ratios (0–2.5%). Notably, the resulting star-shaped topological structure effectively regulates charge transport and dielectric behavior through a cooperative mechanism. It increases the Gap, introduces deep-level traps, and stabilizes the Ag/dielectric interface, which together suppress conduction loss and charge injection, effectively disrupting long-range charge-transport pathways. The optimized QbPI-1.75 exhibited outstanding capacitive performance, delivering 5.39 J cm−3 (Ue) with 94% (η) at 25 °C, and retaining 3.29 J cm−3 with 78.41% at 200 °C, far exceeding that of pure PI (1.35 J cm−3, 87.6% η at 25 °C). This work establishes a fundamental structure-property relationship for topological PIs and provides a facile design strategy applicable to other high-temperature polymer dielectrics.

verified_metadata.title: Explainable reinforcement learning designs a LRP1-targeted BBB-penetrating peptide with spatial selectivity for glioblastoma therapy
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a formidable challenge. While peptide-mediated transcytosis is promising, the rational de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides lacks systematic principles. Here, we developed a novel multi-receptor, explainable, and uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning framework that integrates multi-task affinity prediction with physicochemical constraints for the de novo design of BBB-penetrating peptides. By integrating multivalent transcytosis datasets and physicochemical constraints, our model generates highly feasible, BBB-permeable candidates. Experimental validation of a representative generated peptide, 1 L, demonstrated that it drives robust nanoparticle transcytosis without compromising vascular integrity. Mechanistically, 1 L specifically targets the LRP1 receptor, orchestrating active endothelial endocytosis and vesicular trafficking. In vivo, 1 L-conjugated nanoparticles achieved profound brain parenchymal accumulation with a unique spatial selectivity—enriching in the cortex and striatum while bypassing limbic septal nuclei, thereby offering a potential “spatial selectivity pattern”, outperforming several established LRP1-targeted systems in brain parenchymal delivery. Systemic administration of 1 L-nanotherapeutics significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged survival in an orthotopic glioblastoma model without systemic toxicity. This AI-driven paradigm provides a powerful, generalizable strategy for designing precision neurotherapeutics.

title: Integrating machine learning and CFD-derived hydrodynamics for predictive scale-up of combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization
abstract: Scale-up of crystallization processes remains a major challenge due to the complex interplay between operating conditions, hydrodynamics, and particle-level phenomena. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting product particle size distributions (PSD) in a combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization process across laboratory and pilot scales. Partial least squares (PLS) regression models with bootstrapping-based uncertainty quantification were constructed using three categories of input variables: (i) operating conditions alone, (ii) operating conditions with empirical hydrodynamic descriptors, and (iii) operating conditions with both empirical and CFD-derived hydrodynamic descriptors. At small scales (400 mL, 500 mL, and 3 L), both (ii) and (iii) improved predictive accuracy relative to (i), with consistent performance across train–test splits. For extrapolation to mid-scale (5 L) and large-scale (100 L) crystallizers, only models including CFD-derived hydrodynamic features provided accurate predictions, demonstrating their critical role in scale-up. The variable importance scores of the PLS models revealed the key operational and hydrodynamic factors that influence PSD predictions across scales. The proposed framework offers a generalizable digital design tool aiding scale-up of crystallization processes, integrating mechanistic hydrodynamic insights with machine learning to enable predictive, data-efficient, and interpretable scale-up.

title: Electron beam and protease–induced modifications of ECM protein hydrogels: Collagen- and elastin-specific structural insights via fast green staining and fluorescence lifetime CLSM
abstract: Collagen–elastin hydrogels have gained increasing attention as versatile extracellular matrix-based biomaterials for tissue engineering, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine. Their tunable mechanical properties, inherent biocompatibility, and responsiveness to external cues make them ideal yet complex systems for biomedical applications. Recent studies have demonstrated that high-energy electron beam irradiation offers a reagent-free approach for crosslinking collagen-elastin hydrogels, enabling precise modulation of network density, mechanical behavior, and thermo-responsiveness under sterilizing conditions. To better understand and visualize the effects of electron beam treatment and enzymatic degradation on the microarchitecture of these hybrid materials we employed fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy combined with Fast Green staining. This technique enabled the simultaneous differentiation of collagen and elastin subnetworks at the fibrillar level and facilitated the investigation of the behavior of individual protein components during radiation-chemical processing, enzymatic degradation, and combinations thereof. Electron beam treated and untreated gels were exposed to selective enzymatic degradation using trypsin and elastase, providing insights into the proteolytic stability of the individual matrix components. Lifetime based imaging revealed significant differences in collagen and elastin susceptibility to enzymatic cleavage following electron beam treatment. To support the analysis, machine learning-based segmentation was applied, with a primary focus on voxel-wise classification using the 3D pixel classifier in AIVIA, allowing for a volumetric and spatially resolved characterization of the datasets. The findings highlight the potential of fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis for characterization of extracellular matrix-mimetic biomaterials and their dynamic remodeling behavior, with implications for optimizing scaffold design in bioengineering applications.

title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR biosensors: From rational design to AI acceleration

ai4s_review.rationale: 实质综述机器学习、蛋白语言模型及视觉模型对gRNA、Cas蛋白和CRISPR生物传感器设计的贡献。

verified_metadata.title: Molecular engineering of CRISPR biosensors: From rational design to AI acceleration
verified_metadata.abstract: The CRISPR/Cas system integrates programmable target recognition with diverse catalytic activities and versatile signal transduction mechanisms, rendering it a powerful platform for molecular detection. The performance of CRISPR/Cas-based sensors is largely determined by the properties of their core molecular components, including guide RNAs (gRNAs), Cas proteins, and signal output elements. Therefore, molecular engineering of these components represents a critical strategy for enhancing target recognition, catalytic efficiency, detection sensitivity, specificity, and overall signal fidelity. Such engineering primarily relies on rational design to regulate sensing performance, including (i) gRNA sequence and structure optimization; (ii) Cas protein engineering via site-specific mutations or functional domain fusions; and (iii) modification of signal probes. These strategies collectively enable the rational design of CRISPR/Cas sensors with tailored performance for diverse applications. With the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and deep learning have expanded the capabilities for designing and analyzing CRISPR/Cas components. Protein language models and computer vision further support the prediction of gRNA activity and off-target effects, the discovery and functional optimization of Cas proteins, and the intelligent analysis of detection signals. These approaches enable more efficient and accurate CRISPR/Cas system development. This paper systematically reviews molecular engineering strategies for CRISPR/Cas sensing elements at three levels: gRNAs, Cas proteins, and signal output. We discuss how rational and AI-assisted approaches leverage sequence, structural, molecular interaction, and experimental data to optimize sensing performance. AI-assisted methods are further highlighted for their potential to reduce screening costs, narrow the design space, and improve engineering efficiency. In closing, we highlight the key challenges and outline future perspectives for realizing CRISPR sensing platforms that combine high sensitivity, specificity, robustness, and broad adaptability.

ai4s_review.rationale: 随机森林和XGBoost分别识别气体组成及定量浓度，支持MOF氧化锌铟双气体传感器。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning assisted identification of MOF-derived ZnO/In dual gas sensor activated by blue light at near room temperature
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient discrimination of multiple volatile organic compounds using a single metal-oxide semiconductor sensor at near room temperature remains challenging. Herein, MOF-derived In-doped ZnO engineered with abundant defects and porous structure exhibits superior dual-gas sensing performance under blue-light activation at near room temperature, making it particularly well-suited for machine-learning-driven gas identification. Among the In-doped samples, comprehensive SEM, TEM, and BET analyses, together with XPS, PL, EPR, EIS, and transient photocurrent measurements, demonstrated that ZnO/In-0.1 achieved the optimal balance among surface area, oxygen vacancy (Ov), and photogenerated carrier transfer. Under 450 nm irradiation at approximately 60 °C, it delivered Δresponses of 527 and 509 to 10 ppm triethylamine (TEA) and N-butanol, respectively, with response times of 57 and 80 s and theoretical detection limits of 6.72 and 5.53 ppb, while exhibiting negligible responses in the dark. RandomForest achieved 97.8% held-out classification accuracy for gas-composition classes, while XGBoost predicted the concentrations of both gases with an overall R2 of 0.956. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations showed that In incorporation lowered the Ov formation energy, introduced defect and band-tail states, and strengthened the adsorption of TEA (−1.8253 eV) and N-butanol (−1.1814 eV). The enhanced sensing performance arises from composition-structure-function coupling among optimized In loading, defect-rich porous structure, sub-bandgap carrier activation, and preferential target-gas adsorption, providing a strategy for intelligent visible light activated dual-gas sensing.

title: Interfacial polarity regulation enables robust self-healing conductive elastomers for wearable motion recognition
abstract: Flexible strain sensors must withstand repeated deformation while preserving mechanical integrity, autonomous repairability, and stable signal transduction. Conductive polymer composites, however, often suffer from filler aggregation and fragile conductive networks, making it difficult to reconcile strength, self-healing capability, and sensing reliability. Here, we report an interfacial polarity regulation strategy to construct a self-healing conductive elastomer composed of furan-functionalized carbon nanotubes and Diels–Alder-crosslinked epoxidized natural rubber (ECNT). Molecular simulations, together with spectroscopic and morphological analyses, reveal that the furan-regulated interface generates localized polar domains and accessible interaction sites, thereby promoting nanotube dispersion and interfacial coupling within the elastomer matrix. The optimized ECNT-2 composite achieves a tensile strength of 7.74 MPa, an elongation at break of 467%, and a self-healing efficiency above 90% after thermal treatment. Enabled by dynamic conductive-network reconstruction and reversible covalent crosslinking, the elastomer sensor delivers a gauge factor of 3.76, response/recovery times below 180/140 ms, and stable piezoresistive signals under cyclic deformation. It reliably monitors large joint motions and subtle physiological activities, including finger bending, elbow flexion, coughing, and smiling. Coupled with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, the sensor achieves window-level validation accuracies of 100% for representative motions and 98.7% for finger gestures, supporting robotic-hand teleoperation. This work links molecular-level polarity engineering with intelligent wearable sensing, offering a rational route to robust self-healing conductive elastomers for adaptive human-machine interfaces.

verified_metadata.title: The cathode–electrolyte interphase meets artificial intelligence: From formation and evolution mechanisms to data-driven interphase design
verified_metadata.abstract: The commercialization of high-energy, high-voltage lithium-ion and next-generation batteries hinges on how precisely the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) can be understood and controlled. Far from being a static boundary, the CEI is a dynamic, compositionally heterogeneous reaction zone in which oxidative decomposition products of the electrolyte accumulate, rearrange, and continuously evolve with cycling. This review (i) establishes the fundamentals of CEI formation, structure, and growth kinetics; (ii) surveys interphase behavior across cathode families—Ni-rich NCM/NMC, high-voltage spinels, Li-rich oxides, sodium/zinc/dual-ion systems, and solid-state cells; (iii) organizes stabilization strategies spanning electrolyte additives, solvation engineering, surface coating and doping, artificial CEIs, and dry-electrode processing; and (iv) compares advanced characterization tools including cryo-EM, in situ TEM, XPS/ToF-SIMS, and EIS/DRT. The review also examines AI and machine-learning approaches relevant to CEI research, including machine-learning interatomic potentials, physics-informed learning, electrolyte and additive screening, multiscale imaging and computational analysis, and battery-level diagnostics. We close by presenting an integrated experiment–simulation–AI framework for data-driven interphase analysis and design.

title: Machine learning strategies integrating knowledge transfer and a cascaded framework: Guiding the discovery of NIR-II organic cocrystals
abstract: Organic cocrystals represent a highly promising class of photothermal materials operating in the near-infrared second (NIR-II) window. However, efficient identification and rational design remain challenging due to the vast chemical space and the complex, nontrivial relationships between molecular structures and functional properties. In this work, we develop a cascaded dual-task (C2T) machine learning (ML) framework that effectively links cocrystal-formability recognition (M1) with NIR-II absorption identification (M2) through feature knowledge transfer. We constructed the first hierarchical organic cocrystal database, comprising 2,648 cocrystal samples and 128 NIR-II cocrystals. By integrating RDKit and PaDEL descriptors to generate dual-representation molecular features, a dual-task prediction model is established. Under small-sample conditions, both M1 and M2 achieve high predictive accuracies (>92%) and demonstrate strong generalization capabilities. Guided by the model, we discover and experimentally validate the DPQ cocrystals, which exhibits intense NIR-II absorption (up to 1200 nm) and efficient photothermal behavior (~120℃@1024 nm). Moreover, multiscale theoretical calculations combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based model interpretability elucidate the structure-property relationships from molecular architecture to macroscopic performance. This work demonstrates the potential of ML for precise cocrystal design and efficient performance identification under small-sample conditions, paving the way for ML-accelerated development of functional molecular materials.

verified_metadata.abstract: Organic cocrystals represent a highly promising class of photothermal materials operating in the near-infrared second (NIR-II) window. However, efficient identification and rational design remain challenging due to the vast chemical space and the complex, nontrivial relationships between molecular structures and functional properties. In this work, we develop a cascaded dual-task (C2T) machine learning (ML) framework that effectively links cocrystal-formability recognition (M1) with NIR-II absorption identification (M2) through feature knowledge transfer. We constructed the first hierarchical organic cocrystal database, comprising 2,648 cocrystal samples and 128 NIR-II cocrystals. By integrating RDKit and PaDEL descriptors to generate dual-representation molecular features, a dual-task prediction model is established. Under small-sample conditions, both M1 and M2 achieve high predictive accuracies (>92%) and demonstrate strong generalization capabilities. Guided by the model, we discover and experimentally validate the DPQ cocrystals, which exhibits intense NIR-II absorption (up to 1200 nm) and efficient photothermal behavior (~120℃@1024 nm). Moreover, multiscale theoretical calculations combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based model interpretability elucidate the structure-property relationships from molecular architecture to macroscopic performance. This work demonstrates the potential of ML for precise cocrystal design and efficient performance identification under small-sample conditions, paving the way for ML-accelerated development of functional molecular materials.

verified_metadata.title: Vacancy–metal–site coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts for CO2-to-CO reduction: DFT screening assisted by multimodal transfer learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Defective oxide supports provide reactive vacancy sites for CO2 activation, but strong initial activation alone does not guarantee favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics because downstream intermediate stabilization must also be optimized. Here, vacancy–metal–site (VMS) coupling in defective MgO-supported single-atom catalysts is systematically investigated by integrating density functional theory (DFT), descriptor-guided screening, multimodal transfer learning, and computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) analysis. The target-domain MgO-Ov-TM space, where Ov denotes a surface oxygen vacancy and TM denotes a transition-metal single atom, contains 120 configurations constructed from 20 3d/4d transition-metal dopants and six representative adsorption environments. DFT calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies promote CO2 bending and charge redistribution, whereas favorable CO2-to-CO thermodynamics require coordinated regulation of *COOH formation and *CO stabilization by metal identity and local adsorption environments. To enrich promising candidates, a Vacancy–Metal–Site Multimodal Transfer Learning (VMS-MTL) framework was adapted from graph–text transfer-learning strategies by integrating geometry-aware graph embeddings pretrained on the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset with structured chemical-text representations. VMS-MTL achieved mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.219 eV for Eads of CO and 0.363 eV for |d-band center|, recovering eight of nine DFT-screened candidates within the top-15 out-of-fold (OOF) rankings. Subsequent CHE analysis identified Sc-T-Mg_Def, corresponding to a Sc atom coupled with the defect-neighboring Mg top site, as the most thermodynamically favorable configuration within the investigated MgO-Ov-TM space, with a limiting free-energy change (ΔGmax) of 0.316 eV. Further analysis shows that strong initial CO2 activation is not directly correlated with thermodynamic favorability, revealing a system-specific Sabatier-type trade-off. These findings establish VMS coupling as a framework linking vacancy-assisted activation with metal/site-regulated intermediate stabilization, while multimodal transfer learning enables data-efficient candidate enrichment before detailed DFT/CHE analysis.

title: Redox-active coordination catalysts for selective thermochemical valorization of biowaste: Mechanistic insights and structure-performance relationships
abstract: The growing demand for renewable energy has intensified global efforts to transform biowastes into value-added fuels and chemicals rather than viewing them as disposal challenges. Derived mainly from lignocellulosic and other organic residues, these wastes are rich in carbon and reactive functional groups, making them promising feedstocks for thermochemical conversion via pyrolysis, gasification, and hydrothermal liquefaction. Yet, their compositional complexity, high oxygen content, and inorganic impurities remain major barriers to efficient transformation and catalyst durability. This review offers an integrated perspective on recent advances in the catalytic valorization of biowaste, with a particular emphasis on how coordination chemistry principles can enhance reaction selectivity and energy efficiency. Redox-active metal complexes, zeolites, and metal-organic frameworks are highlighted for their ability to mediate controlled bond activation and electron transfer during reforming and aromatization processes. By linking feedstock chemistry, pretreatment strategies, and catalytic mechanisms, this work establishes structure-activity-selectivity relationships that underpin syngas and aromatic production. Finally, emerging concepts such as AI-guided catalyst design, integration with circular bioeconomy frameworks, and dual-function redox systems, are discussed as promising pathways toward scalable, low-carbon, and sustainable energy technologies.

title: Machine learning-guided design of glycosaminoglycans composite fiber scaffolds for neuro-osteogenic regeneration
abstract: Repairing large bone defects caused by trauma or disease poses a significant clinical challenge. Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major components of organic matrix, play a crucial role in osteogenesis. Here, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided strategy for enhancing the design of osteogenic multicomponent GAGs. First, we constructed a dataset of 169/173 data for cell differentiation and viability of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) cultured on different GAGs formulations to build an optimal formulation screening model through random forest (RF) and XGBoost (XGB) algorithms. We efficiently screened 59 good GAGs from 10,000 formulations generated in the whole space that own maximized cell differentiation and viability through the model. Based on cell mineralization activity, secondary screening identified 3 optimal formulations (GAG3–5). Based on these formulations, optimal formulation GAGs adsorbed into magnesium doped amino modified mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) as the core, nerve growth factor (NGF) adsorbed into silk fibroin (SF) as the shell to form a composite fiber MBG/GAG@SF/NGF scaffold through coaxial electrospinning. Interestingly, we observed that MBG/GAG3,5@SF/NGF scaffolds promoted the osteogenesis process by activating the Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (Bmp2)/Smad and p-Erk1/2 signaling pathways in vitro . Furthermore, we found that MBG/GAG3,5@SF/NGF scaffolds enhanced the neurogenesis process in vitro . Intriguingly, we also observed that MBG/GAG5@SF/NGF scaffold effectively guided functional bone regeneration accompanied with enhanced neurogenesis and angiogenesis in mouse cranial defect model in vivo . This study not only provides an efficient MBG/GAG5@SF/NGF composite fiber multifunctional scaffold for bone defect repair but also establishes a scalable paradigm for ML-guided screening of bioactive formulations.

title: AI-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics simulation for polymer cross-linking
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulation based on reactive forcefield enables atomic-scale investigation of polymer cross-linking processes but is limited by high computational cost. In polymer cross-linking simulations, a large fraction of simulation time is spent in chemically inactive stages, during which the continuous use of a reactive forcefield is inefficient. In this work, an artificial intelligence-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics framework is developed, which adaptively switches between reactive and non-reactive forcefields to improve computational efficiency while maintaining chemical accuracy. A machine learning model is trained on reactive molecular dynamics trajectories to predict continuous reaction probability using physically interpretable structural, chemical, and energetic descriptors extracted from simulation outputs. This probabilistic criterion enables reliable identification of low-reactivity states and stable forcefield switching without manually defined heuristic rules. The proposed approach is applied to the cross-linking process of epoxy as a representative example. Compared with full reactive forcefield simulations, the hybrid approach achieves up to 80% reduction in computational cost. Structural and mechanical properties of the cross-linked epoxy network obtained from the hybrid simulations show excellent agreement with full reactive forcefield results and experimental reference data. This work provides a framework that accelerates polymer cross-linking simulations while preserving key reaction chemistry, network evolution, and final material properties. Using epoxy-amine cross-linking as a representative case, the study establishes a proof-of-concept strategy for coupling chemically faithful reactive sampling with efficient nonreactive relaxation. The framework may be extended to other reaction-relaxation systems after system-specific descriptor construction, threshold calibration, and independent validation.

verified_metadata.title: AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery in chemistry and chemical engineering: A methodological and bibliometric review
verified_metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing molecular and materials discovery by linking chemical data with predictive modeling, inverse design, reaction planning, experimental optimization, and increasingly integrated laboratory workflows. This review critically examines AI-assisted molecular and materials discovery from methodological, bibliometric, application-oriented, and chemical engineering perspectives. We first outline the core workflow for reliable chemical machine learning, covering data acquisition and curation, chemical representation, model construction, and evaluation, with particular attention to data regimes, generalization, uncertainty, applicability domains, interpretability, and experimental validation. A bibliometric analysis of Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved from 1 January 2016 to 10 April 2026, with 2026 treated as partial-year coverage, contextualizes the evolution and interconnection of major research themes. Four application directions are examined: property prediction and virtual screening; reaction planning, reaction engineering, and process optimization; generative inverse design; and large language model (LLM)-enabled multimodal and increasingly automated workflows. Across these directions, we compare method suitability and validation strength and distinguish computational prediction and generation from prospective experimental validation, closed-loop optimization, and autonomous experimentation. Translation to chemical engineering practice is evaluated in terms of reactor and operating constraints, transport phenomena, scale-up, process control, process safety, and techno-economic feasibility. Finally, challenges are organized into four categories: data, representation, model, and deployment, with emphasis on representative datasets, chemically and physically constrained representations, realistic validation, uncertainty-aware decisions, and tighter integration of computation, experiment, and process engineering.

title: Physics-informed neural network reconstructions of free surfaces and flow fields from sparse data in turbulent regimes, with applications in stirred tanks
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless framework for fluid dynamics, capable of solving both forward and inverse problems, and incorporating observational data into the model. However, their application to coupled multiphase turbulent flows remains limited, particularly in industrial inverse problems, where measurements may be sparse, expensive, and are often devoid of turbulence values. In this work, we develop a PINN framework for reconstructing the free surface, along with the velocity and pressure fields from sparse data, and test it on a mixing tank. Models are trained on limited velocity and pressure data from a time-averaged, axisymmetric CFD reference simulation. The data are free of direct measurements from the free surface or turbulence terms. Models are evaluated across varying impeller speeds and fluid viscosities. Both laminar and turbulent models are tested, including with eddy viscosity closures and anisotropic stresses. A Spalart–Allmaras turbulence closure is used, while including anisotropic stresses can improve the pressure and free surface predictions. From as few as 25 measurement locations, models are able to reconstruct, with low error, the velocity and pressure fields, and the final model achieves average free-surface errors below 1 mm in all tested operating conditions relative to a CFD reference. Additionally, models can accurately detect features such as additional vortices, jet splitting and impingement regions.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-informed LSTM for lignocellulosic pyrolysis kinetics at elevated heating rates: Integrating Arrhenius constraints with data-driven modeling
verified_metadata.abstract: Reliable prediction of lignocellulosic intermediate pyrolysis kinetics is critical for scaling up thermochemical conversion processes, yet remains challenging at high heating rates. We developed a physics-informed long short-term memory network (PINN-LSTM) integrating particle swarm optimization (PSO) with recurrent neural networks, trained on only 13 thermogravimetric/derivative thermogravimetric (TG/DTG) curves from pure components, blends, and real straws. PSO inversely determines apparent phenomenological kinetic triplets (E, A, n), embedded as Arrhenius-based soft constraints in the LSTM loss function, enforcing physical feasibility without compromising flexibility. On the three held-out straws PINN-LSTM attains RMSE values of 0.80, 0.78 and 0.80 wt%·min−1, corresponding to a 43% reduction in mean RMSE relative to the vanilla LSTM and approximately 76% relative to HRF, the strongest tree ensemble; each comparison is stated against a single named baseline rather than as a combined range. The model accurately captures shoulder-peak transitions and high-temperature tails, with peak-temperature errors below 1 K. The E-lnA relationship observed is that expected under single-heating-rate inversion and is reported as an apparent, jointly determined descriptor rather than as an independently established physical law. A web-based interface enables real-time parameter estimation (E=228 kJ·mol−1, lnA=42.1 s−1, n=2.31) with automated visualization, facilitating industrial adoption. This synergy between data-driven learning and physics-based constraints demonstrates broader applicability to thermochemical systems with mechanistic priors and data scarcity.

title: AI-assisted design of metal-organic frameworks for hydrogen storage: From databases to generative models
abstract: Nowadays, the development of a sustainable hydrogen economy and the widespread deployment of high-capacity hydrogen storage for hydrogen vehicles and energy systems are of great importance. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their diverse structures, have emerged as the most promising materials for next-generation gas storage due to their high surface area, tunable pore size, and diversity of chemical bonds. However, the fabrication of MOF materials through manual experimental screening is very time-consuming and costly. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms, combined with quantum databases, advanced modeling, and screening strategies for discovering MOF structures, have revolutionized materials science. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in AI-assisted discovery of novel MOF materials specifically for hydrogen storage applications. We present MOF databases, modeling strategies based on material structure descriptors and materials discovery, large language model (LLM) algorithms for automated data mining, and ML-assisted force fields (FFs) at the atomic level for hydrogen storage. Furthermore, we discuss key challenges such as data quality, model transferability, and discrepancies between simulations and experiments. Finally, this review paper outlines future prospects for this rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field, with an emphasis on advancing MOF materials discovery through accurate AI models.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven glycosaminoglycan-mimetic polymer design for cartilage regeneration

ai4s_review.rationale: 机器学习整合文献和天然软骨基质信息，指导糖胺聚糖模拟聚合物支架设计及软骨再生。

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-driven glycosaminoglycan-mimetic polymer design for cartilage regeneration
verified_metadata.abstract: Clinical cartilage repair remains limited by fibrocartilage formation rather than hyaline-like cartilage repair after microfracture. Engineering an instructive extracellular matrix (ECM)-mimetic microenvironment is therefore essential for directing the fate of endogenous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Here, we introduced a data-driven strategy integrating literature-derived machine learning with native cartilage matrix analysis to guide scaffold design for cartilage regeneration. Guided by this framework, a chondrocyte-mimetic polymer scaffold (HRC) was constructed using recombinant human type II collagen (rhCol II), type I collagen (Col I), and thiolated hyaluronic acid (HA-SH). Within the scaffold, Col I self-assembled into a strong fibrous framework that provided structural support, while rhCol II participated in the intermolecular organization of the composite matrix. In vitro, HRC enhanced BMSC migration and chondrogenic differentiation. Furthermore, HRC promoted regeneration of a smooth articular surface with an ordered matrix architecture and abundant proteoglycan deposition in cartilage defect models. RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of PI3K–Akt-related signaling, while PI3K inhibition supported its involvement in the in vitro chondrogenic response. Taken together, these findings support the relevance of tissue-specific matrix design for cartilage repair. Overall, the machine learning (ML) strategy used in this study can extend to other tissues constituting with collagen such as the meniscus.

title: Deciphering the water-thermal stability trade-offs via interpretable machine learning for reliable design of dual-stable MOFs

verified_metadata.title: Deciphering the water-thermal stability trade-offs via interpretable machine learning for reliable design of dual-stable MOFs
verified_metadata.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold immense promise for industrial adsorption and catalysis. However, practical deployment is often hindered by insufficient simultaneous water and thermal stability under harsh hygrothermal conditions. Furthermore, the mechanistic differences and potential trade-offs underlying water and thermal stability remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish an interpretable machine-learning framework integrating molecular descriptors and synthetic parameters to decode the mechanisms governing dual stability. Subsequent feature attribution analyses quantitatively reveal the asymmetric regulation underlying dual-stability. Thermal stability is synergistically determined by multidimensional parameters, including nuclearity and synthesis conditions. In contrast, the water-stability model shows a pronounced association with elemental electronegativity, with additional variation associated with structural descriptors within the sampled chemical space. Notably, increasing certain features (e.g., ligand-to-metal ratio > 1, topological polar surface area (TPSA) > 150 Å) enhances water stability at the expense of thermal stability, exposing pronounced trade-offs. Guided by these insights, we delineate a quantitative design space for dual-stability (e.g., metal electronegativity < 1.8, TPSA < 150 Å, 0.3 < ligand-to-metal ratio < 1.1). Targeted synthesis and characterization of representative MOFs confirm that materials within these parameters reliably achieve superior stability. These findings establish quantitative design rules for overcoming stability trade-offs and enabling the rational engineering of robust MOFs, accelerating industrial application under complex hygrothermal conditions.

title: Ultrasound-enhanced goethite coprecipitation for synergistic enrichment of Ga, Ge and In: A combined molecular dynamics, artificial neural network and EXAFS study

ai4s_review.rationale: ANN-GA优化超声针铁矿共沉淀回收镓锗铟工艺，并结合EXAFS与分子动力学验证机制。

verified_metadata.title: Ultrasound-enhanced goethite coprecipitation for synergistic enrichment of Ga, Ge and In: A combined molecular dynamics, artificial neural network and EXAFS study
verified_metadata.abstract: Amid the global energy transition, digital infrastructure upgrading, and rapid growth of high-end manufacturing, the efficient recovery and high-value utilization of critical metals (Ga, Ge and In) have become important research priorities in resource recycling and strategic mineral security. To address the challenges of the dispersed distribution of Ga, Ge and In in zinc sulfate solution, and the low efficiency of their co-recovery. This study investigated the ultrasonic-enhanced goethite co-precipitation method for simultaneously pre-enriching Ga, Ge and In from a simulated acidic zinc sulfate solution. Based on these findings, an ANN-GA optimization model was developed to achieve precise optimization of multi-parameter coupling. The results indicated that ultrasonic enhancement can significantly improve the goethite formation process and the solid-liquid distribution behavior of Ga, Ge and In, enabling the efficient synergistic enrichment of three rare metals under optimized conditions (ωFe = 99.91%, ωGa = 99.81%, ωGe = 99.71%, ωIn = 99.70%). To elucidate ultrasound effects, conventional characterization techniques were combined with mineral liberation analysis (MLA), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS). The results show ultrasonic cavitation enhances mass transfer, oxidation, and hydrolysis, while modifying microstructure, crystal defects, and interfacial properties of the goethite coprecipitation residue. Ultrasonic treatment produces a more porous and defect-rich goethite coprecipitation residue with increased surface accessibility, thereby promoting the enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In. Molecular dynamics simulations (MD) further indicated element dependent spatial distributions of Ge(OH)4, Ga3+, and In3+ near the goethite/water interface. Overall, ultrasound enhanced goethite co-precipitation provided an effective process for the simultaneous pre-enrichment of Ga, Ge, and In from zinc sulfate solutions and provided a scientific basis for their subsequent selective separation and recovery.

title: Unveiling the atomic scale synthesis dynamics of lithium thiophosphate electrolytes via machine learning interatomic potentials

ai4s_review.rationale: CHGNet机器学习势能分子动力学重现实验合成轨迹，解释硫代磷酸锂电解质原子合成动力学。

verified_metadata.title: Unveiling the atomic scale synthesis dynamics of lithium thiophosphate electrolytes via machine learning interatomic potentials
verified_metadata.abstract: The rational design of inorganic materials is often hindered by the complexity of solid-state synthesis, which remains largely empirical and reliant on trial-and-error optimization. Bridging the gap between atomistic mechanisms and macroscopic processing, we present a fully reactive computational synthesis framework capable of predicting phase evolution directly from precursor materials. By leveraging machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) driven by the Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network (CHGNet) potential, we successfully reproduced the experimental synthesis trajectories of the Li2S-P2S5 solid electrolyte system. Our simulations captured the composition-dependent formation of local structural environments characteristic of Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li7PS6 phases from 70, 75, and 87.5 mol% Li2S precursors, respectively. Detailed structural analyses revealed the systematic cleavage of bridging sulfur bonds and the dominance of terminal PS43− tetrahedra with increasing Li content, closely mirroring experimental thiophosphate speciation. Although limited simulation timescales restricted full crystallization, the resulting structures exhibited high fidelity to experimentally reported glassy intermediates, as confirmed by structure factor calculations and SOAP-based similarity analysis. This work demonstrates the feasibility of a “virtual reactor” for exploring synthesis pathways, offering a safe and efficient strategy to accelerate the discovery of complex solid-state materials.

title: NanoChef: AI framework for simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions at autonomous laboratories
abstract: We present NanoChef , a deep learning-based framework for the simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions in autonomous laboratories. Unlike traditional AI models focused solely on continuous variables, NanoChef incorporates positional encoding and MatBERT embedding to represent reagent sequences as vectorized inputs, enabling joint modeling of sequential and continuous variables in nanoparticle (NP) synthesis. In virtual experiments, NanoChef consistently searched for the best-identified optimum across synthesis-order-sensitive landscapes in under 40 cycles. Despite the complexity of 17.5 billion candidate recipes driven by 24 possible sequences in a four-reagent system, this framework achieved an optimal recipe for Ag NP synthesis, characterized by a λ max of 513 nm and a 36% reduction in full width at half maximum within fewer than 350 experiments. This search efficiency was underscored by the reductant-last strategy, which consistently yielded optimal results across all permutations of two- to four-reagent systems. Additionally, NanoChef newly discovered an oxidant–last strategy that produces monodisperse NPs on average. By optimizing both continuous volume and the order of reagent addition, the framework redefines synthesis order as a tunable design variable and demonstrates how AI can accelerate autonomous chemistry while handling high-dimensional combinatorial challenges that exceed the capabilities of fixed-order methods.

title: Role of artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in pyrolytic liquefaction of biomass and waste polymers: From mechanistic insights to process automation

ai4s_review.rationale: 系统综述AI与可解释机器学习联结废生物质塑料轮胎热解机理、特征及工艺自动化。

verified_metadata.title: Role of artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in pyrolytic liquefaction of biomass and waste polymers: From mechanistic insights to process automation
verified_metadata.abstract: Continuous disposal of various organic wastes and polymers causes environmental and economic drawbacks. Pyrolysis converts scrap tyres, waste plastics, and biomass into bio-oil, syngas, and char, via co-processing. However, optimizing yield and quality across these heterogeneous feedstocks demands models that can navigate highly nonlinear, scale-dependent thermochemistry. This review uniquely couples artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for all three waste streams in a single mechanistic and automation-oriented framework. The present review documents the reaction kinetics of tires, plastics and biomass and maps these pathways directly to input features and explainable AI techniques. A comparative synthesis of reported R2, RMSE, and MAE data across various feedstocks in literature show that gradient-boosted tree ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM) outperform deep neural architectures on small pyrolysis datasets. For instance, a deep mixture of experts model collapsed under 10-fold cross validation on a 468-record dataset, underscoring that model complexity without adequate data is counterproductive. The challenges with AI/ML applications in pyrolysis are briefly outlined and mapped with possible recommendations. In addition, an autonomous robotic development platform was framed as a future scope of the present review.

title: Towards generalizable wet foamability predictions: A dimensional analysis approach incorporating dynamic surface tension and symbolic regression
abstract: This study presents a groundbreaking chemical engineering approach to modeling wet foam formation through mechanical mixing and gas-sparging processes. Situated at the intersection of physico-chemistry, dimensional analysis, chemical engineering, and predictive modeling, this work utilizes an extensive experimental dataset covering a broad spectrum of operating conditions.For each foaming process examined, a single dimensionless correlation – capable of accurately predicting foam heights – is derived, irrespective of surfactant type, provided that dynamic surface tension is explicitly accounted for. The findings emphasize the pivotal role of surfactant dynamics in macroscopic foaming behavior, demonstrating that the time-dependent evolution of surface tension must be incorporated into foaming process models. This study serves as a compelling example of how chemical engineering principles can bridge molecular-scale mechanisms (e.g., surfactant migration at bubble interfaces) with macroscopic physical variables (e.g., foam height) observed at the process scale.Beyond its immediate relevance to the foaming community, this work highlights the feasibility of integrating non-constant properties into dimensional analysis frameworks – a practice rarely applied in the chemical engineering field – while adhering to rigorous similarity theory principles. Most importantly, the study underscores a broader message for chemical engineers: modern semi-empirical correlations can achieve unprecedented robustness by synergistically combining dimensional analysis (retaining physical interpretability and scalability, unlike purely data-driven approaches) with AI-driven techniques.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-integrated wearable sensors for intelligent disease diagnosis and personalized healthcare
verified_metadata.abstract: Wearable sensors have emerged as a technology for advancing healthcare through non-invasive, continuous, and real-time monitoring of physiological signals. Despite progress, healthcare systems face challenges in prevention, screening, diagnosis, and management due to reliance on invasive procedures, intermittent measurements, bulky equipment, and interventions. Although wearable sensors can generate data and improve accessibility, their ability to provide clinical insights remains limited. Meanwhile, the complexity of wearable health data places demands on clinical interpretation. Machine learning (ML) offers an approach to uncover patterns from datasets and establish relationships between physiological signals and health outcomes. However, the integration of wearable sensors and ML into practice remains constrained by challenges of data quality, model robustness, interpretability, privacy, and regulatory compliance. In this review, we examine recent advances in wearable sensor-ML systems for healthcare applications. We first introduce the operating principles and classifications of wearable sensors alongside the concepts and methodologies of ML. Then we survey the application of wearable sensor-ML technologies across a wide range of diseases, highlighting representative studies and comparing the performance, advantages, and limitations of ML approaches in wearable healthcare scenarios. Furthermore, we discuss the technical, clinical, and ethical barriers to real-world implementation and summarize strategies to overcome these limitations. By integrating developments with an assessment of challenges, this review underscores the potential of wearable sensor-ML systems for enabling more accurate, continuous, and personalized healthcare. The perspectives provide a roadmap for future research and translation, accelerating the development of intelligent healthcare technologies and advancing the realization of predictive, preventive, personalized, and participatory (4P) medicine.

verified_metadata.title: From molecular discovery to system management: A mini-review on machine learning driving full-cycle optimization of aqueous flow batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: With the growing global demand for long-duration energy storage technologies, redox flow batteries (RFBs) have become a major research hotspot owing to their decoupled power and capacity and high safety. Nevertheless, challenges including slow screening of active materials, complex multi-physics field coupling and insufficient accuracy of system state monitoring hinder their large-scale commercialization. For aqueous systems in particular, inherent challenges throughout the entire lifecycle of research, development and operation remain, such as coupled pH-potential effects, solubility-potential trade-offs, aqueous solvation effects, as well as hydrolysis and polymerization side reactions. As an emerging data-driven technology, machine learning (ML) features powerful nonlinear fitting and cross-scale modeling capabilities, which are transforming the research paradigm of aqueous flow batteries at an unprecedented rate. This paper systematically reviews the state-of-the-art applications of machine learning across the full lifecycle of flow batteries. First, it summarizes data-driven strategies for property prediction and high-throughput screening of electrolyte molecules in terms of material design. Second, hardware optimization covers membrane design, electrode optimization, and flow-field simulation and topology optimization. Third, the applications of machine learning in state of charge and state of health estimation during system operation are elaborated. Furthermore, the great potential of machine learning in mapping and regulating the full-cycle operation of aqueous flow batteries is demonstrated in the development of surrogate models and digital twins. Finally, this paper concludes the overall research advances and highlights the key challenges facing the future development of intelligent research and innovation systems for aqueous flow batteries.

title: From molecular generation to process-relevant performance: AI-driven identification of novel working fluids
abstract: The search for working fluids that balance thermodynamic performance, safety, and environmental sustainability remains a pressing challenge for refrigeration and heat pump technologies. Here, we present a hybrid computational workflow combining deep generative learning with classical thermodynamic modelling to identify novel working fluid candidates. Using a graph-based diffusion model, we generate and screen molecules against a quantitative physicochemical profile derived from known working fluids. We characterise five selected candidates in depth through molecular dynamics simulations, the polar soft-SAFT equation of state, COSMO-RS calculations, and two neural network predictors for flammability and GWP. We find that the predicted thermophysical and transport properties of the candidates fall within the range of established hydrofluorocarbons. Benchmarking against R-245fa and R-134a identifies a new compound (3,3,3-trifluoro-2-methylpropene) as the most promising candidate for high-temperature heat pump applications, and confirms another (1,1,1,2,2-pentafluoropropane) as a viable refrigerant for vapour compression cycles. Our work establishes a scalable framework for the rational, data-driven discovery of next-generation working fluids.

title: Combining physics-informed machine learning and heterogeneous transfer learning for hydrodenitrogenation of co-processed feedstocks
abstract: Accurately predicting the nitrogen content of co-processed petroleum feedstocks after hydrotreatment is a common challenge in refining, exacerbated by the limited experimental data available for each new feedstock. Transfer learning addresses this scarcity by leveraging knowledge from a related, data-rich source. For the source, the hydrodenitrogenation (HDN) of fossil vacuum gas oil, a rich dataset and an accurate prior ordinary differential equation (ODE) are available; for the target, the HDN of co-processed vacuum gas oil and tire-pyrolysis oil, the ODE structure is unknown and an additional descriptor (the tire fraction) is present, making the problem heterogeneous. To recover this unknown ODE, we propose HTL-HyODE, a heterogeneous transfer learning hybrid ODE in which small neural networks encode its unknown components while the rest is kept explicit and transferred from the source. For comparison, we also develop physics-informed variants (HTL-PINNs) of data-driven heterogeneous transfer networks. On simulated data, HTL-HyODE reduces the test mean absolute error (MAE) by up to 52% relative to a no-transfer hybrid baseline at a training size of n t = 25 when the networks are correctly placed. On experimental data, the benefit with respect to the no-transfer hybrid baseline depends on the target size and on the retained structure: at n t = 15 the best-matched structure reduces the MAE by about 50%–57%, whereas at n t = 50 the data-driven and physics-informed networks overtake it, DHTLFT-PINNs reaching the lowest error. Embedding the kinetic structure explicitly is thus most effective when it is reliable and data are scarce, while network-based transfer becomes preferable as data accumulate; the learned hybrid components remain physically consistent in both regimes.

title: Engineering precision antimicrobials: AI-driven design of self-assembling non-natural peptide nanostructures

verified_metadata.title: Engineering precision antimicrobials: AI-driven design of self-assembling non-natural peptide nanostructures
verified_metadata.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has evolved from a clinical challenge into a system-level engineering problem that demands therapeutic platforms capable of retaining efficacy in protease-rich, heterogeneous, and dynamically evolving infection microenvironments. Conventional antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are limited by inadequate proteolytic stability and insufficient selectivity, while isolated advances in AI-driven sequence design, non-natural peptide chemistry, and supramolecular self-assembly have yet to be integrated into a coherent engineering framework. This review presents an integrative perspective on the co-design of molecular composition, supramolecular organization, and computational prediction for self-assembling non-natural peptide antimicrobial nanostructures. We survey chemistry-aware graph encoders, conditional generative models, and multi-task phenotype predictors, and critically assess the evidence for their applicability to peptoid, halogenated, and stapled scaffolds. On the materials side, we analyze stimulus-responsive shape transformation for biofilm eradication, self-assembling hydrogels for infected wound repair, and supramolecular shielding as a safety-by-design strategy. The review makes four engineering contributions: (i) an AI-ready minimum characterization data set spanning six interoperable domains; (ii) a critical analysis of four major AMP clinical failures (pexiganan, omiganan, iseganan, brilacidin) with translatable lessons; (iii) a manufacturability framework linking continuous-flow SPPS to closed-loop design; and (iv) a maturity-tiered assessment of what AI-guided peptide design can and cannot yet deliver. We argue that the field is mature enough to generate chemically-expanded libraries and integrate manufacturability constraints, but not yet ready to replace in vivo validation with in silico surrogates.

title: Fast parameter identification for elementary-step surface mechanisms using kinetically parameterized neural networks
abstract: Microkinetic models provide physically grounded descriptions of catalytic systems. However, quantitative prediction of catalyst performance requires refinement of elementary-step parameters against reactor-level measurement data. This calibration is computationally demanding because it involves repeated reactor simulations with computationally expensive microkinetic models. Surrogates that approximate the kinetic model reduce evaluation cost, but are currently tied to fixed kinetic parameters and therefore cannot be used for mechanism calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce kinetically parameterized Global Reaction Neural Network (pGRNN) surrogates that map both operating conditions and elementary-step kinetic parameters of a detailed microkinetic mechanism to species source terms. By embedding stoichiometry, thermodynamic consistency, and elementary-step structure, the surrogate replaces expensive kinetics evaluations while retaining a mechanism-consistent representation. Using the preferential CO oxidation on platinum, we show that the pGRNN predicts source terms across a broad range of operating conditions and kinetic parameters with a relative error of 1.2%. Reactor model evaluation is accelerated by a factor of 3100. The pGRNN is used in place of the kinetic model during mechanism calibration, reducing calibration time by factors of approximately 2400 for a synthetic single light-off curve and a synthetic multi-experiment campaign. Finally, we demonstrate the workflow by efficiently calibrating the mechanism against measured reactor-performance data from two experimental setups. A differentiable implementation of kinetic and reactor model further enables efficient gradient-based calibration. The proposed workflow provides an accelerated route for adapting detailed microkinetic models to catalyst-specific performance data.

title: CatRetriever: Contrastive representation learning for slab-to-bulk retrieval in generative catalyst discovery

verified_metadata.title: CatRetriever: Contrastive representation learning for slab-to-bulk retrieval in generative catalyst discovery
verified_metadata.abstract: Inverse design is an emerging data-driven paradigm for efficiently navigating vast chemical spaces to discover new materials with targeted properties, and in the context of heterogeneous catalysis, surface generative models have recently advanced this goal by directly generating catalyst surface-adsorbate structures. However, these models typically operate at the slab level and do not provide the corresponding parent bulk structure, making it difficult to assess bulk-dependent properties such as formation energy, surface energy, crystallographic symmetry, and synthesizability. Here, we address this missing slab-to-bulk connection as a retrieval problem and introduce CatRetriever, a contrastive representation learning model that aligns slab and bulk crystal representations in a shared latent space. From a slab query, CatRetriever accurately retrieves plausible parent bulk candidates with R@1 > 91% and R@3 > 98%. We further extend the CatRetriever framework into an adsorption energy-guided candidate screening pipeline that combines bulk retrieval, generative search space expansion, and adsorption energy distribution analysis. This workflow evaluates candidates by both structural compatibility with the query slab and their ability to access the target adsorption energy range across diverse surface environments. CatRetriever therefore provides a scalable route for connecting catalyst generative models with physically plausible and adsorption energy compatible bulk catalyst discovery.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted development of high-performance Cr-doped tungsten oxide triethylamine gas sensors
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate detection of triethylamine (TEA) is essential for environmental and industrial safety. However, conventional metal oxide semiconductor sensors exhibit insufficient sensitivity and selectivity. This study develops an intelligent TEA sensor based on Cr-doped WO3 nanomaterials integrated with machine learning. The 1 wt% Cr-WO3 sensor exhibited optimal performance, with a response of 330.1 to 50 ppm TEA at 240 °C (4.78 times higher than pristine WO3), rapid response/recovery times (11 s/44 s), and a low detection limit of 42 ppb. The sensor also demonstrated excellent selectivity, repeatability, and stability, attributed to Cr-induced surface oxygen vacancies that enhance gas interactions. Based on machine learning, we established a gas recognition model using the KNN algorithm and a concentration prediction model using the neural network algorithm. This work integrates material optimization and intelligent algorithms to establish a “high-sensitivity detection-smart analysis” framework, thereby advancing gas sensors toward systematic intelligence for next-generation monitoring systems.

verified_metadata.title: AI-driven SERS biosensing chip for digital biomarker detection in diagnosis and monitoring of early-stage HCC
verified_metadata.abstract: For complex diseases, sensing and decoding patterns in biofluids are crucial for accurate diagnosis. However, it has been challenged by suboptimal sensitivity and inadequate information processing for accessing measurable outcomes. To address this gap, we present an intelligent diagnostic sensor platform that synergistically integrates fabrication-compatible silicon-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) biosensing chips with a self-learning explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework by enabling digital biomarker-based diagnosis of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The SERS biosensing chip, named SEARCH (Silicon-Etched Au-Reduced silver electro-Chemical deposition Heuristic), exploit hierarchical noble metal nanoarchitectures with dense electromagnetic hot spots, high enhancement of Raman signals, and superior inter-batch consistency, enabling sensitive detection of vibrational molecular fingerprints in serum. To interpret the high-dimensional Raman spectra, we developed a self-learning convolutional neural network (CNN)-based XAI framework that autonomously identifies and refines class-specific digital biomarkers, allowing it to dynamically adapt to population heterogeneity via iterative learning and unveil multidimensional spectral signatures encoded in serum-derived Raman spectra. In a multi-population cohort (N = 300), our platform demonstrated exceptional diagnostic performance, consistently achieving area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.93 across multiple classifiers in distinguishing early-stage HCC from both healthy controls and high-risk individuals. Comparative analysis revealed that SEARCH-derived digital biomarkers outperformed three conventional HCC serum markers. This work underscores the translational potential of combining scalable SERS biosensing with intelligent spectral analysis for digital cancer biomarker learning. The platform offers a robust, cost-efficient (<1.4 USD per test), and clinically actionable solution for the early diagnosis of HCC, showcasing the future of intelligent biosensing in precision oncology.
