verified_metadata.title: Electrochemically enhanced anaerobic ammonia oxidation: Performance prediction and mechanism elucidation based on big data and machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Anaerobic ammonia oxidation (anammox) is a promising energy-efficient biological nitrogen removal technology, but its widespread application is constrained by slow bacterial growth, prolonged startup periods, and strict dependency on nitrite. This study systematically investigated the enhancement effects of applied voltage on biofilm-based anammox systems using big data analysis and machine learning (ML) approaches. Over 800 sets of literature data were collected and analyzed, revealing that nitrogen removal rate (NRR) increased 3.45-fold at optimal voltage (0.4–0.5 V) compared to non-voltage control. Four ML algorithms (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and Categorical Boosting) were employed to develop predictive models for the NRR. The Categorical Boosting model exhibited superior performance, achieving R2 values of 0.974 and 0.852 for the training and testing sets, respectively. SHAP analysis identified applied voltage as the critical influencing factor, while partial dependence plots revealed its nonlinear regulatory effects and the synergistic interactions among multiple features. A 106-day continuous reactor experiment validated the model's effectiveness: at the predicted optimal voltage of 0.4 V, the system achieved an NRR of 720 mg N/(L·d) with a nitrogen removal efficiency of 87%. Notably, the system maintained stable performance even with a 24% reduction in influent nitrite concentration, alleviating the inherent nitrite dependency of anammox processes. Microbial community analysis revealed that anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing bacteria maintained 80% contribution ratio, significantly higher than other functional bacteria, confirming the strong activation effect of applied voltage. This study confirms the core role of ML in precise performance prediction and key parameter identification, providing data-driven support for the identification of optimal conditions, intelligent control, and scaled application of electrochemically enhanced anammox processes.

verified_metadata.title: Exploration of salivary biomarkers for accurate diagnosis of anxiety, depression, and somatic symptom disorder by the integration of microfluidic chip and machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Depression represents a major global public health concern, affecting hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide. The World Health Organization forecasts that, by 2030, depression will emerge as the primary driver of the global healthcare challenge. Consequently, the identification of biomarkers specific to anxiety (ANX), depression (DEP), and somatic symptom disorder (SSD) is crucial for early and accurate diagnosis and timely treatment. Here, we explicited a diagnosis model to screen the patients by a salivary biomarkers panel in the of a cohort consisting of healthy individuals and patients with ANX, DEP, and SSD, through a microfluidic chip. The detection results show that the expression levels of inflammatory cytokines were elevated in patients compared with healthy individuals. A four-biomarker panel was employed to train the machine learning (ML) model (M4D) based on the random forest (RF) algorithm for early and accurate differential diagnosis, which includes tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and Interferon-gamma (IFN-γ). It can identify the specific type of mental disorder for an individual with AUC > 0.98, without invasive procedures. The diagnostic accuracy in the test set reached 92.22%. The proposed non-invasive diagnostic method presents promising applications in making precise diagnosis of mental disorders.

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。实质综述AI加速光催化制氢材料发现及结构性能机制联结。

verified_metadata.title: Photocatalytic hydrogen production: Materials design, system engineering, and data-driven advances
verified_metadata.abstract: Photocatalytic hydrogen production offers a sustainable solar-to‑hydrogen conversion route by splitting water under light irradiation. However, most systems remain confined to laboratory conditions because of limited efficiency, stability, and scalability. This review provides an overview of how materials design, system engineering, and data-driven tools can be integrated to advance photocatalytic hydrogen production toward practical deployment. Fundamental strategies for improving solar-to‑hydrogen efficiency are first summarized, focusing on band-structure modulation, charge-carrier dynamics, surface catalytic-site optimization, and stability enhancement. Representative photocatalyst families—including metal oxides, metal sulfides, MOFs, MXenes, and their heterostructures—are discussed in terms of how S-scheme and Z-scheme architectures, cocatalyst loading, facet control, and defect engineering collectively govern light absorption, charge separation, and reaction kinetics. Beyond powder suspensions, approaches such as photothermal catalysis, photoelectrocatalysis, magnetic-field-assisted photocatalysis, and photobiocatalytic systems that couple biological components with inorganic photocatalysts are highlighted. Emphasis is placed on the role of artificial intelligence in accelerating materials discovery, elucidating structure–property–performance relationships, and guiding reactor and process optimization. By linking mechanistic insights with system-level design and using quantitative performance indicators such as AQE and STH, this review outlines a framework for developing efficient, durable, and scalable photocatalytic hydrogen production technologies suitable for real-world deployment.

title: Loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole fiber-skeleton hydrogels for machine-learning-assisted multimodal flexible sensor

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。机器学习解析可回收MXene水凝胶的多模态应变压力湿度信号，实现交互传感。

verified_metadata.title: Loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole fiber-skeleton hydrogels for machine-learning-assisted multimodal flexible sensor
verified_metadata.abstract: Flexible hydrogel sensors that are strong, multimodal, and recyclable are highly desirable for wearable electronics but remain difficult to realize because conventional conductive gels are mechanically isotropic, single responsive, and structurally fragile. Here, we report a loofah-inspired recyclable MXene/polypyrrole (PPy) fiber-skeleton hydrogel (PBMA) constructed from PPy, bacterial cellulose (BC) fibers, a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/tannic acid (TA) matrix, and well-dispersed Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene, in which directional freeze-thaw processing generated an aligned loofah-like porous architecture with anisotropic mechanical and conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogel simultaneously achieves high tensile strength (~1.8 MPa), large toughness (~6 MJ·m−3), and stretchability up to ~250%, while exhibiting low hysteresis and durable piezoresistive response over 5000 loading–unloading cycles. PBMA functions as a multimodal strain–humidity sensor with a gauge factor (GF) up to 4.66, fast electromechanical response/recovery (~160 ms), and humidity sensitivity over 10–80% RH with ~10 s response time. Benefiting from strong adhesion, antibacterial activity, and thermal reprocessability that retained over 90% of its original sensing performance, PBMA enables long-term conformal monitoring of physiological motions, respiration and ambient humidity, Morse-code communication, object-diameter and spatial pressure mapping, and machine-learning-assisted gesture recognition with 99.75% accuracy. This loofah-inspired fiber-skeleton design provides a sustainable route to high-performance, recyclable hydrogel electronic skins.

title: Kinetic modeling and machine-learning optimization of a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier for hydrogen-rich and low-tar syngas production

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。支持向量回归结合动力学和实验设计优化三段流化床富氢低焦油气化工艺。

verified_metadata.title: Kinetic modeling and machine-learning optimization of a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier for hydrogen-rich and low-tar syngas production
verified_metadata.abstract: Biomass gasification remains a key pathway for clean fuel production; however, conventional fluidized-bed reactors continue to suffer from limited carbon conversion and persistent tar formation, constraining system efficiency and industrial adoption. This study introduces a novel three-stage fluidized-bed gasifier—integrating controlled devolatilization, high-temperature steam/air reforming, and char gasification—to simultaneously enhance syngas quality and suppress tar generation. A kinetics-based Aspen Plus model was developed and rigorously validated against experimental data. To capture multivariate interactions across operating conditions, Design of Experiments (DOE) and Response Surface Methodology (RSM) were coupled with Support Vector Regression (SVR), significantly outperforming classical regression in predictive accuracy. Multi-objective optimization using NSGA-II identified Pareto-optimal trade-offs among cold gas efficiency (CGE), carbon conversion efficiency (CCE), and tar yield. Results demonstrate that increasing the reformer temperature from 1050 to 1200 °C elevates CGE from 82% to 92% and boosts CCE from 88% to 97%, while reducing tar yield from 4 to 0.3%. The optimized operating window yields hydrogen-rich syngas (up to 27% H₂) with an LHV of 7.75 MJ/Nm3, alongside near-complete carbon conversion and minimal tar yield (<0.1%). Overall, the proposed three-stage configuration—supported by advanced kinetic modeling and machine-learning-assisted optimization—establishes a robust platform for high-efficiency, low-tar biomass-to‑hydrogen conversion, offering strong potential for deployment in next-generation renewable energy and low-carbon fuel systems.

title: A bioinspired electronic skin with orthogonal hydrogel and cascaded deep learning for decoupling tangential force and deformation mapping

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。级联深度学习解耦电子皮肤切向力和变形场，构建双向物理接触感知。

verified_metadata.title: A bioinspired electronic skin with orthogonal hydrogel and cascaded deep learning for decoupling tangential force and deformation mapping
verified_metadata.abstract: Human skin interprets physical contact by jointly sensing surface deformation and multidimensional forces, a dual-vector capability that underpins dexterous interaction. However, existing robotic tactile sensors fundamentally lack this dual-vector perception, failing to capture simultaneously both tangential forces and deformation fields. Prompted by this gap, we present a bioinspired electronic skin (e-skin) for the high-precision perception of tangential forces and deformation fields. Inspired by the mechano-transduction pathway of Ruffini corpuscles, the e-skin features an orthogonal hydrogel grid architecture to mimic this transduction mechanism. We further employ a cascaded deep regression framework to reverse-engineer this transduction, forming a “sensing” and “perception” integrated paradigm. Crucially, this biomimetic e-skin first reconstructs deformation vectors (ΔX, ΔY) with high fidelity (MAE < 0. 5423 mm, R2 > 0.9955) over a ± 20 mm range, then infers tangential forces (Fx, Fy) from the estimated deformations with remarkable accuracy (MAE < 0.247 N, R2 > 0.9931) within ± 7.5 N. Validated through deformation field reconstruction and human-robot interaction, this system is capable of perceiving nuanced physical interactions, enabling a robot to interpret interaction intentions.

title: Data-driven discovery of high-performance surface passivators for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven discovery of high-performance surface passivators for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells
verified_metadata.abstract: Effective passivation of interface defect is vital for improving perovskite solar cell (PSC) performance. Traditional trial-and-error methods to identify passivators represent slow, costly, and dependent on expert input, limiting thorough exploration of potential candidates. This study introduces an automated platform, “MatInsight”, to extract key PSC parameters from literature, creating a dataset for training seven machine learning (ML) models. The categorical boosting (CatBoost) model excelled as the top predictor, identifying influential molecular descriptors—dihedral angle (Phi), topological complexity (BertzCT), molar refractivity (MolMR), and minimum absolute EState index (MinAbsEStateIndex)—for optimizing power conversion efficiency (PCE). We predicted passivation efficacy within a molecular library, followed by experimental validation. Notably, PSCs using 3-fluoro-4-aminobenzonitrile (FABN) demonstrated superior defect passivation, achieving a PCE of 25.7% and maintaining 84% efficiency over 1400 h in ambient conditions. This scalable approach offers a robust framework for rapidly identifying effective passivators, significantly advancing the development of stable, high-efficiency PSCs.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-driven COD real-time monitoring electrochemical analysis system based on nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond electrode
verified_metadata.abstract: Industrial development and urban expansion exert considerable ecological pressure due to organic wastewater discharge, necessitating fast, real-time water-quality monitoring to oversee treatment processes and warn against unsafe discharge. In this study, a miniaturized electrochemical (EC) detector and artificial intelligence (AI)-based real-time water quality analysis software were developed to monitor organic components, concentrations, and chemical oxygen demand (COD) in wastewater. A nitrogen-etched boron-doped diamond (NBDD) sensing electrode, with a surface composed of relatively intact (100) diamond planes and graphene-covered nanocrystals, was employed. This electrode demonstrated high responsiveness, electrocatalytic activity, and long-term stability toward all six dyes (carmine, methylene blue, methylene green, basic fuchsin, rhodamine B, and indigo). The AI software employed principal component analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction; support vector machine (SVM) for dye classification; and a fusion algorithm (iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS)/multilayer perceptron (MLP)/gradient boosting machine (GBM)) for predicting COD and concentration. It achieved dye identification accuracies ranging from 82.7% to 100%. The NBDD-EC detector combined with the AI analysis system achieved high correlations between the predicted and actual values of dye concentration and COD. When deployed industrially, it predicted dye wastewater COD with 96 ± 2% accuracy, providing a reliable hardware-software solution for real-time monitoring, crucial for discharge oversight.

title: Dynamic optimization of coke formation in dry reforming of methane using a neural quasi-steady-state model

verified_metadata.title: Dynamic optimization of coke formation in dry reforming of methane using a neural quasi-steady-state model
verified_metadata.abstract: This work develops a microkinetic-surrogate-based dynamic optimization framework for identifying coke-aware operating strategies in dry reforming of methane. A neural quasi-steady-state model (NQSSM) is introduced in which the fast-reacting species are predicted using an artificial neural network, while coke coverage is retained as an ordinary differential equation(ODE) state. This structure enables transient system prediction at a fraction of the computational cost of the full microkinetic model, thereby allowing dynamic optimization that accounts for catalyst deactivation. Bayesian optimization is integrated with the NQSSM to efficiently determine dynamic operating schedules that maximize performance. Dynamic optimization under multiple coke constraints on reactor coke coverage reveals a clear trade-off between syngas production and coke accumulation. This trade-off is quantified by a weighted syngas performance index (WSPI), which is introduced in this research to reflect the productivity of H2 and CO and the consumption of CH4 and CO2 over time. With tighter constraints, the optimal operating regime shifts toward more oxidation-favoring conditions. This shift manifests systematically in the optimal profiles, including decreasing temperature, increasing pressure, and reduced early-stage flow rate. The NQSSM accurately captures these time-dependent strategic adjustments while preserving mechanistic interpretability. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mechanistically grounded and computationally efficient approach for designing degradation-aware operating strategies and can be readily extended to other reaction systems in which dynamic behavior and catalyst deactivation are closely coupled.

verified_metadata.title: Crosstalk-free dual-mode electronic skin enabled by selective electrospinning and machine learning-based decoupling
verified_metadata.abstract: Electronic skins play a crucial role in health monitoring, human motion detection, and soft robotics. Nevertheless, achieving an integrated dual-mode electronic skin using compatible and simplified processes while reducing crosstalk between different sensing signals remains a significant challenge. This study developed dual-mode electronic skin using selective electrospinning deposition of functional layers for pressure and temperature sensing. The electronic skin consists of two parts: a top layer based on electrospun polyvinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene (PVDF-TrFE) nanofibers sandwiched between interlocked mortise-tenon structured electrodes for pressure sensing; and a bottom layer based on PVDF-TrFE and silver nanowires (AgNWs) for temperature sensing. The mortise-tenon structured electrode design and selective-deposition electrospun nanofiber significantly enhances the piezoelectric response. Each layer is process-compatible and specific structures are set up according to the different signals collected, thus achieving excellent sensing performance. The electronic skin utilizes two different sensing mechanisms with dual-parameter decoupling method, which successfully eliminate cross-sensitivity interference between temperature and pressure. The system inherently corrects for the temperature coefficient of the pressure signal, yielding higher accuracy than single-parameter sensors. Furthermore, an intelligent decoupling optimization algorithm via machine-learning is introduced to enable high-precision decoupling pressure and temperature stimuli to identify different materials like human perception of touch.

title: Learning from limited data and feedback for cell culture process monitoring: A comparative study
abstract: In cell culture bioprocessing, real-time batch process monitoring (BPM) refers to the continuous tracking and analysis of key process variables – such as viable cell density, nutrient levels, metabolite concentrations, and product titer – throughout the duration of a batch run. This enables early detection of deviations and supports timely control actions to ensure optimal cell growth and product quality. BPM plays a critical role in ensuring the quality and regulatory compliance of biopharmaceutical manufacturing processes. However, the development of accurate soft sensors for BPM is hindered by key challenges, including limited historical data, infrequent feedback, heterogeneous process conditions, and high-dimensional sensory inputs. This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking analysis of machine learning (ML) methods designed to address these challenges, with a focus on learning from historical data with limited volume and relevance in the context of bioprocess monitoring. We evaluate multiple ML approaches – including feature dimensionality reduction, online learning, and just-in-time learning – across three datasets, one in silico dataset and two real-world experimental datasets. Our findings highlight the importance of training strategies in handling limited data and feedback, with batch learning proving effective in homogeneous settings, while just-in-time learning and online learning demonstrate superior adaptability in cold-start scenarios. Additionally, we identify key meta-features, such as feed media composition and process control strategies, that significantly impact model transferability. The results also suggest that integrating Raman-based predictions with lagged offline measurements enhances monitoring accuracy, offering a promising direction for future bioprocess soft sensor development.

title: Autonomous characterisation of fouling-free feasible operating regions in continuous flow precipitation of ketoprofen nanoparticles
abstract: Continuous antisolvent precipitation enables efficient pharmaceutical manufacturing but is susceptible to fouling, which disrupts operation and compromises product quality. To address this challenge, we developed and validated a closed-loop, autonomous screening platform for identifying non-fouling conditions in continuous antisolvent precipitation, demonstrated for ketoprofen nanoparticle formation in a confined impinging jet reactor using ethanol as solvent, water as antisolvent, and Kollidon VA 64 (PVP/VA) as additive. The platform integrates real-time, pressure drop-based fouling detection with adaptive experimental design. Initially, it performs design of experiments to generate feasibility labels (fouling or non-fouling). A class balancing strategy then targets under-represented regions, and active learning with Gaussian Process (GP) classification selects subsequent experiments to reduce uncertainty in feasibility prediction. With an experimental budget of 50 precipitation experiments, the system autonomously mapped the boundary separating fouling and non-fouling regions across three key process variables: total volume flow rate (1–11 mL min −1 ), antisolvent-to-solvent volume flow rate ratio (4–10), and drug-to-additive mass ratio (0.2125–4.25). The resulting GP classifier achieved high prediction accuracy with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) greater than 0.8 in cross-validation experiments and an AUC of 1.0 in a set of eight follow-up validation experiments. The methodology revealed complex interactions between process conditions and fouling behaviour, identifying robust non-fouling operating windows. This autonomous framework provides a systematic and efficient approach for fouling detection and operating region characterisation in continuous pharmaceutical precipitation, reducing development effort and improving process reliability.

title: Competitive adsorption performance of volatile organic compounds on ZSM-5: Key influence factors and mechanisms
abstract: The zeolite rotor-regenerative thermal oxidizer (RTO) system has been widely applied to control volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions from automotive coating processes. Zeolite selection was crucial for treatment efficiency. Given fluctuations in VOC emissions, this selection was influenced by the ZSM-5 characteristics, VOCs types and competition among these VOCs. Herein, the key influencing factors and mechanisms for competitive adsorption of typical VOCs (butyl acetate, acetone and aromatic hydrocarbons) on ZSM-5 with varying Si/Al ratio was investigated by correlation analysis, LightGBM model with SHapley Additive exPlanation and molecular simulation. The competition between components, determined by adsorption strength and sites of VOC molecules, was identified as the key factor. Among these VOCs, butyl acetate, with the strongest adsorption force, always dominated the adsorption process, while acetone and aromatic hydrocarbons showed weaker adsorption and were significantly influenced by inter-component competition. The competitive intensity also depended on adsorption sites of VOCs on ZSM-5, which was related to the Si/Al ratio. At Si/Al < 150, butyl acetate shared fewer adsorption sites with these weaker-adsorbed VOCs resulting in relatively weak competition, which made this ZSM-5 suitable for aromatic hydrocarbon-rich exhaust. At Si/Al ≥ 150, extensive overlap between the adsorption sites for butyl acetate and weaker-adsorbed VOCs contributed to high selectivity of butyl acetate, making this ZSM-5 effective for ester-dominant exhaust. These will provide theoretical guidance for selecting and regulating zeolites to efficiently treat different VOC components.

verified_metadata.title: Neural network-based multi-objective optimization of a biomass polygeneration system with chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient and cost-effective utilization of biomass is crucial for mitigating energy and environmental pressures. This study proposes a new biomass polygeneration system integrating chemical looping carbon dioxide displacement of nitrogen (CLCDN) for simultaneous electricity and fuel gas production. In the proposed system, high-temperature O2 and CO2 mixtures produced by the CLCDN process are used as the gasifying agent, and externally concentrated solar energy supplies the heat required for gasification. A neural network-based multi-objective optimization model is developed to improve exergy and exergoeconomic performance, and enhance syngas quality. The model development involves two stages. First, Bayesian optimization is employed to determine the optimal hyperparameters of a multilayer perceptron (MLP). Then, multi-objective optimization is conducted using the trained MLP model. Under optimal hyperparameters, the MLP achieves a coefficient of determination of 0.99. The optimization results indicate that the proposed system achieves optimal performance at a CLCDN reaction temperature of 841.34 °C, a CO2 to biomass mass flow ratio of 0.44, and a gasification temperature of 1016.14 °C. Compared with the reference system, the exergy efficiency (74.09%) and effective carbon efficiency (99.49%) increase by 2.19% and 33.17%, respectively. Meanwhile, the CO2 mass flow rate in syngas decreases by 2.514 ton/h, while the unit exergy cost of total products (0.019 $/kWh) increases by 5.56%. Overall, the proposed system enables efficient biomass gasification and improves syngas quality. The developed optimization framework provides a theoretical basis for system design and performance improvement.

verified_metadata.title: Accurate and expandable graph deep learning for accelerating predictive identification of high-potential organic photovoltaics
verified_metadata.abstract: Organic photovoltaics (OPVs) are a leading renewable energy technology, yet the discovery of high-performance non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) is often hindered by the vastness of chemical space and the synthetic costs of complex fused-ring systems. In this study, we develop a robust, physics-informed graph deep learning framework based on a directed message passing neural network (D-MPNN) to accelerate the predictive identification of high-potential OPVs. By representing molecules as fragment-level graphs enriched with computable descriptors—including DFT-derived frontier orbital energies and molecular mechanics-calculated structural parameters—our model achieves excellent predictive accuracy, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.93 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.89% under 10-fold cross-validation. The model's capability was rigorously validated through a temporal “blind” test of 42 newly reported NFA ternary OPV devices (published after model training), where it maintained a high predictive accuracy (MAE = 1.17%) even for systems containing novel molecular fragments. Leveraging this framework, we performed high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) of approximately 334 million ternary combinations, identifying 4904 novel systems with predicted power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) surpassing the training dataset ceiling of 19.36%. Furthermore, fragment-level Z-score analyses identified key structural motifs, such as specific non-fused rigid cores and the benefit of “No-p-spacer” architecture, providing actionable design rules for experimental development. This accurate and expandable framework offers a powerful platform for the predictive identification of high-potential ternary OPVs.

verified_metadata.title: AI-guided discovery of an efficient chitinase enables green production of chitobioses with distinct cadmium stress-alleviating efficacy in rice
verified_metadata.abstract: Abiotic stresses, particularly heavy metal contamination, induce excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) in plants, causing oxidative damage and severe crop yield losses. Structurally defined chitobioses are promising natural antioxidants hold great promise as biostimulants to enhance plant stress tolerance in sustainable agriculture. However, their green, cost-effective synthesis remains a bottleneck. Here, we employed an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven structure-based enzyme mining strategy to identify a thermostable, highly specific endochitinase (CT10) from Paenibacillus elgii, which efficiently hydrolyzes low-cost colloidal crustacean chitin into N, N′-Diacetylchitobiose (GlcNAcβ1-4GlcNAc, AA) with minimal byproducts. Coupling CT10 with regioselective chitin deacetylases (VcCDA/NodB) in one-pot cascade reaction yielded three additional structurally defined chitobioses: GlcNAcβ1-4GlcN (AD), GlcNβ1-4GlcNAc (DA), and GlcNβ1-4GlcN (DD), all with >95% purity. Among these, DA exhibits superior hydroxyl radical (OH•) scavenging activity comparable to l-ascorbic acid. Exogenous application of the four chitobioses alleviated cadmium (Cd) stress in rice (Oryza sativa L.), restoring growth, reducing ROS/MDA accumulation, and upregulating antioxidant enzyme genes (sod, pod, cat). Notably, DA showed the most potent efficacy in promoting root biomass recovery and activating antioxidant defense pathways. This study establishes a scalable, green platform for the synthesis of structurally defined chitobioses and delineates their structure-specific roles in alleviating heavy metal toxicity, providing a nature-based strategy to improve crop resilience in abiotic stress-affected agricultural systems.

title: High mechanical-sensing hydrogels coupled with machine learning for acoustic signal recognition
abstract: Flexible wearable electronic devices and engineering require that functional materials have the characteristics of strong mechanical adaptability, high sensing sensitivity and system integration capability. Hydrogels have broad application prospects in this field due to their inherent biocompatibility and flexibility of tissue simulation. However, traditional hydrogels are limited in their large-scale and engineering applications due to their core limitations, including elusive mechanical sensing balance, limited functionality and inadequate system integration. In order to solve these key shortcomings, a design strategy combining covalent-non-covalent synergistic crosslinking and ion regulation for the preparation of P(AM-co-AA-co-CAVIm)/HEC composite hydrogels is developed. The obtained materials combine the covalent bond stability with the energy dissipation and microenvironment modulation capabilities of dynamic non-covalent interactions, thus establishing an optimized structural framework to enhance the mechanical and sensing performance. The resultant PMAIH-3 hydrogel achieves an elongation at break of 3204.58% and a tensile strength of 512.9 kPa, alongside segmented linear sensing responses (GF1 = 3.18, GF2 = 10.1), rapid response dynamics of 0.36 s, and stable operation over 200 cycles, effectively overcoming the inherent compromise of traditional hydrogels. Further integration of the hydrogel’s sensing capabilities with machine learning enables the construction of a voice-authentication system that delivers accurate sound signal capture and high-precision performance across multiple users. Collectively, this integrated material-system approach furnishes a powerful platform for advancing high-performance intelligent wearable bioelectronic devices.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted dual-mode sensing array: NIR-enhanced Cu-Co3O4 nanozymes for high-throughput antioxidant discrimination
verified_metadata.abstract: Antioxidants play a critical role in sustaining physiological balance, making the rapid and accurate identification of multiple antioxidants essential for disease diagnosis and analysis. Conventional single-mode sensing arrays often suffer from inefficiency and inconsistency. Addressing this challenge, we engineered Cu-doped Co3O4 nanozymes (Cu-Co3O4) with tunable doping ratios using a self-templating approach. By integrating the optimized Cu-Co3O4 nanozyme with near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, we developed a dual-mode sensing platform that combines colorimetric and photothermal signals for high-throughput, precise antioxidant detection. Under NIR exposure, Cu-Co3O4 demonstrates significantly enhanced catalytic oxidation of TMB, driven by synergistic non-radiative relaxation and redox reactions of photogenerated carriers, amplifying both chromogenic and photothermal responses. Leveraging the distinct reducing capacities of various antioxidants on oxidized TMB (oxTMB), our sensing array—combined with machine learning—effectively processes unique response patterns. Linear discriminant analysis enabled the discrimination and quantification of key antioxidants, including ascorbic acid, dopamine, uric acid, glutathione, and melatonin, while hierarchical clustering and random forest algorithms validated methodological accuracy. Notably, the random forest model successfully predicted component concentrations in binary antioxidant mixtures. This study not only advances the strategic modulation of enzyme-like activity and photothermal properties in transition metal oxides but also establishes a robust framework for high-throughput target analysis in complex matrixes.

title: Bioleaching of critical minerals from marine sediments by indigenous microbial communities: Experimental and predictive analysis
abstract: Marine sediments represent a valuable source for critical minerals that prompts growing research interest in their potential for sustainable resource recovery. This study investigated the impact of bioleaching microorganisms, evaluating three different microbial inocula: sediment indigenous Fe-oxidizing bacteria, sediment indigenous Fe- and S-oxidizing bacteria, and Acidhiobacillus ferrooxidans. Key operational parameters including initial pH (2.0-7.0), energy source availability (Fe and S), and total solids content (5-10%) were also systematically varied to optimize bioleaching efficiency. The highest metal bioleaching for Al, Mg, and K was achieved using Fe- and S-oxidizing bacteria enriched from the marine sediment. The maximum concentrations in the leachate were detected as 806 mg/L (17.6%), 506 mg/L (65.7%), and 169 mg/L (22%) for Al, Mg and K, respectively. Alicyclobacillaceae was one of the key microorganisms which dominated microbial community over time. On the other hand, Sulfuristis played a key role in the early shifts in the microbial community. Additionally, Least Square Boosting (LSBoost), Random Forest Regression (RF), and Linear Regression (LR) were employed to evaluate the influence of experimental variables. All models demonstrated predictive performance for critical mineral release from the sediment, with LSBoost showing superior predictive accuracy.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted property prediction and virtual screening of polyimides for flexible electronic applications
verified_metadata.abstract: Polyimides (PIs) are indispensable high-performance polymers for advanced flexible electronics, owing to their remarkable thermal stability, mechanical strength, and optical properties. To accelerate the design of colorless, transparent, and thermally stable PIs, this work introduces a machine learning (ML)-driven inverse design framework. By integrating molecular fingerprinting with ML models, we first developed accurate quantitative structure-property relationship (QSAR) models. Gradient Boosting (GB) model with RDKit fingerprints was identified as the optimal predictor (R2 > 0.94) for optical absorption (λmax), charge transfer (CTe), and thermal decomposition temperature (Td5). SHAP interpretability analysis further elucidated the roles of key substructures such as flexible ether linkers, fluorinated groups and conjugated structure. Guided by polycondensation chemistry, PIs disassembled into dianhydride (A) and diamine (B) building units and combinatorially expanded through flexible ether linkages (O) to create a virtual library consisting of 1530 AB-type and 175,664 ABOC-ype hypothetical monomers. High-throughput screening under stringent criteria (λmax < 400 nm, CTe < 0.2 e, Td5 > 530 °C) using a multi-task learning sparse encoder (MTL-SE) model successfully identified top candidates, including the outstanding h-BPDA-162 and 287 high-performance h-ABOC-type PI monomers. This work provides a scalable computational framework and specific structural guidelines as leads for the rational design and synthesis of advanced PI materials.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-driven lipase engineering for highly enantioselective synthesis of chiral florfenicol intermediate via enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system
verified_metadata.abstract: (2S,3R)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine ethyl ester [(2S,3R)-p-MPSE], a key chiral building block of the aryl β-hydroxy-α-amino ester family, serves as one of the critical intermediates for the synthesis of the veterinary antibiotic florfenicol. Kinetic resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE by lipases represents a highly promising route. However, low catalytic efficiency of natural enzymes restricted its application. In this study, a lipase BSL from Bacillus subtilis was mined and rational design was performed to obtain a series of mutants. A robust Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression model, integrated with multi-dimensional encoding from the Amino Acid Index Database (AAindex) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based data processing technology, was constructed and trained. Using this machine learning (ML)-driven enzyme engineering approach, a mutant E115F/L67D/I421Q/P317I was successfully created, showing a 15.4-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km). Under the load of 1 M high substrate concentration, this mutant could achieve complete resolution of rac-threo-p-MPSE within 4 h, yielding optically pure (2S,3R)-p-MPSE (e.e.s > 99%) with a yield of 97.4% (based on the theoretical amount of single enantiomer). Additionally, the inactive isomer (2R,3S)-p-methylsulfonylphenyl serine [(2R,3S)-p-MPS] was recycled via chemical racemization based on a reversible retro-aldol cleavage mechanism and re-esterification, which facilitated the recycling of the substrate. This study not only breaks through the bottleneck of low catalytic efficiency of natural lipases through a machine learning-mediated precise enzyme engineering strategy, but also establishes a high-benefit chiral preparation process for (2S,3R)-p-MPSE via an enzymatic resolution-chemical racemization coupling system.

verified_metadata.title: Machine-learning-assisted cancer detection and classification based on selective CTC capture and sequential in situ biomarkers quantification by polyvalent dual-aptamer DNA hydrogel
verified_metadata.abstract: Early and accurate cancer classification based on circulating tumor cells (CTCs) is limited by inefficient enrichment, release-induced perturbation, and the lack of integrated strategies for cell-resolved multimodal biomarker analysis, particularly for aggressive subtypes such as triple-negative breast cancer (TN-BC). Herein, we report a unified engineering platform based on polyvalent dual-aptamer (PDApt)-DNA hydrogel that enables selective CTC encapsulation and sequential in situ quantification of membrane-bound and intracellular biomarkers without cell release or lysis. The PDApt-DNA hydrogel is constructed from two rolling-circle-amplified strands bearing polyvalent aptamers, enabling efficient and broad-spectrum CTC capture. In a cohort of 31 participants, the platform enables effective separation between cancer and healthy samples and clear identification of TN-BC (100% sensitivity and 100% specificity). Overall, this work establishes a non-release, multimodal CTC engineering strategy that couples gentle enrichment of CTCs with in situ biomarkers quantification, providing a generalizable framework for CTC-based precision diagnostics and clinical stratification.

title: Synthetic data-driven prediction and interpretation of biomethane production in direct interspecies electron transfer-stimulated anaerobic digestion process

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。合成数据增强结合多类机器学习与实验，预测磁铁矿介导DIET厌氧消化甲烷增产。

verified_metadata.title: Synthetic data-driven prediction and interpretation of biomethane production in direct interspecies electron transfer-stimulated anaerobic digestion process
verified_metadata.abstract: Direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) simulation has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance methane production in anaerobic digestion (AD). However, reliable prediction and interpretation of DIET-AD performance remain challenging due to nonlinearity and limited experimental datasets. In this study, we propose an integrated, synthetic data-assisted machine learning (ML) framework to predict methane enhancement in magnetite-mediated DIET-AD systems, combining data augmentation, robust modeling, and experimental validation. The synthetic dataset was generated by generative adversarial network (GAN), which was rigorously validated from statistical, principal component, clustering analysis, and Kolmogorov–Smirov test to ensure consistency with original experimental data. Multiple ML models, including ensemble-based, neural network-based, and attention- based algorithms, were systematically evaluated. Among them, an attention-based algorithm showed superior performance and robustness, achieving an average coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.92, root mean squared error (RMSE) of 6.30, and mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.04 on test data. Explainable artificial intelligence analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) indicated that substrate concentration and magnetite dosage were dominant drivers of methane enhancement. Experimental biomethane potential (BMP) tests further confirmed model reliability, with observed enhancements of 5.1% and 15.8% falling within the predicted 95% confidence intervals of 3.5–6.6% and 15.6–21.3%, respectively. Therefore, this framework contributes to practical insight into a transferable strategy for robust prediction, interpretation, and experimental guidance of nonlinear bioprocesses under data-scarce conditions.

verified_metadata.title: S/N induced coordination isomerism hydrogels on 3D-printed device for machine learning-assisted multiplex detection of heavy metal ions
verified_metadata.abstract: A portable hydrogel-based colorimetric sensing material integrated with machine learning analysis has been developed for the simultaneous on-site sensing of five toxic heavy metal ions (Cd2+, Pb2+, Hg2+, Cr6+, As3+). This capability stems from atomically designed hydrogels that enable visual recognition of metal ions through coordination differences. Notably, coordination-isomerism-driven differential recognition enables the simultaneous detection of these five ions. Three hydrogel sensing units (HP1, HP2, HP3) are synthesized via Ba2+ coordination of sodium alginate (SA) backbone molecule (Pr2) with response molecules (Pr4, Pr6, Pr8) featuring thiocyanate (–S–C≡N) and isothiocyanate (–N=C=S) groups. These units are spatially arranged in a 3D-printed device. The dominant coordination sites are S atoms in HP1 and HP3, whereas the dominant coordination site in HP2 is the N atom. Smartphone-captured RGB signals are converted into Euclidean distance (d-value) and processed using the machine-learning technique of linear discriminant analysis (LDA), achieving multiplex quantification with detection limits of 3.76 nM (Cd2+), 6.33 nM (Pb2+), 4.19 nM (Hg2+), 7.84 nM (Cr6+), and 6.42 nM (As3+) across a linear range of 0.01 to 5 μM for all five heavy metal ions. The platform demonstrates exceptional specificity against interferents and robust discrimination for binary to quinary heavy metal mixtures. This integration of rationally designed hydrogel probes, a 3D-printed device, and machine learning technology establishes a sensitive, accurate, and low-cost strategy for POCT (point-of-care testing) of multiple coexisting toxic heavy metal ions in environmental and food safety applications.

verified_metadata.title: Nanocellulose-reinforced deep eutectic solvent-based smart hydrogel sensor for adaptive window regulation and machine learning-assisted low-temperature motion monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: Wearable hydrogel sensors often suffer from poor environmental stability and mechanical mismatch under temperature fluctuations, leading to signal drift and unreliable performance in real-world applications. To overcome these limitations, we developed a skin-inspired multifunctional hydrogel based on a green deep eutectic solvent (DES) system reinforced with cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs). The hydrogel was fabricated via UV-initiated polymerization of polyacrylamide (PAM) and gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), with phytic acid and CNFs forming a dynamically cross-linked network through covalent, hydrogen-bonding, and ionic interactions. The incorporation of DES provides stable ionic conductivity and enhanced environmental tolerance, while CNF reinforcement significantly improves mechanical robustness. As a result, the PDGCP hydrogel exhibits high tensile strength (0.65 MPa), large stretchability (1862%), and stable sensing performance over thousands of cycles. The hydrogel also exhibits antibacterial activity and excellent biocompatibility. As a wearable strain sensor, it achieves a wide sensing range (up to 1200%) and enables reliable monitoring of human motion as well as high-fidelity ECG and EMG signals. In addition, the hydrogel can function as a smart window component with bidirectional temperature responsiveness. By integrating machine learning algorithms, the system enables real-time recognition of complex ice-skating motion postures with an accuracy of 98.25%. This work highlights a sustainable DES-based hydrogel platform with enhanced mechanical stability and environmental adaptability, offering promising applications in wearable electronics, intelligent sports monitoring, and adaptive building systems.

verified_metadata.title: Scalable expanded-graphite coating for high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes with data-driven optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: Single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes possess a monolithic structure that effectively suppresses the formation of microcracks, even under repeated volumetric changes during charge–discharge cycling. However, these single-crystal cathodes often exhibit slow Li-ion diffusion kinetics and poor rate capability, primarily due to the long diffusion pathways within the micron-sized particles. In this study, we introduce a simple and scalable one-pot method for applying an expanded-graphite (EG) surface coating to single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes. EG forms a uniform and conductive carbon layer through ball milling after surface activation with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane. This conductive coating significantly enhances the electrical conductivity of the cathode and effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced side reactions, thereby improving cycling stability while maintaining compatibility with existing industrial regeneration processes. A data-driven optimization approach based on Gaussian-process-based Bayesian optimization was employed to determine the optimal EG loading for maximizing electrochemical performance. The method is further demonstrated at kilogram scale, highlighting its feasibility for large-scale manufacturing. Overall, this work presents a practical approach for producing high-performance single-crystal Ni-rich cathodes and provides a promising route toward commercially viable cathode regeneration beyond laboratory-scale studies.

title: Data-driven mechanism derivation in hydrogenation reaction systems: A hybrid approach integrating machine learning and mathematical models

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。ANN学习实际加氢运行数据并用XAI解释反应物影响，推导副反应机制及数学模型。

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven mechanism derivation in hydrogenation reaction systems: A hybrid approach integrating machine learning and mathematical models
verified_metadata.abstract: This study proposes a hybrid approach that integrates a black-box model with an equation-based mechanism verification model to identify the causative reactants of side reactions occurring in hydrogenation reaction systems and to derive their mechanisms. Due to the complex reaction network inherent in hydrogenation systems, exhaustive exploration and prediction of all side reactions are practically difficult, and such predictive uncertainty can lead to deterioration in product quality and economic losses. Accordingly, this study constructed a reliable dataset by performing preprocessing steps to remove missing values and outliers based on actual operating data, and designed an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. As a result of enhancing the generalization performance of the model through data transformation that reflects domain knowledge in the form of reaction rate expressions, the coefficient of determination (R2) improved to 0.97, and the root mean squared error (RMSE) decreased markedly to 0.04. In addition, the influence of each reactant was quantified and visualized using eXplainable AI (XAI) techniques, based on which the side reaction mechanisms were derived. To verify the derived mechanisms, reaction rate expressions were formulated using the Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) and Power Law models, and a Monte Carlo-based mathematical model was developed. The validation results showed very high performance for all products, with R2 values greater than 0.98 and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) lower than 2.31%. This study has academic and industrial significance in that it systematically elucidates actual side reaction mechanisms while presenting a highly reliable predictive model applicable to reaction control design.

title: Smart bearings enabled by the tribovoltaic effect and machine learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。可解释机器学习与深度学习解析摩擦伏特轴承电信号，估计转速并进行早期故障诊断。

verified_metadata.title: Smart bearings enabled by the tribovoltaic effect and machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: The tribovoltaic effect, which directly converts mechanical energy into electricity at dynamic semiconductor interfaces, presents a novel pathway for intrinsic mechanical sensing. Here, we materialize the “surface-as-sensor” paradigm by harnessing this effect to create a self-sensing bearing. This is achieved through a spontaneously formed molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂) layer on the bearing races, which establishes dynamic Schottky contacts with the steel balls, effectively turning the bearing surface itself into the sensing element. Mechanical friction at these interfaces directly generates a continuous stream of real-time electrical signals via the tribovoltaic effect. We analyze the underlying mechanism of this effect within the dynamic bearing system and demonstrate that the magnitude and characteristics of the resulting tribovoltaic outputs are intrinsically modulated by operational conditions, serving as highly sensitive and direct fingerprints of rotational speed and load. By employing explainable machine learning and deep learning to decode these signals, we achieve accurate monitoring of operational states, such as rotation speed, with the identification accuracy exceeding 96%, and further demonstrate its capability in early fault diagnosis. This work successfully establishes the tribovoltaic effect as a practical and powerful sensing mechanism, validating the “surface-as-sensor” concept as a pathway to a new generation of embedded, self-sensing intelligent machinery.

title: Machine-learning assisted decoupling of strain and temperature via an antagonistic sensing ionic elastomer

verified_metadata.title: Machine-learning assisted decoupling of strain and temperature via an antagonistic sensing ionic elastomer
verified_metadata.abstract: The simultaneous perception of multiple physical stimuli is essential for intelligent soft robotics and personalized healthcare. However, the concurrent detection of strain and temperature is fundamentally hindered by signal crosstalk, which compromises accuracy and reliability. Existing solutions, often relying on heterogeneous integration or intricate circuitry, inevitably sacrifice mechanical stability and scalability. Here, we introduce a sensing paradigm that leverages intrinsic material properties to achieve physical signal orthogonality. We design a solvent-free ion-conductive elastomer that exhibits antagonistic electrical responses to strain and temperature: its resistance increases but capacitance decreases upon stretching, whereas both resistance and capacitance increase with heating. This inherent signal decoupling stems from distinct ion migration and interfacial polarization mechanisms under mechanical and thermal stimuli. To translate this orthogonal relationship into precise quantitative readings, we employ a random forest regression model that directly maps the coupled resistance-capacitance signals to strain and temperature values, bypassing the need for complex analytical inversion. Our sensor achieves high-fidelity decoding, with determination coefficients of 0.90 for strain and 0.94 for temperature. It also maintains robust performance over 300 stretching cycles. We further demonstrate its practical utility in a firefighter safety warning system that simultaneously monitors body motion and detects extreme heat exposure. This work establishes a material-centric and algorithm-powered roadmap for multi perception, paving the way for high-fidelity sensing in complex environments.

verified_metadata.title: A unified kinetic Monte Carlo and Bayesian optimization framework for the circular design of poly(methyl methacrylate): From synthesis to recycling
verified_metadata.abstract: Polymer recycling is a significant challenge in the development of sustainable materials, motivating the design of strategies that balance recyclability with performance. Here, we present a unified method that links an integrated kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) model with a Bayesian optimization routine to determine synthesis conditions for poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) that balance recyclability with target molecular weight requirements. Validated against experimental benchmarks, the model explicitly correlates synthesis conditions with microstructural defects and subsequent depolymerization kinetics. Mechanistic analysis reveals that aggressive synthesis conditions increase polymerization process and defect density, which hinders depolymerization process and may yield polymer too short chains for practical application. To address this, we developed an autonomous three-dimensional optimization routine that efficiently navigates the design space, identifying a synthesis protocol that minimizes the total processing time while maintaining target molar mass strictly. This work establishes an effective, data-driven methodology for the rational design of closed-loop recycling polymers.

verified_metadata.title: Strong dipole-dipole interaction-enhanced dual-network piezoelectric hydrogels for long-term pulse monitoring and machine learning-based object recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Flexible piezoelectric hydrogel skins are promising for wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction and soft robotics. However, their application faces a critical challenge in reconciling tissue-level compliance with bias-free, high-SNR, and environment-resilient outputs, while simultaneously circumventing the need for bulky power supplies. Here we introduce a dual-network PAAM/PVDF-TrFE hydrogel via solvent-exchange processing that promotes β phase formation and dipole-dipole alignment, enabling mechanically robust piezoelectric skins. The resulting sensors exhibit linearity within the range of 1–600 kPa, with sensitivities of 2.76 mV·kPa−1 below 280 kPa and 1.11 mV·kPa−1 in the secondary regime above 280 kPa, while demonstrating fast response and recovery times (43 ms and 63 ms, respectively) and robust cyclic stability over 6500 cycles. Functionally, the sensors can decode finger-joint and facial micro-movements, precisely resolve arterial pulse waveforms (P1/P2/P3), and drive a five-pad array for object recognition using a lightweight RBF-SVM. By bridging molecular dipole alignment with machine-learning, this materials-to-algorithms platform advances the frontier of bias-free, self-powered sensing and low-power human-machine interfaces, showing significant potential for multi-element arrays and soft-robotic manipulation.

verified_metadata.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is primarily diagnosed based on clinical symptoms, reflecting the absence of reliable molecular markers. Although cortisol has been implicated in MDD, its clinical relevance remains unclear, partly due to reliance on single time-point measurements that overlook circadian dynamics. Here, we develop an iontronic platform that enables sensitive profiling of salivary cortisol and permits systematic evaluation of its diurnal variation. The sensing strategy integrates aptamer-based molecular recognition with a transcription-driven amplification pathway, converting weak cortisol-binding events into measurable modulation of ion transport under nanoconfinement, achieving a detection limit of 3.4 pM. Using this approach, we analyzed cortisol rhythms in healthy individuals and patients with MDD. In addition to elevated basal levels, MDD patients exhibited markedly increased diurnal amplitude, indicating disrupted neuroendocrine rhythmicity. Notably, dynamic features of cortisol fluctuation provided substantially greater discriminatory power than static concentration values. When combined with basic clinical parameters and evaluated using a support vector machine model, these rhythm-based signatures enabled reliable differentiation between MDD and control groups. These findings identify amplified diurnal cortisol fluctuation as a quantifiable neuroendocrine phenotype of MDD. Rather than emphasizing absolute hormone levels, this work highlights temporal dysregulation as a potential molecular marker and provides a noninvasive framework for objective neuroendocrine assessment in psychiatric research.

title: Dynamic aggregation control via machine learning-integrated PBM for minimizing impurity entrapment

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。机器学习从原位显微图像提取晶体团聚分形维数，耦合PBM动态控制杂质包埋。

verified_metadata.title: Dynamic aggregation control via machine learning-integrated PBM for minimizing impurity entrapment
verified_metadata.abstract: The achievable purity in crystallization is limited by a multiscale structural transition, where loose aggregates densify into bridged agglomerates that readily entrap impurities. A specialized machine learning model applied to in situ microscopy images yields a time-resolved fractal dimension that quantifies the evolving morphology of crystal aggregates and serves as a descriptor of their structural state. We embed this descriptor into a turbulence-informed breakage formulation for crystal aggregates and couple it with the system's aggregation and breakage dynamics, defining a multiscale framework that identifies the structural threshold at which loose aggregates transition into bridged, impurity-entrapping agglomerates. Building on this mechanism, we develop the Morphology–Evolution-informed Purity Strategy (MEPS), which identifies an extraction window before the formation of bridged agglomerates, thereby yielding crystals formed from loose aggregates that readily release entrapped mother liquor, in contrast to the several-fold higher retention of mother liquor observed at later extraction times. This approach provides a mechanistic basis for determining optimal extraction timing, offering a practical route for suppressing impurity entrapment in crystallization processes.

verified_metadata.title: Ag nanowire-embedded core (PS)-shell (PVDF) nanofibers for high-performance triboelectric nanogenerators and artificial intelligence-driven material recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Over the past decade, extensive research has focused on surface engineering and multi-layer approaches to enhance the contact electrification and electrostatic induction of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). However, most of these techniques involve time-consuming, multi-step fabrication processes, highlighting the need for innovative approaches. In this study, we introduce a core-shell nanofiber (NF) architecture composed of a polystyrene (PS) core embedded with silver nanowires (Ag NWs) and a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) shell. This core (PS/Ag)-shell (PVDF) structure significantly enhanced both charge trapping and β-phase induction. Systematic optimization demonstrated that embedding 0.04 vol% Ag NWs into the PS core increased the average peak-to-peak voltage to 319.9 V, representing a 94.3% enhancement compared with pristine core-shell NFs. Comprehensive analysis confirmed that the core-loaded structure outperformed its shell-loaded counterpart because the spatial confinement of Ag NWs within the PS core, together with shielding by the PVDF shell, enhanced charge storage and suppressed leakage current. The core–shell structure also exhibited faster charge accumulation, which is particularly advantageous in applications where external mechanical work is supplied momentarily. Finally, a model trained on triboelectric voltage data achieved 98.3% classification accuracy for five distinct materials, highlighting the potential of this self-powered TENG sensor for intelligent material recognition.

title: Sense, think, and robot control: Multimodal material recognition sensing integrated with large language model reasoning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。LLM推理融合多模态传感完成材料识别并控制机器人，属于实体机器人工程。

verified_metadata.title: Sense, think, and robot control: Multimodal material recognition sensing integrated with large language model reasoning
verified_metadata.abstract: Touch is fundamental to human material perception, involving diverse receptors and complex cognitive processing. However, existing studies are often limited to single-modal sensing and stop at recognizing material type. In this work, multimodal sensing is integrated with a large language model (LLM) to improve material recognition accuracy and enable deeper thinking. The proposed compact flexible multimodal sensor can simultaneously acquire pressure, thermal, and dielectric signals, achieving an overall recognition accuracy of up to 99.13% across 23 representative materials. Based on the recognition results and task requirements, the LLM generates robot control decisions. Augmented reality (AR) provides system visualization and user control, enabling intuitive human–robot interaction. This system demonstrates intelligent robotic sorting driven by material recognition in real-world scenarios and may inspire the application of multimodal sensors in embodied intelligence.

title: Niobium doping enables durable Ni-rich layered cathodes through interfacial and morphological stabilization with data-driven performance validation
abstract: The addition of a small amount of niobium oxide during the synthesis of Nb-modified 9-series Ni-rich layered oxides yields multiple beneficial effects. These include suppression of aluminum segregation from the precursor, refinement of primary particle size within dense spherical secondary particles, mitigation of oxygen release during electrochemical cycling, and reduced structural changes associated with the H2–H3 phase transition at voltages up to 4.3 V vs. Li|Li + . The optimized Nb-doped material with 0.5 mol% Nb addition demonstrates excellent rate capability and improved cycling stability, achieving 85.3% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C, even for electrodes with a high active-material mass loading of approximately 8.5 mg cm −2 . The role of Nb in structural and electrochemical stabilization is elucidated using operando X-ray diffraction, ex situ soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and complementary microscopy studies. In addition, a gated recurrent unit-based approach enables effective prediction of long-term cycling stability. Overall, this strategy demonstrates a viable pathway toward stabilizing high-energy Ni-rich cathodes while accelerating performance assessment for practical lithium-ion battery applications.

title: Integrating experiments, numerical simulations and Bayesian optimisation to maximise drug permeability of hollow pyramidal microneedle arrays
abstract: This study presents an experimental–numerical framework integrated with Bayesian optimisation (BO) for the design of hollow pyramidal microneedle (MN) arrays to enhance transdermal drug permeability across the skin. Finite element (FE) simulations have been carried out to model coupled fluid flow and drug delivery in multilayered skin, including convection–diffusion of the drug in HMN and fluid slip condition at fluid (MN tip)–skin (porous) interfaces. The geometric design parameters, including lumen diameter, array pitch, and needle count, have been optimised using a Gaussian process–based BO (GP-BO) framework implemented in Python via the scikit-learn library. Experimental validation has been performed using hollow microneedle (HMN) arrays loaded with ibuprofen (IBU) sodium, applied to ex vivo neonatal porcine skin in Franz diffusion cell setups. Drug permeation has been subsequently quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. The results revealed that approximately 150 μg (≈3%) of the administered drug permeated into the receptor compartment after 24-h, whereas 295.79 ± 148.95 μg remained within the dermal layers, indicating prolonged drug retention and effective localised delivery. The integrated BO methodology significantly improved permeability predictions while minimising computational costs, resulting in optimal HMN geometries that maximised both volumetric flow rate and transdermal permeability. The improvement in performance represents around 5% enhancement over the previously optimised configuration, demonstrating both the effectiveness and robustness of the BO framework.

verified_metadata.title: A digital twin framework for predictive modeling of liver-on-a-chip system dynamics using limited experimental data
verified_metadata.abstract: This study presents a data-efficient digital twin framework for a liver-on-a-chip (LoC) integrated optical biosensor platform that integrates a computational microfluidics solver with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) model to predict doxorubicin-induced hepatotoxicity. A learning-based model discrepancy term, trained on glutathione S-transferase alpha (GST-α) release as a biomarker, corrects structural mismatches and aligns simulations with measurements. The microfluidics module computes steady, incompressible, laminar velocity fields and transient advection-diffusion-reaction of drugs and oxygen, providing spatiotemporal concentration profiles that inform the PBPK-PD compartments. A hybrid uncertainty quantification approach, combining Bayesian inference to calibrate transport and kinetic parameters from sparse data with an XGBoost discrepancy model that captures residual bias, estimates posterior predictive intervals that account for both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. The calibrated twin reproduces time-resolved GST-α trajectories at various dose levels, with observed responses falling within the posterior intervals. For the high-dose doxorubicin condition (20 μM), the predicted GST-α concentration shows a relative deviation of about 9% for the 2D model and 5–6% for the 3D model compared to the filtered experimental measurements. The learned discrepancy extends to previously unseen drug concentrations, enabling conservative extrapolation within quantified uncertainty bounds. Overall, the framework addresses common issues of data scarcity and model-experiment mismatch in organ-on-a-chip studies, informing preclinical decision-making for drug safety and toxicity assessments.

verified_metadata.title: Smart thrust bearing with integrated discharge-based energy harvesting and deep-learning fault detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising energy harvesting devices that convert wasted energy into electrical energy from ambient environments, especially in the form of friction. However, they have a few drawbacks, such as low output and severe wear. To address these drawbacks, we adopt a phenomenon known as electric discharge. Rotation is a representative input form for mechanical components, and we are inspired by a thrust bearing structure for generating our TENG as bearings are widely used in many industries and are constantly rotating. In this paper, a thrust ball bearing TENG (TBB-TENG) is proposed. The TBB-TENG exhibits characteristic patterns on the stator by modifying its surface to induce an electric discharge and ultimately enhance the output. Additionally, a mechanical stability analysis is performed theoretically in response to the modification. Furthermore, parametric studies are conducted to optimize the proposed TBB-TENG. Finally, we present the practical use of TBB-TENG as a self-powered defect diagnosis sensor using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), demonstrating its high accuracy.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven discovery of targeted CuM nanoparticles on 2D CuBa for CO2 fixation: Synergistic effects of ionic liquids in C–C/N coupling
verified_metadata.abstract: Revealing the mechanism of CO2 electroreduction (CO2R) to multicarbon (C2+) products remains challenging, especially at the complex electrode−liquid interface and under potential-dependent energy conditions. This study presents comprehensive density functional theory calculations and data-driven screening of CO2R to ethylene and acetamide over Cu-based bimetallic nanoparticles (NPs) loaded on a CuBa surface. Given that 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate ([Bmim][BF4]) can promote local enrichment and activation of CO2 under potential-dependent energy conditions and achieve efficient CO2R, 25 electric double layer models were constructed using CuBa@CuM NP catalysts and [Bmim][BF4] ionic liquid (IL) in an acidic explicit solvent microenvironment. The Gibbs free energy profile for each proton-coupled electron transfer process of CO2 was calculated via potential-dependent energy integration, with the IL solvent model considered under a constant potential. First CO2 is reduced to CO, after which C–C coupling can occur in *CO–*CHO and *CO–*COH or during *CO direct dimerization toward ethylene synthesis, while C–N coupling in *CCO–*NH3 is most feasibly favored toward acetamide synthesis. CuZr, CuPd, CuPt, and CuBi NPs loaded on CuBa demonstrated outstanding activity, with limiting potential (UL) values of −1.27, −1.21, −1.28, and −1.37 V, respectively, which were smaller than those of other catalysts used in ethylene and acetamide synthesis. Then, based on structural, thermodynamic, and electronic calculations, various quantitative indicators of the structure–activity relationship were established, such as correlations between Bader charge transfer and the binding energy of the intermediate, d-band center difference, and UL of the maximum free energy change step. These results were quantitatively related to CO2R reaction activity through key species interactions and electronic property descriptors. Furthermore, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations were performed in the NVT ensemble at 300 K for 10 ps to estimate CO2 activation over different CuBa@CuM NP catalysts, including the radial distribution function, coordination number of O–H, bond length (C=O), and bond angle (OCO) variations in the CO2 molecule. Finally, various machine learning models were adopted to predict the optimal UL of CO2R to ethylene in a Python3 environment. The coefficient of determination and mean absolute error were employed to evaluate model performance, with values of 0.92 and 0.16 for the extreme gradient boosting model, respectively, indicating its optimal ability to predict catalytic activity. By combining high-performance computing and big data screening for complex catalytic reaction mechanisms, the study provides a better understanding of the catalytic process and offers guidance for future catalyst design for C2+ product synthesis via CO2R.

verified_metadata.title: Capacity prediction of cobalt nickel phosphide supercapacitors based on machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Nickel cobalt phosphide (NiCoP) has emerged as a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its strong redox activity, high conductivity, low cost, and excellent chemical/thermal stability. This study proposes a high-precision hybrid machine learning model, CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks)-BiGRU(Bidirectional gated recurrent unit)-Attention model, for predicting the capacitance of NiCoP-based electrode materials. The dataset consists of 803 experimental instances with 9 input parameters: Ni and Co molar ratios, morphology, specific surface area, current collector, electrolyte concentration, potential window, current density and the output parameter of the supercapacitors' capacity. The relationship between material composition, microstructure, electrochemical properties, and capacitance was successfully fitted. After normalization, R2, RMSE, and MAE values of the CNN-BiGRU-Attention algorithm reach 0.98, 0.021, and 0.18, respectively, demonstrating exceptional model accuracy and fitting capability. The generalization ability of the model was verified through experiments with a mean relative error of 9.20%, indicating remarkable stability and reliability. Furthermore, a novel NiCoP electrode material with a nonstoichiometric ratio of Ni1.3Co0.55P was screened out by searching the space generation method, which exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 2263.3 F/g at a current density of 1 A/g. This work provides an innovative and effective method for predicting NiCoP performance, while significantly optimizing of multicomponent phosphide-based supercapacitors with enhanced specific capacitance.

verified_metadata.title: An AI-guided framework for discovery and evolution of sulfotransferases enables efficient sulfotyrosine bioproduction
verified_metadata.abstract: The discovery of efficient enzymes for specific biotransformation remains a rate-limiting step in synthetic biology, traditionally relying on laborious experimental screening. Here, we demonstrate how artificial intelligence (AI) dramatically accelerates this process by establishing a streamlined pipeline for sulfotransferase (SULT) discovery and engineering. We leveraged the deep learning model UniKP to predict enzyme kinetic parameters from protein sequences alone, enabling rapid in silico prioritization of candidate SULTs for sulfotyrosine (sTyr) synthesis. This AI-guided approach identified active enzymes with a 50% success rate from a random pool and outperformed traditional BLAST selection from a library of 1000 homologs. An AI-prioritized SULT was successfully engineered through directed evolution, yielding a variant with 7.25-fold enhanced activity while maintaining broad substrate promiscuity. When integrated into engineered Escherichia coli (E. coli), this evolved enzyme enabled high-level sTyr production (1578 μM). Our work establishes AI as a powerful tool to shortcut the enzyme discovery and optimization timeline, serving as a case study that illustrates how AI can be integrated into the rapid development of biocatalysts.

title: Multiscale pulsating intensification and wavelet entropy-driven AI optimization of fluidized biomass hydrogen production

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多尺度流动分析及小波熵深度网络优化流化生物质制氢过程。

verified_metadata.title: Multiscale pulsating intensification and wavelet entropy-driven AI optimization of fluidized biomass hydrogen production
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the issue of suboptimal hydrogen production efficiency resulting from particle agglomeration and channeling during biomass fluidized bed gasification, this paper presents a method for process intensification and prediction that integrates multiscale flow analysis with deep learning. Initially, pressure pulsation signals are decomposed using power spectral density (PSD) and wavelet transforms to identify the system's eigenfrequencies. The mechanisms by which pulsed gas flows are intensified across the micro, meso, and macroscales are examined. This involves overcoming diffusion limitations at the microscale, disrupting bubbles and particle agglomerates at the mesoscale, and enhancing bed mixing and promoting reaction equilibrium at the macroscale. Secondly, the multiscale coupling relationship between flow complexity and hydrogen yield is elucidated. The trends of wavelet flow-reaction entropy and gas yield exhibit synchronization with increasing pulsation frequency. This study establishes wavelet flow-reaction entropy as a key feature characterizing the correlation between flow complexity and reaction performance. Finally, a two-level Deep Neural Network model driven by wavelet flow-reaction entropy is developed. This model follows the flow trends of the fluidized bed system and enables the accurate prediction of hydrogen yield under various operating conditions, achieving an overall R2 of 0.969. Furthermore, the optimal pressure and pulsation frequency ranges (Zones A and B) are identified, enhances hydrogen production performance. The predicted maximum H2 yield is 12.67 mol/kg-biomass under conditions of 4.4 bar and 3.5 Hz. This study not only unveils the multiscale flow-reaction coupling mechanism underlying pulsed fluidized hydrogen production but also offers a novel theoretical foundation for the intelligent control of biomass pyrolysis gasification processes.
