verified_metadata.title: Water-induced porous MWCNT/PDMS-based triboelectric nanogenerator for small-sample machine learning-assisted hand action recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: To clarify the individual and coupled roles of multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) incorporation and water-induced porosity in triboelectric sensing and address the challenge of wearable human action recognition with limited training data, a porous MWCNT/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-based triboelectric nanogenerator (PMP-TENG) was developed. The effects of MWCNT concentration and deionized (DI) water addition on triboelectric output and pressure-sensing performance were systematically investigated. Based on the overall performance, the PMP-TENG containing 0.75 wt% MWCNTs and 12.5 wt% DI water was selected. The device operated over 3–200 kPa and exhibited normalized sensitivities of 0.0581 and 0.109 kPa−1 at 3–70 and 70–200 kPa, respectively. Comparative dielectric, mechanical, and sensing analyses showed that MWCNT incorporation enhanced dielectric polarization, output amplitude, and effective force-response range, whereas DI-water-induced porosity reduced the apparent compressive modulus, increased compressive deformability, and promoted the force-dependent evolution of the effective contact area, thereby improving low-force sensitivity and delaying response saturation. Their cooperative effects enabled the PMP-TENG to maintain relatively high triboelectric output while enhancing pressure sensitivity and sensing range. The device also exhibited frequency-independent voltage responses and stable output over more than 20,000 cycles. When mounted on the hand, multiple PMP-TENGs generated graded voltage responses to different finger and wrist movements. Using a random forest classifier, nine representative hand actions were recognized with mean test accuracies of 99.58% and 96.67% using 220 and 18 training samples, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of the PMP-TENG for self-powered pressure sensing and machine-learning-assisted hand action recognition with limited training data.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-assisted mediator-regulated copper-based nanozyme sensor array for visual on-site identification of phenolic acids
verified_metadata.abstract: While nanozyme sensor arrays are capable of simultaneously recognizing and quantifying various target analytes, boosting the catalytic activity of nanozymes to improve their sensing performance still represents a critical technical challenge. Herein, we discovered that two laccase mediators (HBT, 4-PA) with N-OH functional groups can distinctly promote the laccase-like (LAC) behavior of copper-based nanozymes (SA-Cu, TA-Cu), thus elevating the catalytic efficiency toward diverse phenolic acids (PAs). According to the above fascinating experimental findings, an innovative mediator-boosted four-channel nanozyme sensor array (2 nanozymes × 2 mediators = 4 sensing channels) was established, enabling the effective discrimination of seven PAs. Furthermore, by optimizing multiple machine learning (ML) models, the precision of the concentration-independent categorization system built on this array was boosted from 43.56% to 100%, facilitating the discrimination of unknown samples. Ultimately, with the adoption of the Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG-16) model, an intelligent sensor platform assisted by ML was additionally constructed to enhance the practicability of the recognition of PAs. The present research is not only carries great significance for promoting the recognition of PAs in complicated samples, but also opens up innovative directions for enhancing the catalytic activity of LAC nanozymes.

verified_metadata.title: DC-SVM-based analysis of responsive signals from a biomimetic olfactory sensor for assessing the effect of fatty acids odors on cardiomyocytes
verified_metadata.abstract: It is of great significance to detect fatty acids odors and assess its effect on cardiomyocytes. Herein, a biomimetic olfactory sensor was constructed using primary cardiomyocytes as biosensitive materials and the microelectrode array as the transducer for the quantitative detection of fatty acids odors. The endogenous olfactory receptor OR51E1 was verified by RT-qPCR and the immunofluorescence staining in primary cardiomyocytes. Five fatty acids odors were selected from potential ligands of OR51E1 and tested by the cardiomyocytes-based biomimetic olfactory sensor. These odors can reduce the firing signals of cardiomyocytes, including decanoic acid, 4-methylnonanoic acid, nonanoic acid, heptanoic acid and pentanoic acid. The detectable threshold concentrations of five odors were determined to be 10 μM, 40 μM, 10 μM 10 μM, 10 μM, respectively. After removing each odor, the firing signals of cardiomyocytes can recover to some extent in 12 min, the average values of the recovery rate reached 85.21%, 60.96%, 80.53%, 93.47% and 108.03%, respectively. Moreover, silencing OR51E1 of cardiomyocytes further confirmed that OR51E1 played a crucial role in the specific recognition of fatty acid odors. Different odors were successfully classified and predicted by supervised learning discrimination calculation-support vector machine (DC-SVM), with the average accuracy rate of 92.97 ± 2.42% and an average AUC of 97.64%. In conclusion, the biomimetic olfactory sensor was successfully developed for the detection and discrimination of fatty acid odors with the aid of DC-SVM, which has great prospects for the drug screening in cardiovascular diseases.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven nanozyme-enhanced microfluidic systems for pathogen diagnostics: Current status and future perspectives

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。实质综述AI赋能纳米酶微流控系统的设计和集成，用于病原体诊断。

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-driven nanozyme-enhanced microfluidic systems for pathogen diagnostics: Current status and future perspectives
verified_metadata.abstract: The diagnosis of pathogens is often challenged by their etiological diversity and overlapping clinical presentations, highlighting an urgent need for high-performance Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) platforms in resource-limited settings. To address this, microfluidic platforms provide an ideal foundation by automating complex biochemical processes at the microscale, while nanozymes—acting as stable and designable alternatives to natural enzymes—serve as powerful signal amplifiers. This review presents a comprehensive landscape of nanozyme-enhanced microfluidic systems, with a specific emphasis on the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in overcoming the inefficiencies of traditional trial-and-error design paradigms. We first classify microfluidic architectures based on their liquid propulsion mechanisms, covering continuous-flow, centrifugal, paper-based, and digital microfluidics. Subsequently, we elucidate the catalytic mechanisms of nanozymes and their diverse signal transduction pathways. Then, the discussion focuses on AI's role in empowering system design and intelligent pathogen detection, including architecture optimization, nanozyme engineering, and signal readout. Finally, we summarize current applications and future perspectives, aiming to provide a valuable reference for the development of next-generation diagnostic tools.

title: Machine-learning-assisted multistage resonant gradient-impedance metastructure for broadband, wide-angle microwave absorption and multifunctional integration
abstract: A multistage resonant gradient-impedance metastructure was fabricated by integrating PACF absorbing units, low-loss N-PA spacer layers, and a laser-induced LI-PACF lossy reflective base through fused deposition modeling, while its optimal geometric parameters were determined by machine-learning-assisted surrogate prediction and multi-objective screening. PACF provided conductive loss, dipolar polarization, and interfacial relaxation, while the N-PA layers regulated impedance transition and interlayer coupling. Meanwhile, the LI-PACF substrate, featuring enhanced surface conductivity and strengthened interfacial polarization, acted as a lossy reflective boundary for secondary attenuation. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of gradient impedance evolution and staged resonant complementarity, the optimized metastructure achieved a simulated effective absorption bandwidth of 33.8 GHz for RL < -10 dB and 24.83 GHz for RL < -20 dB at normal incidence, with a minimum reflection loss of -43.56 dB at a thickness of 14.7 mm; experimental arch-method measurements confirmed EAB proportions of 88.94% (RL < -10 dB) and 65.47% (RL < -20 dB) under TE polarization. Remarkably, under 60° TE incidence, it still retained effective absorption bandwidths of 33.01 and 17.12 GHz for RL < -10 and -20 dB, respectively. Additionally, it exhibited an average radar cross-section reduction of 23 dBsm over 2–40 GHz, together with a compressive modulus of ≈1.8 GPa, a first peak compressive strength of 129.5 MPa, and rapid deicing within 60 s at 25 V.

title: A colorimetric and photothermal dual-mode nanozyme platform: Multimodal deep learning guided real-time freshness sensing and predicting of aquatic products under challenging lighting conditions

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多模态深度学习融合颜色和光热纳米酶传感信号，在变化光照下预测水产品新鲜度。

verified_metadata.title: A colorimetric and photothermal dual-mode nanozyme platform: Multimodal deep learning guided real-time freshness sensing and predicting of aquatic products under challenging lighting conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: Timely and accurate freshness assessment of aquatic products with complex matrices remains significant challenge. Hypoxanthine (Hx)-based monitoring methods using colorimetric sensing with smartphone are widely used but affected by variable lighting conditions throughout the food supply chain, causing detection results remain inaccurate. Here, a colorimetric/photothermal dual-mode Hx detection and freshness prediction platform was constructed by cascading a thermostable 2D Fe/Ni-MOF nanosheet with xanthine oxidase, enabling stable and sensitive on-site detection of Hx. A linear response to Hx was exhibited in the range of 0.2–100 μM, with detection limits of 0.12 μM (colorimetric mode) and 4.21 μM (photothermal mode), respectively. To address ambient lighting effects, seven lighting conditions (∼50, ∼100, ∼500, ∼1000, ∼5000, ∼10,000, and ∼50,000 lx) were simulated to construct a dataset integrating lighting, colorimetric, and photothermal information for the model training and testing. A light-adaptive multimodal fusion network based on YOLOv11 and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) achieved a prediction accuracy of 98% in freshness classification, remarkably higher than that of the single colorimetric (89%) and photothermal (93%) modes, when trained on 4536 labeled images and 108 photothermal data points, demonstrating strong robustness under complex and varying lighting conditions. Coupled with the self-developed “Food Track” application, this work not only provides a practical and reliable approach for the early freshness prediction in aquatic products, but also highlights the potential of multimodal fusion algorithms to handle lighting variations in food supply chains.

title: Machine-learning assisted one-tube LAMP melting analysis for SNPs genotyping

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。XGBoost抑制环介导等温扩增熔解信号伪影并分类曲线，实现SNP基因分型。

verified_metadata.title: Machine-learning assisted one-tube LAMP melting analysis for SNPs genotyping
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) is essential for personalized medicine and infectious disease surveillance. Although loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) provides outstanding speed and sensitivity, the highly concatenated and heterogeneous structure of LAMP amplicons has historically limited reliable probe-based melting curve analysis for SNPS discrimination. Here, we present a robust LAMP–Melting platform that exploits the intrinsic “DNA breathing” dynamics of LAMP amplicons to enable allele-specific genotyping without reliance on predefined loop regions or complex strand-displacement probe designs. After isothermal amplification, transient dissociation–rehybridization fluctuations allow fluorescent probes to intermittently access nominally double-stranded target regions, generating distinct and reproducible melting fingerprints for single-base variants. Using this mechanism-driven strategy, we successfully genotyped the human MTHFR C677T polymorphism and the SARS-CoV-2 D614G mutation with high analytical sensitivity, achieving limits of detection of 1 ng/μL for gDNA and 10 RNA copies per reaction. To address the biochemical complexity and signal heterogeneity inherent to isothermal amplification products, a XGBoost–based machine-learning framework was integrated to suppress artifacts and enhance melting curve classification. Moreover, the assay exhibits excellent compatibility with lyophilized reagents and portable fluorescence detection instruments, enabling a one-pot, closed-tube workflow suitable for decentralized and point-of-care testing. Collectively, this work redefines probe–amplicon interactions in isothermal systems by shifting from static hybridization to dynamic, fluctuation-enabled recognition and establishes a versatile, mechanism-guided framework for next-generation molecular diagnostics.

verified_metadata.title: Thermofluorochromic materials via distinct mechanisms for machine learning-enhanced triple cross-validated accurate high-temperature prediction and advanced anti-counterfeiting encryption
verified_metadata.abstract: Organic thermofluorochromic materials (TFMs) hold great promise for large-area, flexible thermal indication and anti-counterfeiting, yet their utility at high temperatures is severely hindered by poor solid-state thermofluorochromism, inaccurate temperature readout, and severe thermal quenching. Herein, we report three heat-resistant TFM films based on distinct thermochromic mechanisms: stepwise stacking modulation with delayed fluorescence and nonadiabatic vibrational coupling (tBu-DHPPO), high-barrier tautomerization (HBT-TPA), and suppression of energy transfer in their hybrids (tBu-DHPPO/HBT-TPA). Leveraging their enhanced thermal robustness, these TFM films deliver outstanding thermometric performance across a wide temperature range (20–300 °C), exhibiting high maximum relative sensitivities of 2.46, 5.87 and 2.49% °C−1 above 150 °C and remarkable optimal temperature resolutions of 0.05–1.07, 0.21–1.26, and 0.05–1.01 °C, respectively. By integrating these three cross-validated TFMs with machine learning, we established a smartphone-based optical readout platform that achieves ultrahigh-accuracy temperature prediction, with a near-perfect coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.99997 and a low root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.4682 °C. Furthermore, these TFM films enable naked-eye, non-invasive thermal imaging, patterning, and anti-counterfeiting encryption under ambient conditions. These findings demonstrate a new strategy that bridges multiple robust thermofluorochromic films and accessible machine learning, paving the way for next-generation intelligent thermal reading and anti-counterfeiting systems.

verified_metadata.title: Unlocking multiscale structure-property relationships in epoxy thermosets: A machine learning-driven approach to superior multi-objective performance
verified_metadata.abstract: The strength–toughness trade-off limits the simultaneous enhancement of mechanical and bonding properties in epoxy resins, while traditional trial-and-error approaches yield only incremental improvements with low efficiency and fail to decipher the underlying structure–property relationships. Herein, an integrated data-driven multiscale paradigm was proposed to address the above challenges, which integrates experimental design, machine learning, and multi-objective optimization. Through systematic formulation design, precise control over the phase-separated domain sizes of epoxy thermosets with polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane-capped poly(ε-caprolactone)s (POSS-PCLn) was achieved across nearly three orders of magnitude, spanning from nano- to submicro- and micro-scales, thereby constructing a high-quality dataset. By combining interpretable machine learning with multi-objective optimization, phase-separated domains in the 100–600 nm range were identified for the first time as optimal for toughening. Moreover, POSS-PCLn synergistically improved bonding strength through a combination of toughening and interfacial compatibility mechanisms. Guided by these mechanistic insights, enabling maximum bonding strength of 40.1 MPa (47% improvement) and maximum fracture toughness of 1.74 MPa·m1/2 (145% improvement), the formulation with optimally balanced performance simultaneously achieved fracture toughness of 1.31 MPa m1/2, tensile strength of 73.6 MPa, and bonding strength of 31.7 MPa, outperforming most reported epoxy systems in terms of both single-property extremes and comprehensive performance. This integrated paradigm not only elucidates the multiscale structure–property relationships, but also achieves significant performance enhancement, providing a generalizable strategy for the rational design of high-performance polymers.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven prediction of organic rejection in forward osmosis: Incorporating hydrophobic and dynamic transport effects
verified_metadata.abstract: The high toxicity and persistence of anthropogenic organic compounds (AOCs) in water environments pose a serious threat to water body environmental safety, which has become an urgent problem to be solved in current wastewater treatment. However, due to the limitations of the forward osmosis (FO) membrane itself and the physicochemical properties of the water environment, as well as the limited experimental data set, accurately predicting and regulating the non-linear transport behavior of these organic compounds still faces significant challenges. To solve this problem, we deployed a TabPFN-2.5 framework, which leverages a prior-trained Transformer architecture for zero-shot tabular inference, evaluated on an experimental FO dataset (N = 616). The test results demonstrate superior performance compared to the integrated model (test R2 = 0.90, RMSE = 6.90%), significantly reducing the burden of empirical parameterization. More importantly, this study has also constructed a multi-level interpretable machine learning architecture to quantitatively decouple the boundary between molecular size exclusion and electrostatic repulsion: there is a S-shaped spatial steric hindrance threshold at 210–220 Da for molecules, and a critical electrostatic barrier failure point occurs when the Zeta potential is close to −4 mV. Through high-throughput virtual screening, the study establishes a multi-objective Pareto-optimal frontier for balancing water flux and rejection rate, providing practical operational benchmarks for advanced FO systems. This work bridges the gap between machine learning-based abstract representations and conventional membrane physics mechanisms, offering a systematic methodological reference for data-driven design of highly selective forward osmosis membranes.

verified_metadata.title: Anti-swelling Janus hydrogels enable long-term muscle fatigue monitoring via machine learning-assisted signal analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Water-induced adhesion failure and swelling compromise the viability of conventional hydrogel electrodes for long-term muscle fatigue monitoring under dynamic and humid conditions. To address these limitations, we report an anti-swelling Janus hydrogel with an asymmetric architecture that simultaneously ensures robust interfacial adhesion and high signal fidelity. The design comprises an adhesive layer of acrylic acid (AA) and lauryl methacrylate (LMA) copolymer with incorporated poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and a non-adhesive layer of pure PVA. Freezing initiates PVA microcrystallization to form the primary network, while subsequent heat annealing further densifies microcrystal formation at the interface. Crucially, the synergistic hydrophobic association and dense physical cross-linking restrict the swelling ratio to below 7% to prevent network dilution. The dynamic hydrogen bonding yields a robust interfacial adhesion of 67 kPa on skin to minimize motion artifacts. This dual stability directly translates into an exceptional initial signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 31 dB (versus 22 dB for commercial alternatives) and a sustained SNR of 25 dB even after a 30-day immersion period. When coupled with a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree algorithm, the acquired signals support autonomous muscle fatigue classification with 92.6% accuracy. This anti-swelling Janus strategy establishes a reliable material-algorithm interface for long-term wearable electromyography.

title: Multilevel optimization for integrated CO2 capture systems under techno-policy transitions
abstract: Membrane CO 2 capture processes are an environmentally benign and low-carbon option removing CO 2 from major point sources. However, the subambient pressure of CO 2 product typically requires energy intensive liquefaction for transportation, utilization, or storage. Consequently, the optimal CO 2 purity and recovery from the membrane process cannot be determined without considering the downstream liquefaction process, highlighting the need for integrated optimization. This study proposes a two-level nested optimization framework for an integrated CO 2 membrane separation and liquefaction process treating approximately 40,000 Nm 3 /h of flue gas originating from natural gas combined cycle. At the upper level, the optimized CO 2 purity and recovery from the membrane process were determined. At the lower level, a deterministic global solver optimizes the membrane superstructure and a Bayesian optimization algorithm optimizes the liquefaction process. The framework optimizes the integrated process under six current and future scenarios involving advanced membrane properties and carbon emission penalties. This optimization simultaneously determines scenario dependent CO 2 recovery and purity by evaluating technoeconomic tradeoffs between membrane specific selectivity and permeability and liquefaction process cost. The results show that the economically optimal membrane purity and recovery points shift with carbon emission penalties and membrane properties. With the optimum futuristic membrane scenario at a carbon emission penalty of 160 USD/t-CO2, the membrane process achieves 93.0% CO2 purity and 77.7% CO2 recovery. The integrated process recovers 72.3% of the CO2 in the flue gas. This represents a significant shift toward higher CO 2 recovery compared to the current baseline of 93.2% purity and 20.0% recovery in the membrane process under near-term membranes. Futuristic membranes reduce the total annualized cost by 4.5–8.6% compared to near-term benchmark scenario. This proposed two-level nested optimization framework provides essential insights for designing integrated capture processes as technology and policy evolve.

verified_metadata.title: An AI-driven, de novo designed all-in-one nanoplatform for cold tumor therapy
verified_metadata.abstract: Most tumors, such as > 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and > 50% of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), are immunosuppressive, which are known as cold tumors and derive little benefit from emerging therapies. A photodynamic nanoparticle JFCN was developed to enable cold tumors to profit by immunotherapy, targeted extracellular matrix (ECM) modulation, and photodynamic therapy (PDT) simultaneously. To be more effective in forming three-component nanoparticle, an AI-driven-designed programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) inhibitor J30 was customized efficiently to self-assemble with photosensitizer Ce6 and fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor UAMC-1110. Contributed to passive targeting of nanoparticle and active targeting of FAP & PD-L1, JFCN demonstrated precise accumulation at the tumor site and achieved robust inhibition of tumor growth (TGI > 85%) in both orthotopic 4 T1 TNBC model and PADC model (co-implanting Panc02+ NIH3T3 cells). The extracellular matrix (ECM) was remolded by reducing FAP, TGF-β and CXCL12, accompanied with photodynamic-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) effect, which promoted the infiltration of oxygen and T cells, thereby facilitating PDT and immunotherapy. In addition, JFCN effectively counteracts the upregulation of PD-L1 induced by PDT to overcome adaptive immune resistance. Overall, JFCN, an AI-driven, de novo designed all-in-one nanoplatform, provides a new sight for the refractory cold tumor.

verified_metadata.title: Customized MXene integrated Janus membrane for energy-efficient machine learning-assisted sensing and personal microenvironment management
verified_metadata.abstract: Smart textiles for personal microenvironment management face a fundamental trilemma: integrating multimodal sensing, active thermal regulation, and autonomous energy supply without compromising breathability or skin comfort. Conventional additive strategies, such as layer stacking or patching, inevitably lead to interfacial failure, pore occlusion, and heavy reliance on rigid batteries. We bypass these constraints by functionally decoupling these roles across a tri-layered asymmetric Janus nanofibrous membrane, MXene-assisted Janus smart cloth (MJSC). Fabricated via sequential electrospinning, MJSC features a hydrophobic (129°)-to-hydrophilic (26°) gradient that actively pumps sweat unidirectionally while maintaining high air permeability (53.482 cm3 m−2 d−1 Pa−1). By spatially partitioning MXene and partially oxidized MXene (MXO, primarily MXene nanosheet/rutile composites), we engineer an optical asymmetry that enables passive radiative cooling (reflecting up to 91% of the solar spectrum and absorbing up to 96% of the atmospheric window) while capturing energy via a moisture-responsive ionic core. This architecture eliminates external power dependencies by harvesting triboelectric and moisture-electric energy, delivering self-powered signals that a convolutional neural network classifies with over 99% accuracy. Furthermore, the MXO-enriched surface provides photocatalytic self-cleaning, removing over 80% of methylene blue from water within 2 h. MJSC provides a material paradigm for next-generation wearables prioritising both capability and physiological comfort.

title: Active learning-driven optimization and pilot-scale validation of a composite-bed vacuum pressure swing adsorption process for ultra-deep CO removal from hydrogen

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。主动学习优化复合床VPSA脱除氢中CO的热力学动力学参数，并进行中试验证。

verified_metadata.title: Active learning-driven optimization and pilot-scale validation of a composite-bed vacuum pressure swing adsorption process for ultra-deep CO removal from hydrogen
verified_metadata.abstract: While vacuum pressure swing adsorption (VPSA) provides a simple and energy-efficient route for removing trace CO from hydrogen to produce high-purity H2 for fuel cell applications, the coupling of kinetic and thermodynamic effects under multi-component competitive adsorption compromises adsorbent bed utilization and separation efficiency. Herein, an active learning-assisted strategy was proposed for optimizing the VPSA process by decoupling thermodynamic and kinetic parameters to achieve ultra-deep CO removal (<0.05 ppmv) from a multi-component gas mixture (N2/CH4/CO/CO2/Ar/H2). A new optimized composite bed consisting of activated carbon, zeolite 13×, and zeolite 5 A was explored to enhance adsorption performance using an artificial neural network model. The reliability of the model was further validated through dynamic adsorption and four-bed VPSA experiments on a pilot scale, in which CO was successfully reduced to below 0.062 ppmv from mixture gas containing 1000 ppmv CO. To further clarify the influence of the other impurities, a six-bed VPSA model was established, and active learning was employed to optimize the operating parameters for evaluating CO separation performance. Based on further multi-objective optimization, a simulation of purified gas with CO less than 0.05 ppmv was achieved under pilot-scale multi-component competitive adsorption conditions. This study provides an effective strategy for the production of fuel cell-grade hydrogen from complex gas mixtures.

title: AI-enhanced superior bionic skin with dual-layer nanofiber membranes for sweat-based multiple biomarker detection
abstract: Wearable smart sweat sensors hold promise for non-invasive health monitoring, but existing devices often face issues with user discomfort and inefficient sweat collection. Herein, we present a novel sandwich-structured bionic skin with dual-layer nanofibers integrating multifunctional detection of glucose, lactate, uric acid, Na + , K + , NH₄ + , skin impedance, and temperature. Fabricated via thermal transfer printing and zone-specific localized compression, the device reduces production time and cost. The inner polyacrylonitrile (PAN/F127) layer enhances sweat absorption, achieving over 8× faster absorption than microchannels, while the outer polydimethylsiloxane (PVB/PDMS) layer provides waterproofing, radiative cooling, and antifouling, ensuring comfort and enzymatic stability. The sensor exhibits high sensitivity, selectivity, and retains over 84% performance after nine days. Integration with a redesigned Deep Learning Continuous Analyte Monitoring with Real-time Engagement (D-CARE) system, featuring two flexible circuits and a deep learning attenuation correction algorithm, enables precise real-time monitoring and health anomaly alerting. In situ exercise tests confirm continuous, accurate physiological monitoring, advancing personalized healthcare with a reliable, user-friendly wearable platform.

verified_metadata.title: Rheological confinement-enabled micro-topological 3D textile triboelectric pressure sensor array for AI-assisted gait monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: Existing 3D textile-based self-powered pressure sensors often suffer from performance degradation during long-term service, largely limited by porous interface delamination and liquid-phase conductive percolation. To address this, we developed a warp-knitted spacer fabric-based triboelectric pressure sensor (WTPS) and smart insole (WTPS-Insole) via an integrated in-situ coating strategy, ensuring electromechanical stability and lightweight characteristics. By suppressing graphene percolation via polymer rheological confinement, a robust liquid-solid conductive network was constructed, simultaneously inducing a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) micro-topological triboelectric layer. This architecture drastically elevates the mechanical robustness, under a 50% compressive strain, the optimized device (at a 65% filling ratio) withstands an ultra-high load of 1416.33 N, representing a 100-fold enhancement. Meanwhile, the WTPS exhibits remarkable environmental adaptability, maintaining up to 98% performance recovery after rigorous washing cycles. Furthermore, a 20-unit smart insole sustained 8000 mechanical cycles with less than 5% thickness loss. The sensing array features ultrafast response and recovery times of 93 ms and 45 ms, respectively. It stably captures signals from conventional gaits (walking, jogging, jumping) and complex spatial maneuvers, including standing-sitting-squatting transitions and 180° turns. By coupling the sensory signals with machine learning algorithms, the system achieves highly accurate predictions of seven distinct locomotive states. Ultimately, this integrated fabrication strategy highlights the immense potential of 3D textile-based self-powered sensors for gait recognition, laying a robust empirical foundation for next-generation wearable sports and health monitoring systems.

title: Sustainable bioconversion of food waste and waste cooking oil into Sophorolipids: Process optimisation using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Network–Genetic Algorithm (ANN-GA)
abstract: Sophorolipids (SLs) are eco-friendly biosurfactants with broad industrial applications. However, their market competitiveness against conventional fossil-based surfactants is often limited by high production costs associated with first-generation feedstocks. To address this issue, this study investigated the synergistic co-utilisation of food waste hydrolysate (FWH) and waste cooking oil (WCO) as the sole carbon sources for lactonic SL production. Notably, FWH outperformed pure glucose in lactonic SL synthesis, and its available free amino nitrogen (FAN) level was enough for the bioprocess, reducing reliance on external nitrogen supplementation. Furthermore, response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural network–genetic algorithm (ANN-GA) models were developed to optimise key fermentation parameters, and their predictive performance was compared. Results showed that, among the tested optimisation routes, the ANN-GA model trained on the extended dataset achieved the lowest optimum-point validation error, with a relative error of 3.7% between the predicted (56.4 g/L) and actual (54.4 g/L) lactonic SL titres. In contrast, ANN-GA trained only on the restricted RSM dataset showed a much higher error (62.5%), highlighting the importance of dataset size in AI-assisted bioprocess optimisation. This study not only demonstrated the full replacement of first-generation carbon sources with waste streams for sustainable biosurfactant production, but also provides broader methodological insights into the integration of experimental data and ANN-GA for complex bioprocess optimisation.

verified_metadata.title: Dual electromagnetic enhancement engineering of hybrid Au film–poly(ionic liquid) nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere–Au nanosphere substrates integrated with machine learning algorithm for ultrasensitive SERS detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a promising trace detection technique, yet its practical application in environmental pollutant analysis remains severely restricted by insufficient electromagnetic enhancement and weak adsorption capacity toward target analytes. Herein, a novel hybrid SERS substrate with dual electromagnetic enhancement and highly efficient molecular enrichment was facilely fabricated, featuring a hierarchical structure of Au film–poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere–Au nanosphere. In this system, the waveguide optical modes of the Au film–PIL nanohole–SiO2 nanosphere structure induce the primary electromagnetic enhancement, while Au nanospheres are precisely positioned in the primary enhancement regions to deliver a secondary electromagnetic enhancement through localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), thereby realizing a high enhancement factor of 2.35 × 107 for pyrene. Meanwhile, PIL nanoholes facilitate specific adsorption and enrichment of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) within hotspots via the hydrophobic effect and π-π stacking interactions, significantly amplifying the SERS response of analytes. The hybrid substrate exhibits excellent analytical performance, with limits of detection (LODs) as low as 5.33 × 10−10 mol/L for pyrene and 3.97 × 10−10 mol/L for anthracene, respectively. Furthermore, a combined principal component analysis (PCA) and support vector machine (SVM) algorithm was employed to efficiently extract spectral features and reduce data dimensionality, achieving a prediction accuracy exceeding 94% for varying concentrations and species of PAHs in actual river water samples. Taken together, the combination of this hybrid SERS substrate and the PCA-SVM algorithm provides a novel sensing platform, enabling ultrasensitive, accurate, and intelligent trace-level detection of environmental pollutants in complex matrices.

verified_metadata.title: A biosafe nano-antimicrobial composite hydrogel sensor for penile erection monitoring and AI-assisted diagnosis
verified_metadata.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is a prevalent male sexual disorder that often requires nocturnal penile tumescence (NPT) monitoring to differentiate psychogenic from organic ED. However, conventional NPT systems are limited by poor comfort and inadequate suitability for long-term monitoring. Herein, this study developed a wearable penile tumescence (PT) sensor based on a hydrogel, termed PGTBA, for wearable NPT monitoring and auxiliary ED assessment. The hydrogel was fabricated through a freeze–thaw-induced physical crosslinking strategy, forming a porous multicomponent network with electrical conductivity, stretchability, toughness, and intrinsic reprocessability. As a resistive strain sensor, PGTBA exhibited stable electromechanical responses over a broad strain range (0–130%) with a gauge factor of 3.006, together with cyclic stability and deformation tolerance. The sensor enabled real-time monitoring of human motions. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated favorable cytocompatibility, antibacterial activity, and biosafety. Specially PGTBA supported the survival of L929 fibroblast cells while inhibiting the growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. In a penile tumescence–detumescence simulation model, the ring-shaped PGTBA sensor generated resistance-response patterns corresponding to normal erection and different ED subtypes. Integrated with support vector machine and XGBoost algorithms, preliminary erectile-state classification was achieved for noninvasive screening and intelligent male reproductive-health management.

title: Generative AI-guided conductive carbon-network regulation in heterogeneous carbon–ceramic composites for transient energy dissipation
abstract: Advanced pulsed-energy systems require dielectric materials that can dissipate transient electrical energy rapidly while resisting localized failure. Carbon–ceramic composites represent a typical heterogeneous ceramic dielectric in which conductive carbon networks, insulating ceramic skeletons and pores coexist across different length scales and jointly govern energy-dissipation behavior. However, carbon aggregation and nonuniform conductive-network distributions readily form locally percolated low-resistance pathways, causing current crowding, localized Joule heating and premature thermomechanical degradation. Such multiscale heterogeneity makes conventional trial-and-error optimization inefficient and also challenges generic data-driven models, which often fail to preserve phase occupancy, conductive connectivity and physical-response consistency under limited characterization data. Here, we propose a generative AI-guided framework for conductive carbon-network regulation in heterogeneous carbon–ceramic composites. A multiphase pseudo-RGB tensor encoding strategy is first developed to represent the carbon phase, ceramic skeleton and pore phase within a unified physically interpretable feature space. A WGAN-GP model constrained by physical-statistical descriptors is then used to expand the microstructure design space while preserving carbon fraction, spatial uniformity and agglomeration characteristics. A phase-field-informed optimization model further redistributes highly agglomerated carbon regions toward more uniform and multibranched conductive networks under mass-conservation, interfacial-regularization and spatial-smoothness constraints. Electrothermal–mechanical simulations and pulse-impact experiments demonstrate that the regulated carbon network suppresses current crowding and localized thermal accumulation, increasing the maximum permissible single-pulse absorbed energy density by approximately 78%. This work establishes a generative-AI route that links image-based microstructure characterization with conductive-network regulation for improved transient energy dissipation in heterogeneous ceramic composites.

verified_metadata.title: A fully physically crosslinked hydrogel with high toughness, fast response, and degradability for deep learning-assisted handwriting recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Hydrogels serve as flexible sensing materials for robotics or wearable devices. To address the challenges of low mechanical strength, slow response, and poor degradability in conventional hydrogels, a fully physically crosslinked polyelectrolyte hydrogel is designed in this work. Based on hydrophobic association and multiple crosslinking strategies, the polymer backbone is formed by copolymerizing the anionic hydrophilic monomers 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropane sulfonic acid (AMPS) and acrylamide (AM), while the cationic surfactant CTAB is introduced to construct hydrophobic association domains, resulting in a dense physically crosslinked network. Low-field (LF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and rheology are employed to elucidate the intermolecular interactions and the evolution of heterogeneous network structures within the hydrogel physically crosslinked by hydrophilic chains and CTAB aggregates. The sulfonic acid groups on the polymer chains together with the free H+ concentration within the network not only enhance electrostatic interactions among chains but also increase the internal ionic concentration, thereby establishing efficient pathways for ion transport. The dynamic and reversible physical crosslinking network endows the hydrogel with excellent mechanical properties (strain up to 1644%), fatigue resistance, and rapid response characteristics (response time 55 ms, recovery time 49 ms). Moreover, the fully physically crosslinked network confers good oxidative degradability, effectively avoiding environmental pollution. As a multifunctional flexible platform, the hydrogel enables smart touch control and supercapacitor applications. Furthermore, when integrated with a deep learning system, the sensor achieves handwriting recognition and information extraction with a recognition accuracy as high as 95.2%. This work provides an effective strategy for developing degradable hydrogel sensors that combine fast response with excellent electrical performance.

title: Oriented β-phase and porous architecture synergistically boost piezoelectricity of poly(vinylidene fluoride) films for wearable electronics
abstract: Oriented β-phase crystallites and well-defined porous structures are two well-established routes to boost PVDF piezoelectricity, yet integrating both in a single material remains an unsolved challenge. Here, we report a film processing strategy by combining ZnO incorporation, irradiation crosslinking, melt stretching, and acid etching to address this issue. ZnO nanoparticles play a dual role, serving as both a promoter to enhance flow-induced β-phase formation and a sacrificial template for pore generation. The synergistic effects of high ZnO loading (60 wt%), slight chain crosslinking, and strong melt stretching (20×) yield highly oriented β-phase with a fraction as high as 81.7%. Meanwhile, flow-induced redispersion of ZnO aggregates forms an interconnected nanofiller network, enabling complete ZnO removal upon acid etching to generate anisotropic pores. The resulting porous architecture, together with the oriented β-phase, enhances piezoelectric performance through three synergistic mechanisms: the intrinsic piezoelectricity of the β-phase, reduced dielectric permittivity, and the piezoelectret effect of the pores. The optimized film achieves a high piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 69.6 pC/N and a figure of merit of 4.6 × 10-11 m2/N, with robust mechanical properties. The corresponding piezoelectric device exhibits a broad force-response range, high sensitivity to weak stimuli, and excellent cyclic stability. Flexible sensors based on these films can monitor human motion and physiological signals, and integration with a two‐dimensional convolutional neural network enables Morse-code-based transmission with 98.4% accuracy. This work offers a scalable melt-processing route for high-performance porous PVDF piezoelectric films toward flexible wearable electronics and self-powered sensing systems.

title: Multimodal E-textiles based on industrial textile technologies for next generation human machine interfaces
abstract: Although wearable electronics have demonstrated significant potential in fields such as motion management, biomedicine, and virtual reality, the low-cost and scalable fabrication of flexible devices that combine multimodal sensing with excellent wearability remains a critical bottleneck for practical deployment. To address these challenges, this paper reports a multimodal electronic textile (e-textile) based on mature industrial textile technologies. In this work, the sensing yarns were developed using a wrapping technique, where silver-coated nylon and nylon yarns were helically wrapped around a highly elastic spandex core. Following the preparation of a custom-knitted pointelle substrate, the capacitive sensor was realized by integrating two sensing yarns via an embroidery process. The e-textile exhibits responsive performance to mechanical stimuli, including stretching, compression, and directional bending, while also providing robust sensing for non-contact proximity, demonstrating high sensitivity, a wide sensing range, and stability. Based on this, a smart wearable glove system was developed, encompassing specifically developed circuitry and visualization software. Combined with a deep learning model, the system achieved a gesture recognition accuracy of 99.8%, enabling the precise control of a robotic arm. This work not only offers a feasible approach for the development of multimodal flexible e-textiles but also facilitates the integration of wearable devices into next generation human-machine interfaces.

title: Molecularly engineered hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent–holey graphene interfaces for matrix-resilient PFOA removal from complex waters
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent and hazardous water contaminant, yet practical adsorptive treatment remains constrained by the lack of materials that combine rapid uptake, high capacity, neutral-pH performance, and stability in complex water matrices. Here, we systematically engineered a hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (HDES)-modified holey graphene nanosheet (HGN) adsorbent, introducing HDES incorporation onto defect-rich HGN for aqueous PFOA capture. An experimentally validated COSMO-RS workflow covering 30 DES constituents across six chemical families and ten HGN-DES adsorbents identified TBAC:DecA (1:2) as the highest-performing tested formulation, achieving about 1.9-fold higher PFOA removal than pristine HGN. Characterization confirmed HDES modification and formation of an HDES-enriched, electrokinetically modified lamellar graphene interface. HGN-HDES reached about 75% of its final capacity within 15 min, compared with about 30% for pristine HGN, and increased maximum adsorption capacity from 563.8 to 834.2 mg g −1 . Statistical-physics modeling identified a double-layer adsorption mechanism involving multi-site surface association, limited second-layer buildup, and thermally promoted site occupation. HGN-HDES retained 65.3% of its initial capacity after five adsorption–desorption cycles. At 0.5 mg L −1 PFOA and pH 7, HGN-HDES removed 92.4% from ultrapure water, 89.5% from municipal wastewater, and 91.4% from seawater, despite organic matter or high ionic strength. An ensemble artificial neural network (ANN) implemented in an interactive GUI further translated the 13-point experimental dataset into an exploratory in-domain process map restricted to the investigated ranges of C₀, t, and T. This DES-enabled graphene strategy offers a modular route to matrix-resilient PFAS adsorbents under environmentally relevant conditions.

verified_metadata.title: MOF-derived porous NiO-Fe₂O₃ heterostructures with machine-learning-assisted signal discrimination for ppb-level H₂S detection and breath analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Detection of trace hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) is important for environmental monitoring and breath-based disease diagnostics, yet achieving strong ppb-level signal modulation and reliable gas discrimination remains challenging for conventional metal oxide sensors. Herein, MOF-derived NiO-Fe₂O₃ composites were synthesized by thermal conversion of Ni-incorporated Fe-BDC precursors to construct porous heterostructured sensing materials. The MOF template provides a hierarchical porous architecture that promotes gas diffusion and exposes abundant reactive sites, while controlled Ni incorporation generates dispersed NiO domains and p-n heterojunction interfaces with Fe₂O₃. Structural, spectroscopic, and electrochemical analyses support the formation of NiO-Fe₂O₃ composites with composition-dependent electronic interactions and modified interfacial charge transport. Gas-sensing measurements reveal a volcano-type composition dependence, with the composite prepared at a nominal Ni:Fe molar ratio of 0.05 delivering the best H₂S sensing performance. At 175 °C, this optimized composite exhibits a high response of 42% toward 5000 ppb H₂S, detectable transient signals below 20 ppb, and fast response/recovery times of 2.1/20.1 s. The sensor also shows good selectivity, repeatability, long-term stability, humidity tolerance, and proof-of-concept discrimination between healthy breath and H₂S-spiked simulated breath. Furthermore, a machine-learning-assisted multi-scale temporal representation framework was developed to improve single-sensor gas discrimination. By integrating multi-scale dynamic features with correlation-based descriptors, the framework improves gas classification under the present controlled testing conditions, as validated by feature-space visualization, confusion matrices, and ROC curves. The enhanced performance is likely associated with the synergistic effects of MOF-derived porosity, defect−/adsorbed‑oxygen-enriched surface chemistry, and heterojunction-induced band modulation.

title: Droplet entrainment in continuous liquid–liquid separators: Role of the small-droplet tail and uncertainty-aware hybrid modelling
abstract: Droplet entrainment in liquid–liquid gravity separators limits separation efficiency, yet both systematic experimental studies and predictive entrainment models remain scarce. In this study, 1077 steady-state operating points were obtained in a DN200 pilot-scale separator using a 1-octanol/water system, varying temperature, ionic strength, volume flow rate, dispersed-phase fraction, and inlet drop size distribution. Inlet drop size distributions were quantified by endoscopic imaging and entrained dispersed-phase fractions online by turbidity probes calibrated against gas chromatography. The results show that entrainment is governed by the small-droplet tail of the inlet drop size distribution, represented by the number-based tenth percentile d 10 ( q 0 ) . Increasing temperature shifted d 10 ( q 0 ) to larger values and thereby reduced entrainment, reproducibly within every ionic-strength campaign. Ionic strength left the small-droplet tail unchanged over most of the investigated range and shifted it only at the highest level tested. Both enter entrainment solely through d 10 ( q 0 ) and therefore do not require separate model inputs. On this basis, we formulated a reduced-order physics-based exponential model using d 10 ( q 0 ) and the critical Stokes diameter as inputs, augmented by hybrid residual-learning models based on Gaussian processes and neural networks. On internal and out-of-distribution test sets, these models, all calibrated on this single material system and separator geometry, slightly outperformed the physics baseline in point accuracy and uncertainty calibration. On external literature data from a DN150 separator and a paraffin-oil/water system, the RMSE of all models increased five- to tenfold, driven by a few under-predicted high-entrainment points. The physics-based model was the most robust in point accuracy, whereas the calibrated uncertainty of the Gaussian-process models did not transfer, with interval coverage dropping to 70%–74% against a nominal 95%.

verified_metadata.title: Metal-ion coordination-regulated TA@rGO dual-network hydrogels for synergistic mechanical-electrical enhancement and machine-learning-assisted motion recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of flexible sensors requires hydrogel materials with high mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and multifunctional adaptability. However, achieving simultaneous enhancement of mechanical and electrical properties remains challenging due to the trade-off between network reinforcement and charge transport. Herein, a modular conductive hydrogel strategy based on metal-ion coordination regulation is proposed. A tannic acid-reduced graphene oxide (TA@rGO) conductive filler is incorporated into a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAM/SA) double-network hydrogel, and the resulting PAM/TA@rGO/SA hydrogel is denoted as PTGS. Subsequently, dynamic coordination interactions between Cu2+/Fe3+ ions and oxygen-containing groups of SA, as well as polyphenolic sites of TA, are utilized to prepare PTGS-Cu2+ and PTGS-Fe3+ hydrogels with tunable properties. Metal-ion coordination significantly improves the mechanical performance, with PTGS-Fe3+ achieving tensile and compressive strengths of 1100 kPa and 3330 kPa, respectively. Unlike conventional ion-conducting hydrogels, where enhanced crosslinking generally suppresses conductivity, TA@rGO-mediated electronic pathways allow metal-ion coordination to simultaneously improve conductivity, reaching 17.8 S m−1 for PTGS-Fe3+. Moreover, different coordination states endow the hydrogels with distinct sensing characteristics, including wide-range strain detection, balanced sensitivity and detection range, and high sensitivity at low strain. Combined with machine learning algorithms, the hydrogels enable material-state recognition and accurate classification of diverse human motions. This work provides a modular strategy for designing multifunctional conductive hydrogels with tunable sensing capabilities.

title: Machine learning modeling and interpretability analysis of piezo-assisted mechanochemical defluorination of PFOA

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。XGBoost拟合并解释压电辅助PFOA机械脱氟反应速率，预测污染物降解性能。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning modeling and interpretability analysis of piezo-assisted mechanochemical defluorination of PFOA
verified_metadata.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), as a typical persistent organic pollutant resistant to degradation. Piezo-assisted mechanochemical degradation technology enables efficient PFOA defluorination under mild conditions, demonstrating promising application potential. However, this process is governed by the coupled effects of multiple factors, including ball milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, and co-agent dosage, and its nonlinear interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, ball milling speed, ball-to-powder ratio, mass ratio of KOH to PFOA, and mass ratio of piezoelectric material to PFOA were used as input features, and the defluorination kinetic constant k (k_defluorination) of PFOA was set as the target output. A dataset comprising 300 experimental samples was constructed. Based on predictive accuracy and interpretability requirements, the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was selected and hyperparameter-optimized. Model interpretability analysis was conducted using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). Results show that the optimized XGBoost model achieves a R2 of 0.974, an RMSE of 0.186 h−1 and an MAE of 0.139 h−1 on the test set, demonstrating excellent generalization capability. SHAP analysis reveals the importance ranking of factors affecting defluorination rate as: ball milling speed > mass ratio of piezoelectric material to PFOA > ball-to-powder ratio > mass ratio of KOH to PFOA. For the first time, data-driven evidence shows that fluctuations in KOH dosage barely affect the reaction rate under excess KOH conditions. Further analysis identifies a significant synergistic effect between rotation speed and piezoelectric material dosage, defining the critical parameters for reaction initiation and the optimal process control range. The established model enables accurate prediction of PFOA mechanochemical defluorination kinetics, and its interpretability analysis reveals inherent nonlinear regulation mechanisms from a data-driven perspective, providing theoretical support and decision-making basis for process optimization and engineering application.

title: Deep learning forecasts and experimentally validates antimicrobial resistance evolution, enabling design of mutation-refractory therapeutics

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。Transformer基因组分析与几何图网络预测耐药突变，并实验验证抗突变治疗分子。

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning forecasts and experimentally validates antimicrobial resistance evolution, enabling design of mutation-refractory therapeutics
verified_metadata.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance represents one of the most urgent challenges in modern biology, yet our ability to prospectively predict resistance emergence remains profoundly limited. Here, we present an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) framework combining transformer-based deep learning for genomic analysis with geometric graph neural networks for three-dimensional protein-ligand modeling, achieving 96.5% accuracy in prospectively forecasting resistance mutations—substantially exceeding existing approaches (73–89%). Through large-scale automated evolution of 1000 independent bacterial lineages across 15 clinically-relevant species over 300 generations, we demonstrate prospective prediction of resistance-associated mutations before their experimental emergence during controlled laboratory evolution, thereby enabling earlier identification of adaptive trajectories and supporting AI-guided antimicrobial detection. We validated 15 AI-predicted variants through high-resolution structural biology (X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM, 1.68–2.6 Å), revealing how single amino acid substitutions reduce drug binding affinity by 4.4–6.3 kcal/mol predominantly through allosteric conformational perturbations. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations (800 ns per system) quantified how resistance mutations increase structural flexibility (RMSF 2.5–4.5 Å versus 1.5–2.0 Å for wild-type) and flatten conformational energy landscapes, enabling entropy-driven resistance. Leveraging these mechanistic principles, we designed 12 novel antimicrobial candidates' scaffolds using generative chemistry, of which 10 showed no substantial resistance emergence (<2-fold MIC drift) after 500 generations of selection, contrasting with 32–512-fold resistance observed for conventional antibiotics under identical conditions. Whole-genome sequencing of evolved lineages (7000 complete genomes) revealed universal evolutionary constraints: resistance mutations impose 6.7–25.6% fitness costs, structuring adaptation pathways. Biophysical characterization by surface plasmon resonance and isothermal titration calorimetry revealed a decreased ligand-binding affinity and altered binding thermodynamics for the TEM-1 M182T variant, providing mechanistic insight that allowed rational antimicrobial design and optimization of hydrogen-bonding interactions. Our framework integrates four scales—from atomic interactions through protein dynamics and genomic plasticity to population-level trajectories—establishing AI-guided antimicrobial resistance prediction and evolutionary analysis applicable to cancer drug resistance.

title: Online detection toward transient intermediates and reaction-selectivity modulation in aryl pentazole cyclization: AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic technology

verified_metadata.title: Online detection toward transient intermediates and reaction-selectivity modulation in aryl pentazole cyclization: AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic technology
verified_metadata.abstract: The cyclization of aryl pentazoles suffers from competing pathways, transient intermediates, and unstable products, leading to low yields. These features hinder mechanistic characterization and selectivity regulation. To address these bottlenecks, we develop an AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic characterization technique to uncover the reaction mechanism of this complex system. High-fidelity dynamic data covering the entire reaction process were acquired by in situ infrared spectroscopy. Combined with an intelligent analysis framework established based on the GPT-5.2 model, two key aryl pentazene intermediates were identified for the first time under practical reaction conditions, and their temperature-dependent concentration evolution was systematically clarified. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the E,Z-isomer serves as the dominant precursor for cyclization, possessing significantly lower formation and conversion energy barriers than the E,E-isomer, which is in excellent agreement with spectroscopic experimental results. Multi-modal characterization with quantitative NMR kinetic tracking further verifies the specific stabilization effect of phenoxide anions on aryl pentazoles. Precise temperature control at −10 °C selectively promotes the target cyclization and inhibits side reactions, finally boosting the yield up to 45%. This work not only provides a feasible strategy for the efficient synthesis of pentazole-type compounds, but also demonstrates the application merits of AI-assisted multi-spectroscopic characterization for highly-reactive complex reaction systems, offering a new paradigm for mechanistic elucidation of intricate chemical reactions.

verified_metadata.title: Regenerable, molecularly engineered bio-based rosin gels for resilient underwater sensing and deep learning-augmented intelligent biometrics
verified_metadata.abstract: Hydrogel-based wearable electronics are pivotal for human-machine interfaces; however, their performance in aquatic environments is fundamentally limited by osmotic swelling and interfacial hydration layers, leading to signal instability and mechanical delamination. Herein, a molecularly engineered rosin-derived gel was synthesized via a streamlined one-pot strategy, strategically utilizing maleic rosin as a “molecular spacer” to regulate the hierarchical crosslinking density. The resulting gel architecture features hydrophobic microencapsulation, which effectively excludes interfacial water molecules, enabling an underwater adhesive strength of 0.25 MPa and a low water permeability (3%). By integrating carbon black and multi-walled carbon nanotubes into a “bridge-island” conductive framework, the sensor delivers high sensitivity (Gauge Factor = 3.0) and dielectric stability over 400 cycles under submersion. Leveraging these synergistic properties, a self-powered communication platform that couples a high-output triboelectric nanogenerator (Voc = 269.2 V) with a deep-learning-assisted decoding framework was developed. This system achieves a remarkable 99% accuracy in underwater Morse-code translation and 97% accuracy in “Behavioral DNA” handwriting recognition, bypassing the acoustic interference of traditional maritime communication. Furthermore, life cycle assessment (LCA) confirms the material's circularity and environmental advantage, establishing a sustainable design paradigm for next-generation flexible electronics in marine exploration, secure digital notarization, and zero-power intelligent biometrics.

title: Machine-learning-assisted energy evolution analysis of lysine oligomers reveals ε-polylysine as an electrolyte additive for stable aqueous zinc batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。机器学习分析DFT低聚赖氨酸链长能量演变，结合实验设计稳定水系锌电解液添加剂。

verified_metadata.title: Machine-learning-assisted energy evolution analysis of lysine oligomers reveals ε-polylysine as an electrolyte additive for stable aqueous zinc batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety and low cost; however, their practical operation is restricted by hydrogen evolution, corrosion, byproduct accumulation, and dendritic Zn growth at the Zn anode. Considering the structural complexity of polymer additives and the difficulty of direct high-accuracy calculations, in this work, an integrated “oligomer-based density functional theory (DFT) calculation-machine-learning- assisted energy evolution analysis-experimental validation” framework for polylysine chain-length-dependent energetics was developed. Lysine oligomers were used as model systems to calculate the molecular energy, additive-water-binding energy, and adsorption energy on Zn surfaces, which were further correlated with the degree of polymerization, functional-group density, charge distribution, and molecular size. The analysis revealed a nonlinear chain length–dependent energy evolution of polylysine, whereas ε-polylysine (ε-PL) lies within a relatively stable energy-response region. Owing to its chain-like multidentate structure, ε-PL synergistically reconstructs the hydrogen-bonding network of water and protects the Zn interface. The experimental results demonstrate that ε-PL facilitates interfacial Zn2+ kinetics involving ion transport, partial desolvation, and charge-transfer processes, while forming an N/O-rich interfacial environment that suppresses parasitic reactions and nonuniform Zn deposition. Consequently, the ε-PL-modified electrolyte enabled Zn||Cu cells to cycle for 2000 cycles with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2%, enabled Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate for more than 4000 h, and enabled Zn||AlVO-NMP full cells to retain 70.63% capacity after 6000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy for the machine learning-assisted design of polymer electrolyte additives for AZIBs.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-assisted three-stepped microconical flexible pressure sensor for efficient motion recognition and plant haptic perception
verified_metadata.abstract: Flexible pressure sensors with high sensitivity and good conformability are important for wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and virtual reality (VR) haptics. However, conventional planar or single-stage microstructure sensors usually suffer from limited sensitivity and poor contact with curved soft surfaces under weak pressures, mainly due to single-scale deformation that induces contact stiffening and restricts stress transfer. Here, a flexible resistive pressure sensor based on three-stepped microcones and a silver-coated PDMS/MXene composite is reported. The stepped microcone structure allows progressive compression under applied pressure, which helps delay contact hardening and improve stress transfer. Meanwhile, the silver-coated PDMS/MXene composite provides stable conductive pathways for resistance variation. The sensor exhibits high sensitivity (131 kPa−1) at low pressures (0–0.4 kPa) and maintains excellent cyclic stability (about 5000 cycles). With the assistance of deep learning, the device distinguishes facial micro-expressions, gait patterns, and vigorous movements with an accuracy of 98.1%. Furthermore, the sensor could detect subtle touch signals from plant leaves, enabling plant species identification and immersive VR tactile simulation. This work provides a flexible pressure-sensing platform for human motion analysis and plant touch perception, showing potential for wearable electronics and agricultural sensing applications.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning-assisted double-pulse laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy and AuAg nanocluster-modified nanofiber membranes for detection of Cs, Sr, and Co in soil
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of heavy metals (HMs) in soil is of importance for ensuring food security and advancing smart agriculture. However, conventional detection methods face numerous limitations, such as complicated operations and time-consuming procedures. This study proposed a novel method using AuAg nanoclusters (AuAgNCs)-modified nanofibrous membranes combined with double-pulse LIBS (DP-LIBS) for the sensitive detection of available cesium (Cs), strontium (Sr), and cobalt (Co) in soil. The AuAgNCs-modified nanofiber membranes were utilized to efficiently adsorb Cs+, Sr2+, and Co2+ from soil solution, with simultaneous DP-LIBS detection. The results revealed that the limits of detection (LODs) for Cs, Sr, and Co in soil reached 0.078 mg/kg, 0.085 mg/kg, and 0.16 mg/kg, respectively. Furthermore, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) model was developed for accurate quantitative analysis and exhibited excellent predictive performance. The residual predictive deviations (RPDs) for Cs, Sr, and Co in soil were 6.0121, 5.1844, and 6.7082, respectively. This method holds great application potential in HMs monitoring, soil risk assessment, and human health protection.

title: Machine learning-based peroxidase-like sensor arrays for the discrimination of thiophene compounds

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。机器学习解析过氧化物酶样阵列反应，定性及定量区分五类噻吩化合物。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-based peroxidase-like sensor arrays for the discrimination of thiophene compounds
verified_metadata.abstract: Thiophene compounds are sulfur containing organic substances present in industrial wastewater and fuels, and are closely associated with environmental pollution. Therefore, it is urgently required to develop a rapid and convenient detection method. In this study, we developed a machine learning-based peroxidase-like sensor array for the efficient discrimination and sensitive detection of five thiophene compounds. By employing platinum‑iron nanowires (PtFe NWs) with peroxidase-like activity and 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) as the chromogenic substrate, the sensor array generated diverse absorbance fingerprint patterns under three pH conditions (3.6, 4.0 and 4.6). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that thiophene compounds generally exhibit stronger adsorption energies on the PtFe NWs surface than H₂O₂, indicating their preferential adsorption onto the nanozyme surface. The adsorbed thiophene molecules inhibit the peroxidase-like activity of PtFe NWs to different extents through π–d interactions between the benzene or thiophene rings and Pt atoms, as well as PtS chemical bonding. These differential inhibitory effects generate unique absorbance fingerprint patterns across the three pH sensing channels. The proposed sensor array enables not only the qualitative identification of five thiophene compounds but also their quantitative determination through machine learning methods such as linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). Moreover, the recognition capability toward thiophene mixtures, resistance to interference, and practical applicability of the sensor array were successfully validated. This work demonstrates the promising application potential of three-channel PtFe NWs sensor arrays for thiophene compounds discrimination.

verified_metadata.abstract: The escalating environmental and health threats from hazardous pesticide residues demand integrated strategies that combine real-time monitoring with effective removal. Herein, we report a bifunctional fluorescent nanohybrid of Au22-ZIF constructed by immobilization of Au22(SG)18 nanoclusters onto ZIF-8. The confinement effect substantially enhances fluorescence quantum yield and photostability. The nanohybrid enables sensitive thiram detection via competitive coordination-induced fluorescence quenching, achieving a limit of detection as low as 0.90 μM. Furthermore, a flexible hydrogel-based sensor fabricated by melt-reduction allows on-site produce analysis. To overcome the limitations of conventional RGB-based image interpretation, an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that autonomously extracts multidimensional latent features from sensor images is proposed, delivering robust and accurate thiram concentration predictions (R2 = 0.95) with full model transparency. Concurrently, the inherently high surface area and porous architecture of ZIF-8 together with the active binding sites of Au22(SG)18 provide exceptional adsorptive removal of residual thiram with outstanding recyclability over multiple cycles. In addition, the hydrogel sensor enables real-time dynamic monitoring of thiram residue evolution on vegetables. By synergizing optical sensing, ML-driven data analytics, and pollutant sequestration within a single portable platform, this work establishes a paradigm for next-generation smart systems aimed at on-site pesticide surveillance and food safety control.

verified_metadata.title: Bioengineered iron nanoparticles for arsenic remediation: Unraveling the adsorption-oxidation-fixation pathway via SHAP-interpretable machine learning and LC-AFS speciation tracking
verified_metadata.abstract: Arsenic-contaminated wastewater poses a persistent threat to public health and ecological safety, while conventional remediation materials often involve trade-offs among performance, sustainability, and economic feasibility. Here, biomolecule-coated iron-based nanoparticles (Ib-FeNPs) were synthesized from Ipomoea batatas (I. batatas) leaf extract through a green one-pot route for the simultaneous removal of As(III) and As(V). In a mixed‑arsenic system, Ib-FeNPs achieved removal efficiencies of 92.4% for As(III) and 100.0% for As(V) after 360 min at a dosage of 0.3 g·L−1. These values exceeded those obtained with bare FeNPs (10.3% and 60.1%), the isolated capping layer (21.5% and 92.0%), and their physical mixture (26.5% and 83.8%). Time-resolved liquid chromatography-atomic fluorescence spectrometry detected the partial conversion of initially added As(III) to As(V). Analysis of the As 3d X-ray photoelectron spectra identified both species on the reacted material. A decrease in the surface Fe(III) fraction accompanied by an increase in Fe(II) was consistent with the participation of Fe-containing sites in redox processes. The component and physical-mixture controls showed that assembly of the Fe-containing phase and plant-derived coating improved simultaneous arsenic removal. Material characterization revealed Fe-containing surface environments and organic functional groups. Liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry identified 18 major plant-derived biomolecules. Six regression algorithms were compared using a four-factor experimental dataset, and SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) were applied to the selected models to assess the contributions of operating variables to predicted removal efficiencies within the investigated range. Together, these findings support an adsorption-oxidation-fixation pathway at the process level. Ib-FeNPs also showed good reusability over five cycles and achieved 80.0% total arsenic removal in a fixed-bed experiment with acid mine drainage (AMD). Overall, Ib-FeNPs provide a plant-mediated platform for arsenic-contaminated water remediation, while the integrated machine-learning and characterization framework offers a transferable approach to developing bio-nano adsorbents from underutilized biomass.

verified_metadata.title: Label-free SERS diagnosis of colorectal cancer assisted by machine learning and integrated with recyclable polyurethane sensor chips
verified_metadata.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is widely used in cancer liquid biopsy due to its rapid, sensitive, and non-invasive nature. In this study, bimetallic silver and gold nanoparticles (Ag NPs/Au NPs) were uniformly deposited onto cellulose filter paper (CFP) via three-phase liquid-liquid interface self-assembly. Subsequently, a polyurethane (PU) coating was applied to the CFP surface to obtain a high-performance PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP SERS sensor for rapid colorectal cancer (CRC) screening. Sensor stability was improved by the PU coating, and the PU-Ag NPs/Au NPs-CFP substrate exhibited stronger SERS enhancement than the uncoated substrate under various conditions, including temperatures from −80 °C to 60 °C and hydrogen peroxide solutions (≤ 3.00%). After 270 days, 87.49% of the initial SERS signal was retained, indicating long-term usability. The substrate also maintained stable SERS signals over five cycles, with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 3.08%, showing potential for recyclability. More importantly, the PU coating effectively reduced protein interference during serum detection. As confirmed by comparative spectral analysis, this allowed accurate identification of diagnostic metabolite fingerprints in the serum. SERS spectra of serum samples from 50 CRC patients and 50 healthy controls (HC) were acquired using a portable Raman spectrometer, and four machine learning (ML) algorithms were applied for classification. Among them, the support vector machine (SVM) model performed best. At the spectral level, it achieved 94.25% accuracy and 88.50% specificity; at the patient level, it achieved 95.00% accuracy and 90.00% specificity. This study integrates a recyclable and stable SERS sensor with ML, offering a new solution for efficient, non-invasive, and low-cost CRC screening.

verified_metadata.title: Feature-fusion cascaded neural network (FFCCN)-assisted optical sensor array for simultaneous detection of multiple pollutants in edible oil based on four-signal fluorescent copper-based nanozyme
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid and reliable identification of diverse pollutants in edible oils remains challenging due to complex matrices and insufficient sensing dimensionality. Herein, we report a multifunctional copper-based nanozyme (Cu-TTPDC) constructed via coordination between Cu2+ ions and a thiadiazole-containing aromatic dicarboxylate ligand, which integrates intrinsic fluorescence with peroxidase (POD)-, laccase (LAC)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a single framework. Unlike conventional sensor arrays assembled from multiple sensing elements, Cu-TTPDC provides four complementary optical responses—three catalytic colorimetric channels and one fluorescent channel—thereby simplifying array construction while retaining multidimensional sensing information. The single-material array generates distinct response fingerprints for eight representative pollutants spanning heavy-metal, phenolic-compound, and pesticide categories, including lead(II) ions (Pb2+), gossypol (GSP), fenthion (FEN), aldicarb (ALD), glyphosate (GLY), flusilazole (FLZ), fluorodifen (DCF), and 2-cyclohexyl-4,6-dinitrophenol (DCP). To decode the correlated and nonlinear multichannel patterns, a feature-fusion cascaded classification network (FFCCN) was developed. The network learns a shared representation directly from the four response channels and concatenates this representation with the predicted pollutant-probability vector in the concentration branch, thereby conditioning concentration-level discrimination on pollutant identity without using the true pollutant label. Under four-fold nested cross-validation, the model achieved out-of-fold accuracies of 91.3% for pollutant identification and 88.1% for five-level concentration discrimination, with an 84.4% joint accuracy. Detection limits as low as 0.15 μg·mL−1. This single-material four-channel array coupled with cascaded learning provides a compact approach for multidimensional screening of chemically diverse hazards in edible oils.
