title: Machine learning-assisted mixed-valence Fe/Cu nanozyme dual-channel sensing platform for high-throughput discrimination of antioxidants

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。机器学习解析混合价铁铜纳米酶双通道比色响应，高通量区别抗氧化分子。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted mixed-valence Fe/Cu nanozyme dual-channel sensing platform for high-throughput discrimination of antioxidants
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate identification and quantitative analysis of antioxidants in complex biological fluids are the keys to the early detection of severe diseases. The single-channel sensors suffer from weak specificity and critical multi-component signal crosstalk, which hardly meet the accurate analytical requirements. Herein, an intelligent colorimetric sensing platform of bimetallic mixed-valence nanozyme was integrated with machine learning (ML) to improve the analytical precision. Fe/Cu nanosheets of mixed valence were successfully acquired through Cu2O-coordinated anchoring in situ into iron porphyrin (TCPP(Fe)). This mixed-valence strategy effectively promoted the synergistic catalysis and valence cycling among the metal active sites, thereby significantly enhancing the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of the Cu2O/Cu-TCPP(Fe) (Vmax as high as 8.107 × 10−7 M·s−1 and Km as low as 0.913 mM). DFT calculations indicated that the introduction of Cu2O promoted strong Cu 3d and Fe 3d orbital hybridization and an upshift of the Cu d-band center, accelerating interfacial electron transfer and Fe/Cu valence cycling, thereby revealing the intrinsic mechanism underlying the enhanced catalytic activity. Taking the differential catalytic responses of the nanozyme with two different substrates, a highly sensitive dual-channel sensor array was designed with machine learning. Combined with algorithms of artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM), etc., 100% accurate qualitative discrimination of six antioxidants was remarkably completed. Relying on the outstanding capability of the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to remarkable robustness in handling high-dimensional sample datasets, the sensor array successfully established a precise quantitative model for multiple antioxidants in complex samples, remarkably and intelligently sensing the diverse components in urine and serum. This work paved a new way for highly active bimetallic nanozymes to construct a trustworthy sensing platform as a diagnostic tool for the intelligent profiling of multi-component biomarkers in complex matrices.

verified_metadata.title: Machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics and reaction mechanism for degradative solvent extraction of low-rank coal
verified_metadata.abstract: Degradative solvent extraction (DSE) is an effective approach for the mild demineralization and upgrading of low-rank coals. However, the inherent high dimensionality and nonlinearity of the DSE reaction system hinder identification of consistent relationships between key predictors and product yields, thereby limiting a deeper understanding of the process. To overcome this limitation, a machine-learning-assisted multidimensional kinetics (ML-MK) framework was developed. This framework combines the predictive capability of machine learning with the interpretability of lumped kinetic models for interpreting apparent pathway behavior. A predictive model for DSE yield was established (R2 = 0.92), enabling quantitative assessment of predictor contributions to model outputs and providing multidimensional insights into the reaction system. The model-derived patterns indicate a temperature-dependent shift in the relative contributions of different processes. The low-temperature response is consistent with solvent-assisted transport and physical dissolution at 25–300 °C. Thermally activated coal-matrix conversion becomes increasingly important at 300–360 °C, followed by greater competition between hydrogen-assisted radical stabilization and condensation above 360 °C. Within the 300–400 °C range, the fitted fractional pathway contributions suggest an approximate, model-derived crossover near 340 °C. Below this approximate crossover, URC cracking contributes more strongly; above it, EX–UCactual interconversion has the larger modeled contribution. Overall, the ML-MK framework provides a novel and effective approach for achieving an in-depth understanding of DSE reaction processes. Moreover, the framework has application potential in fields characterized by complex reaction networks and numerous real components, such as coal liquefaction, petroleum refining, and biomass thermochemical conversion.

verified_metadata.title: Anti-swelling and antibacterial multifunctional conductive hydrogel for flexible sensing, intestinal palpation and machine learning-assisted recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Multifunctional conductive hydrogels show great potential for flexible bioelectronics, but their performance is often limited by trade-offs between mechanical strength, environmental stability, and functional integration. To address this, we propose a three-step preparation strategy combining thermal polymerization, freeze-thaw cycling, and LS post-treatment to regulate a multiscale network structure. This approach combines a chemically crosslinked polymer matrix, freeze-thaw treatment, and lignosulfonate (LS) incorporation to obtain a mechanically robust multicomponent hydrogel. An ethylene glycol (EG)/water binary solvent system further enhances the hydrogel's environmental adaptability. The resulting PPSH-L hydrogel exhibits optimized mechanical and functional properties, including high strength (0.86 MPa), large stretchability, excellent fatigue resistance, and remarkable anti-swelling and anti-freezing capabilities (down to −22.6 °C). Its stable conductive network ensures high sensitivity, broad response range, rapid signal response, and excellent stability under repeated deformation. The incorporation of zwitterionic SBMA and LS provides an antibacterial interface with >95% efficiency and good biocompatibility. Leveraging these advantages, the hydrogel supports multifunctional sensing for motion monitoring, non-verbal patient-clinician communication, intestinal tactile sensing, and abnormal tissue palpation. Combined with a Transformer model, it enables intelligent recognition of tissue mechanical properties, offering a new approach for minimally invasive diagnosis. In simulated colonoscopy applications, the hydrogel effectively detects mechanical changes in abnormal intestinal tissues, enhancing early-stage lesion detection. This strategy overcomes the performance trade-offs in hydrogels and advances their applications in intelligent healthcare and flexible electronics.

title: Dual-modal signal decoupling strategy based on cascaded machine learning for intelligent food freshness monitoring

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。随机森林等级联模型解耦荧光电阻双模传感信号，改善食品新鲜度监测。

verified_metadata.title: Dual-modal signal decoupling strategy based on cascaded machine learning for intelligent food freshness monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: Real-time monitoring of pH and humidity is essential for evaluating food freshness. However, changes in humidity can affect ion migration, interfere with resistive pH sensing signals, and significantly hinder simultaneous accurate quantification of the two parameters. To address this challenge, a dual-mode sensing patch that combines fluorescence and resistive sensing, coupled with a cascaded machine learning framework, was developed for monitoring food freshness. The fluorescence response unit consists of a cellulose/polyvinyl alcohol composite system embedded with AuNCs. Additionally, graphene electrodes were fabricated on both sides using 3D printing technology to facilitate the simultaneous acquisition of optical and electrical signals. The fluorescence intensity increases as humidity decreases, whereas the resistance signal exhibits a linear response within the pH range of 6.0 to 9.0. To mitigate cross-interference between the dual-mode signals, a cascaded machine learning framework was developed, including random forest model and Bayesian ridge regression. Humidity information was first extracted from fluorescence features and subsequently introduced as a compensation parameter for pH prediction based on resistance signals. This hierarchical analysis framework approach effectively decoupled the coupled humidity and pH signals, enabling accurate quantification of both parameters. This strategy enables intelligent food freshness monitoring and flexible multi-parameter signal decoupling.

verified_metadata.title: Gram-scale de novo biosynthesis of phenylethanoid glycosides in Escherichia coli via mechanism-guided AI-assisted engineering of a BAHD acyltransferase
verified_metadata.abstract: Phenylethanoid glycosides (PhGs), such as verbascoside and echinacoside, are valuable plant natural products with significant pharmacological potential. Their sustainable supply remains a challenge due to the limitations of plant extraction and chemical synthesis. In this study, we report high-level de novo production of complex PhGs in Escherichia coli from glucose by combining machine learning-aided enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering. To overcome the catalytic bottleneck of the BAHD acyltransferase SiAT1, we developed a computational pipeline that integrated deep learning with mechanistic constraints to select candidate variants for experimental screening. Subsequent experimental screening and mechanistic analysis identified Lys30 as a critical acceptor-gating residue, and the SiAT1K30A variant exhibited a 243-fold enhanced affinity for salidroside. We systematically engineered the E. coli chassis by constructing a high-yield supply module for the key precursors salidroside and p-coumaric acid, optimizing the expression of SiCYP98A20 and its reductase AaCPR, expanding the intracellular UDP-sugar pool, and introducing the RgTALS9N/A11Y mutant to redirect flux toward p-coumaric acid and alleviate the upstream supply imbalance. This integrated platform enabled fed-batch fermentation in 5-L bioreactors to achieve gram-scale de novo production of verbascoside (1.84 g/L) and echinacoside (1.35 g/L), along with an unprecedented accumulation of the key intermediate osmanthuside B (12.91 g/L). This work establishes E. coli as a scalable industrial host for complex PhGs and provides a potentially generalizable, data-driven framework that synergistically combines AI-assisted enzyme engineering with systematic metabolic engineering for the biomanufacturing of high-value plant natural products.

title: Scale-up prediction of breakthrough curves via shape–timescale decomposition in a hybrid deep learning framework

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。深度学习分解吸附突破曲线形状和时间尺度，预测过程放大响应。

verified_metadata.title: Scale-up prediction of breakthrough curves via shape–timescale decomposition in a hybrid deep learning framework
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of breakthrough curves (BTCs) remains a major challenge in scaling up fixed-bed adsorption systems, as conventional models often fail to generalize across operating conditions. Here, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework based on explicit decomposition of BTCs into normalized shape and characteristic timescale components. The normalized BTC shape is learned using a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) model in a dimensionless time domain, while the characteristic breakthrough time is predicted using a multilayer perceptron (MLP). The full BTC is reconstructed through a scaling-based mapping of these two components. Trained on lab-scale datasets, the proposed model achieved high predictive accuracy for unseen pilot-scale conditions (R2 = 0.975, RMSE = 0.053), reducing prediction errors by up to 3–5 times compared to conventional end-to-end models. Interpretability analyses using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and accumulated local effects (ALE) reveal that the characteristic timescale is primarily governed by influent concentration and hydrodynamic conditions, with nonlinear and interaction effects consistent with expected adsorption behavior. These results demonstrate that separating intrinsic dynamics from temporal scaling provides a structurally effective and interpretable approach for robust and transferable BTC prediction, offering a new pathway for data-efficient scale-up in adsorption-based water treatment systems.

verified_metadata.title: AI-enabled wireless gas sensor based on mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure for rapid detection of 3-hydroxy-2-butanone
verified_metadata.abstract: The growing adoption of smart food packaging, processing, and storing units demands advanced sensing systems capable of real-time food quality monitoring to enhance safety and reduce waste. This research presents a wireless miniaturized resistive gas sensor based on a mesoporous Cr2O3-In2O3 heterostructure, engineered for the highly sensitive and selective detection of 3-Hydroxy-2-Butanone (3H2B), which is a key volatile organic compound (VOC) marker of microbial spoilage in perishable foods such as dairy and meat. The synergistic interface between Cr2O3 and In2O3 optimises charge transfer and surface reactivity, enabling outstanding sensor performance with a detection limit of about 50 ppb and rapid response times under 12 s, while maintaining measurable response across a wide humidity range. These results are achieved through interdigitated electrodes with a spacing of 100 μm, enhancing sensitivity and signal stability. The mesoporous nanostructure offers high surface area and interconnected pores for rapid adsorption and diffusion, enabling consistent detection across wide concentration ranges. Wireless connectivity integrates the sensor into IoT-enabled smart packaging, processing lines, and storage facilities, streaming data to mobile, cloud, and automated control systems. AI models for supervised classification deliver instant spoilage alerts, continuous QA, and predictive inventory management across industrial and commercial supply chains. By combining advanced nanomaterials with scalable fabrication and IoT integration, this work advances the vision of intelligent, waste-minimising food systems and offers a platform for broader applications in large-scale food processing and cold-chain logistics. Data collected from multiple devices is periodically aggregated on a central server to refine the detection models. It predicts remaining shelf life from thousands of data points in order to improve predictive food quality control and also support safer and more sustainable operations.

verified_metadata.title: High-performance “brick-mortar” MXene/CNF/PVA aerogel pressure sensors for deep-learning-assisted gesture recognition and medical communication
verified_metadata.abstract: Communication barriers faced by patients with laryngeal disorders due to voice limitations have become a significant challenge in clinical diagnosis, and medical-patient communication, which could be potentially addressed by the wearable sensors. However, currently reported wearable sensors generally suffer from high manufacturing costs, slow response time, and limited stability. Here, inspired by “brick-mortar” porous structures, we report a MXene/cellulose nanofibers/polyvinyl alcohol (MCP) aerogel-based pressure sensor and develop the wearable smart glove to assist real-time and efficient communication during medical interactions. The pressure sensor features an ultra-low pressure detection limit (3.3 Pa), fast response and recovery time (66 ms /64 ms), a wide detection range (0–80 kPa), outstanding stability over 8000 compression cycles, and excellent thermal insulation properties at temperatures around 1600 °C, surpassing existing MXene-based aerogels pressure sensors. Further, a wearable smart glove was developed by using prepared pressure sensor array to realize multifunctional applications such as synchronized human-machine interaction (HMI) and remote media control. Combined with deep learning algorithms, the smart glove system achieved 100% recognition accuracy of 10 hand gestures. These findings provide an effective solution to the communication challenges faced by patients with speech disorders.

title: Micro-CT-based permeability characterization of virgin and pyrolyzed wood using deep learning segmentation and image-based pore-scale simulations
abstract: Permeability governs gas transport in pyrolyzing wood and strongly influences predictions of devolatilization and internal pressure build-up as the pore network evolves. We present an image-based workflow to quantify how pyrolysis modifies the intrinsic permeability tensor of Pinus pinaster (maritime pine) earlywood using synchrotron micro-CT, deep-learning segmentation, and pore-scale flow simulations. Anatomically matched submicron microtomography volumes were acquired before and after in-situ pyrolysis under nitrogen, up to 525 °C. Orientation-robust 3D pore/solid segmentation was obtained using three 2D U-Net models trained on longitudinal, radial, and tangential slice sets and fused by majority vote. Steady incompressible creeping-flow simulations, with Re ≪ 1, were then performed in OpenFOAM using simpleFoam to compute the full permeability tensor. Sensitivity analyses and a permeability-based REV study selected a representative cube size of 390 µm, corresponding to 1300³ voxels. Pyrolysis slightly increased porosity and shifted local pore diameters toward smaller values. Longitudinal and radial permeabilities decreased by 47% and 24%, whereas tangential permeability increased by a factor of 5.86, substantially reducing anisotropy. These trends indicate that pyrolysis restructures transport primarily by modifying constrictions and transverse connectivity rather than uniformly enlarging conduits.

verified_metadata.title: Micro-CT-based permeability characterization of virgin and pyrolyzed wood using deep learning segmentation and image-based pore-scale simulations
verified_metadata.abstract: Permeability governs gas transport in pyrolyzing wood and strongly influences predictions of devolatilization and internal pressure build-up as the pore network evolves. We present an image-based workflow to quantify how pyrolysis modifies the intrinsic permeability tensor of Pinus pinaster (maritime pine) earlywood using synchrotron micro-CT, deep-learning segmentation, and pore-scale flow simulations. Anatomically matched submicron microtomography volumes were acquired before and after in-situ pyrolysis under nitrogen, up to 525 °C. Orientation-robust 3D pore/solid segmentation was obtained using three 2D U-Net models trained on longitudinal, radial, and tangential slice sets and fused by majority vote. Steady incompressible creeping-flow simulations, with Re ≪ 1, were then performed in OpenFOAM using simpleFoam to compute the full permeability tensor. Sensitivity analyses and a permeability-based REV study selected a representative cube size of 390 µm, corresponding to 1300³ voxels. Pyrolysis slightly increased porosity and shifted local pore diameters toward smaller values. Longitudinal and radial permeabilities decreased by 47% and 24%, whereas tangential permeability increased by a factor of 5.86, substantially reducing anisotropy. These trends indicate that pyrolysis restructures transport primarily by modifying constrictions and transverse connectivity rather than uniformly enlarging conduits.

verified_metadata.title: Self-assembled carbon dot-based biochip for ultrasensitive multiplex biomarker detection and machine learning-assisted diagnosis of esophageal carcinoma
verified_metadata.abstract: Early diagnosis and timely treatment of esophageal cancer (EC) remain challenging due to the lack of ultrasensitive, high-throughput, rapid, and minimally invasive approaches for multiplex protein biomarker detection in biofluids. In this study, we developed a highly efficient carbon dots (CDs)-assembled immunoassay biochip for the simultaneous detection and evaluation of six EC-related biomarkers, including CEA, CA199, CA724, HSP70, IL6, and IL8. The assembled CDs enhanced the biochip substrate by enabling high-density immobilization of capture antibody barcodes through π–π stacking and hydrogen bonding, while their surface-proximity-dependent fluorescence quenching capability effectively reduced nonspecific background fluorescence. This design achieved both high capture antibody immobilization efficiency and efficient quenching of nonspecific signals. The immunoassay biochip enabled rapid multiplex detection with a total assay time of approximately 45 min, with limits of detection (LODs) reaching the pg/mL level. The combined biomarker panels exhibited superior diagnostic capability in terms of sensitivity and specificity, with the six-marker combination providing the highest diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, machine-learning analysis demonstrated the diagnostic potential of the six-biomarker panel for distinguishing EC patients, including different TNM-defined subgroups, from healthy donors, with accuracies generally exceeding 90%. Owing to its excellent stability, ultrasensitivity, high throughput, and reproducibility, this immunoassay biochip holds great promise for minimally invasive EC diagnosis, disease-stage assessment, and evaluation of therapeutic outcomes.

verified_metadata.title: Hyperbranched network engineering enables tissue-soft, low-hysteresis and ultrastretchable hydrogel strain sensors for machine learning-assisted fruit recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Hydrogel strain sensors are promising for soft robotics and wearable electronics, but their sensing accuracy is often compromised by hysteresis arising from irreversible chain rearrangement and energy dissipation. Here, we develop a multiple reversible physical crosslinking strategy to regulate polymer-chain topology and reinforce a polymerized network through reversible multivalent interactions, thereby producing a low-hysteresis and highly stretchable (LHS) conducting polymer hydrogel. The optimized hydrogel exhibits a low Young's modulus of approximately 17 kPa, comparable in magnitude to the modulus reported for soft brain tissue, together with an elongation at break of approximately 2200%, and an electrical hysteresis ratio of 0.76% at 400% strain. The resultant strain sensor provides reversible strain-dependent resistance responses, a maximum gauge factor of 2.4, and stable operation. When four sensors are integrated into a robotic hand, the multichannel signals capture fruit-specific grasping characteristics. Coupling these signals with a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network enables the classification of five fruits with an accuracy of 98.66%. These results demonstrate that hyperbranched topology regulation offers an effective route for constructing low-hysteresis conducting polymer hydrogels for high-fidelity robotic perception.

title: Fidelity-aware machine learning for reliable screening of low melting-point molten salts from heterogeneous experimental data

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多保真组合神经模型分级预训练微调，整合异质实验筛选低熔点储热熔盐。

verified_metadata.title: Fidelity-aware machine learning for reliable screening of low melting-point molten salts from heterogeneous experimental data
verified_metadata.abstract: Low melting-point salts may lower auxiliary-heating demand and increase the operational flexibility of thermal-energy-storage systems. Reliable machine learning (ML) screening of low melting point molten salts requires exploiting broad literature evidence while calibrating predictions against standardized measurements. Here, a fidelity-aware ML framework based on fidelity-separated fine-tuning is developed for nitrate/nitrite salts by pretraining a composition-based neural model on 5892 records from 593 publications and recalibrating only its final prediction layer using 107 unified-protocol measurements. Four neural data-utilization strategies and two regularized regression baselines are compared through composition-grouped cross-validation; the four neural strategies are further evaluated using an independent post-development measurement set comprising six predefined salt families (S1–S6). The conventional neural strategies show residual average bias or a larger fitted-to-held-out error increase on the standardized dataset. The fidelity-aware strategy achieves a held-out-group mean absolute error (MAE) of 17.9 °C, a mean signed error of +1.1 °C, and a 3.0 °C fitted-to-held-out MAE gap. At the predefined 150 °C cutoff for this screening task, it retains all five candidate families subsequently confirmed below the cutoff, whereas literature-only, standardized-data-only, and direct-mixing strategies would have rejected four, three, and two families, respectively. Among the four neural strategies assessed independently, only the fidelity-aware strategy retains salt families S3 and S4, which are experimentally confirmed with family mean transition temperatures of 130.9 and 99.2 °C. Across six independent family means, the model achieves an MAE of 19.9 °C and a root mean square error of 23.9 °C. These results support separating broad representation learning from standardized final-scale calibration for candidate retention in nitrate/nitrite screening on the measurement scale used here.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-guided prediction and design of coal-based carbon materials toward enhanced specific capacitance for supercapacitors
verified_metadata.abstract: Supercapacitors are promising energy-storage devices whose specific capacitance (SC) can be effectively improved through the proper design of electrode materials. Coal-derived carbon materials have attracted increasing attention as supercapacitor electrode candidates, yet their design remains heavily dependent on trial-and-error experimentation, making the optimization of SC performance inefficient and costly. Herein, a machine learning-assisted approach is proposed for SC prediction and regulation of coal-based carbon materials. Specifically, an XGB-SC model is developed to rapidly predict the SC, showing good predictive performance (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 24.57 F g−1), thereby enabling the rapid screening of high-performance electrode candidates. Interpretable analysis methods further identify specific surface area (SSA) as the dominant feature governing SC prediction and reveal its favorable range, thereby providing guidance for the design of electrode materials. A workflow integrating the XGB-SC model, the XGB-SSA model and a coal property dataset is then constructed to demonstrate the data-driven design of high-SC coal-based activated carbon electrodes. Using this workflow, a Yulin coal sample is identified as a promising precursor among more than 100 coal samples. The resulting activated carbon delivers a SC of 354.5 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 in a three-electrode system and also exhibits favorable performance in a symmetric device. This work may facilitate the screening and development of coal-based carbon electrodes with high SC, while providing a useful reference for the rational design of supercapacitor electrode materials.

title: Physically constrained machine-learning design of high-entropy BaTiO₃-based ceramics for capacitive energy storage

verified_metadata.title: Physically constrained machine-learning design of high-entropy BaTiO₃-based ceramics for capacitive energy storage
verified_metadata.abstract: Lead-free BaTiO3-based dielectrics are candidates for high-power pulse capacitors, yet the high-entropy (Ba,A)(Ti,B)O3 compositional space at 1 mol% resolution exceeds 105 plausible combinations, making exhaustive experimental screening impractical. Here, we integrate physical constraints, including composition windows, charge balance, tolerance factor, and configurational entropy, into a machine-learning workflow to navigate this compositional space. Using a dataset of 126 reported BaTiO3-based ceramics, we construct a 61-feature physicochemical descriptor set spanning A-/B-site elemental properties, local bonding, structural stability, and thermodynamic characteristics, and reduce it to 11 core descriptors by correlation filtering and recursive feature elimination. Compared with a field-only baseline, incorporating the intrinsic compositional descriptors increases the pooled out-of-fold R2 from 0.744 to 0.842 and reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) by 29.9%, demonstrating that the model captures composition-related information beyond the field-dependent trend. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further identifies the applied electric field and B-site local bonding descriptors as the dominant predictors of recoverable energy density. The model-predicted optimal composition, (Ba0.65Bi0.30Ca0.05)(Ti0.70Mg0.15Zr0.15)O3, forms a pseudocubic perovskite with homogeneous elemental distribution and relaxor dielectric behavior, delivering Wrec = 6.6 J cm−3 and η = 91.7% at 540 kV cm−1. The ceramic exhibits stable frequency (10–500 Hz), temperature (20–180 °C), and cycling (104 cycles) responses, while Weibull breakdown analysis indicates reliable dielectric breakdown behavior associated with the dense microstructure and homogeneous solid solution. This work shows that physically constrained machine learning can effectively navigate high-entropy perovskite composition space, providing an interpretable and transferable route for designing lead-free ABO3 capacitive energy-storage ceramics.

verified_metadata.title: Flexible temperature sensor based on SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 thermoelectric materials for respiratory monitoring and machine learning-assisted material identification
verified_metadata.abstract: Flexible thermoelectric sensors that combine temperature sensitivity, mechanical compliance, and long-term stability are important for wearable electronics. Herein, we fabricated a flexible single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT)/Ni3(HITP)2-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film (SNPF) via an ultrasound-assisted, water bath-confined in situ growth method followed by single-sided PDMS encapsulation. Ni3(HITP)2 nanocrystals were anchored onto the surfaces of SWCNT forming an integrated conductive network. Benefiting from the unique interfacial structure of SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2, the optimized SNPF exhibited a Seebeck coefficient of 44.7 μV/K. The SNPF device exhibited exceptional temperature sensing performance, featuring a high resolution (0.5 K) and outstanding long-term stability over 500 cycles, rendering it suitable for both contact/non-contact thermal source identification and passive respiratory monitoring. Furthermore, a multilayer SNPFs device constructed by vertically stacking and electrically connecting five films demonstrated an enhanced equivalent Seebeck coefficient of 221 μV/K. When worn on the arm outdoors, this device generated an open-circuit voltage of 1.33 mV and an output power of 0.67 nW. In addition, transient thermoelectric responses generated during contact with seven materials were analyzed using machine-learning algorithms. The ExtraTrees model achieved a test accuracy of 98.04% under the present recording-level data-splitting protocol. These results demonstrate that SWCNT/Ni3(HITP)2 composites can serve as flexible thermoelectric platforms for temperature sensing, low-level body-heat-derived signal generation, and thermoelectric material recognition.

title: Machine learning-optimized design principles for multiple-resonance TADF emitters in organic light-emitting diodes

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。XGBoost由分子数据库预测TADF发光体结构性质，指导OLED分子设计并实验验证。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-optimized design principles for multiple-resonance TADF emitters in organic light-emitting diodes
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of multiple-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters is critical for advancing organic light-emitting diodes. However, navigating the highly constrained chemical space of these emitters requires moving beyond empirical trial-and-error. Here, we present an experimentally validated, machine-learning-guided molecular-design workflow to accelerate the targeted optimization of double‑boron MR-TADF materials. We constructed a database of over 400 MR-TADF molecules from scratch and trained an XGBoost model (test R2 = 0.77) to establish a statistical framework. This framework systematically quantifies the multi-parameter trade-offs associated with boron substitution patterns, π-conjugation positions, and heterocycle conjugation degrees. To validate this predictive workflow, we synthesized a double‑boron derivative, DPAC-DB, which possesses a moderate experimental ΔEST of 0.14 eV, close to our estimated value of 0.17 eV. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs based on DPAC-DB achieved a maximum external quantum efficiency of 35.6%, significantly outperforming its mono‑boron parent. By successfully translating computational prioritization into a highly efficient physical device, this work establishes a robust, data-driven paradigm for the rational optimization of MR-TADF emitters.

verified_metadata.title: One-pot, ultrasensitive duplex genotyping of ctDNA in lung cancer via machine learning-assisted SERS spectral decoding
verified_metadata.abstract: Precision treatment of lung cancer relies on accurate mutation profiling. Although minimally invasive, liquid biopsy is constrained by low ctDNA abundance and insufficient sensitivity for low-frequency mutations. To address this challenge, a catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA)-triggered magnetic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) system was developed to accurately identify dual EGFR mutation subtypes in serum samples simultaneously. Driven by a target-initiated CHA reaction, a core-satellite nanostructure is constructed, which integrates plasmonic magnetic nanoparticles (NPs) embedded with a silent-region Raman internal standard and SERS-encoded Au@gap@Au NPs. Integrating hierarchical hot spots with internal calibration enhances quantitative reliability, enabling a broad dynamic range and enzyme-free attomolar sensitivity within a 2-h isothermal reaction. To further improve analytical precision, the narrow Raman spectral footprints were coupled with an OPLS-DA algorithm, achieving exceptional classification accuracy with an AUC of 1.00 for distinct EGFR mutation subtypes in cellular assays. Clinical proof-of-concept validation in a serum cohort comprising 39 individuals showed reliable profiling performance, with concordance of next-generation sequencing results. Owing to its robust one-pot multiplexing capability, low instrumental demands and stable analytical performance, the machine learning-assisted, CHA-triggered magnetic SERS system offers a powerful strategy for ctDNA genotyping, holding significant promise for advancing personalized and precision medicine in lung cancer.

title: From waste to wideband: achieving ultra-broadband absorption with bio-inspired, machine learning-optimized metamaterials
abstract: The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave-absorbing materials that combine cost efficiency and environmental sustainability remains a critical challenge in the fields of functional materials and stealth technology. Although the magnetoelectric coupling strategy has emerged as an important approach for designing high-performance absorbers by introducing magnetic loss and improving impedance matching, its ability to enhance absorption bandwidth remains limited, thereby restricting its application in scenarios requiring broadband absorption. To address this issue, this study proposes an innovative strategy for fabricating a hierarchical composite absorber derived from waste-based activated carbon spheres (ACSs). Inspired by natural biological structures, a sweet potato leaf-inspired electromagnetic wave absorber (SPL) has been designed. Leveraging electromagnetic wave localization theory and machine learning-assisted structural optimization, the resulting SPL successfully maximizes the localization of electromagnetic waves within the material distribution region. This leads to exceptional electromagnetic wave absorption performance, achieving a reflectivity below -10 dB across the entire 3–50 GHz frequency range at a matching thickness of only 10 mm. Simultaneously, owing to the inherent absorption characteristics of the activated carbon base, the composite retains its excellent capacity for adsorbing harmful gases. This work not only provides a high-performance, low-cost, and multifunctional electromagnetic wave absorber but also offers valuable insights into the value-added reuse of waste resources and the rational design of bio-inspired structures for advanced electromagnetic protection applications in both military and civilian architectural domains.

title: Co-optimization of algorithm and sensor array for precise diagnosis of HER2-positive breast cancer and trastuzumab response prediction
abstract: Accurate and rapid diagnosis of human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer, coupled with prediction of trastuzumab therapeutic efficacy, is critical for clinical decision-making to the patients with breast cancer. However, there is still no standard to be clinically used without suffering from inherent limitations. In this work, we propose a machine learning-assisted multifunctional biosensing platform utilizing enzyme-embedded hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs). In this design, diverse HOFs@enzyme composites with distinct assembly configurations serve as sensitive array elements to interact with breast cancer-derived exosomes. Moreover, these interactions can modulate HOF-enzyme activity, generating diagnostic signal patterns that form unique exosomal molecular “fingerprint” profiles. Simultaneously, coordination with machine learning enables processing of complex sensor array-based data to amplify subtle differences of exosome between different subtypes of breast cancer, thereby enhancing the discriminatory capacity of this platform. By establishing reference fingerprints using exosomes from 96 training-set patients and validating classification accuracy against immunohistochemical in 76 test-set patients, the platform achieved 100% concordance in identifying the HER2-positive subtype, demonstrating exceptional discriminative capacity. Remarkably, the platform can also predict trastuzumab treatment response with 87.5% accuracy through clinical outcome correlation. So, by enabling precise exosome characterization from peripheral blood, this non-invasive liquid biopsy technology offers a transformative approach for precision oncology in HER2-positive breast cancer, overcoming critical limitations of current diagnostic paradigms.

title: Sn-Doped selector-only memory with stable threshold voltage margin for robust binary neural network inference
abstract: Abstract With the rise of data-centric applications such as edge AI and neuromorphic computing, there is increasing demand for memory solutions that overcome the limitations of conventional nonvolatile devices. Selector-only memory (SOM), which stores data through threshold voltage (V th ) modulation in chalcogenide-based selector materials, offers a compact and scalable alternative. However, narrow read window margins and V th drift remain major reliability concerns. In this work, we introduce a Sn-doped GeSbSeTe (Sn-GSST) material system that enhances SOM performance by reducing trap depth, increasing the population of shallow band-tail trap states, and widening the V th margin. These improvements enable stable multibit switching and improved endurance. We evaluate the device’s system-level applicability through binary neural network (BNN) inference on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset, where V th -induced bit error rate (BER) are modeled using statistical distributions. Sn-GSST devices show significantly lower BER of less than 0.01, leading to improved inference robustness. Finally, Shannon entropy-based error correction code (ECC) analysis confirms that the reduced BER of Sn-GSST leads to lower redundancy overhead and higher inference efficiency. This study demonstrates how material-level engineering can directly translate to system-level reliability and performance in neuromorphic memory applications.

title: Computational strategies for designing PEDOT-Based electrodes in electronic applications
abstract: Abstract Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) and its derivatives have emerged as critical materials in modern electronic applications due to their exceptional electrical conductivity, biocompatibility, and processability. This comprehensive review examines the state-of-the-art computational strategies employed for designing and optimizing PEDOT-based electrodes across various electronic applications. We systematically assess multiscale modeling approaches, from quantum mechanical calculations to macroscopic device simulations, including Density Functional Theory (DFT), atomistic and coarse-grained Molecular Dynamics (MD), Finite Element Method (FEM), and emerging Machine Learning/Artificial Intelligence techniques. The review elucidates how these computational methods provide critical insights into PEDOT’s electronic structure, charge transport mechanisms, morphological characteristics, and interfacial behaviors. Particular emphasis is placed on structure-property relationships, including the aromatic-to-quinoid transition upon doping, the formation of polarons and bipolarons, the influence of π-π stacking on charge mobility, and the critical role of counterions in modulating electronic performance. We demonstrate their application in designing optimized electrodes for supercapacitors, organic electrochemical transistors, and flexible electronics. Finally, we analyze existing limitations in current computational frameworks and identify promising future directions, including multiscale integration, improved force fields, and quantum machine learning, that will accelerate the rational design of next-generation PEDOT-based materials with tailored functionalities. Graphical Abstract This review highlights the integration of computational strategies like DFT, MD, FEM, and ML/AI in designing PEDOT-based electrodes, emphasizing their role in understanding electronic structure, charge transport, morphology, and mechanical behavior. It explores recent advancements, applications, limitations, and future directions for optimizing PEDOT electrodes in electronic devices.

title: Leveraging explainable AI in the design of carbon composites with high thermal conductivity for thermal management
abstract: Achieving high thermal conductivity in polymer composites with low filler loading is crucial for thermal management. Constructing continuous and directional carbon networks has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance thermal conductivity. However, challenges remain, including the absence of accurate predictive models and explainable optimization strategies. In this study, we propose a design methodology leveraging explainable AI to optimize geometric patterns formed by carbon fillers, with a focus on sub-10 wt% carbon content. High-throughput finite element simulations are employed to generate datasets for prediction models, which incorporated variables including filler content, interfacial conductivity, connectivity, and gap distance. Symbolic regression yields predictive equations for thermal conductivity with high accuracy (R 2 > 0.99), and SHAP analysis identifies the filler connectivity and content as key determinants. As a proof of concept, graphene-based composites with continuous and directional networks achieve thermal conductivities exceeding 33 W m − 1 K − 1 , demonstrating that sub-10 wt% carbon fillers can reach high thermal conductivities, achieving high directional conductivity without requiring high global loading in composites. This work establishes an explainable AI-driven strategy for enhancing thermal conductivity in low-content carbon composites, expanding their applications in thermal management.

title: Zinc oxide photocatalysis for pollutant degradation: a review of elemental doping, morphology, and microstructure, integrated with machine learning-based performance modelling
abstract: ZnO nanoparticles are effective photocatalysts for the degradation of organic pollutants; however, there are gaps of knowledge about the effects of their morphology, microstructure, doping elements, and estimation of photocatalytic performance. Accordingly, the effects of morphology, microstructure, and elemental doping are reviewed first. Notably, ZnO microstructure is an important parameter influencing its photocatalytic performance. Specifically, the wurtzite phase, which is the most stable phase of ZnO, has been widely utilized in photocatalytic applications. However, the rocksalt phase of ZnO, a metastable phase, could exhibit higher photocatalytic activity than both wurtzite ZnO and anatase TiO2. In addition to the review study, robust machine learning algorithms, including coupled simulated annealing-least square support vector machine, decision tree-particle swarm optimization, random forest- particle swarm optimization, and extreme gradient boosting-particle swarm optimization, were used to predict the photodegradation yield of various pollutants. The prediction is based on various parameters, including the molecular weight of the pollutants and dopants, topological polar surface area, hydrogen bond donor count, hydrogen bond acceptor count of the pollutants, initial concentration of pollutant, solution pH, light source, weight ratio of doping element to Zn, dosage of catalyst, and reaction time, using ZnO-based photocatalysts. A comprehensive dataset of 1176 entries was gathered from 22 different sources. To the best of our knowledge, for the first time in the field of photocatalysis, a web-based model using extreme gradient boosting-particle swarm optimization method has been developed in Python. This model can be easily accessed online to predict the photodegradation efficiency of various pollutants using ZnO-based photocatalysts.

title: Shape memory smart textile composites open a new era of human limb function rehabilitation: principles, design and applications
abstract: The evolution of rehabilitation aids from passive mechanical devices to intelligent systems is reshaping human motor function recovery. However, traditional orthoses often lack adaptability and comfort, highlighting the need for advanced material solutions. This review systematically explores the role of Shape Memory Textile Composites (SMTCs) in limb orthotics, bridging material science with clinical rehabilitation. We first analyze biomechanical regulation strategies for distinct limb deformities to establish design requirements. Subsequently, we discuss how SMTCs leverage advanced resin matrices and intelligent textile structures to resolve the inherent conflict between mechanical support and physiological compliance, emphasizing their environmental adaptability and active responsiveness. Furthermore, we propose a closed loop rehabilitation paradigm that integrates multi source sensing with artificial intelligence algorithms. The study concludes that fusing SMTCs with intelligent systems facilitates a transition from passive support to active neural remodeling, offering a critical pathway for next generation precision rehabilitation ecosystems.

title: Research advances towards multidimensional signal processing strategies for polymeric multimodal flexible sensors
abstract: The inherent advantages of polymer materials, such as excellent flexibility, processability, and molecular structure tunability, make them critical materials for fabrication of multimodal flexible sensors, which can be applicated in complex scenarios to perceive and monitor diverse stimuli, particularly in physiological signal acquisition and human-machine interaction. However, the widespread existence of signal crosstalk and coupling phenomena, which originate from the intrinsic material properties and device integration strategies, severely compromise the performance and reliability of multimodal flexible sensors. This paper systematically reviews the strategies of signal processing to identify the correct signal for multimodal flexible sensors from multiple perspectives, containing signal processing based on material combination, structural optimization, differences of signal response characteristics, and artificial intelligence technology. Previously, the basic structural composition, commonly used materials, fundamental sensing mechanisms and common fabrication methods of flexible sensors are systematically introduced. Signal decoupling by extracting the characteristic differences of output signals in terms of sensing behavior dependent on test condition, time response and variations in amplitude, and utilizing differential measurement techniques are systematically discussed. Moreover, the fundamental types and principles of machine learning algorithms, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them are also introduced in detail before discussing their application in signal decoupling and recognition. Simultaneously, the advantages of signal processing strategies based on machine learning compared with traditional signal processing strategies and their current limitations are elaborated in detail. Finally, the paper summarizes the persistent challenges in multimodal flexible sensing and offers a forward-looking perspective on the developmental trajectory of polymeric multimodal sensors, with the goal of providing a reference for future research and promoting the practical application of multimodal flexible sensors.

title: Introducing a novel epoxy adhesive with BCP and calixarene for aluminum- aluminum bonded joints: a complete picture applying thermomechanical analyses and ANN modeling
abstract: This study proposes a novel hybrid modification strategy to enhance the mechanical performance, thermal stability, and lap shear strength of epoxy-based structural adhesives by incorporating p-tert-butyl calix[4]arene (C4A) as a reinforcing agent and poly(butyl acrylate-block-vinyl acetate) block copolymer as a toughening agent. C4A particles were successfully synthesized and characterized. Tensile and single-lap shear tests were conducted to evaluate bulk mechanical properties and adhesion performance. The curing behavior and thermal stability were investigated using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), respectively. The fracture morphology of optimized samples was examined by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and an artificial neural network (ANN) model was developed to predict mechanical responses. The results show that the simultaneous incorporation of 3 phr copolymer and 3 phr C4A increased tensile strength, tensile modulus, and toughness by 34%, 48%, and 270%, respectively, compared with neat epoxy. The optimized formulation exhibited a lap shear strength of 11.6 MPa, representing a 68% improvement and demonstrating a pronounced synergistic effect between the two modifiers. Contact angle measurements revealed a 39° decrease, indicating enhanced wettability on aluminum substrates. DSC results showed a 5 °C reduction in the onset curing temperature, suggesting improved curing behavior. TGA confirmed enhanced thermal stability, with the onset degradation temperature (Ti) and maximum degradation temperature (Tmax) increasing by 55 °C and 50 °C, respectively. The ANN model achieved high prediction accuracy, with a mean relative error (MRE) below 1.4%.

title: Temporal control engineering in 4D printing materials for adaptive systems: a biomedical perspective
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) printing introduces time as an explicit design parameter, enabling materials to undergo programmed transformations in response to environmental stimuli across timescales from milliseconds to months. Existing reviews have largely organized the field around stimulus types, material classes, or application examples; however, a clear and actionable framework for translating time-domain requirements—such as response rate, programmed delay, and multi-stage sequencing—into material and structural design strategies is still lacking. Here, we establish a temporal control engineering framework for 4D printing materials, categorizing systems into rapid-response, gradual-evolution, and sequential-response regimes based on transformation kinetics, and analyzing the physicochemical mechanisms governing their time-dependent behavior. By explicitly linking molecular architecture, transport constraints, and multiphase structural design to kinetic outcomes, this framework enables practical design rules for programming temporal behavior in adaptive systems. While the framework is broadly applicable, this review adopts a biomedical perspective, examining translational relevance in depth, with bone regeneration serving as a representative and clinically demanding model for time-critical functional adaptation. We further highlight emerging opportunities—including in situ characterization, advanced manufacturing strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven design—that may advance 4D printing from empirical material selection toward systematic temporal engineering. A comprehensive framework introducing temporal control engineering in 4D-printed materials for bone regeneration. The evolution from rapid-response through gradual-evolution to sequential-response mechanisms is systematically analyzed, emphasizing molecular architecture-kinetics relationships and spatiotemporal synchronization with biological healing cascades for patient-specific therapeutic applications.

title: Sustainable hybrid rubber nanocomposites: a review of green solvents processing and machine learning-driven optimization
abstract: The rubber industry faces increasing pressure to transition from energy-intensive, fossil-fuel-based processing to sustainable manufacturing. This review critically assesses the development of green rubber hybrid nanocomposites, focusing on the synergistic integration of green solvents-specifically Ionic Liquids (ILs) and Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs)-with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) optimization. We first evaluate the efficacy of ILs and DESs as sustainable alternatives to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) for enhancing hybrid nanofiller dispersion (e.g., silica and carbon black) and interfacial compatibility. A comparative analysis highlights that while ILs offer superior thermal stability and tunability, DESs present a more viable pathway for industrial scale-up due to their biodegradability, significantly lower cost, and ease of synthesis. Secondly, to address the high dimensionality and time constraints of optimizing these novel multi-component hybrid formulations, we review recent ML-driven approaches. We demonstrate how data-driven algorithms, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), accelerate material discovery by accurately predicting key rheological and mechanical properties, thereby clarifying complex structure-property relationships and reducing the reliance on traditional trial-and-error experimentation. Herein, we conclude by identifying a critical research opportunity: the convergence of green solvent chemistry with computational intelligence offers a robust framework for designing the next generation of high-performance, environmentally sustainable elastomers.

title: Synergistic development of micro/nano fabrication for lab-on-the-needle devices: Recent advances, biomedical applications, and challenges
abstract: Lab-on-the-needle (LON) devices fabricated with micro/nanotechnology-derived methods have shown considerable attention towards the development a new type of biosensor and diagnostic device that addresses the challenges and limitations that remain in the conventional system. In particular, these LON devices, consisting of either a LON patch or a micro/nanopipette tip (M/NPT), have been emerging as a new technological frontier in biomedical analysis. This phenomenon is because of their high aspect ratio and geometrical dimensions, as well as their needle-like biomimetic structural strategy, portability, and functionalization with nanomaterials and coatings. Moreover, by leveraging recent advances in the LON patch and M/NPT platforms, they have received significant attention in biomedical and clinical settings, particularly for biomolecule and neurochemical detection, disease diagnosis, and bioimaging. This review article provides a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements to the fabrication of the LON patch and M/NPT platform, including the focus on 3D printing and pulling approaches, followed by the functionalization and coating with nanomaterials. Furthermore, it analyzes and discusses the improved detection of specific biomolecules and neurochemicals through colorimetric, electrochemical, and Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) methods utilizing the LON patch and M/NPT platform. This approach results in low cost, minimal invasiveness, and increased patient comfort. Nevertheless, it is essential to address the challenges of its unique capabilities and the gap between the LON patch and the M/NPT platform to design a hybrid system that integrates detection, diagnostics, and treatment technologies on a single LON platform. Therefore, we present a forward-looking view on next-generation hybrid LON systems, which utilize functionalized nanomaterials and coatings. Furthermore, we have discussed the challenges of incorporating nanomaterials with LON by using the AI/ML predictive analysis model tool and translational approach for real-time detection and diagnosis in future biomedical and clinical settings.

title: Oxygen vacancy-mediated linear, long-term retention weight tuning in amorphous ITZO optoelectronic synapses for high-performance neuromorphic visual systems
abstract: Optoelectronic synaptic devices featuring linear weight updates are essential for high-precision visual information perception, storage, and processing, meeting high-efficiency and low-power demands in artificial visual systems. This study leverages the oxygen vacancy states in amorphous indium-tin-zinc oxide (ITZO) to design Al/ITZO/Al two-terminal optoelectronic synaptic devices with highly linear weight updates and long-term retention of light-encoded information. A large number of oxygen vacancy defect levels with a broad energy distribution in ITZO thin films provide efficient pathways for carriers to transition under illuminations with sub-bandgap energy and allow carriers to be stored in these defect levels for an extended period, providing conditions for linearly enhanced weight updates and long-term current retention. Devices with different oxygen vacancy concentrations exhibit stable synaptic characteristics, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF) index exceeding 190%, highly linear pulsed light-modulated plasticity (adjusted R 2 values of linear fitting ≥ 0.98), and learning-forgetting-relearning processes (standard deviation of ΔEPSC < 0.02%). In addition, the different “learning attitudes” (simulated by tuning oxygen vacancy concentrations to mimic neurotransmitter concentrations) are visualized via light-encoded images. Benefiting from the multi-level linearity and uniformly distributed photoresponse current, the devices are applicable for hexadecimal light-encoded information processing, image convolution processing, and image reconstruction with high fidelity. Notably, the ITZO(9:1:3) device simulates the fully opened eyelids and thus retains the most image information. When used for CIFAR-10 image classification in a convolutional neural network (CNN), it achieves an accuracy of 87.58%, verifying the potential of ITZO optoelectronic synapses in artificial vision systems.

title: Advanced design for electrochemically flexible iontronic tactile sensing
abstract: Abstract Electrochemically flexible iontronic tactile sensing (EFITS) has emerged as a promising technology in artificial touch, alleviating inherent limitations of traditional electronic sensors by emulating the ion-driven electrochemical transduction of biological skins. Enabled by advances in electrochemistry, materials science, structural design, interfacial engineering, advanced manufacturing, and artificial intelligence, EFITS can convert mechanical stimuli into electrochemical signals, featuring high sensitivity over wide pressure range, low limit of detection, reliable long-term operation, and intelligent recognition. With electrochemical double-layer capacitive iontronic tactile sensing emerged, pseudocapacitive and battery-type devices have shown promising developments in EFITS. However, a systematic overview of advanced EFITS remains lacking. Herein, we comprehensively review the latest advancements in EFITS. Beginning with the electrochemical tactile sensing principles, we critically summarize progress in composite materials, device architectures, and micro-nano interfaces, followed by an examination of fabrication strategies. We further carry out a statistical comparison of key performance metrics to enable quantitative benchmarking across high-performance EFITS devices and highlight representative applications in healthcare, environmental monitoring, human-machine interaction, and intelligent robotics. Finally, we discuss interdisciplinary challenges and outline possible pathways toward fully adaptive, intelligent, and durable EFITS, aiming to provide a consolidated understanding and guidance for future research. title: Modulation strategies of nanozyme activity applied to food quality and safety analysis: From rational design to intelligent assistance
abstract: Nanozymes combine the catalytic properties of natural enzymes with the distinctive structural features of nanomaterials, offering significant potential for applications in food quality and safety analysis. Machine learning (ML) algorithms enable precise control over the active sites and electronic structures of nanozymes by integrating data mining, predictive modeling, and theoretical calculations. This review systematically summarizes key strategies for enhancing nanozyme activity, including morphology modulation, optimization of interfacial electron transfer, micro-environment engineering and ML-assisted design, and highlights their emerging applications in food quality and safety analysis. Particular emphasis is placed on ML-enabled high-throughput screening, which elucidates complex structure–activity relationships, accelerates the identification of high-performance nanozymes, and supports their practical application in food contaminants detection, product quality monitoring, and adulteration identification. The current challenges and future prospects for ML-assisted activity modulation, with the aim of advancing both nanozyme engineering and their translation for food quality and safety field.

title: Nano-engineered precision strategies for hematological malignancies: current advances and translational roadmap
abstract: Hematological malignancies (HMs), encompassing acute and chronic leukemia, malignant lymphoma, and multiple myeloma (MM), are among the most lethal cancers globally. Their high mortality is driven by complex genomic alterations, protective effects of the bone marrow (BM) and lymph node microenvironments, and systemic dissemination. Despite advances in chemotherapy, radiotherapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and targeted or immunotherapies, patients continue to face significant challenges, including drug resistance, treatment-related toxicity, and difficulties in disease monitoring and relapse prevention. To overcome these limitations, research has increasingly focused on nanomaterials. With tunable sizes and programmable surface chemistries, nanocarriers can evade immune surveillance in circulation, preferentially accumulate in BM and lymphoid tissues, and facilitate site-specific drug release within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Moreover, they can integrate multiple therapeutic and diagnostic functionalities, including magnetothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy (PDT), imaging, and immune modulation, positioning them as powerful platforms for integrated diagnosis and treatment. Consequently, nanomedicine is emerging as a critical link between the complex pathology of HMs and the clinical need for precise, individualized interventions. In this review, we first elucidate the biological foundations of therapeutic challenges in HMs and highlight the potential of nanomedicine to address these obstacles. We then categorize and summarize the structural characteristics and biological behaviors of five major classes of nanoplatforms applied to HMs: inorganic, polymeric, hybrid, biogenic, and stimuli-responsive systems. Key advances and representative studies are presented to illustrate how nanomaterials enhance treatment, diagnosis, disease monitoring, and theranostic applications. Finally, we discuss the primary barriers to clinical translation, including scalable GMP-compliant manufacturing, reliable in vivo predictability, and rigorous regulatory assessment, and propose potential solutions such as artificial intelligence (AI)­driven design, modular continuous-flow production, and adaptive clinical trial frameworks. By connecting disease-driven requirements with rational material design and clinical validation, this review provides a comprehensive reference to advance nanotechnology-enabled precision medicine and improve long-term outcomes in HMs.

title: Self-powered human motion health monitoring and machine learning analysis system based on magnetic implantable triboelectric nanogenerators
abstract: To break through the bottlenecks of traditional implantable medical devices, which rely on limited-life batteries and lack intelligent analysis capabilities. This research has developed an innovative solution that combines self-powered with intelligent monitoring. Distinct from existing biocompatible TENGs, this work features a unique design of the polyethylene oxide/BaTiO 3 /Fe 3 O 4 (PBF) composite film. In this design, Polyethylene oxide served as the biocompatible matrix, BaTiO 3 acted as the triboelectric performance enhancer, and Fe 3 O 4 functioned as the magnetic functional component. This rational combination overcame the inherent defects of a single material and achieved a synergistic effect of biocompatibility, high triboelectric performance, and macroscopic magnetism. Based on the potential of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) in self-powered sensing and the utilization of endogenous mechanical energy in the human body (e.g. heartbeat and breathing), this research synthesized a biocompatible PBF composite film. This film effectively enhances its triboelectric properties and endows the material with macroscopic magnetism by introducing functional components. After assembly with the silicone triboelectric layer, a biocompatible implantable TENG (BI-TENG) was constructed. The electrical output performance of this BI-TENG is outstanding, featuring an open-circuit voltage of 286.1 V, a short-circuit current of 19.3 µA, and a peak output power density reaching 951.2 mW·m − 2 . Furthermore, this research also constructed a BI-TENG-machine learning (ML) collaborative intelligent system. A key contribution of this work is the validation that the BI-TENG-ML system can not only utilize BI-TENG to monitor motion signals in real time but also conduct accurate intelligent analysis of these high-dimensional and nonlinear signals through ML technology, overcoming the limitation of traditional threshold-based signal interpretation. It aims to achieve more intelligent and proactive health monitoring and disease management, laying the foundation for the next generation of permanent self-powered intelligent implantable systems.

title: A tutorial review on designing pluripotent olefinic hybrids via covalent adaptable networks: integrating dynamic chemistry with machine‑learning
abstract: Olefinic polymers form the basis of modern materials infrastructure; however, their low recyclability leads to irreversible environmental accumulation. Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have emerged as a highly attractive approach to address these challenges by incorporating dynamic covalent bonds that reversibly crosslink, thereby restoring mechanical performance. Furthermore, they impart true pluripotency (the ability to regenerate their pristine characteristics) to olefinic polymers, enabling unimpeded upcycling. This review critically analyzes the design, synthesis, and structure-property relationships of covalent adaptable networks in olefin-based hybrid materials, including transesterification, disulfide metathesis, imine exchange, silyl-ether exchange, olefin metathesis, and related dynamic motifs. The aim of this review is to examine how these approaches are leveraged to deliver advanced materials with functions such as reprocessability, self-healing, weldability, shape memory, improved creep resistance, and mixed-waste compatibilization. Beyond these experimental breakthroughs, this review highlights the expanding intersections between computational modeling and machine-learning algorithms, thereby facilitating the understanding of mechanisms in dynamic bonds, prediction of rheological and thermomechanical properties, and inverse design of vitrimer networks. Molecular-level chemical designs combined with machine-learning algorithms seek to redefine the polyolefin lifecycle. This review critically introduces how covalent adaptable networks generate pluripotent olefinic hybrids with tunable mechanical and dynamic properties. By integrating reversible bonding motifs with machine learning driven design, the review uncovers structure-reactivity relationships that accelerate materials discovery towards truly pluripotent polyolefin-based plastics

title: Enhanced non-invasive and non-enzymatic detection of Saliva glucose using CuO nanoparticles modified CuO nanorods: An experimental and machine learning modelling of electrochemical sensing
abstract: The conventional monitoring of blood glucose is invasive, painful, and often inhibits patient compliance, driving the urgent need for reliable, non-invasive alternatives. This research work investigated the fabrication of a CuO nanoparticles modified CuO nanorods (CuONP/CuONR) based high-performance, non-enzymatic electrochemical glucose sensor electrode for the direct and non-invasive glucose detection in human saliva. The microstructural, optical and crystallinity structure of CuONP/CuONR were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), UV-visible optical spectroscopy (UV-Vis), Raman-spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Electrochemical glucose sensing performance of CuONP/CuONR were analysed using cyclic voltammetry (CV), square wave voltammetry (SWV), amperometric i-t and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The CuONP/CuONR electrode has demonstrated a fast glucose sensing response time, high linear glucose detection range (0 to 325 µM), high sensitivity (5272 µAmM −1 cm − 2 ), very good repeatability, reproductivity, stability and selectivity. Additionally, various machine learning model were also implemented to enhance the detection limit and increase the accuracy of glucose detection. The artificial neural network (ANN) model appeared as a most suitable ML model to interpret the current density vs. glucose concentration relationships, revealing the CuONP/CuONR electrode working capability in real-world application for high precision/intelligent healthcare system. The practical applicability of CuONP/CuONR was validated by successfully detecting glucose in human saliva and also correlated with blood glucose concentration, highlighting its potential as a scalable, cost-effective, non-enzyme and non-invasive platform for glucose sensing application.

title: Hosta-inspired hierarchical metamaterials for electromagnetic absorption: synergistic design of composition and structure
abstract: Integrating intrinsic material properties with structural design to develop lightweight electromagnetic wave absorbers that simultaneously balance impedance matching and energy dissipation remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the sophisticated multi-scale light-harvesting strategies found in Hosta, this study proposes a methodology that synergizes the intrinsic characteristics of materials with the physical effects of their structural configuration. Driven by fully connected neural networks and refined through optimization via genetic algorithms, the optimized material achieves an absorption rate exceeding 90% across the extremely wide frequency band of 1–40 GHz. Remarkably, this performance is accomplished with an areal density of only 0.096 g/cm 2 and a physical thickness equivalent to about 1/20 λ max . Electromagnetic simulations reveal that the deliberate modulation of the structural phase successfully localizes the electromagnetic energy loss domains precisely within the material distribution regions. Simultaneously, the synergy of magnetoelectric properties ensures the efficient and rapid dissipation of this captured energy. This innovative approach to synergistic design offers exceptional generalizability, providing a robust theoretical framework and technical inspiration for the future development of next-generation, lightweight metamaterials designed for ultra-broadband absorption. By bridging the gap between microscopic material responses and macroscopic structural layouts, this research paves the way for advanced shielding and stealth technologies that require minimal weight and maximum bandwidth efficiency in complex electromagnetic environments.

title: Green by design: self-assembly of plant natural products into nanoparticles – mechanisms, computational dissection, and comparison with synthetic systems
abstract: Natural products derived from plants exhibit substantial potential in the field of self-assembled nanoparticles, owing to their structural diversity, biocompatibility, and inherent bioactivity. However, the traditional “trial-and-error” research paradigm is inefficient, making it difficult to unravel complex assembly mechanisms and achieve precise regulation. Given the significant application potential and research value of computational technology and artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of natural product self-assembled nanotechnology, this review focuses on analyzing self-assembly mechanisms driven by computational techniques. Notably, this review presents the first analysis of the key differences in self-assembly driving forces and mechanisms between plant-derived natural product self-assembled nanoparticles (SA-PNP-NPs) and other self-assembly systems. This review then discusses the preparation strategies and the conditions required for the self-assembly of SA-PNP-NPs. Subsequently, the characterization techniques employed for these nanostructures are summarized. Finally, the practical application challenges of SA-PNP-NPs are analyzed. This work pioneers the introduction of a data-driven and model-guided paradigm into the fabrication of SA-PNP-NPs. This approach not only significantly accelerates scientific discovery and process development but, more importantly, enables the precise harnessing of natural principles. It facilitates the efficient conversion of structurally diverse and functionally rich plant-derived molecules into high-performance smart nanomaterials with broad applicability. The primary objective of this work is to provide theoretical guidance for the efficient and precise synthesis of self-assembled nanomaterials, thereby offering technical support for the development of advanced functional materials.

title: Advanced fluorescent materials for intelligent food freshness monitoring: design, mechanisms, and multi-target applications
abstract: Fluorescent biopolymer-based intelligent monitoring systems enable rapid, intuitive, and quantifiable optical transduction of chemical signals associated with food spoilage, including volatile bioamines, pH shifts, and redox reactions, representing a highly promising strategy for food freshness assessment and intelligent packaging. This review systematically outlines recent progress in the design and construction of such intelligent platforms by integrating five representative fluorescent materials—metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), metal nanoclusters (MNCs), carbon dots (CDs), aggregation-induced emission (AIE) materials, and fluorescent dyes—into biopolymer matrices including polysaccharides and proteins. Core stimulus–response mechanisms are comprehensively discussed, covering fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET), intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), and AIE, which collectively give rise to fluorescence enhancement/quenching, ratiometric responses, colorimetric transitions, and multichannel signal output. For lanthanide MOFs, particular emphasis is placed on the regulation of coordination chemistry, including metal nodes, ligand structures, pore microenvironments, and the antenna effect, which govern energy transfer efficiency, adsorption affinity toward biogenic amines, and sensing sensitivity. Representative applications of single-channel, multichannel, and monitoring–preservation integrated systems with antibacterial and antioxidant capabilities are comparatively evaluated in real food matrices such as meat, aquatic products, and dairy products, with key performance indicators including sensitivity, response time, stability, visualization efficiency, and practical applicability highlighted. Finally, critical challenges are identified concerning precise coordination structure modulation, signal stability in complex food environments, fluorescent component migration and biosafety, green scalable fabrication, and regulatory compliance. Future directions are also prospected, highlighting synergistic opportunities from coordination chemistry, high-throughput screening, machine learning, and sustainable biopolymer processing. This review provides theoretical support and design principles for developing robust, safe, reliable, and practically viable fluorescent biopolymer-based intelligent food monitoring systems.
