verified_metadata.title: Dual-stream adaptive graph convolutional network with enhanced skeleton representation for human-robot collaborative assembly intention recognition
verified_metadata.abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA), which combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, has become a core paradigm for smart manufacturing in Industry 5.0. Dynamic action intention recognition is a key technology for seamless human-robot interaction. However, the complexity of industrial assembly scenarios makes it difficult for collaborative robots to accurately understand the operator's assembly action intentions. Most existing methods rely on graph convolutional networks with fixed skeletal topologies, lacking the capability to capture cross-joint dependencies tailored to different action samples. These approaches depend on a single type of human skeletal feature (e.g., joint coordinates) and fail to effectively integrate multi-level dynamic information (e.g., joint trajectory kinematics and bone-level geometric transformations), resulting in an incomplete semantic representation of human action intention. To address these issues, this paper proposes an HRCA action intention recognition method based on a Dual-stream Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (DS-AGCN) model. Firstly, a simplified human skeletal structure is designed by removing redundant joints irrelevant to assembly actions, making it more suitable for recognizing upper-body movements in HRCA scenarios. Secondly, to enhance the model's generalization capability against operators’ individual differences, six data augmentation strategies are introduced. Then, an adaptive adjacency matrix is incorporated into the proposed method to strengthen the learning of dynamic dependencies between human joints that are not naturally connected. Finally, a dual-stream feature fusion mechanism is proposed. By embedding a motion stream within the joint stream, the operator's assembly actions are characterized from two dimensions: raw joint coordinates and joint motion features, thereby improving the accuracy of HRCA intention recognition. In the experiment, a HRCA experimental platform for a cylinder gear reducer is designed and developed, and an HRCA action video dataset is constructed based on it. The proposed method is experimentally validated using this dataset. The experimental results, including the model's training convergence performance, the enhancement effect of data augmentation strategies and adaptive adjacency matrix, and visualizations of the learning process across different network layers, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with eight other state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method achieves the best performance on four evaluation metrics, with an Accuracy of 96.97%, Precision of 97.08%, Recall of 96.97%, and F1-score of 96.95%, demonstrating its superiority in the recognition accuracy for HRCA intention.

verified_metadata.title: A new explainable artificial intelligence algorithm integrated with multi-agent system for joint decision-making of smart manufacturing systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Smart manufacturing systems increasingly rely on integrated production, inspection, and maintenance decisions to achieve high economic performance while satisfying stringent quality and reliability constraints under nonstationary operating conditions. Fixed inspection thresholds and periodic maintenance schedules often fail to adapt to evolving equipment states, leading to infeasible operation and suboptimal profit. This paper proposes a new Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based Multi-Agent System (MAS) decision-making algorithm for quality-critical smart manufacturing systems, addressing production, inspection, and maintenance decisions within a unified framework. A data-driven wear proxy triggers condition-based maintenance, while XAI fidelity signals dynamically adjust both inspection thresholds and effective maintenance wear thresholds when explanation fidelity indicates unreliable predictions. Global feasibility with respect to false-positive and false-negative constraints is enforced through an augmented Lagrangian optimization that supports policy parameters over long horizons. Case studies using large-scale industrial data demonstrate that the proposed MAS-XAI policy significantly outperforms both periodic maintenance strategies and a Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy. Relative to DQN, MAS-XAI achieves a 14.28% profit increase. Compared with periodic maintenance, it reduces maintenance interventions by 55.2% while maintaining a strict false-negative rate of 0.82%. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improves operational robustness and economic performance in smart manufacturing systems under dynamic conditions.

verified_metadata.title: A novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model
verified_metadata.abstract: In the autonomy problem of large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing orders, three steps are usually involved: allocating orders among enterprises, assigning parts to 3D printers, and arranging parts on the printer’s build platform. Among these steps, the layout of parts on a 3D printer serves as the underlying layer of the autonomy loop, providing the basis for obtaining feedback during part-equipment matching and enabling real-time adjustments. It also affects the allocation of orders among enterprises. Currently, artificial intelligence (AI) agents specifically designed for part layout remain underdeveloped, and practical engineering applications still rely heavily on manual operations. Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model (SPVLM), aiming to provide an effective AI agent solution for the autonomous parts layout stage. We propose an autonomy architecture for large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing. For the part layout problem in 3D printing, we propose a visual-text evidence enhancement method and construct a dataset of 10,000 scene samples. We further propose an improved generative reinforcement policy optimization (GRPO) technique to enhance the layout decision-making capability of SPVLMs. Finally, based on the SPVLM, we build an AI agent using a reasoning and acting (ReAct) architecture. The AI agent continually acquires part-layout experience through a memory-augmentation strategy and supports lightweight deployment. A representative subset of the dataset is made publicly available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RTYGFb2dvBAsXXD5v7OTXq07QpIXMcTA?usp=drive_link

verified_metadata.title: Bridging 2D vision and 3D CAD: Integrating cross-modal deep learning and LLM-assisted semantic graph reasoning for spatial disassembly constraint modelling
verified_metadata.abstract: To advance automation in the remanufacturing sector, this paper proposes a novel spatial disassembly constraint modelling method that integrates cross-modal deep learning with the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). A significant challenge in robotic disassembly is accurately identifying spatial constraints for used products, which often exhibit uncertain conditions and structural deviations from original designs. To address this, we introduce a cross-modal deep learning technique that unifies the detection mechanism for both captured images of used products and CAD models of original products, effectively resolving multimodal data fusion issues during model training. Furthermore, we leverage LLMs to construct and match semantic graphs based on the spatial positional relationships among components. This allows for the precise identification of the optimal matching CAD model and the correct numbering of detected components, thereby deriving specific spatial constraints for each component. The rigour and performance of this method are validated through a case study involving the removal of used bolster springs from railway wagon bogies on a robotic platform. The results demonstrate that the proposed method enables robots to accurately construct spatial disassembly constraints under complex and uncertain conditions, facilitating automated disassembly operations.

verified_metadata.title: MET-Net: An equivalent-section mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning in bilayer tube springback prediction under data scarcity and incomplete physical mechanisms
verified_metadata.abstract: Industry 4.0 requires transparent and reliable prediction of manufacturing outcomes, which is often constrained by scarce data and incomplete physical mechanisms. These constraints are particularly severe for bent bilayer metal tubes, whose springback prediction is essential for process planning. This work proposes MET-Net, a mechanism-guided neural framework for explainable transfer learning that reuses abundant single-layer springback knowledge for data-scarce bilayer prediction. MET-Net maps bilayer cross-section parameters to an equivalent single-layer representation through a differentiable equivalent-section module, whose adaptation is restricted to two physically meaningful correction parameters. The model is trained in two stages: physics-based initialization and single-layer pretraining, followed by conservative bilayer fine-tuning with sparse physics-residual guardrails, and a lightweight affine calibrator. On a copper-aluminum rotary draw bending case, MET-Net achieves a median RMSE of 0.4835° using only 100 bilayer samples, approaching the accuracy of a single-layer baseline trained on ten times more data. A paired zero-shot environment-perturbation evaluation further indicates stable performance under environment-level perturbations. Beyond accuracy, MET-Net supports manufacturing transparency through a structurally interpretable mechanism pathway, DeepLIFT-based training monitoring, and post-hoc diagnosability analyses. These strategies identify validity regimes of the embedded equivalent-section theory and quantify where systematic correction is required. MET-Net therefore provides accurate bilayer springback prediction together with actionable mechanism insight for process planning under data scarcity and incomplete physics.

verified_metadata.title: Proactive energy-carbon aware production scheduling in SMT lines: A novel graph meta-reinforcement learning approach
verified_metadata.abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing requires Surface Mount Technology (SMT) lines to adopt energy-carbon aware production scheduling. Traditional paradigms treat machines as discrete states, failing to capture the continuous thermodynamic inertia of thermal equipment like reflow ovens. Coupled with dynamic electricity prices and fluctuating carbon factors, classical optimization and standard multi-agent reinforcement learning become inadequate. To address the deep coupling of discrete manufacturing logic and continuous thermodynamics, we reformulate the scheduling problem as a semi-Markov decision process and propose a novel graph meta-reinforcement learning architecture termed GMeta-MATD3. Specifically, graph neural networks are utilized to extract spatial–temporal topologies across production and microgrid networks. To navigate environmental non-stationarity, a meta-learning module is embedded within each agent to infer latent physical contexts and predict peer behaviors, enabling temporal energy arbitrage via deliberate “wait” actions. Additionally, an attention-based centralized critic dynamically decomposes joint values to resolve the multi-agent credit assignment problem. Extensive experiments on real SMT data coupled with IEEE distribution systems demonstrate significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. GMeta-MATD3 achieves the best Pareto front, yielding a 13.1h makespan, 1020.5 RMB energy cost, 810.2 kgCO2 emissions, a 1.5% tardiness rate, and zero grid violations. Crucially, its thermodynamic stepping mechanism reduces transition energy from 12.5 to 3.2 kWh/batch, and proactive peak avoidance cuts the load peak-to-valley difference by 34.5%, maintaining daily carbon intensity below 0.55 kgCO2/kWh. Scalability tests confirm that executing 500-batch schedules in under 500 ms.

title: Towards semi-supervised and unsupervised source verification of additively manufactured parts with sparse data
abstract: A common challenge for manufacturing supply chains is to determine whether parts were made correctly, using the intended machines and processes. This study presents a deep learning framework that can discover and verify the source of additively manufactured (AM) components from surface texture visible in part images, with minimal pre-training or supervision. We develop a machine learning (ML) architecture that integrates self-supervised feature extraction using a vision transformer masked autoencoder (ViT-MAE) with unsupervised Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering. A simple classification head guides feature extraction when labels are available. To evaluate the model performance, we procured 3744 AM parts from six contract manufacturers. These manufacturers produced the parts using a total of 11 Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printers. Part images were used to evaluate the model across various unsupervised and semi-supervised tasks for predicting manufacturing origin. With no part labels, the model achieves an F1 score of 0.595 identifying the specific printer that produced the part. With minimally labeled data, only 36 parts from a single build per printer, the F1 score exceeds 0.9, outperforming existing supervised models. The architecture identifies anomalous parts from unknown sources in complex recognition tasks, including Open Set Recognition (OSR) and Generalized Category Discovery (GCD). The model identifies other fine-grained manufacturing attributes including the printer model, material, specific build, and location of the part in the printer. The research presents an image-based deep learning method that could enable manufacturers to validate parts from suppliers in data-scarce environments.

title: Optimizing contact-guided search for robotic screw unfastening under position uncertainty in electronic waste dismantling
abstract: Automating the disassembly of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) is crucial for the circular economy and the recovery of strategic materials like Rare Earth Elements. However, autonomous fastener removal remains a significant bottleneck due to the high positional uncertainty and degradation inherent in End-of-Life (EoL) products. This research proposes a deterministic, geometry-adaptable framework that integrates deep learning-based vision for coarse localization with a Hybrid Force/Velocity Control (HFVC) architecture for robust unscrewing. Five search geometries, including the Circular Spiral, Square Spiral, Windmill Search, Raster Scan, and Spiral with Noise, are compared in simulation, identifying the first of these as the most optimal strategy for industrial applications. Unlike empirical methods, we mathematically derive the kinematic constraints — specifically the maximum allowable spiral pitch and the optimal rotational velocity windows — required to guarantee successful insertion without heuristic tuning. Experimental validation using an industrial manipulator demonstrates the framework’s scalability across four distinct drive profiles (Allen, Hexagonal, Torx, and Phillips) without any parameter readjustment. The system successfully absorbs initial positional errors of up to 3 mm, achieving an overall 99% success rate with cycle times ranging from 11 to 13 s/screw depending on the fastener type, proving highly competitive for high-throughput automated dismantling lines.

verified_metadata.title: A graph isomorphism attention network and graph information embedded reinforcement learning-based dual-arm robot teleoperation and manipulation skill acquisition method
verified_metadata.abstract: Many human working environments are arduous, and entirely replacing on-site workers with robots remains challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes a teleoperation and manipulation skill learning framework for physical avatar robots. For teleoperation, a real-time, dual-arm motion retargeting method based on a graph isomorphism attention network (GIAN) and robust kalman filtering (RKF) has been developed. This method eliminates the need for manually labeled human-to-robot joint mappings. By representing human motion as graph-structured data and leveraging a learning approach with kinematic physical constraints, accurate retargeting is achieved. The RKF is adopted to suppresses noise and outliers for enhancing stability. For skill learning, the study introduces a graph information-embedded reinforcement learning (GIERL) method that integrates imitation and reinforcement learning. Graph features extracted by GIAN are incorporated into both the observation space and reward design, enabling efficient acquisition of dual-arm manipulation skills. Furthermore, a shared control strategy is designed by integrating GIERL with GIAN to augment manipulation, forming a synergistic closed loop between perception and decision-making. Experiments involving desktop organization, as well as dual-arm box lifting and transportation in both simulated and real environments, demonstrate the superior performance and practicality of the proposed framework.

verified_metadata.title: Vision language model-enhanced embodied intelligence for AR-assisted HRC assembly: Multimodal cognition, task reasoning, and autonomous execution
verified_metadata.abstract: Human-robot collaborative (HRC) assembly is pivotal to modern manufacturing, yet it suffers from critical bottlenecks that hinder its performance. The fusion of visual, textual, and operational multimodal information remains inefficient, and human-robot task partitioning is often ambiguous. This ambiguity arises from inadequate integration of domain knowledge with perceptual outputs, while manual assembly operations lack consistency and a notable disjunction exists between abstract task reasoning and embodied robotic execution. These issues collectively impede the intelligence and coordination of HRC assembly systems. To resolve these issues, this study proposes an end-to-end Vision-Language Model (VLM)-enhanced embodied intelligent framework for HRC assembly’s cognitive reasoning and autonomous execution. The framework adopts a closed-loop architecture with four cascaded core modules, synergistically supporting perception, knowledge reasoning, human-robot interaction, and autonomous execution. First, a VLM-driven multimodal cognition module innovatively fuses VLMs with BERT (textual semantic processing) and ResNet-50 (visual feature extraction), capturing fine-grained features of assembly personnel, parts and tools to generate structured perceptual representations via semantic triplets and state matrices. Second, a domain knowledge-driven reasoning module is developed, which constructs an assembly knowledge graph by extracting semantic triplets from corpora via VLMs and encodes domain experience into machine-readable form. It adopts Graph RAG for semantic alignment, conflict detection and structured retrieval, and leverages LLM-aided reasoning to decompose global tasks into robotic and manual subtasks with clear boundaries. Third, an AR-assisted assembly guidance module is proposed to enable seamless HRC interaction and precise manual operations through multi-dimensional guidance. It covers visual-textual prompts, 3D positioning overlays, real-time monitoring and remote consultation, translating reasoned manual subtasks into actionable guidelines. Finally, a VLM-driven robotic code generation module realizes autonomous execution by generating modular action functions, sequences and trajectory parameters based on reasoned task representations. Integrated with hardware components, it uses an embodied controller to convert abstract robotic subtasks into concrete physical operations. Comparative experiments with traditional models and LLMs confirm the proposed HRC assembly system’s superiority.

verified_metadata.title: Adaptive parameter optimization for turbine blade manufacturing: A novel personalized federated learning framework
verified_metadata.abstract: In high-precision machining processes such as turbine blade manufacturing, optimizing process parameters is crucial for improving production efficiency and precision. However, process parameter optimization in current industrial practice still suffers from two major drawbacks: the slow convergence speed of high-dimensional parameter optimization and the protection of manufacturing data privacy. To address these issues, this article proposes a Sophia Extended (SophiaX) optimization algorithm under the novel personalized federated learning (DecePFL) framework. Specifically, the SophiaX algorithm is proposed, which efficiently utilizes second-order information through adaptive estimates of diagonal Hessian, significantly accelerating the convergence of high-dimensional process parameter optimization for complex blades. Furthermore, the DecePFL framework is constructed, which achieves personalized federated learning (PFL) through parameter decoupling and performs decentralized federated aggregation, thereby ensuring the privacy protection of industrial data. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conduct experiments on three series of aviation turbine blades (Blade A, Blade B, and Blade C). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves optimization efficiency, reducing optimization iterations from 84 to 27 for Blade A, from 80 to 28 for Blade B, and from 90 to 38 for Blade C.

verified_metadata.title: Chat with the manufacturing process: A knowledge-guided cross-modal large language model for machining condition predictive maintenance
verified_metadata.abstract: Predictive maintenance for manufacturing processes has become critically urgent to enhance system reliability in modern manufacturing. This paper proposes a cross-modal large language model for conversational diagnosis of machining process, where an interactive decision-making system that integrates multi-source sensor data fusion and knowledge enhancement was constructed. Firstly, the study introduces a knowledge guided graph fusion method to address challenges in information integration. Secondly, a cross-modal image–text generation model is developed to achieve low-parameter alignment between time-series imaging features and language models, enabling the generation of interpretable diagnostic reports. Finally, to tackle knowledge fragmentation issues of general large language models in industrial scenarios, a domain knowledge graph is constructed, covering tool wear mechanisms and the impact of machining parameters. A parameter-efficient fine-tune strategy is employed to inject structured knowledge, mitigating knowledge hallucination issues inherent in general large models. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves an accuracy of 94.2% in tool remaining useful life prediction tasks, representing a 11% improvement over traditional deep learning models, while providing dynamic maintenance recommendations through natural language interaction. This research offers theoretical support for the development of human–machine collaborative machining systems in intelligent manufacturing, advancing online monitoring technologies toward interpretable and interactive paradigms.

title: Deep transfer learning with graph neural networks for the selection of manufacturing processes
abstract: The quality of process planning, linking product design and manufacturing, critically depends on selecting suitable manufacturing processes. In recent years, several deep learning approaches have been proposed for selecting manufacturing processes, frequently relying on synthetically created datasets. While such datasets allow models to capture general manufacturing patterns, they fail to reflect the complexity and variability of industrial 3D CAD models. As a result, the effectiveness of deep learning for predicting manufacturing processes is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality, annotated industrial data. To mitigate the effort for annotation of industrial data, this paper investigates deep transfer learning for the selection of manufacturing processes. Models are first pre-trained on a synthetically designed dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on smaller sets of real industrial data. verified_metadata.title: Deep transfer learning with graph neural networks for the selection of manufacturing processes
verified_metadata.abstract: The quality of process planning, linking product design and manufacturing, critically depends on selecting suitable manufacturing processes. In recent years, several deep learning approaches have been proposed for selecting manufacturing processes, frequently relying on synthetically created datasets. While such datasets allow models to capture general manufacturing patterns, they fail to reflect the complexity and variability of industrial 3D CAD models. As a result, the effectiveness of deep learning for predicting manufacturing processes is constrained by the limited availability of high-quality, annotated industrial data. To mitigate the effort for annotation of industrial data, this paper investigates deep transfer learning for the selection of manufacturing processes. Models are first pre-trained on a synthetically designed dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on smaller sets of real industrial data. The findings demonstrate that deep transfer learning enables improved performance in the selection of manufacturing processes.

title: CA-DLM: Causal-aware diffusion language model for interpretable industrial defective image generation

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。因果感知扩散语言模型学习指令到缺陷类型的因果映射，生成工业缺陷图像补足质检数据。

verified_metadata.title: CA-DLM: Causal-aware diffusion language model for interpretable industrial defective image generation
verified_metadata.abstract: This research proposes a Causal-Aware Diffusion Language Model (CA-DLM) for interpretable generation of defective images to address the scarcity of defective samples in industrial settings. Firstly, a causal inference mechanism is integrated into DLM to establish a causal mapping among “natural language instructions, model causal variables, and defective image generation”. The counterfactual causal intervention strategy enables interpretable, fine-grained control over defect, texture, and background features during image generation. Secondly, a learnable Structural Causal Model (SCM) is constructed to disentangle semantic features into causal and non-causal variables, effectively separating useful semantic features from confounders during image generation. A causal loss function is also designed to enforce sparsity and acyclicity in the SCM, guiding the model toward a causally consistent structure. Finally, the causal intervention approach is designed to perform do-intervention on SCM to achieve interpretable defective image generation. The do-intervention activates relevant causal variables and suppresses non-causal variables according to the learned SCM, thereby enabling precise control over key defect attributes while preserving the consistency of texture and background. Comparative experiments across three public datasets show that CA-DLM enables interpretable, controllable generation of high-fidelity defective images, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Detection models trained on CA-DLM generated images achieve significant improvements in downstream defect detection tasks, with accuracy exceeding 95%. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing that high-fidelity defective images can be generated using only 30% of causal variables.

title: A compositional dual-hand action recognition method for LLM-driven assembly assistance
abstract: Effective assistance in manual assembly requires perceiving the operator’s actions in real time and advising the operator flexibly. Traditional action recognition methods classify a video clip into a single holistic label for one action stream, failing to resolve the parallel dual-hand actions or expose the fine-grained semantics for downstream assistance reasoning. Moreover, conventional assistance systems retrieve predefined content keyed to recognized steps and cannot respond to an operator’s situated needs, whereas large language models (LLMs) can respond flexibly but are too slow and hallucination-prone for the real-time, safety-critical path. This paper connects the two through a compositional action representation that expresses each hand’s action as a structured tuple of action verb , manipulated object , target object , and tool . A compositional dual-hand action recognition model, CoDuAR, is proposed to predict the action tuples of both hands in a single forward pass through a shared encoder and hand-specific compositional decoders. On the HA-ViD benchmark, CoDuAR outperforms state-of-the-art recognizers that require a separate model per hand, while using 23% fewer parameters and roughly doubling the dual-hand inference throughput of the strongest parameter-comparable baseline, VideoMAE V2. Built on the compositional representation, a dual-process assistance system, Assembly Copilot, is developed. A deterministic System 1, driven by CoDuAR, maps the predictions to a symbolic task state, tracking the task progression, recommending next tasks, and detecting operational errors in real time, while an LLM-powered agent, System 2, reasons over the symbolic state to answer the operator’s queries and generate post-session performance reviews, gaining flexibility without placing the language model on the latency-critical path. A case study on a gear-plate assembly validates the functionality of the integrated system. The results indicate that the compositional action representation can serve as an effective interface between real-time perception and language-based assembly assistance within the evaluated scenario.

verified_metadata.title: A pose estimation method for aeroengine blade assembly based on geometric priors and reinforcement learning
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the challenges encountered in the automated assembly of aeroengine blades, where non-conformal insertion, irregular boundary features, and insufficient pose alignment accuracy occur between the blade root and disk slot, this paper develops a force-vision-guided robotic assembly platform. Based on the 3D point cloud measured by structured light, a pose estimation method integrating geometric priors (GP) and reinforcement learning (RL) strategies is proposed. Firstly, the key tasks and coordinate transformations in the automated blade assembly process are systematically defined, the geometric constraint mechanisms during assembly are analyzed, and a mathematical chain linking point cloud input to robotic motion control is constructed for pose estimation. Subsequently, during the coarse registration stage, three types of geometric priors—planar constraint, coaxial constraint, and boundary contour constraint—are incorporated to improve the accuracy and robustness of initial pose alignment. In the fine registration stage, the pose refinement of point clouds is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and a hybrid sparse–dense reward mechanism is designed. The Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is then employed to efficiently optimize the registration policy. Finally, assembly validation experiments were performed on both dovetail and fir-tree blades using the CoppeliaSim simulation platform and a self-developed structured- light measurement system. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves superior performance over existing registration algorithms in pose estimation accuracy, alignment stability, and assembly feasibility. This study provides an effective and generalizable solution for the intelligent assembly of complex structural components.

title: Toward provably safe AI-driven perception and motion planning for robotic manufacturing: A review

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。实质综述学习型机器人制造感知及运动规划的可证明安全技术和不确定性处理。

verified_metadata.title: Toward provably safe AI-driven perception and motion planning for robotic manufacturing: A review
verified_metadata.abstract: Safety is a crucial requirement for robotic systems operating in manufacturing environments, where perception and motion errors lead to unsafe physical interactions and process failures. While recent advancements in embodied AI and learning-based robotic systems have significantly improved adaptability, their black-box nature and sensitivity to uncertainties make safety assurance challenging. In response to such challenges, this article provides a comprehensive review of safety-oriented robotic perception and motion planning, along with complementary safety layers such as Digital Twins (DTs) that support the validation and monitoring of AI-driven robotic systems in manufacturing. In particular, our review first establishes optimization- and feasibility-based problem formulations to analyze and categorize this broad topic from a unified perspective. Then, we discuss mathematical principles and methodologies for improving safety in robotic perception and motion planning, including their learning-based counterparts, as well as their synergies with existing safety layers in smart manufacturing. Finally, we identify key challenges and future research directions toward safer and more trustworthy AI-driven robotic manufacturing.

title: Multi-information guided adaptive transfer learning for multi-point deformation prediction of blades in CNC machining based on Auto-MultiDeF

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多信息自适应迁移学习预测CNC叶片多点热机械变形，改进航空叶盘加工精度。

verified_metadata.title: Multi-information guided adaptive transfer learning for multi-point deformation prediction of blades in CNC machining based on Auto-MultiDeF
verified_metadata.abstract: As core components of aero-engines, the surface precision of blisks directly determines the aerodynamic performance and service reliability of the entire engine. During milling on CNC machine tools, workpiece deformation is primarily driven by mechanical factors and further perturbed by thermal effects, exhibiting strong nonlinearity and multi-factor coupling. Despite extensive research, existing prediction methods encounter significant bottlenecks: (1) multi-source monitoring signals are highly aliased and non-stationary, hindering the precise decoupling of physical features reflecting machining mechanisms; (2) limited sample sizes and sparse parameter distributions in target domains restrict the model's generalization capabilities; (3) the complex nonlinear mapping relationships inherent in machining processes are difficult to learn effectively. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a machining deformation prediction model (ATL-PAMDF) based on adaptive transfer learning integrated with physics-informed guidance and Auto-MultiDeF feature extraction. Firstly, the Auto-MultiDeF module is developed to accurately extract and fuse component features from multi-channel aliased signals via a multi-scale decomposition and multi-channel fusion mechanism. Secondly, a pre-training and fine-tuning transfer paradigm under joint multi-channel reconstruction is constructed to facilitate rapid model convergence under sparse sample conditions. Finally, a mechanical model with error compensation is embedded into the training process as a structural prior, guiding the network to learn deformation responses consistent with physical laws. Multi-point deformation prediction experiments on a self-collected blade dataset demonstrate that the proposed ATL-PAMDF model achieves superior prediction accuracy and stability compared to state-of-the-art methods (RMSE&MAE at least 35% and 24% lower, respectively). The results validate its exceptional performance in complex physical scenarios and under aliased, small-sample machining conditions. The proposed method also offers an extensible solution for deformation prediction of other workpieces in CNC machining.

verified_metadata.title: SEIT-Agent: An experience memory enhanced inspection and testing agent for high-safety special equipment with risk-aware LLM evaluation
verified_metadata.abstract: The inspection and testing of high-safety special equipment (HSSE) is crucial for ensuring its safe and stable operation. However, two core tasks still require substantial manual effort: damage mode analysis requires synthesizing dispersed damage-related knowledge, while equipment quality grading involves determining and applying standard-specified rules. Existing LLM-based research augmented with RAG mainly focuses on information retrieval and Q&A, lacking mechanisms to autonomously and deterministically execute context-dependent rules. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the special equipment inspection and testing agent (SEIT-Agent), an AI Agent framework that integrates an LLM-based planner, a specialized tool library, an experience memory pool and a domain knowledge base. The tool library encapsulates quality grading rules for reliable autonomous grading, while the knowledge base integrates damage mode information and is accessible to the LLM via a hybrid vector–keyword RAG approach. The experience memory pool stores successful task execution trajectories to enhance consistency and accuracy in repetitive quality grading tasks. Furthermore, we introduce an expert-guided risk-aware LLM evaluation strategy where domain experts define critical and supporting assessment points and an external large-scale LLM evaluates response quality under a critical-point gating mechanism. Experiments on real-world data from an HSSE enterprise demonstrate that SEIT-Agent outperforms baseline methods on two core tasks.

verified_metadata.title: Rec-PdM: Decision-calibrated recursive multi-agent systems for uncertainty-aware prescriptive maintenance in smart manufacturing
verified_metadata.abstract: Predictive maintenance creates industrial value only when uncertain health evidence leads to an appropriate intervention under asymmetric failure costs and operational constraints. We present Rec-PdM, a decision-calibrated recursive multi-agent system for uncertainty-aware prescriptive maintenance. Its six decision agents maintain specialized beliefs about asset condition, fault state, remaining useful life, economic risk, action selection, and verification; production-impact and human-prescription interfaces connect these beliefs to factory context and operator-facing decisions. RecursiveLink reconciles local beliefs with downstream decision consequences while preserving the provenance of each update. The method treats maintenance as a partially observable degradation process and calibrates prediction and uncertainty against decision regret, tail risk, feasibility, and communication overhead. Evaluation on six public datasets spans degradation prognosis, process failure, vibration-based diagnosis, and acoustic anomaly detection, with controlled decision studies of cost asymmetry, coordination, resource constraints, dependent faults, and operating drift. RecursiveLink achieves the best mean-cost rank among the evaluated coordination mechanisms, while calibrated Rec-PdM ranks in the top two in 98.3% of the evaluated cost regimes without an unexpected failure. Under shared fleet constraints, the coordinator remains in the top two by mean cost in 88.8% of 240 scenarios; prequential recursive guarding reduces unserved failures from 70 to 5 under drift. These results show that decision cost, tail risk, and traceable coordination complement predictive accuracy when maintenance evidence must be converted into action.

title: A production continuity-guided domain-generalized topological transformer for production line real-time health assessment

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。拓扑Transformer和领域泛化结合生产连续性，对实际生产线健康状态实时评估。

verified_metadata.title: A production continuity-guided domain-generalized topological transformer for production line real-time health assessment
verified_metadata.abstract: Conventional fault diagnosis methods primarily focus on improving the recognition accuracy of individual equipment while overlooking differential risks that various faults pose to production line continuity. This accuracy‑oriented paradigm tends to significantly increase unplanned downtime when equipment importance is unevenly distributed, especially in the presence of bottleneck processes. To address this, this paper proposes a production continuity-guided production line‑level health assessment method named unplanned downtime minimization-driven domain-generalized topological transformer (UDMDGTT). From the novel perspective of production continuity, the proposed method quantifies equipment importance and shutdown risks in multi‑process workflows based on Birnbaum importance. A process‑dependent unplanned shutdown risk matrix (USRM) is constructed as a core tool for assessing production continuity, and the downtime cost caused by diagnosis decisions is integrated into the model training process. The USRM is used to construct the production line shutdown risk loss within the UDMDGTT framework, enabling the model to strategically avoid high‑cost misclassifications on critical equipment. To simultaneously pursue accuracy improvement and downtime minimization, a multi‑task loss function with a two‑stage training strategy is designed, and a time‑varying equipment importance mechanism that adapts to process reconfiguration without retraining is introduced to enhance cross‑process generalizability. Experiments on a manufacturing system comprising one lathe and two milling machines demonstrate that UDMDGTT reduces production line downtime while maintaining competitive cross‑domain recognition accuracy. Compared with the ablation model without unplanned downtime minimization, UDMDGTT reduces downtime by 16.88%, 47.08%, and 26.74% on the three machines, respectively, with only minor decreases (1.33%, 0.56%, and 0.72%) in recognition accuracy.

title: ViSTR-GP: Online cyberattack detection via Vision-to-State Tensor Regression and Gaussian Processes in automated robotic operations
abstract: Industrial robotic systems are central to automating smart manufacturing operations. Connected and automated factories face growing cybersecurity risks that can potentially cause interruptions and damages to physical operations. Among these attacks, data-integrity attacks often involve sophisticated exploitation of vulnerabilities that enable an attacker to access and manipulate the operational data and are hence difficult to detect with only existing intrusion detection or model-based detection. This paper addresses the challenges in utilizing existing side-channels to detect data-integrity attacks in robotic manufacturing processes by developing an online detection framework, ViSTR-GP, that cross-checks encoder-reported measurements against a vision-based estimate from an overhead camera outside the controller's authority. In this framework, a one-time interactive segmentation initializes SAM-Track to generate per-frame masks. A low-rank tensor-regression surrogate maps each mask to measurements, while a matrix-variate Gaussian process models nominal residuals, capturing temporal structure and cross-joint correlations. A frame-wise test statistic derived from the predictive distribution provides an online detector with interpretable thresholds. We validate the framework on a real-world robotic testbed with synchronized video frame and encoder data, collecting multiple nominal cycles and constructing replay attack scenarios with graded end-effector deviations. Results on the testbed indicate that the proposed framework recovers joint angles accurately and detects data-integrity attacks earlier with more frequent alarms than all baselines. These improvements are most evident in the most subtle attacks. These results show that plants can detect data-integrity attacks by adding an independent physical channel, bypassing the controller's authority, without needing complex instrumentation.

A frame-wise test statistic derived from the predictive distribution provides an online detector with interpretable thresholds. We validate the framework on a real-world robotic testbed with synchronized video frame and encoder data, collecting multiple nominal cycles and constructing replay attack scenarios with graded end-effector deviations. Results on the testbed indicate that the proposed framework recovers joint angles accurately and detects data-integrity attacks earlier with more frequent alarms than all baselines. These improvements are most evident in the most subtle attacks. These results show that plants can detect data-integrity attacks by adding an independent physical channel, bypassing the controller's authority, without needing complex instrumentation.

verified_metadata.title: Temporal task graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for efficient human-robot collaborative assembly planning
verified_metadata.abstract: Human–robot collaboration (HRC) has emerged as a promising assembly paradigm that exploits the complementary capabilities of humans and robots to achieve efficient and flexible task execution. However, existing assembly planning methods still have limited capability in representing dynamic task evolution and often suffer from inefficient policy learning, which restricts their applicability to complex HRC assembly scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a temporal task graph modeling and multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for HRC assembly sequence planning. First, a dynamic node graph is constructed from assembly-task relationships to represent task precedence, execution states, and human–robot interaction dynamics. Multi-dimensional task evaluation indicators are further incorporated to establish a structured multi-agent learning environment. Based on this environment, a multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm enhanced by temporal graph network (TG-MAPPO) is developed, in which temporal graph representation and multi-agent policy optimization are jointly coupled to improve exploration efficiency and training stability in partially observable dynamic graph environments. To evaluate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method, two assembly cases with different task structures, including an electric gripper and an electric vehicle battery (EVB), are used for comparative validation. Furthermore, a physical HRC assembly workstation is established, and a real-world HRC assembly experiment for the electric gripper is conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can generate feasible and efficient HRC assembly sequences. Compared with conventional schemes, the proposed method improves collaborative assembly efficiency, reduces the overall operation time by 44%, and alleviates operator fatigue during task execution.

verified_metadata.title: Geometry-aware deep reinforcement learning for real-time integrated scheduling and nesting in additive manufacturing
verified_metadata.abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a promising technology for small-volume and customized production. However, the diversity of parts, coupled with batch scheduling and geometric constraints on heterogeneous machines, poses significant challenges for production planning. Unlike most existing studies on AM scheduling that underestimate geometric features, this paper investigates a real-time integrated scheduling and nesting problem with dynamic batch processing and geometric feasibility to minimize the overall makespan across heterogeneous AM machines. We propose GeoPPO, a geometry-aware deep reinforcement learning approach based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The proposed approach employs dedicated state encoders and specialized decoders within an actor–critic architecture and potential-based reward shaping strategy to produce geometry-aware decisions for part selection, machine assignment, and batch formulation. Computational experiments are conducted on synthetic and real-world instances with representative AM machine configurations and industrial part geometries. The results show that GeoPPO achieves near-optimal makespan on small-scale instances with an average deviation of 5.3% from the best MILP solutions, while reducing computation time from 1200 s to 1-3 s. With increasing problem scale, GeoPPO outperforms MILP on medium-scale instances, whereas MILP becomes computationally intractable for large-scale problems. Across all instances, GeoPPO reduces makespan by 18.1% relative to the best heuristic, and achieves solution quality comparable to the metaheuristic baseline among GA, ALNS, and GWO, while requiring only about 1% of the computational time. Ablation studies and generalization experiments further demonstrate the efficiency and practical applicability of GeoPPO. This research provides an effective and practical solution paradigm for complex scheduling and nesting challenges in AM.

title: Simulation-based multi-objective decision support for Comprehensive Digital Twins of smart manufacturing systems
abstract: Decision support in Smart Manufacturing Systems (SMSs) often requires balancing conflicting objectives related to multiple system dimensions, such as maximizing the number of completed products while minimizing energy consumption and CO₂ emissions. Comprehensive Digital Twins (CDTs) integrate multiple system dimensions within one executable model to support multidimensional analysis and multi-objective decision-making. However, an automatically extracted, simulation-ready CDT is not inherently optimization-ready because controllable parameters, admissible ranges, optimization objectives, and decision-to-model mappings remain unspecified. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a semi-automated framework that prepares an automatically extracted CDT for simulation-based multi-objective optimization. Starting from multidimensional event logs, Multi-Flow Process Mining extracts dimension-specific Stochastic Petri Nets and integrates them into an executable Multidimensional Stochastic Petri Net represented in Multidimensional Petri Net Markup Language. An optimization-preparation layer combines model parameter information with expert-defined selections, bounds, and objectives, and maps decision vectors to executable model configurations evaluated through simulation. The framework is demonstrated using an illustrative manufacturing line for robotic assembly and welding with rework. The Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied as the primary Pareto-based optimizer, while equal-weight weighted-sum scalarization is evaluated as a comparative baseline. The NSGA-II Pareto-front approximation supports post-search scenario selection. In a 100-replication reference-model evaluation, the selected scenario reduced CO₂ emissions by 3.81%, while completed products and grid-energy consumption changed only marginally ( − 0.29 % and + 0.17 % , respectively). These results support the proof-of-concept feasibility of extending an automatically extracted multidimensional simulation model to multi-objective decision support.

verified_metadata.title: ProcessLLM-R1: A hypergraph retrieval-augmented and reinforcement learning-driven assembly process planning for commercial aircraft
verified_metadata.abstract: As a key stage in the intelligent manufacturing of commercial aircraft, process planning plays an important role in improving production efficiency and ensuring product quality. Traditional process planning relies heavily on manual review of scattered, frequently updated technical documents, which is not only time-consuming and labor-intensive but also prone to errors due to limited experience. With the development of large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based intelligent process planning methods have achieved significant progress. However, existing RAG-based process planning generation methods typically rely on static one-shot querying and passive filtering. As a result, LLMs lack the ability to autonomously assess knowledge sufficiency, which limits their effectiveness in handling fragmented process knowledge and complex interrelationships. To this end, this paper proposes ProcessLLM-R1, an intelligent method for commercial aircraft assembly process generation based on hypergraph retrieval and reinforcement learning. First, a process knowledge hypergraph is constructed to organize process knowledge, and hypergraph retrieval strategy is designed that can be autonomously invoked by LLM, thereby enhancing the models’ ability to dynamically acquire and organize process knowledge. Second, retrieval is modeled as a multi-round interaction between the agent and knowledge hypergraph, and GRPO is introduced to perform parameter-efficient fine-tuning of the agent, thereby improving its adaptability to process generation tasks. Finally, experimental results on the commercial aircraft machining and assembly process datasets show that ProcessLLM-R1 outperforms the evaluated LLM-based generation and retrieval-augmented baselines across the reported metrics. It is hoped that the research can provide valuable insights and support for the application of LLM-based solutions in the field of aircraft manufacturing.

title: A structured taxonomy of autonomous manufacturing systems: Capabilities, definitions, and enabling technologies
abstract: Smart manufacturing has introduced adaptive, data-driven systems to the shop floor and beyond. However, current deployments operate near their technological limits, lacking the contextual adaptability, resilience, and independent decision-making required to manage unplanned disruptions. Autonomous manufacturing systems have emerged as a promising solution to overcome these deficiencies. These systems fulfill industry’s growing need for proactive rather than reactive approaches, balancing efficiency, safety, and agility. However, the field remains fragmented by inconsistent definitions, inadequate classification frameworks, and unclear capability-technology mappings. Terms like adaptive, autonomous, intelligent, smart, and cognitive systems are used interchangeably, creating confusion that hinders broader development and adoption. Critically, manufacturing lacks domain-specific autonomy taxonomies comparable to automotive industry standards, preventing systematic capability specification and solution comparison. Existing taxonomies frequently conflate service robotics and military systems with manufacturing applications, which demand precision, repeatability, and interoperability. This paper presents a manufacturing-specific autonomy taxonomy developed through analysis of cross-domain industrial taxonomies and maturity frameworks. The taxonomy establishes a six-tier classification: Cyber-Physical, Intelligent, Smart (semi and fully mature tiers), Autonomous, and Cognitive manufacturing systems. Classic automated manufacturing systems and adaptive manufacturing systems are pre-autonomy baselines below the entry tier and are excluded from the six-tier count. Each tier is defined by distinct capabilities, decision-making authority, learning mechanisms, enabling technologies, and human-machine collaboration requirements. First, this work provides standardized terminology and capability-technology mappings, functioning as an analytical tool rather than an absolute classification that divides the world into rigid classes. Second, it aims to serve as a structured, practical reference to guide practitioners and stakeholders in defining system objectives, identifying enabling technologies, and aligning operational requirements with appropriate autonomy levels. Ultimately, the proposed taxonomy establishes a common benchmark for system development and evaluation toward achieving autonomous and cognitive production.

title: A novel machining operation strategy prediction method based on self-supervised B-rep learning

verified_metadata.title: A novel machining operation strategy prediction method based on self-supervised B-rep learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Manufacturing operation strategy, as a crucial element in part manufacturing, directly impacts processing efficiency and manufacturing quality. Current machine learning-based manufacturing operation decision methods inevitably lose geometric and topological information when converting 3D CAD models into intermediate formats such as point clouds, voxels, or meshes, while also facing the challenge of insufficient training data. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative hybrid learning approach combining self-supervised pre-training with supervised fine-tuning that learns B-Rep representations from large-scale unlabeled CAD data to achieve manufacturing operation strategy prediction on small-sample datasets. The method consists of two key modules: first, a pre-training model based on an encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder learns latent representations of CAD model face topological entities, and the decoder reconstructs the signed distance function of model faces; second, a supervised learning phase that utilizes pre-trained facial latent space representations to complete model segmentation tasks based on manufacturing strategies and modeling information using labeled data. Compared to traditional rule-based 3D shape representation sampling methods, directly using B-Rep data representation significantly improves accuracy; compared to existing supervised learning methods based on B-Rep input, the hybrid approach proposed in this study demonstrates superior performance on small-scale training sets.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-grounded multi-agent architecture for traceable, risk-aware human–AI decision support in manufacturing
verified_metadata.abstract: High-precision CNC machining of free-form aerospace components requires bounded compensations informed by inspection, simulation, and process knowledge. Off-the-shelf large language model (LLM) assistants can generate text, but they do not reliably execute risk-constrained multi-step numerical workflows or provide auditable provenance for high-stakes decisions. We present multi-agent knowledge analysis (MAKA), a decision-support architecture that separates intent routing, tools-only quantitative analysis, knowledge graph retrieval, and critic-based verification that enforces physical plausibility, safety bounds, and provenance completeness before recommendations are surfaced for human approval. MAKA is instantiated on a Ti-6Al-4V rotor blade machining testbed by fusing virtual-machining path-tracking error fields, cutting-force and deflection simulations, and scan-based 3D inspection deviation maps from 16 blades. The analysis decomposes deviation into an evidence-linked pathing component, a drift-based wear proxy capturing systematic evolution across parts, and a residual systematic compliance term. In a three-level tool-orchestration benchmark spanning single-step to three-or-more-step stateful sequences, MAKA increased the pass rate for correct tool selection, argument assignment, and dependency-consistent execution by a mean, median, and maximum of 22.9, 8.0, and 64.0 percentage points, respectively, across 15 model-level comparisons over the stronger of the ReAct-style and structured function-calling baselines with identical model and tool access. Digital twin what-if studies show MAKA can coordinate traceable compensation candidates that reduce predicted surface deviation from order 10−2 in to approximately ±10−3 in over most of the blade within the simulation environment, providing a pre-deployment verification signal for risk-aware human decision-making.

verified_metadata.title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning using a world model for multi-objective optimization of micro-milling
verified_metadata.abstract: Existing micro-milling optimization methods often rely on fixed objective weights or direct parameter control, limiting their ability to handle state-dependent trade-offs among surface quality, energy consumption, and machining time. This study proposes a preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic framework with a learned world model for sequential parameter optimization. Unlike direct-parameter reinforcement learning, the proposed method separates objective-level preference learning from feasible command generation. A high-level Dirichlet policy selects an interpretable preference vector over surface quality, energy, and time, while a constrained inverse control module maps it to spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut within prescribed bounds and rate limits. A multimodal temporal convolutional gated recurrent unit (MTC-GRU) world model trained on 900 physical Ti-6Al-4V micro-milling trials serves as the rollout environment for policy learning. Controller performance is evaluated through closed-loop rollouts within the frozen learned environment, while three predetermined variable-parameter trajectories, each physically replayed nine times, are used to assess recursive world-model fidelity under low, medium, and high transition intensities. Within the learned environment, preference-constrained hierarchical actor-critic (PC-HAC) improves surface quality, energy use, and machining time under the stationary objective, and achieves larger gains in the cumulative energy-budget task. At κ = 0.80, PC-HAC reduced the budget-penalized score by 53.9% relative to the greedy controller. The recursive physical replay evaluation yields overall R2 values of 0.810 for surface roughness and 0.975 for energy, with prediction error increasing as transition magnitude increases. These findings support the proposed preference-space control strategy within the investigated micro-milling setting and provide a foundation for future physical closed-loop validation.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-data fusion multi-modal deep learning for spindle current prediction in digital twin-driven machining state perception
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate perception of machining states is essential for intelligent Computer Numerical Control (CNC) systems, yet modeling key process variables remains challenging due to the nonlinear and multi-modal nature of cutting processes. Empirical models lack adaptability, while purely data-driven methods often neglect physical constraints. Direct measurement of cutting force is challenging in practice, as complex workpiece geometries, limited ranges of detection instruments, and high deployment costs make large-scale force data acquisition difficult. Therefore, spindle current is adopted as a more practical and accessible variable for state perception. In consideration of this problem, this study proposes a physics–data fusion multi-modal deep learning framework for spindle current prediction in a Digital Twin (DT)-driven environment. The framework integrates multi-modal inputs, including acceleration signals, STEP-NC semantic metadata, and cutter-workpiece engagement (CWE) geometric descriptors derived from the 3D engagement volume, into a unified representation that is processed by a data-driven branch for feature extraction. The architecture features a Sequence Head for residual regression and an attention-pooled Point Head for next-step prediction. Spindle dynamics constrain sequence outputs through a physics-informed module. Conditioned on process embeddings, a multi-objective loss adaptively balances dual heads and physical heuristics. The framework, deployed in a DT environment, supports synchronized multi-source data acquisition and real-time prediction. Experimental validation on a dedicated DT platform confirms framework feasibility, consistently maintaining R2>0.95 and superior error metrics across diverse machining regimes.

verified_metadata.title: Bridging cognition, reasoning and action for polymorphic embodied agents towards human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly with vision-language model and digital twin
verified_metadata.abstract: With the advent of Industry 5.0, human-robot collaborative assembly has become a core production paradigm that combines human cognitive flexibility with robotic operational efficiency. Single-robot systems cannot meet the diverse requirements of complex assembly tasks. Therefore, collaboration between human operators and heterogeneous multi-robot teams is required for flexible and efficient manufacturing. However, current collaborative systems are limited by fragmented perception-reasoning-execution pipelines. Poor generalization of general-purpose models in industrial environments is also observed. Additionally, integrated safety mechanisms for dynamic shared workspaces remain insufficient. These challenges indicate the need for embodied intelligence, through which agents can perceive, reason, and act seamlessly in physical environments. To address these issues, a vision-language model (VLM)-enabled, digital twin-assisted polymorphic embodied agent framework was proposed in this paper. A complete closed loop of embodied cognition, embodied reasoning, and embodied execution was established for human-heterogeneous multi-robot collaborative assembly. In the embodied cognition layer, a domain-specific VLM was developed to achieve robust real-time perception of human behaviors, assembly components, and environmental states, with integrated depth information for accurate spatial localization and collision detection. In the embodied reasoning layer, a digital twin system with bidirectional virtual-to-real mapping enables virtual pre-simulation and optimal task scheduling that effectively leverages the complementary strengths of human and robots. In the embodied execution layer, the model directly generates executable control code for heterogeneous robots, which is pre-verified in the digital twin environment before physical deployment. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms traditional visual algorithms and mainstream general-purpose vision-language models on all evaluation benchmarks. The system achieves three tiered latency indicators for decoupled functional modules. It delivers ultra-low single-frame perception delay below 150 ms for environmental safety sensing, and attains outstanding reasoning accuracy paired with an online task reasoning latency of 0.75 s to support real-time human-robot closed-loop interaction. The 4.8 s full assembly code generation delay only takes effect during offline pre-generation before task startup. This offline process is isolated from the online control loop and imposes no negative impact on the system’s real-time dynamic response and obstacle avoidance capacity. Continuous robotic operation was ensured. Human comfort and safety were maintained through differentiated task allocation. This paper provides a practical and effective solution for intelligent and safe collaborative assembly. It also offers important implications for the development of next-generation intelligent manufacturing systems.

title: Intelligent assembly support systems for human-centric manufacturing: A survey
abstract: This survey provides a structured analysis of intelligent assembly support systems, examining how these systems perceive tasks, reason about assembly processes, generate support actions, and interact with human operators in complex industrial environments. A systematic literature review of 184 publications from 2015 to 2026 was conducted, combining thematic analysis with bibliometric and temporal analyses to identify research trends, technological developments, and persistent challenges across perception, reasoning, interaction, and deployment. The analysis is structured around three perspectives: perception and task understanding under uncertain industrial conditions, adaptive support for heterogeneous workers, and emerging technologies with implications for industrial deployment. The review reveals that current systems remain predominantly focused on vision-based perception, action recognition, and predefined support strategies, with limited consideration of perception uncertainty arising from visual ambiguity and environmental changes, variations in human assembly behaviour, and diverse worker capabilities and support needs. By synthesising fragmented research streams across technical, human, and deployment perspectives, this survey identifies a fundamental transition from recognition-oriented support tools towards uncertainty-aware decision-support systems that enable adaptive human–AI collaboration. Key challenges include robust perception under environmental and visual variability, adaptive support for heterogeneous workers, trustworthy integration of emerging technologies, such as large language models and human-centric digital twins, and practical requirements for industrial deployment. This review establishes a broader perspective for evaluating intelligent assembly support systems, proposing that future progress should be assessed not only through technical performance but also through adaptability, trust calibration, human autonomy, and long-term operational viability. The findings provide a roadmap for Industry 5.0 assembly environments in which intelligent systems augment rather than replace human expertise.

title: Synthetic data generation in smart manufacturing applications: A systematic review and outlook
abstract: Data-driven methods, particularly those based on machine learning and artificial intelligence, are transforming decision-making in smart manufacturing. However, these methods typically require large volumes of high-quality labeled data for training, which are often difficult to obtain due to limited availability, class imbalance, privacy concerns, and the high costs and time demands of data collection. Synthetic data generation (SDG) has emerged as a promising approach to address these challenges. Over the past two decades, SDG techniques have evolved through diverse paths, including classical data augmentation, rule-based methods, simulation-based methods, and deep generative methods. Despite these advances, the adoption of SDG in manufacturing is still in its nascent stage, with applications mostly confined to proof-of-concept demonstrations and narrowly scoped use cases. Furthermore, a comprehensive, systematic literature review of SDG in manufacturing applications is lacking. To address this gap, this paper presents a systematic literature review of SDG for smart manufacturing applications, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Drawing on 201 identified publications spanning 2018 to early 2025, the review synthesizes the current state of the field and identifies key opportunities for future research. Viewed through the lens of the product lifecycle, the findings demonstrate how SDG can serve distinct functions at each stage of manufacturing, thereby revealing opportunities for advancing its integration into various smart manufacturing practices.

title: Microbiota-derived propionate suppresses Salmonella virulence gene expression via LuxS quorum sensing
abstract: Abstract Background Despite mounting evidence that commensal microbes enhance host defenses, whether and how they directly suppress pathogen virulence remains elusive. Here, we investigate metabolites from the gut microbiota of infection‑resistant Tibetan chickens for their ability to reduce Salmonella virulence gene expression and elucidate the molecular mechanism by which these compounds inhibit the LuxS/AI‑2 quorum‑sensing system. Results Initially, we compared the expression of the quorum‑sensing gene luxS and biofilm-associated virulence genes in Tibetan chickens and broiler chickens post- Salmonella infection. Notably, Tibetan chickens exhibited significantly lower virulence gene expression than broiler chickens. Subsequently, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from Tibetan chickens to broiler chickens reduced virulence gene expression in infected recipients. Further, 16S rRNA gene sequencing of cecal contents revealed that FMT enhanced microbial diversity and altered composition in infected broiler chickens, specifically enriching short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing beneficial bacteria (e.g., Bacteroides , Rikenellaceae _ RC9 _ gut _ group , Phascolarctobacterium , Desulfovibrio ). Critically, using Transwell chambers to separate microbes and metabolites, we identified metabolites as mediators of this effect. Subsequent liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC–MS) quantification demonstrated significantly elevated propionate concentrations in both uninfected and infected Tibetan chickens, and FMT-recipient broiler chickens. Propionate levels correlated negatively with key virulence factor expression. Moreover, in vitro experiments showed that propionate inhibited Salmonella biofilm formation, reduced autoinducer-2 (AI-2) activity, and downregulated the expression of virulence genes. In vivo, we further confirmed that propionate decreased the expression of Salmonella virulence genes. Taken together, these results support that propionate suppresses Salmonella virulence gene expression by targeting the LuxS/AI-2 quorum-sensing pathway. To validate this mechanism, we generated a luxS knockout strain by homologous recombination; strikingly, propionate failed to attenuate virulence gene expression in this mutant, thereby establishing the essential role of LuxS/AI-2. Finally, molecular docking identified propionate-LuxS binding sites (Ile53), and site-directed mutagenesis validated critical functional residues, highlighting structural determinants for virulence gene expression regulation. Conclusion These findings underscore the role of the gut-derived metabolite propionate in directly modulating pathogen virulence gene expression by targeting the LuxS/AI-2 quorum‑sensing system, offering novel insights into microbiota-based strategies for infectious disease management. title: Cross-kingdom genomic variation in chicken gut microbiomes: insights from China’s diverse local breeds
abstract: Abstract Background The gut microbiome possesses substantial genetic diversity that supports microbial adaptation, but the genomic variation patterns across its prokaryotic and viral populations remain incompletely characterized. Results Through integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analysis of ten indigenous chicken breeds from China, we recovered 1527 representative prokaryotic MAGs, 37,555 representative DNA viral contigs, and 1867 representative RNA viral contigs (primarily comprising Bacillota/Bacteroidota, Uroviricota, and Lenarviricota/Pisuviricota, respectively). By integrating complementary short-read and long-read metagenomics with metatranscriptomics, we identified structural variants (SVs) and single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) in these cross-kingdom genomes. Positive SV-SNV density correlations occurred consistently across all microbial groups, indicating coordinated mutational processes. DNA viruses exhibited the highest variant prevalence (86.9% SNVs, 47.7% SVs), with temperate phages accumulating significantly more variants than virulent phages. Functionally, prokaryotic variants accumulated in carbohydrate metabolism and amino acid metabolism, while viral variants demonstrated broad metabolic hijacking. Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) was characterized by a strong virus-associated signature (69.40% of 536 events) and marked by an asymmetric pattern, with phage-to-bacteria (P-to-B) flow alone constituting 37.50% of all events. Random forest analysis revealed a strong bidirectional predictive relationship between SV and SNV densities across prokaryotic, DNA viral, and RNA viral populations, suggesting coupled genomic instability. Niche breadth emerged as a major driver of SNVs across kingdoms and was positively correlated with variant density. In prokaryotes, HGT events significantly shaped variant patterns. For viruses, genomic GC content was an important factor and consistently showed a negative correlation with SNV density in both DNA and RNA viruses. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that coordinated mutational processes and kingdom-specific intrinsic factors drive genomic variation, with viruses serving as key genetic exchange vectors in chicken gut ecosystems. title: The interplay between Peptostreptococcus and Fusobacterium as novel signatures in colorectal cancer recurrence
abstract: BACKGROUND: After resection surgery, recurrence occurs in more than 30% of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. Previous studies have highlighted the role of the gut microbiota in CRC initiation and progression; however, the microbial features associated with recurrence remain not completely understood. In particular, integrated multi-omics biomarkers, the interactions between microorganisms, as well as those between microbes and the host, and their relevance to recurrence risk require further investigation. RESULTS: In this study, 120 tumor mucosal samples collected during surgery from CRC patients underwent 16S rRNA gene sequencing and LC-MS metabolomic profiling. Recurrence status was determined through postoperative follow-up. Compared to the relatively minor variations in mucosal microbial and metabolomic signatures across different tumor node metastasis (TNM) stages, recurrent patients exhibited a distinct landscape. Machine learning analysis identified an integrated signature comprising five bacterial genera (Peptostreptococcus, Fusobacterium, Bacteroides, Porphyromonas, and Prevotella) and five metabolites (alanylglutamic acid, putrescine, arginine, histidine, and sebacic acid), which demonstrated strong discriminatory performance between recurrent and non-recurrent patients (AUC = 0.89). By integrating 10 biomarkers, a comprehensive risk score for patient stratification was derived. After adjusting for TNM stage, patients classified as high-risk had a significantly shorter recurrence-free survival (adjusted HR = 1.59, 95% CI 1.35-1.88, P < 0.0001). The microbial biomarkers Fusobacterium and Peptostreptococcus displayed positive correlation and were observed to co-aggregate and form dense dual-species biofilms. Further cellular and murine experiments revealed that P. anaerobius significantly enhanced the adhesion of F. nucleatum to tumor cells and its colonization of colonic mucosa. KEGG pathway analysis of differential metabolites identified enrichment of arginine and proline metabolism pathways in the recurrence group. Concurrently, arginine was found to disrupt F. nucleatum-P. anaerobius co-aggregation, while its metabolite putrescine significantly promoted dual-species biofilm formation. CONCLUSION: Our study identified integrated microbial and metabolic features associated with CRC recurrence and proposes an exploratory risk stratification framework. Furthermore, a previously unrecognized link between pathobionts and metabolites relevant to recurrence was reported, which requires further validation in a larger independent cohort. Video Abstract.
