title: A hybrid learning framework for real-time fire dynamics prediction using diffusion models and spiking neural networks

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。扩散模型扩充火警数据并用脉冲神经网络预测火灾动态，研究明确的火灾安全过程。

verified_metadata.abstract: Fire safety state prediction is crucial in rail transit safety management, especially given the dynamic nature of fire incidents. This paper addresses challenges such as data sparsity, stage-specific feature complexity, and temporal dynamics by proposing a method that combines data diffusion techniques with Spiking Neural Networks (SNN). Using fire experiment datasets from the National Fire Research Laboratory (NFRL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the fire stages—ignition, spreading, and extinction—are modeled and predicted. A diffusion model extends the dataset, improving the quality of fire alarm data. A stage-specific data augmentation strategy enhances the representativeness of features across fire stages. Additionally, temporal feature extraction is applied through a segmentation-based approach, providing dynamic inputs to the model. The proposed SNN architecture alternates between fully connected layers and Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron layers. Experimental results show a classification accuracy of 97.97 % on the test set, outperforming traditional recurrent neural networks (LSTM) and transformer models by better capturing the dynamic characteristics of fire and improving processing efficiency. While the SNN does not outperform LSTM or transformer in all aspects, it provides an optimal trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, particularly in low-power environments. The diffusion model-generated data is consistent in feature distribution and correlation, offering reliable support for fire state prediction.

title: A bayesian network approach to ship safety assessment: integrating machine learning and expert opinions

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。贝叶斯网络结合机器学习、船舶及环境因素分析海事事故与风险，属于实际交通系统安全建模。

verified_metadata.abstract: Maritime accidents pose a significant threat to maritime operations. With technological advancements, a substantial amount of objective data can now be collected and utilized to improve ship safety assessment. This study proposes an assessment model that leverages comprehensive objective data collection to enhance maritime safety management. Theoretically, this study introduces a novel multi-factorial accident model, termed nSmE (n Subjects – m Environments), which emphasises the interaction between human behaviours and environmental conditions in accident causation. Methodologically, a Bayesian Network (BN)-based hybrid approach is employed to model the 2S2E (2 Subjects – 2 Environments) ship accident framework, systematically integrating factors across ship-related factors, human factors, internal environmental factors, and external environmental factors. A scenario-based deduction approach is employed to establish factor structure relationships. To model the conditional probability tables, a two-part modelling strategy is adopted. Machine learning techniques are applied to model context-dependent factors, while a combination of Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, IF-THEN rule-based reasoning, and Dempster-Shafer Evidence Theory is employed for directly measurable factors through incorporating expert opinions. Finally, case studies validate the model’s effectiveness and provide key recommendations for improving ship risk management. The results show that human reliability is a critical factor in accident prevention which requires targeted efforts to enhance seafarers' working conditions. Improving crew safety and performance through specialised equipment, such as protection against extreme temperatures and excessive noise exposure, is essential. Additionally, safety improvement strategies should be tailored to the specific risk factors present in each scenario to ensure effective risk mitigation and accident prevention.

title: Towards efficient data-driven fault diagnosis under low-budget scenarios via hybrid deep active learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。残差变分自编码器及主动学习降低工业故障诊断对标注的需求，并验证具体故障识别。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis using deep learning (DL) has become essential for effective quality control, maintenance, and process automation in various industrial processes. However, an efficient labeling strategy is required because constructing large-scale labeled datasets to train DL-based predictive models entails considerable cost and labor. While active learning (AL) has been a prominent solution for efficient data labeling in fault diagnosis, existing AL approaches are unsuitable in practice due to low-budget scenarios where there is insufficient labeled data to train the model stably. In this regard, this work proposes a novel method, called a hybrid deep active learning for low-budget (HDAL-LB) scenarios, that addresses emerging challenges in the label-scarce regime to perform efficient fault diagnosis. First, self-supervised learning is performed with a deep stacked residual variational auto-encoder to efficiently initialize an encoder for latent feature extraction. Second, an evidential learning-based training technique is developed to enable a cost-efficient generation of calibrated predictive uncertainty. Third, a hybrid query selection is systematically formulated under a combinatorial optimization framework, utilizing both uncertainty and data diversity for deep AL. The efficacy of the proposed method (i.e., HDAL-LB) in fault diagnosis is validated through four case studies, utilizing three public benchmark datasets and one private real-world dataset. The comprehensive experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of HDAL-LB under low-budget scenarios compared to existing baseline and state-of-the-art (SOTA) AL methods. Furthermore, extensive ablation studies demonstrate that HDAL-LB consistently exhibits effective fault diagnosis performance across various experimental settings, highlighting its label efficiency and practical applicability in real-world practice.

title: Transfer learning from physical scale information: A signal identification method for mine system security monitoring

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。一维卷积网络从地震信号迁移到矿山微震信号识别，服务矿山地质灾害监测。

verified_metadata.abstract: Earthquake signals and microseismic signals are elastic waves excited by the sudden release of energy inside the geological medium, but they differ in the scale of their respective seismic sources. This makes it possible to learn from physical information at different scales. We proposed a one-dimensional convolutional neural network under transfer learning framework to learn how to identify microseismic signals using the discrimination of earthquake magnitude. We first trained the convolutional neural network using numerous labeled seismic signal data and then fine-tuned the partial weights using a small amount of microseismic data. Experimental results demonstrate the classification results on the microseismic database are as high as 100 %. When the number of samples is reduced to 100 signals, the model can still maintain a minimum accuracy of 96 % on the same dataset. When the signal-to-noise ratio gradually increases to 0dB, the minimum accuracy of the model reaches 95.35 %. Compared with traditional machine learning (SVM, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes), the accuracy of the model increased by 6.19 %, 16.00 % and 40.30 % respectively. The research result above show the model has excellent classification accuracy and high robustness, providing better pre-technical support for the safety and stability of mine systems.

title: Human-AI interactive framework for smart evacuation safety analysis in large infrastructures

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。LSTM和GAN从真实建筑平面疏散仿真学习疏散时间、流量及人群密度，服务火灾安全设计。

verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing scale and complexity of large urban infrastructures have led to greater pedestrian concentrations and high risks of crowd-related incidents in emergencies. This study develops an Intelligent Evacuation Prediction Tool (IEPTool) with a human-AI interactive framework for evacuation prediction and safety assessment in large infrastructures. The tool is equipped with a deep learning engine trained from a comprehensive evacuation-simulation database of 66 real-life architectural floor plans, including air terminals, exhibition centers, large stadiums, and various stations. By integrating long-short-term memory (LSTM) networks and generative adversarial networks (GANs), key metrics, including evacuation time, the pedestrian flow rate at each exit, and dynamic pedestrian density distribution, are predicted with a high accuracy of over 90 %. Subsequently, a large language model (LLM) is incorporated for interactive risk analysis, enabling intelligent evacuation safety assessments and providing optimization guidance. The integrated graphical user interface allows fast and accurate evaluation of evacuation safety for complex floorplans. This intelligent framework provides practical and reliable support to fire safety design analysis and urban resilience management.

title: Is there difference in landslide susceptibility model based on explainable artificial intelligence from the perspective of slope units with different scales?

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。随机森林与可解释分析检验坡单元尺度对滑坡易发性预测的影响，研究地质灾害空间规律。

verified_metadata.abstract: The scale of mapping units significantly affects the accuracy and reliability of landslide susceptibility assessment. However, existing landslide susceptibility studies lack a clear determination of the appropriate slope unit scale, and the impact of different slope unit configurations on the modeling process and model interpretability has not been thoroughly investigated. This study conducted an empirical analysis using extensive real-world landslide data from the core area of the Three Gorges Reservoir region, comprehensively investigating the effect of slope-unit scales on the landslide susceptibility assessment. Initially, a geospatial dataset comprising 3594 historical landslide events and 22 initial condition factors was compiled. Subsequently, 30 different slope unit schemes of varying scales were generated by the r.slopeunits tool. For each scheme, the dataset was randomly divided into training and testing subsets with a 7:3 ratio and modeled using random forest model. This study reveals the significant impact of slope unit scales on hyperparameter optimization, factor selection, and model interpretability. The results highlight that: (1) appropriate slope unit scale can improve the quality of input variables, thereby enhancing the generalization ability and interpretability of landslide susceptibility assessments, reducing the risk of overfitting. (2) Finer and more concentrated slope units do not always lead to better results; they may excessively rely on distance metrics, resulting in overly conservative high susceptibility classifications in landslide susceptibility models. This study provides valuable insights into selecting the appropriate slope unit scale for landslide susceptibility assessment.

title: Probabilistic evaluation for early wind turbine yaw misalignment detection
abstract: Nowadays, one of the biggest challenges for wind turbines is to reduce operation and maintenance costs. Therefore, it is essential to develop predictive maintenance, anticipating failures early and thus avoiding unnecessary actions on the wind turbine. In this way, the uptime and performance of the turbine are maximized, and its useful life is extended. This work describes a general methodology for fault detection based on probabilistic models and its evaluation. This methodology combines a fault detection method based on the Fisher Test and the development of probabilistic models of wind turbine power curves. Several probabilistic models of power curves have been evaluated: Gaussian mixture model (GMM), Frank copula model, Gaussian mixture copula model (GMCM), Gaussian process regression (GPR) and epsilon-insensitive loss function support vector regression (ε-SVR). The results indicate that the Gaussian mixture copula model is the most efficient in terms of accuracy and computational cost. The detection of a wind turbine orientation misalignment error has been tested as a use case. It is shown how with this probabilistic approach it is possible to detect the fault in a short period of time from its appearance, 10–30 times faster than other techniques found in the literature with which it has been compared.

title: Dual-channel dynamic spline graph convolutional network for bearing remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。动态图卷积网络融合振动特征并嵌入物理退化约束预测轴承剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings is crucial for predictive maintenance in industrial systems; however, traditional methods frequently fail to account for dynamic topological changes and nonlinear degradation patterns within vibration data. To address these challenges, we propose the Dual-Channel Dynamic Spline Graph Convolutional Network (DDSGNet), different from traditional methods that rely on discrete feature aggregation, this paper models the spatial correlation among vibration features using a global topology aggregation module. The continuous local evolution operator captures stationary degraded dynamic features, whereas the time-dependent learner maintains long-range sequence information. This approach addresses the challenge of modeling continuous local feature changes. Furthermore, a novel activation function, DSAF, is proposed to dynamically adjust to nonlinear signal changes by smoothing gradients, thereby resolving issues of gradient roughness and vanishing. Lastly, a loss function named PhyMAE, which is based on physical constraints, is proposed to align with the physical characteristics of bearing degradation, ensuring accurate and physically consistent RUL prediction. Experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that DDSGNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in prediction accuracy, offering a robust solution for bearing RUL estimation.

title: Time-variant reliability analysis via advanced most probable point trajectory tracking
abstract: Structural reliability evolves due to environmental conditions and varying loads, leading to gradual structural deterioration. Accurately capturing this time-variant behavior is essential for assessing failure probability over a specified time horizon. This study proposes an adaptive virtual model-assisted most probable point trajectory-based (AdaVM-MPPT) approach for time-variant reliability analysis under stochastic loadings, focusing on the trajectory tracking of the most probable point (MPP). A stochastic process discretization technique is adopted to decompose the time-variant limit state function in the time domain. To enhance computational efficiency and accuracy, the Extended Support Vector Regression (X-SVR) is utilized for virtual model construction. The virtual model approximates the relationship between the structural uncertainty inputs, including geometries, material properties, degradation processes, applied loading conditions, and the limit state hyperplane. Therefore, a two-stage adaptive sampling strategy is developed to effectively establish the virtual model and capture the MPP at all discretized time instants. The identified MPPs are then used to approximate the most probable point trajectory (MPPT), enabling continuous prediction at any time point within the specified period. The proposed framework consistently generates MPPs over the specified time period based on the MPPT, allowing for efficient computation of time-variant reliability using the multivariate normal distribution. The proposed AdaVM-MPPT method for time-variant reliability analysis offers several advantages. The X-SVR algorithm and two-stage adaptive sampling strategy improve the MPP capturing efficiency significantly. Furthermore, the computational cost of time-variant reliability analysis associated with the stochastic process discretization size can be significantly reduced based on the availability of MPPT. These two advancements significantly improve the efficiency of traditional time-variant reliability analysis methods. Finally, the applicability and computational efficiency of the proposed method are fully demonstrated through a test function and practice-stimulated engineering problems.

title: An integrated approach of knowledge-driven and neural network for fatigue remaining useful life prediction within small sample conditions

verified_metadata.abstract: Fatigue remaining useful life (RUL) prediction plays a vital role in improving the operational performance and reducing the failure risk of machinery through effective maintenance management. As a result, it has extracted increasing attention and is furtherly investigated within diverse industrial fields, wherein small sample condition poses to several challenges. Consequently, we propose an integrated fatigue RUL prediction approach based on the fusion of knowledge and neural network under small sample case. Specifically, the crack propagation mechanism is determined referring to correlated domain knowledge, and large scales of fault statistics are obtained via updated model firstly. Furthermore, a fusion approach based on multiple failure mechanisms is devised to generate pseudo-labeled fault data. Then, a three-stage pre-training model based on deep neural network oriented to RUL prediction is designed, wherein both generated and a few of experimental data are utilized fully. The proposed approach is implemented in a practical case study regarding an aircraft fuselage panel and the results demonstrate the enhancement in RUL prediction accuracy.

title: Reliability analysis of tensile membrane structures using active learning-aided metamodeling

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。主动学习代理模型逼近张拉膜结构极限状态并估计可靠性，直接用于结构安全分析。

verified_metadata.abstract: The design and construction of tensile membrane structures (TMS) are undergoing standardization currently. Modern structural design is generally based on reliability analysis which assesses the structural performance under various limit states in a probabilistic sense. Traditional reliability methods work well for linear or mildly nonlinear systems, and are therefore unsuitable for the highly nonlinear TMS behavior. Probabilistic simulation methods provide a more robust framework for complex limit states, but are computationally prohibitive, besides the already computation-heavy form-finding and load analysis of TMS. To alleviate this computational burden, metamodeling techniques offer a surrogate for full-scale simulations. However, accurate metamodels often require a large number of training points, increasing the computational cost. This paper proposes the integration of active learning techniques into metamodeling by strategically choosing training points within the region of interest near the limit state, enabling a more accurate estimation of the reliability index, with fewer training samples compared to standard metamodeling methods. The proposed methodology is tested on diverse TMS shapes to demonstrate its effectiveness in evaluating their reliability for different (and complex) limit states. The results clearly demonstrate how the proposed approach achieves this with reduced computational costs and higher accuracy, compared to “conventional” approaches.

title: Identifying key regions in spatial networks through graph neural networks

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。图网络学习拓扑与空间特征识别基础设施和道路网络关键区域，研究真实空间网络失效鲁棒性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Complex systems are frequently modeled as spatially embedded networks, where nodes and edges are distributed within a physical space. A critical challenge in spatial network analysis is identifying key regions whose activation or removal of nodes and edges can significantly enhance or degrade network functionality with broad applications ranging from disease prevention and traffic congestion optimization. Although many advanced methods perform well in general topological networks, effective integration of topological and geographical features in the identification of critical regions remains unresolved. Here, we propose a novel spatial network disintegration model that employs square regions as the fundamental units of analysis, addressing the regional overlap issue inherent in circle-based disintegration models. We further introduce a deep learning framework, Key Region Identification with Graph Neural Networks (KRIG), trained on numerous small synthetic spatial networks to identify key regions in diverse real-world applications, including infrastructure and road networks. Extensive experiments validate that KRIG significantly outperforms existing approaches in detecting critical regions. The framework effectively balances topological and spatial characteristics through large-scale data-driven learning. The proposed deep learning framework opens up a new direction for analyzing spatial networks using deep learning techniques, which enables us to identify critical regions to resist attacks and failures and improve network reliability.

title: An active-learning method based on hierarchical Kriging model for multi-fidelity reliability analysis

verified_metadata.abstract: An active-learning method based on hierarchical Kriging model (AHK-MCS) for multi-fidelity reliability analysis is proposed. It is a two-stage method that includes: building the low-fidelity (LF) model using LF samples firstly, and constructing the high-fidelity (HF) model based on the LF model using HF samples secondly. Additionally, an experimental design method based on the LF model is proposed. The two-stage framework facilitates the high-precision LF model and initial HF samples selection, consequently enhancing the efficiency of the HF active-learning process. The AHK-MCS method is compared with two one-stage methods through eight numerical examples. The results show that the proposed method is capable of providing an accurate estimation of failure probability with fewer HF samples. Moreover, the proposed experimental design method is evaluated and demonstrated to result in a reduction of HF samples. The influence of the LF model is assessed, indicating that the utilisation of a precise LF model can diminish the number of HF samples required for the construction of the HF model. The performance of the AHK-MCS method under different cost ratios is also investigated.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for optimal planning of production line maintenance with deterioration
abstract: Manufacturing companies often contend with deteriorating production systems that can significantly hinder overall performance. Therefore, optimizing maintenance planning strategies plays a crucial role in enhancing production efficiency. In this study, we address a novel maintenance decision-making problem in serial production lines, where machine degradation leads to product quality deterioration and throughput loss at the final stage. We propose a new framework that jointly considers product quality trends, buffer dynamics, and machine production states to optimize a preventive maintenance policy for the last machine in the line. To achieve this, we utilize an average-reward deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach within a discrete event simulation environment and compare their effectiveness to conventional dispatching methods. Our results, based on a digital twin enriched with real production data, show that the proposed DRL approach consistently outperforms traditional dispatching rules and practitioner-designed heuristics. This study is the first to apply DRL to maintenance decision-making in serial production systems that explicitly model product quality degradation, machine production states and buffer interactions—addressing a key gap in current literature.

title: A physics-constrained Bayesian neural network for machinery remaining useful life prediction and uncertainty quantification

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。物理约束贝叶斯神经网络结合Weibull及退化方程预测机械剩余寿命和置信区间。

verified_metadata.abstract: Remaining useful life prediction is crucial for predictive maintenance in industries such as aerospace, energy, and manufacturing. While deep learning methods have become prevalent for estimating system degradation and failure time, many of these models overlook predictive uncertainty, resulting in forecasts that are overconfident, difficult to interpret, and potentially unreliable in safety-critical applications. To address this issue, we propose a novel physics-constrained Bayesian neural network framework for remaining useful life forecasting that integrates uncertainty quantification, enabling the generation of confidence intervals and probabilistic lifetime distributions. The proposed Bayesian approach employs a Weibull distribution as the likelihood function to model time-to-failure data, capturing both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. Furthermore, the model incorporates time as an input and embeds a partial differential equation—derived from a deep hidden physics model—into the loss function, offering a more accurate and physically consistent representation of the degradation process. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through experiments on datasets from turbofan engines and ball bearings. Results show that the model outperforms state-of-the-art probabilistic remaining useful life prediction methods, providing superior prediction accuracy, enhanced uncertainty quantification, and more physically consistent, generalizable forecasts.

verified_metadata.abstract: Faults in chemical processes industries can lead to significant economic losses, environmental damage, and safety risks, making effective fault diagnosis critical for ensuring operational reliability. Graph-based learning methods have shown great promise in capturing complex relationships in time-series data for fault diagnosis. However, traditional data-driven fault graph construction methods often suffer from limited expressive potential due to their reliance on single rules. To address this limitation, a node-distance-adaptive Graph Reinforcement Learning (GRL) method Graph Double Deep Q Network (GDDQN) is proposed, which leverages the decision-making capabilities of Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize graph construction strategies. Furthermore, to handle the noise and inherent similarities in fault time-series data, an Enhanced Graph Convolutional Network (EGCN) is introduced. By encouraging angular diversity in the weights, the EGCN model demonstrates superior feature extraction and generalization capabilities, effectively processing node features represented by time-series signals. Combining these advancements, we developed the GDDQN-EGCN algorithm, which effectively integrates adaptive graph construction with robust feature processing. Extensive experiments on two datasets from the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process validate the outstanding performance of the proposed method in fault diagnosis, showcasing its potential for real-world applications.

title: Prediction of navigation risks in the Arctic Northeast Passage based on Bayesian and neural networks
abstract: This study proposes a hybrid method for predicting and analysing navigation risks in the Arctic Northeast Passage, where the accelerated melting of sea ice due to global warming has led to increased maritime traffic. Ensuring the safe navigation of ships in ice-covered waters has become a critical issue. A Bayesian network model is developed to quantify the risks associated with ship besetting in ice and ship-ice collisions. The model comprehensively incorporates environmental, ship-related, human, and organisational factors. Expert knowledge and satellite-based environmental monitoring data are combined to parameterise the Bayesian network, while probability distributions and Monte Carlo simulation are employed to address the uncertainty arising from experts’ subjective judgements. The probabilistic risk estimates generated by the Bayesian network are subsequently used to train a neural network, enabling the model to capture complex non-linear relationships and enable rapid prediction of navigation risks. This integration leverages the interpretability of probabilistic reasoning and the adaptability of machine learning. The proposed method exhibits strong predictive performance and produces spatial visualisations of navigation risk under varying conditions, providing robust decision-support for route planning and enhancing navigational safety in Arctic waters.

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。扩散生成模型与物理信息图卷积网络融合稀疏观测和扩散方程重建天然气泄漏浓度场。

verified_metadata.abstract: The sparse measurement point data after a natural gas leak can hardly reflect the concentration distribution in the whole area, and cannot provide data support for emergency response to the leak. This paper proposes a novel method for reconstructing the concentration field of natural gas leakage diffusion by integrating diffusion models with physics-informed graph convolutional networks (DM-PIGCN). The diffusion model is introduced to extract the basic features of the initial sparse observation data to form the distribution evaluation function of the prediction results. Meanwhile, the physical laws of gas diffusion are incorporated into the model training process in the form of a loss function. Together with the distribution evaluation function and the mean squared error, they constitute a joint loss function that collectively constrains the training process of the PIGCN. In addition, the effect of concentration data sparsity on the reconstruction results is discussed and compared with other models. The results show that the reconstruction accuracy of the DM-PIGCN model reaches 0.9834, which is effectively improved in accuracy and robustness compared with the traditional PINN model. This method provides critical decision-making support for emergency response to natural gas pipeline leaks.

verified_metadata.abstract: Maritime accidents are rare yet catastrophic events that can lead to significant consequences, involving a complex interplay of human, ship, and environmental factors. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in understanding the influential factors of maritime accidents to reduce navigational risk. However, the limited interpretability of exclusively data-driven modelling approaches requires incorporating background knowledge before training the risk models. This paper proposes a novel semi-data-driven Bayesian network (BN) approach that integrates the chi-square independent test and expert knowledge to construct the background knowledge. The Bayesian searching algorithm is then applied to analyse the causation and severity of maritime accidents and the resulting BN is assessed through a two-step validation process. The effectiveness of the model is evaluated through a comparative analysis using accident data from Chinese coastal waters between 2012 and 2023. Finally, the proposed model is employed to perform a real-time assessment of maritime traffic risks in the Xiamen Port area. The research findings highlight the significance of various risk factors and critical scenarios in coastal waters, offering guidance to support risk prevention and enhance the maritime safety management system. The study contributes to the development of a comprehensive framework for maritime traffic risk management and provides a valuable reference for future research in the field.

title: Deep learning-driven efficient running safety assessment and reliability analysis for the stochastic train-track-bridge system

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。CNN与改进LSTM代理随机车轨桥振动响应并计算行车安全可靠性，实测数据验证物理任务。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate and efficient safety assessment of the stochastic train-track-bridge (TTB) dynamic system is critical in railway engineering. However, conventional assessment methods are hindered by high computational costs and low efficiency, making it difficult to meet the demands of rapidly advancing railway projects. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel deep learning model for analyzing the running safety and ride comfort of the TTB system. The model effectively captures the essential physical characteristics of the system's stochastic vibration response. The probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to derive the probability density function (PDF). Building upon a convolutional neural network (CNN)-improved long short-term memory (ILSTM) framework, the traditional LSTM unit is enhanced into a probabilistic cell that incorporates the system's random distribution. Subsequently, a Bayesian optimization (BO) algorithm facilitates the transformation from the deterministic model to the stochastic model, significantly improving computational efficiency. Utilizing the proposed deep learning model, we conducted a running safety assessment and performed a reliability analysis of the TTB system. Furthermore, validation against field-measured data demonstrates the model's effectiveness, providing crucial technical support for the intelligent operation and maintenance of high-speed railway systems.

title: Probabilistic fault tree analysis and dynamic redundancy optimization for next-generation avionic flight control systems
abstract: The increasing complexity of next-generation avionic systems necessitates advanced reliability frameworks to ensure fault tolerance while meeting stringent constraints on weight, cost, and certification. This paper presents a novel probabilistic modeling approach that integrates Dynamic Fault Tree Analysis (DFTA), Bayesian Belief Networks, and semi-Markov processes to assess failure probabilities in safety-critical flight control architectures, such as Fly-by-Wire (FBW) systems and Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA). To complement this, a Dynamic Redundancy Optimization (DRO) framework using a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) is introduced to optimally allocate redundancy under realistic conditions, including common-cause failures and intermittent faults. The methodology is validated on a triplex-redundant Flight Control Computer (FCC), achieving a 41.8 % improvement in mean time between failures (MTBF) and a 36.5 % reduction in catastrophic event probability compared to static baseline models. Importantly, the framework conforms to DO-178C and ARP4761A standards, ensuring traceability and certification readiness. The results reveal a Pareto frontier representing optimal tradeoffs between reliability enhancements and system resource overheads, providing critical guidance for the design of next-generation avionic systems and regulatory assessment.

title: A digital twin framework for real-time operation monitoring and its future prediction for space nuclear power

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。高斯过程回归支撑空间核电数字孪生的实时状态校正与未来状态区间预测。

verified_metadata.abstract: To address the scarcity of data in space nuclear power (SNP) systems, this study presents a novel digital twin (DT) framework for SNPs that integrates offline and online stages. The framework ensures real-time interaction and supports online state correction and prediction. In the offline stage, sensitivity and grey relational analyses are combined to identify measurement parameters. A real-time multivariate filter is developed to suppress noise and outliers, and the Gaussian process regression is optimized to establish an effective data-driven model. In the online stage, a hybrid data–model driven framework corrects the DT system and predicts future state intervals, supported by an adaptive period update method to balance real-time response and computational accuracy. Six transient datasets are used to validate the framework. The results show that the maximum relative error is reduced from 10.58 % to 1.56 %, with the filter achieving a maximum average error of 0.3 % and an average computational time of 897 ms per 1 s step. The uncertainty interval encompasses the true value with a coverage probability of approximately 99 %, and the corrected results for the 3D reactor and 2D heat pipe agree well with the reference results. Therefore, the DT framework meets real-time and accuracy requirements.

title: A data-driven model for pipeline corrosion under insulation-induced failure analysis

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。贝叶斯因果网络融合腐蚀环境因素和检查证据，并与蒙特卡洛耦合预测保温管道失效，针对具体腐蚀机制。

verified_metadata.abstract: Corrosion under insulation (CUI) remains a major integrity threat because degradation occurs hidden from view and is driven by interacting environmental and operational factors under significant uncertainty. This current study develops a data-driven probabilistic framework that couples a Bayesian Network (BN) with Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to estimate time-dependent failure probabilities for insulated pipelines. The BN encodes causal dependencies among key variables (e.g., temperature cycling, moisture, insulation defects, contaminants, oxygen, pH) and supports evidence-based updating as new inspection/monitoring data arrive. Literature- and expert-informed priors and conditional-probability tables are provided for transparency, and continuous variables are statistically checked; in particular, corrosion rate is modeled as lognormal based on goodness-of-fit testing. The MCS engine translates BN-estimated susceptibility into a thinning-mode failure profile and includes convergence diagnostics. Benchmarking against a range of approaches, the proposed method’s ability to represent dependencies while propagating uncertainty. Validation uses an independent published failure case together with k-fold cross-validation and ROC analysis, showing competent discrimination, and sensitivity analysis (tornado plots) identifies temperature, moisture, and insulation integrity as dominant drivers. Model outputs are mapped to risk-based inspection thresholds aligned with industry guidance to support practice, enabling defensible inspection timing and maintenance planning. Although this work focuses on thinning, the modular framework can be extended to pitting/MIC and burst/rupture modes as richer datasets become available.

title: Research on multi-factor hydrogen leak accident diagnosis and optimization of monitoring sensors’ layout through CFD-based data-driven approach

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。CFD生成氢泄漏浓度场，SVM据少量传感器识别泄漏源条件并优化监测布局。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate identification of hydrogen leakage sources under interference scenarios is essential for safety assurance and accident prevention in confined environments. In this study, a coupled CFD–machine learning framework is developed for hydrogen leakage characterization and diagnosis. High-fidelity CFD simulations are employed to generate spatiotemporal concentration fields under diverse leakage conditions, including varying numbers of sources, directions, and mass flow rates. These data are combined with dimensionality reduction, clustering, and classification algorithms to enable reliable diagnosis of complex leakage scenarios. Comparative analysis shows that K-means clustering provides superior performance over DBSCAN, with a Silhouette Coefficient of 0.46 vs. –0.18 and a Calinski–Harabasz Index of 193.27 vs. 4.9, successfully distinguishing six leakage categories consistent with physical configurations. For classification, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) demonstrates robust generalization in small-sample, high-dimensional cases: with only six sensors, SVM achieves an accuracy of 0.833, substantially outperforming the neural network (0.368). Even when the number of sensors increases from 9 to 12, SVM maintains stable performance, with accuracy decreasing from 0.815 (9 sensors) to 0.695 (12 sensors), while NN remains lower (0.468–0.524). Through the application of the “majority correct prediction” principle, six critical monitoring points (7, 13, 9, 11, 12, and 17) were identified, achieving 100% leakage recognition accuracy and ensuring fault-tolerant diagnosis. In addition, the 40–60 s interval is shown to provide the best prediction performance, as dispersion patterns stabilize and noise effects diminish. Overall, the framework establishes an optimized spatiotemporal monitoring strategy, advancing both methodological reliability and practical applicability in hydrogen safety management.

title: A novel multi-source sensor correlation adaptive fusion framework with uncertainty quantification for intelligent fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis using multi-source sensor fusion holds significant promise but faces challenges related to reliability due to variations in signal quality across sensors and inconsistencies in fault features. To tackle these issues, a multi-source sensor correlation adaptive fusion (MSCAF) framework with uncertainty quantification is proposed to enhance identification trustworthiness for intelligent fault diagnosis. The proposed MSCAF integrates Dempster-Shafer theory with Dirichlet distribution to model sensor uncertainty and split multi-source sensors into high-confidence and low-confidence sensors based on the consistency of cross-sensor fault information. High-confidence sensors are given greater weight, ensuring more reliable fusion. Then, the reward and penalty functions are introduced to assess their correlation weights. Meanwhile, Convolutional and graph neural networks are employed to enhance feature extraction and output category probabilities, which can ensure robust fusion across varying diagnostic scenarios. This approach allows adaptive weighting, optimizes fusion reliability, and enables manual intervention for low-confidence sensors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MSCAF achieves superior diagnostic performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, confirming its efficacy in extracting reliable features with uncertainty quantification for intelligent fault diagnosis. • A novel multi-source sensor correlation adaptive fusion framework enhances the reliability of fault diagnosis. • Uncertainty quantification effectively addresses low-confidence sensors. • Diagnostic performance surpasses traditional multi-source sensors fusion methods.

title: Pipeline RUL prediction method that considers the coupling of multiple corrosion factors: Integrating deep learning and stochastic processes

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。Wasserstein GAN、贝叶斯网络和LSTM预测埋地钢制燃气管腐蚀速率分布及剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Given that buried pipeline remaining useful life (RUL) data are scarce, existing end-to-end RUL prediction approaches suffer from poor reliability and lack of interpretability, failing to provide engineers with effective operational status information and thus limiting their practical applicability. This study proposes a method to predict the RUL of urban steel buried gas pipelines in consideration of the coupled effects of multiple corrosion factors by integrating deep learning and a multistage stochastic degradation model to improve the model’s ability to adapt to the uncertainty and randomness of the prediction results. First, the coupling influence of multiple corrosion factors is considered, and the hierarchical relationship between multiple factors is analyzed. Second, the Wasserstein generative adversarial network–Bayesian neural network–long short-term memory deep learning model is proposed. The model is trained, verified, and tested using expanded open-source data to predict the corrosion rate and obtain the corrosion probability distribution. Third, a multistage degradation model on the basis of the jump diffusion process is established, the pipeline degradation stage is divided, and the drift and diffusion coefficients are obtained using the deep learning model to achieve multistage degradation prediction of corrosion depth. Finally, RUL prediction is realized using the degradation model to obtain the failure probability distribution. Results show that this method has high prediction accuracy and can adapt to the randomness and diversity of the service environment.

title: Risk resolution of airport surface based on hybrid Petri nets and inverse reinforcement learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。逆强化学习结合Petri网处理机场滑行冲突，在真实机场数据中降低冲突与延误，属于交通安全工程。

verified_metadata.abstract: Risk evaluation and conflict risk resolution of airport surface are two correlated challenge problems; however they are rarely studied jointly to reduce operation risk. Moreover, risk resolution performance of current methods also should be improved. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel risk resolution approach based on hybrid Petri nets and inverse reinforcement learning. Firstly, a hybrid Petri nets based on Bayesian fusion is presented to get taxiing risk evaluation of airport surface and its theorem of strict conservation and structure boundedness is proved. Secondly, a new risk model is proposed to minimize total operation cost of flights. Thirdly, a new risk evaluation method based on hybrid Petri nets is studied, and corresponding time complexity analysis is presented. Fourthly, a novel risk resolution algorithm based on inverse reinforcement learning strategy and game model is developed. Finally, datasets from Nanjing Lukou International Airport are used and experimental results show that: 1) our approach reduces delay time in multi-scale samples by 25% on average than state-of-the-arts methods; 2) taxiing conflicts with unacceptable risk are all resolved successfully; 3) it achieves stable convergence results while traditional methods oscillate uniformly, and even fail to reach a state of convergence; 4) sensitivity analysis and statistical result results verify the effectiveness of our method.

verified_metadata.abstract: Despite promising developments of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in predictive maintenance, existing RUL prediction models tend to be incapable of dynamical update using sequentially-collected online data and are then probably with low prognostic accuracy. This study addresses the following challenges of online remaining useful life (RUL) for industrial devices under varying even unknown operating conditions: (1) Degradation data of target machine are unavailable to model training, while data distribution drifts from offline data exist, (2) The degradation tendency of target machine is difficult to be captured because of the varying online operating condition. This paper proposes a Wiener process-assisted deep incremental transfer learning method for online RUL prediction. This method includes a pretraining prognostic model, which captures the essential degradation information from offline machines, and a Wiener process-assisted incremental update mechanism, which dedicates to capture of dynamic tendency information from online data. A Bayesian status feedback strategy is designed to generate pseudo-labels from Wiener process for the online RUL prediction. Numerical experimental results on three run-to-failure rolling element bearing datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, thus providing a deployable prognosis solution for practical applications.

verified_metadata.abstract: For evaluating reliability level of complex structure/system, a moving regression artificial neural network (MRANN) framework is proposed based on artificial neural network (ANN), moving regression technique and intelligent optimization algorithm. Under this framework, four methods of ANN-based moving least squares (MLS) (MLS-ANN), enhanced ANN-based MLS (MLS-EANN), ANN-based improved MLS (IMLS-ANN) and enhanced ANN-based improved MLS (IMLS-EANN) models are developed by introducing the Ivy algorithm and MLS technique into the ANN model. Herein, the Ivy algorithm is used to find the optimal radius of compact support region for selecting effective modeling samples or to search the optimal values of weights and thresholds of ANN model, the MLS technique is applied to assign weights for these effective modeling samples and to resolve unknown coefficients of ANN model, and the ANN model is employed to reflect the relationship of structural response and input parameters. Furthermore, three examples, including multivariate function approximation and probabilistic analyses, aeroengine high-pressure turbine blisk deformation reliability assessment and aircraft flap system deflection angle reliability analysis, are performed to validate and verify the effectiveness of these developed approaches. The analytical results show that MRANN framework holds excellent ability in the modeling and simulation features relative to the existing surrogate models.

title: Reconstruction of existing buildings for evacuation assessment under emergency situations using 3D Gaussian splatting and machine learning

verified_metadata.abstract: Existing buildings characterized by aging and structurally complex layouts pose significant challenges for emergency evacuation, necessitating advanced and dynamic risk assessment methods that go beyond conventional static evaluations. The primary scientific objective of this study is to develop and validate an integrated computational framework that combines high-fidelity 3D modeling with machine learning to quantitatively assess and predict evacuation risks in such structures. Using laser-scanned structural data, we reconstructed detailed building information models (BIM) via anisotropic 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling accurate spatial representation. These models were coupled with agent-based Pathfinder simulations to examine evacuation dynamics under diverse crowd densities and movement speeds. Simulated egress capacity informed a risk stratification mechanism. Further, we developed four machine learning models to predict evacuation time, among which the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization-integrated Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (IPSOCNN-LSTM) model achieved superior predictive accuracy. The results confirm the efficacy of the proposed framework in identifying critical evacuation risks and supporting real-time emergency decision-making. This research contributes a scientifically grounded, data-driven paradigm for dynamic risk assessment in built environments and offers scalable solutions for enhancing safety in aging urban infrastructure under various emergency scenarios.

title: Early warning and prevention of mud cakes in large-diameter slurry shields: Insights from construction parameter data analysis and interpretable machine learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。NGBoost和SHAP分析盾构施工参数并预警泥饼形成，学习模型处理具体土机相互作用风险。

verified_metadata.abstract: Mud cake blockage in large-diameter slurry shield (LDSS) construction is one of the key factors affecting the high efficiency and quality of tunnel construction. To address the lack of intelligent methods for mud cake detection, an early warning interpretable machine learning approach based on Exponential-Trigonometric Optimization (ETO)-Natural gradient boosting (NGBoost)- Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for LDSS is proposed. Twenty-four types of construction-related parameter data for LDSSs are selected as input indicators. The knowledge-driven method is used to analyse the construction parameters to obtain the risk level of the mud cake, and the degree of mud cake formation is classified via the ETO-NGBoost intelligent algorithm. The results are as follows: (1) ETO-NGBoost can obtain mud cake supervised classification results with high precision and high generalization performance, and the precision, recall and F1 score values in the test set are all above 0.93. (2) SHAP improves the interpretability and determines the important factors of slurry shields that influence the formation of mud cakes. (3) The supervised classification model driven by knowledge and data can be used to build a mud cake detection and early warning framework to judge the degree of mud cake formation in time. On this basis, effective prevention and control measures can be taken.

title: Fed-Joint: Joint modeling of nonlinear degradation signals and failure events for remaining useful life prediction using federated learning
abstract: Many failure mechanisms of machinery are closely related to the behavior of condition monitoring (CM) signals. To achieve a cost-effective preventive maintenance strategy, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction based on the signals is of paramount importance. However, the CM signals are often recorded at different factories and production lines, with limited amounts of data. Unfortunately, these datasets have rarely been shared between the sites due to data confidentiality and ownership issues, a lack of computing and storage power, and high communication costs associated with data transfer between sites and a data center. Another challenge in real applications is that the CM signals are often not explicitly specified \textit{a priori}, meaning that existing methods, which often usually a parametric form, may not be applicable. To address these challenges, we propose a new prognostic framework for RUL prediction using the joint modeling of nonlinear degradation signals and time-to-failure data within a federated learning scheme. The proposed method constructs a nonparametric degradation model using a federated multi-output Gaussian process and then employs a federated survival model to predict failure times and probabilities for in-service machinery. The superiority of the proposed method over other alternatives is demonstrated through comprehensive simulation studies and a case study using turbofan engine degradation signal data that include run-to-failure events.

title: An anomaly detection method for gas turbines in power plants using conditional variational autoencoder optimized with self-attention

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。自注意力条件变分自编码器分离变工况效应并诊断电厂燃气轮机异常。

verified_metadata.abstract: An innovative anomaly detection (AD) framework designed for gas turbines (GTs) in power plants working under variable operating conditions (OCs) was proposed based on conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) optimized with self-attention (SA) in this paper. Three key factors contribute to the model's superior performance in AD. First, the marginal distributions (MDs) of parameters were transformed into conditional probability distributions (CPDs) by incorporating OC variables as conditional inputs in the variational autoencoder (VAE) model, and decoupled modeling of equipment states and external OCs is achieved. Second, by embedding SA modules, the method dynamically adjusts weight allocation of the parameters to capture complex dependencies among them, which can enhance the capability of the model to represent intricate coupling relationships in multi-dimensional parameters. Third, the logarithmic reconstruction probability (LRP), derived from the probabilistic output of SA-CVAE, serves as a unified health indicator (HI) to evaluate the health condition of the GT. The indicator not only accounts for the discrepancy between the reconstructed and original inputs but also incorporates the influence of latent variable (LV) variance on the reconstruction results. Experiments were carried out on one synthetic, one public, and two real-world datasets, with SA-CVAE compared against six leading AD methods. The results demonstrate that under varying OCs, SA-CVAE exhibits superior performance in AD tasks, achieving leading or competitive results across key evaluation metrics.

title: Confidence interval-based robust topology optimization with active learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。主动学习Kriging估计结构响应置信区间并开展鲁棒拓扑优化，AI直接替代昂贵力学采样。

verified_metadata.abstract: Robust topology optimization (RTO) designs material distribution to improve structural performance while reducing its sensitivity to uncertainties. However, for classical probabilistic RTO, it remains challenging to achieve a trade-off between efficiency and applicability to problems involving complex multi-source uncertainties. To address this difficulty, a confidence interval-based RTO (CI-RTO) method is proposed in this paper, which simultaneously improves the structural response and its robustness through minimizing a weighted sum of the median and the width of the confidence interval. The method integrates Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) and the Kriging model to estimate the objective function. Inheriting non-intrusiveness from MCS and imposing no restrictions on input uncertainties, CI-RTO is capable of addressing complex multi-source uncertainties and non-linear relationships between response and random variables. Meanwhile, the Kriging model alleviates the computational burden arising from large-scale sampling, and a confidence interval active learning (CIAL) strategy is developed for its efficient construction. By adaptively improving modeling accuracy around the median and confidence bounds, CIAL significantly reduces the training cost of the Kriging model, thereby further accelerating CI-RTO. In addition, regarding sensitivity analysis, CI-RTO holds a natural advantage over classical RTO methods that minimize mean and standard deviation, since its computational cost is merely three times that of deterministic topology optimization (DTO). The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using four numerical examples, including macro, micro, and 3D design problems, where multiple uncertainties and non-linear responses to uncertain parameters are incorporated. Comparisons with other methods confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of CI-RTO.

title: Estimating node importance in transportation networks: A scalable machine learning approach

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。集成机器学习预测交通节点失效造成的总旅行时间变化，量化实际道路网络关键节点。

verified_metadata.abstract: Urban transportation networks are vulnerable to performance degradation from node-level congestion, such as accidents or capacity overloads. Traditional vulnerability analyses employ iterative traffic assignment to quantify the impact of each congested node on total travel time (TTT). Although accurate, this process results in substantial computational costs and becomes prohibitively slow for large or dynamic networks. To address these limitations, we develop a scalable machine learning framework that predicts the TTT impact of individual node failures. Our model uses features drawn from origin–destination demand data, link attributes, network centrality measures, and socio-economic contexts. We construct an ensemble of four base learners — Random Forests, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Support Vector Classifier — combined via Logistic Regression as a meta-learner to classify nodes into high, medium, and low importance categories, and include a Multi-Layer Perceptron model for comparison. Evaluation across six real-world transportation networks demonstrates that our approach consistently achieves up to 85% classification accuracy while reducing computation time by up to 94%. We enhance interpretability through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identify initial link flow estimates as the most influential predictor. Furthermore, we verify model transferability by training on small variants of the Berlin and Birmingham networks and successfully applying the same models to their full-scale networks and two additional transportation networks. Our results confirm that the proposed framework offers rapid and reliable identification of critical intersections, facilitating more efficient network planning and resilience assessment.

title: A reinforcement learning approach to network-level maintenance planning of co-located road and water infrastructures with interdependencies

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。强化学习联合交通和水力仿真规划道路与水管的相依退化维护，并在实际城区验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Due to co-location and spatial proximity, deteriorating transportation infrastructure (TI) and water infrastructure (WI) are geographically interdependent, exhibiting complex interactions both within and across systems. Failures from degradation or maintenance disruptions in one system can impair its own performance and cascade into the other. However, many existing studies address long-term maintenance only at the component, subsystem, or single-system level, without fully accounting for interdependencies both within and across co-located infrastructures. This paper proposes a network-wide joint long-term maintenance planning framework that integrates traffic and hydraulic simulations to capture interdependencies within and across multiple infrastructure systems. A reinforcement learning-based optimization model is formulated to minimize the expected cumulative costs of co-located TI and WI systems over a long-term planning horizon while accounting for future uncertainties in the deterioration of roads and pipes. The model jointly quantifies both short-term and long-term economic impacts of joint maintenance decisions at network level by comprehensively investigating diverse topological relationships and interactions between co-located roads and pipes. The framework is further validated through a realistic case study in Ybor City, Tampa, and benchmarked against alternative maintenance strategies, demonstrating cost savings achieved through proactive, coordinated decision-making across interdependent TI and WI systems.

title: Multi-modal graph convolutional network for vessel trajectory prediction based on cooperative intention enhance using conditional variational autoencoder

verified_metadata.abstract: Advances in maritime instrumentation and measurement (I&M), particularly through the widespread adoption of automatic identification system (AIS), have significantly accelerated the development of intelligent situational awareness systems (ISAS). As a critical component of ISAS, cooperative navigation demands greater accuracy and reliability in vessel trajectory prediction. Nevertheless, challenges arising from complex inter-vessel interactions and implicit intention inference expose limitations in modeling explicit and implicit relationships and ensuring the robustness of trajectory prediction. To address these challenges, we propose a cooperative intention enhance multi-modal graph convolutional network (CIE-MGCN) to learn and predict the future vessel trajectories. The CIE-MGCN is composed of three primary components: Interaction Extractor, Intention Constructor, and Trajectory Generator. In Interaction Extractor, we designed the social-community extractor (SCE) to construct diverse interaction graphs that capture both cooperative and adversarial relationships among vessel trajectories, and the multi-modal transformer (MMT) to fuse explicit interaction features across various modalities. In Intention Constructor, we introduce a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)-based approach to infer implicit relationships and capture potential future behavioral variations and multi-modal probability distributions of future trajectories are produced by Trajectory Generator. Extensive experiments on real-world navigation data show that CIE-MGCN outperforms state-of-the-art models in accuracy and robustness, owing to its strong reasoning and learning capabilities. These reliable predictions further support cooperative navigation within ISAS by enhancing coordination and decision-making among multi-vessel.

verified_metadata.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely applied to remaining useful life (RUL) prediction driven by multi-source information fusion. However, the conventional GNN-based approaches use the shared node features for both RUL prediction and spatial dependency modeling, which may induce implicit information conflicts. Moreover, they have no effective mechanisms for identifying the weakly correlated nodes, which causes the prediction accuracy to be easily disturbed by noise. To resolve potential information conflicts, we propose a novel node feature contrastive decoupling module (NFCDM). The NFCDM employs a cross-fusion-contrastive decoupling strategy to explicitly decompose node features into global degradation features for RUL prediction and local relational features for spatial dependency modeling. Task-specific contrastive decoupling constraints are further designed to ensure the task relevance and information independence of the decoupled features. In addition, to achieve the effective node screening, a deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (DDCS) is proposed. This novel selector is capable of constructing joint evaluation metrics based on the deviation of global degradation features and the information diffusion capability of nodes to adaptively discard redundant nodes. Built upon these two novel modules, the contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (CDGNN-DDCS) is proposed for RUL prediction. Comparative experiments on public datasets confirm the superiority of the proposed method. Lastly, its engineering practicality is successfully verified via an RUL prediction experiment on actual wind turbines.

verified_metadata.abstract: Soil spatial variability significantly affects slope stability and landslide behaviors, particularly under complex geological conditions where traditional finite element analysis (FEA), while precise, incurs prohibitive computational costs. This study introduces a new surrogate model leveraging graph attention networks (GAT) equipped with sample and aggregate (SAGE) sampling, designed to efficiently handle large-scale data while predicting slope safety factors and identifying potential slip surfaces. The GAT model utilizes a spatial graph construction based on k-dimensional trees (KD-Trees), enabling the effective representation of complex mechanical interactions within the soil. The results indicate the superior performance of this model over traditional machine learning methods such as random forest, feedforward neural networks, support vector regression, and convolutional neural networks, achieving a mean squared error of 0.000218 and an R2 of 0.995. The application of GAT with SAGE sampling highlights the potential of graph neural networks to significantly enhance real-time slope stability monitoring and risk assessment in the geotechnical engineering field, demonstrating a promising direction for computationally efficient surrogate modeling.

title: Reverse Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic inference framework for structural health monitoring and inverse analysis in engineering

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。反向变分自编码器执行结构响应的贝叶斯反演，网格结构实验验证多解弯曲、应变与位移重建。

verified_metadata.abstract: Inverse analysis in structural engineering involves inferring uncertain parameters from limited external observations, which is crucial for structural health monitoring and maintenance. However, real-world applications often face under-constrained problems with multiple possible solutions due to sparse measurements. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning-based framework, termed Reverse Variational Auto-Encoder (RVAE), to fulfill efficient probabilistic structural inverse analysis. The RVAE framework modifies the original VAE structure to consider the causality relationship underlying inverse problems, enabling a semi-supervised learning paradigm for label-agnostic scenarios. The effectiveness of the RVAE framework is validated through a grid structure experiment. The implemented model successfully reveals all possible solutions for bending amplitudes, strains, and node displacements, with root-mean-squared reconstruction errors of 1.21 %, 2.77 %, and 1.36 %, respectively. A comparative analysis is conducted between mainstream inversion algorithms and RVAE. The results demonstrate that while all the other inversion algorithms achieve low reconstruction errors, they provide single-solution estimation, thus highlighting RVAE's capability to provide the most comprehensive information. RVAE's capability for real-time probabilistic estimation of structural parameters is further discussed and demonstrated in a full-scale bridge tower experiment, where it utilizes multi-sensor data to infer critical structural parameters, showing strong adaptability to noisy, incomplete, and heterogeneous monitoring inputs. In summary, RVAE tackles the challenges of large-scale parameter inversion in engineering structures by enabling efficient probabilistic inference under sparse observations. It supports semi-supervised learning in label-agnostic scenarios and real-time prediction of multiple plausible solutions, thereby fulfilling the synchronous updating requirements of digital twin systems.

verified_metadata.abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) has become a key enabler for condition-based maintenance, yet its “black-box” nature limits explainability and reliability. Explainability concerns understanding the model’s decision process, including the physical meaning and contribution of extracted features, while reliability addresses the rationality and stability of diagnostic results under varying conditions. As explainability analysis reveals potential biases and irrational dependencies, it serves as the foundation for improving reliability, spurring extensive research on explainable intelligent fault diagnosis (XIFD). This survey first reviews the core components of IFD to clarify how XIFD enhances model transparency, and then categorizes existing approaches into ante-hoc and post-hoc methods. Ante-hoc methods focus on building inherently interpretable models, whereas post-hoc methods explain results through external analysis. Then, we provide the usage and disadvantages of existing post-hoc XIFD methods and emphasize the significance of ante-hoc XIFD by giving insights into the most popular signal processing-informed IFD methods. Finally, we consolidate the pressing challenges that necessitate immediate attention within the realm of XIFD research, and offer insights into promising prospects for future research endeavors. The library is available at: https://github.com/HazeDT/Awesome-Explainable-IFD-Library.

title: Predictive maintenance: A historical survey of models with imperfect inspections
abstract: The review article thoroughly examines predictive maintenance models where the conditional probabilities of inspection outcomes rely on prognostics. The demand for effective predictive maintenance models has increased due to various industries adopting data-driven strategies for improved operational effectiveness. The study retraces the historical development of these models up to significant improvements in methodologies to cover uncertainties related to inspections performed in predictive maintenance. Building on previous work, we further analyze how to input conditional probabilities of inspection outcomes into predictive maintenance modeling for better prediction of equipment breakdown and optimization of maintenance scheduling. Comparative analysis highlights a clear trade-off between model accuracy and computational complexity, showing that simpler models with the constant-probability of inspection outcomes are more interpretable but less precise, while advanced models that incorporate inspection timing, dependence on failure time, multiple time-correlated inspections, or machine learning offer higher accuracy at the expense of complexity. This synthesis also identifies the relative advantages and disadvantages of different approaches, proposing guidance for practical application in industrial systems. The article concludes by discussing future research opportunities and the potential of new technologies to enhance predictive maintenance strategies related to imperfect inspections.

title: Evacuation under terrorist attacks: A crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。深度强化学习优化应急人群疏散并控制拥堵，验证具体公共基础设施安全仿真任务。

verified_metadata.abstract: Terrorist attacks pose severe security challenges for crowd evacuation, especially in high-density scenarios where panic-induced congestion significantly increases the number of casualties. Although existing research mainly focuses on the direct impact of attacks, the critical issue of low evacuation efficiency and increased mortality rates caused by congestion is often overlooked. Therefore, effectively regulating crowd congestion during terrorist attacks to enhance evacuation efficiency and reduce the number of casualties is a major challenge. To address this, this paper proposes a crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning under terrorist attack scenarios to enhance evacuation efficiency and safety. First, a congestion–threat coupled cellular automaton (CTCA) is constructed to simulate individual risk-avoidance behavior in a threatening environment. Second, by introducing the attack-aware Dueling Double Deep Q Network (D3QN), a congestion control method based on attack-aware D3QN and CTCA is proposed to learn optimal evacuation strategies that avoid high-risk and high-density areas. Finally, a crowd evacuation navigation system integrating CTCA and D3QN is developed. The experimental results show that the proposed method demonstrates outstanding performance in reducing congestion levels, shortening evacuation times, and lowering mortality rates. It provides theoretical support and technical tools for public safety emergency response systems.

title: A cascaded machine learning model for identification of ship breach characteristics during flooding using sensor data fusion

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。时序卷积估计进水体积，SVR和ANN反演船体破口参数，并用驳船进水实验验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Water ingress in damaged ships can severely impair navigation and cause sinking. Accurate breach identification is vital for effective incident response. Due to multi-characteristic interaction of breach parameters, minor identification errors can cumulatively lead to significant inaccuracies in subsequent flooding assessment. This study proposes a cascaded machine learning model for breach identification of damaged ship using sensor data. First, the model employs temporal convolutional network to estimate floodwater volume by integrating data from internal water level and floating state sensors. Then, the model combines support vector regression and artificial neural network to identify and fine-tune breach parameters using the floodwater volume data. The hyperparameters of the models are automatically tuned based on particle swarm optimization. Strategies for training data generation and sensor fusion are explored. The model effectiveness is validated through tests on a barge under transient and progressive flooding, demonstrating consistent results with benchmark data for breach parameters and flooding consequences.

title: Dynamic ensemble model incorporating deep reinforcement learning for earthquake casualty prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。动态集成与DDQN依据不同地震灾害场景预测伤亡，AI用于灾害影响的量化预测。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of earthquake casualties is crucial to inform decision-making for efficient government rescue operations. This paper proposes a Stacking Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II Double Deep Q-Network Dynamic Ensemble (SND-DE), a unified prediction framework that integrates a two-layer Stacking architecture, Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for multi-objective parameter optimization and a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) decision agent for dynamic parameter selection. Within SND-DE, the ensemble prediction model utilizes a two-layer stacking structure, selecting high-performance base models and meta-models through experiments and employs a five-fold cross-validation method for prediction. A multi-objective optimization algorithm optimizes the key parameters of the prediction model, aiming to minimize both bias and variance of the prediction. Embedding the non-dominated solutions of the key parameters of the prediction model into the DDQN environment enables the model to adapt to the characteristics of different disaster scenarios and dynamically parameterize the model to reduce prediction errors. The effectiveness of the proposed model is comprehensively evaluated through a series of experiments, whose results indicate that: (1) the SND-DE model is well-trained, exhibits high predictive accuracy and achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.95279; (2) the performance of the ensemble model surpasses that of all individual base models; (3) the NSGA-II optimization algorithm effectively reduces the model's bias and variance; (4) the DDQN model exhibits strong convergence and achieves high reward values.

title: BMTR-former: Accelerating RUL prediction on scarce and censored data via bayesian-based multi-task reconstruction transformer

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多任务Transformer利用删失设备传感器数据同时重建信号与估计剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: To overcome the limitations of data censoring in Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, we introduce BMTR-Former, a Bayesian Multi-Task Reconstruction Transformer. Our framework uniquely treats censored data not as a limitation but as a resource, integrating a supervised RUL prediction task with a self-supervised signal reconstruction task. This multi-task paradigm leverages all available trajectories to learn robust degradation patterns. The self-supervised component uses both censored and uncensored data to learn degradation patterns, enhancing RUL prediction. A hierarchical Bayesian model first denoises sensor signals to provide clean inputs for the Transformer core. Experiments show BMTR-Former excels on highly censored datasets, not only achieving state-of-the-art accuracy but also demonstrating remarkable training efficiency and rapid convergence, decisively outperforming competing models. By transforming censored data into a key asset for generalization, our work offers a new, data-efficient paradigm for industrial prognostics.
