verified_metadata.abstract: This paper presents a systematic framework for integrating large language models (LLMs) and AI agents into disaster-resilient infrastructure research. By examining seven key task domains—knowledge anchoring, prediction, assessment, intelligent design and simulation, data augmentation, embodied intelligence, and decision support—we show how LLMs and AI agents can reshape traditional disaster-resilience workflows through enhanced multimodal perception, long-horizon reasoning, cross-stage coordination, and automated task execution. Two representative case studies further demonstrate the feasibility of this paradigm: (1) a multimodal building-damage assessment system capable of city-scale semantic reasoning and transparent diagnostic interpretation, and (2) a LangGraph-based reasoning agent for automated seismic resilience assessment and recovery decision-making of infrastructure systems. These cases highlight the potential of LLMs and AI agents to bridge fragmented data sources, orchestrate multi-stage analytical workflows, and support high-impact resilience applications. Despite these advances, key challenges remain, including data scarcity, reliability and consistency issues, deployment constraints, and ethical or security concerns. Addressing these limitations is essential for developing trustworthy, efficient, and scalable intelligent disaster-prevention systems. Overall, this work establishes a unified cognitive–action paradigm that offers forward-looking pathways for the next generation of intelligent and resilient infrastructure technologies.

title: AI-augmented modeling of post-fire soil hydraulic conductivity across environmental gradients for geohazard assessment

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。GAN、VAE和混合专家生成火后土壤水力传导率数据，并通过边坡稳定模型检验地质灾害影响。

verified_metadata.abstract: Wildfires substantially alter soil hydraulic and mechanical properties, reshaping infiltration dynamics and increasing susceptibility to rainfall-triggered geohazards such as debris flows and landslides. A key challenge is the scarcity of paired pre- and post-wildfire soil hydraulic conductivity measurements across vegetation types, soil textures, and burn severities. The main objective of this study is to use generative AI algorithms, together with a curated dataset of measured pre- and post-fire soil hydraulic properties, to augment sparse observations and produce realistic synthetic conductivity pairs across diverse environmental gradients. A curated cross-site dataset of 46 paired conductivity measurements was compiled, and six tabular generators, Gaussian Copula, GAN, VAE, Copula+GAN, VAE+GAN, and a Mixture of Experts (MoE), were trained to produce synthetic conductivity tables conditioned on soil, vegetation, and burn severity. Model performance was evaluated using distributional fidelity metrics, rare-group behavior, memorization diagnostics, and Train-on-Synthetic/Test-on-Real (TSTR) utility. Scale effects were also assessed by varying synthetic sample sizes, and synthetic conductivity contrasts were propagated through a slope stability model to evaluate downstream geotechnical implications. Results show that VAE, VAE+GAN, and MoE provide the strongest balance of fidelity and predictive utility (normalized MAE within 5 to 10% of the real-data baseline) while maintaining low memorization risk (MI ≈ 0.40 to 0.52, versus >0.8 for copula-based baselines). Synthetic datasets enlarged to approximately three to six times the real sample size stabilize dependence structures and improve downstream accuracy. In slope-stability propagation, GAN and MoE most closely reproduced reference factor-of-safety distributions, whereas VAE slightly smoothed lower tails.

title: A low-altitude emergency event grade prediction model integrating attention mechanism and spatio-temporal graph neural network

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。时空图网络与注意力结合物理约束预测低空应急事件等级，服务航空基础设施预警。

verified_metadata.abstract: Low-altitude safety serves as a critical safeguard for the development of low-altitude economic activities, yet traditional early warning methods struggle to effectively address the complex spatiotemporal dynamic correlations during emergencies. This paper proposes a Low-altitude Emergency Level Prediction Model (GSTA-Net) that integrates attention mechanisms with spatiotemporal graph neural networks. By constructing an adaptive spatial domain graph that combines physical constraints with semantic associations, and designing a gated fusion mechanism incorporating dual spatial and temporal attention, the model achieves precise localization and efficient representation of dynamic spatiotemporal risk patterns. Experiments on an independently developed low-altitude safety dataset demonstrate that the model significantly outperforms mainstream spatiotemporal prediction models in key metrics such as macro-average F1 score and high-level event detection rate. The visualization of attention weights aligns closely with domain experts' analytical logic, showcasing excellent predictive accuracy and decision-making interpretability. This study provides an effective approach for building precise and reliable intelligent early warning systems for low-altitude operations.

title: A review on prognostics and health management applications with federated learning for advanced engineering systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。综述联邦学习用于先进工程设备健康管理与寿命预测，实质比较方法、隐私和工业部署任务。

verified_metadata.abstract: Modern engineering systems are increasingly complex and interconnected, making their health management and operational reliability more challenging. Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) enables condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, yet conventional centralized approaches face regulatory barriers, privacy risks, and difficulty in modelling heterogeneous sensor data, while incurring high communication costs at the edge. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative model training without raw data sharing. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of PHM technologies, FL methodologies, and their integration for distributed, privacy-sensitive industrial environments. We first survey advances in physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid prognostic methods, together with intelligent maintenance and condition-based decision strategies, critically evaluating their adaptability under heterogeneous, resource-constrained settings. We then classify FL approaches by data distribution, network architecture, and participant type, and assess their applicability to PHM tasks through quantitative comparison of privacy-preserving techniques and lightweight deployment strategies. Building on this, we establish a structured mapping between PHM challenges and FL mechanisms, analyse applications in RUL prediction, fault diagnosis, and health monitoring, and identify unresolved gaps. The review concludes with a forward-looking roadmap covering domain-adaptive FL algorithms, resource-efficient edge architectures, and verifiable privacy mechanisms, as well as integration with emerging technologies such as large language models and digital twins. By bridging methodological advances with industrial deployment realities, this work offers actionable guidance for developing scalable, secure, and high-performance PHM solutions in the Industrial Internet of Things era.

title: Causal-enhanced machine learning framework for long-term wind power probabilistic forecasting

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。因果图网络、LSTM与WGAN联合气象信息预测风功率分布及不确定性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Various and uncertain meteorological factors are the primary reason that makes long-term wind power forecasting formidable, which significantly constraints the reliability and economic viability of wind power. Evaluating the causal relationships between meteorological factors and wind power generation is a promising approach to addressing this issue. Therefore, we propose a novel day-ahead wind power forecasting framework that fuses a directed acyclic graph (DAG)–graph neural network (GNN) causal analysis model a data-driven long-term autoregressive model (autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA)–long short-term memory (LSTM)) and weather condition recognition model based on Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) algorithm to identify main meteorological features with influential causal effect on wind power then quantify uncertainty and perform time series wind power forecasting. An incremental learning strategy is employed to update and calibrate the prediction model continuously. The proposed framework is validated against real-world meteorological and wind power generation data from a wind farm in China. The experimental results demonstrate that this framework effectively captures the inherent uncertainty in long-term wind power forecasting, achieves high probabilistic forecasting performance, and exhibits high prediction accuracy.

title: Multi-sensor spatial and multiscale temporal transformer guided by frequency-domain attention for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多传感器时空Transformer结合频域低秩先验，在C-MAPSS与N-CMAPSS预测发动机剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for aeroengine prognostics and health management. However, standard Transformer-based models struggle to capture multiscale temporal dynamics and cross-sensor dependencies in aeroengine sensors. Moreover, time-domain scaled dot-product attention does not exploit the degradation characteristics of onboard sensor series or the low-rank structure evident in the frequency domain. We propose Multi-sensor Spatial and Multiscale Temporal Transformer guided by Frequency-Domain Attention (MSMT-FDA), which couples a dual-branch encoder-encompassing multiscale temporal cues and multi-sensor spatial correlations-with frequency-domain low-rank distance attention, leveraging spectral low-rank priors of engine degradation signals. On C-MAPSS (FD001-FD004) and DS02 of N-CMAPSS, our method attains state-of-the-art performance and remains robust across flight regimes, enabling predictive maintenance.

title: Convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network-based state of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。卷积注意力通道分解网络估计锂电池健康，在三种材料和充放电策略数据中验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health (SOH) is critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the performance of existing methods is often compromised by redundant information present in monitoring data. To address this issue, we propose a novel method for SOH estimation based on a convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network (CACFMN). This method consists of a feature extraction module, several channel factorization mixture and temporal processing (CFMTP) modules, and an estimator module. Specifically, a dual-branch convolutional attention module is established to adaptively capture health characteristics from the charging data of LIBs. Furthermore, the CFMTP module is designed to reduce redundancy among the various channels of these characteristics. Subsequently, the estimator module is developed to estimate the SOH of LIBs. Finally, the proposed method was validated using three battery datasets that employed distinct materials and charging-discharging strategies. The experimental results indicate that the designed CFMTP module effectively reduces redundant information across channels, thereby enhancing the accuracy and generalizability of SOH estimation.

title: Joint condition-based maintenance and production of manufacturing systems under flexible decision timing using deep reinforcement learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。HAPPO深度强化学习在设备状态与退化约束下联合决策多机维护和生产时机，属于制造系统可靠运行。

verified_metadata.abstract: In manufacturing systems, deterioration increases the risk of unmet demand due to reduced product quality and increased downtime. To sustain high productivity and effectively meet demand, efficient coordination between maintenance and production decisions is essential. However, conventional policies typically do not adjust production decisions in response to system deterioration, which can lead to decreased productivity and service levels. This paper proposes a novel and well-motivated framework for the joint decision-making of maintenance and production in parallel manufacturing systems, formulated as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP). Specifically, we incorporate flexible decision timing that allows real-time adjustments to production speeds whenever system deterioration occurs, in order to maintain a high demand fulfillment rate. To solve the resulting large-scale decision-making problem, characterized by a high-dimensional information space encompassing system condition, inventory, demand, and maintenance status, we apply a deep reinforcement learning algorithm: heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization (HAPPO). Numerical discussion shows that the proposed method, which derives the joint policy with flexible decision timing and production speed control using HAPPO, outperforms three alternative methods. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that flexible production speed control not only increases total rewards but also improves demand fulfillment. The proposed joint decision-making framework offers a practical and effective solution for deteriorating systems, contributing to the development of more resilient and adaptive manufacturing operations.

title: Spatiotemporal causal modeling of cascading failures in power systems
abstract: • A spatiotemporal causal model is proposed for cascading failure analysis. • A novel counterfactual method performs robust root cause analysis of cascades. • Causal metrics guide more efficient grid hardening than traditional methods. • Causal metrics identify critical components for robust system monitoring. The interconnected nature of modern power grids makes them susceptible to cascading failures, complex events that can trigger widespread blackouts. Data-driven analysis of these events is often limited by an undue on statistical correlation, which hinders model explainability and prevents true root cause analysis. This paper proposes a spatiotemporal causal inference framework that learns the underlying cause-and-effect mechanisms of failure propagation from historical data. The proposed Structural Causal Model enables forward-looking prediction, backward-looking root cause analysis via counterfactuals, and guides grid reinforcement through causal metrics. Results on standard literature test cases validate the framework’s effectiveness. The model achieves high prediction accuracy (84.29%), outperforming several benchmarks, and correctly identifies the initial failure in over 70% of scenarios. Furthermore, a hardening strategy guided by causal metrics is shown to be significantly more efficient than traditional approaches, requiring less than half the number of reinforced components to achieve a comparable level of system reliability. The proposed framework offers a robust, explainable, and actionable methodology for understanding and mitigating cascading failures.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven framework for predicting cascading failure paths in power grids

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。比较随机森林、MLP等AI方法预测IEEE电网级联故障传播路径，研究具体电力系统失效。

verified_metadata.abstract: As evidenced by large-scale blackouts with severe economic impacts, cascading failures remain a critical challenge that demands intelligent methods to detect hidden propagation paths before they escalate. This work proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework that encompasses codified data generation, methodical model comparison, meticulous hyperparameter optimization, and holistic performance evaluation for propagation paths prediction. Using training data generated under diverse operating conditions for power systems, including IEEE 39, 89, 118 and 300-bus models, this study investigates the performance of decision tree, logistic regression (LogR), k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) in predicting cascading failure paths, alongside a comparative analysis with the influence model and graph neural networks using graph-level and branch-level accuracy metrics and efficiency metrics, as well as a proposed composite reliability index. To further improve model performance, Bayesian optimization is applied for hyperparameters tuning of the AI methods. Comprehensive numerical experiments are performed, revealing that MLP, SVM, and LogR consistently achieve robust performance while the other models exhibit vulnerabilities under moderate load scaling conditions. The proposed framework can support industry stakeholders in selecting and deploying suitable AI methods for cascading failure prediction in real-world power grid applications.

title: Towards intelligent safety assessment under blast loading: A large language model-powered multi-agent framework

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。LLM多智能体调用领域工具进行爆载作用下目标结构损伤与安全评估，包含具体力学工程任务。

verified_metadata.abstract: Reliable and timely safety assessment under blast loading constitutes a critical, expertise-driven challenge, requiring the accurate evaluation of damage effects on specific targets under prescribed conditions. Despite advances in related fields, such as ammunition theory and vulnerability analysis, fully reliable and intelligent safety assessment systems are still in their fancy. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates large language model (LLM) reasoning with multi-agent coordination, featuring domain expertise embedded in customized safety assessment tools, which eliminates the dependency on large-scale training datasets. Experiments across diverse LLM scales, query complexities, and target conditions demonstrate the excellent stability and adaptability of the proposed framework to autonomously complete complex tasks without human intervention. An empirical investigation of system-level target safety assessment substantiates the necessity of an agentic design framework, as the standalone LLM fails to produce correct results even despite employing detailed chain-of-thought reasoning. Complementary evidence from a case study on component-level targets further underscores the importance of the multi-agent architecture. Specifically, the simplified dual-agent configuration struggles to effectively handle more complex task demands. This study highlights the potential of combining artificial intelligence with traditional methodologies, offering a promising pathway for advancing safety assessment and its engineering applications.

title: Adaptive and robust scheduling subject to machine degradation and breakdowns in networked multi-factory systems via hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。层次多头强化学习模拟机械退化和故障下多工厂系统的稳健运行调度，处理技术设备失效约束。

verified_metadata.abstract: In equipment-intensive manufacturing, machine degradation and breakdowns threaten system robustness and production continuity, while multi-layer couplings and dynamic collaboration in mass-customized networked multi-factory systems exacerbate these challenges. This study addresses the robust scheduling problem for networked multi-factory systems with machine degradation and breakdowns under mass customization (MC-NMFRS-MDB) and proposes a hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning (HMH-DRL) approach. The problem is formulated as a multi-Markov decision process with a high-dimensional state space capturing degradation and breakdown dynamics, a dual-layer action space addressing coupled subproblems, and a multi-head reward balancing performance and robustness. A hierarchical multi-head policy architecture enables coordinated decision-making and multi-objective optimization. The training process employs prioritized experience replay to improve learning efficiency, nonlinear clipping to stabilize policy updates, and a retraining mechanism for continual adaptation. Numerical results indicate that HMH-DRL reliably converges, improving scheduling performance and robustness by over 10.59% and 10.98%, respectively, compared with four DRL methods, three metaheuristic algorithms, and one reliability-driven heuristic, confirming its effectiveness in complex and dynamic scenarios.

title: A deep-learning-based approach for temporal transportation network dismantling

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多头图注意力学习时变交通网络高阶特征并识别影响网络效率的关键节点，研究网络鲁棒性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurately assessing the importance of individual nodes at different time for maintaining the efficiency of temporal transportation networks is an important challenging problem. It is for the first time that this issue has been formulated as a temporal network dismantling (ND) problem, which aims to identify the minimal set of nodes with time information whose disruption can rapidly degrade temporal network efficiency. This paper proposes a deep-learning-based network dismantling framework for its solution. Specifically, a directed acyclic graph representation is used to capture the continuous topological changes in a temporal network. Then, our framework employs multi-head graph attention networks to learn latent higher-order features by aggregating different temporal features of nodes and their neighbors, and incorporates the shortcut connections technique to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms baselines and exhibits significant robustness. Furthermore, an early warning signal indicator is adopted to quantify the dismantling risk of temporal networks. Our approach offers a practical tool for identifying critical nodes in temporal transportation networks, thereby assisting stakeholders in enhancing robustness of transportation services.

title: An adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for remaining useful life of rolling bearings

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。稀疏贝叶斯神经网络增量学习滚动轴承动态退化与预测不确定性，两处试验台验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: The high prediction accuracy of deep neural network (DNN) relies on abundant high-quality training data. However, the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings is confronted with scarce failure data and poor degradation consistency, which severely restrict the generalization ability of DNN models and the reliability of prediction results. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for rolling element bearings. Specifically, a temporal cascaded Bayesian neural network framework is designed through the collaborative coupling of Bayesian probabilistic modeling and temporal cascaded network structure, thereby enabling quantitative characterization of prediction uncertainty while capturing the dynamic degradation trend of bearings. Aiming at the widespread issue of high complexity of BNN models, an importance-guided parameter preservation mechanism is constructed to retain parameters encoding professional knowledge while pruning redundant network components for explicit model lightweighting. At the incremental prediction stage, a stage-adaptive correlation alignment strategy is developed to dynamically learn the intrinsic knowledge correlations between different stages, thus alleviating degradation inconsistency issues and improving the model’s generalization and robustness. Experimental results on two test benches indicate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and excellent generalization ability, while comparative experiments with several state-of-the-art methods further validate its robustness and superiority.

title: Interpretable deep learning framework for urban bus traffic safety situation forecast

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。深度学习时序特征框架预测城市公交交通安全，并量化路网构造和温度等影响。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate forecasting of urban bus traffic safety is essential for transportation authorities to plan traffic systems, formulate safety policies, and promote public transit use. However, the current understanding of the evolutionary patterns and correlation mechanisms of bus traffic safety with operation-related factors remains limited.​ Thus, this study proposes an Adaptive Three-Stage Temporal Feature Forecasting(ATS-TFF) framework. Taking a mountainous Chinese city as an example, it forecasts the trend of urban bus traffic safety situation (BTSS) and analyzes the relationships between BTSS and multiple influencing factors.​ The results reveal at the feature level, factors such as the mean number of downstream bus stops in the road sections, the mean number of tunnels allowing lane changes along the routes, and the maximum temperature all have substantial effects on BTSS. Temporally, BTSS most significantly affects itself five days later. At the interaction level, the mean number of downstream bus stops in the passed road sections four days prior has the most important impacts on BTSS. ​Overall, the proposed ATS-TFF framework and findings provide data-driven support for proactive bus system safety management, advancing the shift from reactive control to forward-looking, targeted intervention strategies.

title: Data-driven co-design of power distribution networks for resilience enhancement through graph neural network aided performance estimation
abstract: To enhance the resilience of critical infrastructures, a co-design optimization framework is developed for the design of the distribution network and its recovery scheduling. Since network representations are distinct from conventional numerical data, the framework needs to be tailored to overcome unique challenges. Due to the networks being represented as graphs rather than numerical values, derivative-free optimization is the most suitable option. In a random search, the neighborhood must be defined considering the graph data structure. In this study, a surrogate model that can estimate the resilience of the network system is built using a deep-learning-based graph neural network (GNN) to reduce the computational burden during a derivative-free optimization algorithm. Network vulnerabilities are identified using centrality measures from graph theory, where the total demand loss is quantified with sequential component removals to represent resilience loss. Integrating the design optimization to the recovery problem defined as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model, the proposed framework can find the optimum solution for network design and recovery resource scheduling. To prove the efficacy of the proposed GNN-based co-design framework, it was applied for a power system benchmark, where the results demonstrated the practicality of the framework.

title: Active learning Kriging with spherical low-discrepancy sampling and gradient refinement for efficient reliability analysis of geotechnical systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。主动Kriging结合球面低差异采样和梯度细化，计算岩土系统结构可靠性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Reliability analysis of geotechnical systems often requires numerous high-fidelity simulations to evaluate complex limit state functions (LSFs), resulting in prohibitive computational cost. Traditional surrogate-based approaches, such as active learning Kriging with Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), often suffer from local clustering of background samples and inefficient exploration of the failure domain, especially in high-dimensional problems. To address these limitations, an enhanced active learning Kriging framework, termed AK-SLDS, is developed. The method integrates a spherical low-discrepancy sampling (SLDS) scheme with a gradient-refined learning strategy to improve the global representativeness of background samples and the local accuracy of surrogate updates. The performance of AK-SLDS is verified through five numerical examples, including two benchmark problems and three engineering applications. The two benchmark problems demonstrate the method’s accuracy and efficiency for low- to medium-dimensional reliability analyses. The engineering examples, involving the bearing capacity of a shallow footing and two slope stability problems, confirm its robustness for strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional geotechnical systems. Results show that AK-SLDS produces failure probability estimates in close agreement with MCS while requiring substantially fewer true LSF evaluations compared with conventional active learning approaches. The method thus provides an efficient and reliable framework for conducting reliability analysis in geotechnical systems.

title: Active learning with dynamic exploitation-exploration balance for aircraft engine remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。贝叶斯深度学习量化预后不确定性，主动选取发动机退化标注样本以改善寿命预测。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aircraft engines using deep learning is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled run-to-failure data. Active learning (AL) addresses this by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, but traditional methods often use fixed criteria and fail to properly balance the exploitation-exploration trade-off. This paper proposes a novel AL framework that dynamically manages this balance. We utilize a Bayesian hybrid deep learning model to quantify prognostic uncertainty. Based on this, we develop a dual-criteria acquisition function, which integrates uncertainty and diversity by using a feedback mechanism to dynamically adjust their balance. To mitigate redundancy in batch queries, we also introduce a greedy selection algorithm to promote intra-batch diversity. Validation on the C-MAPSS and PHM08 benchmark datasets demonstrates that our framework achieves high RUL prediction accuracy with significantly fewer labeled samples than the compared AL strategies.

title: A data-driven framework for failure probability prediction of water supply pipelines: Integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。ANN与SVR结合特征选择和同质分组，预测上海实际供水管道失效概率。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of water supply pipeline failure probability over a future period is vital for risk prevention. Within the prediction period, pipeline failures are typically modeled as a Poisson process. Nonetheless, the scarcity and poor quality of historical failure data necessitate homogeneous grouping to estimate average failure rates. A key challenge in this process is determining how to select appropriate features for grouping, as it directly affects prediction accuracy. This study proposes a data-driven framework integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping to improve failure probability prediction. First, failure observation samples for a specific time period are generated based on the pipeline’s failure records. A layered feature selection strategy combining filter and wrapper methods is designed to balance selection efficiency with model performance. Filter methods are used to identify candidate feature subsets based on correlation with failure rates. These subsets are then used for grouping, resulting in multiple failure probability labeled datasets. For each, prediction models are developed using Artificial Neural Network and Support Vector Regression. The optimal feature subset and corresponding model are determined by comparing predictive performance. The framework’s effectiveness is validated using a case study of water supply pipelines in the central area of Shanghai, China.

title: A Bayesian uncertainty-guided transfer learning method for trustworthy fault diagnosis of rotating components

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。CNN注意力编码、贝叶斯分类和领域对齐共同实现齿轮等旋转部件跨域故障诊断。

verified_metadata.abstract: The overall reliability and safety of mission-critical equipment, such as aero-engines, largely depend on the health of their rotating parts. Therefore, trustworthy fault diagnosis is essential for achieving reliability-centered health management. Existing methods face several challenges under cross-working conditions, including computational redundancy, a high risk of negative transfer, and a lack of awareness of uncertainty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel trustworthy fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning. More specifically, first, a domain-shared feature encoder that fuses sparse self-attention and a deep CNN is designed to extract local and global features. Second, a Bayesian classifier based on variational inference is constructed and combined with Monte Carlo sampling to quantify epistemic uncertainty. Then, a domain alignment mechanism combining explicit and implicit discrepancy measures is introduced. Meanwhile, the uncertainty is mapped via an exponential decay function into adaptive weights that guide domain alignment, thereby prioritizing the transfer of high-confidence samples and suppressing unreliable ones. Finally, the experimental results on the gear dataset show that the proposed method achieved the highest accuracy rate of 99.11% in three transfer tasks. Moreover, among the correct predictions, 91.84% fall within the low-uncertainty region, while all misclassifications are flagged as high-uncertainty. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide trustworthy, uncertainty-aware diagnostics to enhance the reliability and safety of complex mechanical systems.

title: A correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework for few-shot prediction of battery remaining useful life

verified_metadata.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for quantifying battery operational safety and longevity, yet the deployment of machine learning techniques is often constrained by a widespread deficiency of high-quality labelled degradation data. To address this challenge, we propose a correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework that establishes a principled bridge between scarce RUL labels and opportunistic ageing cues. The framework employs a bilateral-branch neural network to explicitly disentangle initial manufacturing variability from in-use degradation dynamics, ensuring robust feature extraction across heterogeneous cells. By recasting a class of differential incremental capacity (ΔIC)-based descriptors as proxy labels, the method leverages their strong intra-cell and through-life correlation with RUL to transform the under-determined few-shot regression problem into a consistency-matching task. This strategy effectively constrains the model’s learning manifold, enabling the exploitation of non-ideal indicators from routine charging events while mitigating the risk of overfitting. Validated across diverse battery chemistries and cycling temperatures, the framework significantly outperforms conventional semi-supervised baselines, delivering more than a 50% improvement in prediction accuracy under extreme few-shot regimes.

title: Virtual sensing by grey-box modelling within an importance sampling Monte Carlo dynamic event tree framework for risk monitoring of small modular reactors
abstract: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) integrate advanced safety features. However, the compactness of their core design renders it difficult to position measurement devices, for operation and risk monitoring. To address this issue, we develop a Grey-Box (GB) modelling framework that ensembles White-Box (WB) physics-based and Black-Box (BB) data-driven models to enable virtual sensing of in-core safety-critical variables. The BB model is trained with condition monitoring data to perform multi-step ahead estimation of measurable variables; the estimates are fed to a physics-based WB model to estimate the non-measurable variables. The GB model developed is embedded within a risk monitoring module that builds on an Importance Sampling Monte Carlo Dynamic Event Tree (IS-MCDET) to provide the risk profile of the SMR. The method is tested on the Small Modular Dual Fluid Reactor (SMDFR), a new-generation SMR whose developed GB model for risk monitoring consists in a zero-dimensional Thermal Hydraulic (TH) WB model and a Bi-directional Long-Short Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) BB model. The developed GB model is shown to comply with the regulatory requirements and explainable response to support risk-informed decision making.

title: Development of urban fire risk index based on fire damage weighting methodologies and AI analysis of meteorological factors

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。K-means和随机森林结合十年火灾气象数据建立城市火灾风险预测，研究温湿风等灾害影响。

verified_metadata.abstract: As urban density increases, the development of reliable quantitative indicators for fire risk assessment becomes essential for disaster management. However, existing studies have tended to rely on single weighting methods without validating their suitability for predictive modeling based on meteorological conditions. This study constructed fire risk indices using three distinct methodologies: principal component analysis (PCA) for statistical objectivity, analytic hierarchy process (AHP) for expert judgment, and value of statistical life (VSL) for economic valuation. Using ten years of fire and meteorological data from Busan, risk grades were classified using K-Means clustering, and predictive models were developed via a Random Forest (RF) classifier based on four key meteorological variables (average temperature, maximum wind speed, effective humidity, and sea-level pressure). Comparative analysis revealed that the AHP and VSL models, which placed excessive weight on fatalities, showed low correlation with meteorological conditions and poor predictive performance for high-risk events (recall < 0.20). In contrast, the PCA-based index effectively captured the physical mechanisms of fire spread under low temperature, dry, and high-pressure conditions. The PCA model achieved a precision and recall of 0.99 in classifying high-risk grades. While AHP and VSL are useful for post-event impact assessment, this study demonstrated that the PCA-based index is the most scientifically valid and reliable measure for a meteorology-based predictive early warning system.

Current approaches rely on either fixed heuristic rules or random selection, resulting in unstable computational performance. To address this challenge, we introduce graph neural networks to intelligently optimize node traversal order. We construct a comprehensive dataset that maps graph structures and node orderings to computational costs, and propose a novel two-stage training framework: a cost prediction network that evaluates ordering quality, followed by a ranking generator guided by predicted costs. Experimental evaluation on industrial fault trees demonstrates that our GNN-based approach consistently identifies efficient traversal strategies, achieving 1.5–40 × speedups over conventional methods and competitive performance against established solvers. By transforming the discrete combinatorial optimization problem into a learnable task, this work provides a new perspective for optimizing topological traversal in minimal cut set analysis.

title: Energy-saving optimization of train speed Profile based on online Policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm under emergency conditions

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。在线深度强化学习融合能耗、准点、舒适和停车精度约束优化列车速度轨迹。

verified_metadata.abstract: In the domain of energy-efficient train-speed-profile optimization, off-policy reinforcement-learning (RL) algorithms and their variants have long dominated the academic landscape. Such approaches typically rely on an experience-replay buffer to reuse historical samples, yet they suffer from low training efficiency, poor numerical stability, and insufficient real-time responsiveness—limitations that become critical in complex metro systems or under emergency conditions. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an on-policy RL framework termed the Energy-Saving Maximization Advantage Distribution (ES-MAD) algorithm. ES-MAD abandons the replay buffer and instead employs dual policy networks (new vs. old): data collected by the newly explored policy are immediately leveraged to update the old policy, thereby markedly improving sample efficiency. In addition, a normalized-and-scaled advantage function is introduced to reduce variance, which significantly enhances model stability in highly dynamic or emergency scenarios. Finally, a multi-objective, self-adaptive reward mechanism is designed that seamlessly integrates energy efficiency, punctuality, ride comfort, and stopping accuracy; this reward structure requires no re-tuning when the system switches between normal and emergency operating modes. Experimental validation on the Yizhuang metro line demonstrates that ES-MAD exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability under regular service, sudden schedule changes, and multi-interval comprehensive tests. Compared with state-of-the-art off-policy deep RL baselines, ES-MAD achieves 24 % and 26 % additional energy-saving under normal and emergency conditions, respectively.

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。批量主动学习识别工程模型有效性边界，在电机温度模型中验证低数据量的可靠校验。

verified_metadata.abstract: In engineering, quantifying the deviation between model prediction and reality is crucial, particularly when simulation or empirical models are used in safety-critical applications or for product release. Model validation aims to quantify this discrepancy by comparing model predictions to experimental results. However, conducting physical experiments for validation is often costly and time-consuming. Active learning strategies can mitigate this problem by reducing the data needed to assess model accuracy. In practice, these strategies must account for experimental uncertainties, such as material variability. This work proposes an active learning framework for model validation focused on efficiently identifying the limit state between valid and invalid model regions under such conditions. Therefore, we introduce a decision-theoretical basis from which we derive two novel misclassification-based acquisition functions for mean-based and quantile-based validation. Furthermore, the framework is extended to the batch setting, allowing multiple points to be proposed for evaluation while considering nonlinear constraints of the input space. The proposed method is compared to alternative approaches for several analytical and engineering problems. Finally, the validation of a temperature model for an electric motor demonstrates the efficiency of the method in a complex scenario.

title: A k-GNN Wiener process interactive RUL prognosis method for stochastic degrading devices monitored by related multiple sensors

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。高阶图神经网络与Wiener过程联合学习多传感器设备健康指标，在发动机和实际磨机数据验证寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for making proactive decisions regarding the health management activities of degrading devices, thereby effectively ensuring safe, reliable, and economic operations. For degrading devices monitored by multiple sensors, hybrid prognosis methods combining statistical-model-based and deep-learning-based approaches, have become popular in the field of prognostics and health management. However, existing studies based on open-loop model architectures, tend to overlook the correlations and complementary relationships among multiple sensors, leading to a reduction in prediction accuracy. Therefore, this paper presents a novel data-model integrative prognosis framework incorporating high-order graph neural networks (GNNs) and Wiener process (WP). Specifically, a k-order GNN (k-GNN) capturing the high-order interaction information among different sensors is utilized to construct a composite health index (CHI). Subsequently, the time-varying stochastics within the CHI is depicted through a WP. By joint learning parameters of the k-GNN with those of the WP, a closed-loop framework is established to improve the matching degree between the constructed CHI and the WP-based degradation models. Both experimental results on simulated datasets including C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS and real-world case study results on milling cutter dataset demonstrate that the proposed k-GNN-WP model achieves a substantial improvement in RUL prediction accuracy.

title: Towards AI-Driven smart maintenance of computed tomography equipment: From health indicator design to transferable remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。双向LSTM与迁移学习从真实CT机X射线管灯丝数据估计退化路径及设备剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Failures of Computed Tomography (CT) equipment can disrupt hospital operations and compromise patient safety. However, research on Predictive Maintenance (PdM) for such systems remains limited. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) provides a practical foundation by enabling real-time acquisition of high-dimensional operational data. This study proposes a deep learning framework for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of CT equipment. First, a physics-guided Health Indicator (HI) is defined as the deviation between the observed current and the predicted nominal current of the X-ray tube filament. Second, a CT-specific degradation path identification module that combines operational state filtering with adaptive signal fusion to extract smooth, physically consistent trends is proposed. Third, a bidirectional LSTM sequence-to-sequence model, combined with cross-equipment transfer learning and uncertainty quantification, is developed for RUL prediction under heterogeneous work states and across different equipment. The framework is validated on real-world IoMT-collected X-ray tube filament datasets from multiple hospitals and CT equipment. The proposed framework achieves prediction errors of 0.3, 3.0, and 2.3 days with error rates of 0.23%, 2.33%, and 1.78%, respectively, outperforming classic and recent strong baselines in temporal alignment and generalization. These results demonstrate the potential of IoMT-enabled PdM to support maintenance decision-making, clinical workflow optimization, and downtime minimization.

title: EPAL: An exponential-penalty based active-learning function for adaptive Kriging models in structural reliability analysis

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。主动学习指数惩罚准则自适应细化Kriging极限状态模型，估计结构失效概率。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of structural failure probability in engineering systems is frequently limited by the high computational cost of evaluating complex performance functions. This paper introduces an exponential-penalty based active-learning (EPAL) function for adaptive refinement of Kriging models in reliability analysis. The EPAL formulation integrates the Kriging predictive variance with a normalized distance measure relative to the predicted limit-state surface through an exponential decay term. This functional form dynamically suppresses the selection of new samples in regions of low predictive uncertainty or those far from the failure boundary. The inherent resistance to sample clustering ensures a balanced sampling strategy that simultaneously explores regions of high uncertainty and refines the vicinity of the failure boundary. A key feature of this design is that the EPAL function is mathematically simple, parameter-free, and continuously differentiable. By removing the need for empirical tuning parameters or auxiliary distance thresholds, the method reduces subjective bias and computational redundancy. Numerical results from multiple benchmark problems confirm that the proposed method provides accurate failure probability with high computational efficiency. Its effective performance in both engineering applications and problems with small failure events further demonstrates its suitability for reliability analysis involving expensive simulations.

verified_metadata.abstract: Reliability assessment of offshore structures subjected to nonlinear hydrodynamic-structural interactions requires uncertainty propagation that is statistically consistent with the full response space. However, fully coupled finite-element (FE) simulations are too computationally expensive for Monte Carlo (MC) analysis, limiting their applicability in nonlinear structural reliability. This study develops a data-efficient structural reliability methodology that integrates nonlinear FE simulations, a firefly-optimized deep neural network (FA-DNN) surrogate model, and MC uncertainty propagation into a unified framework. The methodological innovation lies in the FA-DNN model, where a multi-objective firefly optimization strategy adaptively tunes hyperparameters to improve learning stability, prevent overfitting under limited FE data, and accurately reproduce nonlinear response behavior required for reliability evaluation. Trained on a small FE-generated dataset, the FA-DNN achieves R² values above 0.996 and reduces prediction errors by over 90% compared with ANN and baseline DNN models, enabling fast and statistically consistent MC-based estimation of failure probability. Application to a deepwater riser system in hang-off evacuation serves as a verification example, demonstrating that the methodology yields reliability-informed operational limits with negligible computational cost. The framework is general and transferable, offering an efficient surrogate-enhanced pathway for nonlinear reliability assessment of offshore and other complex structures under stochastic loading.

verified_metadata.abstract: Wheel profile prediction is critical to the maintenance of high-speed electric multiple units. This study proposes a geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network for high-accuracy prediction of worn wheel profiles. A vehicle–track dynamic simulation model is further employed to determine whether predicted worn profiles exceed the limit and to estimate the time-dependent reliability associated with profile degradation. The proposed approach is evaluated via quantitative and qualitative comparisons with a conventional wheelset wear prediction method. Results indicate that the geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network improves wheel wear prediction accuracy. In addition, the simulation-based prediction is more conservative, and the wear range observed in service is wider than that obtained from simulation. Wear patterns of wheels within the same wheelset also show strong correlations. Moreover, wheel diameter affects wear behaviour, including the wear degradation rate, equivalent conicity, the vehicle critical speed, and the Sperling index. Hence, Maintenance scheduling should therefore account for wheel diameter effects to ensure robust performance and durability.

verified_metadata.abstract: Pesticide transport and transformation in soil pose potential threats to ecological environments and human health, while traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit high computational costs and difficulty in accurately quantifying prediction uncertainty. A Bayesian deep learning framework is developed for pesticide transport modeling, integrating uncertainty quantification, interpretability analysis, and risk assessment. Surrogate models including deterministic, MC Dropout, and Deep Ensemble architectures are constructed based on 447,300 COMSOL simulation data points. The Deep Ensemble model achieves the optimal balance between prediction accuracy (R2>0.96) and uncertainty quantification, with calibration errors of 0.0350–0.0467. SHAP analysis reveals the dominant role of second-layer soil hydraulic parameters, which simultaneously constitute the primary sources of model uncertainty. Spatiotemporal uncertainty analysis shows that the mean prediction uncertainty decreases from 0.21 to 0.05 within 14 days and remains stable at 0.04–0.08 over the full 365-day period.The risk assessment framework reveals that contamination risk escalates from a mean probability of 0.476 (t=2 days) to 0.837 (t=28 days) with 72.1% of the domain classified as very high risk, and the early warning system indicates that the alert and emergency thresholds are triggered at 2.0 and 4.0 days, respectively. Climate change impacts are quantified through 10 scenario analyses: warming reduces the near-surface mean concentration by 18.8% via the Q10 effect, while precipitation changes affect transport through the source concentration (c0) and infiltration forcing (Hp0) pathways, with the c0 pathway dominating most exposure metrics. Under extreme drought conditions, the high-concentration area of aldicarb sulfoxide reaches 20.0–57.2%, far exceeding baseline levels. The framework provides a comprehensive approach to uncertainty-aware pesticide transport prediction, with future extensions needed for three-dimensional heterogeneous systems and multi-pesticide synergistic effects.

verified_metadata.abstract: This article primarily focuses on tackling the challenge of adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for singular Markovian jump systems under actuator attacks The singular Markovian jump system exhibits adaptive uncertain parameters and inaccessible states. Furthermore, due to vulnerable control signals during transmission, the actuator may receive compromised commands from malicious attacks. To mitigate the effects stemming from actuator attacks, neural network (NN)-based strategy is employed to approximate and evaluate the fraudulent information introduced by adversaries. Subsequently, the online estimation of uncertain system parameters is conducted by leveraging the derived adaptive law. Meanwhile, a newly designed sliding mode observer is integrated into the system to evaluate the unobservable states, thereby significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of system state monitoring. An innovative adaptive neural sliding mode control strategy is presented, which is designed to ensure that both the estimated states and their corresponding errors are capable of converging to the sliding manifolds. Simultaneously, this strategy guarantees the stochastic admissibility of the uncertain singular Markovian jump systems. Ultimately, the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method are demonstrated through empirical research on the direct-current (DC) motor and the Quarter-Car active suspension (QCAS) model.

verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid restoration of bridge networks following earthquake events is crucial to ensuring transportation continuity, reducing economic disruption, and supporting emergency response. This study proposes a novel graph-based deep reinforcement learning framework (GNN-DRL) that synergistically integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and a Top-k action filtering mechanism, to enable adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network repair scheduling under resource constraints. The proposed approach captures network topology and dynamic bridge states to prioritize sequential bridge repair decisions across a restoration planning horizon. The GNN-DRL decision policy is evaluated on several case-study bridge networks with varying sizes and is compared to other restoration policies including ranking-based, mixed-integer linear programming, and DRL-only policies. Sensitivity analyses are carried out to examine the effect of the Top-k filtering mechanism on balancing bridges network resilience and computational complexity, for practical real-time deployment. Results show that the proposed GNN-DRL policy consistently achieves faster and more effective restoration as well as higher final functionality throughout the planning horizon, demonstrating the potential of AI-guided infrastructure restoration to enhance disaster resilience in complex transportation systems. The framework offers a practical balance of resilience, scalability, and computational efficiency suitable for rapid post-earthquake restoration decision support.

verified_metadata.abstract: During the full life cycle of engineering products, structural performance inevitably degrades over time and is affected by uncertainties. Time-variant reliability analysis (TRA) plays a crucial role in ensuring safety and evaluating service life. However, accurately characterizing the time-variant failure probability within limited computational resources remains a challenging task. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel method termed parallel time-variant stepwise error reduction (PTSER) for efficient TRA within the single-loop Gaussian process framework. The core lies in constructing a look-ahead learning function to explicitly account for the impact of current sampling decisions on the future model accuracy. Subsequently, parallel sampling is achieved by combining probability-weighted importance and correlation-based diversity control. In addition, to accelerate the training process, a pruning mechanism is introduced to construct a truncated objective integration set and a compact candidate pool, thereby reducing computational complex while preserving reliability-critical information. Meanwhile, a hybrid stopping criterion combining uncertainty reduction and estimate stabilization is developed. The performance of the proposed method is illustrated on several examples. Experiment results show that the proposed method can obtain more accurate failure probability estimates with higher efficiency.

verified_metadata.abstract: Reliability analysis faces the challenge of accurately estimating failure probabilities while minimizing the number of time-consuming model evaluations. Surrogate models can significantly alleviate the computational burden. However, the increasing dimensionality of modern engineering systems poses substantial challenges to the performance of traditional surrogate models. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel cross-domain paradigm for high-dimensional reliability analysis, where the dimensionality of random variables is conceptually mapped to the sequence length in natural language processing (NLP). Building on this mapping, a Reliability Analysis Transformer (RAT) is designed to capture complex dependencies between random variables and system responses. Furthermore, based on the principle that similar samples contribute less new information, an attention-based sampling strategy is proposed to measure sample similarity and iteratively select the least similar samples to existing ones from the candidate dataset, thereby improving the accuracy of the RAT. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through four high-dimensional numerical examples and a liquid rocket engine case study. Results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and efficiency in handling high-dimensional and large-scale engineering problems.

verified_metadata.abstract: System-level fault localization remains a critical challenge in vehicle powertrain health management, hindered by complex fault propagation, data scarcity, and the "one/multiple-phenomenon, one/multiple-cause" problem. While data-driven methods excel at component-level diagnosis, their reliance on large annotated datasets and inability to model system topology limit their effectiveness for system-level applications. This paper proposes SPKL-RL, a likelihood-driven reinforcement learning framework that synergizes supervised pre-training with knowledge graph embedding to address these limitations. The framework formulates fault localization as a likelihood optimization within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP). A supervised pre-training module provides a warm-start policy using historical data, mitigating RL's cold-start issue. A knowledge graph embedding module encodes system topology and fault propagation into interpretable vectors. A likelihood-driven mechanism then guides exploration by integrating information gain and knowledge consistency into the reward function. Experimental results on a real powertrain dataset show SPKL-RL achieves 89.3% diagnostic accuracy across 15 fault types, reduces average diagnostic steps from 38 to 16 (58% efficiency gain), and significantly outperforms baselines, particularly in complex cascading (86.9% accuracy) and coupled fault (80.7% accuracy) scenarios. The framework demonstrates substantial advantages in reducing data dependency, improving generalization, and enhancing interpretability for complex system diagnostics.

title: Machine learning-assisted reliability assessment of main girder deflection in suspension bridges

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。TCN-BiGRU及高斯混合利用实桥温度、车载与挠度监测预测悬索桥主梁变形分布及可靠性。

verified_metadata.abstract: This study presents a probabilistic reliability assessment method for vertical deflection in long-span suspension bridges, addressing uncertainties and multifactor coupling in deflection prediction. A hybrid model integrating temporal convolutional network (TCN), bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is developed within a unified probabilistic framework. Trained on field data from Nanxi Suspension Bridge using temperature, vehicle load, and historical deflection inputs, the model estimates both the mean and standard deviation of deflections. It achieves a 38.4%–54.4% improvement in point-prediction accuracy and a 3.5%–15.6% increase in interval coverage compared to conventional methods. An extreme-value framework combining the peaks-over-threshold method with a filtered Poisson process is used to fit a generalized Pareto distribution (GPD), with threshold selection guided by diagnostic plots and statistical tests. Convergence toward the generalized extreme value distribution (GEVD) is confirmed. Extrapolation over a 100-year service life and multi-section integration yields a full-span reliability model, identifying critical sections at 2/8l and 6/8l of the main span. The approach offers a theoretically sound and practical tool for life-cycle performance evaluation of bridges under complex environmental and loading conditions.

title: Constraint-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning with adversarial training for resilience enhancement in multi-microgrid voltage control
abstract: The multi-microgrid system faces severe challenges in maintaining voltage stability when subjected to false data injection (FDI) attacks. This paper proposes a constraint-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning (CAMARL) framework, which combines graph neural networks (GNN) to achieve topology-aware state representation, periodic adversarial training, and dynamically adjusted Lagrange multipliers to achieve constraint enforcement. Experiments on IEEE 33-bus, 57-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus systems show that CAMARL consistently achieves the lowest voltage deviation, both in normal conditions and under attack conditions, outperforming multi-agent soft actor–critic, multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient, and five other multi-agent reinforcement learning benchmarks. Under normal conditions, CAMARL maintains a 99.8% constraint satisfaction rate on the IEEE 33-bus system, the Lagrange penalty mechanism reduces 94.3% of violations compared to the unconstrained benchmark, and keeps the voltage between 0.95–1.05 p.u. Communication resilience analysis indicates that under a full denial-of-service (DoS) attack, 89.2% of constraints are satisfied, and in the worst-case combination of FDI and DoS threats, this proportion is 87.4%. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of components. Removing GNN and the global state sharing module can increase the voltage deviation by up to 433%, and the removal of any single component alone will lead to a 270% performance degradation.

title: Extrapolating optimal selective maintenance strategy in new environments: A meta-reinforcement learning approach

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。元强化学习将选择维护策略迁移到未见设备环境，并以部件及输煤系统验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Selective maintenance, a widely adopted strategy in industry and military fields, has attracted increasing attention over the past decades. It involves selecting a subset of feasible maintenance actions to maximize the success probability of subsequent missions under limited resources. Most existing studies on selective maintenance optimization assume that the system degradation process is known. In many real-world applications, however, when a system is deployed in a new environment, the environmental effects on its degradation process are typically unknown, rendering these methods ineffective. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL) approach for extrapolating optimal selective maintenance strategies from known environments to unseen ones. Within the proposed framework, a meta-agent is trained across multiple known environments to acquire generalized decision-making knowledge. When encountering a new environment, the trained meta-agent infers environmental characteristics from collected observations and adapts its strategy accordingly. Furthermore, a data augmentation method is introduced to mitigate performance loss during the initial explorations in new environments. Results from a two-component system and a coal transportation system demonstrate that the optimal selective maintenance strategies vary substantially across environments and highlight the importance of extrapolating adaptive maintenance strategies under unknown environments.

title: Data-Driven break size detection model for small modular reactors based on convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model and SHapley Additive exPlanations

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。CNN-LSTM反演小型模块化反应堆失水事故破口尺寸，SHAP识别物理诊断关键特征。

verified_metadata.abstract: During a loss of coolant accident (LOCA), timely and accurate detection of the break size is crucial for nuclear power plant safety. However, current methods rely on the personal judgment of operators, which fail to meet the requirements of both speed and accuracy in high-risk situations. In this study, a CNN-LSTM model is proposed to detect the break size of LOCA, with six optimization algorithms used to tune the model hyperparameters. The GWO-WOA optimized model achieves the lowest validation loss (0.1563) and standard deviation (0.01462), outperforming the unoptimized model. To enhance model interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was conducted. Its results align with actual accident analysis, indicating that the model effectively captured the key features of the accident and enhanced the operators' trust in the AI model. Furthermore, three SHAP-based feature selection strategies were analyzed to reduce the number of required features and improve model performance. The results show that the selection strategy based on the mean SHAP value, which reduces the test set MSE from 0.196 (original feature combination) to 0.0396, is closest to the optimal feature combination. These findings offer practical guidance for developing LOCA break size detection systems, enhancing accident response timeliness and effectiveness.

title: Zero-shot cross-domain transfer for remaining useful life prediction of aero-engines via iterative diffusion refinement

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。扩散Transformer通过后验迭代去噪零样本迁移航空发动机剩余寿命预测。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of turbofan engines is critical for effective predictive maintenance. However, conventional models often struggle to generalize when sensor data distributions shift due to variations in operating profiles, environmental conditions, or system configurations. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods alleviate this issue by exploiting unlabeled target-domain data, but they still require additional data sampling. In this paper, we present RUL-DiT, a Diffusion Transformer architecture that combines Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models with a Transformer backbone and a novel LSTM-based conditioning network to iteratively refine RUL predictions via diffusion-based posterior denoising. At each reverse-diffusion step, RUL-DiT refines a Gaussian latent posterior whose mean and schedule-defined variance progressively concentrate the RUL estimate, enabling more faithful modeling of gradual degradation processes than conventional models. Crucially, when trained on a single subset of CMAPSS and NCMAPSS, two established benchmark datasets for aircraft engine prognostics, RUL-DiT achieves strong performance relative to previously reported baselines on both datasets. Moreover, RUL-DiT enables zero-shot cross-domain transfer and achieves competitive performance across transfer tasks on several source-target pairs, without requiring any target-domain labels or fine-tuning. This source-only capability enables direct deployment on unseen subsets and engine operating conditions, substantially reducing data collection overhead for RUL prognostics.

title: Intelligent analysis of ship collision accidents via Low-Rank Adaptation-based fine-tuning of medium-scale Large Language Models
abstract: The rapid advancement of intelligent maritime accident analysis requires processing large-scale, multilingual data across wide geographic regions. However, significant challenges remain in objectively constructing Risk Influencing Factors (RIFs) and ensuring accurate information extraction with limited computational resources. To address these gaps, a framework for intelligent analysis of ship collision accidents based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning of medium-scale large language models (LLMs) with limited labeled data was proposed. A bilingual dataset comprising 503 ship collision accident reports was established, and the RIF ontology was derived using a Grounded Theory approach. Using 60 labeled samples, models with ≤ 8 B parameters were fine-tuned, achieving an F1 score of 94.11% on the most challenging accident RIF extraction subtask, surpassing base models by 34.82%. Then, the extracted information was transformed into a 1061-row ×24-column training data matrix via a semantic similarity model, enabling construction of a TAN-BN model. Finally, sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify key RIFs, and case studies were performed to evaluate model performance and validate the proposed framework. The research results showed that the proposed approach advances large-scale, cross-lingual intelligent maritime accident report analysis by improving accuracy and efficiency, reducing computational costs, and supporting reliable safety management decisions.

title: A machine learning-enhanced real-time reliability assessment framework for maritime autonomous surface ships propulsion systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。Transformer和BiGRU诊断自主船推进部件故障，并更新动态贝叶斯网络评估真实推进系统可靠性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Driven by industry-wide digitalization and the pursuit of autonomy, maritime autonomous surface ships (MASS) are transitioning from conceptual design to real-world operation, emerging as a vital future maritime transportation. Among the challenges confronting MASS, the reliability of propulsion systems stands out as a paramount concern due to its direct impact on safety and mission continuity. This study proposes a real-time reliability assessment framework for MASS propulsion systems based on a diagnosis-informed dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN). The framework integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Transformer, and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) models to diagnose faults and update the DBN with real-time evidence, allowing dynamic and adaptive reliability assessment. This approach incorporates real-time fault diagnosis at the component level to refine system-level reliability predictions. The feasibility of the approach was validated using a case study on a diesel-electric hybrid propulsion system using failure rate data and operational data from simulated fault scenarios. The results indicated that the reliability of related subsystems declined significantly, and the hybrid propulsion system dropped to 0.986 on Day 30, after the navigation mission was completed. This framework introduces a causal inference mechanism that bridges the gap between component-level diagnostics and overall reliability assessment, providing a promising approach for intelligent health monitoring and proactive maintenance planning in MASS operations. The results can provide valuable support for decision-making in scheduling, degradation management, and maintenance planning for the MASS propulsion system with actual operation data.

title: Maritime accident severity modeling with operationally realistic multi-factor data-driven bayesian networks
abstract: • Trains and benchmarks TAN, ANB, and expert BNs for severity forecasting • Integrates two-layer geography: named sea regions plus operating locale • Uses multi-state met ocean factors: visibility, wind, sea state, storms, ice • Adds PSC inspection outcomes as a compliance signal in severity modelling • Provides scenario, sensitivity, SoI, and TRI analyses for actionable levers Maritime accident severity analysis supports safety management and emergency preparedness, yet operational realism remains limited in many quantitative models. Common limitations include coarse geographic representation, reduced-granularity met-ocean descriptors, and the omission of Port State Control (PSC) compliance signals. These constraints can mask actionable thresholds and hinder the identification of interpretable, decision-relevant severity pathways. To address this, the study develops Bayesian Network (BN) models to forecast accident severity using a globally distributed, multi-year (2015-2024) dataset of 1050 reports, with granular descriptors of route/region, operating locale, weather, sea-state, visibility, ship profile, human error, and accident type. It assembles a harmonized severity dataset unifying investigation narratives, PSC outcomes, ship registries, and met-ocean validation within a single standardized schema; embeds two-layer geography, multi-state environmental conditions, and compliance signals into one BN severity framework; and benchmarks three BN families, Tree-Augmented Naïve (TAN), Augmented Naïve Bayes (ANB), and a literature/expert topology, on the same dataset. Beyond structure comparison, a unified inference workflow combines Strength-of-Influence, state-wise tornado decomposition, True Risk Influence (TRI), and sequential and simultaneous scenario analysis. All three models were estimated via Expectation–Maximization (EM) and evaluated using stratified 10-fold ROC/AUC. The literature/expert BN achieved the strongest cross-validated discrimination across severity states and was selected for analysis, indicating that structure should be selected empirically rather than assumed a priori. Diagnostic, scenario, and sensitivity analysis show that severity escalates when open-sea operations on dense traffic corridors coincide with adverse environment (storm, poor visibility, rough sea, high winds), human error, and loss-of-control typologies (grounding/capsizing); severity attenuates under benign conditions and contact-type events. Strength-of-Influence results highlight the central roles of route/region→traffic density and weather/visibility→severity pathways. A targeted TRI assessment isolates Accident Type as the dominant lever shifting probability mass into the high-severity state. The findings enable consequence-aware routing and vessel traffic prioritization, type-conditioned emergency preparedness, and human-factor/equipment readiness.

title: Real-time crash risk level prediction of freeways based on a hybrid spatiotemporal deep learning framework with channel redistribution

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。CNN-Transformer从高精度车辆轨迹学习时空交互，实时预测高速公路碰撞风险。

verified_metadata.abstract: The accurate prediction of crash risk from massive traffic data has become a critical challenge for enhancing road safety. To improve real-time crash risk prediction capabilities, a novel hybrid deep learning framework combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformers, and STar Aggregate-Redistribute (STAR) Module is proposed (i.e., CNN-Transformer-STAR). Using high-resolution vehicle trajectory data from the NGSIM dataset, the model extracts complex spatiotemporal interaction features to classify the crash risks into three categories: low level, medium level, and high level. Specifically, the CNN branch is employed to capture local spatiotemporal dynamics and cross-feature coupling relationships, while the Transformer models global temporal and spatial dependencies. Additionally, the STAR module implements a centralized scheme to extract a global latent representation, which is then redistributed across feature channels to optimize inter-channel interactions. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a superior AUC of 0.90, outperforming baselines. The transferability of the predictive framework is validated using an external dataset, which shows a good robustness (AUC = 0.86) in different freeway scenarios. The results provide policy guidance for freeway traffic safety management.

title: Hierarchical domain-physical topology enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network for remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。物理拓扑图网络与贝叶斯不确定性模块预测航空发动机退化寿命，在C-MAPSS验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate and reliable Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is paramount for ensuring the operational reliability and safety of complex industrial systems. However, existing deep learning paradigms often fail to incorporate explicit structural biases derived from physical dependencies, neglecting inherent physical mechanisms and failing to provide rigorous uncertainty quantification. To surmount these challenges, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology Enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network (HDPT-FC-STGNN). First, to bridge the heterogeneity between symbolic domain knowledge and continuous sensor streams, a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology (HDPT) is constructed leveraging high-dimensional semantic embeddings. A hierarchical message-passing mechanism is subsequently devised to explicitly encode topological dependencies, thereby fusing static physical priors with dynamic sensor streams. Second, to mitigate spurious correlations in noise-intensive environments, a Structure-Aware Probabilistic Graph Sampling strategy is introduced. By selectively injecting stochasticity into unreliable data-driven edges, this mechanism treats the graph topology as a latent variable, bolstering the model robustness against epistemic ambiguity. Finally, a Bayesian uncertainty quantification module, governed by a risk-sensitive hybrid loss function, is implemented to yield high-fidelity RUL estimates alongside well-calibrated confidence intervals. Extensive experiments on the C-MAPSS benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both deterministic precision and probabilistic reliability, notably reducing the RMSE by approximately 6.9% on the FD001 subset while ensuring high probabilistic reliability.
