verified_metadata.title: AI and spectroscopy synergy: Revolutionizing fungal infection detection in fresh fruits for enhanced quality control
verified_metadata.abstract: Fungal infection in fresh fruits (FIFF) causes quality and quantity loss, posing potential health risks and economic loss, respectively. Since it occurs asymptomatically in postharvest stages, its detection, quantification, and monitoring cause mistaken-prone and time-consuming visual observation and manual handling. Recent advancements in computer vision (ComV) technologies, alongside non-destructive imaging and non-imaging spectroscopic technologies, have enabled the real-time investigation of disease detection in fruits. Therefore, the synergistic integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with spectroscopic techniques is revolutionizing the quantification, characterization and detection of FIFF by rapid, non-destructive and data driven analysis. Thus, this article particularly synthesizes the recent applications of advanced spectroscopic techniques, ComV, and AI-driven (machine learning, deep learning) approaches for quantification of FIFF. Additionally, highlights how imaging and AI-driven techniques depict the strong potential for real-time detection and severity estimation of fungal contamination. These offer solutions to the limitations of traditional methods, which are often prone to error, destructive, and labor-intensive. Future research is expected to focus on integrating techniques with optimized algorithms and implementing them within assembly lines for enhanced commercial value.

verified_metadata.title: Intelligent terahertz data analysis in agriculture: A systematic review of AI-driven approaches
verified_metadata.abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology, renowned for its unique molecular fingerprint recognition ability and penetration properties, holds revolutionary potential in agricultural field. However, THz data analysis faces significant challenges, including high-dimensional datasets and complex feature extraction. Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms have emerged as transformative tools to overcome these limitations. Unlike previous reviews on THz technology or chemometric methods in agriculture, this work systematically reviews AI-driven THz data analysis across six core agricultural domains: foreign object detection, transgenic crop recognition, variety identification, quality evaluation, component analysis, and detection of hazardous substances/pesticide residues. This review analysis reveals that AI-enhanced frameworks consistently surpass conventional methods. In optimized scenarios, deep learning-enhanced models have demonstrated accuracy levels as high as 95%-100%, marking a 12%-25% improvement over chemometric approaches. Crucially, this work highlights the AI-THz paradigm that bridges lab-grade precision with scalable farm monitoring. It provides a strategic roadmap for sustainable farming, filling a critical Agri-Tech literature gap.

verified_metadata.title: Assessing microplastic impacts on insect behaviour through artificial intelligence tools
verified_metadata.abstract: Behavioral analysis is pivotal for understanding insect ecological functions and stress responses. Recently, microplastics have emerged as widespread contaminants capable of inducing biologically significant behavioral alterations, even at sub-lethal levels. However, detecting these fine-scale effects remains challenging for conventional ecotoxicological methods that rely on coarse endpoints like mortality. This review synthesizes current knowledge on microplastic impacts and critiques traditional assessment limitations. Furthermore, we highlight how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping behavioral ecotoxicology through advanced bioimage analysis, including machine vision tracking and deep-learning pose estimation (e.g., DeepLabCut, SLEAP). These computational approaches function as digital biosensing tools, facilitating the ultrasensitive detection of subtle changes in movement dynamics. By integrating AI, researchers can achieve higher sensitivity and throughput, strengthening behavioral endpoints within the One Health framework. Finally, we outline future directions for applying AI to quantify microplastic-induced behavioral effects in insects.

verified_metadata.title: Application of artificial intelligence in unveiling the adsorption of organic pollutants by microplastics in aquatic environments: Status, challenges, and perspectives
verified_metadata.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and organic pollutants (OPs) commonly coexist in the environment. In aquatic environments, the adsorption of OPs onto MPs can increase the ecological risks associated with MP pollution. The multifaceted interactions between MPs and OPs are complex, making traditional manual analysis both time-consuming and labor-intensive. The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) offers powerful tools to address these challenges by rapidly processing large datasets and uncovering hidden patterns. This review focused on the transformative role of AI in advancing our understanding of MPs adsorbing OPs. We outlined the key stages in AI model development—including data collection, preprocessing, algorithm selection, and model evaluation—with the aim of improving insights into MPs–OPs interactions. Furthermore, we critically evaluated recent research progress, assessed the capacity of AI methods to unravel complex adsorption mechanisms and influencing factors, and discussed prevailing challenges. Finally, we proposed directions for future research to overcome these limitations.

verified_metadata.title: Integration of sustainable nanotechnology with artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) for environmental applications
verified_metadata.abstract: The technological progress over the time has enabled the convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet-of-Things (IoT) with nanotechnology, making a paradigm shift in the realm of sensing and catalytic management of hazardous substances such as water contaminants, airborne particulates, and soil-based toxins. In contrast to conventional laboratory-centric analytical approaches with a resource-intensive and time-consuming nature, it is significant to develop advanced monitoring systems for real-time detection and predictive capabilities. This review explores green nanomaterials-based modern sensors and catalysts for the detection and management of hazardous substances in different environments, i.e., water, air, and soil, along with fuel generation. Life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches are significant for evaluating and guiding the development of green nanomaterials. The integration of sustainable nano-enabled sensors and catalysts with artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) systems is also deliberated. The convergence of these technologies can help in overcoming the complexities in the detection and management of pollutants occurring due to the dynamic nature of the environment. This study seeks to empower humans, stakeholders, and pollution monitoring industries through rapid sensing and predictive analysis on the basis of sensor-generated informatics using AIoT. The analysis of AIoT informatics can help in the possible risk assessment of pollutants and optimization of necessary safety measures. Finally, the real-world limitations of sustainable nanotechnology-enabled AIoT systems are discussed with significant emphasis on associated challenges and potential progress.

title: Accelerating plastic particle morphology analysis: Comparing manual, semi-automated, and machine learning-based image analysis methods
abstract: Determining plastic particle metrics, such as diameter and surface area, from soils and compost is crucial for assessing their behavior and potential impacts in terrestrial environments, yet it remains challenging due to the lack of standardized methods and the labor-intensive nature of manual image analysis. This study compares three image analysis approaches for particle characterization: manual segmentation in ImageJ, semi-automated analysis with the pliman package in R, and a machine-learning–based workflow using the trainable Weka segmentation plugin in ImageJ. A total of 926 plastic particles, extracted from organic fertilizers and ranging in Feret diameter from 0.23 to 13.9 cm, were analyzed. Manual processing required over 46 hours, whereas the Weka method took approximately 2-3 h, and the pliman method was fastest, completing batch processing of all images in approximately 20 minutes, with an additional 1 hour for manual verification. However, it correctly segmented only 42 % of the particles. The Weka approach performed better, achieving 64 % segmentation accuracy, though it required thorough model training. Both automated approaches correlated strongly with the manual results (R > 0.9, p < 0.001). On average, Weka slightly underestimated particle diameter (-2.1 %) and overestimated area (+2.3 %), while pliman overestimated area more substantially (+12.8 %). This comparative assessment highlights the potential of machine-learning approaches to accelerate plastic analysis workflows while maintaining accuracy. The study supports the development of reproducible, automated pipelines by offering practical recommendations for imaging plastic particles, an open-source Weka workflow, and a model trained to characterize particles commonly found in organic fertilizers and, thus, in soils.

title: Evolution and impact of Smart Analytical Chemistry in non-destructive spectroscopy for food applications
abstract: This review critically explores the transformative evolution of Smart Analytical Chemistry (SAC) and its profound impact on the field of non-destructive spectroscopy for food analysis and safety. SAC represents a paradigm shift that integrates green, sustainable, and white analytical chemistry principles with intelligent technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), automation, and miniaturized sensing platforms. This fusion enables the development of highly efficient, portable, eco-friendly, and real-time analytical systems tailored for complex food matrices. The review systematically examines the advancements in spectroscopy-based techniques, including near-infrared (NIR), mid-infrared (MIR), Raman, UV-Vis, fluorescence, and hyperspectral imaging and their smart adaptation for detecting contaminants, assessing authenticity, monitoring nutritional profiles, and ensuring food integrity without sample destruction. By highlighting the synergistic interplay between sustainability goals and technological innovation, this review offers a forward-looking perspective on how SAC is reshaping the landscape of modern food safety, traceability, and quality assurance.

verified_metadata.title: Empowering Traditional Chinese Medicine with artificial intelligence: Innovations in quality control, therapeutic applications, and industrialization
verified_metadata.abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) faces critical bottlenecks in quality control and efficacy validation due to its complex matrices and subjective traditional evaluation methods. By benchmarking 116 high-impact studies (2010–2025), this review highlights a strategic transition from shallow-learning pattern recognition to cognitive knowledge reasoning, facilitated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and Explainable AI (XAI). Although deep learning architectures achieve superior accuracies (up to 100%) across modalities like HPLC and SERS, cognitive intelligence remains essential for decoding TCM's non-linear pharmacological networks. Synthesizing “medicine-food homology” with multi-modal data fusion, we elucidate a paradigm shift from empirical practices to mechanism-interpretable precision therapies. Ultimately, this work provides a technical roadmap for AIoT-driven quality-by-design, offering a systematic blueprint to harmonize international standards and accelerate the global integration of the TCM industry.

verified_metadata.title: From passive chips to intelligent platforms: AI-enabled design, control, and signal decoding in microfluidic and paper-based analytical devices
verified_metadata.abstract: Microfluidic technologies and paper-based analytical devices are increasingly expected to deliver laboratory-grade decisions from microliter samples, often under field conditions rather than controlled environments. This demand exposes a central bottleneck: signals are multiplexed and noisy, device-to-device variation is consequential, and manual readout cannot scale. Artificial intelligence and machine learning address these limits by linking platform design, data generation, and inference into a single development loop—the organizing principle of this review. Device architecture and materials selection are discussed alongside data-efficient optimization of channel geometry, droplet operations, and digital actuation. Scenario-specific pipelines are then synthesized for image-based readout, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy decoding, and electrochemical or impedance quantification, with emphasis placed on calibration and distribution-shift performance instead of single-cohort accuracy. Biomedical diagnostics and biological analysis are treated as demanding proving grounds, where automated readout and robustness determine whether performance translates beyond demonstration. Deployment is positioned as an upfront design requirement rather than an afterthought. Accordingly, edge-capable inference, disciplined benchmarking, dataset governance, and tamper-evident provenance are treated as practical prerequisites for translation. In combination, these elements move microdevices beyond passive hardware and toward intelligent analytical systems that deliver reproducible, decision-ready evidence.

verified_metadata.title: A vigor signal mechanism framework guided non-destructive detection of seed vigor: Integrating spectroscopy, imaging, and artificial intelligence
verified_metadata.abstract: Seed vigor serves as a critical determinant of crop establishment and yield stability, yet conventional vigor assessment methods remain destructive, time-consuming, and labor-intensive. In response, the field is undergoing a paradigm shift toward non-destructive detection (NDD) techniques, which integrate advanced spectroscopy, imaging modalities, and artificial intelligence (AI) for rapid and scalable evaluation. This review introduces the Vigor Signal Mechanism (VSM) model as a solution to the “black box” nature of AI-driven seed vigor predictions. This model elucidates how biochemical and structural deteriorations manifest as measurable spectral and imaging features. By mapping sensor responses to established vigor indicators, the VSM framework enhances the biological interpretability of AI models and guides the rational selection of sensing modalities. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances in spectroscopy/imaging technologies, including near-infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, terahertz sensing, multispectral imaging, hyperspectral imaging, machine vision, magnetic resonance imaging, X-ray radiography, and their confluence with AI-driven analytical frameworks for seed vigor prediction. We further underscore the inherent limitations of unimodal approaches and the crucial role of multimodal information in effectively augmenting model performance. By bridging seed physiology, sensing physics, and AI, this work provides a systematic theoretical and technical reference for the academic research of seed vigor non-destructive detection, and lays a foundation for the industrialization of high-throughput, mechanism-aware seed phenotyping systems.

title: Towards instant diagnostics: The role of ambient mass spectrometry devices in point-of-care clinical practice
abstract: ABSTRACT Ambient mass spectrometry (AMS) enables rapid, preparation-free molecular profiling and is increasingly impacting clinical diagnostics and point-of-care (POC) testing. Advances in soft/ambient ionization (DESI, DART, paper spray, MasSpec Pen, REIMS, PESI, and related hybrid sources) broaden analyte coverage, enabling real-time detection of metabolites, lipids, proteins, pathogens, drugs, and other biomarkers directly from tissues, biofluids, and swabs. In parallel, portable and miniaturized mass spectrometers have improved the feasibility of selected bedside, intraoperative, and field workflows, particularly for targeted screening and quantification. Machine-learning integration increasingly automates spectral interpretation for tissue classification, disease diagnosis, and therapeutic drug monitoring. However, routine clinical adoption remains constrained by standardization requirements, multicenter validation, and regulatory pathways. This review summarizes the evolution of AMS and portable MS, surveys emerging clinical applications, and outlines priorities for broader implementation. We also discuss workflow integration, quality assurance, data sharing, and training needs for non-specialist users.

title: Matrix effect resolution in artificial intelligence-driven bacteria detection
abstract: Accurate detection of bacteria in complex biological, food, and environmental matrices is essential for infection control, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance, and public health decision-making. However, matrix effects arising from heterogeneous sample compositions remain a major barrier to the reliable deployment of rapid novel detection technologies. These effects can distort analytical signals, reduce reproducibility, and complicate data interpretation, particularly outside controlled laboratory settings. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities to overcome matrix-induced variability by enabling data-driven signal correction, pattern recognition, and adaptive learning across diverse sample types. In this review, we synthesized emerging strategies from the last 5 years for matrix-effect resolution in AI-assisted bacterial detection systems, including electrochemical, optical, and spectroscopic platforms. We discuss how AI models can integrate biological variability, environmental context, and sensor heterogeneity to improve robustness, analyte discrimination, and even quantitative accuracy, with emphasis on high-risk pathogens, such as those in the ESKAPE group. The workflow for AI-assisted bacterial detection is critically analyzed, beginning with pretreatment of complex samples, processing of raw data to extract the most relevant features, and then continuing with the implementation of the algorithm.

verified_metadata.title: SERS–AI for biomedical applications: From single spectrum to multidimensional analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has emerged as an important molecular sensing platform for biomedical analysis owing to its high sensitivity, chemical specificity, and label-free detection capability. When coupled with artificial intelligence (AI), SERS enables automated spectral processing, feature extraction, and pattern recognition in complex biological systems. However, most current SERS–AI studies still rely primarily on single spectrum inputs, which provide only limited information about the biochemical heterogeneity of clinical samples and may thereby constrain model robustness, interpretability, and generalizability. This review examines the development of SERS–AI from an information dimensionality perspective and highlights its conceptual evolution from single-spectrum analysis toward multidimensional information integration. We first discuss SERS enhancement mechanisms, substrate design, and AI-assisted spectral analysis, followed by a summary of representative biomedical applications of single-spectrum SERS–AI, including cancer screening, pathogen identification, disease diagnosis, pharmaceutical analysis, and therapeutic monitoring. We then discuss the transition from information-limited analysis to high-dimensional integrated diagnosis, as well as the new challenges introduced by this shift. Particular emphasis is placed on multispectral and multimodal SERS–AI strategies. Multispectral approaches, including multi-substrate, multi-excitation wavelength, and multi-biofluid, expand information dimensionality within the SERS domain, whereas multimodal approaches integrate SERS with orthogonal information from fluorescence/infrared spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, omics, imaging, or clinical data. Furthermore, we discuss data fusion strategies, validation issues, standardization requirements, and interpretability challenges, all of which are critical for advancing the clinical translation of SERS–AI. Finally, we outline future directions for developing reliable, robust, and clinically translatable SERS–AI platforms for precision biomedical analysis.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-powered imaging of microfibers: Microscopy, vibrational and hyperspectral analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Microfibers have emerged as environmental pollutants of increasing concern because of their widespread sources, persistence, confusion with natural fibers, and ecological and health risks. Detection techniques, including microscopic imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and hyperspectral imaging, are important for microfiber identification, characterization, and analysis. However, complex environmental matrices and background interference still cause poor signal quality, low throughput, and limited adaptability. Artificial intelligence (AI), with strong nonlinear feature extraction and pattern recognition capabilities, offers a feasible solution. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-assisted microfiber detection, compares traditional machine-learning and deep-learning models, outlines relevant neural network architectures, and discusses strategies such as data augmentation, multimodal fusion, and transfer learning. We further review AI applications in microscopic imaging, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) and Raman spectroscopy, and hyperspectral imaging, focusing on identification, segmentation, counting, and polymer classification, and discuss future opportunities and challenges.

verified_metadata.title: Advances in AI-assisted odor sensing using colorimetric sensor arrays: From sensor design to high-dimensional data intelligence
verified_metadata.abstract: Odor sensing using colorimetric sensor arrays (CSAs) provides a rapid, low-cost, and non-destructive strategy for food safety and quality evaluation. However, practical deployment of conventional CSAs is constrained by limited stability, humidity tolerance, and reproducibility, while conventional chemometric methods often struggle with complex gas mixtures. Recent advances in nanomaterial-enabled sensor engineering have improved CSA performance, while spectroscopic and imaging approaches enable more information-rich and often high-dimensional readouts with complementary chemical and spatial information. AI offers flexible tools for high-dimensional data via feature learning, dimensionality reduction, and predictive modeling. This review provides an integrated synthesis of AI-assisted CSAs (CSAs-AI) across sensor engineering, high-dimensional readouts, AI-based modeling, and food-monitoring applications. Sensing mechanisms, fabrication strategies, spectroscopic techniques and advanced imaging methods are summarized, with emphasis on how deep learning improves qualitative and quantitative analysis of high-dimensional responses. Representative applications, current deployment bottlenecks, and future directions are also highlighted.

verified_metadata.title: Intelligent microdevices for aquatic monitoring: High-Performance sensing integration and AI-enabled signal decoding
verified_metadata.abstract: Water quality deterioration rarely manifests as a sudden collapse; it is more often a gradual accumulation of deviations. Changes in ion balance, trace organic matter content, or microbial dynamics are particularly difficult to detect routinely, yet they continuously create ecological stress. These signals are often too subtle for routine spot sampling or network-level surveillance, so reliable detection may occur only after regulatory or ecological thresholds have already been exceeded. Microdevice technologies are reshaping how such analytical gaps are approached. In microfluidic platforms, fluid transport, chemical reactions, and signal transduction are intrinsically co-localized, allowing rapid extraction of chemical information from minimal sample volumes with reduced latency. Microfluidic paper-based analytical devices advance this paradigm by eliminating external pumping and fixed infrastructure, relocating measurement directly to sites of concern. Integrated high-performance sensors increase both sensitivity and temporal resolution without compromising operational simplicity, even in chemically heterogeneous aquatic systems. Accordingly, microfluidic devices, paper-based platforms, and high-performance sensor hybrids are considered here as complementary—rather than competing—strategies for aquatic monitoring. Moreover, recent advances in materials science, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly expanded their analytical performance, robustness, and data interpretation capability. Device architectures, material functions, and sensing mechanisms are examined across analyte classes spanning nutrients, toxic metals, pathogens, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, emerging micropollutants, and microbial indicators. This review provides a comprehensive survey of the technologies of microdevices, their working principles, representative applications, and performance characteristics. Particular attention is given to challenges related to stability, scalability, selectivity, and real-world deployment, as well as emerging solutions. Finally, the growing role of AI in signal processing, pattern recognition, and predictive modeling is examined, and future perspectives for intelligent, autonomous water monitoring systems are proposed.

verified_metadata.title: Application of spectroscopic techniques with machine learning for high-throughput phenotyping of seed vigor: A comprehensive review
verified_metadata.abstract: Seed vigor is a crucial agronomic trait that strongly influences crop establishment, agricultural productivity, and global food security. Conventional detection methods are often destructive, time-consuming, and subjective, and they frequently fail to capture internal biochemical deterioration within seeds. This review first clarifies the major physiological and biochemical factors affecting seed vigor, including membrane integrity, reserve metabolism, oxidative damage, enzyme activity, moisture status, and embryo integrity. It then systematically summarizes advanced non-destructive technologies for seed vigor assessment, including near-infrared, Raman, terahertz, fluorescence, and photoacoustic spectroscopy, as well as hyperspectral imaging, X-ray imaging, and biospeckle laser techniques. Multi-spectral fusion strategies are also discussed, as they integrate complementary physical and chemical information to improve detection sensitivity and robustness. Methodologically, this review highlights the integration of spectral data with chemometrics, machine learning, and deep learning for qualitative classification and quantitative prediction of seed vigor. As data-driven models become increasingly complex, algorithm interpretability has become a key concern. Therefore, this review further analyzes how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods help address the “black box” problem, verify model reliability, and reveal links between spectral features and physiological mechanisms such as lipid peroxidation and protein denaturation. Overall, coupling molecular spectroscopy with interpretable intelligent algorithms can enhance detection accuracy, robustness, and generalization, providing technical support for high-throughput seed quality management and precision agriculture.

verified_metadata.abstract: Mass spectrometry (MS) is one of the most powerful tools in environmental analysis due to its excellent analytical performance. The significant applications of GenAI in sample preparation methodology and MS data process are highlighted. The opportunities and challenges for further development of GenMS are also discussed.

verified_metadata.title: AI-driven electrochemical biosensing platforms for skin cancer: Analytical advances toward intelligent theranostic and drug-delivery systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Electrochemical biosensors have emerged as powerful analytical platforms for the early detection and monitoring of skin cancer biomarkers owing to their high sensitivity, rapid response, miniaturization, and compatibility with point-of-care diagnostics. However, their clinical translation remains limited by biofouling, signal drift, interfacial instability, matrix interference, and poor long-term reproducibility. Beyond biomolecular recognition, biosensor performance is governed by interfacial electrochemistry, electron-transfer kinetics, mass transport, and signal transduction, which collectively determines signal generation, amplification, and analytical reliability. This review critically examines these physicochemical processes from a mechanistic and systems-level perspective. Emphasis is placed on clinically relevant biomarkers for melanoma and selected non-melanoma skin cancers, including proteins, nucleic acids, extracellular vesicles, and metabolic markers, together with challenges arising from biomarker heterogeneity, low abundance, and complex biological matrices. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for electrochemical data analysis is evaluated, highlighting advances in feature extraction, pattern recognition, predictive modeling, and decision support, as well as limitations related to data quality, overfitting, interpretability, and clinical generalizability. Emerging AI-assisted electrochemical theranostic systems are discussed as closed-loop platforms integrating biomarker sensing, data-driven analysis, and therapeutic actuation for personalized disease management. Finally, key barriers to clinical translation, including standardization, validation, regulatory requirements, wearable and minimally invasive sensing technologies, and skin cancer-specific therapeutic delivery, are assessed. By integrating electrochemical sensing principles, AI-driven analytics, and translational considerations, this review provides a systems-oriented framework for developing reliable, intelligent, and clinically viable electrochemical biosensing platforms for next-generation skin cancer diagnosis and theranostics.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted Raman spectroscopy in determination of ophthalmic markers
verified_metadata.abstract: Raman spectroscopy is an analytical tool for label-free detection of diagnosis-related biomarkers with high specificity and sensitivity, which can be attributed to the fact that Raman spectra serve as molecular fingerprints that are unique to each target molecule. However, high spectral complexity and low signal-to-noise ratios pose challenges in data interpretation for Raman spectroscopy. To overcome these challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) has been employed to facilitate Raman spectroscopy by unlocking complex information from spectral data. A typical application scenario of AI-assisted Raman spectroscopy is ophthalmic diagnosis, in which non-invasive, real-time monitoring is of great significance. This review explores recent advances, focusing primarily on literature published between 1982 and 2026, in the integration of AI algorithms and Raman spectroscopy for the diagnosis of ophthalmic diseases. First, AI algorithms (e.g., dimensionality reduction algorithms, classification algorithms) commonly used to facilitate Raman spectroscopy are briefly introduced. Then, evolution and state-of-the-art cases of Raman spectroscopy in the diagnosis of different ophthalmic diseases are addressed, including corneal disease, retinal/fundus disease, cataract, glaucoma, and dry eye disease. Additionally, limitations (e.g., safety, database unification) and outlook (e.g., diagnosis-treatment integration) of AI-assisted Raman spectroscopy are discussed. This review provides insights for applications of AI-assisted Raman spectroscopy in real-time monitoring of diagnosis-related biomarkers.

title: Convolutional neural networks in Vis–NIR chemometrics: From contradiction to conditional design
abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR and Vis–NIR) is widely used for rapid, non-destructive analysis in food, agriculture, pharmaceutical, process analytical technology (PAT), and bioprocess-monitoring applications. Yet, deep-learning studies in NIR chemometrics often report conflicting conclusions about convolutional neural network (CNN) design: small versus large kernels, shallow versus deep architectures, raw spectra versus preprocessing, compact models versus multi-scale networks, and random-split performance versus transfer robustness. This review argues that many of these apparent contradictions arise from incomplete conditioning rather than from inherently incompatible results. CNN performance in NIR chemometrics depends on the interaction between spectral physics, dataset regime, acquisition protocol, validation design, and deployment scenario. We therefore organize the literature around three central moderators. First, NIR signals are indirect, highly collinear, and often dominated by broad overlapping bands, scattering, temperature, and matrix effects. Second, convolutional design choices should be interpreted through receptive-field reasoning: kernel size, depth, dilation, and multi-scale branches determine which wavelength spans are available to the model, whereas the effective receptive field determines which parts of that span are actually used. Third, validation design can act as a hidden hyperparameter, because random splits may favour architectures that exploit shared batch, instrument, season, or process-run structure rather than transferable chemical information. Building on these points, we propose a conditional design framework in which preprocessing, architecture, hyperparameter tuning, transfer evaluation, interpretability, and reproducibility are treated as coupled components of the modelling pipeline. The goal is not to identify a universally optimal CNN for NIR spectra, but to move CNN–NIR chemometrics toward physics-aware, shift-aware, and reproducible model comparison.

verified_metadata.title: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and machine learning for saliva biosensing: From substrate design to clinical diagnostics
verified_metadata.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) technology significantly amplifies Raman signals through plasmonic enhancement mechanisms, providing unique molecular fingerprint spectra for biomedical analysis. As a non-invasive and biomarker-rich biofluid, saliva has emerged as a promising medium for disease diagnostics. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-assisted SERS strategies for saliva biosensing, with emphasis on substrate engineering, spectral analysis, and clinical diagnostic applications. Recent advances in SERS substrates, ranging from noble metal nanostructures to hybrid materials, as well as surface functionalization strategies for improving stability and specificity, are systematically reviewed. AI-assisted analytical approaches, especially machine learning (ML), have increasingly been integrated with SERS to improve spectral processing, feature extraction, disease classification, and predictive performance. Representative analytical methods, including principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares (PLS), linear discriminant analysis (LDA), support vector machine (SVM), and deep learning (DL), are highlighted within standardized spectral analysis workflows. The synergy between SERS and ML has demonstrated exceptional performance in the diagnosis of cancers, oral and infectious diseases, pathogen identification, and illicit drug detection using salivary biomarkers. While challenges persist in substrate reproducibility, spectral standardization, and model generalization, future development of cost-effective materials, standardized databases, and interpretable algorithms positions SERS-ML systems as promising high-throughput tools for clinical diagnostics and point-of-care testing.

verified_metadata.title: AI-driven nanostructured aptasensor engineering: Integrating biosensing, intelligent nanomedicine, and programmable therapeutics
verified_metadata.abstract: The convergence of AI, nanotechnology, and aptamer engineering is transforming the landscape of precision biosensing and responsive therapeutics. Despite the vast theoretical diversity of oligonucleotide libraries (∼1015 variants), conventional SELEX remains constrained by experimental limitations, amplification bias, and incomplete resolution of sequence-structure-function relationships, often necessitating iterative enrichment cycles. Recent advances integrating high-throughput sequencing with machine learning have transformed aptamer discovery into a predictive, data-driven paradigm, enabling the early identification of high-affinity candidates, motif extraction, and in silico affinity optimization. Simultaneously, innovations in nanostructured platforms and surface engineering have enhanced aptamer functionality through controlled orientation, density, and stimuli-responsive interfaces, thereby facilitating ultrasensitive detection and efficient signal transduction. Beyond conventional biosensing, these developments are driving a paradigm shift toward intelligent nanomedicine. AI-driven design frameworks now enable multivariate optimization of aptamer-nanoconstruct systems, improving target specificity, pharmacokinetics, and therapeutic payload delivery. In cancer applications, aptamer-functionalized nanoplatforms enable precise tumor targeting, receptor blockade, and controlled drug release, minimizing systemic toxicity while enhancing therapeutic efficacy. Emerging DNA nanostructures further integrate molecular recognition with logic-gated activation, allowing autonomous, biomarker-triggered therapeutic responses within the tumor microenvironment. Such systems can selectively inhibit oncogenic pathways, disrupt tumor vasculature, or enhance immune-mediated clearance, representing a new generation of precision therapeutics. As a result, the integration of AI-driven selection, structural modeling, and nanoconstruct engineering is transitioning aptamer technologies from empirical tools to intelligent, adaptive systems. While challenges related to data standardization, structural resolution, and clinical translation remain, these advances establish a robust foundation for next-generation cancer diagnostics and smart therapeutics, positioning AI-guided aptamer nanoplatforms at the forefront of precision oncology.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-driven smart nanomaterials for pan-cancer diagnosis: A review of recent advances
verified_metadata.abstract: The pan-cancer screening agenda is moving past single-analyte assays toward platforms that read several molecular layers from one specimen and a single measurement. Smart nanomaterials — plasmonic colloids, quantum dots, upconversion phosphors, magnetic colloids, DNA origami, and stimuli-responsive carriers — supply the physical contact with tumour-derived analytes; modern deep-learning architectures (1-D and 2-D convolutional networks, transformers, graph neural networks, self-supervised foundation models) supply the inference engine that converts raw spectra, magnetisation curves, electrochemical traces, and image stacks into a clinical readout. We searched PubMed on 25 April 2026 with a Boolean string combining cancer, nanomaterial, and machine-learning terms; the query returned 527 indexed records between January 2018 and the search date. Eighteen study–cancer entries from 12 PMID-verified primary studies were extracted with explicit AUC values and re-analysed alongside the four established cfDNA-based multi-cancer early detection (MCED) trials [1–4]. The sample-size-weighted pooled AUC across these entries is 0.886, with per-cancer values ranging from 0.840 (lung, plasma exosome SERS) to 0.999 (thyroid, serum SERS plus ResNet (Lin and et al., 2025) [5]. Fifty-two PMID-verified references span the chemistry, the algorithmic toolkit, the pan-cancer evidence base, and the regulatory framework. The pipeline that emerges — sample → smart nanoprobe → multi-channel readout → AI decoder → pan-cancer label, with a longitudinal feedback loop — is shared across solid and haematological tumours. We discuss what is in place and what still has to be built before AI-coupled smart nanomaterials become a routine component of the cancer diagnostic stack.

title: Microfluidics for particle production in drug delivery: From physical basics to perspective applications
abstract: In recent years, micro- and nanoparticles have gained interest due to their applicability to diverse biomedical fields, especially drug delivery. Typical batch methods, including solvent evaporation or homogenization, achieve high production volumes but are often characterized by low reproducibility and high polydispersity. For this reason, microfluidics has recently emerged as a promising method for producing monodisperse, finely controlled, and highly tunable carriers. Depending on the material and device geometry, a wide range of particles can be obtained, spanning from the microscale to the nanoscale and from metallic to biomimetic systems. Microfluidics can reduce waste and costs because of the limited volumes employed, while enhancing throughput through parallelization. This review provides an overview of microfluidic technologies for particle production, ranging from the underlying physical principles, including dimensionless numbers, to market applications. Particular attention is devoted to the latest device geometries and materials, as well as to the implementation of artificial intelligence and emerging autonomous formulation strategies for reducing industrial costs and development times. The strengths, limitations, and potential improvements associated with each geometry and material are critically evaluated and compared to provide a comprehensive understanding of microfluidics for drug-delivery applications. Although substantial progress is still required for microfluidics to become a leading technology for industrial particle production, owing to limitations such as device clogging, chip-material compatibility, and the cost and standardization hurdles of large-scale GMP manufacturing, an increasing number of FDA-approved drug carriers may be produced through this innovative approach in the coming years.

verified_metadata.title: Hyperspectral imaging and machine learning for mycotoxigenic fungi and mycotoxins: surrogate detection, evidence standards and industrial deployment
verified_metadata.abstract: Mycotoxigenic fungi and their toxins remain among the most persistent threats to global grain and food safety. By uniting spectral and spatial information in a single acquisition, hyperspectral imaging (HSI) resolves both the chemical composition and the heterogeneous distribution of contamination non-destructively and at high throughput. Taking the mycotoxigenic fungus as the central object and machine learning as the connecting thread, this review examines what the measurement actually reports, how strong the supporting evidence is, and where the technique belongs industrially. We first establish the spectroscopic basis of the infection–metabolism–toxin cascade and show that, at regulatory microgram-per-kilogram levels, the toxin contributes negligibly to the spectrum: detection is surrogate, carried by infection-induced changes in protein, starch, lipid and water. A three-tier evidence scheme is introduced and applied to characteristic wavebands, crop-matrix effects, masked toxins and the still unproven separability of toxigenic and atoxigenic strains. Tracing the methodological evolution from chemometrics to convolutional networks, transfer learning and multimodal fusion, we show how pixel-level data splitting, artificially inoculated material and incomparable metrics inflate reported performance, and we set out a validation hierarchy and minimal reporting criteria. Finally, we examine the laboratory-to-industry transition and standardization needs, positioning HSI as multispectral triage and sorting upstream of confirmatory chromatography, and identify mechanism-driven modelling, shared benchmark datasets and early warning before toxin accumulation as priority directions.

verified_metadata.title: Deep learning integrated spectral technologies in monitoring food hazards: A review of next generation approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Ensuring food safety increasingly depends on analytical technologies capable of rapidly identifying chemical contaminants and biological hazards across complex and heterogeneous food systems. While spectroscopy-based approaches provide rapid and non-destructive measurements, their broader adoption is often constrained by spectral complexity, matrix interference, and the difficulty of extracting meaningful information from high-dimensional datasets. Deep learning (DL) has emerged as a key enabler for overcoming these limitations, transforming spectral signals into actionable insights through automated feature learning and data-driven pattern recognition. This review positions DL as the central driver linking spectral data acquisition, feature representation, and hazard identification within modern food safety monitoring frameworks. Major spectroscopic platforms, including near-infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and hyperspectral imaging, are discussed from the perspective of their integration with DL models. Recent applications in detecting pesticide residues, veterinary drugs, mycotoxins, heavy metals, and foodborne pathogens are critically evaluated to illustrate how intelligent spectral analysis improves sensitivity, robustness, and adaptability under practical conditions. Beyond analytical performance, emphasis is placed on challenges that increasingly govern translation to real-world deployment, including data standardization, model interpretability, transferability across food matrices, and scalable implementation. The convergence of DL and spectroscopy is redefining food hazard detection from conventional signal measurement toward intelligent sensing systems capable of supporting rapid, automated, and decision-oriented food safety management.

verified_metadata.title: Mechanistic modeling of flow-transport-reaction coupling in lateral flow assays: From capillary wicking to physics-AI hybrid design
verified_metadata.abstract: Lateral flow assay (LFA) performance is governed by the coupled processes of capillary flow, mass transport, and biochemical reactions. However, these internal processes are difficult to observe directly, making LFA design and optimization heavily dependent on empirical trial-and-error. Mechanistic modeling provides a means to describe these processes quantitatively and to relate internal transport and reaction behavior to assay performance. Despite these advances, there have been no LFA simulation-related reviews in the past five years to summarize the progress. This review therefore systematically examines mechanistic modeling in LFA, from capillary wicking to coupled flow-transport-reaction processes and emerging mechanistic modeling strategies empowered by artificial intelligence (AI). We first compare saturated and unsaturated flow models, including Lucas-Washburn, Darcy-based, Richards, and two-phase models, with emphasis on their assumptions, applicability, and limitations. We then summarize multiphysics convection-diffusion-reaction (CDR) models that couple flow, mass transport, and reaction kinetics to describe signal formation and support sensitivity enhancement, dynamic range expansion, and structural optimization. Building on these mechanistic foundations, we further discuss simulation data-driven machine learning, machine learning-assisted mechanistic modeling, and physics-informed machine learning as three strategies for improving prediction, optimization, and parameter inference. Alongside these advances, we discuss current challenges associated with model assumptions, parameter uncertainty, and experimental validation. By comparing these approaches within a unified model-selection framework, this review provides practical guidance for selecting models according to research objectives and dominant physical processes, and supports the transition of LFA development from empirical optimization toward predictive and mechanism-guided design.

verified_metadata.title: Recent advances in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) assisted by machine learning for the exploration of geochemical and environmental resources: A comprehensive review
verified_metadata.abstract: Traditional analytical techniques have key problems such as time-consuming, low accuracy, and easy destruction of samples in mineral resources development and environmental monitoring. Therefore, it is urgent to develop efficient and rapid multi-element accurate analytical techniques. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) technology offers the distinct advantages of rapid and remote detection, simultaneous multi-element determination, minimal sample preparation requirements, and strong field adaptability. Recently, the combination of LIBS and machine learning methods has shown broad application potential in geological resource exploration and environmental analysis. This paper systematically reviews the research progress and application status of LIBS technology combined with machine learning in the field of geological resource exploration and environmental analysis during the past six years. It mainly introduces LIBS equipment, sample preparation methods, spectral fusion technology, portable on-site and remote LIBS systems, machine learning methods in LIBS, and the application of LIBS combined with machine learning methods in the analysis of different geological and environmental materials during the last years. At the same time, it is pointed out that the current LIBS technology faces challenges such as matrix effect, and the future development direction of improving field applicability and analysis accuracy through multi-modal fusion and other methods is prospected.

title: Challenges and opportunities in the network medicine of complex diseases
abstract: Network medicine applies fundamental principles of complexity science and systems medicine to integrate and analyze complex structured data, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, to characterize the dynamical states of health and disease within biological networks. In this perspective, we discuss the major successes of the field and how incorporating techniques based on statistical physics and machine learning in network medicine has significantly refined our understanding of disease networks. Despite these achievements, the maturation of network medicine presents challenges that must be addressed. Limitations in defining biological units and interactions, interpreting network models, and accounting for experimental uncertainties hinder the field's progress. The next phase of network medicine must expand the current framework by incorporating more realistic assumptions about biological units and their interactions across multiple relevant scales. This expansion is crucial for advancing our understanding of complex diseases and improving strategies for their diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

title: μPharma: A microfluidic, AI-driven pharmacotyping platform for single-cell drug sensitivity prediction in leukemia
abstract: Background Pharmacotyping, the ex vivo measurement of tumor cell responses to drugs, is particularly important for cancers lacking actionable genomic markers. However, current pharmacotyping methods are not clinically feasible due to prolonged drug incubations (days to weeks), extensive manual handling, and analytical limitations, including overlooking single-cell characteristics. Addressing these hurdles is critical for pediatric T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), an aggressive cancer with limited therapeutic options. Methods We developed μPharma, a pharmacotyping platform that predicts single-cell drug sensitivity without direct drug exposure by quantifying pretreatment biomarkers associated with therapeutic response. μPharma integrates an automated digital microfluidic immunofluorescence assay, optimized for suspension cells, with machine learning models trained on comprehensive single-cell features. We validated μPharma using T-ALL cell lines and patient-derived xenografts, predicting sensitivity to dasatinib and venetoclax by quantifying their target proteins, LCK and BCL2, respectively, including protein expression, phosphorylation status, spatial distribution, and cellular morphology. Findings We confirmed that phospho-LCK is predictive of dasatinib sensitivity, consistent with prior studies, and identified phospho-BCL2 as a previously unreported biomarker for venetoclax sensitivity. Integrating multiple biomarkers into machine learning models significantly enhanced predictive accuracy compared to single-marker analyses. Key informative features included spatial protein distribution and integrated protein-morphology metrics. Additionally, single-cell analysis revealed distinct cell subpopulations, suggesting intratumor heterogeneity in drug responses. Conclusions μPharma provides rapid (4-h assay), accurate, and automated prediction of drug sensitivity at single-cell resolution using minimal clinical samples, potentially enabling same-day precision oncology decision-making. Funding This work was supported by institutional start-up funds from the University of Utah, including internal supplements provided through the Immunology, Inflammation & Infectious Disease (3i) Initiative and the Diabetes & Metabolism Research Center (DMRC).

title: A machine learning model integrating circulating Temra cell transcriptional profiles to predict immunotherapy efficacy
abstract: Background While immunotherapy has transformed treatment paradigms for cancer, durable response rates remain below 30%. Currently available biomarkers are insufficient for precise patient stratification. Blood-based biomarkers, as minimally invasive and accessible tools, have attracted attention for their potential to dynamically monitor immune checkpoint inhibitor response. Methods Paired peripheral blood and tumor samples from 15 patients were analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing and T cell receptor sequencing. To construct a comprehensive CD8 + T cell transcriptomic atlas, we integrated 13 publicly available single-cell datasets. A logistic regression-based model was trained on the transcriptional profiles of terminally differentiated effector memory CD8 + T (Temra) cells and then validated in a prospective, multi-center non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cohort undergoing first-line immunotherapy. Findings Circulating Temra cells were the most clonally expanded CD8 + subset identified in peripheral blood. These cells exhibited distinct differentiation trajectories between responders and non-responders, with transcriptional profiles correlated with treatment efficacy. In the aggregated dataset comprising 748,082 CD8 + T cells, Temra transcriptional signatures were consistently associated with therapeutic outcomes. The predictive model, built upon the transcriptional profiles of Temra cells, achieved high accuracy (87%-95%) across two external validation cohorts. Validation in a prospective cohort of 131 patients with advanced NSCLC (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06054152) confirmed strong predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.834). Conclusions Circulating Temra cells serve as robust predictors of immunotherapy efficacy. This study establishes a machine learning-based, pan-cancer, blood-derived transcriptomic biomarker that was prospectively validated in an NSCLC cohort and may substantially improve clinical decision-making in immuno-oncology. Funding This study was funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (no. 92259205).

title: Capturing multi-disease states on a spectrum with machine learning and routine clinical data
abstract: Background Diseases exist on spectra of risk factors, cellular perturbations, organ dysfunction, and clinical manifestations. It is unknown whether the analysis of routine laboratory tests and vitals using artificial intelligence presents a scalable and portable system for capturing the spectral nature of common diseases. Methods We constructed and validated machine learning models targeting seven common diseases-atrial fibrillation, breast cancer, coronary artery disease, migraine, rheumatoid arthritis, schizophrenia, and type 2 diabetes-using routine clinical measurements from 394,957 electronic health records (EHRs) in the BioMe Biobank and UK Biobank. The Resulting model outputs, termed spectral health index from machine measurements of electronic records (SHIMMER), were assessed for association with disease diagnosis, risk factors, biomarkers, onset, survival, complications, and medications in two cohorts. Findings SHIMMER was associated with disease diagnosis, known risk factors, and biomarkers in expected directions in both cohorts. With greater SHIMMER, the prevalence of risk factors, complications, and medications continuously increased; for instance, age and hypertension, stroke risk and cardiac arrest, and beta blockers increased, respectively, with atrial fibrillation SHIMMER. Biomarker levels for type 2 diabetes, such as glucose, hemoglobin A1c, C-reactive protein, and triglycerides, changed stepwise as SHIMMER increased. Rising SHIMMER also revealed gradations of earlier disease onset and decreased survival, particularly for coronary artery disease and schizophrenia. Conclusions A holistic, non-invasive marker derived from machine learning trained on routine clinical measurements snapshots multiple common diseases on a spectrum, quantifying disease risk, severity, onset, survival, sequela, and treatment. Funding This study was supported in part by the National Institutes of Health.

title: AI-driven therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide for processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies
abstract: BACKGROUND: Progeroid laminopathies (PLs), including Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS), are rare premature aging disorders in which cardiovascular complications drive early mortality. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy, yet optimal design principles and their impact on cardiovascular pathology remain insufficiently defined. METHODS: We developed an AI-driven pipeline to design ASOs targeting the 3'UTR of LMNA transcripts to suppress processing-deficient pathogenic lamin A isoforms. Lead candidates were evaluated in patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (PL-iCMs), 3D cardiac organoids, and LMNA transgenic mouse models. Efficacy, toxicity, and systemic transcriptional responses were assessed using molecular, histological, and serum biochemical analyses. FINDINGS: The optimized ASO, LM2556, selectively reduced progerin and farnesylated pre-lamin A expression while preserving lamin C. LM2556 mitigated cellular senescence and improved structural and functional phenotypes in PL-iCMs and cardiac organoids. In vivo, LM2556 decreased pathogenic lamin A isoforms across multiple tissues without evidence of hepatotoxicity or nephrotoxicity. Long-term administration ameliorated progeroid features, improved cardiovascular pathology, extended median lifespan by 82.86%, and enhanced overall healthspan in LMNA transgenic mice. CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish an AI-based framework for therapeutic ASO design and provide proof-of-concept evidence that targeting the 3'UTR of LMNA transcripts can effectively suppress pathogenic lamin A isoforms and ameliorate systemic progeroid phenotypes. FUNDING: This work was funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (82450116 and 82502251).

title: A unified multi-task framework enables interpretable chest radiograph analysis
abstract: Background While multimodal deep learning has advanced medical imaging analysis, existing black-box systems may remain confined to isolated tasks, often overlooking the trust-sensitive nature of clinical diagnosis as a multi-task process. Methods We propose IMT-CXR (interpretable multi-task transformer for chest X-ray analysis), a framework that emulates radiologists' diagnostic workflow through three evidence-driven stages: (1) disease recognition, (2) attribute characterization (e.g., size, location, and severity quantification), and (3) evidence-integrated report generation with traceable decision pathways. The framework employs a unified transformer architecture optimized via medical-domain instruction tuning, which sequentially executes four clinical tasks: multi-label disease classification, lesion localization, anatomical segmentation, and radiology report generation. Findings Experimental validation demonstrates competitive performance on ten CXR benchmarks under direct inference and fine-tuning settings. In a blinded evaluation of 160 historical reports from four medical centers, three radiologists rated 66% of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated reports as comparable to or surpassing original clinical reports in diagnostic clarity, highlighting the framework's translational potential. Conclusions By establishing traceable diagnostic pathways from anatomical findings to conclusions, this work bridges the gap between AI technical metrics and clinical utility, advancing trustworthy AI systems in medical imaging. Funding This research was partially supported by the Centre for Perceptual and Interactive Intelligence (CPII) Ltd. under the Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC)'s InnoHK.

title: Plasma proteomics linking primary and secondary diseases: Insights into molecular mediation from UK Biobank data
abstract: Background Diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia are major risk factors for cardiovascular, neurological, renal, and pulmonary diseases, yet clinically accessible molecular mediators linking these cardiometabolic conditions to downstream complications remain unclear. Methods We analyzed plasma proteomic data from 53,030 UK Biobank participants with longitudinal follow-up. Mediation analysis evaluated circulating proteins linking three primary cardiometabolic diseases to 18 secondary outcomes. Mendelian randomization assessed potential causal relationships, and machine learning evaluated the predictive value of identified mediators. Findings We identified 998 significant mediation pathways involving 337 unique plasma proteins. GDF15 consistently mediated associations between diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, and ACE2 linked poorly controlled diabetes to increased risk of nerve root and plexus disorders. Mediators were enriched in receptor-mediated signaling and molecular-interaction pathways. Mendelian randomization supported potential causal roles for 44 proteins. Incorporating mediator proteins into machine-learning models improved prediction of secondary disease risk beyond traditional clinical factors and other plasma proteins. Conclusions Plasma proteins help mediate progression from cardiometabolic diseases to downstream complications. These findings provide a molecular map of disease mediation pathways, nominate biomarkers and therapeutic targets, and support improved risk stratification and targeted intervention. Funding This this study was supported by the National Institutes of Health, the American Heart Association, and institutional funding.

title: The human oral and airway viral genome catalog from metagenomes enables virome characterization informing respiratory health
abstract: Background Viral communities of the upper aerodigestive tract represent an important component of the human microbial ecosystem but remain poorly characterized due to the limited availability of habitat-specific reference resources. Methods We integrated 19,997 public and 2,673 newly sequenced oral and airway metagenomes to establish the Oral and Airway Viral Genome Catalogue (OAVGC). Viral genomes were reconstructed and characterized through taxonomic assignment, prokaryotic host prediction, functional annotation, and assessment of putative antibacterial activity. Our prospective longitudinal aging cohort, alongside 5 in-house datasets and publicly cohorts, were analyzed to investigate associations between airway virome profiles and respiratory health. Findings The OAVGC comprised 141,459 high-quality viral genomes (completeness ≥90%) clustered into 68,708 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs). Approximately half of these viruses and families are previously undescribed, with independent cross-cohort detection and PCR assays providing additional support for their occurrence. Across multiple respiratory infection cohorts, the virome exhibited convergent diversity reductions and compositional signatures. In the prospective cohort, the baseline airway virome was correlated with host lung function and geriatric health scores. Virome-based machine learning classifiers demonstrated potential for predicting the future occurrence of upper respiratory tract infections up to 12 months in advance, outperforming bacteriome-based models in our prediction analyses. Conclusions The OAVGC provides an unprecedented genomic and functional resource for investigating the ecological and clinical associations of the oral-airway virome, revealing its potential impact on respiratory health and capacity to predict future infections. Funding National Natural Science Foundation of China (82341113) and National Key R&D Program of China (2022YFA1304303).

title: An adult proteomic signature associated with very low birth weight and chronic disease risk
abstract: BACKGROUND: Adults born at very low birth weight (VLBW, <1.5 kg) have elevated risks of chronic disease, but it is unclear whether adult plasma proteomics contains a detectable signature associated with recalled VLBW. METHODS: We analyzed 2,923 plasma proteins in 26,061 UK Biobank participants (median sampling age 56.4 years) with recalled birth weight, including 368 with VLBW and 25,693 with normal birth weight. We derived a machine learning proteomic prematurity index (PPI) distinguishing these groups and evaluated associations with 425 adult diagnoses, discrimination relative to birth weight and electronic health record (EHR) information, incident diseases after proteomic sampling, and exploratory biological interpretation. FINDINGS: The PPI was associated with recalled VLBW (odds ratio [OR], 7.32; 95% confidence interval [95% CI], 4.01-13.42) and remained independently associated after adjustment for EHR-derived VLBW probability (OR, 5.82; 95% CI, 3.99-8.47). Recalled VLBW was associated with adult disease burden, and PPI showed higher discrimination than birth weight for 370 of 425 diseases. Incident-only analyses preserved the cross-disease hazard ratio patterns, while fewer events and adult factor adjustment attenuated some associations. Exploratory biological annotations paralleled the disease patterns. Among participants with normal birth weight, higher PPI was associated with disease burden and subsequent disease risk, indicating that PPI is not VLBW specific. CONCLUSIONS: Adult plasma proteomics identifies a signature associated with recalled VLBW that provides information about adult disease risk beyond birth weight and EHR-derived measures. These findings are hypothesis generating and do not establish a direct molecular consequence of prematurity. External validation is required before clinical application. FUNDING: The March of Dimes, the Alfred E. Mann Foundation, the Universe of Mind, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (INV-037517 and INV-076306).

title: Early detection of gastric cancer using DNA features in red blood cells, with multicenter validation
abstract: Background Early detection of gastric cancer (GC) is limited by invasive endoscopy and poor sensitivity of blood-based biomarkers. Red blood cells (RBCs), the most abundant cells in the circulation, are anucleate but can retain DNA remnants that have been associated with pathological stress. Here, we report a non-invasive strategy for GC detection based on genome-wide profiling of DNA remnants retained in RBCs (rbcDNA). Methods We performed shallow whole-genome sequencing of rbcDNA from 1-2 mL of peripheral blood of 865 individuals, including 434 treatment-naive GC patients and 431 non-GC controls with benign gastric conditions. In the discovery cohort, we identified 1,000 reproducible rbcDNA read-depth features distinguishing GC from non-cancer states. A machine learning classifier based on dimensionally reduced GC-associated rbcDNA features was trained in the discovery cohort (n = 435), with the cutoff fixed at 90% specificity, and evaluated in a test cohort (n = 109) and three independent multicenter validation cohorts (n = 321). Findings The classifier achieved the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 84% in nested cross-validation of the discovery cohort and 95% in the test cohort. Across three hospital-based multicenter validation cohorts, performance remained consistent, with 83%-90% overall sensitivity and 82%-89% sensitivity for stage I GC. Additionally, the classifier distinguished early-stage GC from precancerous lesions and other tumors and detected ∼80% of GC cases negative for tumor markers. Conclusions These findings demonstrate the potential of rbcDNA as a non-invasive biomarker for early-stage GC detection. Funding This work was supported by the Key Research and Development Program of Zhejiang Province (2026C02A1176 and 2024C03170).

title: Application of generative artificial intelligence to utilize unstructured clinical data for acceleration of inflammatory bowel disease research
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) research is a dynamic field. However, the growing volume of electronic health records (EHRs) and research data presents significant challenges. Traditional methods for structuring unstructured medical records are labour-intensive and lack scalability. Large language models (LLMs) may present a solution, yet their usefulness in data standardisation in the context of IBD remains unknown. Objective To evaluate the use of LLMs in structuring free-text histology and radiology reports from IBD patients, compare their performance to manual clinician curation, and assess the usefulness of fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Design We developed an IBD-specialised LLM-based framework utilising structured prompt engineering and fine-tuning. Reports were manually curated and processed using various LLMs. Performance was assessed and RAG was used to enhance model responses with clinical guidelines from European Crohn’s and Colitis Organisation (ECCO) and the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN). Results Overall, Llama 3.3 achieved the highest F1 for histology and imaging (1 ± 0 and 0.85 ± 0.29, respectively) in extracting findings and anatomical regions, surpassing other models in structured data generation. Fine-tuning improved the performance of the smaller Llama 3.1 8B model for imaging reports (0.7 ± 0.46 vs 0.82 ± 0.35), enabling better extraction with reduced computational requirements. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of LLM-based automated structuring of IBD-related medical records. Unstructured data from free text reports can be reliably converted to standardised ontologies with location, severity, and qualifiers. These advancements enable scalable, privacy-compliant AI-driven solutions for data standardisation. VISUAL ABSTRACT Key Messages What is already known on this topic Traditional methods for structuring unstructured medical records for research are labour-intensive and lack scalability. IBD patients generate vast quantities of longitudinal medical data due to the chronicity of disease. Large language models (LLMs) are well-positioned for data extraction and standardisation purposes. What this study adds This study demonstrates that Llama 3.3-70B and fine-tuned smaller models (Llama 3.1 8B) can accurately structure IBD-related histology and radiology reports. Additionally, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances clinical interpretability by incorporating guideline-based context. How this study might affect research, practice or policy The use of LLMs in structuring EHR data can significantly accelerate IBD research, improve data standardisation, and facilitate privacy-compliant AI-driven solutions for clinical decision support and policy development.

verified_metadata.title: Application of generative artificial intelligence to utilize unstructured clinical data for acceleration of inflammatory bowel disease research
verified_metadata.abstract: Background Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) research is a dynamic field. However, the growing volume of electronic health records (EHRs) and research data presents significant challenges. Traditional methods for structuring unstructured EHRs are labor-intensive and lack scalability. Large language models (LLMs) may present a solution, however, their usefulness in data standardization in the context of IBD remains unknown. We sought to evaluate LLMs in structuring free-text histology and radiology reports from IBD patients ( n = 32,041), compare their performance to manual clinician curation, and assess the usefulness of fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Methods We developed an IBD-specialized LLM-based framework utilizing structured prompt engineering and fine-tuning. Free-text reports from two independent sites were manually curated and processed using various LLMs ( n = 120). Findings Overall, Llama 3.3 achieved the highest F1 scores for histology and imaging (1.00 ± 0 and 0.85 ± 0.29, respectively) in extracting findings and anatomical regions, surpassing other models in structured data generation. Fine-tuning improved the performance of the smaller Llama 3.1 8B model for imaging reports (0.70 ± 0.46 vs. 0.82 ± 0.35), enabling better extraction with reduced computational requirements. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of LLM-based automated structuring of IBD-related medical records. Unstructured data from free-text reports can be reliably converted into standardized ontologies with location, severity, and qualifiers. These advancements enable scalable, privacy-compliant AI-driven solutions for data standardization. verified_metadata.abstract: Summary Background Morphological changes of abdominal organs in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain uncharacterized. This study aimed to automatically quantify these changes using deep learning, assess their treatment-related outcome associations, and evaluate prognostic value. Methods Abdominal computed tomography (CT) images from 2,747 patients with HCC and 2,869 healthy controls across 15 cohorts from 10 centers (8 Chinese and 2 international) were analyzed. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested nonlinear relationships between adrenal and kidney volumes and survival. Conclusions HCC is associated with systemic abdominal organ remodeling. Automated CT-based multi-organ quantification offers reproducible, non-invasive prognostic biomarkers, particularly in cases involving adrenal glands, spleen, and kidneys, supporting personalized treatment and prognosis assessment. title: Deep learning-enabled screening of chronic kidney disease from echocardiography
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects nearly 850 million individuals globally. The prevalence of undiagnosed CKD is over 60%. METHODS: Taking advantage of the relationship between CKD and cardiovascular disease, we developed a deep learning (DL) model to detect CKD from parasternal long-axis (PLAX) videos, using 325,377 PLAX videos from 62,818 patients at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center (CSMC). We externally validated our model in two independent cohorts of 2,762 patients at Stanford Healthcare (SHC) and 41,611 patients at Kaiser-Permanente Northern California (KPNC). FINDINGS: In a held-out test cohort at CSMC, our model detected any stage of CKD with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.756 (95% confidence interval: 0.749-0.763), with consistently strong performance in the KPNC (AUC: 0.718 [0.714-0.723]) and SHC (AUC: 0.719 [0.704-0.735]) cohorts. Our model performed well across subgroups with and without metabolic comorbidities, suggesting that it learned imaging features specific to CKD. CONCLUSIONS: Our DL echo model detected CKD with robust performance at two external clinical sites, thus offering an avenue for noninvasive screening and improved detection rates. FUNDING: This work was supported by the Sarnoff Cardiovascular Research Foundation, the American Heart Association (25POST1357984 and 25AHAI1487693), and the National Institutes of Health (R00HL157421, R01HL173487, and R01HL173526).

title: Assessing context-dependent effectiveness of heat adaptation through human mobility under different heatwave regimes
abstract: As heatwaves intensify under climate change, cities increasingly rely on adaptation strategies to mitigate risk. Yet, the real-world effectiveness of climate adaptation measures in influencing human behavior to support daily functioning across cities remains limited. Using daily intracity mobility data aggregated from over 1.1 billion mobile devices across 366 Chinese cities in 2023, we apply a causal inference framework based on causal random forest to quantify the heterogeneous effects of three key adaptation measures: access to cooling centers, urban greenness (NDVI), and heat warnings during daytime-only and compound day-night heatwaves. We find that the adaptation effectiveness varies markedly by heatwave type and local socioeconomic conditions. Public cooling facilities reduced mobility during daytime-only heatwaves but promoted it under day-night heatwaves, especially in low GDP per capita, aging and agriculturally dependent cities. In contrast, greenness consistently failed to sustain mobility in elderly or agriculturally dominant cities. Heat warnings exhibited paradoxical effects: although intended to discourage heat exposure, they were often associated with increased mobility at extreme temperatures in vulnerable cities, while showing only modest suppressive effects in younger, less agricultural cities. These findings reveal that the benefits of adaptation are highly context-dependent and unequally distributed, highlighting the need for precision adaptation: strategies tailored not only to environmental conditions but also to behavioral, demographic, and socioeconomic variability. By linking adaptation measures to near real-time behavioral responses, our study offers a scalable, data-driven framework to guide more equitable and effective urban climate-resilient planning.
