verified_metadata.title: Exploring the impacts of logistics space on urban carbon emissions: A hybrid MNL-LightGBM method
verified_metadata.abstract: As a major source of urban carbon emissions, logistics space and its interaction with the surrounding environment have become critical to understanding the dynamic patterns of urban carbon emissions. Deeper investigation into how urban logistics land use and facility layouts contribute to the spatial heterogeneity of carbon emissions holds significant implications. Taking the Wuhan Metropolitan Development Area as a case study, this paper proposes the concept of Spatial Environment Induced Carbon-Emission Discrepancy (SEICD), which quantifies emission heterogeneity into carbon mitigation and carbon exacerbation. A hybrid MNL‑LightGBM model is constructed to identify key factors and reveal their nonlinear mechanisms, focusing on the combined effects of logistics facility layout and spatial variables on carbon emissions. Results show that spatial variables, such as industrial land proportion and floor area ratio, exhibit strong nonlinear associations with SEICD. Interactive associations between the number of logistics facilities and distance to small facilities, as well as with FAR and distance to residential land, play particularly prominent roles. Furthermore, grid-scale analysis based on the SHAP method reveals that the layout of large logistics facilities adjacent to industrial land in the urban periphery, as well as areas with high floor area ratio and high land use mix in the central urban area, are conducive to carbon mitigation. By integrating mechanisms across different functional zones, this study constructs an optimization framework and regulatory methods for logistics facility layout based on spatial environmental adaptability, providing quantitative support and planning guidance for the low‑carbon transition of urban logistics systems.

title: A LSTM-EGAN framework for forecasting land surface temperature in urban areas based on time-series datasets
abstract: Land surface temperature (LST) is a key parameter for understanding urban thermal environments and is strongly shaped by both historical and contemporary urban land-use patterns. Jointly considering past land-use trajectories and current planning schemes is therefore essential for understanding the spatio-temporal relationships between urban form and LST, and for anticipating the thermal impacts of future development. This paper proposes a spatio-temporal prediction framework based on a Long Short-Term Memory–Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network (LSTM-EGAN) to generate fine-grained LST predictions from urban planning inputs and historical heat maps. Using Istanbul city as a case study, we train the model on a 10-year historical dataset comprising 1600 paired samples constructed from land-use maps, satellite imagery, and LST products. After quantitative accuracy assessment, we conduct scenario-based simulations to explore planning-relevant principles for urban heat mitigation. In addition, we develop an interactive user interface application for future projects. This study proposes a framework and application with the potential to support data-driven urban planning and design under increasing heat stress.

title: CausalSolar: Leveraging causal representations of residential solar adoption to enhance image-based detection of rooftop solar panels
abstract: Accurate mapping of residential rooftop solar panels is essential for understanding distributed energy transitions. Conventional image-based models often confuse solar panels with visually similar objects, such as skylights or HVAC units, relying solely on visual cues. Conversely, while existing studies identify demographics, building types, and policy as key drivers of solar adoption, these factors are typically used for ex post explanation of past trends rather than a priori prediction. To bridge this gap, this study introduces CausalSolar, a framework that integrates high-resolution visual learning with a Causal Reasoning Module to enhance residential rooftop solar detection and reasoning. Our framework operationalizes adoption mechanisms across domains of People (PE), Place (PL), Neighborhood Effects (NE), and Regional Effects (RE) as active constraints for object detection. Capitalizing on Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), the framework filters out spurious visual correlations and evaluates rooftop candidates based on both appearance and contextual reality. Applied to 428 census tracts across five North Carolina counties (6,419 km²), CausalSolar achieves an F1 score of 92.91%, outperforming state-of-the-art image-only baselines by 7% to 27%. Beyond detection, our framework characterizes the relative contributions of causal factors that shift along the urban-rural gradient: demographic factors (PE) dominate in dense urban cores and peri-urban neighborhoods, while structural, spatial, and policy cues (PL, NE, and RE) drive detection in moderate- to low-density rural neighborhoods. By embedding socio-behavioral evidence into computer vision, CausalSolar provides an accurate and interpretable tool for large-scale renewable energy mapping and sustainable urban planning.

title: Estimating the causal effects of landscape interventions on urban thermal environments using generalized random forests
abstract: A growing wave of urban thermal studies has used machine learning models and post-hoc explanation tools, particularly Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), to rank landscape factors and detect nonlinear thermal responses. Yet such predict-then-explain frameworks are designed to explain fitted models rather than real-world interventions, making them vulnerable to spurious correlations, unstable importance rankings, and ambiguous planning implications. This study applies a causal-diagram-informed generalized random forest (GRF) framework to estimate the effects of landscape interventions on land surface temperature (LST) at the city-block scale in Beijing. Built on adaptive local weighting, GRF constructs randomized-controlled-trial-like comparisons among observationally comparable city blocks, enabling the estimation of unit-specific dose-response intervention effects. The results show that replacing impervious surfaces with water bodies, trees, and croplands significantly reduced LST by 0.050 ± 0.023, 0.042 ± 0.011, and 0.034 ± 0.012 °C per 1% increase, respectively, while increasing building coverage raised LST by 0.022 ± 0.014 °C per 1%. Building height, building-height variability, and surface albedo also generated strong cooling effects, whereas all landscape configuration metrics showed no significant effects after accounting for land-cover composition. We also detected strong nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous effects: vegetation, water, and albedo interventions generally showed diminishing marginal cooling returns, and the cooling effects of trees, building-height variability, and albedo were strongest in highly built-up or central urban areas. This GRF workflow can support unit-specific and spatially heterogeneous landscape strategies for targeted urban heat mitigation.

Building height, building-height variability, and surface albedo also generated strong cooling effects, whereas all landscape configuration metrics showed no significant effects after accounting for land-cover composition. We also detected strong nonlinear and spatially heterogeneous effects: vegetation, water, and albedo interventions generally showed diminishing marginal cooling returns, and the cooling effects of trees, building-height variability, and albedo were strongest in highly built-up or central urban areas. This GRF workflow can support unit-specific and spatially heterogeneous landscape strategies for targeted urban heat mitigation.

title: Space–nature–human associations with land surface temperature across nested planning-spatial units: Evidence from Karst Mountainous Guizhou
abstract: Understanding how urban-spatial, natural, and human-social factors jointly relate to land surface temperature (LST) across nested planning contexts is important for climate-adaptive planning in mountainous cities. Integrated comparisons across planning units that are spatially nested but differ in function, environmental background, and development conditions remain limited. In mountainous karst Guizhou, Southwest China, this study examines the Qianzhong Urban Agglomeration, Guiyang Metropolitan Area, and Gui'an New Area. Hot–cold spot analysis, XGBoost–SHAP, and MGWR are integrated within a space–nature–human (S–N–H) framework to compare LST patterns, model-based variable contributions, nonlinear pairwise interactions, and variable-specific spatial associations under four seasonal–diurnal scenarios. Summer daytime hot spots mainly coincide with built-up areas and development corridors, whereas winter hot spots shift toward western and southern slopes and karst areas; forested mountains and large water bodies remain relatively stable cold spots. Natural-background associations are most prominent in the urban agglomeration, regional gradients coexist with localized built-form and human-activity associations in the metropolitan area, and selected associations become more localized and patchy in the new area, although some remain near-global. S–H, S–N, and N–H interactions vary in direction, magnitude, and response range across planning–spatial and seasonal–diurnal contexts rather than following a uniform cross-level progression. Sensitivity analyses support the principal interpretations across alternative grid resolutions and variable specifications. By linking relative contributions, interaction configurations, and spatial ranges, the framework shifts thermal-environment analysis from isolated factors to context-specific relationships and supports differentiated climate-adaptive planning across nested mountainous planning units.

title: Mapping environmental noise across mainland China using a two-stage stacked ensemble framework
abstract: Rapid urbanization has intensified environmental noise in China, yet a national-scale environmental noise exposure map remains absent. This study developed a two-stage stacked ensemble learning framework to map acoustic environments across mainland China and assess socioeconomic disparities in noise exposure. We integrated 554,948 observations from 103,102 environmental noise monitoring stations with multisource geospatial predictors, including transport networks, land use, population density, nighttime lights, GDP, building footprints, points of interest, air pollutants, meteorological variables, elevation, and vegetation. The modelling framework combined Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost as base learners, followed by a LightGBM meta-learner and residual calibration. The final model achieved an R 2 of 0.660, RMSE of 4.720 dB, and MAE of 3.631 dB at the national scale, with performance varying across regions and urbanization strata. The predicted 1 km × 1 km noise maps revealed spatial and temporal gradients, including higher exposure in eastern urban agglomerations and sustained evening-nighttime noise in metropolitan cores. Population-weighted L den declined across GDP per capita quintiles, whereas the proportion of the population exposed to L den >53 dB was highest in the lower-middle group and declined across the higher quintiles. These findings provide macro-scale evidence of environmental noise exposure and inequality in China and support differentiated strategies for sustainable urban noise management.

verified_metadata.title: LLM-empowered agents for lifeline network recovery with graph-guided MCP tools
verified_metadata.abstract: Post-disaster recovery of lifelines is critical, with numerous studies proposing tools for interdependent lifeline network recovery (LNR). However, existing tools themselves, whether standalone or embedded in systems, lack task-solving capabilities and still depend on human orchestration and execution for handling LNR tasks. Hence, this study proposes a development approach of large language model (LLM)-empowered agents that can intelligently utilize tools to solve LNR tasks. The approach comprises (i) the development of graph-guided LNR tools hosted on model context protocol (MCP) servers, (ii) the construction of LNR agents with the pattern of tool chain generation-tool execution (TCG-TE), and (iii) the evaluation and comparison of agents’ performance. The findings indicate that among the 32 compared agents, 5 out of 8 TCG-TE agents can successfully solve 50 LNR tasks, while none of the 24 traditional agents can solve all tasks. Agents following TCG-TE pattern with graph-guided MCP tools empowered by 8 LLMs solve 13.9% more tasks and reduce 68.2% of unnecessary tool invocations compared to the best-performing agents in traditional patterns. This study contributes by providing a development approach of LNR agents with task-solving capacities. Moreover, the proposed TCG-TE pattern alleviates agents’ difficulty in selecting and orchestrating tools.

verified_metadata.title: Quantifying the effects of lift-up building morphology on pedestrian-level wind and comfort in dense urban arrays: A data-driven study
verified_metadata.abstract: Pedestrian-level wind (PLW) strongly influences outdoor comfort in high-density cities. Lift-up buildings are widely adopted to enhance near-ground ventilation, yet the nonlinear aerodynamic interactions between their morphology and surrounding urban arrays remain insufficiently quantified. This study develops an integrated framework combining parametric CFD, surrogate modeling, and explainable machine learning to examine how lift-up building morphology influences pedestrian wind environments in dense urban arrays. A dataset of 180 cases was generated for a central lift-up building surrounded by low-rise buildings. The simulations were validated against wind-tunnel measurements, and a Random Forest surrogate model (R² = 0.966) enabled efficient prediction of pedestrian-level wind velocity and pressure-related indicators. Statistical analysis first identifies a morphological control hierarchy in which main-body height shows the strongest association with improved pedestrian-level ventilation, while plan proportions show weaker associations with airflow organization. To further reveal nonlinear relationships, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and one-dimensional accumulated local effects (ALE) were employed. Three key aerodynamic patterns emerge. First, increasing main-body height markedly improves ventilation, but the gains diminish at the upper sampled levels. Second, main-body aspect ratio and plan ratio exhibited non-monotonic responses, with lower unfavorable wind comfort ratios at intermediate values of approximately 1.5–2.0. Third, building height and wind orientation showed a pronounced interaction. Low-rise configurations showed greater contrasts between sampled alignments, whereas taller cases exhibited more favorable and less direction-sensitive pedestrian-level wind conditions. These findings clarify the nonlinear aerodynamic role of lift-up morphology and provide preliminary quantitative guidance for early-stage climate-responsive urban massing design within comparable dense-array settings.

verified_metadata.title: Decoding the spatiotemporal cascade effects of compound heat-flood risks in a sinking coastal city: A GCN-LSTM based multi-scenario projection
verified_metadata.abstract: Global warming continues to exacerbate compound heat-flood risks in high-density coastal cities yet forecasting their nonlinear spatiotemporal cascade effects under land subsidence regulation remains highly challenging. This study aims to systematically identify the spatiotemporal evolution and underlying driving mechanisms of compound heat-flood risks in Jakarta across various subsidence gradients and future scenarios. We utilized the Hazard-Exposure-Vulnerability framework to quantify historical single and compound risks, specifically the Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD), from 2017 to 2024. Furthermore, a Graph Convolutional Network and Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model, integrated with GeoShapley spatial attribution, was developed to dynamically project risk evolution under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) from the year 2025 to 2050. The results indicate: (1) The compound heat-flood risk exhibits a significant non-linear synergetic pattern, with high-CCD zones remaining primarily concentrated in the northern coastal and central built-up areas, with growing compound risk pressure in the southern HSZ. (2) Impervious surface area acts as the primary anthropogenic driver escalating both hazards, while land subsidence substantially amplifies flood retention and compound stress in the southern region. (3) Multi-scenario projections reveal a structural breakpoint around 2035, after which the risk trajectories under different SSPs diverge more clearly. (4) Differentiated spatial interventions balance local geological constraints, enabling the highly vulnerable high subsidence zones (HSZ) to achieve the most significant risk mitigation. Ultimately, prioritizing localized groundwater control and spatial ecological renewal is absolutely crucial for cutting the destructive cascade transmission and achieving resilient urban development.

verified_metadata.title: Environmental justice and urban heat thresholds in Istanbul: An explainable machine learning approach with spatial residual diagnostics
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid urbanization intensifies the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, yet neighborhood-level surface thermal exposure remains unevenly distributed across urban populations. While the environmental justice dimensions of UHI have received attention in Global North contexts, empirical evidence from rapidly developing megacities remains limited, and conventional machine learning applications in urban climatology frequently overlook spatial autocorrelation, risking biased inference. To address these gaps, this study develops a hybrid spatial machine learning framework to examine the drivers of mean summer Land Surface Temperature (LST)—a radiometric surface temperature proxy, not a direct measure of thermal comfort—across 750 neighborhoods in Istanbul. An XGBoost regressor was integrated with a post-hoc Spatial Error Model (SEM) diagnostic filter, reducing residual Moran's I from 0.449 (p = 0.001) to −0.011 (p = 0.321) under a district-grouped spatial cross-validation design (Test R² = 0.937; CV R² = 0.870 ± 0.070). SHAP analysis was applied to a 25-variable dataset fusing Landsat 8/9 remote sensing imagery, NASA SRTM topographic data, and neighborhood-level socioeconomic records to quantify non-linear feature contributions to LST. NDBI and NDVI emerged as the primary morphological determinants, followed by distance to coastline and population density. A density-dependent vegetation efficacy transition band was estimated at approximately 27,000–34,000 persons/km² (primary breakpoint estimate: 28,070; bootstrap 95% CI: 27,176–30,744; district-grouped spatial sensitivity range: 26,914–34,312 persons/km²), above which NDVI cooling contributions diminish substantially regardless of greenness level. A systematic thermal disparity was identified across socioeconomic groups: A+ (elite) neighborhoods exhibited a mean summer LST of 39.4 °C, compared with 42.8 °C in D (low SES) neighborhoods (Δ = 3.4 °C), indicating an associational thermal gradient along socioeconomic lines. These findings suggest that urban greening strategies should be calibrated to local population-density transition bands, and that surface heat mitigation planning should explicitly account for the unequal spatial distribution of surface thermal exposure across socioeconomic groups.

verified_metadata.title: Fine-scale urban heat mapping by machine learning downscaling of MODIS land surface temperature in a hyper-arid megacity
verified_metadata.abstract: Fine-scale land surface temperature (LST) underpins assessment of the surface urban heat island and heat exposure in cities, yet thermal sensors trade spatial detail against temporal frequency. Evaluate a reproducible machine learning framework that downscales seasonal-median MODIS daytime LST from 1 km to 100 m over the hyper-arid megacity of Greater Cairo, Egypt, for summer 2025. A scale-consistent regression of coarse LST on fine predictors—Sentinel-2 indices, terrain derivatives, and sub-pixel ESA WorldCover fractions—is combined with an additive residual correction; seven algorithms are compared. Products are assessed by cross-validation, scale-consistency on re-aggregation, and comparison with Landsat-8/9. At the coarse scale the predictor–LST relationship is strong (histogram gradient boosting: R² = 0.94, RMSE = 0.77 °C; 0.93–0.92 under 3–8 km blocking); re-aggregation shows approximate MODIS consistency (R² = 0.83–0.99, model-dependent; small bias for signal-consistent models); and the 100 m fields recover the intra-urban thermal pattern. Against Landsat, however, every product consistent with the coarse signal shows a large systematic cold bias (−5.5 to −6.1 °C) and a negative R², while retaining moderate spatial correlation (r up to 0.84); the bias is minimal over water and largest over built-up and bare surfaces. The un-downscaled MODIS field carries the same offset (−5.93 °C), as do twelve same-day pairs (−6.3 ± 2.0 °C), so it is inherited from the MODIS–Landsat product pair to within the empirically measured scale-consistency error, rather than being created by sharpening. Statistical sharpening faithfully redistributes the parent sensor’s information but cannot reconcile inter-sensor differences; a non-coincident finer image is not a valid absolute reference for downscaled urban LST.

verified_metadata.title: Towards an urban digital twin: An XAI-integrated prototype framework for sustainable mobility modelling in Algiers, Algeria
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid urbanisation across North African metropolises—Algiers in particular—places transport systems under mounting stress: congestion erodes economic productivity, vehicle emissions degrade public health, and energy-intensive mobility patterns accelerate carbon expenditure. These pressures are compounded by the absence of interpretable tools capable of jointly quantifying congestion, energy demand, and air quality in forms actionable for governance. This underscores the need for integrated spatiotemporal modeling of traffic congestion, energy demand, and air quality for sustainable urban mobility planning. This study constructs, validates, and applies a prototype framework towards an Urban Digital Twin for Algiers, integrating eight heterogeneous urban data streams within a unified geospatial environment to jointly model traffic congestion, energy demand, and air quality. A comprehensive hybrid dataset, comprising directly observed and statistically augmented records for model robustness, encompasses 500,000 spatiotemporal records across 5,000 road segments and 57 communes. Random Forest and XGBoost models were benchmarked with SHAP attribution and scenario simulation. The proposed framework provides an exploratory, scenario-based decision-support tool directly applicable to the ongoing revision in Algiers. The Compact Mixed-Use and TOD scenarios demonstrate substantial energy and environmental gains—energy reduction and NO2 improvement—establishing a scenario-based, quantitative evidence base for transit-integrated land use revisions to Algiers' master planning frameworks, utilizing a hybrid dataset comprising both directly observed and statistically augmented records to directly inform temporally targeted demand management policy for North African cities.

verified_metadata.title: A continental-scale XGBoost framework for multi-hazard susceptibility and socioeconomic exposure in South America
verified_metadata.abstract: Floods, droughts, and wildfires affect many South American cities, but continent-scale assessments rarely connect hazard susceptibility with urban exposure. We present a continental-scale (∼1 km) framework that compares a simple weighted benchmark with hazard-specific Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models built from 27 Earth observation and socioeconomic datasets. On identical held-out test pixels, XGBoost increased ROC-AUC from 0.65 to 0.93 for flood, from 0.59 to 0.89 for drought, and from 0.74 to 0.92 for wildfire, with similar gains in PR-AUC, F1 score, and balanced accuracy. We therefore used XGBoost to generate the final susceptibility maps. The mapped classes are relative continental quantile classes, not absolute event probability thresholds. The mapped patterns place higher flood likelihood in humid lowlands and river corridors, higher drought likelihood in water-limited hot regions, and higher wildfire likelihood in hot, dry frontier regions. A city-scale synthesis for 758 South American cities places the strongest combinations of high composite hazard and lower adaptive capacity in northeastern Brazil, Caribbean-facing Colombia and Venezuela, and lowland Bolivia, while lower-hazard and stronger-capacity settings are more common in parts of the Southern Cone and Andean corridors. The maps, input layers, municipal classes, and city-level summaries can be explored in MIRA, the Multi-hazard Index for Risk Assessment, at https://riskframeworksa.github.io/data_viewer/.

verified_metadata.title: Urban wind field reconstruction for low-altitude flight: A comparison of Gappy POD and deep autoencoder strategies using CFD and sparse sensing
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban wind field reconstruction from sparse observations is important for real-time monitoring, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flight safety, and smart city applications. However, accurately recovering complex wind fields in dense urban areas remains challenging because building-induced flow distortion creates strong spatial heterogeneity. In this study, four reconstruction frameworks, namely Gappy Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Gappy POD combined with fully-connected Neural Networks (POD+NN), Autoencoder (AE), and AE combined with NN (AE+NN), are developed and evaluated for sparse sensor urban wind field reconstruction using a high-resolution CFD database for a central district in Shenzhen. The results show that deep learning-based methods outperform the traditional linear Gappy POD approach, with AE+NN achieving the best overall accuracy and robustness. At 120 m height, which is highly relevant to low-altitude UAV applications, AE+NN reduces wind speed reconstruction errors by about 20–30% compared with Gappy POD. AE+NN also remains stable under sparse sensor configurations, whereas Gappy POD requires substantially more sensors to avoid large errors. Reconstruction accuracy is strongly influenced by height and wind direction, while the effect of sensor layout (randomly or uniformly distributed) is comparatively small. AE-based methods show stronger generalization across wind directions and better reproduce local wind variations and wake-affected regions along representative UAV trajectories. In addition, introducing a physics-based regularization term improves the spatial consistency of AE reconstruction by reducing physically inconsistent solutions and narrowing the full-field error distribution. This study demonstrates that combining nonlinear manifold learning with latent-variable prediction provides an efficient and accurate framework for sparse sensor urban wind reconstruction. The proposed AE+NN approach shows strong potential for practical applications such as UAV route planning, urban wind hazard assessment, and smart-city wind monitoring.

title: MTML-EV: Multi-target meta-learning for cross-zone urban electric vehicle charging infrastructure management
abstract: Rapid electric vehicle (EV) adoption is reshaping urban mobility and energy systems, intensifying challenges for charging infrastructure management, including congestion, uneven spatial demand, and grid stress. Addressing these challenges requires reliable forecasting of multiple charging-system states across both near-real-time operation and short-term planning horizons, particularly for newly deployed or evolving zones with limited historical data. Existing urban EV charging forecasting approaches often focus on individual charging-system variables and exhibit limited adaptability to previously unseen zones. To address this limitation, this paper presents MTML-EV, a multi-target meta-learning framework that jointly predicts charging occupancy, energy demand, and electricity price across 1-, 6-, and 12-hour forecasting horizons. MTML-EV formulates each traffic zone as a learning task and leverages a BiGRU-based temporal encoder optimized with first-order model-agnostic meta-learning (FOMAML) to learn transferable temporal representations that enable rapid adaptation to previously unseen zones. Extensive experiments on the UrbanEV benchmark evaluate MTML-EV across multiple forecasting horizons and unseen-zone adaptation scenarios against deep learning, hybrid, and Transformer-based baselines. For 1-hour ahead prediction on unseen zones, MTML-EV reduces RMSE by 7.5% for energy demand and 59% for electricity price compared with the strongest Transformer baseline while maintaining high occupancy forecasting accuracy. Additional robustness analyses across multiple unseen-zone partitions demonstrate that these performance gains remain stable under varying zone configurations, while interpretability analysis confirms that the model relies on meaningful temporal, charging-related, and contextual factors. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of MTML-EV for multi-target cross-zone forecasting under heterogeneous urban conditions, highlighting the value of transferable temporal representations for adaptive EV charging infrastructure management.

title: Optimizing urban green space spatial pattern to reduce land surface temperature: A greedy-based adaptive strategy
abstract: Urban green space (UGS) planning often draws on average relationships between spatial configuration and land surface temperature (LST), whereas phased interventions require choices for specific locations and landscape states. This study compares three predefined greening rules with a greedy-based adaptive strategy (AS) in Philadelphia. A CNN-XGBoost model provides a common scenario-evaluation engine; the adaptive decision procedure selects among centralized, irregular, and decentralized rules for each planning unit and round. The original 420 m group-based split yielded a test R² of 0.909. An additional validation excluding overlapping predictor windows yielded a mean R² of 0.886, providing a more conservative assessment of within-city prediction. Under the stated scenario assumptions, AS achieved the greatest cumulative predicted cooling and the highest average cooling efficiency, 0.159°C per percentage-point increase in UGS cover. This efficiency exceeded those of the irregular, decentralized, random-switching, and centralized strategies by 12.0%, 14.4%, 25.2%, and 57.4%, respectively. In the reference allocation, 72% of planning units changed their selected rule at least once over four rounds. Repetition and sensitivity analyses supported the comparative advantage of AS across the tested settings. The findings support reassessing a defined set of greening alternatives as local conditions and implementation stages change, providing a practical framework for adaptive scenario comparison during phased urban greening.

verified_metadata.title: Research on spatial heterogeneity of urban flood susceptibility and model attribution in Beijing: An XGBoost-SHAP analysis based on spatial cross-validation
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban waterlogging exhibits significant spatial autocorrelation and extreme class imbalance, which may lead to overestimation of model generalization performance when random data splits are used. Taking 68,104 500 m grid cells in Beijing as evaluation units, this study constructs an urban waterlogging susceptibility model based on 405 historically waterlogged positive samples and 16 static geo-socioeconomic indicators covering hazard, exposure, and vulnerability. Fivefold spatial block cross-validation at 0.1° resolution is employed to compare Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Linear SVM, LightGBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost, together with class-imbalance handling techniques including class weighting, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, Balanced Random Forest, and EasyEnsemble. Results show that XGBoost achieves a spatial cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.888±0.020 and a PR-AUC of 0.052±0.011, with a recall of 0.796±0.067 for the waterlogging class. Although it attains the highest PR-AUC among all models, its precision is only 0.024, indicating that the model is better suited as a high-recall screening tool than as a deterministic forecasting system. ROC-AUC values across the three pseudo-negative sampling strategies range from 0.882 to 0.887, and the SHAP rankings of slope, population density, and vegetation coverage remain generally stable. Full-sample SHAP attribution identifies slope, vegetation coverage, total population, and elevation as the most influential variables. Breakpoints derived from piecewise regression are interpreted as internal statistical associations within the model rather than as hydrological or planning thresholds. . Street typology based on 19 aggregated indicators retained eight principal components explaining 92.3% of variance. Although K=2 achieved the highest silhouette coefficient (0.375), the K=5 solution was retained for governance-oriented classification because its seed stability was high (mean ARI = 0.991) and its 80% subsample stability remained acceptable (ARI = 0.891 ± 0.090). Its silhouette coefficient was 0.221, so it is not presented as the unique statistical optimum. This study repositions the model from "risk prediction" to "static susceptibility identification," while explicitly acknowledging limitations arising from unobserved factors such as drainage network capacity, pumping station performance, event rainfall characteristics, and monitoring biases.

verified_metadata.title: Dual friction mapping of urban pedestrian spaces: Integrating street-view visual analytics and Geographically Neural Network Weighted Regression in Izmir, Türkiye
verified_metadata.abstract: Pedestrian comfort is undermined both by physical obstructions that compress usable sidewalk space and by thermal stress in hot weather. Yet physical and thermal friction are usually measured separately, leaving planners without a fine-grained basis for deciding where obstacle removal, sidewalk widening, or shade and cooling interventions are actually needed. This study introduces the Pedestrian Friction Index (PFI), combining a Physical Comfort Score (visual obstruction from street-view imagery, including effective clear walking width) and a Thermal Friction Score (land surface temperature, albedo, greenery, and sky openness) in equal measure, applied across 5663 street-view points in Izmir, Türkiye. Street-view images were segmented for physical indicators, while satellite imagery supplied thermal and terrain metrics. We modelled PFI using Geographically Neural Network Weighted Regression (GNNWR), allowing spatial non-stationarity across the city, and benchmarked it against four spatial regression models. GNNWR achieved an out-of-sample R2 of 0.407 under repeated hex-blocked cross-validation. Local coefficients indicated that clear walking width and tree canopy height consistently reduced friction, whereas morphological density, street canyon ratio, ground coverage, and park distance increased it in specific spatial contexts. A bivariate vulnerability atlas identified locations where high physical and thermal friction coincide, guiding sidewalk widening, obstacle removal, tree planting, and heat mitigation in Mediterranean cities. The findings support a planning transition from generic walkability rankings to diagnosis-specific pedestrian infrastructure policy.

verified_metadata.title: Spatiotemporal evolution and spatially heterogeneous drivers of urban flood risk: A K-means optimized XGBoost model
verified_metadata.abstract: With the intensification of climate change and rapid urbanization, urban flooding events have become increasingly frequent, posing serious threats to urban safety and sustainable development. However, existing studies often regard cities as homogeneous spaces, which limits the understanding of spatially heterogeneous flood drivers. Taking the Ningbo urban area as the study area, historical urban flood points from 2010 to 2024 collected from social media and government websites were analyzed using kernel density estimation and standard deviational ellipse analysis to reveal spatiotemporal evolution patterns. Based on flood records and multisource influencing factors, a K-means optimized XGBoost (KXGBoost) model was developed, combined with SHAP and Partial Dependence Plot (PDP) analyses to interpret the contributions and nonlinear response patterns of key factors across different zones. The results show that high and very high risk areas were mainly distributed in the central urban area, and the spatial pattern of urban flooding evolved from a highly concentrated monocentric pattern toward a more dispersed and polycentric pattern. The KXGBoost model considering spatial heterogeneity improved the AUC from 0.84 to 0.89 compared with the baseline XGBoost model. The highly urbanized Zone 1 was mainly influenced by Drainage, Road and NDVI, whereas Zone 3 showed higher contributions from NDVI, Road and MBH. PDP results further revealed nonlinear relationships of drainage density and vegetation coverage with flood risk, and these response patterns varied under different road and building conditions. These findings provide scientific support for differentiated urban flood management strategies and enhance urban resilience under climate change.

verified_metadata.title: From optimization to generation: A machine learning and morphology-constrained GAN framework for improving energy and thermal performance in residential clusters
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban morphology substantially affects energy and thermal performance in residential clusters. However, existing studies have mainly focused on performance prediction or parametric optimization, with limited attention to translating optimized parameters into spatial layout solutions. This study proposes an optimization-generation framework that combines machine learning and a morphology-constrained generative adversarial network (MCGAN) for residential clusters. Using 5466 samples from five representative climate zones in China, four performance indicators were computed: energy use intensity (EUI), solar energy generation intensity (SEGI), net energy use intensity (NEUI), and outdoor thermal comfort autonomy (OTCA). Machine learning-based surrogate models and SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) analysis were used to predict performance and identify dominant morphological drivers. The best-performing surrogate model was integrated with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) and MCGAN to generate residential layouts from optimized morphological parameters. The results indicate that energy-related indicators are mainly influenced by the perimeter-to-area ratio and facade-to-roof area ratio, whereas outdoor thermal comfort is primarily governed by the sky view factor and buildings enclosure ratio. XGBoost and LightGBM achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with R² values exceeding 0.89 across all indicators. A residential cluster in Wuhan was used to validate the proposed framework, where 1211 candidate layouts were generated and 161 Pareto-optimal solutions were identified through the optimization-to-generation process. Equal-weight TOPSIS evaluation of the re-simulation results indicated that the optimized schemes achieved better overall performance than the original design. The proposed framework provides interpretable decision support for early-stage residential cluster planning and design.

verified_metadata.title: Investigating the Nonlinear and Spatially Heterogeneous Impacts of Urban Form on Land Surface Temperature Using Geographic Explainable Artificial Intelligence
verified_metadata.abstract:
ABSTRACT
Previous studies have extensively examined urban form–land surface temperature (LST) relationships. However, nonlinear responses, spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and local predictive contributions have not been adequately examined within a unified framework. This study examines these relationships in Sana’a City, Yemen, using multi-temporal Landsat data from 2005, 2015, and 2025 within a geographically and temporally weighted random forest–GeoShapley (GTWRF–GeoShapley) framework. The analysis distinguishes local linear sensitivity, unsigned local random-forest importance, and signed predictive attribution. Results indicate that elevated LST has progressively expanded from the urban core into developing peripheral zones, with the area exceeding 25°C increasing from 22% to 47%. Spatially, regions of grid cells dominated by built-environment indicators increased from 28% to 50%, while the proportion dominated by vegetation-related indicators declined from 72% to 50%. Positive contributions associated with the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI) and built-up density (BUD) became increasingly spatially contiguous across central built-up areas; the mean absolute GeoShapley contribution of NDBI increased from 0.52 to 0.60°C, while BUD remained stable at approximately 0.50°C. Urban compactness exhibited a localized core–periphery pattern, with the largest proportional increase in mean absolute contribution (+25.0%). Conversely, cooling contributions associated with vegetation fraction became increasingly fragmented and were largely confined to less urbanized peripheral areas. Furthermore, BUD exhibited a nonlinear warming response, with its positive contribution increasing from +1.2 to +1.6°C beyond an empirical transition near 30% BUD. These findings provide geographically explicit insights for managing urban growth. Strategies aimed at preventing fragmented built-up expansion from reducing connected green spaces and generating localized thermal hotspots could help curb fragmented urban expansion at city fringes, ultimately supporting sustainable morphological transitions for rapidly growing cities.

title: Air-quality-sensitive urban design on NO2 Mitigation in the high-rise high-density City of London: A machine-learning land-use regression analysis
abstract: Elevated nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) remains a persistent urban air-quality and public-health concern. In the UK, despite progressive emissions-control policies, exceedances have historically occurred in central London. This study quantifies neighbourhood-scale NO₂ variability in the high-rise, high-density City of London and evaluates how air-quality-sensitive urban design, alongside traffic measures, influences concentrations in a morphology-constrained street network. We developed machine-learning land-use regression (LUR) models to predict NO₂ distribution: the Random Forest (RF) model performed best (adjusted R² = 0.88; RMSE = 7.6 μg m⁻³; MAE = 6.25 μg m⁻³). The RF-LUR model was then applied to assess air-quality-sensitive urban design scenarios. Increased built fraction associated with population growth was associated with widespread NO₂ increases (up to 5.5 µg m⁻³), consistent with reduced dispersion in dense street-canyons. A 50% reduction in heavy-vehicle activity was associated with corridor-focused NO₂ decreases of 1–6 µg m⁻³. Introducing additional high-rise buildings increased height variability and was associated with NO₂ reductions up to ∼7 µg m⁻³ in the eastern cluster. Targeted tree-canopy expansion was associated with hotspot reductions of up to ∼4 µg m⁻³ but produced small local increases in some areas. The combined intervention package was associated with the largest overall improvement, with NO 2 reductions up to ∼7 µg m⁻³. The results show that integrating urban morphology within machine-learning LUR models can provide a practical, fine-scale evidence base for spatial targeting and comparative appraisal of NO₂ mitigation options in high-density urban districts.

verified_metadata.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based UAV navigation in 3D urban boundary layers
verified_metadata.abstract: Low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation in urban environments is challenged by complex building geometry and unsteady wind disturbances, including wakes, recirculation, and vertical motions within the urban boundary layer (UBL). To improve autonomous navigation under partial observation and unsteady wind disturbances, this study proposes a Latent actor and Random Network Distillation (RND) augmented Soft actor critic method (LARA-SAC). A high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) unsteady urban wind field generated by large-eddy simulation (LES) is incorporated into the navigation environment, enabling the agent to learn continuous control policies under explicit building constraints and wind forcing. LARA-SAC integrates historical observation memory, latent trajectory exploration, and state action novelty estimation within the SAC framework. A history queue and a Gated Transformer eXtra Large (GTrXL) encoder extract recent wind disturbances, target direction changes, and obstacle approach trends, while latent exploration improves directional consistency and RND enhances early value learning through novelty feedback. Compared with recent benchmark methods, LARA-SAC shows more stable learning behavior, stronger task completion ability, and lower collision risk. The learned policy adapts both horizontal motion and flight altitude according to the target position, building layout, and local wind variations, rather than following fixed routes. Additional energy and generalization tests further indicate that LARA-SAC maintains safe and continuous navigation in larger urban wind fields, demonstrating good stability, safety, and adaptability in complex 3D urban environments.

title: Explainable AI for targeted green infrastructure allocation: A predictive framework for urban heat island mitigation
abstract: Semi-arid cities, where vegetation is scarce and thermal vulnerability is increasing, are particularly exposed to urban heat island (UHI) effects. This study develops an explainable machine-learning framework for prioritising urban greening in a semi-arid city, applied to Shiraz, Iran. The target is the local surface thermal anomaly, derived from Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature over the summers of 2013 to 2022 at 90 m support, predicted from 72 vegetation, built-up, land-cover, population, proximity, topographic, spectral and building-height predictors that exclude absolute surface temperature. Under random ten-fold resampling (map completion within the sampled city) gradient boosting reaches R² = 0.879; under buffered spatial block cross-validation (transfer to unseen parts of the city) it reaches a fold-mean R² of 0.648 (RMSE 1.76°C), and five tree-ensemble implementations agree within 0.01. SHAP attribution identifies the bare-land fraction and population density as the leading predictors and the anthropogenic, proximity and landscape-configuration predictors as the leading family. Hotspot detection recovers 42.5 % of the hottest decile of cells at equal treated area, a 5.6-fold improvement over random siting, and conformal prediction intervals cover 0.874 of held-out cells at a nominal 0.90. Five greening allocation strategies are compared at equal treated area; under the predictor-update rule tested, an area-of-applicability test places 15 to 98 % of treated cells outside the domain of the fitted model, so no cooling magnitude is reported. The framework gives a transparent basis for targeting green infrastructure in semi-arid cities and identifies when data-driven cooling estimates should not be used.

title: Satellite-derived LST can overstate vegetation cooling benefits: Evidence from surface and air temperature analyses in Sydney
abstract: Urban vegetation cooling is often assessed using satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) and individual vegetation indicators. However, it remains unclear whether relationships between different vegetation indicators and LST are reflected in near-surface air temperature (Ta), and how they vary across seasons, between day and night, and along the coastal–inland gradient. Using an integrated 2019–2025 framework for Sydney, this study combines LST, dense Ta observations, vegetation indicators, urban morphology, and coastal proximity. Statistical and machine-learning analyses quantify bivariate and multivariate relationships and rank predictor contributions. We find from the multivariate analysis that the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), a greenness proxy, is strongly associated with lower daytime LST, leading to a −1.92°C reduction in summer and −1.78°C in spring per 0.1-unit increase. In contrast, NDVI is related to lower Ta only during summer daytime, with a smaller impact (−0.18°C per 0.1-unit increase), indicating that NDVI–LST patterns are weakly reflected in Ta. For air temperature, Leaf Area Index (LAI) anomaly is the leading summer vegetation predictor, leading to a −0.68°C reduction during daytime and −0.46°C at night per 0.1-unit increase, although LAI–temperature relationships reverse in winter. Summer feature importance reinforces this contrast, with NDVI ranking highest for LST and LAI anomaly ranking highest for Ta. Overall, LST-based vegetation–temperature relationships can overstate Ta responses with variation across vegetation indicators and along the coastal-inland gradient. Heat-adaptation planning should distinguish surface-temperature responses from Ta responses and combine greenness with canopy-structure metrics.

title: Monitoring and forecasting of urban air pollution and exceedance events: implications for environmental risk assessment and early warning communication using machine learning in sustainable cities
abstract: Short-term pollution episodes are often hidden by annual-average reporting, and machine-learning forecasts are rarely benchmarked against persistence or evaluated at the 24-h/8-h periods defining regulatory exceedance. This study analyses 15,502 hourly observations (Nov. 2024-Aug. 2026) of PM 2.5 , PM 10 , NO 2 , NO, NO x , O 3 and SO 2 at an urban background station in Iasi, Romania. Random Forest and XGBoost were trained at three horizons (1, 6, 24 h) via season-balanced walk-forward validation, and separately to forecast next-day (D+1) regulatory indicators. PM 2.5 , PM 10 and NO 2 complied with current EU limits (2008/50/EC) in 2025 but exceeded WHO 2021 guidelines 1.5-2.9x and already exceed 2030 EU limits (Directive 2024/2881). At 1 h, persistence matched or exceeded both models for every pollutant (O 3 R² = 0.87 vs. 0.81 for XGBoost), relative skill versus persistence became positive for most pollutants at 6 h, but remained horizon and pollutant-dependent thereafter. Direct D+1 forecasts achieved modest skill (R² = -0.27 to 0.22), with persistence matching or exceeding XGBoost for four of five indicators, SO2 excepted. Event-based validation showed usable detection for PM2.5 and NO2 (POD 0.67-0.85 and 0.75-0.87 respectively) but XGBoost detected none of 39 ozone exceedances at the WHO threshold, versus 64% for persistence. These results show machine-learning value is horizon and pollutant-dependent, not automatic: persistence remains highly competitive, and for ozone superior. The contribution is methodological: season-balanced validation, horizon/averaging-period reconciliation, and event-based validation against naive baselines.

verified_metadata.title: Forecasting Urban Heat Island hotspots using spatially aware machine learning: Explainable multi-model prediction with spatial validation and uncertainty analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban Heat Island (UHI) hotspot forecasting is essential for proactive climate-resilient urban planning, yet existing machine learning approaches often overlook spatial dependence, temporal dynamics, and prediction uncertainty. This study proposes a spatio-temporal GeoAI framework for forecasting future UHI hotspot distributions in Gautam Buddha Nagar (Noida–Greater Noida), India, using multi-temporal Landsat observations from 2018, 2020, 2023, and 2025. Five environmental variables, namely the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), and UHI intensity, were derived using Google Earth Engine(GEE). To characterize the spatial structure of urban thermal patterns, the framework integrates Global Moran’s I, Getis–Ord Gi*, and Ripley’s L-function, providing complementary assessments of spatial autocorrelation, hotspot localization, and multi-scale clustering. Spatial-lag and temporal-change (Δ) features were further engineered to explicitly capture neighbourhood interactions and temporal evolution. Five forecasting models representing feature-based (Random Forest and XGBoost) and sequence-based (LSTM, Transformer, and SSM-Mamba) learning paradigms were evaluated using ten independent random seeds. Performance was assessed using Accuracy, Macro-F1, Cohen’s κ, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). XGBoost achieved the best overall performance, attaining an Accuracy of 98.9%, Macro-F1 of 0.924, Cohen’s κof 0.881, and MCC of 0.883. Ablation experiments showed that focal loss improved the sequence models; spatial-lag features were retained to represent neighbourhood conditions. SHAP analysis identified built-up intensity, vegetation, neighbourhood interactions, and temporal-change variables as the main associations used by the models of hotspot evolution. Agreement between SHAP explanations and Getis–Ord Gi∗ maps was moderate. A multi-model consensus layer, checked on labelled 2025 cells, was applied to a 2027 projection. No ground truth exists for 2027, so that map is an unvalidated scenario. The framework is an interpretable, spatially checked forecasting audit for this district.

verified_metadata.title: Nonlinear and heterogeneous effects of 2D/3D factors on global urban heat island using explainable spatial machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Although global research communities widely acknowledge the significant challenges posed by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, existing studies seldom simultaneously investigate the nonlinear and spatially non-stationary effects of 2D/3D factors on Surface UHI Intensity (SUHII) at the global scale. This study employed an explainable spatial machine learning framework that integrates Geographically Weighted Random Forests (GW-RF) and Shapley values to explore the complex effects of 2D/3D factors on SUHII across 2488 cities worldwide. Results reveal that mean SUHII varied significantly across continents, ranging from 1.201 °C in Africa to 2.121 °C in North America. Among 2D factors, rural vegetation ratio and urban impervious surface fraction are the most important drivers of SUHII, whereas among 3D factors, rural elevation and urban building height variability are the most important. Nonlinear analysis indicates that the percentage of urban building footprint has a positive effect on SUHII when it exceeds 16%, whereas building height variability exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship, with positive effects mainly between 3 and 10 m. Spatially non-stationary analysis indicated that urban impervious surface fraction has a greater influence in Eastern North America, Eastern Asia, and Central South America, whereas rural vegetation ratio exerts a stronger influence in European and Asian cities. Furthermore, urban irregularity has a strong effect in megacities, and the percentage of building footprint is influential in inland cities. These insights support the design of targeted, localized measures to counteract UHI.

verified_metadata.title: A comparative machine learning assessment for urban flood susceptibility modeling and future flood susceptibility projections in Dhaka Metropolitan Area (DMA), Bangladesh
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid urbanization and changing rainfall patterns are exacerbating flood-related issues in growing megacities. This study assessed flood susceptibility considering 17 Sentinel-1 flood events, 1451 modeling samples, and 13 conditioning factors to compare three standard ML models (Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM) with spatial cross-validation. Model interpretation was informed by SHAP and accumulated local effects. Scenario-based projections through 2060 under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 were supported by four climate models from CMIP6 and CA-Markov land-cover simulations. In the reported classifier comparison, LightGBM achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.969 and an F1-score of 0.861, with a mean spatial cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.954. The primary predictive factors were elevation, rainfall, and nearness to rivers. In the baseline scenario, 35.01% of Dhaka was highly and very highly susceptible. Projected built-up coverage increased from 63% in 2040 to 76.1% in 2060. In 2051-2060, high and very high susceptibility shares were reported as 38.82% under SSP2-4.5 and 45.01% under SSP5-8.5, with persistent concentrations in the eastern and southeastern parts of Dhaka. Long-term interpretation is limited by uncertainties in land-cover hindcasting, climate projections, and unrepresented drainage operations. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrated geospatial modeling to identify flood susceptibility hotspots and support climate-resilient urban planning through flood-sensitive zoning, wetland conservation, and targeted drainage improvements.

verified_metadata.title: Temporal non-stationarity limits urban heat model transferability: Evidence from interpretable spatial machine learning across ten highly urbanized bay areas (1990–2022)
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban heat assessments inform long-term land-use and adaptation decisions, yet the relationships on which they rely may change as cities evolve. We examined the temporal stability of land surface temperature (LST) relationships across ten highly urbanized bay areas during 1990–2022, using seven historical stages, 70 spatially validated XGBoost–SHAP models and 210 forward-transfer tests. Results show that: (1) Mean hot-season LST increased in nine bay areas, with endpoint changes ranging from −0.5 to +5.4 °C. (2) Five bay areas experienced changes in their dominant predictors. Natural-surface importance was higher on average in Global North cases (p = 0.063), whereas topographic importance was higher in Global South cases (p = 0.032). (3) Nonlinear SHAP contribution positions varied across historical stages, while clustering identified two broad long-term predictor pathways. (4) Of the 210 forward transfers, 208 underperformed their paired target-stage models. Mean R² was 0.434 versus 0.876, a difference of −0.442 (95% bay-bootstrap confidence interval −0.643 to −0.279). Intercept recalibration increased mean R² to 0.788, although 207 transfers still underperformed, with a residual difference of −0.088 (−0.122 to −0.059). Explanatory structures showed partial persistence, with mean Top-3 overlap of 0.706 and rank correlation of 0.748. Overall, these findings reveal that historical LST models can retain recognizable explanatory structures while experiencing substantial losses in predictive accuracy. Regular evaluation of historical models against updated thermal observations can inform model recalibration and support more responsive urban heat adaptation planning.

title: Manipulating starch crystalline structure for controlled digestibility and glycemic response
abstract: Postprandial hyperglycemia is a key driver in the development of type 2 diabetes, and dietary starch is a major modulator of glycemic response. The crystalline structure of starch is a principal determinant of its digestibility and postprandial glycemic response. This review synthesizes evidence establishing that the molecular packing density and stability of A-, B-, and V-type crystals often outweigh the influence of crystallinity or crystalline type alone in governing digestion resistance. We demonstrate how advanced processing techniques can precisely engineer these structural features to reduce starch digestibility. While in vitro models provide valuable mechanistic insights and animal studies elucidate underlying metabolic pathways, human trials consistently show significant individual variability in glycemic responses to crystalline transformations. This discrepancy underscores the limitation of a one-size-fits-all approach and highlights the necessity of integrating human data for meaningful predictions. Finally, we discuss the promising convergence of artificial intelligence and food structure engineering, such as 3D printing, as a transformative strategy for designing personalized low-glycemic-index foods based on tailored starch crystalline architectures. This work provides a timely synthesis to guide future research and practical applications in functional foods and diabetes management.

title: Protein-starch interaction in encapsulation systems: From functional group distribution to physicochemical and release properties
abstract: Protein-starch complexes are increasingly applied in the food and related industries as encapsulation matrices, such as pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals, for their ability to stabilize, protect, improving bioavailability and enabling controlled release of sensitive bioactive compounds, thereby enhancing product shelf-life, sensory attributes, and nutritional value. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the physicochemical foundations, molecular interactions (based on molecular dynamics simulations), and functional group distribution of protein-starch complexes, with emphasis on their application as wall materials in delivery systems. Subsequently, the review highlights key physicochemical, thermal, and release behaviors of protein-starch-based delivery systems. Finally, it outlines emerging strategies in controlled design, release modulation, and matrix engineering as promising solutions for developing next-generation carriers of bioactive compounds. Protein-starch interactions significantly influence solubility, thermal stability, emulsification properties, retrogradation behavior at a complex formation level, and the physiochemical properties (particle size, surface charge and morphology, and interface properties) and encapsulation efficiency of bioactive compounds. These biopolymeric matrices show strong potential for stimuli-responsive (pH and enzyme) and site-specific release in the gastrointestinal tract. Future research should emphasize hybrid systems, responsive architectures, and AI-based wall material formulations to enhance the stability and functionality of encapsulated nutraceuticals.

title: Emerging strategies for polysaccharide modification and functional enhancement in food systems
abstract: Polysaccharides, the most abundant natural biopolymers, exhibit outstanding biocompatibility and versatile functionality, making them valuable for applications in food, biomedicine and sustainable packaging. However, their native forms often suffer from limitations such as poor mechanical strength, thermal instability and rapid enzymatic degradation, which hinder broader industrial applications. This review critically examines recent advances in emerging modification techniques such as high-pressure processing, microwave treatment and cold plasma, etc., for enhancing the structural and functional properties of polysaccharides. Influence of modifications on rheological behavior, emulsification, hydrophobicity and gelation capacity were addressed, enabling advanced applications such as 3D-printing, plant-based meat structuring and controlled bioactive delivery. Special attention is given to green and sustainable modification strategies especially valorization of agri-food waste. Furthermore, the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) and molecular dynamics in predicting structure-function relationships are discussed, paving the way for data-driven design of polysaccharide-based materials. Despite these advancements, challenges remain in integrating modification techniques across disciplines and understanding their interactions within real food matrices. The unified framework addressing these challenges, emphasizing the need for scalable green technologies, life cycle assessments and AI-enabled digital twins are also proposed. This perspective positions modified polysaccharides as pivotal components of future clean label for multifunctional food systems, which are aligned well with circular bioeconomy goals.

title: Molecular mechanism and structure-activity relationships of natural source polysaccharides in intervening type 2 diabetes mellitus through antioxidant effects: A systematic review
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T 2 DM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder closely associated with oxidative stress. Natural source polysaccharides (NSPs) show great potential in T 2 DM management due to their remarkable antioxidant activity and favourable biosafety. This review systematically elaborates the multi-target mechanisms and structure-activity relationships of NSPs against T 2 DM. Key mechanisms include regulating oxidative stress, modulating insulin/PI3K/Akt signalling, inhibiting α-glucosidase/α-amylase, protecting pancreatic β-cells, and improving hepatic lipid metabolism. Furthermore, through cluster analysis and structural visualization, we delineate the critical influence of molecular weight, monosaccharide composition, and glycosidic bond types on antioxidant efficacy. Specifically, low-molecular-weight NSPs with high solubility and bioavailability often exhibit superior activity. Polysaccharides rich in glucose, galactose, or galacturonic acid demonstrate enhanced antioxidant effects, while diverse glycosidic bonds contribute to varied functional patterns through synergistic interactions with other structural features. This work provides a theoretical foundation for the precise application of NSPs in anti-diabetic therapeutics and functional foods. Future research should integrate multidimensional structural analysis, dynamic conformation monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted design to accelerate their clinical translation.

title: Predicting acetalated dextran nanoparticle features: Controlled synthesis, formulation, and testing in a high-throughput process
abstract: The hydrophobic, pH-labile, and biodegradable acetalated dextran (Ac(e)Dex) is a promising material for drug delivery in nanomedicine. However, fundamental knowledge about the structure-property relationships is still missing, which hinders its application in preclinical and clinical trials. In this study, we synthesized a library of 36 Ac(e)Dex derivatives with different molar masses, types, and degrees of functionalization. A high-throughput formulation screening (> 1000 formulations) was conducted using a liquid handling robot optimizing the concentration of polymer, the solvent, and the addition of additives. Selected formulations were scaled up and evaluated for their stability. To further correlate polymer properties with stability, a machine learning (ML) model was developed, providing a predictive tool for Ac(e)Dex nanoparticle degradation based on synthesis/formulation data. The novelty of this work lies in the integrated synthesis-to-prediction pipeline combining controlled polymer synthesis, high-throughput formulation, and ML-based stability modeling, rather than introducing new chemical mechanisms. By eludicating how structural parameters (molar mass, type, and degree of functionalization) influence formulation properties (i.e., size, dispersity, repeatability) and particle stability, this work enables standardized comparisons of Ac(e)Dex between different studies and supports its future preclinical development.

title: Unlocking the potential of functional food polysaccharides: The zebrafish model as a revolutionary high-throughput screening platform
abstract: Functional food polysaccharides (FFPs) offer significant health benefits, but their development is hampered by the limitations of cell-based models and the high cost of mammalian studies. The zebrafish model has emerged as a powerful screening platform, bridging the gap between in vitro and in vivo research by combining whole-organism biology with high-throughput capabilities. This review details a systematic zebrafish screening framework, covering model selection, polysaccharide administration routes, and multi-level activity assessment. We consolidate evidence of its utility in evaluating FFPs across key areas: immunomodulation, metabolic homeostasis, gut health, neuroprotection, and anti-tumor activity. While acknowledging translational challenges like anatomical differences, we summarize an integrated validation pipeline combining zebrafish, human cell models, and rodent studies to de-risk clinical development. Finally, we highlight how emerging technologies such as AI and CRISPR will further enhance mechanistic studies. We conclude that zebrafish are a cost-effective and efficient tool for accelerating the discovery of evidence-based functional foods derived from bioactive polysaccharides.

title: Quaternized polysaccharides: A focused review on molecular engineering, antimicrobial mechanisms, and advanced applications
abstract: The escalating threat of antibiotic resistance has intensified the search for sustainable antimicrobial alternatives. Quaternized polysaccharides, a class of cationic biopolymers derived from renewable biomass, offer significant potential due to their potent broad-spectrum activity, unique non-specific mechanisms, and excellent biocompatibility. This review systematically elucidates the molecular engineering of quaternized polysaccharides, covering diverse chemical modification strategies such as direct quaternization, etherification, graft copolymerization, and green synthesis pathways. A comprehensive analysis of multidimensional synergistic bactericidal mechanisms-encompassing electrostatic adsorption, membrane disruption, and intracellular targeting-is provided, alongside a detailed summary of structure-activity relationships governed by parameters like degree of substitution, alkyl chain length, and molecular weight. Furthermore, application-driven material designs in wound dressings, food packaging, water treatment, and medical coatings are highlighted. The discussion concludes by addressing critical challenges in precision synthesis and industrial translation while envisioning future frontiers, including smart-responsive systems and artificial intelligence-assisted design. This focused review provides a strategic roadmap for the rational design and development of high-performance polysaccharide-based antimicrobial materials.

title: An AI-informed framework for flavor design: How κ-carrageenan sculpts low-sodium myofibrillar protein architecture for aldehyde capture and bitterness masking
abstract: Designing healthy, palatable foods is a grand challenge in materials science, particularly in quest for low-sodium products where flavor is often compromised. The central problem is not merely replacing NaCl, but re-engineering the food matrix itself to manage off-flavors and retain desirable aromas. Here, an AI-informed framework demonstrates how the biopolymer κ-Carrageenan (KC) can sculpt the myofibrillar protein (MP) architecture for enhanced aldehyde capture and bitterness masking in low-sodium systems. Results showed KC acts as a molecular scaffold, transforming the protein from a rigid state into a porous, aggregated network. This remodeling significantly boosted binding for key flavor aldehydes (3-methylbutanal + , masking bitterness while enhancing saltiness and umami. To decipher this interplay, an interpretable machine learning model (R 2 > 0.9) quantitatively linked conformational changes to flavor. SHAP analysis then revealed aldehyde concentration, protein solubility, and thiol group availability as the most critical features governing aldehyde absorption and bitterness perception. This work pioneers a structure-driven, Al-based strategy for flavor design, offering a new paradigm for the rational formulation of next-generation healthy foods.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled flexible surface-enhanced Raman scattering substrate based on silver nanoparticles/polypyrrole/chitosan film for sensitive uric acid detection in saliva, serum and urine
abstract: Selective detection of uric acid (UA), a key biomarker associated with cardiovascular diseases, gout and preeclampsia, is important for preventive healthcare and accurate diagnosis. Conventional analytical methods often suffer from low sensitivity, rely on complex and expensive instrumentation. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has emerged as a powerful tool for non-invasive and highly sensitive detection of a wide range of molecules with their unique fingerprint information. Its high sensitivity arises from two cooperative mechanisms: electromagnetic enhancement, in which localized surface plasmon resonances in metallic nanostructures create intense near field "hotspots" that greatly amplify Raman scattering, and chemical enhancement, in which charge transfer interactions between the substrate and adsorbed molecules modify molecular polarizability and increase Raman cross sections. In this work, a flexible chitosan (CHT) film integrated with polypyrrole (PPy) nanowires and silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) was fabricated using a simple drop and peel-off method. By tuning the Ag precursor concentration, optimized hotspot formation was achieved. The synergistic effects of plasmonic Ag NPs, conductive PPy and biocompatible CHT generated strong Raman enhancement, enabling ultrasensitive UA detection. The flexible substrate exhibited an enhancement factor of ∼10 7 , a lower limit of detection (LOD) of 10 -9 M, uniformity and reproducibility with the relative standard deviation (RSD) values of <10%. Mechanical stability was verified after 100 cycles of bending and torsion. This platform enabled reliable UA detection in serum, saliva, and urine. Furthermore, coupling with artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms achieved precise UA quantification with excellent accuracy. This study presents an innovative approach that integrates flexible SERS substrates with AI for next-generation and non-invasive diagnostics.

title: Three-dimensional (3D) printing of cellulose/metal-organic frameworks (CelloMOFs)-based materials
abstract: The integration of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), cellulose-derived materials, and additive printing presents a robust approach for producing tailored, high-performance porous structures. MOFs offer a remarkably high active area, adjustable porosity, and chemical functionality; however, their limited processability and mechanical fragility hinder commercial application. Cellulose and its derivatives mitigate these issues by providing sustainability, enhanced mechanical strength, adjustable rheology, and a diverse range of surface chemistries. This review highlights developments in the three-dimensional (3D) printing of cellulose/MOF (CelloMOF) composites. It focuses on strategies to customize the structural, mechanical, and functional attributes of 3D-printed cellulose/MOF composite materials. 3D printing methodologies, e.g., extrusion-based printing, direct ink writing (DIW, or robocasting), and inkjet/reactive inkjet printing, are examined in conjunction with ex situ and in situ strategies for MOF integration. The utilization of 3D-printed CelloMOF composites in biological, electrical, textile, environmental, and energy sectors is emphasized. Furthermore, the existing constraints regarding printability, stability, and scalability are examined, and prospective advancements facilitated by artificial intelligence (AI) in the exploration, design, and enhancement of MOFs and printable composite systems are highlighted. Collectively, these advancements may advance 3D-printed cellulose/MOF composites as a viable foundation for next-generation functional and sustainable materials.

title: Precise design of clean-label starch: Mechanisms underlying the regulation of multiscale structure induced by non-thermal physical modification
abstract: Amid the global shift toward clean-label and sustainable food production, this review highlights green, non-thermal physical modification (NTPM) technologies such as high hydrostatic pressure (HHP), ultrasonic (US), cold plasma (CP), magnetic field (MF), pulsed electric field (PEF), γ-irradiation (IR), and along with other emerging techniques, as promising alternatives to conventional chemical and thermal starch modification methods. These approaches enable precise, multiscale structural regulation of starch from molecular chains to crystalline and morphological levels. The review elucidates how physical field energy modulates, by perturbing hydrogen bond networks, depolymerizing chains, and reconstructing crystalline order, key functional properties such as gelatinization, rheology, gel network formation, and digestion kinetics. It further establishes quantitative structure-property relationships within the physical field-structure-function paradigm, and discusses the potential of modified starches to support gut microbiota health and low glycemic index (GI) food development through controlled digestibility. Key knowledge gaps remain in mechanistic elucidation, scale-up, and the synergistic effects of combined technologies, which await direct experimental validation. Future directions include integrating hurdle strategies, advanced in-situ characterization, and machine learning-based predictive modeling. This review provides a scientific roadmap toward healthier and more sustainable food systems through the advancement of clean-label starches.

title: Recent advances in smart responsive actuators based on chitosan materials
abstract: Smart responsive actuators, as the core component of modern detection and sensing technology, harness unique stimuli-perception and self-adaptive deformation abilities, enabling precise signal capture and intelligent conversion. Owing to intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability and modifiability, chitosan has become an ideal available matrix for construction of smart actuators, exhibiting great using potential in fields of biomedical engineering, soft robots, wearable health monitoring and human-computer interaction. This paper reviews recent advances in chitosan-based smart actuators, including matrix materials forms (stimuli-responsive gels and shape memory polymers), stimuli types such as moisture, pH, light, heat, electricity and magnetism, applications in fields of biomedical engineering, soft robots and real-time monitoring, current challenges and develop trends. In future, functional optimization of chitosan, integration of interdisciplinary technologies and combining artificial intelligence might achieve the focus, promoting the developments of actuators toward precision, minimally invasive and modularization.
