title: Heterogeneous graph neural networks for building attribute prediction from hierarchical urban features and cross-view imagery
abstract: Data on building properties are essential for a variety of urban applications, yet such information remains scarce in many parts of the world. Recent efforts have leveraged instruments such as machine learning (ML), computer vision (CV), and graph neural networks (GNNs) to assess these properties at scale by leveraging urban features or visual information. However, extracting holistic representations to infer building attributes from multi-modal data across multiple spatial scales and vertical building characteristics remains a significant challenge. To bridge this gap, we present a innovative framework, that captures both hierarchical urban features and cross-view visual information through a heterogeneous graph. First, we construct a heterogeneous graph that incorporates multi-dimensional urban elements — buildings, streets, intersections, and urban plots — to comprehensively represent multi-scale geospatial features. Second, we automatically crop images of individual buildings from both very high-resolution satellite and street-level imagery, and introduce feature propagation on semantic similarity graphs to supplement missing facade information. Third, feature fusion is applied to integrate both morphological and visual features, with holistic representations generated for building attribute prediction. Systematic experiments across three global cities demonstrate that our method outperforms existing CV, ML, and homogeneous GNN-based models, achieving classification accuracies of 86% to 96% across 10 to 12 distinct building types, with mean F1 scores ranging from 0.70 to 0.73. The framework demonstrates robustness to class imbalance and produces more distinctive embeddings for ambiguous categories. In additional task of inferring building age, the method delivers similarly strong performance. This framework advances scalable approaches for filling gaps in building attribute data and offers new insights into modeling holistic urban environments. Our dataset and code are available openly at: https://github.com/seshing/HeteroGNN-building-attribute-prediction .

title: TLNet: A deep learning framework for tree detection in forest point clouds using multi-layered forest structure
abstract: Individual-tree detection underpins forest inventory, growth monitoring, silvicultural planning, and disturbance assessment. Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) provides the 3D structure needed for this task; however, severe occlusion, irregular and range-dependent point density, and platform-dependent sampling geometry and visibility still hinder consistent performance across sites and sensors. We present Tree-Layer Network (TLNet), a deep learning framework that addresses these challenges by slicing forest point clouds into a stack of thin horizontal slabs that mirror the natural multi-layered organization of forest strata (understory, midstory, and overstory). Within each slab, 3D points are embedded via sparse-voxel convolutions and mapped onto a 2D grid of local features. To capture vertical context, TLNet fuses these grid feature maps in two directions: a bottom-up pass that propagates stable stem and lower-crown cues upward, and a top-down pass that injects overstory information downward. Learnable scalar gates adaptively re-weight each slab’s grid features to emphasize the most informative forest layers, and a lightweight decoder predicts a tree-location heatmap and coordinate offsets for precise localization. To mitigate limited real-world labels, we pre-train TLNet on fully labeled synthetic forests and fine-tune on datasets from three LiDAR platforms: terrestrial laser scanning, mobile laser scanning, and unmanned aerial vehicle-borne laser scanning. Across both coniferous- and deciduous-dominated sites, TLNet attains an average F1 score (harmonic mean of precision and recall) greater than 0.88, outperforming three point-based deep-learning backbones and three platform-specialized heuristic detectors. These results suggest improved cross-platform consistency and accurate stem localization for downstream inventory and silvicultural analyses.

title: Automatic tree-level based forest inventories retrieval via ultra-high resolution UAV images and deep learning
abstract: Forest inventories play an essential role in managing and protecting forest resources as well as quantifying carbon stocks. Recent advances in Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have enhanced capabilities for efficiently monitoring forest dynamics across large geographic areas. RGB cameras are typically preferred for rapid and scalable forest inventory missions owing to three distinct advantages, including low cost, ease of use, and high resolution. However, compared with multispectral or hyperspectral sensors, the limited spectral signals of RGB cameras pose challenges for tree crown detection and classification. The ability of deep learning methods to capture structural and contextual cues from imagery helps alleviate some of the limitations of RGB data. In this study, we propose an Individual Tree Crown (ITC)-based framework leveraging UAV data and advanced deep learning models for inventories of individual trees in dense and natural forests. First, we develop the ITC-based Multi-Task Convolutional Neural Network (ITCMNet), which incorporates multi-scale contexts to simultaneously and accurately identify individual tree crowns, discriminate tree species, and assess tree vitality. Second, structural parameters for each individual crown are extracted to estimate forest carbon storage using species-specific allometric models. Unlike conventional pixel-based methods, our proposed ITCMNet enables precise forest investigations at the ITC level, enhancing both performance and interpretability. We collected a comprehensive dataset consisting of 2456 ultra-high resolution (1.6 cm) UAV RGB images and 27,160 labeled trees across 105 plots distributed in three dense forests and one city park in Germany to evaluate our framework. The ITCMNet demonstrated robust tree crown delineation performance, achieving an F1 score of 0.81. Additionally, our method attained an F1 score in species classification (i.e., 0.54 for angiosperms and 0.76 for gymnosperms) and vitality identification (0.66). Utilizing precise tree parameters, species information, and species-specific allometric models, our carbon storage estimation surpassed current satellite-based carbon products. The carbon stock estimation achieved an R 2 of 0.83 and the carbon storage range in the Bamberg forests is approximately 50 to 110 Mg C/ha. These results show that our proposed framework provides detailed, cost-effective forest inventories, highlighting its potential to support various downstream forestry applications. The dataset and source code are available ( https://www.dlr.de/en/eoc/about-us/remote-sensing-technology-institute/photogrammetry-and-image-analysis/public-datasets/bamforests ; https://github.com/WendyFan52/ITCMNet ).

verified_metadata.title: Mapping snow algae in West Antarctic Peninsula from Sentinel-2 images using a machine learning based approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Snow algae are crucial terrestrial carbon sinks and light-absorbing impurities in Antarctica. However, the distribution of snow algae across the West Antarctic Peninsula (WAP) remains poorly understood due to their high spatiotemporal variability and complex polar imaging conditions. This study develops a robust, large-scale mapping framework for green and red snow algae using machine learning. Our approach outperformed traditional spectral-index and spectral-unmixing methods across multiple challenging scenes, with the Kappa score improving from 0.51 and 0.49 to 0.82. By synthesizing 2676 Sentinel-2 images, the 2019–2024 composite distribution of WAP snow algae and the interannual variability of bloom intensity were assessed. Results reveal a total bloom area of 54.34 km2, and uncover significant negative association between bloom intensity and the Antarctic Oscillation index. This research establishes a novel, transferable tool for mapping snow algae in cryosphere systems and provides a baseline for evaluating their ecological implications in a changing climate.

title: Spatiotemporal CNN framework for quantifying crop-specific salinity damage in coastal agriculture
abstract: Coastal delta agricultural systems are facing severe threats from saltwater intrusion (SWI), which further impacts global food security. However, how to accurately and timely assess the vulnerability of coastal agriculture to SWI at a regional scale remains challenging. Most existing methods rely on either manually-designed multi-index systems or the identification of severely salinized areas, resulting in high uncertainties and more granular crop-scale evaluations. Meanwhile, they remain inadequate for early-risk warning, as initial crop canopy obscures the underlying soil spectral signatures critical for early SWI detection. Critically, two unresolved issues persist regarding the effects of crop cover on SWI: the objective quantification of early-stage SWI impacts at the field scale under crop cover conditions, and the variation along with precise measurement of differential SWI responses across crop types. Taking the Po Delta in Italy as an example-a well-known hotspot affected by SWI but with unknown quantification, we proposed a crop damage probability assessment framework fully driven by machine learning and satellite imageries. Based on crop classification, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was employed to quantify the probability of SWI effects. Furthermore, this method enables crop damage probability mapping during early-stage SWI upon each satellite revisit. This study presents the first application of CNN to generate crop-specific, monthly mappings of SWI impacts on coastal agriculture, addressing a critical gap in early and objective damage quantification. The results indicated that the CNN-based algorithm enabled quantitative risk assessment of crop damage from saltwater intrusion on a monthly scale. During the saltwater intrusion period (May-September), the CNN-based model achieved an identification accuracy of 82.4% to 92.5% in damaged agricultural areas based on known episodes of salinization, and the quantitative risk maps of crop damage can be used to reveal agricultural hotspots threatened by saltwater intrusion. Analysis of crop-specific damage probability showed that the highest risk occurs in June and July, followed by a gradual decline, with alfalfa in the Po River Delta experiencing the greatest risk. The proposed framework avoided subjective judgment while delivering crop-scale quantification of potential SWI effects on agricultural systems, serving as a preliminary tool for early detection of vulnerable areas and supporting timely management and mitigation strategies.

verified_metadata.title: A soybean mapping framework via multi-index-derived pseudo-label enhancement and contrastive embedding neural network
verified_metadata.abstract: Soybean is one of the most important oilseed crops globally, serving as a key ingredient in soy-based foods, meat alternatives, and animal feed. Accurate and timely monitoring of its spatial distribution is critical for ensuring food security and promoting the formulation of mutually beneficial international trade policies. However, large-scale mapping continues to face two major practical challenges: (i) index-based methods exhibit limited transferability across regions and years due to their sensitivity to threshold setting, and (ii) classifier-based methods are constrained by the scarcity, high acquisition cost, and potential inaccuracy of training samples. We propose a fully label-free soybean mapping framework that combines multi-index pseudo-label generation and the Pseudo-label Enhanced Contrastive Embedding Network (PEACE-Net). Pseudo-labels are generated by applying a majority voting mechanism to three well-validated soybean indices (GWCCI, GWCCI2, and SMCI), which collectively capture a broad spectrum of discriminative features of soybean, with cross-validation implemented across the indices to enhance reliability. PEACE-Net is a dual-head Transformer architecture incorporating a soft probability update mechanism: (i) a contrastive head that constructs a discriminative embedding space, and (ii) a classification head whose soft outputs iteratively refine pseudo-labels, thereby progressively reducing the risk of overfitting under weak supervision. The framework was evaluated across five representative sites in the United States, Brazil, Argentina, and China from 2021 to 2024, and through three large-scale regional mapping experiments. Multi-index pseudo-labels demonstrated more accurate and stable performance than single-index labels. PEACE-Net outperformed baseline methods (RF, DCM, and Transformer) across sites and years, achieving an average OA of 90.72% and F1-score of 0.91, with balanced Precision and Recall. Large-scale regional mapping in three areas shows a strong linear correlation (R2 > 0.90) between mapped soybean area and county-level data, closely matching official records. These findings underscore the significant potential of the proposed framework for large-scale soybean mapping at both regional and global scales. By integrating the complementary strengths of index-based and classifier-based methods, the framework achieves fully automated, end-to-end, and label-free mapping with high efficiency and precision.

verified_metadata.title: A semi-supervised deep learning framework based on multi-source data for wheat: from counting to yield estimation
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient quantification of wheat ears and spike grains is crucial for yield estimation but is currently hindered by the heavy reliance on labor-intensive manual annotations and complex field environments. There is also no unified approach for the simultaneous segmentation and counting of wheat ears and spike grains. To address these issues, this study proposed a semi-supervised deep learning framework for wheat. First, we constructed a Wheat Segment Anything Model (Wheat-SAM), which integrates adapters and is fine-tuned on a large-scale dataset of wheat ear and spike grain images to generate high-quality training samples. Subsequently, we developed the Wheat Segmentation and Counting U-Net (WSCU-Net), an innovative dual-task framework that combines Depthwise Separable Convolutions (DSConv) and Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA), enabling simultaneous segmentation and counting of wheat ears and spike grains. Specifically, we fine-tuned Wheat-SAM to generate pseudo labels, which were subsequently used to train WSCU-Net. The trained WSCU-Net was then employed to predict segmentation masks and count outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that the fine-tuned Wheat-SAM achieved the highest segmentation accuracy across multiple scales and maintained stable performance under different prompt modes, confirming its capability in generating high-quality pseudo annotations. Furthermore, the semi-supervised WSCU-Net trained on pseudo labels outperformed other dual-stage fusion methods in both segmentation and counting tasks, achieving an IoU of 0.8409 and a Coefficient of Determination (R2) of 0.766, approaching the performance of fully supervised models. Notably, WSCU-Net maintained robust performance across different wheat cultivars, highlighting its applicability in diverse field scenarios. Preliminary correlation analysis between the predicted count results and actual yield showed a strong positive statistical relationship, with an average Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.6918. Our approach provides valuable insights into leveraging foundation models in wheat phenotyping tasks and holds great promises for intelligent wheat yield estimation. It offers strong support for wheat breeding, remote sensing yield prediction, and other smart agriculture applications.

verified_metadata.title: A spherical-harmonic deep learning framework for generic tree morphology and species identification
verified_metadata.abstract: Tree biodiversity is declining at an unprecedented pace, threatening forest ecosystems and their ecological functions. Reliable tree species identification is essential for monitoring biodiversity change and developing strategies to mitigate further losses; however, spectral intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, and the structural complexity of trees continue to hinder tree species identification by intelligent algorithms. Herein, we constructed a generalized framework from a transdisciplinary perspective to characterize tree morphology, based exclusively on LiDAR data for tree species identification. First, we devised multiple point cloud projection strategies and radial manifold-derived geometric features in spherical space to comprehensively depict tree morphogenesis. Second, we developed an innovative deep learning model based on spherical harmonics and the rotation group SO(3) to explore the structural commonalities for each tree species and identify tree species across mesoscale forest landscapes. By analysing point clouds of nearly 200,000 trees from 59 species, we demonstrated that our framework has the ability to capture the spatial clustering behaviour of foliage clumps, the uneven appearance of tree crowns, and the canopy architectures of diverse trees. Our framework achieved species identification overall accuracies of 85.42% on the Chinese dataset and 85.03% on the FOR-species20K dataset, surpassing state-of-the-art deep learning approaches by 5.19% and 5.02%, respectively. The results present the effectiveness of our framework as a robust tool for assessing forest diversity at both community and ecosystem levels and have the potential to be applied to larger geographical regions.

title: GeoSight v2: strengthening disaster impact assessment with coordinate referencing, inpainting, and similarity models
abstract: Post-disaster imagery collected by communities and field teams provides critical visual evidence for assessing damage and guiding emergency responses. However, the geocoordinates embedded in these images often capture the camera’s location rather than the position of the depicted building, introducing spatial misalignment that reduces mapping accuracy and weakens machine learning–based decision support. To address this challenge, we present an enhanced version of GeoSight, a geolocation refinement framework that integrates three key components: (i) coordinate referencing to constrain candidate search areas, (ii) building detection with inpainting to isolate structures and remove unrelated objects such as vehicles and debris, and (iii) perceptual similarity analysis using DreamSim to match query images against a georeferenced database. Using NOAA’s 2023 Norman, Oklahoma tornado building-damage imagery, the enhanced framework improves retrieval accuracy from 53% to 67% (Top-1) and 77% to 84% (Top-3), while reducing average geolocation errors by 26.1 m, with maximum corrections up to 46.5 m. By combining coordinate data, object-level preprocessing, and perceptual similarity, this framework provides a scalable and generalizable approach for refining the geolocation of community-driven disaster imagery, enabling more accurate and timely damage mapping for disaster response and recovery.

title: A continual evolving Visual-Inertial Odometry for drones in flight
abstract: Deep learning-based Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) algorithms for drones show great application potential, but their model parameters are typically fixed and cannot be optimized online during flight. These fixed models lack the ability to self-evolve to changes in drone flight scenarios, leading to significant fluctuations in positioning accuracy. To address this limitation, we propose Evolvable VIO (E-VIO), a novel approach that enables real-time online training and inference on flying drones. Our approach leverages a robust dual-replay-memory continual learning strategy to facilitate efficient online adaptation, while a minimalist Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer cascade backbone ensures low computational complexity. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that under changing environmental conditions, E-VIO improves the average positioning accuracy by 84.60% compared to fixed-model VIO. Furthermore, it maintains real-time performance with an inference speed of 21.2 fps and an online training speed of 5.0 fps on an edge computing platform. To benefit the community, we make the source code publicly available.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Ranking-aware continual learning for LiDAR place recognition
abstract: Place recognition plays a significant role in SLAM, robot navigation, and autonomous driving applications. Benefiting from deep learning, the performance of LiDAR place recognition (LPR) has been greatly improved. However, many existing learning-based LPR methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting, which severely harms the performance of LPR on previously trained places after training on a new environment. In this paper, we introduce a continual learning framework for LPR via Knowledge Distillation and Fusion (KDF) to alleviate forgetting. Inspired by the ranking process of place recognition retrieval, we present a ranking-aware knowledge distillation loss that encourages the network to preserve the high-level place recognition knowledge. We also introduce a knowledge fusion module to integrate the knowledge of old and new models for LiDAR place recognition. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that KDF can be applied to different networks to overcome catastrophic forgetting, surpassing the state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean Recall@1 and forgetting score.

title: MaOutCNN: A physical mechanism coupled MambaOut-CNN detection network with maiden-released interference polarized ship detection dataset
abstract: Unlike traditional ship detection, polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) intelligent ship detection faces the following critical challenges: inaccurate revelation of polarimetric responses, insufficient physical interpretable network and lack of consideration of complex electromagnetic environment. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physical mechanism coupled MambaOut-CNN network for PolSAR ship detection under complex interference scenarios. First , by arduously collecting six types of spaceborne and airborne real PolSAR data covering three mainstream frequency bands, this paper releases an interference polarized ship detection (IPSD) dataset for the first time, wherein four types of typical interferences are involved and a total of 934 samples are presented. Second , a regularized systematic polarimetric decomposition (RSPD) framework for ship targets is proposed. On the basis of introducing rotated dihedral and planar resonator scattering models unique to ships, by defining the hierarchical absolute dominant scattering principle and designing a simultaneous model inversion strategy, this decomposition framework achieves fine characterization of ship target scattering in terms of emphasis of its exclusive scattering. Finally , with physical prior of the RSPD, a physical mechanism coupled MaOutCNN ship detection network by designing CNN and MambaOut dual-branch inputs is proposed, which integrates multi-scale parallel, multi-branch convolution and dynamic feature fusion modules, and introduces a collaborative perception loss function. This guarantees a generalized and reliable detection of dense targets in near-port areas and widespread targets in open seas. Experimental results show that the proposed RSPD accurately reveals and outlines prominent the global and local structural scattering of ship targets. Moreover, compared with 12 advanced ship detection networks, MaOutCNN achieves the optimal detection performance on both the IPSD and non-interference datasets, with average detection accuracies of 89.7% and 94.2% respectively, which are 3.6% and 3.1% higher than the baseline model. In addition, the results of ablation experiments and heatmap visualization are also discussed. The dataset and benchmark are publicly available at https://github.com/zzandcc/ipsd.git .
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Benchmarking individual tree segmentation using multispectral airborne laser scanning data: The FGI-EMIT dataset
abstract: Individual tree segmentation (ITS) from LiDAR point clouds is fundamental for applications such as forest inventory, carbon monitoring and biodiversity assessment. Traditionally, ITS has been achieved with unsupervised geometry-based algorithms, while more recent advances have shifted toward supervised deep learning (DL). In the past, progress in method development was hindered by the lack of large-scale benchmark datasets, and the availability of novel data formats, particularly multispectral (MS) LiDAR, remains limited to this day, despite evidence that MS reflectance can improve the accuracy of ITS. This study introduces FGI-EMIT, the first large-scale multispectral airborne laser scanning (ALS) benchmark dataset for ITS. Captured at wavelengths 532, 905, and 1550 nm, the dataset consists of 1561 manually annotated trees from a variety of boreal forest environments, with a particular focus on small understory trees. Using FGI-EMIT, we comprehensively benchmarked four conventional unsupervised algorithms and four supervised DL approaches. Hyperparameters of unsupervised methods were optimized using a Bayesian approach, while DL models were trained from scratch. Among the unsupervised methods, Treeiso achieved the highest test set F1-score of 52.7%. The DL approaches performed significantly better overall, with the best model, ForestFormer3D, attaining an F1-score of 73.3%. The most significant difference was observed in understory trees, where ForestFormer3D exceeded Treeiso by 25.9 percentage points. An ablation study demonstrated that, under the tested input configuration, i.e., high-density MS ALS data combined with standard input concatenation strategies, current DL-based approaches may generally fail to effectively leverage reflectance information, although single-channel reflectance can yield marginal accuracy improvements, particularly for understory trees. A performance analysis across point densities further showed that DL methods consistently remain superior to unsupervised algorithms, even at densities as low as 10 points/m 2 . To support future benchmarking efforts and method development, we make the FGI-EMIT dataset publicly available ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19351234 ).
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

verified_metadata.title: Make more pixels usable: A data-driven framework for customizable cloud and shadow processing in satellite imagery
verified_metadata.abstract: Atmospheric interference, particularly cloud cover, remains a persistent challenge in the effective utilization of optical remote sensing imagery. Existing cloud processing methods either localize cloud positions or remove cloud interference but fail to adaptively process cloudy imagery, leading to substantial loss of valuable pixel information. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a data-driven framework for optimizing pixel utilization in satellite images. First, we proposed an adjustable cloud intensity index to quantify the interference of cloud and shadow, facilitating selective processing of different cloud pixels. Furthermore, a novel cloud simulation strategy was applied to Landsat-8 data, generating globally-distributed cloud samples and constructing the benchmark CloudL8-LC dataset. The CloudL8-LC dataset comprises over 5.2 billion pixels and has the widest coverage among the existing cloud datasets, and supports cloud detection, cloud removal, and adjustable cloud processing. Based on this dataset, we developed a single-image cloud intensity estimation network (SCIENet) equipped with a relevance-aware attention module (RAAM) and a gating-based channel-spatial feature pruner (GCSFP), both designed to accommodate the inherent variability of cloud formations. Once the cloud intensity index is predicted by SCIENet, the threshold can be flexibly adjusted to accommodate user-specific requirements, enabling customizable cloud and shadow processing within single imagery. Additionally, we introduced a suite of evaluation metrics to assess cloud-processing performance in terms of pixel quantity, quality, and practical utility. Extensive experiments demonstrated that the proposed cloud intensity index functions as a dynamic thresholding parameter for single-image cloud processing, enabling selective masking of highly contaminated pixels while reconstructing minimally affected regions. This provides users with tunable cloud processing solutions and exhibits robustness across diverse cloud types. Compared to cloud detection approaches, SCIENet significantly enhances pixel availability while maintaining reliable classification accuracy, ensuring consistent performance across various land-cover scenarios. Furthermore, in some real-world cloud conditions where the classic cFmask algorithm achieves a cloud detection precision below 70%, the proposed SCIENet model attains a precision of up to 90%. Additionally, relative to manually annotated masks, the SCIENet can increase the number of clear pixels by over 15%, making more pixels usable.

verified_metadata.title: Unsupervised anomaly localization with high-resolution and time-series satellite imagery: from global disaster dataset to zero-shot model via SAM
verified_metadata.abstract: The stable and balanced conditions of our living environment are upset by land surface disasters like earthquakes and floods, which frequently result in fatalities and wildly unpredictable damage. However, achieving generalizable damage localization for first-response humanitarian assistanc e poses significant challenges due to the diverse types of disaster scenes (e.g., urban, mountain, rural) and damaged objects (e.g., buildings, roads, croplands), none of which we can predict in advance. Most of existing studies are often limited to either certain disaster type or certain damage object type including both supervised and unsupervised models. To achieve a unified damage localization, we first propose a new unsupervised anomaly change detection paradigm for damage localization, which takes an arbitrary number of time steps and makes use of all previous images as a guide to differentiate between “anomaly changes” and “normal changes” brought on by sporadic human activity or changing imaging circumstances. This paradigm is motivated by the observation that catastrophic damages correlate with anomaly changes not seen in any historical image, without the need of any damage annotation and being damage-aware. We implement the paradigm as a zero-shot anomaly change detection model called AnomalyCD, which adapts the single-temporal foundation model (i.e., segment anything model (SAM)) for our task with designed feature-mask interaction. Proposed adaptation maps the segmented objects into feature space and conducts temporal comparison to calculate the change score with bi-temporal images and anomaly change score with all historical images. AnomalyCD is validated on the constructed global-scale dataset called GDL involving six disaster types and six damage types, which has multiple time steps (3–7), high resolution (0.15–2.39 m/pixel), and cover a large area (2052.82 km2 in total) collected globally. Without any training process, AnomalyCD have surpassed the best previous unsupervised methods by 7 points in F1 metric (from 42.66 to 50.27) and achieved comparable performance with supervised specialized models for certain damage type, emphasizing the ability of AnomalyCD to help national emergent agencies respond quickly to disasters. Code would be released at https://github.com/Jingtao-Li-CVer/AnomalyCD.

verified_metadata.title: Annual wetland changes across China (2016–2024) from multisource temporal data and knowledge-driven machine learning approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Timely and accurate data on wetland dynamics are crucial for effective conservation planning, policy implementation, and the achievement of sustainable development. However, obtaining high-resolution wetland change data at the national scale remains a significant challenge, with the lack of a comprehensive, long-term dataset for China. In this study, we present an enhanced wetland mapping framework that integrates multi-source temporal data with a prior knowledge-driven machine learning approach. By incorporating prior knowledge from the estimated probability of wetland occurrence, this method spatially constrains the potential distribution of wetlands, significantly boosting computational efficiency and reducing both misclassification and training data requirements. Leveraging over 2.59 million Sentinel images, we produced China’s annual 10-m resolution wetland change product for the period of 2016–2024, with an average overall accuracy of 81.72% (ranging from 80.55% to 82.17%). The results indicate that China’s total wetland area remained broadly stable from 2016 to 2024, with a marginal net gain of 0.5%. Water bodies showed the greatest interannual variability (1.23 × 103 km2) and expanded overall (+1.24%), while coastal swamps also increased slightly. By contrast, coastal marshes (−0.62 × 103 km2) and tidal flats (−0.71 × 103 km2) declined, inland marshes decreased marginally (−0.11%), and inland swamps exhibited no significant change. Regionally, the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau and Northeast China displayed the highest variability. This high-resolution, annually updated wetland dataset provides a critical resource for wetland conservation, restoration, and ecological management, and will play a pivotal role in supporting both national and global efforts to assess and achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

verified_metadata.title: An integrated machine learning approach for efficient gap-filling of cloudy Landsat LST imagery
verified_metadata.abstract: Cloud contamination causes substantial gaps in Landsat land surface temperature (LST) records, limiting their spatiotemporal continuity amid growing demand for long-term high-resolution thermal data. Despite progress, gap-filling Landsat LST remains challenging due to large spatiotemporal gaps, realistic under-cloud representation, and multi-source discrepancies. To address these challenges simultaneously, this study proposes an integrated machine learning approach that combines complementary strengths of spatial reference-based fusion and temporal reference-based interpolation in a simple yet efficient way. Specifically, the cost-efficient Light Gradient Boosting Machine model is employed as a unified architecture, into which key factors are jointly incorporated: the adjacent Landsat image (LR) as a high-resolution spatial anchor, annual temperature cycle pattern (ATC) as a physically-guided temporal baseline, surface-energy-balance-guided all-weather thermal changes bridging large temporal gaps under cloudy conditions, and synchronous environmental variables facilitating adaptive adjustment over heterogeneous surfaces. The method was evaluated on both simulated and actual cloudy Landsat images during 2017–2021 across SURFRAD regions. Results show consistent recovery of spatially complete, high-resolution thermal patterns with RMSEs of 0.99 K (satellite-based) and 2.01 K (ground-based). The accuracies are comparable to clear-sky Landsat products, superior to GOES LST under cloudy conditions, and outperform four representative methods, reducing RMSEs by 1.23–2.72 K (satellite-based) and 0.58–3.94 K (ground-based). Impact analyses confirm robustness under varied cloud cover and temporal gaps. Model interpretation reveals that LR and ATC dominate the learning process, while others provide secondary refinements, supporting the rationale, interpretability, and generalizability of the proposed approach. This study facilitates the generation of continuous high-resolution thermal datasets for diverse applications.

verified_metadata.title: Shallow-water reef detection driven by few-shot learning with airborne LiDAR bathymetry
verified_metadata.abstract: Shallow-water reefs play an important scientific and practical role in ensuring navigational safety and supporting marine aquaculture. However, traditional detection methods such as shipborne sonar and multibeam echo sounding face significant challenges in achieving high-precision detection. These challenges stem from complex reef morphology and grounding risks associated with unmanned surface vehicles. In contrast, airborne LiDAR bathymetry (ALB) provides an effective alternative, enabling non-contact, high-accuracy measurements over broad spatial extents. This study proposes a few-shot learning–based detection method using ALB data. It addresses challenges posed by large morphological variability and limited training samples in shallow-water reef detection. We developed upon an enhanced You Only Look Once version 10 (YOLOv10) framework, incorporating a Cross-Scale Attention Module (CSAM) to strengthen feature perception and representation. Moreover, a joint training strategy is employed to enhance model adaptability. This strategy integrates data augmentation with meta-learning to ensure robustness under few-shot scenarios. The proposed approach was validated using ALB data collected over Jiaozhou Bay, Qingdao, China. Experimental results under few-shot conditions (10 samples) show that the proposed method achieves a precision of 97.9% and a recall of 98.4%, demonstrating superior detection accuracy and stability compared with existing algorithms. These findings establish a reliable technical foundation for high-precision shallow-water reef detection in marine engineering and environmental monitoring applications. For benchmarking and reproducibility purposes, the constructed ReefFeat-Img dataset and the source code of the proposed method are publicly available at: https://github.com/biguanglu350/FSAM-YOLO.git.

title: Wetland mapping from sparse annotations with satellite image time series and temporal-aware segment anything model
abstract: Accurate wetland mapping is critical for ecosystem monitoring and management, yet acquiring dense pixel-level annotations is prohibitively costly. In practice, only sparse point labels are typically available. Existing deep learning-based models face significant challenges in capturing accurate wetland extents under such weak supervision, particularly when coupled with the strong seasonal dynamics of wetlands, which, meanwhile, makes single-date imagery insufficient and causing substantial omission and commission errors when mapping. Although powerful foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) provide promising generalization from point prompts, it is intrinsically designed for static natural images, resulting in spatially fragmented masks in heterogeneous wetland environments and cannot exploit satellite image time series. To address these challenges, we propose WetSAM, a novel SAM-based framework that effectively leverages satellite image time series to enhance wetland mapping from sparse point annotations. WetSAM adopts a dual-branch design: (1) The temporal branch extends SAM to learn temporal contexts from satellite image time series via hierarchical adapters and a dynamic temporal aggregation module. This branch equips SAM with the ability to capture and model temporal features of wetlands, allowing it to learn complex temporal patterns and phenological changes; (2) The spatial branch reconstructs distinct boundaries via a temporal-constrained region-growing strategy, iteratively expanding sparse points into reliable dense pseudo-labels; (3) A bidirectional consistency regularization enforces minimizing the discrepancy of the predictions from two segmentation heads of two branches. We validate the effectiveness of WetSAM across eight diverse global locations, each covering an area of around 5000 k m 2 and with various wetland types and geographical features. WetSAM reaches an average F1-score of 85.58%, considerably outperforming other state-of-the-art algorithms. Results demonstrate that WetSAM achieves accurate, structurally consistent segmentation from sparse labels. With minimal labeling effort, our framework shows strong generalization ability and holds promise for scalable, low-cost wetland mapping at high spatial resolutions.

verified_metadata.title: Sparse multimodal feature fusion transformer with frequency-convolution collaboration for wildlife multi-object tracking in UAV monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: Lightweight unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are gradually becoming important remote sensing tools for wildlife monitoring. Wildlife tracking using UAVs faces challenges, including small targets, highly similar appearances, and strong camouflage in natural environments. To address these issues, we propose a multimodal wildlife multi-object tracking model based on text–image feature fusion. First, the Density Multimodal Fusion (DTF) module combines spatial-density-guided sparse sampling with text priors to focus on high-density foregrounds while suppressing background redundancy. Second, the frequency-convolution collaborative encoder (LST-Encoder) performs spatially conditioned spectral modulation to enhance informative frequency components and preserve global semantics, improving discriminability for camouflaged and visually similar targets. Finally, the Hybrid-Decoder mitigates ID switches and identity fragmentation by integrating global spatiotemporal modeling with hierarchical identity modulation, maintaining cross-frame feature continuity and reinforcing identity-specific cues for stable long-sequence tracking. We validate our approach on the newly constructed MiluDrone dataset and public datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms several representative trackers, achieving a 4% increase in MOTA, a 3.7% increase in IDF1, and a 47% reduction in ID switches on the MiluDrone dataset. These results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework for challenging UAV-based wildlife monitoring scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/yzxhao123/De-MOTR.git.

verified_metadata.title: Deviation-guided dual-model machine learning SAR coherence change detection framework for extracting changes in low-coherence areas
verified_metadata.abstract: Coherence Change Detection (CCD) is a crucial technique for monitoring surface dynamics in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), and it has wide-ranging applications in natural disaster monitoring and urban analysis. However, conventional CCD methods based on dual-temporal coherence typically rely on a single coherence estimate for decision-making. This makes it difficult to effectively distinguish between decoherence caused by real surface changes and that induced by other factors, such as geometric decorrelation, temporal decorrelation, system noise, and co-registration inaccuracies. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel dual-model framework for coherence change detection that integrates machine learning with coherence and deviation modeling. The proposed framework first employs a machine learning (ML) model for coherence estimation, followed by a deviation prediction model that learns the mapping between statistical features and estimation errors. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method is then applied to interpret the deviation model. Based on the joint output of coherence and deviation estimates, a dual-threshold segmentation strategy is adopted to effectively extract low-coherence regions caused by genuine surface changes. Experimental results confirm the method’s robustness in small-sample and low-coherence scenarios. Validation with real-world data across different resolutions and scenarios confirms the method’s ability to accurately identify low-coherence regions caused by changes. By jointly utilizing coherence and deviation information, the proposed framework enhances detection accuracy and interpretability, providing a robust and reliable new CCD solution.

title: Geographically-weighted weakly supervised Bayesian High-Resolution Transformer for 200 m resolution pan-Arctic sea ice concentration mapping and uncertainty estimation using Sentinel-1, RCM, and AMSR2 data
abstract: Although high-resolution mapping of pan-Arctic sea ice with reliable corresponding uncertainty is essential for operational sea ice concentration (SIC) charting, it is a difficult task due to key challenges, such as the subtle nature of ice signature features, inexact SIC labels, model uncertainty, and data heterogeneity. This study presents a novel Bayesian High-Resolution Transformer approach for 200 meter resolution pan-Arctic SIC mapping and uncertainty quantification using Sentinel-1, RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM), and Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) data. First, to improve small and subtle sea ice feature (e.g., cracks/leads, ponds, and ice floes) extraction, we design a novel high-resolution Transformer model with both global and local modules that can better discern the subtle differences in sea ice patterns. Second, to address low-resolution and inexact SIC labels, we design a geographically-weighted weakly supervised loss function to supervise the model at region level instead of pixel level, and to prioritize pure open water and ice pack signatures while mitigating the impact of ambiguity in the marginal ice zone (MIZ). Third, to improve uncertainty quantification, we design a Bayesian extension of the proposed Transformer model, treating its parameters as random variables to more effectively capture uncertainties. Fourth, to address data heterogeneity, we fuse three different data types (Sentinel-1, RCM, and AMSR2) at decision-level to improve both SIC mapping and uncertainty quantification. The proposed approach is evaluated under pan-Arctic minimum-extent conditions in 2021 and 2025. Results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 0.70 overall feature detection accuracy using Sentinel-1 data, while also preserving pan-Arctic SIC patterns (Sentinel-1 R\textsuperscript{2} = 0.90 relative to the ARTIST Sea Ice product).

verified_metadata.title: Multimodal deep learning with aerial imagery and nDSM for true-slope-aware rooftop photovoltaic potential estimation
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate assessment of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) potential is essential for renewable energy planning and carbon-neutral urban development. Most existing studies rely on a single data modality: aerial image-based methods often lack true-slope information, while three-dimensional (3D) building model-based methods usually omit roof superstructures and their impact on installable area. These limitations can introduce systematic errors and lead to biased PV potential estimates. To address these challenges, we propose SolarFusion, an innovative multimodal deep learning framework for high-precision, true-slope-aware rooftop PV potential assessment. SolarFusion combines semantic features from RGB aerial imagery with geometric-spatial attributes from normalized digital surface model (nDSM) data. At its core is the FusionPIRNet architecture, which integrates the cross-modal multi-scale feature integration (CMFI) module for adaptive coupling of heterogeneous data and the continual fusion optimization (CFO) module for progressive refinement of fused features. Two high-quality RGB-D benchmark datasets, RID1-Depth (0.10 m/pixel nDSM) and RID2-Depth (0.08 m/pixel nDSM), are constructed to enable robust evaluation and introduce true-slope awareness into rooftop PV analysis. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SolarFusion outperforms state-of-the-art multimodal fusion methods in both rooftop parsing and PV potential estimation. In particular, SolarFusion achieves the lowest estimation error, reducing the annual solar potential estimation error by at least 98.85 MWh/year on RID1-Depth and 44.61 MWh/year on RID2-Depth. A city-wide case study in Munich, Germany (374 km2) further highlights the framework’s scalability, identifying an annual generation potential of 3.2 TWh and successfully handling diverse urban morphologies, including high-density districts with complex rooftop configurations.

verified_metadata.title: Towards comprehensive multi-task land cover change detection leveraging vision-language model and LLM-driven agents
verified_metadata.abstract: Land cover change detection is essential for assessing the impacts of urbanization on ecological systems and economic development. As urbanization accelerates, land cover changes involve both semantic transitions and structural modifications, substantially increasing the complexity of detection tasks. However, existing research has primarily focused on 2D change detection, with limited integration of multi-dimensional and multi-modal data. This limitation has restricted the effective modeling of inter-class transitions and spatial structural evolution. Moreover, most methods lack end-to-end pipelines adapted to real-world scenarios, constraining their capacity for comprehensive representation and quantitative impact assessment. To address these challenges, we introduce UrbanChange, the first dataset designed for multi-task (2D and 3D) land cover change detection. It integrates semantic and structural change maps from multi-sensor data with fine-grained change captions, providing a comprehensive foundation for evaluating and analyzing land cover transformations. Leveraging UrbanChange, we develop a vision–language model that directly infers multi-dimensional changes from optical imagery. We further develop GaiaAgent by incorporating this model as a core perception module, forming the agentic workflow for land cover change detection and analysis. GaiaAgent coordinates five task-specific agents in an automated pipeline for instruction interpretation, task decomposition, detection, and quantitative analysis. A Human-in-the-Loop mechanism is incorporated to produce interactive, interpretable reports, enhancing robustness in complex scenarios. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of GaiaAgent. On the UrbanChange dataset, GaiaAgent achieves a 3.9% improvement in F1 and a 0.35 m reduction in cRMSE compared with the strongest baseline. In downstream applications across multiple analytical scenarios, GaiaAgent demonstrates improved reliability and adaptability in land cover change detection and interpretation.

verified_metadata.title: Hemispheric-scale mapping of thaw slumps using a cloud-native and transferable deep learning framework
verified_metadata.abstract: Accelerating permafrost degradation is driving the rapid expansion of thaw slumps (TS) across the Northern Hemisphere, posing increasing risks to ecosystems, infrastructure, and the global carbon cycle. However, reliable TS identification at continental to hemispheric scales remains challenging due to strong environmental heterogeneity, fragmented remote sensing workflows, and limited cross-regional transferability of existing methods. Here, we address the cross-regional transferability gap in hemispheric TS identification by developing a reproducible framework that couples cloud-native multi-source data fusion in Google Earth Engine (GEE) with a modular PyTorch-based deep learning pipeline. The framework operationalizes transferability through three coordinated components: (1) a physically interpretable channel design that integrates Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and topographic data to encode TS-relevant processes; (2) a structure-preserving feature representation using PCA-guided dimensionality reduction and SNIC-based superpixel segmentation to suppress noise while maintaining geomorphic consistency; and (3) a standardized cross-regional training and ablation strategy that identifies model configurations maximizing generalization rather than region-specific accuracy. Evaluations across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), the Arctic, and the broader Northern Hemisphere demonstrate that late-summer observations and fused optical–SAR channels consistently outperform single-sensor inputs. The LinkNet-EfficientNet-B7 configuration achieves intersection-over-union (IOU) scores of 0.802 in the QTP, 0.770 in the Arctic, and 0.776 at hemispheric scale. Cross-regional transfer experiments further confirm robust generalization, with the hemispheric model maintaining IOU values exceeding 0.63 across distinct permafrost domains without region-specific retraining. These results indicate that transferable TS mapping is not primarily determined by model complexity, but by the consistency between process-informed feature representation and cross-regional training design. The proposed GEE-PyTorch framework provides a computationally efficient and reproducible foundation for operational monitoring of thaw-induced geomorphic disturbances.

verified_metadata.title: Rectify-Match-Reconstruct (RMR): Framework for dense and accurate metric 3D reconstruction via neural homography alignment
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate digital representations of civil infrastructure are essential for damage prognostics, condition assessment, and remaining-life prediction. While LiDAR-based sensing can generate dense geometric models, high deployment cost and extensive post-processing limit widespread use. Image-based photogrammetry offers a scalable alternative but struggles with scale ambiguity, unreliable feature correspondence, and degraded performance under wide baselines, repetitive textures, and geometric misalignment. These limitations significantly reduce the accuracy of dense metric 3D reconstruction required for structural assessment. This paper formulates a rectify-match-reconstruct (RMR) framework for generating dense, metrically accurate 3D reconstructions from field image collections. The method is built on the key insight that correspondence errors arise primarily from severe geometric misalignment between image pairs. To address this, a self-supervised, patch-wise neural homography alignment network is developed to geometrically rectify local image regions prior to dense matching. An iterative refinement process progressively improves alignment, enabling dense correspondence estimation to operate in a stable regime even under wide-baseline viewpoints and nonplanar scene geometry. The resulting correspondences are mapped back to the original images and combined with camera calibration referenced to the Building Information Model (BIM) to achieve dense metrically consistent 3D reconstructions. Extensive validation across structures of varying scale, texture, and viewpoint separation demonstrates that RMR brings over 90% reduction in correspondence error relative to state-of-the-art optical flow methods. The framework also enables self-supervised fine-tuning of dense matching models using field imagery, further improving reconstruction accuracy. By reframing homography as a geometric preconditioning mechanism, the proposed approach provides a practical and scalable pathway toward reliable, low-cost digital twin generation and automated structural condition assessment. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tmatiki2/RMR.

title: Uncertainty-aware semi-supervised framework with supervised contrastive learning for sugarcane leaf disease detection
abstract: Sugarcane leaf diseases severely impact crop yield and quality, making accurate and timely detection critical for sustainable agriculture. Conventional deep learning models for plant disease detection depend on large annotated datasets, which are expensive to obtain and challenging to prepare due to challenges commonly observed across crop disease detection tasks, including (i) high intra-class variation caused by diverse symptom expressions across growth stages, (ii) subtle inter-class similarities between diseased and healthy tissues, and (iii) the risk of noisy labels degrading model reliability. To handle these challenges, we presented an Uncertainty-aware Mean-Teacher based Semi-Supervised Learning Disease Detection Network (U-SSDNet) that leverages unlabeled data while maintaining robustness. First, discrete wavelet transform preprocessing is applied to enhance lesion visibility and reduce intra- class variation. Subsequently, the KL divergence is employed to refine the pseudo-labels and reduce the impact of confirmation bias. At the same time, supervised contrastive learning is applied to make the features more distin- guishable and improve the separation among different classes. Experimental evaluations on sugarcane leaf disease datasets, considered a representative case study, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves performance close to that of fully supervised models while requiring far fewer annotated samples and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised approaches.

title: Multi-temporal calving front segmentation
abstract: The calving fronts of marine-terminating glaciers undergo constant changes. These changes significantly affect the glacier’s mass and dynamics, demanding continuous monitoring. To address this need, deep learning models were developed that can automatically delineate the calving front in Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery. However, these models often struggle to correctly classify areas affected by seasonal conditions such as ice mélange or snow-covered surfaces. To address this issue, we propose to process multiple frames from a satellite image time series of the same glacier in parallel and exchange temporal information between the corresponding feature maps to stabilize each prediction. We integrate our approach into the current state-of-the-art architecture Tyrion and accomplish a new state-of-the-art performance on the CaFFe benchmark dataset. In particular, we achieve a Mean Distance Error of 184.4 m and a mean Intersection over Union of 83.6 . Furthermore, we empirically demonstrate that our modifications are highly robust to seasonal conditions, achieving a Mean Distance Error of 213.0 m under adverse conditions and outperforming prior state-of-the-art methods, such as Tyrion, by more than 100 m. The CaFFe benchmark dataset is publicly available at https://doi.pangaea.de/10.1594/PANGAEA.940950 and the code at https://github.com/ki7077/Multi-Temporal-Tyrion .

verified_metadata.abstract: The calving fronts of marine-terminating glaciers undergo constant changes. These changes significantly affect the glacier’s mass and dynamics, demanding continuous monitoring. To address this need, deep learning models were developed that can automatically delineate the calving front in Synthetic Aperture Radar imagery. However, these models often struggle to correctly classify areas affected by seasonal conditions such as ice mélange or snow-covered surfaces. To address this issue, we propose to process multiple frames from a satellite image time series of the same glacier in parallel and exchange temporal information between the corresponding feature maps to stabilize each prediction. We integrate our approach into the current state-of-the-art architecture Tyrion and accomplish a new state-of-the-art performance on the CaFFe benchmark dataset. In particular, we achieve a Mean Distance Error of 184.4 m and a mean Intersection over Union of 83.6 . Furthermore, we empirically demonstrate that our modifications are highly robust to seasonal conditions, achieving a Mean Distance Error of 213.0 m under adverse conditions and outperforming prior state-of-the-art methods, such as Tyrion, by more than 100 m. The CaFFe benchmark dataset is publicly available at https://doi.pangaea.de/10.1594/PANGAEA.940950 and the code at https://github.com/ki7077/Multi-Temporal-Tyrion .

verified_metadata.title: Integrating physical modeling and data-driven learning: A DCNN for InSAR phase filtering and applications
verified_metadata.abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) phase filtering is crucial for stable phase unwrapping and accurate topographic mapping and deformation retrieval. However, conventional spatial, frequency, and nonlocal filters, as well as existing learning-based methods, often struggle to balance noise suppression and detail preservation, especially under extremely low coherence and high fringe density, where oversmoothing and artifacts are prone to occur. This paper proposes InSAR-Net, a deep neural network for phase filtering targeting severely noisy InSAR scenarios. The network is trained on a high-fidelity physics-based synthetic dataset that spans a wide range of coherence levels, fringe densities, and deformation patterns, with enriched extremely low-coherence samples to improve robustness. InSAR-Net integrates Feature Separation Coding (FSC) to enhance phase-related physical representations, residual dense encoding with a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) for multi-scale modeling, and Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) with phase consistency loss to suppress pseudo fringes while preserving edges and fine structures. Experiments on simulated and real SAR datasets demonstrate that InSAR-Net achieves superior performance over representative SOTA methods in terms of RMSE, PSNR, and SSIM, with more pronounced gains under strong noise conditions. Further validation using low-coherence masking, detrended residual phase analysis, and unwrapped phase stability assessment shows that InSAR-Net reduces random phase fluctuations and scattering-related noise in valid coherent areas, improves phase unwrapping reliability, and avoids physical interpretation of signal-void regions. The dataset and trained model will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/yangwangyangzi48/InSAR-Net.git.

verified_metadata.title: SyneFloor: Synergizing zero-shot geometric priors and active learning for weakly supervised floorplan reconstruction
verified_metadata.abstract: Indoor floorplan reconstruction from 3D point clouds is a fundamental task for digital twin and architectural modeling. However, fully supervised approaches heavily rely on exhaustive polygon-level annotations, which are notoriously time-consuming and labor-intensive to acquire. To address this bottleneck, we propose SyneFloor, a weakly supervised framework that achieves accurate floorplan reconstruction under extreme label scarcity. First, to overcome the structural degradation caused by sparse supervision, we extract robust instance-aware structural priors by leveraging the zero-shot segmentation capabilities of vision foundation models (e.g., SAM3). We then propose an Adaptive Mask-Query Synergistic Fusion (AMQSF) module to dynamically fuse these explicit geometric priors into Transformer queries. Second, to maximize the data efficiency of the limited annotation budget, we design a stage-wise, multi-criteria active learning strategy. By comprehensively evaluating predictive uncertainty and architectural complexity, the model actively selects the most informative and challenging scenes for annotation. Third, to fully exploit the remaining unannotated data, we introduce a topology-aware pseudo-label generation mechanism within a dual-network collaborative framework. By explicitly detecting and resolving topological conflicts, this mechanism produces high-quality, structurally valid pseudo-labels, which fundamentally guarantees the robustness of the semi-supervised learning process. Extensive experiments on the synthetic Structured3D and real-world SceneCAD datasets demonstrate the superiority of SyneFloor. It not only exhibits robustness by consistently outperforming current state-of-the-art methods under extreme label scarcity (1% to 10% budgets), but also matches or surpasses several 100% fully supervised methods with much less labeled expenditure (e.g. utilizing only 40% of labels). This dual capability thereby establishes a highly scalable and annotation-efficient paradigm for automated indoor floorplan reconstruction in practical applications.

verified_metadata.title: Arctic sea ice motion retrieval via vision foundation model and cross-sensor SAR
verified_metadata.abstract: Monitoring Arctic sea ice motion (SIM) is of critical importance for polar climate research. Although synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables all weather observations, the relatively long revisit interval of a single sensor constrains the spatial and temporal extent of SIM monitoring. Cross-sensor SAR collaboration can overcome this limitation, yet it is challenged by pronounced nonlinear radiometric distortions (NRDs) and geometric distortions between images. To address these issues, this study proposes a vision foundation model-driven framework for cross-sensor SAR collaborative monitoring of Arctic SIM. First, a cross-sensor feature extraction module via the DINOv2 vision foundation model is developed to derive robust semantic features that mitigate NRDs. Second, a multi-scale optical flow estimation module with embedded SIM Physics is designed to alleviate geometric distortions. Experiments using Sentinel-1, ALOS-2, RCM, and C-SAR data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in vector retrieval under both summer and winter conditions. Comparisons with IABP buoy measurements indicate that the retrieved velocity RMSE is within 0.73 cm/s and the directional RMSE is within 4.6°. In addition, the proposed framework substantially enhances spatiotemporal coverage, increasing the average number of effective coverage days over the Arctic by 53% and the average effective coverage area by 75%. This work provides a new technical pathway toward large scale, high precision SIM monitoring across the entire Arctic.

title: SARMelt: MGLANet-driven high-resolution surface melt mapping of circum-Antarctic ice shelves from Sentinel-1 imagery during 2015–2023
abstract: Surface melt on Antarctic ice shelves is a key precursor to hydrofracture, structural weakening, and potential ice-shelf collapse. However, existing passive and active microwave products, while valuable for long term monitoring, remain inadequate for resolving fine-scale melt features over heterogeneous ice shelf surfaces. Moreover, conventional retrieval methods are limited in capturing fragmented melt boundaries and in generalizing across the highly variable surface conditions of Antarctic ice shelves. To address these limitations, we developed a Multiscale Global-Local Attention Network (MGLANet) for circum-Antarctic surface melt mapping. Within this framework, LSAM focuses on local fine-scale structure extraction, GLA models long-range contextual dependencies to characterize macro-scale melt distribution, and MCIM improves multiscale feature fusion across decoder levels. Using a standardized Sentinel-1 archive from the CASEarth Cloud Service Platform, we generated a high-resolution (40 m) surface melt product spanning 2015–2023. Quantitative evaluation on the test set demonstrates strong model performance, achieving a mean IoU of 90.84% and an F 1 score of 94.83%. The SARMelt product includes (1) monthly high-resolution surface melt maps capturing the spatiotemporal evolution of meltwater; (2) annual melt occurrence maps quantifying seasonal persistence; and (3) time-series statistical record for rapid climatological analysis, providing a new basis for analyzing the spatiotemporal evolution of Antarctic surface melt. Cross-comparison with ASCAT, SSMIS, and the deep-learning-based UMelt product shows that SARMelt maintains high consistency in capturing interannual melt variability while substantially improving the delineation of melt boundaries and localized melt features in grounding-line zones. By bridging the gap between kilometer-scale microwave observations and fine-scale ice shelf surface melt information, SARMelt provides a high-resolution benchmark for cryospheric monitoring, regional climate model validation, and investigations of melt-related ice shelf instability under ongoing climate change. The proposed SARMelt dataset is available on the CASEarth platform at https://doi.org/10.12237/casearth.OSD20260002 .

title: GeoGS: Geometric Prior-Guided Gaussian Splatting for robust urban reconstruction from sparse views
abstract: Gaussian Splatting (GS) has emerged as an efficient representation for large-scale urban reality capture, yet reliable reconstruction in complex built environments typically requires dense image collections with high view overlap. Under sparse observations, it often yields geometrically inaccurate and incomplete reconstructions, making external geometric priors essential for robust optimization. Geo-referenced 3D city models provide complete and metrically reliable structural priors but lack fine as-built details, whereas visual foundation models infer dense local geometric cues from images yet remain less reliable in occluded, weakly textured, or sparsely observed regions. We present GeoGS, a geometry-aware GS method that integrates worldwide-available CityGML Level of Detail (LoD) 2 models with pose-conditioned depth cues from visual foundation models for robust urban reconstruction from sparse views with known camera poses. It initializes Gaussians directly from LoD2 surfaces and optimizes them in two stages. In the Anchoring Stage, depth rendered from the 3D city model establishes a metrically consistent building backbone, while a proximity-based geometry protection mechanism prevents structural drift. In the Refinement Stage, dense visual depth is introduced with a lightweight structural anchor and adaptive weighting to recover local geometric details without compromising the established topology. Experiments on the UAV-based TUM2TWIN dataset and the street-level egenioussBench dataset demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. On TUM2TWIN, GeoGS improves average PSNR by 1.13 dB in 2D rendering assessment and reduces extracted-mesh M3C2 distance by 14.3% in 3D geometric evaluation, compared with the respective best-performing baselines. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating structured geospatial priors with data-driven visual cues, advancing sparse-view Gaussian Splatting toward scalable and geometrically reliable urban digital twin generation. The project page is available at https://github.com/zqlin0521/GeoGS .

verified_metadata.title: Advancing hyperspectral nutrient modeling through transfer learning: Insights from foliar N–P–K estimation in cranberries
verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient and accurate monitoring of crop nutrient status is essential for optimizing fertilization and promoting sustainable production. Hyperspectral remote sensing offers a promising approach for estimating foliar nutrient concentrations, yet the transferability of predictive models across different spatial, temporal, and plant domains remains a major challenge. In this study, we systematically evaluated the effectiveness of transfer learning techniques for improving the transferability of hyperspectral models in predicting cranberry foliar nitrogen (Nmass), phosphorus (Pmass), and potassium (Kmass) concentrations. We assessed four transfer scenarios: (1) across geographic locations (from NEON domains to a cranberry farm in Wisconsin); (2) across growth stages; (3) across leaf types; and (4) from PROSAIL-PRO–derived synthetic datasets to field-measured datasets. Four representative transfer learning approaches — transfer component analysis (TCA), transfer adaptive boosting for regression (TrAdaBoostR2), parameter regularization, and fine-tuning — were applied to partial least squares regression (PLSR) and deep neural network (DNN) models. Results showed that baseline models trained on source domains performed poorly when directly applied to target domains, with median normalized root-mean-square-errors (nRMSE) ranging from 16 to 71 % across scenarios. Transfer learning substantially improved model performance and reduced prediction uncertainty, with parameter regularization and TrAdaBoostR2 generally outperforming TCA. Model transferability varied with nutrient type: Nmass exhibited higher temporal variability and greater distributional shifts, whereas Pmass and Kmass were more reliably predicted due to their indirect spectral correlations. Fine-tuning the DNN on as little as 10–30 % of target-domain data achieved significant improvements, highlighting the efficiency of hybrid transfer learning. Our findings provide practical insights into selecting effective transfer learning strategies for hyperspectral nutrient mapping and demonstrate the feasibility of scaling nutrient monitoring across diverse crop systems, growth stages, and leaf types.

verified_metadata.abstract: LiDAR place recognition determines one’s position on a prior point cloud map. The most studied ground-level LiDAR place recognition suffers from pre-visit requirements, incomplete coverage, and limited perspectives. Using pre-acquired Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS) data with broad spatial coverage as an aerial prior map overcomes these drawbacks, making cross-view place recognition necessary and advantageous. However, aerial–ground LiDAR place recognition faces a significant challenge from the domain gap between aerial and ground point clouds. Existing studies are limited by false positives in initial retrieval and the lack of large-scale benchmarks. To overcome these limitations, we present a novel retrieval and re-ranking framework for aerial–ground LiDAR place recognition. Based on the prior that neighboring point cloud patches share related semantics and geometries with the anchor patch, we select similar neighboring patches at multiple scales and aggregate their features to refine the anchor patch representation. Our retrieval network integrates these patch-level self-supervised learning modules with scene-level learning to improve the discriminativeness of global features across aerial and ground point clouds. As a self-supervised approach, it eliminates the need for manual annotations and demonstrates strong generalization. Furthermore, leveraging the structured spatial distribution of ALS point clouds, we introduce an Expanded Reciprocal (ER) re-ranking algorithm to exploit neighborhood information maximally and refine each feature based on neighbor features, which are then used to update the similarity matrix for final ranking. To evaluate our approach, we establish a new large-scale benchmark named CS-Urban-Scenes. Collected via a backpack mobile mapping system with post-processed kinematic (PPK) optimized trajectories, the dataset features an 18.1 km trajectory and a 7.2 km2 coverage area. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our retrieval network outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving a 9.8% improvement in average Recall@1 and a 3.2% improvement in average Recall@1% on the CS-Urban-Scenes, while also showing the best performance on the CS-Campus3D dataset. Additionally, our ER re-ranking algorithm further boosts the average Recall@1 by 4.9% on CS-Campus3D and 10.2% on CS-Urban-Scenes without additional training.

verified_metadata.title: Aerial Image Gravity Direction Estimation (AGE): Robust single-image estimation by fusing foundation model features with camera geometry
verified_metadata.abstract: Estimating the gravity direction from a single aerial image provides an absolute vertical prior, which is valuable for spatial reasoning when multi-view stereo or external spatial references are unavailable. Although onboard inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide platform attitude, transferring these measurements to the camera coordinate frame requires precise synchronization and accurate extrinsic calibration, which are not always satisfied for low-cost aerial platforms. Moreover, such calibration information is often unavailable for crowdsourced or historical aerial imagery. These limitations make vision-based approaches a practical alternative for estimating gravity direction directly from images. However, reliable estimation from a single aerial image remains challenging due to the wide range of aerial viewing angles, which often leads to ambiguous geometric cues. In this work, we propose Aerial Image Gravity Direction Estimation (AGE), a framework for estimating gravity direction from a single aerial image. To resolve geometric ambiguity under diverse viewing configurations, AGE combines semantically rich features from a frozen DINOv2 backbone with camera-aware geometric features derived from known camera intrinsics. Geometric reasoning is guided by supervision from an intermediate Perspective Field, while gravity is predicted as a 3D unit vector for stable learning across aerial viewpoints. To facilitate training and evaluation, we construct AGE-Pano, a large-scale synthetic dataset containing 28,500 images with accurate ground-truth gravity directions and diverse camera viewpoints and intrinsics. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world aerial imagery demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness under aerial viewing conditions.

title: Toeplitz-structured deep unfolding network for TomoSAR 3-D reconstruction
abstract: Urban area 3-D imaging is a key application of synthetic aperture radar (SAR). Classical compressive sensing-based tomographic SAR methods rely on iterative optimization, which is computationally expensive and sensitive to hyperparameter tuning, limiting its scalability for large scenes. Deep unfolding networks offer a promising alternative but still suffer from inaccurate estimation of target elevations and amplitudes. Therefore, this paper proposes the Toeplitz-structured learned iterative shrinkage–thresholding algorithm with an adaptive elevation target determination module (Toe-LISTA-Ada) for efficient and accurate TomoSAR 3-D reconstruction. First, complex-valued operators are employed to directly process SAR measurements, ensuring the preservation of phase information. Then, by exploiting the Toeplitz structure of the Gram matrix of the TomoSAR observation model, Toe-LISTA-Ada replaces explicit matrix multiplication with a convolutional operation, significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters while retaining physical consistency, thereby accelerating convergence and improving reconstruction accuracy. Finally, an adaptive elevation target determination module is incorporated to account for the limited number of dominant scatterers along the elevation direction in urban scenes, enhancing target separability and elevation estimation performance under severe layover and noise conditions. The proposed network is trained on simulated data that are consistent with real imaging parameters and evaluated on measured datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that Toe-LISTA-Ada achieves improved accuracy in both elevation target localization and amplitude estimation, while exhibiting a capability for 3-D point cloud denoising. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ormosia6/TomoSAR-Toe-LISTA .
