verified_metadata.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of solar photovoltaics development and ecological implications in Japan from cropland to forest
verified_metadata.abstract: Rapid expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) installations has raised concerns regarding land-cover change and ecological impacts, yet long-term, nationwide assessments remain limited in densely populated and forest-dominated countries. This study addresses this gap by developing a nationwide, long-term solar PV dataset for Japan from 2008 to 2024 and examining associated land-cover transitions. A national solar PV map at 10 m resolution was produced for 2024 and integrated with time-series analysis to estimate installation years from 2008 onward using satellite data on the Google Earth Engine platform. The PV map achieved an overall accuracy of 0.910 (Cohen’s kappa = 0.805), and estimated installation years showed temporal agreement with reference data with a root mean squared error of approximately 2.0 years. Detection of installations smaller than 50 kW remained challenging due to spatial resolution limits; as a result, approximately 60–90% of total installed solar PV capacity was captured by the satellite-based analysis. Results indicate a shift in PV deployment from cropland and paddy fields toward forested areas after the mid-2010 s, with peak annual land conversion exceeding 7,000 ha during the early expansion phase. PV installations primarily occurred in planted and secondary forests and were associated with increased forest fragmentation during periods of rapid expansion. Within national parks, most PV installations were located in “Ordinary Areas,” although PV presence in surrounding buffer zones indicates potential spatial pressure on landscapes adjacent to park boundaries, particularly in small or spatially constrained parks. Despite remaining uncertainty related to the incomplete detectability of PV systems smaller than 50 kW, this study provides a long-term picture of solar PV expansion and its land-use and institutional implications in land-constrained and environmentally sensitive settings in Japan.

title: LightFormer: An efficient lightweight decoder for optical remote sensing semantic segmentation
abstract: Deep learning techniques have achieved remarkable success in the semantic segmentation of remotesensing images and in land-use change detection. However, in real-time tasks such as natural disasterresponse, most mainstream decoders struggle to balance computational overhead with segmentationaccuracy, which limits their practical applicability. Herein, we introduce LightFormer, a lightweightdecoder for time-critical tasks that involve unstructured targets, such as disaster assessment, unmannedaerial vehicle search-and-rescue, and cultural heritage monitoring. LightFormer employs a feature-fusion and refinement module built on channel processing and a learnable gating mechanism toaggregate multi-scale, multi-range information efficiently, which drastically curtails model complex-ity. Furthermore, we propose a spatial information selection module (SISM) that integrates long-range attention with a detail preservation branch to capture spatial dependencies across multiplescales, thereby substantially improving the recognition of unstructured targets in complex scenes.On the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark, LightFormer attains 99.9% of GLFFNets mIoU (83.9% vs.84.0%) while requiring only 14.7% of its FLOPs and 15.9% of its parameters, thus achieving anexcellent accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Consistent results on LoveDA, ISPRS Potsdam, RescueNet,and FloodNet further demonstrate its robustness and superior perception of unstructured objects.These findings highlight LightFormer as a practical solution for remote sensing applications whereboth computational economy and high-precision segmentation are imperative.

verified_metadata.abstract: Deep learning techniques have achieved remarkable success in the semantic segmentation of remote sensing images and in land-use change detection. However, in time-sensitive tasks such as natural disaster response, most mainstream decoders struggle to balance computational overhead with segmentation accuracy, which limits their practical applicability. Herein, we introduce LightFormer, a lightweight decoder for time-sensitive tasks that involve unstructured targets, such as disaster assessment, unmanned aerial vehicle search-and-rescue, and cultural heritage monitoring. LightFormer employs a feature-fusion and refinement module built on channel processing and a learnable gating mechanism to aggregate multi-scale, multi-range information efficiently, which significantly reduces model complexity. Furthermore, we propose a spatial information selection module (SISM) that integrates long-range attention with a detail preservation branch to capture spatial dependencies across multiple scales, thereby improving the recognition of unstructured targets in complex scenes. These findings highlight LightFormer as a promising and practical solution for remote sensing applications where both computational economy and high-precision segmentation are imperative.

title: Challenges in reliable bias correction of hydro-climatic and energy data: Towards a reconstruction of datasets
abstract: Regular gridded datasets commonly exhibit significant biases and therefore require correction before being used in impact studies. This study highlights the challenges involved in improving the adjustment of climate variables (precipitation and temperature), hydrological variables (soil water content, streamflow, evapotranspiration), and radiative variables (longwave and shortwave radiation). Eighteen bias-correction (BC) methods were selected, covering a wide range of approaches, including classical statistical techniques (e.g., quantile mapping), distribution-based methods (e.g., kernel smoothing), and machine learning approaches (e.g., random forests). BC outputs from CMIP6 models and ERA5 reanalyses were evaluated against observations from contrasting climatic regions of Benin. The evaluation relied on Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Pearson correlation coefficient, relative-mean-absolute-error (RMAE), and fraction within tolerance (FTI), computed at hourly, daily, and monthly temporal scales. It also considered the representation of diurnal and monthly cycles, as well as consistency with mean values and trends of various climatic extreme indices. Three calibration strategies were explored: (i) using the first half of the time series for calibration to assess the preservation of future trends; (ii) the second half to evaluate the ability to reconstruct missing data; and (iii) 80% of the series to investigate the effect of sample size. Finally, bias corrections were applied by stratifying the data by month and intensity ranges to assess the limitations of global BC methods. Results show that machine learning methods do not systematically outperform classical bias-correction approaches. Performance varies considerably by variable, station, and climatic context. It is therefore important to select methods suited to the specific conditions and intended use, to improve the reliability of future climate and hydrological projections.

title: LSFC-Net: Lightweight Spatial-Frequency Collaboration Network with sparse interaction for remote sensing change detection
abstract: Deep learning-based remote sensing change detection (RSCD) models have shown significant progress, yet they still face two major challenges. First, most methods struggle to effectively cooperate spatial-frequency information and generate complementary dual-domain features, thereby weakening the structural integrity of change objects. Additionally, the abundance of irrelevant semantic information in remote sensing scenes hinders spatiotemporal difference modeling, and the generation of redundant difference information can result in false positives. To this end, this study proposes a Lightweight Spatial-Frequency Collaboration Network (LSFC-Net) with sparse interaction for RSCD. Specifically, a Spatial-Frequency Context Aggregator (SFCA) is developed to decompose the original input into spatial and frequency streams. The former further refines spatial features, while the latter captures frequency discrepancies and texture details, finally integrating the dual-domain information in a complementary manner. Furthermore, a Feature Sparse Interactor (FSI) is designed to highlight genuine changes and suppress the influence of irrelevant semantics. FSI performs cross-temporal interaction on bi-temporal images through a sparse interaction attention mechanism, dynamically selecting the tokens most relevant to genuine changes. Experimental results show that LSFC-Net outperforms most representative RSCD methods in accuracy and efficiency.

title: Construction of high spatiotemporal resolution beach SBT-DEM using multi-source data fusion
abstract: Sandy coastlines are increasingly threatened by severe erosion, necessitating high-resolution topographic data for effective coastal management. Traditional ground surveys are limited by high costs and inefficiency, while remote sensing inversion techniques often suffer from low resolution and accuracy. This study presents a multi-platform collaborative observation and data fusion approach to construct a seamless bathymetric and digital elevation model (SBT-DEM) with enhanced accuracy and resolution. The approach integrates terrestrial laser scanning, shore-based video imaging, and an unmanned surface vessel with single-beam echo sounders to capture topography across the backshore, foreshore, and submerged zones. Reliability was assessed using Global Navigation Satellite System Real-Time Kinematic measurements. A random forest regression further refined the foreshore topography, reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) by about 0.1 m. The resulting SBT-DEM achieves high spatial–temporal resolution and accuracy (mean absolute error = 0.106 m, RMSE = 0.141 m), providing a robust dataset for coastal monitoring and erosion control.

title: Aridity thresholds Reveal transitions in dominant drivers of partitioned Water–Carbon coupling across Central Asian drylands
abstract: Intensifying global aridification is reshaping the water–carbon balance in dryland ecosystems, yet when and how this coupling reaches critical thresholds remains poorly understood—posing major uncertainties for predicting ecosystem resilience under climate change. Using Central Asia as a representative dryland region, we partitioned ecosystem water-use efficiency (WUE = GPP/ET) into transpiration efficiency (WUEc = GPP/Ec) and the transpiration-to-evapotranspiration ratio (TET = Ec/ET) to probe threshold responses. We identified distinct aridity thresholds associated with nonlinear shifts in water–carbon coupling: WUE and WUEc declined and then rebounded beyond aridity levels of 0.75 and 0.81, respectively, indicating tighter coupling between carbon gain and water loss under severe climatic stress. In contrast, ET, Ec, GPP, and TET declined sharply at thresholds of 0.80, 0.85, 0.86, and 0.88, indicating broader constraints on ecosystem carbon assimilation and hydrological functioning. SHAP-based machine learning revealed threshold-dependent shifts in ecosystem controls, with vegetation traits dominating carbon–water coupling under lower aridity, and hydroclimatic stressors—including soil moisture, precipitation, temperature, and vapor pressure deficit—emerging as dominant regulators beyond critical thresholds. Notably, temperature was positively associated with WUE and WUEc, while VPD exerted persistent negative effects post-threshold. These findings characterize nonlinear, threshold-dependent changes in dryland carbon–water coupling and highlight the need to evaluate apparent efficiency gains in the context of declining ecosystem fluxes under future drought intensification.

title: Hybrid retrieval fractional vegetation cover for maize canopy by considering row-sun azimuth angle
abstract: Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) is a fundamental indicator for crop yield prediction and carbon cycle assessments. Despite the widespread adoption of row-based planting in modern agroecosystems, most existing FVC retrieval methods fail to adequately account for the anisotropic reflectance effects driven by row-planted crop, row orientation, and solar geometry, leading to increased retrieval biases. To address this issue, 167 maize plots were measured during 2021–2023, and maize canopy geometry characteristics were parameterized based on the field dataset as the LESS input variables. An improved FVC retrieval model was developed by integrating 3D radiative transfer simulations with machine learning, which partially mitigated errors induced by maize row orientation changes. First, the effect of row orientation on maize canopy reflectance was confirmed by the LESS simulation dataset with a relative change magnitude of ∼37.7%, and it held for vegetation indices. Second, the FVC retrieval accuracy was improved by incorporating row orientation into retrieval algorithms, as indicated by a decrease in relative error of 1.24% and 1.6% for the simulated and field dataset respectively (FVC ∈ [0.3 ∼ 0.8]), and greater improvements were achieved in the direction perpendicular or parallel to the sun. This improvement was also observed in the FVC mapping of the large-scale Youyi County. This study proposes a scalable and transferable retrieval framework that improves FVC retrieval in row-structured maize canopies, with potential applications for retrieving other biophysical parameters in row-crop systems.

title: Geometry-aware mapping with MI-IWNet reveals topographic modulation effects in internal wave evolution
abstract: Accurate mapping of oceanic internal waves (IWs) is essential for understanding ocean mixing and energy transfer, yet remains challenging due to weak and transient sea-surface signatures and heterogeneous sensor limitations. In this study, we propose a geometry-aware deep learning framework, MI-IWNet, which incorporates a direction-aware encoder design (including Direction-Aware Strip Convolution, DASC) to represent the anisotropic and curvilinear morphology of IW crests in multi-sensor satellite imagery; we further develop a graph-based Structure-Aware Wave Packet Aggregation algorithm to assemble pixel-level predictions into object-level Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBBs) for robust geophysical analysis. Experiments on large-scale Sentinel-1 SAR and optical observations demonstrate that the proposed framework enables geometry-consistent mapping. By mapping these extracted OBBs onto regional bathymetry in a decoupled post-processing analysis, we reveal distinct topographic modulation effects in IW evolution across marginal seas: in the South China Sea, IW packets exhibit coherent trans-basin propagation with local obstacle-induced modulation and shelf-break accumulation; in the semi-enclosed Sulu Sea, wave packets show source-controlled radiation confined by basin boundaries; and in the Andaman Sea, the Andaman–Nicobar Ridge induces strong directional anisotropy and complex interference patterns. These results highlight how key topographic units systematically modulate packet density, pathway continuity, and directional organization, and indicate that MI-IWNet provides an effective and transferable tool for automated IW segmentation, characterization, and comparative regional analysis.

title: Synergizing greening and resilience: a remote sensing-driven spatial optimization framework based on landscape configuration
abstract: Satellite observations have revealed widespread global greening driven by ecological restoration; however, achieving long-term sustainability remains a challenge due to a growing discrepancy between vegetation expansion and ecosystem resilience. While climatic and anthropogenic drivers of this asynchrony have been extensively studied, the potential of landscape configuration to regulate resilience dynamics remains under-explored, lacking mechanism-informed tools for optimizing greening layouts. To bridge this gap, we proposed a data-driven framework integrating long-term remote sensing time series, interpretable machine learning, and a novel vegetation-landscape spatial optimization model (VLSOM). We first quantified the nonlinear contributions of landscape metrics to resilience dynamics, revealing that landscape configuration serves as a critical regulator with distinct, type-specific effects. Leveraging these mechanistic insights, the VLSOM was developed to actively search for spatial solutions that maximize resilience. Empirical results demonstrate that the VLSOM achieved a threefold resilience improvement compared with random greening. With only a 3.3% alteration in land cover, the model mitigated the regional resilience decline trend by 27.4%. Furthermore, iterative analysis revealed a diminishing marginal return in greening, identifying a 7.6% forest expansion threshold as the optimal cost-benefit equilibrium. These findings expose the limitations of coverage-centric restoration strategies and demonstrate the capacity of integrating earth observation data with spatial optimization algorithms to maximize the cost-effectiveness of restoration efforts. By providing empirical and methodological references for precision restoration, this study advances a paradigm shift in ecological management toward climate-smart, structure-aware spatial planning.

title: Interannual Dynamics of Boreal Forest Wildfires (2020–2024) Derived from MODIS-Constrained Sentinel-2 Burned-Area Mapping
abstract: Boreal forests are increasingly affected by wildfires, creating a strong need for consistent annual burned-area datasets to support carbon-budget and climate studies. Existing annual burned-area products covering the entire boreal forest are mainly derived from Landsat imagery at 30 m resolution and may still suffer from omission and temporal misallocation in annual mapping. Here, we present BS2BAM, an automated burned-area mapping framework that integrates MODIS fire products and Sentinel-2 time-series imagery for annual mapping across the boreal forest. MODIS active-fire and burned-area products were first used to define wildfire candidate zones (WCZs). Burned and unburned samples automatically generated from the 2023 Canadian fire season were then used to train a random forest model, which estimated burn probability from Sentinel-2 spectral indices within the WCZ. The resulting probability maps were further refined through region growing to produce annual burned-area maps on a 10 m output grid for 2020–2024. Independent validation showed that, relative to Fire_GFL, BS2BAM reduced omission error from 30.82% to 15.98% and improved the Dice coefficient from 73.39% to 86.73%. Spatiotemporal statistics for 2020–2024 indicate that BS2BAM better captured the 2021 Siberian and 2023 Canadian wildfires than Fire_GFL and GABAM. BS2BAM provides a consistent high-resolution annual burned-area dataset for investigating interannual wildfire dynamics in boreal forests and supporting related carbon-cycle and climate studies.

verified_metadata.title: Interannual Dynamics of Boreal Forest Wildfires (2020–2024) Derived from MODIS-Constrained Sentinel-2 Burned-Area Mapping
verified_metadata.abstract: Boreal forests are increasingly affected by wildfires, creating a strong need for consistent annual burned-area datasets to support carbon-budget and climate studies. Existing annual burned-area products covering the entire boreal forest are mainly derived from Landsat imagery at 30 m resolution and may still suffer from omission and temporal misallocation in annual mapping. Here, we present BS2BAM, an automated burned-area mapping framework that integrates MODIS fire products and Sentinel-2 time-series imagery for annual mapping across the boreal forest. MODIS active-fire and burned-area products were first used to define wildfire candidate zones (WCZs). Burned and unburned samples automatically generated from the 2023 Canadian fire season were then used to train a random forest model, which estimated burn probability from Sentinel-2 spectral indices within the WCZ. The resulting probability maps were further refined through region growing to produce annual burned-area maps on a 10 m output grid for 2020–2024. Independent validation showed that, relative to Fire_GFL, BS2BAM reduced omission error from 30.82% to 15.98% and improved the Dice coefficient from 73.39% to 86.73%. Spatiotemporal statistics for 2020–2024 indicate that BS2BAM better captured the 2021 Siberian and 2023 Canadian wildfires than Fire_GFL and GABAM. BS2BAM provides a consistent high-resolution annual burned-area dataset for investigating interannual wildfire dynamics in boreal forests and supporting related carbon-cycle and climate studies.

title: Phenology-driven hierarchical framework for grass species classification in coastal wetlands based on Sentinel-1/2 imagery: A case study of the Jiangsu Coast, Eastern China
abstract: Coastal wetlands are among the most vulnerable and valuable ecosystems, yet they are undergoing persistent changes in land surface conditions and vegetation composition driven by climate change and intensive human activities. Accurate mapping of grass species distribution is essential for the control of invasive plants, biodiversity conservation, and vegetation carbon accounting, yet the task remains challenging due to tidal inundation, frequent cloud cover, and the high spectral similarity among coastal grass species. This study developed a hierarchical classification framework to mitigate these limitations. The intertidal zone was first delineated from multi-temporal Sentinel-2 observations by exploiting temporal differences in water coverage, which compensated for the omission of grass species affected by tidal fluctuations that conventional classification methods have overlooked. Subsequently, two phenology-based vegetation features derived from monthly NDVI were constructed to improve the discrimination of spectrally similar species in the supratidal zone and were incorporated into a random forest classifier. The proposed framework achieved an overall accuracy (OA) of 0.94, notably higher than the OA of 0.85 from the traditional single-level classification, and effectively reduced misclassifications among species with overlapping spectral signatures. The hierarchical framework increased the total detected grassland area by approximately 13657.91 ha, with Spartina alterniflora contributing the majority of the improvement due to enhanced detection in the intertidal zone. In 2023, Jiangsu coastal zones supported 177,464.8 ha of grassland, with Spartina alterniflora occupying 52490.8 ha and showing substantial dominance along the Yancheng coasts. The successful detection of large areas of S. alterniflora that were omitted by a single-level model confirmed the importance of addressing tidal interference and demonstrated the benefits of incorporating phenological differences among grass species into the classification process. These findings demonstrate that the hierarchical strategy provides a more reliable solution to large-scale grass species mapping in dynamic coastal environments and offers practical support for invasive species management and ecosystem protection.

title: Quantifying the influence of DEM elevation errors on regional gravity forward modeling through DEM correction and fusion
abstract: High-precision characterization of the Earth’s gravity field is essential for geological structure analysis, volcanic activity monitoring, and resource exploration. As direct measurement of a high-resolution global gravity field remains impractical, forward modeling based on Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) is a key method for recovering its high-frequency components and is essential for regional high-resolution gravity field modeling. However, the accuracy of this method is severely limited by substantial errors in existing global DEMs, particularly those induced by vegetation cover. Currently, a systematic research quantifying the full pathway from DEM error correction to its impact on gravity field accuracy is lacking. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework for correcting DEM errors and evaluating their propagation in gravity field modeling. Specifically, we develop a hybrid Random Forest-Inverse Distance Weighting (RF-IDW) method to fuse multi-source remote sensing data and generate a regionally optimized, high-precision DEM. The proposed framework is evaluated in the Wudalianchi volcanic region using in-situ gravity observations. Comparative forward modeling based on the original TanDEM-X DEM and the optimized DEM demonstrates a 42.35% improvement in elevation accuracy, resulting in a 17.89% increase in the accuracy of the modeled terrain gravity field. Furthermore, DEM elevation errors exhibit a moderately strong correlation with gravity anomaly error (R = 0.648), accounting for approximately 42.0% of their variance. These findings provide both a quantitative assessment of elevation errors in gravity field modeling and a transferable methodological framework for enhancing the accuracy of DEM-based gravity field solutions in diverse topographic and vegetation environments.

title: OpenPineDet: An open-set detection framework for the detection of dead pine wood in forests
abstract: Early and accurate detection of dead pine wood (DPW) is essential to mitigate the spread of pine wilt disease (PWD), a destructive affliction of pine forests. Deep learning-based object detection methods have been widely employed for DPW detection. However, these approaches typically assume that both the training and test datasets contain only instances from a single, known class (i.e., DPW). This closed-set assumption often results in unknown targets in the test data being misclassified as DPW. To address this limitation, we collected high-resolution drone imagery of pine forests, resulting in a dataset of 7,733 images (the GSD ranged from 10.4 to 15.5 cm/pixel for flight altitudes between 800 and 1200 m) comprising 29,575 samples of DPW and 7,334 samples of unknown categories. We then introduced an open-set object detection framework, OpenPineDet (OPDet), designed to accurately identify DPW while recognizing other similar objects (e.g., bare soil and houses) as unknown categories. OPDet integrates two novel modules: (1) a Bottleneck Channel Attention Network (BNCA) that leverages the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism to enhance the model’s focus on DPW targets; and (2) a Dual Contrastive Learning (DCL) module, which combines Instance-Level Contrastive Learning (ICL) with Focal Loss (FL) to improve detection accuracy of hard-to-classify DPW instances. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that OPDet outperforms existing methods, achieving an Average Precision (AP K ) of 92.67 % and a Recall (R K ) of 97.24 %, while reducing Wilderness Impact (WI) and Absolute Open-Set Error (AOSE) to 1.80 and 242, respectively. Additionally, the proposed model demonstrates stable performance across different scenarios (such as simple scenes with only pine trees and complex scenes with other unknown categories), and exhibits better regional generalization capabilities. These results indicate that OPDet effectively reduces the misclassification of unknown targets as DPW, highlighting its effectiveness for open-set detection methodologies in forest management applications.

title: Advancing green tide monitoring: a spatiotemporal analysis in the Southern Yellow Sea using a novel deep learning and remote sensing fusion approach
abstract: Green tides caused by the macroalga Ulva prolifera are recurrent marine disasters in the Southern Yellow Sea (SYS), China. Accurate monitoring and spatiotemporal characterization are essential for effective mitigation. However, conventional remote sensing methods struggle to detect fine filamentous structures, and prevailing deep learning models suffer from spatial detail loss and scene-dependent variability that undermines multi-temporal consistency. To address these challenges, we propose UPS-Net-LDU, an improved semantic segmentation model that integrates a Hybrid Attention Gate (HAG) and an Edge-Enhanced Strip (EES) module into the U-Net architecture. Using 170 GF-1 WFV images from 2018 to 2025, we construct a multi-year distribution dataset covering the high-incidence period (May–August) of U. prolifera in the SYS. Quantitative validation shows that UPS-Net-LDU achieves an IoU of 73.44%, Precision of 82.93%, Recall of 86.52%, and an F1-score of 84.68%, outperforming several mainstream benchmarks. Ablation experiments confirm the individual contributions of the HAG and EES modules. Spatiotemporal evolution analysis reveals a persistent spatial pattern: source area in the Subei Shoal → northeastward transport corridor → convergence zone in the southeastern Shandong Peninsula, with notable interannual variability including an alternating pattern of high- and low-intensity years between consecutive years. Integrated analysis with sea surface temperature (SST) data indicates that SST warming within 15–24 °C during May–June facilitates algal expansion, whereas persistently high temperatures (>24 °C) during July–August suppress growth and promote decay, clarifying a dual-phase regulatory mechanism. This study offers a robust methodological tool for precise monitoring and delivers critical insights into the dual-phase thermal regulation of green tides, supporting early warning and management in the region.

title: A global 500 m dataset of tree crown morphology to advance vegetation modeling and management
abstract: Tree crown architecture varies widely across the globe and strongly influences ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, the carbon cycle, and land-atmosphere interactions. However, its global variability and spatial patterns remain poorly quantified due to sparse field and LiDAR measurements, limiting large-scale ecological and modelling applications. Here, we present a globally consistent 500 m tree crown structure dataset, including crown depth (CD), crown width (CW), and aspect ratio (AR, defined as CD/CW) across eight plant functional types (PFTs). The dataset was generated using an allometric upscaling framework that links more than 340,000 field observations with satellite-derived canopy height and bioclimatic predictors. Moving beyond classic power-law allometry, this approach captures transferable crown structure–height relationships via Random Forest models, enabling wall-to-wall global mapping. It outperforms traditional allometric equations, increasing R2 from 0.26 to 0.84 and reducing RMSE from 2.43 m to 1.14 m for temperate PFTs. The resulting map reveals distinct PFT-specific patterns, with large crowns in tropical rainforests, deep narrow crowns in boreal PFTs (mean AR = 1.8±0.7), and wide shallow crowns in temperate regions (mean AR = 0.95±0.4). We also found that AR remains relatively invariant with height, suggesting its potential as a robust structural parameter for modeling. This dataset provides a novel gridded benchmark for ecological studies, remote-sensing retrieval applications, and Earth system models to advance vegetation dynamics and the carbon cycle.

verified_metadata.title: A global 500 m dataset of tree crown morphology to advance vegetation modeling and management
verified_metadata.abstract: Tree crown architecture varies widely across the globe and strongly influences ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, the carbon cycle, and land–atmosphere interactions. However, its global variability and spatial patterns remain poorly quantified due to sparse field and LiDAR measurements, limiting large-scale ecological and modeling applications. Here, we present a globally consistent 500 m tree crown structure dataset, including crown depth (CD), crown width (CW), and aspect ratio (AR, defined as CD/CW) across eight plant functional types (PFTs). The dataset was generated by linking tree-level crown observations, including 218,942 CW records and 6,109 CD measurements, with tree height and bioclimatic predictors. PFT-specific Random Forest models were used to characterize crown structure–height relationships and then applied globally to produce wall-to-wall maps. These models outperform the best-fitting allometric equations, increasing R2 from 0.26 to 0.84 and reducing RMSE from 2.43 m to 1.14 m for temperate PFTs. AR showed weak dependence on tree height, suggesting that it captures ecologically meaningful variation in crown form beyond overall tree size. We also provide uncertainty estimates for CD and CW to support cautious interpretation and downstream use. This dataset provides a novel gridded reference for understanding plant physiological processes along environmental gradients, improving biomass estimation, and supporting more realistic representation of crown geometry in Earth system models.

title: MS-AFNet: A multi-scale adaptive fusion network with high-resolution feature enhancement for tiny object detection in UAV imagery
abstract: Detecting tiny objects in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery remains a formidable challenge due to the diminutive pixel footprint of targets, severe background clutter, and the progressive degradation of spatial fidelity during multi-stage downsampling. This paper proposes MS-AFNet, an advanced deep learning architecture specifically optimized for robust tiny object detection in complex UAV scenarios. To counteract information loss in deep layers, we introduce a Multi-Scale High-Resolution Feature Enhancement (MS_HRFE) module at the P2 level, which effectively captures fine-grained morphological details through parallel multi-scale context branches and a dual-attention mechanism. Furthermore, an Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASC_FSF) mechanism is integrated to dynamically recalibrate spatial weights during cross-scale feature interactions, thereby suppressing background noise and enhancing adaptability to significant scale variations. Additionally, the RTAS_C3k2 module is designed to construct a parameter-efficient backbone, leveraging spatially sensitive guidance and partial texture enhancement to preserve localization accuracy. Experimental evaluations on the VisDrone2019-DET dataset demonstrate that MS-AFNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models. Specifically, evaluated on the rigorous test-dev set, MS-AFNet achieves an mAP 50 of 30.0%, exhibiting an absolute improvement of 7.7% over the YOLO11n baseline. Notably, the proposed model maintains a compact architecture with only 2.4M parameters, achieving an optimal trade-off between detection precision and computational efficiency in resource-constrained environments. This research provides a robust, high-precision detection solution for intelligent urban traffic management and large-scale UAV surveillance.

title: AFDINet: Adaptive frequency disentanglement and interaction in hybrid Mamba–CNN for optical-SAR land cover classification
abstract: The synergistic integration of optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery enables robust Earth observation by overcoming the limitations of single-sensor modalities, such as atmospheric occlusion and spectral deficiency. However, prevailing fusion paradigms typically treat multi-modal integration as a homogeneous spatial operation, neglecting the distinct physical properties inherent in different frequency domains. This oversight often results in the loss of high-frequency (HF) details, leading to fragmented boundaries in fine-grained land cover classification (LCC). To bridge this gap, this study introduces the Adaptive Frequency Disentanglement and Interaction Network (AFDINet), a hybrid architecture fusing CNN and Mamba. We devise a Learnable Frequency Disentanglement (LFD) module that reformulates wavelet decomposition as a data-driven process, adaptively separating structural consensus from modality-specific textures. Subsequently, a High–Low Frequency Fusion (HLF 3 ) module implements a role-aware interaction strategy, calibrating low-frequency (LF) geometry while enhancing HF details. Extensive empirical evaluations on the Xi’an, YYX-OPT-SAR, and WHU-OPT-SAR datasets demonstrate that AFDINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in terms of OA, mIoU, and Kappa, while exhibiting exceptional resilience to cloud interference.

title: Global assessment of climate-driven lag and cumulative effects on vegetation using Earth Observation data and multivariable machine learning models
abstract: Vegetation rarely responds instantaneously to meteorological variations; instead, its adjustment often reflects delayed and accumulated climatic influences. However, these temporal effects have not been comprehensively analyzed at the global scale, particularly with higher-resolution Earth Observation (EO) data and across multiple climate drivers. By leveraging EO datasets and modeling approaches, this study characterizes global trends in vegetation and climate, evaluates time effects, and develops climate–vegetation regression and prediction models. Our results revealed normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) increase alongside shifts in key climatic variables during the study period. A large proportion of vegetated regions showed temporal responses, with heterogeneity in major climate zones. title: A framework for assessing rainfall extremes induced aboveground biomass loss from multisource remote sensing data
abstract: Increasingly frequent and intense rainfall extremes can trigger flooding, landslides, and severe soil erosion, leading to substantial losses of vegetation aboveground biomass (AGB). However, event-scale assessments of rainfall extremes induced AGB loss remain largely unexplored. Here, we propose a framework to estimate event-scale AGB loss induced by extreme rainfall events. The framework integrates high-resolution change detection techniques to identify vegetation loss sites with an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-based downscaling approach to derive sub-meter AGB from coarse-resolution AGB products. We evaluated the framework across three extreme rainfall events in China: Beijing (2023), Luochuan (2021), and Zixing (2024). The framework achieved high accuracy across all case studies, with F1 scores of 0.94, 0.92, and 0.94 for three events in identifying loss sites, as well as an R 2 value of 0.88 and RMSE of 4.44 Mg/ha for downscaled high-resolution AGB estimates. We further apply a Random Forest-based residual modeling to investigate model errors, indicating that terrain-related factors play a dominant role in shaping the variability of AGB estimation errors. The average AGB loss densities within identified sites are 75.21 Mg/ha, 67.08 Mg/ha, and 90.94 Mg/ha for three events, respectively. These findings highlight the framework’s potential in assessing event-scale AGB loss, providing a practical tool for ecological monitoring and disaster response under intensifying climate variability.

title: Spatiotemporal prediction of grass curing in Victoria, Australia using Multi-Source remote sensing and deep learning models
abstract: Degree of Curing (DoC) is an important ecological indicator for assessing grassland dryness and vegetation flammability, and accurate monitoring and prediction are critical for wildfire risk assessment in fire-prone regions. Focusing on Victoria, Australia, this study developed and compared several deep learning models for monthly spatiotemporal DoC prediction using multi-source remote sensing datasets derived from MODIS and ERA5-Land. Among the tested models, the Temporally Enhanced Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory model (TE-ConvLSTM) achieved the best overall performance, with an RMSE of 9.18 and an R 2 of 0.834. By integrating explicit temporal encoding and multi-scale spatial feature extraction, the model effectively captured seasonal DoC dynamics, more accurately reproduced elevated curing conditions and seasonal peaks during the fire-prone period and better represented spatial gradients and regional heterogeneity across the study area. The results demonstrate that the proposed temporally enhanced convolutional framework provides an effective approach for modeling spatiotemporal DoC dynamics and establishes a promising foundation for future investigations of predictive grass curing modelling for regional wildfire risk assessment and monitoring.

title: High-resolution (30-m) multi-decadal reconstruction of coastal water quality via Landsat-Sentinel fusion and ensemble machine learning (1985–2024)
abstract: Coastal water quality monitoring is pivotal for marine ecosystem management. However, current monitoring capabilities are constrained by a trade-off between the high accuracy of sparse in-situ sampling and the broad coverage but coarse resolution of traditional ocean color satellites. To bridge this gap, this study establishes a cloud-native framework coupling multi-source satellite fusion with machine learning to reconstruct a high-resolution (30 m) water quality dataset for the coastal waters of Guangdong, China, spanning a 40-year period. Leveraging the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, we harmonized Landsat-5/7/8 and Sentinel-2 MSI, processing over 22,172 valid scenes via a hierarchical regression strategy to overcome cross-sensor spectral inconsistencies. A Random Forest ensemble model was developed to retrieve Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD, R 2 = 0.76), Total Nitrogen (TN, R 2 = 0.86), and Total Phosphorus (TP, R 2 = 0.88). The time series unveils a significant upward trajectory in COD concentrations (+4.08 × 10 −3 mg/L/yr) with a regime shift around 2013. Spatially, COD plumes exhibited a “Westward Expansion” pattern during the wet season, contrasting with winter maxima for TN and TP. This parameter‑specific divergence demonstrates that organic and nutrient pollutants are governed by different source and transport mechanisms – a finding that single‑parameter studies would miss. We further explored the associations between water quality variations and environmental drivers, revealing a “Human-Climate Coupled” control pattern. Beyond this qualitative mechanism, we identify a dual‑process pathway and quantify a 6‑month lag between ENSO events and peak COD anomalies, moving the discussion from simple correlation to potentially predictive understanding. This study provides the first multi-decadal, high-resolution benchmark for the Greater Bay Area and demonstrates the value of cloud-based multi-sensor fusion for precision coastal management.

title: Machine learning correction of C2-Net for chlorophyll-a retrieval in optically complex small reservoirs
abstract: Accurate recovery of chlorophyll-a concentration in small inland reservoirs remains challenging due to optical complexity, land-water adjacency effects, and scaling mismatches in atmospheric correction algorithms. This study evaluates the performance of the C2-Net atmospheric processors (C2RCC, C2X, and C2XC) applied to Sentinel-2 images of 32 small reservoirs in Extremadura, Spain, using 94 satellite scenes and in situ chlorophyll-a measurements. While C2RCC showed moderate correlation with field data, it exhibited systematic underestimation, whereas C2X and C2XC produced extreme overestimations despite preserving strong monotonic relationships. To address these limitations, a machine learning-based correction framework was developed, combining rescaled processor outputs, interaction terms, and aggregate statistics. The proposed approach significantly improved recovery accuracy, reducing the RMSE by up to 35\% compared to the best baseline processor. Regularized regression models provided a solid balance between accuracy, stability, and interpretability, while more complex models achieved superior peak performance. Validation results confirmed good spatial transferability across reservoirs and trophic conditions, with greater uncertainty in hypertrophic scenarios. The proposed framework offers an operational and transferable solution for improving satellite monitoring of chlorophyll a in small, optically complex inland water bodies.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning correction of C2-Net for chlorophyll-a retrieval in optically complex small reservoirs
verified_metadata.abstract: Chlorophyll-a is a key indicator of phytoplankton biomass, eutrophication risk, and overall water quality in inland water bodies. Its accurate monitoring is particularly critical in small reservoirs, which serve essential functions in water supply, irrigation, and ecosystem services, yet remain largely underserved by conventional remote sensing products. Accurate retrieval of chlorophyll-a concentration in these systems remains challenging due to optical complexity, land–water adjacency effects, and scaling mismatches in atmospheric correction algorithms. This study evaluates the performance of the C2-Net atmospheric processors (C2RCC, C2X, and C2XC) applied to Sentinel-2 images of 32 small reservoirs in Extremadura, Spain, using 94 satellite scenes and in situ chlorophyll-a measurements. While C2RCC showed moderate correlation with field data, it exhibited systematic underestimation, whereas C2X and C2XC produced extreme overestimations despite preserving strong monotonic relationships. Rather than discarding these well-established processors, a machine learning-based correction framework was developed to extend their applicability to waters for which they were not originally designed. By combining rescaled processor outputs, interaction terms, and aggregate statistics, this strategy leverages the physics-based atmospheric correction already embedded in C2-Net while correcting its systematic biases through data-driven post-processing, thereby minimizing error propagation and maximizing operational applicability. The proposed approach significantly improved retrieval accuracy, reducing the RMSE by up to 35% compared to the best baseline processor. Regularized regression models provided a solid balance between accuracy, stability, and interpretability, while more complex models achieved superior peak performance. Validation results confirmed good spatial transferability across reservoirs and trophic conditions, with greater uncertainty in hypertrophic scenarios. The proposed framework offers an operational, transferable, and open-source solution for improving satellite-based chlorophyll-a monitoring in small, optically complex inland water bodies, directly applicable within existing Sentinel-2 processing workflows.

title: Hybrid physics–AI aerosol property retrieval algorithm for AMI/GK-2A with a deep learning radiative transfer emulator
abstract: Computational advances have enabled the evolution and refinement of satellite aerosol retrieval algorithms to mitigate issues in previous versions and improve their results. This study addressed a fundamental limitation in operational satellite remote sensing which is the trade-off between computational efficiency and retrieval accuracy in conventional look-up table (LUT)-based algorithms. The hybrid-Yonsei Aerosol Retrieval (hybrid-YAER) algorithm for the Advanced Meteorological Imager (AMI) incorporates a flexible aerosol model input, which became available by using a deep learning (DL) radiative transfer model (RTM) that replaces the interpolation-based inversion with LUTs. The DLRTM, trained with 100,000 Vector LInearized Discrete Ordinate Radiative Transfer (VLIDORT) code simulations using a Set Transformer architecture, accurately reproduces top-of-atmosphere reflectance (the root-mean-square error is about 0.002 for Mie calculations) at computation times about 0.1% of those of a conventional RTM. Additionally, a dust call-back procedure and an extended surface reflectance database based on multi-year minimum reflectance are introduced in the hybrid-YAER algorithm. Validation against AERONET and comparison with Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Dark Target (DT) and Deep Blue (DB) AOD products demonstrate that the new algorithm mitigates underestimation of low values of aerosol optical depth (AOD) and discontinuities of AOD values between adjacent land and ocean, while improving overall correlation (R increased from 0.757 to 0.767 for land pixels and from 0.856 to 0.881 for ocean pixels) and reducing bias. Over ocean, bias patterns become more linear, and the retrieval stability is improved (R² increased from 0.88 to 0.94) compared to the original version. Uncertainty analysis shows that retrieval uncertainty scales linearly with AOD, confirming the robustness of the hybrid algorithm. The concept of advancement in aerosol retrieval via hybrid algorithm can be applied to any other aerosol remote sensing algorithms.

title: An AI system for residential building damage estimation using multimodal remote sensing data fusion
abstract: The increasing intensity of tropical storms has created an urgent need for rapid, reliable damage assessment. Although recent AI-based approaches have improved upon manual inspection, many rely on proprietary satellite imagery or ad hoc UAV datasets, limiting scalability, repeatability, and operational deployment. In this study, we develop a multimodal AI framework for post-disaster damage assessment using only publicly available remote sensing and geospatial data, including NOAA aerial imagery, Microsoft building footprints, and FEMA damage labels. A key methodological contribution is the use of spatially disjoint training and validation regions in the Hurricane Michael dataset to prevent geographic data leakage and to more realistically evaluate generalization to unseen locations, an issue that is frequently overlooked in geospatial AI studies. Using this rigorous validation strategy, we conduct a comparative evaluation of leading deep learning architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (ResNet and VGG) and the Vision Transformer (ViT). Model performance in classifying buildings as affected or destroyed is assessed using disaster-relevant evaluation metrics. Results demonstrate that the Vision Transformer consistently outperforms CNN-based models, likely due to its global self-attention mechanism, which more effectively captures spatial context in dense urban environments. Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of a scalable, public-data-based framework for rapid damage assessment, while identifying severe class imbalance as a key operational challenge, motivating the use of specialized loss weighting and data augmentation strategies in future deployments.

title: Navigating Hierarchies in Hyperbolic Space: A Knowledge-Driven Graph Network for Semantic Segmentation of Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Semantic segmentation of multi-scale remote sensing objects faces two key challenges: representing complex relationships and effectively integrating geographic knowledge. These relationships generate hierarchical patterns embedded with eigen properties, forming a nested system that exhibits exponential growth, a characteristic poorly captured by Euclidean-based deep learning models limited to polynomial expansion. Hyperbolic space offers a geometrically faithful alternative, but current hyperbolic neural networks rely on tangent space projections for computation, introducing significant approximation errors that degrade network performance. To address these challenges, we introduce a knowledge-driven framework founded on fully hyperbolic neural network operators. These operators are designed to be manifold-preserving, enabling all computations to be performed directly within hyperbolic space and thereby eliminating tangent space approximation errors. Building on this foundation, we propose a novel Fully Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network (FHGAT) that operates on a multi-relational heterogeneous graph representation of remote sensing objects. Our model effectively mines and integrates embedded knowledge from complex, multi-scale relationships in a bottom-up fashion. Extensive experiments validate its superiority; compared to a standard Euclidean baseline, our model increases object-level accuracy and Mean Intersection over Union (MIoU) by 7.2% and 7.6%, respectively. Notably, it also surpasses a state-of-the-art tangent-space approximation model by 5.4% in accuracy, confirming the benefits of its end-to-end hyperbolic design for resolving spectral confusion. This research marks a significant step in advancing remote sensing analysis from a data-driven to a more robust and interpretable knowledge-driven paradigm.

title: An optimization AI model based on MoE for retrieving land surface temperature and emissivity
abstract: The main drawbacks of contemporary MODIS land surface temperature (LST) and emissivity (LSE) outputs stem from cloud pollution, imprecision in atmospheric moisture vapor rectification, preliminary miscalculations of variable surface emissivity, and heterogeneity at the sub-pixel level, leading to significant potential for advancements in the reliability of these outputs. This study proposes an iterative optimization strategy based on an Optimization Artificial Intelligence Model Based on Mixture of Experts (Opt-MoE) model. Initially, a logical analysis based on physical principles was conducted using the radiative transfer equation to verify that the model’s input and output parameters align with the principles and determination criteria of parameter inversion. Subsequently, the radiative transfer framework was applied to model and progressively refine the MODIS thermal infrared channels, confirming the practicality of enhancement and determining the most suitable band configuration. Then, brightness temperature, LST, and LSE product data were collected in five MODIS thermal infrared bands. An iterative fine-tuning strategy was constructed based on the Adam optimizer to gradually optimize the Opt-MoE and obtain a product dataset that more closely approximates the real LST and LSE. Lastly, the Opt-MoE underwent retraining and was implemented for retrieving MODIS information. Outcomes demonstrate that, during the experiment with modeled data, in contrast to the four-band arrangement, the mean absolute error (MAE) in LST retrieval employing five-band inputs dropped from 0.6346 K to 0.5238 K, the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) rose from 0.9981 to 0.9993, and the precision of LSE retrieval likewise experienced substantial enhancement. Additionally, the discrepancy between the refined perturbed simulation data and the true simulation data was negligible. The optimization validation using observational data showed that, after iterative fine-tuning, the MAE of LST retrieval decreased from 1.7748 K to 0.7199 K, while the PCC increased from 0.9817 to 0.9973.

title: SAR2LiDAR: A deep learning-based cross-modal matching framework between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) are two fundamental active remote sensing technologies. Their synergistic use can significantly enhance the effectiveness of remote sensing applications. However, existing studies primarily focus on product-level integration, and direct mapping between SAR images and LiDAR remains a challenge due to cross-dimensional modality differences. In this paper, a deep learning-based SAR-to-LiDAR (SAR2LiDAR) matching framework is proposed, which enables direct matching between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds. The framework features a dataset generation method that creates accurate 2D-3D correspondences between SAR images and LiDAR point clouds. It explicitly models the geometric and scattering visibility relationships of SAR imaging, and employs an autoencoder-based deep learning model with specific global feature representation and cross-modal alignment capabilities. The proposed model is trained and evaluated using airborne LiDAR datasets from five urban regions: Barcelona, Hong Kong, Los Angeles, Tarragona, and Girona. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed SAR2LiDAR framework achieves accurate and robust matching performance across diverse urban scenarios, attaining an average recall@1 of 95.64%, which significantly outperforms the best competing methods by 13%. Moreover, an average recall@1 of 91.68% on out-of-distribution (OOD) test regions demonstrates the strong generalization capability of the proposed framework and its potential for large-scale remote sensing applications.

title: Federated learning in forest resource modelling and monitoring: Bridging data confidentiality and collaborative research
abstract: The availability of reliable ground-truth data is one of the main bottlenecks for improving high-resolution forest attribute maps from Earth observation data. This is underpinned by the European Union (EU) Forest Strategy for 2030 that underscores the need for harmonized, cross-border forest resource assessments that integrate both remote sensing and field-based National Forest Inventory (NFI) data. However, confidentiality constraints on NFI plot coordinates present a significant barrier to aligning these datasets, thereby limiting the development of unified forest monitoring systems that can fully leverage the potential of Earth Observation data. To overcome these data-sharing limitations we explored the effectiveness of a privacy-enhancing technique, known as Federated Learning (FL), that is a form of distributed computing aimed at preserving the privacy and confidentiality of data owned by different organizations. This methodology has been tested for the collaborative modelling and mapping of forest timber volume across four European countries: Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Italy. We employed a time-series convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture tailored to integrate 40 years of Landsat or 7 years of Sentinel imagery and terrain variables with harmonized NFI data from more than 85,000 sample plots. This model architecture was used for the FL approach and compared to traditional country-specific and centralized modelling strategies. FL models achieved predictive performances comparable to the traditional models, which proofs the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Centralized or global models showed slightly reduced performance compared to the national models, highlighting the value of fine-tuning with local ground-truth data. By aligning with the EU’s forest monitoring objectives, FL facilitates the generation of harmonized models and maps of forest features, like timber volume and biomass, that are critical to support evidence-based forest policy and management. The findings underscore the potential of FL to transform collaborative environmental monitoring, particularly in domains where data confidentiality and interoperability are critical.

title: A two-stage machine learning framework for Chl-a reconstruction and short-term prediction in eutrophic lakes using GOCI observations
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) in eutrophic lakes threaten aquatic ecosystems and public health, but short-term chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) prediction remains challenging because satellite observations are often discontinuous and bloom dynamics are regulated by interacting environmental and ecological factors. This study developed a two-stage Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) framework for satellite-derived Chl-a reconstruction and short-term prediction in Lake Taihu. The first-stage model (XGBoost_Interp) reconstructed Chl-a on dates without valid GOCI/GOCI-II retrievals and generated a continuous daily Chl-a series for 2011–2024, achieving good performance (R 2 = 0.83, RMSE = 5.72 μg/L, MAPE = 9.16%). Using the reconstructed series and environmental variables, the second-stage model (XGBoost_Pred) predicted subsequent Chl-a with comparable accuracy (R 2 = 0.83, RMSE = 5.62 μg/L, MAPE = 8.97%). However, independent validation from January to March 2025 showed lower accuracy (R 2 = 0.69, RMSE = 9.45 μg/L) and some overestimation, suggesting that further calibration and evaluation are still needed when valid satellite observations are unavailable for extended periods. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified wind speed, temperature, atmospheric pressure, day of year, and antecedent Chl-a as important predictors. After lake-specific recalibration, the framework also performed well in Lake Chaohu, indicating its practical potential for other large eutrophic lakes. Nevertheless, broader application requires further validation with nutrient-related variables, multi-sensor data, high-frequency field observations, and more lakes with different environmental conditions.

title: A high-resolution interchange classification model enhanced by multi-scale geometric structural feature fusion
abstract: High-accuracy classification of interchange structures from remote sensing imagery is crucial for urban transportation planning, intelligent transportation systems, and autonomous driving technologies. However, current research on classifying high-resolution remote sensing images of interchanges remains limited, particularly due to the lack of dedicated high-resolution datasets. In addition, existing GIS databases often suffer from incompleteness, lack of structural semantic labels, and limited timeliness, motivating the need for automated interchange classification from remote sensing imagery. To address this issue, this study constructs a high-resolution interchange classification dataset (HRIC dataset) using Gaofen-2 and Jilin-1 satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of 0.5–0.75 m. The dataset covers six common types of urban interchanges, including cloverleaf interchange, diamond interchange, roundabout interchange, T-interchange, trumpet interchange, and turbine interchange. Based on this dataset, we evaluate the performance of multiple deep learning models on the interchange classification task and propose a structural feature–enhanced classification framework tailored for accurate interchange recognition. The framework incorporates core structural modeling concepts from the StarInterchange module into the ResNet18 backbone to strengthen structural feature representation, while integrating the ELA attention mechanism to enhance sensitivity to local features. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized model achieves strong performance in identifying various interchange structures, reaching an overall classification accuracy of 79.10%. This study provides an effective method for the automatic recognition and analysis of complex transportation infrastructure and lays a foundation for future research on road segmentation and topological structure extraction.

title: From flood extent mapping to mechanism-aware flood products: integrating flood type classification into satellite-based flood monitoring
abstract: Flood type information is critical for effective flood risk management because dominant flood types are associated with distinct hydrodynamic behaviour, contamination pathways, and recovery trajectories. However, most operational flood mapping products provide only binary inundation extent, offering limited information for interpreting the dominant flood type and its likely impact characteristics. Existing flood type classification approaches rely predominantly on hydrometeorological observations and modelling, which are often unavailable in data-scarce regions and can be unstable in mechanism-complex environments such as estuarine deltas, urban river corridors, and coastal cities. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multi-CNN framework that integrates flood type classification directly into satellite-based flood mapping. The framework first uses a U-Net model for flood extent segmentation and then applies a CNN-based classifier for scene-level flood type identification by combining satellite imagery with auxiliary topographic and hydrological-context features, including DEM information and water connectivity ratios. Several CNN architectures were compared for flood type classification, with Inception-ResNet selected based on its performance–complexity trade-offs. To support model training and evaluation, this study introduces the World Flood Type (WFT) dataset, a new multi-event flood dataset containing 464 flood scenes from 120 flood events across 48 countries. Results show effective performance in both inundation segmentation and flood type classification. The U-Net model achieved 83.8% overall accuracy on an independent test dataset, while the final Inception-ResNet-based classifier achieved 93.0% scene-level overall accuracy and a scene-level macro-F1 score of 0.73 under dominant-mechanism conditions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of extending conventional flood extent products with scene-level attribution of dominant flood types using remotely sensed imagery and ancillary geospatial data, thereby providing more decision-relevant information for emergency response and post-disaster assessment.

title: LC-SLab — An object-based deep learning framework for large-scale land cover classification from satellite imagery and sparse in-situ labels
abstract: Large-scale land cover maps generated using deep learning play a critical role in data-driven analysis and decision-making across a wide range of Earth science applications. Open in-situ datasets from principled land cover surveys offer a scalable alternative to manual annotation for training such models. However, their sparse spatial coverage leads to fragmented and noisy predictions when used with existing deep learning-based land cover mapping approaches. A promising direction to address this issue is object-based classification, which assigns labels to semantically coherent image regions rather than individual pixels, thereby imposing a minimum mapping unit that controls spatial fragmentation. Despite this potential, object-based methods remain underexplored in deep learning-based land cover mapping pipelines, especially in the context of medium-resolution imagery and sparse supervision. To address this gap, we propose LC-SLab, the first deep learning framework for systematically exploring object-based deep learning methods for large-scale land cover classification under sparse supervision. LC-SLab supports both input-level aggregation via graph neural networks, and output-level aggregation by postprocessing results from established semantic segmentation models. Additionally, we incorporate features from a large pre-trained network to improve performance on small datasets. We evaluate the framework on annual Sentinel-2 composites with sparse LUCAS labels, focusing on the tradeoff between accuracy and fragmentation, as well as sensitivity to dataset size. Our results show that object-based methods can match or exceed the accuracy of common pixel-wise models while producing substantially more coherent maps. Input-level aggregation proves more robust on smaller datasets, whereas output-level aggregation performs best with more data. Several configurations of LC-SLab also outperform existing land cover products, highlighting the framework’s practical utility.

title: Generation of high-precision precipitable water vapor products from morphed integrated microwave imagery
abstract: Water vapor is a key component in regulating Earth’s climate system, and precise monitoring of its variability is essential for advancing weather forecasting and climate research. While the Morphed Integrated Microwave Imagery at the Cooperative Institute for Meteorological Satellite Studies (MIMIC) provides near real-time, high-resolution estimates of Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV), its utility is constrained by notable inaccuracies and systematic biases. To address these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid calibration framework combining Spherical Cap Harmonic Analysis (SCHA) with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to enhance the accuracy of MIMIC-derived PWV. The resulting dataset offers high-precision PWV estimates over North America spanning 2016–2024. Validation against Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) PWV measurements demonstrates substantial improvements, with root mean square errors (RMSEs) reduced from 4.1 mm to 1.6 mm for the 0.25° resolution product and from 4.1 mm to 1.4 mm for the 0.02° product—representing accuracy gains of 61% and 66% over the original MIMIC PWV. The optimized PWV exhibits negligible bias relative to GNSS data and improved spatial and temporal consistency. Additionally, the hybrid approach effectively mitigates common artifacts in the original MIMIC products, including striping, shot noise, land–water boundary discontinuities, and excessive spatial smoothing. Further validation using radiosonde observations and ERA5 PWV yields RMSEs of 2.2–2.3 mm (0.25°) and 2.1–2.3 mm (0.02°), corresponding to 44–49% and 41–55% improvements. This work significantly enhances the reliability of MIMIC PWV data, providing a robust, high-quality resource for weather and climate applications.

title: Pioneering Test-Time training for robust Fine-Grained chlorophyll-a retrieval from Sentinel-2: Unveiling China’s lake eutrophication dynamics (2018–2025)
abstract: Remote sensing retrieval of lake chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) concentration is essential for eutrophication assessment and water quality management, yet conventional models suffer severe degradation in large-scale, long-term monitoring due to domain shifts arising from inconsistent atmospheric correction (regional aerosol variability) and spatiotemporal heterogeneity in aquatic optical properties. This study pioneers Test-Time Training (TTT) for robust lake Chl-a retrieval. The TTT dual-task architecture—a primary regression head paired with a self-supervised spectral reconstruction head—enables real-time adaptation to test-domain distributions without retraining, effectively compensating for residual atmospheric errors and regional apparent optical properties (AOP) distortions. Based on the proposed algorithm, this study comprehensively analyzed the spatiotemporal evolution of Chl-a in 2,621 lakes (≥1 km 2 ) in China from 2018 to 2025. The results showed the proposed model achieved superior performance in Chl-a retrieval ( R 2 = 0.79, RMSE = 9.99 μg/L), outperforming conventional machine learning approaches by approximately 28 %-36 % and underscoring its robustness in optically complex inland waters. National Chl-a distribution exhibits a clear east-high, west-low pattern, with mean concentrations of 31.29 μg/L in the Eastern Plain versus 13.83 μg/L on the Tibetan Plateau. Regional analysis indicated that most regions exhibited a downward trend in Chl-a concentrations, suggesting an improvement in water quality. Bloom risk assessment, based on over 170,000 observations, indicates that the Eastern Plain lakes face “extremely high risk” (44.7 % bloom occurrence), requiring targeted management. The proposed lake Chl-a remote sensing retrieval algorithm provides a new paradigm for fine-grained global water quality monitoring and spatiotemporal analysis, holding landmark significance for global water environment surveillance and proactive management. The code is available at https://github.com/KustAIRS/SR-TTA .

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of grasshopper habitats under future climate projections, vegetation growth, and land use change
abstract: Grasshopper outbreaks pose a persistent threat to grassland ecosystems and livestock production, yet large-scale monitoring of their suitable habitats under future climate change remains challenging due to complex interactions among climate, vegetation, and land use. Consequently, this study, taking China’s grasslands as the research area, explores the relationships between grasshoppers, host plants, and the environment and constructs habitat monitoring indicators using future climate, land use, and topographic data. Building on this, an ensemble model comprising Random Forest, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine is established to monitor the grasshopper suitable habitats under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5) from 2021 to 2100. Results indicate that elevation, temperature seasonality, slope, and precipitation during the nymph and egg stages significantly influence grasshopper occurrence. Moreover, elevation, temperature seasonality, precipitation seasonality, slope, precipitation during the growth period, and isothermality are major contributors to host plant distribution. Suitable habitats are projected to remain concentrated in Inner Mongolia, northern Shaanxi, southern Gansu, Qinghai, and northern Xinjiang, with pronounced regional shifts over time. Low emission scenarios (SSP1-2.6) consistently possess the smallest and declining extent of most suitable habitats, whereas high emission pathways have the largest habitat, potentially creating environmental conditions that are more favorable for grasshopper persistence and expansion. The results provide spatially explicit insights for early warning, targeted monitoring, and sustainable grassland pest management in a warming world.

title: A transferable framework for roof vegetation mapping across tropical cities based on open-source multimodal data and morphology-aware UDASS
abstract: Green roofs play a vital role in urban sustainability, offering substantial environmental, ecological, and social benefits. However, automated roof vegetation extraction mostly relies on costly high-resolution data, with limited investigations in Global South cities. Existing methods insufficiently fuse multimodal priors and overlook domain adaptation, thereby constraining extraction accuracy and cross-regional generalization. This work presents a transferable open-source data-driven framework for cross-domain multimodal extraction and analysis of roof vegetation. Specifically, we introduce a multimodal transformer encoder to fuse Google imagery, Sentinel-2-derived products and OpenStreetMap building footprints at the feature level to improve extraction accuracy. We then propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive semantic segmentation (UDASS) model with morphology-aware pseudo-label correction to improve cross-domain generalization cost-effectively. Validated across six Southeast Asian cities, our framework achieves an F1-score of 81.71% for supervised source domain extraction and up to 70.85% for UDASS. Further validation on four additional cities spanning East Africa, South America, West Asia, and South Asia verifies its strong cross-regional generalization ability. Finally, approximately 297 ha of roof vegetation are detected across the six Southeast Asian cities, mainly on low-to-mid-rise buildings with distinct regional disparities and diverse vegetation intensity. This study delivers the first large-scale dataset on roof vegetation and green roofs for tropical Southeast Asia, establishes a cost-effective and scalable multimodal paradigm for cross-regional monitoring, and supports evidence-based green roof planning and analysis.

title: HeightCLIP: A vision-language network for height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery
abstract: Accurate height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery is a fundamental task with broad applications in urban planning and management. However, existing vision-based methods rely solely on visual features, which limits their ability to fully exploit height-related semantic information. Vision-language models, e.g., CLIP, offer a promising alternative by leveraging multimodal information, yet directly adapting them to height regression remains challenging due to their weak perception of continuous numerical values. To overcome this limitation, we propose HeightCLIP , a novel vision-language framework tailored for height estimation from monocular remote sensing imagery. The task-adaptive textual prompts and image-side representations are optimized under height supervision to derive pixel-text similarity features for accurate height estimation. Specifically, we design an interval-based prompting strategy that integrates learnable context tokens and a fixed natural language template with parameterized interval values, allowing CLIP to better comprehend height-related semantics. In addition, we incorporate a reciprocal cross-attention fusion mechanism to facilitate bidirectional interaction between visual and textual features, thereby improving cross-modal feature integration. Finally, building upon this enriched feature space, we impose cross-modal consistency constraints to ensure pixel-level correspondence between height descriptions and visual features, providing more informative representations for subsequent height prediction. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets i.e., Vaihingen, Potsdam, and Data Fusion Contest 2019 (DFC2019), demonstrate that HeightCLIP achieves competitive or superior performance compared with existing state-of-the-art methods, and comprehensive ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/songtaowhu/HeightCLIP .

title: MFRXG: A multi-feature stacking ensemble RF-XGBoost model for total nitrogen retrieval in the Yellow River from Landsat 8/9 data
abstract: Total nitrogen (TN) is a key indicator for assessing eutrophication in aquatic systems, and its concentration dynamics are influenced by a combination of hydrometeorological factors, terrain, and other pollution sources. However, traditional retrieval models based solely on remote sensing reflectance often suffer from limited generalization capability. This study develops a multi-feature stacked random forest (RF)-extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm (MFRXG) based on field TN data from automatic stations along the Yellow River (YR). The MFRXG integrates Landsat 8/9 satellite data, ERA5 hydrometeorological data, and terrain data to estimate the TN concentration in YR. Using an independent validation dataset in 2025, MFRXG demonstrates robust prediction accuracy and stability, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.75, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.53 mg/L, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 mg/L, outperforming multiple linear regression (MLR), support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural networks (ANN), RF, and XGBoost. Subsequently, the spatiotemporal changes of TN concentration in YR are investigated from 2015 to 2025. Results show that spatially, TN concentrations exhibit a fluctuating pattern with a generally increasing gradient from the upstream to the downstream of the YR. Temporally, over the past decade, TN concentrations along the main stream show an overall slight upward trend, which is primarily attributable to changes in concentration contributions from upstream areas. Overall, the proposed modeling approach provides effective technical support for long-term and dynamic monitoring of TN concentration changes in YR and fills the gaps in spatial and temporal coverage and assessment efficiency of traditional monitoring methods.
