title: Satellite-derived population-weighted NO2 exposure and inequality across African subnational regions for SDGs 3 and 11
abstract: Air-pollution exposure is a growing public-health and urban-governance concern in Africa, but comparable subnational evidence remains limited. This study constructs an Africa-wide Administrative Level 1 (ADM1) panel for 2019–2023 using Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), LandScan population, settlement, meteorological, and topographic data. We estimate area-mean NO 2 and population-weighted NO 2 exposure, quantify within-country inequality, assess population-pollution alignment, and examine interpretable natural and human-related associations. Population-weighted NO 2 exposure is spatially persistent and highly uneven, with elevated burdens concentrated in North African coastal and Nile-corridor regions, Southern African urban-industrial zones, and selected metropolitan or industrial ADM1 units elsewhere. Continental mean exposure declined slightly in 2020 and rebounded above the 2019 level from 2021 onward, consistent with a short-lived disruption of traffic and industrial activity during the COVID-19 period. National averages concealed strong internal concentration, with a limited number of ADM1 units carrying disproportionate national burden. Random held-out validation indicated strong predictive structure, while country-blocked validation exposed limited out-of-country transferability. Interpretable machine-learning attribution using XGBoost and SHAP showed that nighttime lights and built-environment indicators were strongly associated with exposure, while wind, temperature, precipitation, elevation, and slope further shaped the observed patterns. Sensitivity analyses showed that ADM1-level exposure rankings were robust to NO 2 -to-population-grid alignment choices and that GHSL built-environment covariates were stable between 2020 and 2025; independent near-surface NO 2 evidence in Accra further showed moderate spatial agreement and consistent Harmattan enhancement with satellite-derived NO 2 . The framework provides an Earth-observation-based baseline for identifying priority subnational regions, tracking exposure inequality, and supporting SDG 3- and SDG 11-relevant air-quality governance in data-scarce African settings.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PG-GVB: A prior constrained backscatter framework for P-band PolInSAR forest height inversion
abstract: Facilitated by the BIOMASS mission, P-band polarimetric SAR interferometry (PolInSAR) provides a key capability for large-scale forest height mapping and biomass estimation. Within this context, the random volume over ground (RVoG) model stands out for its physical consistency and broad applicability. However, at P-band, deviations of canopy backscattering from the exponential extinction assumption in RVoG lead to biased height estimates. While gaussian vertical backscatter (GVB) offers greater flexibility, its surplus parameters and unconstrained convergence raise robustness concerns, resulting in estimation biases that limit its widespread application. To address these challenges, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to link structure parameters to SAR observations, thereby imposing prior constraints. A parameter-guided GVB (PG-GVB) variant is developed within a three-stage framework, achieving improved performance while explicitly analyzing how different parameters influence robustness. Validation on BioSAR-2008 and AfriSAR-2016 shows that the best-constrained configuration reduces forest height errors by 20.5% (4.83 m to 3.84 m) and 26.5% (7.49 m to 5.50 m) relative to the exponential model at Krycklan and Lopé, respectively. These results reveal transferable optimization strategies, with shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis further quantifying feature contributions.

title: A machine learning framework for predicting agricultural terrace suitability using positive and unlabelled datasets: an application for the Troodos Mountains, Cyprus
abstract: Terraces are a defining feature of Mediterranean mountain landscapes, enabling agriculture on steep slopes while providing multiple ecosystem services. Land suitability analysis (LSA) can guide authorities and land users to sustainably manage and expand these environments. It typically requires fully labelled datasets, but in many real-world applications only a fraction of positive examples is available, with the rest unlabelled. This study aims to present an integrated predictive modelling framework that combines GIS with data-driven Machine Learning (ML) techniques, capable of learning from Positive and Unlabelled (PU) datasets for LSA. The proposed framework was applied to develop a terrace suitability map for Cyprus’ Troodos Mountains. A 5-m DEM was processed to extract the mountain area, with elevation ≥ 500 m and slopes ≥ 15%, defining the study area. Crop plots registered under the Single Area Payment Scheme of the European Common Agricultural Policy were used to classify the study area into Terrace-Present (TP) and Terrace-Absent (TA) cells, with TP serving as labelled positive and TA as unlabelled samples. A two-step ML approach was applied, first identifying reliable negatives from TA cells, then using these with TP cells for suitability prediction. The developed PU-classifier was evaluated under the selected completely-at-random (SCAR) assumption, achieving a Recall of 84.6%, Precision of 81.5% and an F1 score of 83%. Feature importance analysis identified land cover, terrain slope and tree cover density as the most influential parameters for terrace suitability. Comparative analysis between 2017 and 2024 revealed abandonment of terraced agricultural land (29% decrease) as well as revitalisation (12% increase). The resulting suitability map and accompanying data layers are accessible through a Google Earth Engine application, aiming to support informed decision-making for sustainable landscape planning.

A 5-m DEM was processed to extract the mountain area, with elevation ≥ 500 m and slopes ≥ 15%, defining the study area. Crop plots registered under the Single Area Payment Scheme of the European Common Agricultural Policy were used to classify the study area into Terrace-Present (TP) and Terrace-Absent (TA) cells, with TP serving as labelled positive and TA as unlabelled samples. A two-step ML approach was applied, first identifying reliable negatives from TA cells, then using these with TP cells for suitability prediction. The developed PU-classifier was evaluated under the selected completely-at-random (SCAR) assumption, achieving a Recall of 84.6%, Precision of 81.5% and an F1 score of 83%. Feature importance analysis identified land cover, terrain slope and tree cover density as the most influential parameters for terrace suitability. Comparative analysis between 2017 and 2024 revealed abandonment of terraced agricultural land (29% decrease) as well as revitalisation (12% increase). The resulting suitability map and accompanying data layers are accessible through a Google Earth Engine application, aiming to support informed decision-making for sustainable landscape planning.

title: Mapping the extent, type and remnant areas of the coastal dunes of Australia and New Zealand by integrating multi-source data
abstract: Accurate large-scale mapping of coastal dune types is critical for coastal management but remains challenging due to the dunes’ high spatial heterogeneity and the spectral complexity in coastal environments. Therefore, this study aims to develop a coastal dune mapping approach and demonstrate its applicability across Australia and New Zealand. Firstly, we leveraged geological maps to delineate the spatial extent of coastal dune fields, effectively masking out non-dune areas. Secondly, we applied an object-based image analysis (OBIA), followed by a random forest classifier that integrated multi-source features to classify six coastal dune types within the delineated coastal dune fields, including active dunes, foredunes, sandy beaches, semi-stabilized dunes, stabilized dunes, and wetlands (dune slacks). Based on this approach, we generated a 10 m fine classification map of coastal dune types across Australia and New Zealand, covering a total area of 27,564 km 2 . Accuracy assessment yielded an overall classification accuracy of 90.68 %. Most categories achieved satisfactory performance, with stabilized dunes showing the highest accuracy (96.81 %). We also found that approximately 498 km 2 of coastal dune area has been converted to urban development land. However, this development pressure was mitigated by conservation efforts, as 15,781.80 km 2 (59.44 %) of the total coastal dune area was situated within protected areas. This study provides a replicable methodology for large-scale fine classification of coastal dune types. The resulting map offers scientific support for monitoring coastal dune systems state and evolution under human intervention.

title: Geomorphology-constrained bathymetric inversion of turbid tidal channels using centerline-network priors and machine learning
abstract: Bathymetric inversion in turbid tidal channels remains challenging because of degraded bottom-related optical signals and complex-branched channel networks. This study investigates whether geomorphic structure can act as a stable prior for bathymetric reconstruction when the spectral-depth relationship breaks down. We develop a geomorphology-constrained framework that integrates UAV multispectral imagery, suspended sediment concentration, RTK-derived channel depths, and adjacent flat DEM constraints. A branching centerline network is first extracted to characterize channel organization, from which geometric and network-structural predictors, including normalized width, width-to-depth ratio, downstream accumulation, tributary order, and distance to junctions, are derived and used to construct a random-forest depth prior. Then, these predictors are refined through constrained optimization with anisotropic smoothing along channel directions and boundary consistency with exposed terrain. The framework is tested in a turbid tidal-channel system along the southern Yellow Sea and further evaluated through a transfer experiment in the Yangtze Estuary. Among all predictors, the width-to-depth ratio provides the greatest improvement in inversion accuracy, reducing RMSE from 0.30 m to 0.18 m (38 %), highlighting the dominantly geomorphological control on channel cross-sectional geometry. Overall, The provided framework achieves RMSE values of 0.15 m (RTK-based) and 0.23 m (DEM-based), outperforming empirical spectral, conventional machine-learning, and deep-learning approaches, particularly in scour zones, narrow tributaries, and channel confluences. In the Yangtze Estuary, the model attains an RMSE of 3.46 m (R 2 = 0.70), suggesting preliminary transferability across more than three orders (from ∼ 10 m to 10 km) of magnitude in channel scale. The results show that the main bottleneck in turbid tidal-channel inversion is not only optical degradation, but also the lack of geomorphic organization in model design. By coupling data-driven learning with structural and boundary constraints, this study advances a transferable inversion paradigm for optically complex coastal environments.

title: Reproducible mapping of marine biodiversity using autonomous surface vehicles and deep learning
abstract: Monitoring shallow-water marine ecosystems requires precise, low-cost and reproducible methods, yet traditional diver-based surveys are labor-intensive, subject to observer bias and limited in spatial coverage. In this study, we present an autonomous framework that integrates deep learning techniques with open-source data acquisition platforms to overcome these challenges. Our approach uses a transformer-based model to classify different coral morphotypes, seagrass species and benthic habitats. This model is trained on the publicly available Seatizen Atlas image dataset . Data were collected using low-cost autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) equipped with action cameras, differential GNSS receivers, single-beam echosounders and inertial measurement units. The ASVs provide precise geolocation, depth and attitude measurements, synchronized with image timestamps and embedded as standardized metadata, ensuring interoperability and reproducibility. Beyond image classification, the ASVs enable bathymetric surveys and photogrammetric reconstruction for three-dimensional mapping of surveyed areas. Field validation at Réunion Island and Aldabra Atoll demonstrates that this framework delivers cost-effective, non-invasive and standardized monitoring, while automating laborious annotation tasks and increasing survey scalability. By combining open-source datasets, AI models and versatile ASV functionalities, this methodology supports reproducible ecological assessments and informs conservation decisions.

title: Label-efficient mapping of unregulated waste dumps via mixed supervision with feature masked recovery
abstract: Mapping unregulated solid waste dumps from remote sensing imagery is important for environmental risk assessment and sustainable development monitoring, but remains constrained by the high cost of pixel-level annotation. Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) with image-level labels reduces annotation effort, yet often suffers from incomplete object activation, especially for waste dumps with irregular morphology, variable object scales, and visually confusing backgrounds. To address this problem, we propose a label-efficient mixed-supervision framework that uses image-level labels as semantic regularization and a small fraction of pixel-level masks as spatial anchors. The framework adopts an asymmetric design: the semantic learning stream regularizes backbone representations during training, while the spatial grounding stream learns the final segmentation path. During inference, the auxiliary semantic stream is removed, enabling direct segmentation without CAM-to-pseudo-label refinement or separate segmentation-network retraining. Within the semantic learning stream, the proposed SAM-FMR module combines an adopted Slice-and-Merge (SAM) strategy with Feature Masked Recovery (FMR). SAM preserves local details through slice-level processing, whereas FMR applies structured masking in the high-level feature space to encourage context-aware feature learning and more spatially distributed semantic responses. The framework further provides modular interfaces for interchangeable CAM-based weak-supervision modules and backbone-adaptive segmentation heads. Experiments on the newly constructed YREB dataset and the enhanced Global Dumpsite benchmark show that the proposed method improves over few-shot, pure weakly supervised, and semi-supervised label-efficient baselines under spatially independent validation, cross-dataset transfer, and conventional patch-level benchmarks. With only 1% pixel-level annotations, it reaches nearly 90% of the same-framework fully supervised reference, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between dense-annotation cost and segmentation performance. The datasets and source code are publicly available.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Integrating UAV image time-series with multi-source environmental features for sequential wildfire spread prediction
abstract: High-resolution UAV observations provide a novel perspective for monitoring wildfire dynamics. This study explores a new approach for wildfire prediction by integrating high-precision, multi-source spatial data. We introduce 3DConv-U-Net, a deep learning model designed to capture spatiotemporal spread patterns. The architecture uses a 3D convolutional backbone to process continuous fire sequences and a separate encoder for environmental factors. To address the scarcity of real-world data, we developed a simulation pipeline to generate minute-level synthetic dataset. This allows the model to learn the physical rules of fire spread at a high temporal resolution. Experimental results show that the model generalizes effectively from 30 m simulation data to 1 m UAV observations. Our approach achieves higher performance with a Sorensen index of 0.959 and a Jaccard index of 0.921. Notably, the model demonstrates improvements in computational complexity and inference for lightweight optimization. Compared to the Transformer-based model, it reduces the parameter count by 70% and achieves an efficient inference time of 47.8 ms/batch, providing a practical tool for real-time edge computing. This work demonstrates that data-driven models can maintain spatial consistency across different scales. The results can support continuous wildfire monitoring and more reliable emergency decision-making.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Self-supervised spectral unmixing using scene-aware deep priors
abstract: High spectral resolution of hyperspectral sensors facilitates the detailed identification of material, but the coarse spatial resolution affects accurate interpretation. In this regard, spectral unmixing techniques attempt to estimate the constituent materials (endmembers) and their fractional areas (abundances) within a pixel’s instantaneous field of view (IFOV). However, many existing methods optimize denoising, endmember detection, and abundance estimation separately, which can limit robustness under noise and spectral variability. The current study proposes a self-supervised deep learning framework for joint hyperspectral unmixing and denoising. A noise-aware probabilistic encoding strategy is adopted to model a structured latent space to implicitly detect the endmembers. Further, the proposed encoding scheme and regularizations ensure spatio-spectral fidelity to improve robustness to noise. Additionally, a contrastive learning mechanism is incorporated to improve latent separability and robustness to spectral variability. The framework also integrates available partial endmember priors when present and employs a policy-based adaptive refinement mechanism to update endmember estimates under complex noise and mixing conditions. In addition, a learnable loss-balancing strategy is introduced to reduce manual tuning and stabilize optimization. Experiments on synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate strong and balanced performance across reconstruction accuracy, spectral fidelity, and clustering quality, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for practical hyperspectral unmixing.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Enabling maize mapping in double-cropping regions of Argentina and Brazil without ground reference data by leveraging multiple satellite platforms
abstract: Large-scale maize mapping is challenging due to the lack of field-level datasets, which were essential for training machine learning models. The United States (US) provides abundant in-situ labels and national maize maps while Argentina and Brazil offered limited data and double-cropping further complicates mapping. In this study, we propose a survey-free method for maize mapping in Argentina and Brazil, with cropping intensity considered. We first pre-trained a maize classifier on US cornfields using Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) Relative Height (RH) metrics and Sentinel-2 imagery, then transferred this model to Argentina and Brazil to produce candidate maize labels at peak growth. We distinguished maize from other crops using phenology-based empirical thresholds. These high-confidence labels were then used to train a Random Forest model. Finally, we validated the maps with Google Street View (GSV) imagery and benchmark maps. Our framework produced 18,481 maize and 15,725 non-maize labels in Argentina and 2,125 first-season maize, 7,406 s-season maize and 7,643 non-maize in Brazil. Evaluation of our maize maps against GSV images showed satisfactory agreement, with accuracies around 90 %. The maps also aligned well with benchmark maps, exhibiting 91 % accuracy for Argentina and 88 % for Brazil. Our proposed frameworks can enhance maize mapping where field surveys are challenging.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SuperDove satellite detection of matter-loaded windrows with a focus on extreme environmental events
abstract: Matter-loaded windrows are high-density submesoscale accumulation structures that form on the ocean surface and are often associated with extreme environmental events. This study presents a framework for windrow detection using a UNet deep-learning model applied to Planet SuperDove (PSD) 8-band satellite imagery (FLODAS). The model is trained on hand-annotated cases representing a variety of windrows and evaluated using complementary performance metrics, demonstrating consistent detection across independent scenes, while also revealing scene-specific patterns of false positives. Spectral analysis and classification based on the spectral angle distance metric is used to examine the potential for discriminating floating matter types using the PSD bands. Limited ground-truth data and the incomplete spectral characterisation of floating matter currently constrain classification performance. Application of the framework in the Aegean Sea enabled the identification of surface matter accumulations linked to storm-driven runoff and riverine discharge. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework to support in situ sampling and debris-removal operations, as well as short-term assessments of matter transport and windrow dynamics. Overall, the proposed framework represents a proof-of-concept step towards the development of operational detection systems for surface matter and marine debris accumulations.

verified_metadata.title: SuperDove satellite detection of matter-loaded windrows with a focus on extreme environmental events
verified_metadata.abstract: Matter-loaded windrows are high-density submesoscale accumulation structures that form on the ocean surface and are often associated with extreme environmental events. This study presents a framework for windrow detection using a UNet deep-learning model applied to Planet SuperDove (PSD) 8-band satellite imagery (FLODAS). The model is trained on hand-annotated cases representing a variety of windrows and evaluated using complementary performance metrics, demonstrating consistent detection across independent scenes, while also revealing scene-specific patterns of false positives. Spectral analysis and classification based on the spectral angle distance metric is used to examine the potential for discriminating floating matter types using the PSD bands. Limited ground-truth data and the incomplete spectral characterisation of floating matter currently constrain classification performance. Application of the framework in the Aegean Sea enabled the identification of surface matter accumulations linked to storm-driven runoff and riverine discharge. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework to support in situ sampling and debris-removal operations, as well as short-term assessments of matter transport and windrow dynamics. Overall, the proposed framework represents a proof-of-concept step towards the development of operational detection systems for surface matter and marine debris accumulations.

title: DINO-Pheno-Cluster: Integrating few-shot foundation models and UAV time-series for spatiotemporal growth and functional characterization of alfalfa
abstract: Precise characterization of alfalfa growth dynamics is essential for breeding accessions with superior regrowth capacity, persistence, and yield stability. However, traditional plot level and coarse scale observations suffer from low signal to noise ratios particularly before canopy closure when phenotypic data are strongly affected by weeds and soil background. Moreover, existing studies rarely capture the dynamic mechanisms of crop development across the entire growth cycle. To address this, the DINO-Pheno-Cluster framework is introduced as a foundation model driven and mechanism decomposed phenotyping approach. This decoupled framework first utilizes DINO-XMem, a few-shot individual plant segmentation network based on DINOv3 and a dual memory mechanism. It subsequently applies parameterized dynamic modeling guided by growth process knowledge. Validation utilized high frequency Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery from 12 time points across three growing seasons covering 127 alfalfa accessions. DINO-XMem achieved an 89.54% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) under a 10-shot setting and maintained 86.77% under extreme 1-shot conditions. It successfully resolved dense canopy oversegmentation outperforming fully supervised baselines by 4.08% to 11.97% in mIoU. Crucially, the extracted high purity time series trajectories were parameterized into specific biological indicators including maximum growth rate, comprehensive regeneration index, and seasonal stability index. Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering based on these mechanistic traits identified four distinct functional ideotypes comprising High yield/High regrowth, Upright/Sparse, High stability/Persistent, and Short/Dense, all validated by ground measured biomass. This workflow establishes a precision screening tool for multi harvest crops advancing crop phenomics toward process level analysis.

title: PLGF-NET: A Physics-Guided Local-Global fusion network for GNSS-R high wind speed retrieval
abstract: Accurate global sea surface wind speed retrieval under high-wind conditions (> 15 m/s) remains a persistent bottleneck for spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R). Conventional data-driven models often experience severe performance degradation in these regimes due to inherent physical limitations, including long-tail data distributions, low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), and scattering signal saturation. To transcend these limitations, this study proposes the Physics-Guided Local-Global Fusion Network (PLGF-NET), establishing a novel physics-data dual-driven paradigm. At the data level, a Comprehensive Difficulty Score (CDS) is introduced to quantify the intrinsic physical complexity of Delay-Doppler Maps (DDMs). This metric drives a difficulty-aware hierarchical sampling strategy that rectifies long-tail biases and dynamically mines the scarce, high-wind scattering signatures. Within the network, a Physics-Guided Spatial Attention (PGSA) mechanism translates specular reflection theory into a structural inductive bias. This enforces a rigorous feature purification process, locking the receptive field onto the effective scattering window while suppressing peripheral thermal noise. Furthermore, geophysical consistency is guaranteed through a selective regularization mechanism governed by Sample Prediction Difficulty (SPD). Rather than applying uniform constraints, this approach adaptively enforces Geophysical Model Function (GMF) constraints exclusively on high-uncertainty samples, providing a robust physical anchor against signal saturation. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the exceptional robustness of PLGF-NET. The framework achieves a state-of-the-art overall root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.38 m/s and drastically compresses the high-wind RMSE to 2.40 m/s, effectively correcting systematic negative biases. Ultimately, this scalable and physically interpretable architecture provides a highly reliable Earth observation tool for high-wind marine environment monitoring.

title: Fusing very high-resolution aerial imagery with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series improves multi-year orchard type classification
abstract: Accurate mapping of perennial orchards is essential for agricultural management but remains challenging due to spatially discontinuous canopies and subtle phenological differences. This study presents an operational, application-oriented framework that integrates annual Very High-Resolution (VHR) aerial imagery (0.2 m) with monthly Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 optical time series to classify twelve orchard types across Israel from 2018 to 2023. By utilizing a multi-year dataset rather than a single seasonal cycle, we specifically evaluate model generalization and temporal robustness against inter-annual variability in phenology and imaging conditions. The dataset includes 106,413 labeled parcel-year samples from 19,950 parcels. We evaluate three model families: (i) satellite-only, (ii) VHR-only, and (iii) a multimodal mid-fusion deep-learning model (integrating spatial-structural and spectral-temporal modalities), under the same-year and cross-year (leave-one-year-out) scenarios. The satellite stream is modeled with a Lightweight Temporal Attention Encoder (LTAE) to capture seasonal dynamics, while the VHR stream uses a Swin Transformer backbone to extract hierarchical spatial features from 0.2 m imagery. The fused model achieved the highest performance across all settings (same-year OA = 0.890 ± 0.009; cross-year OA = 0.881 ± 0.014), outperforming both satellite-only (0.83) and VHR-only models (same-year OA = 0.846; cross-year OA = 0.795). In the best-performing fused cross-year scenario, class-wise F1-scores ranged from 0.71 for apple to 0.99 for banana. Fusion provided the largest gains in early-stage orchards (ages 1–3), where sparse canopy cover weakens spectral signals, but VHR imagery reveals planting geometry. Per-class analyses show that fusion benefits decrease with increasing mean NDVI, highlighting strong gains for sparse or deciduous orchards and minimal gains for dense evergreens. Overall, the results demonstrate that phenological time series and VHR spatial structure are highly complementary, enabling robust, operational orchard-type mapping and informing cost-aware workflows that selectively prioritize VHR acquisitions for young or low-NDVI orchards.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatially varying NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine forests across Poland using HLS, LiDAR metrics and GGP-GAM
abstract: Satellite-derived vegetation indices are widely used in forest monitoring, yet their interpretation is complicated by the fact that canopy reflectance integrates both environmental stress signals and structural variation in stands. This challenge is particularly important across broad ecological gradients, where relationships between optical metrics and stand attributes may be spatially non-stationary. Here, we analysed NDVI–stand structure relationships in Scots pine-dominated forests across the whole of Poland using 30 m HLSS30 imagery, LiDAR-derived stand metrics, and a Geographic Gaussian Process Generalised Additive Model (GGP-GAM). The study focused on closed-canopy, undisturbed Scots pine stands and examined annual NDVI variation in 2016–2022 across eight forest natural regions in relation to stand age, stand volume, top height, and the Relative Spacing Index (RSI). Mean NDVI showed persistent regional differentiation across Poland and ranged from 0.64 to 0.84. The proportion of NDVI variability explained by stand characteristics varied markedly among years and forest natural regions, indicating strong spatial and temporal heterogeneity in NDVI–structure relationships. In general, structural predictors explained a larger share of NDVI variation in years with more favourable moisture conditions, whereas in drought years this structural signal was less apparent, partly coinciding with lower and more compressed NDVI distributions. An illustrative regional analysis further showed that the direction and magnitude of the partial effects of stand attributes changed among years, demonstrating that the structural meaning of NDVI was not constant through time. The results show that NDVI should not be interpreted as a spatially invariant proxy of stand structure across heterogeneous forest landscapes. Instead, its information content depends on both regional context and annual moisture conditions. By combining harmonized optical time series, LiDAR-derived stand descriptors and spatially varying modelling, this study provides a framework for more robust interpretation of canopy greenness in large-area forest monitoring.

title: V-BUILD: A graph Transformer-based decision framework for selective updating of vector building data
abstract: Keeping vector building databases current requires deciding which database operations should be applied, rather than merely detecting binary geometric differences. Minor discrepancies caused by acquisition noise, representation style, or cartographic generalization may trigger unnecessary updates when using hand-tuned geometric thresholds. We present V-BUILD, a hybrid decision framework that assigns each matched building unit one of four operations: addition, deletion, replacement, or preservation. Deterministic rules handle existential decisions, while a geometry-aware graph Transformer learns the more ambiguous morphological decisions between replacement and preservation directly in the vector domain. The model encodes 1:1 to m:n matching relationships via Unified Correspondence Graphs and uses Adaptive Multi-stream Fusion to integrate node-, edge-, and graph-level geometric descriptors. Experiments on Amsterdam TOP10NL, Hamburg LoD1, and Mercer County OSM data, together with a difficult Amsterdam subset, show that V-BUILD performs well in within-domain evaluations on both authoritative and crowdsourced vector data, while leave-one-domain-out analysis indicates that direct cross-source transfer remains challenging under strong domain shift. On Amsterdam, V-BUILD achieves the best Replacement F1 of 89.44 %; on Mercer, it obtains the best Macro F1 of 88.51 %, outperforming the strongest GNN baseline by 4.22 percentage points; and on the difficult Amsterdam subset, it achieves a 4.51-percentage-point higher Replacement F1 than the strongest GNN baseline, with the associated reduction in paired sample-level errors confirmed by a two-sided exact McNemar test. These results indicate that V-BUILD reduces dependence on manually tuned geometric decision thresholds and provides a practical decision module for incremental vector building database updating.

title: Global cloud phase monitoring from FY-3G multi-angle polarimetric observations using the new MAPLE-CP framework with independent multi-site lidar validation
abstract: Global cloud-top phase monitoring is constrained by an observing gap: passive imagers provide broad coverage but limited vertical phase information, whereas active sensors provide stronger physical constraints only along narrow tracks. Here we develop MAPLE-CP, a Multi-Angle Polarimetric Latent-Enhancement framework for FY-3G PMAI cloud-top phase retrieval. MAPLE-CP links shortwave-infrared multi-angle polarimetric scattering information, DQ-1 ACDL cloud-top lidar labels, physics-guided feature screening, compact latent augmentation, and independent lidar validation. From approximately 140 PMAI variables, 50 physically interpretable predictors were selected and enhanced with six self-supervised latent descriptors. Using a 142,362-sample PMAI–ACDL cloud-top phase corpus, MAPLE-CP achieved internal accuracy, macro-F1, and AUC of 0.946, 0.897, and 0.991, respectively, on the original internal test split. Grouped split diagnostics clarified the evidence boundary of this internal benchmark, and independent validation using 6,433 ground-based lidar samples from 31 Chinese sites gave an agreement of 0.788 and macro-F1 of 0.780 within this external network. On an availability-limited shared-collocation subset with MODIS, Himawari-9, and ground-based lidar, MAPLE-CP showed higher agreement and macro-F1, suggesting complementary PMAI polarimetric phase information rather than a global product ranking. Overall, MAPLE-CP supports scalable cloud-top phase mapping and exposes residual mixed-phase uncertainty.

title: Deep spatial-spectral fusion of UAV RGB and hyperspectral imagery for potato plant disease detection
abstract: Accurate plant disease detection remains challenging when using single-modality data, which fails to capture comprehensive disease-related features. However, many existing studies rely on pixel-level classification or prior plant segmentation and lack explicit modeling of cross-modal interactions, limiting their ability to distinguish between healthy and diseased plants. This study presents a spatial–spectral fusion deep learning framework (S2-PDD) that fuses uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV)-based RGB imagery and hyperspectral-derived feature representations for plant-level detection of potato diseases (blackleg and Potato virus Y (PVY)), employing early fusion (modalities combined at the input stage) and middle fusion (features integrated at intermediate stages within the model backbone) strategies. The multimodal fusion models were compared against single-modal models and an existing S2ADet model. Model performance, assessed through five-fold cross-validation, demonstrated that multimodal models integrating RGB and vegetation index features achieved the highest mAPs of 86.65 ± 1.71 (%; E-RV model) and 85.74 ± 1.96 ( M-RV ), respectively. These mAPs were higher than those of all single-modal models, including the RGB-only (83.21 ± 1.46) and hyperspectral-only models (PCA features: 79.71 ± 1.45; vegetation index features: 85.31 ± 2.36). They also exceeded mAPs of multimodal models combining RGB with PCA features (early fusion: 83.00 ± 2.81; middle fusion: 83.11 ± 2.46; S2ADet: 84.04 ± 2.73), regardless of the fusion strategy. The superior performance highlights that vegetation index features provide strong class separability compared to other hyperspectral representations. The proposed models achieved strong plant-level detection performance, with AP of 78.65 ± 4.14 ( E-RV ) and 77.40 ± 3.46 ( M-RV ) for blackleg disease, as well as 84.82 ± 3.59 ( E-RV ) and 83.28 ± 3.86 ( M-RV ) for PVY. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV-based multimodal sensing for disease monitoring in cropping systems. A potato plant disease detection dataset was constructed and made publicly available, containing paired RGB and hyperspectral image tiles with bounding box annotations. title: FSIF-PCNN: A physics-constrained neural network for full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence reconstruction
abstract: Full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF; 650–800 nm) provides a powerful means to characterize vegetation functional status. However, current retrieval methods still exhibit substantial uncertainties due to their reliance on fixed spectral-shape assumptions or strong priors for SIF and reflectance reconstruction, introducing inherent model-form biases when these assumptions mismatch observations. To address this limitation, we propose a physics-constrained neural network, FSIF-PCNN, for flexible and robust full-spectrum SIF reconstruction. FSIF-PCNN leverages a U-Net architecture to extract multi-scale spectral features, while enforcing physical plausibility through radiative-transfer consistency constraints and spectral smoothness regularization. The method was evaluated using simulated test datasets and independent tower-based measurements through comparison with two existing methods (FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI). On the simulated test datasets, FSIF-PCNN achieved minimal systematic bias (ARE = -0.034 %) and superior spectral reconstruction accuracy (RMSE = 0.011 mW m −2 nm −1 sr -1 ; mean RRMSE = 3.87 %), outperforming FSIF-iPCA (mean RRMSE = 13.70 %) and SIFFI (mean RRMSE = 11.98 %). Tower-based validations confirmed exceptional agreement with SFM retrievals in the O 2 -A and O 2 -B bands (site-specific R 2 > 0.95). Compared with FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI, FSIF-PCNN demonstrated stronger accuracy and robustness across all validation sites, achieving site-mean RRMSE values of 5.74 % (DM), 4.46 % (GC), and 9.62 % (XTS) in the O 2 -A band, and 14.64 % (DM), 6.85 % (GC), and 11.22 % (XTS) in the O 2 -B band. These results demonstrate that FSIF-PCNN provides a flexible and physically constrained framework for full-spectrum SIF reconstruction, achieving improved agreement with independent references at the validated red and far-red bands.

title: Joint learning of frequency-spatio-temporal dependencies and structural context for optical-SAR change detection
abstract: Multimodal change detection combines multi-source remote sensing data, such as optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, to overcome the inherent limitations of single-mode imaging mechanisms, thereby enhancing the robustness and timeliness of change information updates. However, previous Optical-SAR change detection methods still face challenges, including inadequate modeling of both modality-invariant and modality-specific characteristics, difficulty in capturing cross-modal spatio-temporal dependencies, and underutilization of land cover structural context. To address these issues, we propose a novel Optical-SAR change detection framework, namely FSTS-Net. It combines semantic features from the frequency, spatial, and temporal domains with structural features to comprehensively capture change. First, we design a frequency-spatio-temporal feature encoder integrating wavelet convolution and graph optimization theory into a state-space model to decouple cross-modal features and model bi-temporal dependencies. Second, a multi-scale graph convolutional network is built to explicitly model the spatial correlations among surface objects, thereby enhancing the representation of structural features. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy dynamically adjusts the contribution weights of semantic and structural features to adapt to changes in information, effectively enhancing genuine change signals while suppressing pseudo-change. Our method demonstrates superior generalization and robustness over existing multimodal change detection (MMCD) methods, achieving mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 67.81 % on BRIGHT, 64.84 % on Wuhan-Het, and 88.55 % on Delta-SN6 datasets. The proposed FSTS-Net provides a reliable solution for multimodal change analysis. The code will be made available at: https://github.com/liuxuanguang/FSTS-Net .

title: Viewing-geometry effects on UAV-based tree height retrieval using BRDF-derived vegetation indices
abstract: Tree height is a key descriptor of forest canopy structure, yet a single nadir view captures only part of the directional structural information contained in canopy reflectance. This study investigated whether viewing geometry provides directional information useful for UAV-based optical tree-height retrieval in a Larix principis-rupprechtii plantation. Multi-angular reflectance observations extracted from overlapping UAV multispectral images were used to fit the RossThick–LiSparseR (RTLSR) kernel-driven bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) model. The fitted model was then used to reconstruct directional reflectance at 27 prescribed viewing geometries along the solar principal plane, while UAV-LiDAR data provided grid-level reference tree heights. Nine vegetation indices were derived and evaluated using linear regression, random forest, and gradient boosting regressor under single- and multi-angle schemes. DVI, EVI, GDVI, TVI, and GOSAVI exhibited consistent angle-dependent sensitivity to tree height, with their strongest correlations and lowest retrieval errors generally occurring within the intermediate forward-viewing sector (30°–45°) in the BRDF-derived dataset. For example, the absolute correlation between GDVI and tree height increased from 0.429 at nadir to 0.507 at 40°. Among the tested index–scheme–model combinations, the lowest validation error was obtained using GDVI under the Forward + 0° scheme with random forest, reducing RMSE from 2.19 m at nadir to 1.79 m (RMSE% = 10.25 %). However, the relative performance of the tested angular schemes varied among models, indicating that angular configuration and retrieval algorithm jointly affected performance, while increasing the number of angular features alone did not consistently reduce retrieval error. Overall, the findings indicate that viewing geometry can provide useful directional information for within-site optical tree-height retrieval and that intermediate forward-viewing information may complement nadir observations.

title: A multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and multi-dimensional attribute extraction in mountainous areas using deep learning technologies
abstract: Accurate mapping and monitoring of forest structure and composition in complex mountainous regions remain challenging because of crown occlusion, crown adhesion, and pronounced topographic variation. Moreover, current monitoring methods often focus on single-attribute retrieval and lack an integrated framework for collaborative multidimensional attribute extraction. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and integrated multidimensional attribute extraction in mountainous forests using deep learning and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. A two-stage segmentation method combining a U-Net++ deep learning model with a marker-controlled watershed algorithm was developed, followed by a sequential transfer learning strategy to facilitate knowledge transfer among individual tree segmentation, tree height prediction, and forest type classification. The proposed method was evaluated over a 5 km × 5 km area within the Wanglang National Nature Reserve (WNNR) using manually delineated tree crowns and canopy height models (CHM) derived from UAV LiDAR data. The results showed that the two-stage segmentation method combined the semantic representation capability of deep learning with the geometric partitioning ability of the watershed algorithm, thereby reducing under-segmentation caused by crown occlusion and adhesion in mountainous forests. The omission rate decreased from 9.12 % to 4.67 %, while the F1-score increased from 0.9298 to 0.9537. Sequential transfer learning also improved individual-tree attribute prediction, with the RMSE of tree height prediction decreasing from 7.1504 m to 3.4825 m and the overall accuracy of forest type classification increasing from 81.68 % to 92.51 %. The proposed method enables integrated mapping of individual-tree location, crown width, tree height, and forest type in complex mountainous forests, providing detailed information for precision forest management and forest carbon assessment.

title: Improving hourly PM2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance through physically constrained multi-task learning
abstract: Geostationary satellite-based PM 2.5 mapping increasingly relies on data-driven models using top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance. However, most existing approaches train a single estimator on temporally aggregated samples, implicitly assuming a stationary relationship between TOA radiative signals and near-surface PM 2.5 . This assumption overlooks the pronounced diurnal variability captured by geostationary satellites and limits the representation of hour-dependent aerosol–radiation interactions. To address this limitation, we developed a physically constrained multi-task learning framework, termed the Multi-Temporal Decoupled Attention Network (MTDAN), for hourly PM 2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance. The framework integrates three components: (1) a physically guided surface–atmosphere decoupling module that suppresses surface-background interference and enhances aerosol-sensitive information; (2) a multi-task attention architecture that jointly learns shared and hour-specific relationships between PM 2.5 and explanatory variables; and (3) a temporal-constrained loss function that exploits diurnal continuity to improve the consistency of sequential predictions. Experiments over eastern China using year-long Himawari-8 observations and ground-based PM 2.5 measurements demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed framework. MTDAN achieved an overall site-based validation R 2 of 0.89 with an RMSE of 9.27 μg m⁻ 3 , outperforming representative machine-learning and deep-learning models by reducing estimation errors by 21.7 %–27.8 %. The model successfully reproduced hourly pollution evolution, captured localized hotspots, and reconstructed season-dependent diurnal PM 2.5 dynamics. Ablation analyses further confirmed the complementary contributions of physical decoupling, adaptive feature weighting, and temporal-consistency constraints. These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling hour-dependent aerosol–radiation relationships can substantially improve geostationary satellite-based PM 2.5 estimation. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and robust solution for high-frequency air-quality monitoring and offers a general strategy for integrating physical constraints and temporal context into Earth observation applications.

title: A multi-scale spatial-conditioned spectral routing network for hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion
abstract: Hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HMIF) aims to reconstruct high spatial resolution hyperspectral images by jointly leveraging the complementary spectral information from hyperspectral imagery and the spatial details from high spatial resolution multispectral imagery. Existing deep learning-based methods typically improve fusion performance by enlarging the receptive field to capture richer spatial–spectral contextual information, which inevitably increase computational complexity and may introduce redundant spatial–spectral interactions. To address these issues, this study proposes a new multiscale Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Network (SCSRNet). Specifically, a Dynamic Fusion Gate (DFG) module is first developed to adaptively regulate the contributions of hyperspectral and multispectral features based on local spatial characteristics. Subsequently, a Large-Kernel Spatial–Spectral Residual Block (LK-SSRB) is designed, in which a Multi-Scale Spatial Perception Module (MSPM) captures spatial contextual information with large receptive fields, while a Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Module (SCSRM) is innovatively designed to dynamically establish spectral dependencies guided by spatial priors. Additionally, a Residual Scaling Connection (RSC) is introduced to improve optimization stability and feature propagation efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets (i.e. Pavia Center, Chikusei, and MDAS) and a self-collected UAV-based Daxing dataset have demonstrated that the proposed method consistently outperforms seven state-of-the-art approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The performance gains of the proposed SCSRNet observed on the MDAS dataset achieves improvements of 6.0%, 9.8%, 0.7%, 9.7%, and 7.2% over the second-best comparative method. Furthermore, SCSRNet achieves superior reconstruction performance with relatively low computational complexity, underscoring its effectiveness and practicality for HMIF.

title: Tropoformer-S: iTransformer-based spatiotemporal reconstruction of three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields integrating ERA5 reanalysis and GNSS observations
abstract: Spatially continuous three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields are essential for Earth observation and atmospheric sensing. The ERA5 reanalysis offers continuous coverage but is delayed by several days, whereas Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations are accurate and near-real-time but pointwise. This study develops Tropoformer-S, an iTransformer-based framework that reconstructs the regional delay field by integrating the two sources. The framework forecasts the ERA5-derived level-wise Zenith Tropospheric Delay (ZTD) at 15 pressure levels from 1000 to 550 hPa for 1 to 120 h, where the variate-token attention explicitly models the spatial correlation among grid points. The forecast field is converted into station ZTD through a physically guided retrieval chain and refined by GNSS-informed corrections along two complementary paths, harmonic self-correction for stations with local GNSS records and spatial reconstruction of the bias field for stations without. Over mainland China, the forecasts attain a level-mean RMSE of 2.84 cm against the ERA5-derived ZTD and outperform five alternative deep-learning architectures. The overall RMSE is 3.20 cm in 2022 and 3.23 cm in 2023 against GNSS, on average 18.64 % and 33.10 % below GPT3 and HGPT2, and the radiosonde evaluation shows a near-zero bias. The harmonic correction path lowers the RMSE to 2.79 and 2.98 cm and reduces the network bias to near zero, while the spatial correction path reaches 2.10 to 2.66 cm at withheld stations under nine network densities and largely removes the lead dependence. The framework thus fills the ERA5 latency gap with continuous tropospheric delay information for geodetic and atmospheric applications.

title: Virtual geographical scene modeling towards geospatial digital twins: A case study of urban highway tunnel scenarios
abstract: As a virtual component of the geospatial digital twin (GDT), the virtual geographic environment (VGE) has significant advantages in enhancing human geographic cognition and analyzing and solving practical engineering problems. However, existing virtual geographic scene modeling methods still have significant gaps compared to GDT, making it difficult to balance the ability to represent dynamic objects as required by GDT while preserving the geographic characteristics of VGE, such as spatiotemporal reference and multiscale representation. Against this backdrop, this paper takes highway tunnel scenes as an example. It proposes a modeling framework that leverages the synergy between perception data and scene knowledge to construct a virtual geographic scene for GDT. First, we constructed a multi-domain integrated knowledge graph of highway tunnel scenes to enhance the standardization and completeness of the modeling process. Second, we established a dynamic object detection network based on an improved YOLOv8 model, endowing the virtual geographic scene with the capability to represent dynamic objects. Third, we proposed a tunnel scene twin modeling method that integrates a knowledge graph with a perception network, enabling effective fusion of the static base and dynamic objects. Finally, we selected a tunnel in China as the study area, developed a prototype system, and conducted experimental analyses. The results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully constructs a GDT-oriented virtual geographic scene for highway tunnels. For the city-level model, over 93.6 % of points have an error of less than 0.1 m; for the component-level model, over 95.4 % of points have an error of less than 0.01 m; the model’s semantic accuracy reaches 95 %; the average modeling time for dynamic targets is 11.8 ms; and the average rendering efficiency of the virtual scene is 133.2 FPS. Furthermore, compared to existing scene modeling methods, the constructed scene integrates advantages such as geospatial and temporal references, multiscale representation, and dynamic object representation. Research results provide an example reference for intelligent management of urban traffic, and provide new ideas for virtual geographical scene modeling.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GICL-Net: A graph-interactive collaborative learning network for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR
abstract: Hyperspectral and LiDAR images, as a class of multi-source remote sensing data, have their own advantageous features. HSI contains rich spectral information, compared to LiDAR, which is more capable of reflecting the height information of the target area. However, determining the intrinsic correlation characteristics between HSI channels and fully exploiting the complementary characteristics of HSI and LiDAR to improve classification accuracy remains a challenging issue. In this paper, we propose a graph-interactive collaborative learning network (GICL-Net) for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR, which consists of a multi-scale spectral-spatial graph feature extractor (MSGE) and a cross-modality adjacency matrix fusion (CAMF) module. Specifically, MSGE is divided into two branches. One branch starts from the spectral dimension, defining each channel of HSI as a node to construct a graph network and mine potential correlations at the channel level, thereby capturing the intrinsic spectral correlation features of the target region. The other branch focuses on the height information of the target area, constructing a graph network at the geometric spatial level to extract representative height features. The CAMF module leverages the fused adjacency matrix to establish a cross-modal graph interaction mechanism, enabling the spectral features and the spatial features to achieve deep synergy through iterative updates in graph convolution. This generates cross-modal fusion features with fine spectral discrimination capability and spatial dimensional structural integrity. This method has been validated for effectiveness across multiple HSI and LiDAR datasets. In particular, on the Houston2013 dataset, the overall accuracy (OA) reached 98.91%, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.9882. Furthermore, compared with the baseline network (i.e., the conventional two-branch graph network, the overall accuracy improved by 6.58%. Our code is available at the link: https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/GICLNet .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mapping selective logging with Sentinel-1 image time series and a novel transformer-based model
abstract: Selective logging (SL) is a major driver of forest degradation, yet its small and short-lived canopy openings remain difficult to detect in persistently cloudy tropical regions. Optical approaches miss many events, while synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time series are challenging to model with architectures that either fuse multivariate features too early or smooth over transient signals. We present InterFormer, a Transformer-based architecture that jointly models feature interactions and temporal dynamics via a feature block with Multi-head Intercross Self Attention (MISA) and a temporal block with Multi-head Self Dissimilar Attention (MSDA). Texture features were further utilized as complementary input. Since precise SL labels are unavailable, the model was trained and internally tested using a weak-label benchmark, in which pixel labels were extracted within the official published Real-Time Deforestation Detection System (DETER) polygons. To complement this internal weak-label benchmark, we designed two independent practical experiments to evaluate the model performance in low-intensity Annual Production Units (UPAs) based on field-inventory data and at the municipality scale ( > 30,000 km 2 ) in the Brazilian Amazon. In the independent UPA validation, InterFormer localized 92.65% of tree-falling gaps in UPA areas and outperformed standard Transformer variants and Planet-based alerts from the Brazilian Forest Service by approximately 20% at the tree level. At the municipality level, our predicted alert polygons achieved the highest Detection Rate against DETER across multiple reference-overlap thresholds in both Paragominas and Feliz Natal, while also producing fewer unmatched alerts than RAdar for Detecting Deforestation (RADD) and Tropical Moist Forest dataset (TMF). However, substantial over-expansion of predicted alert regions remained. These results suggest that InterFormer provides a useful framework for representing weak and short-lived SL signals in Sentinel-1 time series, and that openly available SAR data have the potential to support large-scale SL monitoring under weak supervision. Nevertheless, the current municipality-scale workflow still relies on optical-derived masking as a supporting step, and the development of a fully SAR-only large-area monitoring framework remains an important direction for future work.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DecAttNet: A decoder-centric multi-task attention network for rapid, large-scale land use change detection and 2 M resolution products generation
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient resolution and a lack of fine-grained categories in traditional land use and land cover (LULC) products, this study integrates lightweight deep learning, a decoder-centric multi-task learning architecture, and a significant change attention mechanism to propose a deep learning framework (Decoder-Centric Attention Network, DecAttNet) for large-scale, high-precision land use change mapping. By mitigating cross‑task feature conflicts within the multitask‑learning framework via its significant‑change attention module, DecAttNet can adaptively focus on key change areas while sharing features and improving computational efficiency. Additionally, this study utilized DecAttNet to generate a 2023 land‑use product for North China (ten provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions) (LULC_NorthChina_2023) comprising 28 fine‑grained land‑cover classes based on 2‑meter high‑resolution imagery. The results of this study demonstrate that (1) DecAttNet significantly outperforms other deep learning models in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, with an average overall accuracy of 90.28 %, which is higher than the figures achieved by the FCNN model (83.12 %), the ChangeMask model (87.73 %), the BGSNet model (86.63 %), and the TripleS model (88.24 %), while improving computational efficiency by approximately 44 % compared to the FCNN model. (2) Based on an independent field validation dataset, the DecAttNet model achieved high extraction precision (precision = 94.86 %) for changed land cover features. (3) The LULC_NorthChina_2023 dataset constructed in this study, which is based on the DecAttNet model, combines high precision (precision = 91.85 %) with high spatial detail. (4) The DecAttNet model demonstrates significant temporal generalization capabilities, achieving average classification accuracies of 89.23 % and 88.78 % in selected sample test regions in 2024 and 2025, respectively, with interannual variability of less than 1.5 %, and exhibits high stability across different geographic re. The DecAttNet framework provides an efficient and accurate solution for large-scale, high-resolution land use dynamic monitoring, and the resulting dataset serves as a valuable benchmark for fine-scale environmental research.

title: A directional feature excavation transformer for oriented detection of small-scale ships in dense SAR imagery
abstract: The precise oriented detection of dense and small-scale ships within Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery constitutes a significant challenge for automated maritime surveillance systems because of intense clutter, minimal target sizes, and arbitrary rotations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a coordinated multi-stage feature refinement framework, termed DiFE-TransOBB, tailored for dense SAR ship detection. Rather than relying on isolated module enhancements, the proposed architecture establishes a progressive interaction mechanism across structural, spatial, and frequency domains. Specifically, the Directional Feature Excavator (DiFE) module can extract geometry-aware structural priors to suppress isotropic clutter interference, the High-Resolution Spatial Fidelity Preservation Branch (HSFPB) preserves fine-grained localization details of tiny ships, and the Dual-Domain Interaction Fusion (DualFusion) performs conditional frequency-domain refinement guided by these spatial-structural cues to disentangle ship contours from unstructured high-frequency sea clutter. Evaluated on the newly constructed DenseSARShip-v1 benchmark and further validated on public datasets, DiFE-TransOBB achieved the highest detection performance among the evaluated methods while maintaining a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and cross-dataset generalization capability of the proposed framework for oriented ship detection in dense and cluttered SAR scenes.

title: Tracking diurnal aerosol dynamics and smoke transport over East Asia using multi-geostationary satellite fusion (GK-2B, Himawari-9, FY-4B)
abstract: Continuous, high-frequency observations of aerosol optical depth (AOD) are crucial for understanding rapid aerosol dynamics and regional air quality. However, single geostationary (GEO) satellite retrievals suffer from severe spatiotemporal gaps and diurnal bias due to cloud contamination, extreme scattering angles, and strong spatiotemporal heterogeneity. To overcome these limitations, we propose a deep-learning fusion framework synergizing the spectral, temporal, and geometric complementarities of three GEO satellites (GK-2B, Himawari-9, and FY-4B) over East Asia. Central to our framework is a TabNet-based dynamic feature selection mechanism that adaptively weights heterogeneous multi-sensor inputs to suppress local retrieval errors. To ensure robust spatial generalization, we implement a two-stage transfer learning strategy: pre-training with spatially extensive MODIS data to establish large-scale spatial priors, followed by fine-tuning with high-accuracy AERONET observations to accurately resolve diurnal variability. Compared to single-satellite baselines, the fused AOD product from May 2024 to April 2025 significantly improves accuracy and spatiotemporal coverage. Specifically, it yields an overall cross-validation correlation coefficient (R) of 0.94, reduces root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 47%, and increases valid hourly matchups by 33.5%. Independent-site validation confirms its robust generalization across diverse terrains (R=0.88). Furthermore, a biomass-burning case study highlights its superior capability to reconstruct hourly smoke-plume gradients during rapid aerosol transport. Ultimately, this deep learning-driven fusion enables precise and continuous tracking of rapid aerosol dynamics over complex environments, thereby providing a robust observational foundation for regional air quality early warning and chemical transport modeling.

verified_metadata.title: Tracking diurnal aerosol dynamics and smoke transport over East Asia using multi-geostationary satellite fusion (GK-2B, Himawari-9, FY-4B)
verified_metadata.abstract: Continuous, high-frequency observations of aerosol optical depth (AOD) are crucial for understanding aerosol dynamics and regional air quality. However, individual geostationary (GEO) AOD products suffer from distinct spatiotemporal gaps and uncertainties driven by cloud screening, surface-reflectance assumptions, and strict algorithmic quality controls. To address these limitations, we propose a deep-learning fusion framework synergizing the spectral, temporal, and geometric complementarities of three GEO satellites (GK-2B, Himawari-9, and FY-4B) over East Asia. Central to our framework is a TabNet-based dynamic feature selection mechanism that adaptively weights heterogeneous multi-sensor inputs to suppress local retrieval errors. To improve spatial generalization, we implement a two-stage transfer learning strategy: pre-training with spatially extensive MODIS data to establish large-scale spatial priors, followed by fine-tuning with ground-based AERONET observations. Compared to single-satellite baselines, the fused AOD product from May 2024 to April 2025 improves accuracy and spatiotemporal coverage. Specifically, it yields an overall cross-validation correlation coefficient (R) of 0.94, reduces root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 47 %, and increases valid hourly matchups by 33.5 %. Independent-site validation shows consistent generalizability (R = 0.88). Furthermore, evaluations of extreme events, including severe biomass-burning and dust transport episodes, demonstrate that the fused AOD product can reconstruct hourly plume gradients during rapid transport. By improving the temporal characterization of complex aerosol environments, this deep learning-driven fusion approach provides a useful foundational dataset for future regional air-quality analyses and chemical transport model assimilation.

title: Automated conversion of unstructured mesh models to structured parametric CAD models for architectural applications
abstract: Parametric models are foundational to Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital construction, enabling efficient design, analysis, and lifecycle management. However, most 3D building models reconstructed from real-world data sources — such as 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or format conversion — are represented as unstructured mesh models. Although these meshes accurately capture geometric shape, they typically lack the parametric constraints, design intent, and procedural history inherent to native BIM objects. This semantic deficiency severely limits their direct applicability in workflows that require model editing, parametric adjustment, or semantic interpretation. To address this challenge, this paper presents an automated framework for semantic lifting of unstructured architectural mesh models into structured, procedural parametric CAD models. The proposed pipeline first analyzes the geometric and topological characteristics of the input mesh and employs a deep learning-based module to predict a plausible sequence of CAD modeling operations. Subsequently, a 2D parametric profile abstraction and parameterization module processes the geometric regions involved in the predicted operations, transforming them into constrained and editable 2D parametric profiles composed of basic geometric primitives, such as lines, arcs, and circles. Finally, a parameterization-driven reconstruction module executes the recovered operation sequence and parametric planar profiles within a CAD environment to procedurally regenerate a structured solid model with full parametric editability. Extensive experiments on diverse architectural datasets demonstrate the robustness of the proposed approach, showing that it can generate parametric CAD models that closely match the original mesh geometry while supporting reliable parameter-driven editing. This research provides an effective pathway for the semantic lifting of mesh-based building models, enabling their reuse in BIM reconstruction, digital twins, and architectural analysis applications.

title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN
abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. This study develops a kinematic interpretation framework that integrates InSAR displacement time series, transfer learning-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classification, and multi-source environmental data to characterize railway-corridor deformation in terms of its occurrence, temporal evolution, and environmental context. Sentinel-1 images acquired from January 2022 to December 2024 were processed to retrieve LOS displacement rates and displacement time series along the Kunming–Yuxi section of the China–Laos Railway. To reduce dependence on labeled InSAR samples, a transfer learning strategy was adopted, in which the TCN was pre-trained using simulated displacement sequences and fine-tuned with labeled InSAR observations to classify six kinematic patterns: stable, linear, step, piecewise linear, power-law, and undefined. The corridor is generally stable, with a mean displacement rate of −0.26 mm/year and stable points accounting for 77.96% of observations. Linear and step patterns account for 12.66% and 7.87%, respectively. Strong subsidence zones, where the localized displacement rate reaches −28.43 mm/year, are dominated by linear deformation. Pattern-based interpretation further shows that non-stable deformation is associated with Quaternary unconsolidated sediments, paddy soils, fine-grained soil textures, and urban expansion areas. These results indicate that InSAR-derived kinematic patterns provide an effective interpretive layer for linking railway-corridor displacement, temporal evolution, and environmental context.

title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
abstract: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNC BAO , Ctr 2 , mNDVI 705 ) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R 2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.

title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.

title: Bridging cloud-induced gaps in MODIS leaf area index products using high-frequency geostationary satellite observations
abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a fundamental variable for characterizing vegetation canopy structure and ecosystem functioning. However, persistent cloud contamination substantially constrains the spatiotemporal continuity of LAI products derived from polar-orbiting satellite observations. In contrast, geostationary satellites provide dense temporal sampling, offering a valuable observational basis for filling data gaps in polar-orbiting satellite products. To bridge this observational gap, this study develops an observation-complementary framework that integrates high-frequency Himawari-8 Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) observations with MODIS LAI products to achieve LAI reconstruction in cloud-prone regions. Within this framework, AHI observations are first used to retrieve LAI at a spatial resolution of 2 km using a Random Forest model trained with a high-quality MODIS-based benchmark dataset, and are then downscaled to 500 m using MODIS-derived spatial texture information. The reconstructed AHI LAI is subsequently integrated into low-quality or missing MODIS pixels to generate a fused AHI-MODIS LAI dataset over China. Validation against in-situ measurements and cross-comparison results show that the fused product maintains reasonable numerical consistency and stable temporal trajectories. Data availability increases from 70.70% to 90.90% under the 4-day compositing cycle. These results indicate that geostationary-polar-orbiting observation complementarity provides a practical pathway for improving the continuity and usability of optical LAI products in persistently cloudy regions, while remaining subject to the constraints of optical observations and cross-scale reconstruction assumptions.
