title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information
abstract: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.

title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM
abstract: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for transferable retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous tidal environments. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. Results showed that GA-ELM consistently outperformed the conventional partial least squares regression (PLSR) model and maintained stable retrieval performance across species, traits, and scales. At the leaf scale, R2 exceeded 0.85 for all traits using mixed-species datasets, indicating strong cross-species generalization capability. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery (R2 > 0.75), demonstrating effective transferability from leaf to canopy conditions. Spectral analysis further revealed that trait-dependent spectral response mechanisms and species-specific canopy organization jointly regulate the stability of trait-spectrum relationships, whereas GA-ELM improved retrieval consistency by stabilizing nonlinear spectral representations under heterogeneous spectral conditions. These findings demonstrate that stabilizing trait-related spectral representations is critical for transferable hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits and provide an effective pathway for large-scale trait mapping in coastal wetlands.

verified_metadata.title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM
verified_metadata.abstract: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for robust retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous mangrove spectral conditions. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. GA-ELM generally outperformed PLSR, RF, and conventional ELM in species-specific comparisons. Leave-one-species-out validation yielded R2 ranges of 0.61–0.75 for Cab, 0.60–0.72 for EWT, and 0.66–0.76 for LMA, indicating moderate predictive capability for previously unseen species, with performance varying among species and traits. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery (R2 > 0.75), demonstrating that the framework can be independently calibrated for canopy-scale retrieval. Independent cross-regional validation yielded R2 values of 0.60, 0.49, and 0.44 for Cab, EWT, and LMA, respectively, indicating moderate but reduced cross-regional transferability. Spectral sensitivity and band-selection analyses revealed species- and trait-dependent patterns that provided context for interpreting variation in predictive performance. These results remain conditional on one GF-5 acquisition per site and 30 m mixed-pixel conditions, and broader tidal-stage and cross-sensor validation is still required. These findings demonstrate the potential of GA-ELM for hyperspectral retrieval and spatial mapping of mangrove functional traits.

title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R 2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A Metro-InSAR Risk Index for corridor-scale displacement risk diagnosis of urban rail infrastructure
abstract: Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides dense displacement observations along urban rail corridors, yet converting point-based measurements into corridor-scale diagnostic information remains challenging. This study proposes the Metro-InSAR Risk Index (MIRI), a diagnostic index designed to convert multi-dimensional InSAR-derived displacement characteristics into displacement-related diagnostic levels for urban metro corridors. MIRI integrates displacement rate, cumulative displacement, local displacement heterogeneity, height-related variability, and temporal residual variability, thereby extending conventional velocity-based interpretation toward corridor-scale displacement-risk diagnosis. The framework was applied to the Kunming Metro Network using 198 descending Sentinel-1 images acquired from March 2018 to December 2024. The time-series InSAR results show that the network was generally stable, with line-of-sight (LOS) displacement rates mainly ranging from −6 to 3 mm/yr and 97.21% of coherent scatterers falling within the stable interval of −3 to 3 mm/yr. Localized displacement anomalies were mainly observed near line intersections, curved sections, construction-affected areas, and the Dianchi Lake shoreline. Based on MIRI, 78%, 17%, 4%, and 1% of valid points were classified as Levels D, C, B, and A, respectively, indicating a distribution dominated by lower diagnostic levels, with spatially confined Level-B and Level-A anomalies particularly along Lines 4 and 5 and in lakeside soft-ground areas. Multi-source contextual variables and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were further used to interpret the environmental, anthropogenic, operational, and displacement-gradient information associated with the MIRI-based diagnostic patterns. The results indicate that the spatial variation in MIRI is mainly associated with terrain-related conditions, corridor-scale displacement variation, metro operation, and urban development intensity. By deriving diagnostic levels directly from PSI-based displacement indicators, MIRI provides an InSAR-based screening tool for prioritizing displacement-related anomalies and supporting maintenance of urban rail transit systems.

title: Robust reinforcement learning multi-baseline phase unwrapping algorithm with JPEG-LS
abstract: Multi-baseline (MB) phase unwrapping (PU) breaks through the limitations of the phase continuity assumption, but existing MBPU algorithms cannot adapt well to noisy environments. A robust reinforcement learning integer programming multi-baseline PU algorithm with JPEG-LS (RL-MBPU) is proposed. First, the CP-PIP cut-selection process is formulated as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem. An efficacy-guided imitation strategy is used to initialize an MBPU-structure-aware single-cut policy, which is further optimized by an actor–critic method using Cut-PAR2-based trajectory returns to reduce the root-node proof cost. Finally, the initial ambiguity number solution is corrected using dynamic median edge detector based on JPEG-LS, and the PU is completed by using the prediction of the left, top, and top-left neighbors of the current pixel and combining it with the local gradient threshold determination. In both simulation and real data experiments, the RL-MBPU algorithm demonstrated stable PU performance, including computational efficiency and noise robustness for interferograms of different sizes. Compared with the minimum-cost flow and cutting plane–pure integer programming algorithms, the RL-MBPU algorithm reduces the root mean square error by approximately 61.2% and 14.5%, respectively, while improving efficiency by approximately 54.1% and 42.4%, respectively. This can further support high-precision synthetic aperture radar interferometry applications.

title: 3D building wireframe reconstruction via edge point regression
abstract: Despite significant progress in point cloud–based 3D building reconstruction, the effectiveness of existing methods remains constrained by four major bottlenecks. These include the scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets, the pervasive incompleteness and noise in real-world point clouds, the substantial memory consumption incurred by the edge search space, and the lack of adequate geometric constraints in network designs, which often causes loss functions to fail in capturing the underlying 3D structural regularities. To address these challenges, we pre-train a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework on large-scale unlabeled point clouds to learn generic geometric representations, and subsequently fine-tune it using only a limited set of annotated roof samples for 3D wireframe reconstruction. The key contribution of this work is the proposal of a new SSL-based framework that utilizes geometry aware edge point identification to facilitate wireframe reconstruction and avoid missing corners, thereby mitigating issues related to dataset quality and computational complexity. Specifically, the framework first leverages a pretrained SSL-based feature extractor to generate robust point-wise representations under sparse and imperfect inputs. Building on these features, an edge point–guided regression module predicts the parametric attributes of roof wireframes. To effectively supervise the training of this regression module, we formulate a joint loss function that optimizes two complementary objectives: (1) minimizing the Euclidean distance between input points and their nearest line segments, and (2) reducing the distance between candidate edge points and their projections on the reconstructed model. Coupled with bipartite edge matching and an edge-aware non-maximum suppression strategy, the proposed method ensures geometric validity while reducing computational redundancy. Extensive experiments across three datasets of varying geometric complexity and scale (Dense, Building3D, and the large-scale Tallinn City dataset) demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The SSL-based pretrained model attains 97% corner precision and 91% edge precision for wireframe reconstruction on the Building3D dataset, surpassing conventional baselines and approaching the performance of fully supervised methods. Remarkably, even under limited supervision, specifically utilizing only 50% partially labeled data during fine-tuning, the model maintains strong accuracy with 86% corner precision and 67% edge precision, underscoring its advantages over current SSL-based approaches.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Towards fractional vegetation cover mapping in complex mountain environments through a knowledge-guided unmixing framework
abstract: Mountain vegetation dynamics serve as sensitive indicators of environmental change, making accurate fractional cover mapping of primary components crucial for understanding ecosystem responses. This task has been facilitated by multispectral satellite imagery, particularly Sentinel-2, which provides continuous observations. To translate these observations into fractional cover maps, existing studies typically apply fraction estimation models to synthetic spectra derived from field-measured signatures. However, limited field surveys in mountain terrain present a data bottleneck for synthetic spectra construction, while complex vegetation composition introduces spectral ambiguities that existing methods struggle to represent. Therefore, this study develops a knowledge-guided unmixing framework for annual mapping of the fractional cover of herbaceous vegetation, woody vegetation, and bare land in mountain environments using Sentinel-2 time series. Specifically, to overcome data bottleneck, we develop a knowledge-guided strategy that automatically builds adaptive physio-phenological feature spaces to extract representative signatures. To resolve spectral ambiguity, we incorporate nonlinear mixing mechanisms to synthesize spectra that better represent complex mixing relationships. The synthetic library was then used to train Unmix-Net, a spectral-temporal regression model for fraction estimation. The framework was applied to the central Qilian Mountains and southern Hengduan Mountains spanning broad climatic gradients, validated with high-resolution UAV data. It achieved MAEs of 12.38 %, 8.58 %, and 9.82 % for herbaceous, woody, and bare land, outperforming existing models by up to 7.80 %. When implemented across landscapes ranging from arid steppes and alpine meadows to tropical rainforests, the framework maintained comparable performance. The comparative experiments further confirmed that the proposed extraction strategy improved the balance of component estimates, while combining complementary mixing mechanisms reduced estimation errors. By integrating domain knowledge into data-driven learning, this framework supports spatially continuous fractional vegetation mapping in mountain environments.

verified_metadata.title: Volcanic rock-supported zero-valent Fe/Ni bimetal activated periodate for the degradation of sulfamethoxazole: Performance, mechanism, and machine learning application
verified_metadata.abstract: This study employed plant extracts as precursors to synthesize a volcanic rock-supported Fe/Ni bimetallic nanocatalyst via pyrolysis for efficient activation of periodate (PI). The results demonstrate that, at a low catalyst dosage (0.1 g⋅L−1), the system effectively activates PI (1 mM), achieving over 95% removal of sulfamethoxazole (SMX, 2 mg⋅L−1) within 120 min. Quenching experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis confirmed that singlet oxygen (1O2) is the dominant reactive species, indicating that the reaction proceeds mainly via a non-radical oxidation pathway. Volcanic rock support optimizes Fe/Ni nanoparticle dispersion and inhibits aggregation; structural characterization verified enhanced defect density and abundant active sites, while the constructed mineral-metal interface accelerates electron transfer and PI activation. Machine learning analysis further identified defect degree (ID/IG) and pore structure as the key factors affecting catalytic performance. LC-MS analysis revealed that SMX degradation mainly proceeds via sulfonamide bond cleavage, aromatic oxidation, and isoxazole ring opening. Application tests using real swine wastewater demonstrated that the catalyst maintains high stability and strong anti-interference capability under complex conditions, sustaining considerable degradation efficiency during continuous-flow operation and repeated cycles. This study offers novel insights into the design of mineral-supported bimetallic catalysts for advanced water treatment applications.

verified_metadata.title: MACE-MAX: A fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potential for high-throughput screening and experimental validation of high-entropy M2AlC MAX phases
verified_metadata.abstract: The vast combinatorial space of multi-element M2AlC MAX phases renders systematic experimental exploration intractable. Here, we fine-tune the MACE-MP-0 foundation model on a compact training set of M2AlC compositions with N = 1–3 M-site elements to obtain MACE-MAX, a machine learning interatomic potential that predicts the formation energies of N = 3–6 compositions with an MAE of 5.3 meV/atom at ~70-fold lower cost than DFT. Combined with Monte Carlo M-site sampling, MACE-MAX screens all 465 equimolar compositions in a nine-element (Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Hf, Ta, Cr, Mo, W) design space, identifies ten synthesis candidates and reveals valence electron concentration and atomic size mismatch as the dominant stability descriptors. Synthesis and characterization of the ten candidates and a Group VIB substitution series validate the predictions on three scales. The IVB/VB compositions with the lowest Ehull form the MAX phase as the main product, whereas none of the compositions containing a Group VIB element does; EPMA confirms the predicted decomposition pathways; and atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM and EDS resolve, for the first time, M-site solid-solution disorder in a six-element HE-MAX phase, (TiVZrNbHfTa)2AlC. MACE-MAX thus provides a validated computational–experimental framework for HE-MAX discovery and for selecting precursors of high-entropy MXenes.

title: Ionically conductive hydrogels containing PEG side chains for mechanical signal sensing, Morse code communication and machine-learning-assisted input

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。机器学习处理含PEG侧链离子水凝胶压力传感信号，进行摩斯码及字符输入。

verified_metadata.title: Ionically conductive hydrogels containing PEG side chains for mechanical signal sensing, Morse code communication and machine-learning-assisted input
verified_metadata.abstract: Ionically conductive hydrogels (ICHs) are promising candidates for flexible sensors and artificial skins, but their conductivity and comprehensive properties are poor in special sensing scenarios. Herein, ICHs containing poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) side chains are developed. In such ICHs, PEG chains exhibit high freedom of motion and hydrophilicity, providing abundant bonding sites for water and cations. The ICHs are prepared by a macromonomer copolymerization method and amphiphilic triblock copolymer is introduced to enhance their mechanical properties. Conductivity of such ICHs is increased by increasing feeding content and molecular weight of double bond end-capped PEG macromonomers and a conductivity of 57.9 mS/cm has been achieved. Interestingly, such ICHs are promising in constructing flexible mechanosensors exhibiting multi-mode response ability, fast response speed, high sensitivity and stability. On the basis of a signal processing model and a machine learning algorithm, piezoresistive pressure sensors of such ICHs are demonstrated in Morse code communication and input of various contents (e.g., letters and numbers). Overall, this work provides a new clue to develop high-performance ICHs by molecular structure design of hydrogel network and candidate materials for for flexible sensing devices.

title: AI-revealed metabolic fingerprinting of ophthalmic diseases via a 3D energy-amplified coral nanomatrix

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。深度神经网络处理大量真实眼病患者代谢指纹图谱，诊断疾病并识别潜在代谢标志物。

verified_metadata.title: AI-revealed metabolic fingerprinting of ophthalmic diseases via a 3D energy-amplified coral nanomatrix
verified_metadata.abstract: The prevalence of irreversible vision-impairing ophthalmic diseases remains high, while current diagnostic methods heavily rely on expert experience, limiting their accessibility in primary care settings. To address this, the present study utilizes iron oxide semiconductor as a scaffold to precisely engineer a multidirectional energy-amplified coral nanomatrix. Combined with nanomatrix-assisted laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry (NMALDI-MS), this approach enables high-resolution metabolic fingerprint mapping of ophthalmic diseases in a single batch analysis. The nanomatrix integrates the semiconductor's superior band structure with a high-density three-dimensional(3D) synaptic tip array, which synchronously amplifies local electric fields across the entire matrix and enhances light absorption capability, significantly promoting the separation of photogenerated charge carriers. The 3D interlaced optical trap structure on the material surface extends the effective light path, further increasing light utilization efficiency. Abundant binding sites strengthen molecular–matrix interactions, accelerating ionization and deionization processes, achieving up to 103-fold signal enhancement compared with other iron oxide morphologies. Leveraging a neural network-based deep learning platform, high-throughput processing and diagnosis of metabolic fingerprint maps were rapidly completed for 398 patients with diverse ophthalmic diseases, leading to the identification of multiple potential metabolic biomarkers. This strategy provides a low-cost, high-throughput, and easily standardized universal diagnostic solution for ophthalmic diseases, demonstrating strong potential for large-scale deployment in primary healthcare institutions.

verified_metadata.title: AI and additive manufacturing driven design of rGO-cobalt oxide nanocomposite electrodes for supercapacitors
verified_metadata.abstract: This work couples statistical synthesis optimization with AI-guided electrode-design to boost the electrochemical performance of additively manufactured rGO-Cobalt oxide supercapacitor electrodes. The optimal synthesis conditions found using a full-factorial design of experiments (DoE), yielding a nanocomposite with well-dispersed Co3O4 and CoO domains embedded on a conductive rGO matrix to be further applied in inks. To decouple geometry-dependent effects from material contributions, 30 printed electrode architectures were systematically evaluated, producing specific capacitances of 59.7–96.2 F/g and establishing electrode topology as a first-order performance determinant. Machine-learning models based on Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) and Random Forest Regression (RFR) were developed using geometric descriptors extracted from the 30 architectures, yielding R2 values of 0.71 and 0.85 for MLR and RFR, respectively, with corresponding Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of approximately 8 and 6 F/g for MLR and 5.5 and 4 F/g for RFR, respectively. The RFR model was subsequently used to identify an optimized electrode architecture, which was experimentally fabricated and achieved a specific capacitance of 104.8 F/g by cyclic voltammetry, representing an approximately 9% improvement over the best-performing architecture in the original pattern library under identical conditions. The optimized electrode further delivered a rate-capability retention of ~92%, an estimated gravimetric energy density of ~12.5 Wh/kg. These findings demonstrate that coupling DoE-validated synthesis control with AI-generated electrode topology enables simultaneous improvement of capacitance, rate performance, and energy/power metrics without chemical reformulation, establishing a scalable and transferable digital-design framework for next-generation high-performance supercapacitor electrodes.

title: Machine learning reveals interaction-driven ecological responses of DNRA-associated taxa toward data-driven operation of anammox systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。随机森林等多模型联结环境变量与DNRA菌群相对丰度，解析厌氧氨氧化生态响应。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning reveals interaction-driven ecological responses of DNRA-associated taxa toward data-driven operation of anammox systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Predicting the relative abundance of DNRA-associated taxa may support microbial monitoring in anammox-based systems. However, the suitability of different predictive models and their taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns under low-carbon, nitrogen-rich conditions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we analyzed 1292 environmental observations and 94 microbial profiles collected over 62 months from laboratory-scale anammox reactors. Multiple machine-learning models were compared to characterize relationships between environmental conditions and taxon relative abundance. Across the evaluated random train–test splits, ensemble models generally outperformed linear approaches, although the best-performing model varied by taxon. Multiple linear regression predicted Candidatus Kuenenia best, whereas random forest or extreme gradient boosting models predicted Candidatus Jettenia, Fimbriimonadaceae, Limnobacter, and Alicycliphilus best under their respective splits. This contrast revealed distinct predictive response structures among taxa within the same engineered environment. SHAP analysis identified taxon-specific predictor contribution patterns: predictions for Candidatus Jettenia and Limnobacter were primarily associated with influent NH4+ and NO2−, whereas Fimbriimonadaceae and Alicycliphilus showed broader distributions of SHAP contributions. Nitrogen loading rate and inorganic nitrogen species (NH4+, NO2−, and NO3−) were important predictors within the fitted models, but their individual contributions were interpreted cautiously because of predictor collinearity. Organic carbon variables showed comparatively limited predictive contributions within the low-carbon operating conditions represented in the dataset. Overall, this study provides a comparative evaluation of taxon-specific abundance prediction models and a descriptive interpretation of their predictor contributions. The findings support hypothesis generation and the selection of variables for microbial monitoring, while independent and temporally structured validation is needed to assess model transferability, and controlled experiments are required to evaluate ecological mechanisms.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven multi-parameter optimization of molecularly imprinted polymers for pico-level vitamin C detection
verified_metadata.abstract: Molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional biological recognition elements because it provides molecular selectivity, chemical stability, and cost-effective fabrication. However, the performance of MIP-based electrochemical sensors remains sensitive to multiple interdependent fabrication parameters, making one-factor-at-a-time optimization inefficient and unable to resolve interactions between variables. Herein, we report a joint Bayesian surrogate-modeling framework for MIP-based electrochemical sensors, demonstrated for vitamin C detection, in which o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) concentration, template concentration, cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycle number, and rebinding pH are modeled jointly rather than independently, and a single-round, uncertainty-aware Bayesian recommendation step is used to select an untested fabrication condition. Twenty-five fabrication conditions generated by Latin hypercube sampling were used to train a four-dimensional Gaussian process regression (GPR) surrogate model, benchmarked against polynomial, support vector, and random forest regression by leave-one-out cross-validation. GPR was retained not for superior point-prediction accuracy but for its native predictive uncertainty, which enables an Expected Improvement acquisition function to recommend fabrication conditions that have not been measured; a recommended condition absent from the training set was confirmed experimentally, and, at five further GPR-recommended conditions, GPR's predictions remained close to the measured responses (R2 = 0.863) while predictions from the fixed, untuned PR and SVR models deviated more substantially under this GPR-conditioned validation. SHAP-based analysis quantified the relative contribution of each parameter to the predicted response, and two-dimensional response surfaces of the joint model visualized conditional response patterns between parameter pairs. Under the identified conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear range from 10 nM to 1 mM, a calculated limit of detection of 778 pM, and high selectivity against structurally related interferents. Detection was demonstrated in human serum and artificial urine, and a preliminary proof-of-concept in real urine collected after vitamin C intake showed good agreement with a commercial ELISA assay. Coupling joint multi-parameter modeling with uncertainty-guided recommendation offers a data-efficient route to the rational optimization of MIP-based electrochemical sensing interfaces.

title: Machine learning-assisted optimization of sewage sludge hydrothermal liquefaction for balanced biocrude oil yield, quality, and energy recovery

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。机器学习多输出建模及优化污泥水热液化，平衡生物原油产率、品质及能量回收。

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning-assisted optimization of sewage sludge hydrothermal liquefaction for balanced biocrude oil yield, quality, and energy recovery
verified_metadata.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of sewage sludge offers a promising route for waste valorization and renewable fuel production. However, existing machine learning studies on sewage sludge HTL remain constrained by insufficient sludge-specific analysis, inadequate multi-output prediction and optimization, and poor model interpretability. To address these gaps, this study developed a machine learning-assisted framework integrating model development and optimization, model interpretation, feature elimination, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization using a PRISMA-guided literature-derived HTL dataset comprising 594 data points from 120 peer-reviewed studies. Statistical analysis revealed that substantial variations in both input features and output variables among the four clearly defined sludge types, highlighting the importance of sludge-specific characteristics. The optimized models achieved reliable multi-target prediction, while SHAP analysis identified temperature, sludge type, and H content as the dominant predictors for yield, oil quality indicators, and energy recovery, respectively. Feature elimination reduced input variables by 38.9–66.7% while preserving predictive performance and maintaining consistent dominant features and response trends, demonstrating the robustness and interpretability of the simplified models. Pareto-based multi-objective optimization further identified a balanced HTL condition at 353.79 °C, 12.29 min, and a liquid/solid ratio of 41.01 mL/g, corresponding to a predicted biocrude oil yield of 43.76%, HHV of 34.63 MJ/kg, energy recovery of 90.14%, nitrogen and oxygen contents in oil of 2.84% and 19.55%, respectively. This work provides new insights and a data-driven strategy for accelerating engineered HTL toward desired biocrude oil production, offering a valuable reference for sustainable sewage sludge management, waste valorization, and renewable fuel development.

title: Interstitial hot-volume plasmonics for machine learning-assisted urinary SERS diagnosis of pancreatic cancer

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。机器学习分析尿液SERS生物流体谱，实现无创胰腺癌筛查及解释性标志物分析。

verified_metadata.title: Interstitial hot-volume plasmonics for machine learning-assisted urinary SERS diagnosis of pancreatic cancer
verified_metadata.abstract: Early detection of pancreatic cancer is hampered by the lack of a sensitive, non-invasive diagnostic platform. Although SERS-based approaches have been proposed for pancreatic cancer diagnostics, most volumetric SERS substrates rely on deeply confined hotspots near polymer templates, where limited analyte accessibility and substrate-derived Raman background can compromise spectral fidelity. Here, we introduce an interstitially localized plasmonic nanostar (IPN) platform that redistributes electromagnetic enhancement into analyte-accessible hot volumes above a three-dimensional Au/polystyrene architecture. Selective nanostar localization within interstitial regions enhances analyte–field overlap while suppressing polymer-derived Raman interference, enabling uniform, reproducible, and trace-level SERS detection. To resolve the complex signals of urine spectra, statistically selected Raman features were integrated with a logistic regression classifier, enabling discrimination between pancreatic cancer patients and healthy controls with an AUC of 0.991 and an accuracy of 96.0%. In parallel, spectral deconvolution using a reference library of urinary metabolites estimated metabolite-associated spectral contributions linked to cancer-related metabolic alterations. This integrated IPN-based SERS–machine learning strategy provides a practical route for non-invasive urinary pancreatic cancer screening and interpretable analysis of complex biofluid spectra.

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。多层感知器由分子描述符预测氧化电位，筛选并验证高压钠电池电解液添加剂。

verified_metadata.title: A machine learning-driven pipeline uncovers superior electrolyte additive for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries
verified_metadata.abstract: The discovery of electrolyte additives for high-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) remains constrained by the inefficiency of empirical trial-and-error screening across vast molecular landscapes. Here we report a machine learning (ML)-driven pipeline that bridges this gap, integrating RDKit molecular descriptors with a multilayer perceptron (MLP) regressor trained on 87,301 molecules to predict molecular oxidation potential (OP). Under a standardized benchmarking protocol spanning 11 regression algorithms, the MLP model achieved an R2 of 0.97 on the held-out test set and showed the lowest errors and the least severe underestimation in the sparsely populated high-OP region among the evaluated algorithms. Deploying this model across 1.03 million PubChem entries yielded 2291 candidates with predicted OP values of 4.0–6.0 V. From this pool, ifosfamide (IFO) was selected for experimental validation. The cells incorporating the IFO-containing electrolyte delivered 107.23 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles at 120 mA g−1, surpassing the baseline electrolyte (99.82 mAh g−1). SHAP analysis, parallel coordinate visualization, and 2D partial dependence plots revealed that the MLP model integrates fragment-level descriptors, molecular topology, conformational flexibility, and surface electronic properties to render its predictions, providing molecular-level insight into candidate prioritization. These findings highlight the effectiveness of ML in narrowing down large chemical libraries and identifying experimentally viable electrolyte additives for SIBs.

title: A physics-guided neural network with McAllister-inspired multibody aggregation: Generalizing viscosity prediction to unseen organic components in strongly non-ideal mixtures

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。物理指导McAllister神经网络学习多体组分相互作用，预测未见有机组分非理想混合物黏度。

verified_metadata.title: A physics-guided neural network with McAllister-inspired multibody aggregation: Generalizing viscosity prediction to unseen organic components in strongly non-ideal mixtures
verified_metadata.abstract: Reliable design of multicomponent fluids requires property-prediction methods applicable to unmeasured mixture systems. Kinematic viscosity is a challenging prediction target because of its sensitivity to intermolecular interactions and non-ideal composition effects. We developed a physics-guided, McAllister-inspired neural network that combines explicit, permutation-invariant n-body composition aggregation with a shared nonlinear mapping from molecular descriptors and pure-component properties to interaction contributions. We evaluated extrapolative performance on ternary mixtures spanning regular solutions and strongly non-ideal water-containing systems using nested leave-one-component-out (LOCO) validation that excluded each of 20 organic components from model development. Diagnostic fits showed that the McAllister n-body form accurately represented composition dependence, whereas a compact shared parameterization constrained the generalized McAllister model's expressiveness. The best-performing 4-body excess-log-viscosity neural network achieved component-macro average absolute relative deviations of 6.47% overall under LOCO and 9.98% for challenging water-containing systems. Under identical data and validation conditions, its errors were approximately half those of two representative general-purpose machine-learning baselines. Ablation analysis identified permutation invariance as the largest source of improvement, with an additional gain from explicit McAllister-type n-body aggregation and a suggested benefit of 4-body interactions in water-containing systems. Combining nonlinear interaction representations learned from molecular structure and pure-component information with physically structured composition aggregation enabled accurate, broadly applicable modeling of non-ideal mixtures. The architecture can accommodate additional components without increasing its trainable parameter count and may provide a general design principle for data-driven prediction of non-ideal mixture properties.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven fiber morphology optimization and phase-engineered piezoelectric nanogenerators for sustainable intelligent transportation monitoring
verified_metadata.abstract: Biodegradable self-powered sensing systems are highly attractive for intelligent logistics and smart packaging. However, their sensing performance is often limited by inadequate control of fiber morphology and insufficient utilization of the piezoelectric responses associated with different crystal phases. In this work, a strategy combining machine learning with crystal phase engineering was developed to fabricate high-performance cellulose acetate (CA)/Ba(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3-(Ba0.7Ca0.3)TiO3 (BCZT) piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs). A machine-learning prediction model was developed to correlate electrospinning parameters with fiber diameter, providing quantitative guidance for regulating fiber morphology. The resulting fibrous structure was associated with relatively uniform dispersion of BCZT fillers, increased interfacial contact, and improved stress transfer, potentially contributing to enhanced interfacial polarization and electromechanical coupling. Among the investigated compositions, the CA-R5T5 composite exhibited the highest piezoelectric output. An intelligent packaging system was further constructed by placing tetragonal-phase PENGs on the top and bottom surfaces to monitor vertical impacts, and rhombohedral-phase PENGs on the sidewalls to detect vibration and tilt. The integrated sensing system achieved real-time transportation monitoring without an external power supply. This work provides an effective strategy for developing sustainable piezoelectric sensing materials by coordinating the optimization of processing parameters, microstructure, and crystal phase, offering promising potential for intelligent packaging and logistics monitoring.

title: A Micromechanics-Based Data-Driven Failure Criterion for Fiber-Reinforced Composites under Multiaxial Stress States
abstract: Abstract Reliable failure criteria for fiber reinforced composites (FRCs) under general multiaxial stress states remain challenging, particularly due to the complex interaction of different failure modes. As a result, considerable research effort has been devoted to the development of data-driven failure criterion (DDFC), combining insights from micro-mechanical modeling and machine learning (ML). However, general multiaxial stress states have largely been excluded from such studies. The present work addresses this gap by deriving a DDFC from synthetic failure data generated with a micro-scale representative volume element (RVE). A neural network (NN) is trained to distinguish FRC-typical failure modes using a dataset comprising both fully general three-dimensional stress states and reduced stress states in which only subsets of the six stress components are active, both from proportional monotonic loading. This dataset composition is essential for obtaining a criterion that is robust across different levels of stress state complexity. The proposed model achieves an overall accuracy of 88% on synthetic test data withheld throughout the training. A detailed analysis of the misclassifications shows that most erroneous predictions occur very close to the decision surface between no failure and inter fiber failure . When this uncertainty is accounted for by accepting a tolerance of $$\pm {2}\%$$ in the predicted failure stress state, the effective accuracy in distinguishing failure from no failure on the test set increases to 95%. The established framework demonstrates how synthetic data from micro-mechanical models can be used to train and critically assess ML-based failure criteria, providing a basis for further development of DDFC for uni-directional FRC and more complex microstructures.

verified_metadata.title: Towards spatial–temporal intelligence on the shop floor: A cyber–physical internet constrained approach for LLM-based explainable traceability
verified_metadata.abstract: The effective operation of manufacturing systems fundamentally relies on the efficient flow and control of materials across the shop floor. However, existing approaches primarily focus on functional execution while neglecting the spatial–temporal context of production processes, resulting in limited traceability and weak interpretability. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces the concept of spatial–temporal intelligence (STI) into shop-floor manufacturing and proposes a unified implementation framework with corresponding enabling technologies. To support STI, a CPI-constrained standardized traceability representation, together with a handshake mechanism, is developed to achieve cyber–physical alignment of heterogeneous manufacturing data. On this basis, a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) is constructed to capture production knowledge, and a spatial–temporal context construction method is developed to integrate real-time localization data, event information, and process dependencies into a coherent representation. Building upon the KG and constructed context, a large language model (LLM)-driven reasoning framework is designed to generate structured, knowledge- and constraint-grounded explanations of operational deviations and their downstream impacts. Experiments conducted in a pilot-scale physical shop-floor testbed demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an explanation correctness of 0.96, exceeding the strongest baseline by 11.8 percentage points, while the cyber–physical alignment mechanism reliably distinguishes compliant, inconsistent, and authorized reconfigured executions. The proposed framework provides a unified foundation for integrating spatial–temporal perception and intelligent reasoning, advancing the development of next-generation smart manufacturing systems.

verified_metadata.title: Large language models for intelligent job shop scheduling systems: A survey of problem modeling, decision-making, and dynamic rescheduling
verified_metadata.abstract: Job shop scheduling is a core execution stage decision interface that connects production requirements with shop-floor execution in intelligent manufacturing systems. Existing studies have mainly improved schedule quality for well-defined scheduling tasks, focusing on efficient and feasible operation plans. However, real manufacturing systems require an end-to-end scheduling process that spans requirement understanding, task modeling, algorithm adaptation, and execution feedback, which still lacks systematic support. Large language models (LLMs), with strengths in natural language understanding, contextual reasoning, and interactive feedback, offer a technical path for strengthening key stages of this process. In response to this trend, this survey reviews recent progress in applying LLMs to job shop scheduling and builds a workflow-oriented analytical framework. It analyzes the technical basis and capability boundaries of LLMs in scheduling systems, discusses their role in transforming unstructured shop-floor requirements into entity relations, constraints, and objective expressions, and clarifies how they enhance scheduling reasoning through candidate schedule generation and assistance to existing optimization algorithms. The survey further examines how LLMs extend from offline scheduling support to dynamic execution, where multi-agent collaboration improves the response of scheduling systems to shop-floor disturbances. The review shows that LLMs connect key stages of the scheduling process, enabling intelligent manufacturing systems to better understand unstructured requirements, explain scheduling results, and support human-machine collaborative decisions. However, current research still faces limitations in output reliability, traceable explanation, real-time deployment, cross-scenario generalization, and industrial data security. Future research should further explore domain knowledge enhancement, human-centered scheduling, multi-agent systems, and sustainable manufacturing, enabling LLMs to become trustworthy, controllable, and deployable scheduling components for intelligent manufacturing systems.

title: Multi Objective Inverse Design of Cement-Based Pseudocapacitive Electrodes Using Interpretable Machine Learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。可解释机器学习学习水泥基电极配方与面能量密度和抗压强度关系，完成多目标逆设计。

verified_metadata.abstract: Integrating electrochemical energy storage into cement-based materials provides a route to multifunctional building components. Multicomponent formulations simultaneously regulate the pseudocapacitive active phase, cement hydration phases, conductive carbon phases and pore structure, leading to coupled electrochemical and mechanical requirements for cement-based pseudocapacitive electrode design. Therefore, an interpretable machine learning workflow was developed to establish predictive relationships between multicomponent formulations and the device level areal energy density and compressive strength of cement-based positive electrodes. The optimized gradient boosting decision tree models achieved testing R2 values of 0.881 and 0.853 for device level areal energy density and compressive strength. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified current density as the most influential feature for energy density. Features related to conductive networks and water-to-solid ratio also contributed to the predictions, with microstructural characterization supporting the proposed material interpretation. A candidate design window with a water-to-solid ratio of 0.80 to 0.83, the carbon black and carbon nanotube contents of 2.00 to 2.13 wt.% and 1.86 to 2.24 wt.%, the carbon fiber and MnO2 contents of 1.97 to 2.20 wt.% and 10.28 to 12.65 wt.% was identified using strength constrained multi objective particle swarm optimization. The selected formulation achieved 0.57 ± 0.01 mWh/cm2 and 3.13 ± 0.08 MPa, with prediction deviations of 5.26% and 3.51%. This work provides a data supported approach for formulation screening under coupled electrochemical and mechanical requirements.

title: Predicting bubble radius for wastewater aeration with diffusion-augmented machine learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of bubble radius is essential for the design and optimization of wastewater aeration systems. Machine learning can capture nonlinear relationships among multiple variables under coupled aeration conditions, but high-fidelity experimental datasets are frequently scarce and often limited to tens or hundreds of experimental data points. Here we show that a quality-controlled diffusion-augmented machine learning framework predicts bubble radius from 150 experimental samples with six input variables. Candidate synthetic samples generated by diffusion and generative adversarial network models were retained through positive value screening, empirical range-based filtering, diversity screening, and validation-guided acceptance. Among the six augmented architectures evaluated, Diff-CatBoost achieved a test-set R 2 of 0.97, with an RMSE of 0.20 mm and an MAE of 0.12 mm. Evaluation using 20 literature-derived samples not included in model development yielded a MARE of 4.12%. Interpretability analysis showed that gas flow rate and orifice diameter were the dominant factors. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity prediction under data scarcity relies on strategic quality filtering rather than unconstrained data expansion, and provide a useful reference for other data-scarce environmental engineering problems.

title: Clinical stewardship for medical AI translation: A systematic review of technological, human, and organizational barriers
abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems may perform well in controlled evaluations, yet challenges remain in their translation and implementation into routine clinical practice. This systematic review examines 247 original studies identified through searches limited to 2024-2025 publication dates and 31 clinical and translational journal titles. The most frequently coded translation-relevant evidence indicator is retrospective design (158 studies, 64.0%), followed by demographic or geographic data limitations (125, 50.6%), lack of qualifying independent external validation (71, 28.7%), small sample or data scarcity (51, 20.6%), and noisy or context-dependent labels (33, 13.4%). Categories are not mutually exclusive, and the estimates describe the sample defined by these filters, rather than all medical AI research. We integrate these findings with a "clinical stewardship" framework that distributes responsibility across clinical teams, developers, health systems, and patients while preserving the capacity of AI to reduce routine workload.

title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications
abstract: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. Segmentation and outcome prediction also show promise, whereas automated report generation remains limited by poor clinical fidelity despite strong linguistic fluency. Broader adoption is hindered by heterogeneous MRI acquisition, limited large-scale paired image-text datasets, and inadequate safety-focused evaluation metrics. Advancing clinical translation will require standardized multicenter datasets, stronger integration with electronic health records and pathology, robust evaluation frameworks, and improved model explainability.

title: In-context learning for medical artificial intelligence
abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables large language models to adapt to new tasks by providing task-relevant examples during prompting, without modifying model parameters. In medical artificial intelligence (AI), it may support rapid task switching and customization without fine-tuning. This review synthesizes ICL applications across medical domains, including clinical question answering, information extraction, documentation, and multimodal imaging. Although ICL can achieve strong performance on research benchmarks and early pilot studies, its behavior is sensitive to prompt design and example selection, raising concerns around robustness, bias, and reproducibility. We examine how emerging ICL approaches may evolve from static prompts into more adaptive clinical systems. Finally, we propose a framework for safe clinical translation through risk-proportionate evaluation, governance, and continuous monitoring. Together, this review positions ICL as a promising but immature adaptation strategy and outlines a structured pathway for its responsible deployment.

title: Physics-Informed Topological Graph Neural Networks for micromechanical insights and uncertainty quantification in void-containing composites

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。物理信息拓扑图网络替代含孔复合材料非线性有限元，并用可解释性分析孔隙聚合及失稳机制。

verified_metadata.abstract: Predicting the performance uncertainty of porous composites necessitates capturing the highly non-linear damage mechanisms governed by authentic defect morphologies. This study proposes an integrated experimental-computational framework to unravel these complex micromechanisms. First, high-resolution in-situ micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is utilized to extract stochastic, process-induced void topologies, directly informing the reconstruction of experimentally validated, elastoplastic Representative Volume Elements (RVEs). To decisively overcome the prohibitive computational cost of finite element analysis (FEA) for large-scale stochastic evaluation, we develop the Physics-Informed Topological Graph Attention Network (PIT-GAT). By abstracting microstructures into a primal–dual graph and integrating label-free physical soft constraints with weakest-link statistical pooling, PIT-GAT achieves an O(104) speedup over traditional non-linear solvers. Leveraging Explainable AI (XAI), the model autonomously reveals that void coalescence is fundamentally driven by diagonal plastic shear bands (30°–45°) rather than perpendicular Mode-I tearing. Furthermore, it naturally captures the classical size effect of void clusters. Finally, predictive uncertainty is reframed as a physically meaningful proxy for material instability, probabilistically mapping this variance to potential micro-damage bifurcation loci to establish robust, risk-aware design guidelines.

verified_metadata.title: Confocal microscopy segmentation via prototype-driven semi-supervised learning
verified_metadata.abstract: The segmentation of anatomical structures like corneal nerves and Langerhans cells in in vivo corneal confocal microscopy is vital for diagnosing many ocular and systemic diseases. While deep learning offers a promising path to automation, its clinical translation is hampered by domain shift and a scarcity of labeled data across multi-center cohorts. To address these limitations, we propose Semi-NC, a semi-supervised framework that learns domain-invariant representations from both labeled and unlabeled data through a synergistic, four-step cycle: (1) extracting multi-scale prototype features, (2) refining them via feature amplification regularization, (3) constructing and updating category-specific prototype pools by aggregating features, and (4) aligning pixels to prototypes via contrastive learning to optimize the feature space for precise segmentation. Extensive evaluations on seven datasets (10,987 images across 22 diseases) show that Semi-NC sets a new state-of-the-art, outperforming fully-supervised baselines with minimal labels. The framework also demonstrates strong generalization under in-distribution and out-of-distribution tests, along with a robust self-evolution capability that allows it to extend its functionality using unseen data while preserving performance on learned tasks. Its broad clinical utility is further validated by superior performance on retinal optical coherence tomography angiography. To support reproducibility, we will open-source the code and the first multi-center, multi-disease dataset with high-quality annotations at https://github.com/iMED-Lab/Semi-NC.

title: Predicting in vitro digestion of gelatin hydrogels using machine learning and representation learning for image processing
abstract: In vitro digestion models enable the study of gastrointestinal processes. In this study, we investigate protein digestion dynamics using hydrogels as substrates together with machine learning (ML) techniques for video-based image analysis to predict digestive conditions. Gelatin hydrogels were crosslinked with transglutaminase (TGase) and immersed in simulated gastric media with varying pH, ionic strength, and pepsin concentration. Their swelling behavior and degree of hydrolysis (DH) were monitored over time. In parallel, videos of the immersed hydrogels were acquired using a camera probe. The videos were analyzed by applying a comparison between a standard feature extraction method of hue saturation values (HSV) and applying representational learning employing a convolutional neural network (CNN) before performing the final classification of the digestion conditions with a multi-layered-perceptron (MLP). TGase-crosslinked gelatin hydrogels exhibit varying swelling and digestion rates, influenced by pH level, ionic strength, and pepsin concentration. Both the CNN-based and the HSV-based approaches determined the DH well over time. The CNN-based approach outperformed the HSV-based approach in identifying pH and ionic strength of the media, while the HSV-based approach better classified the pepsin concentration. The best results were achieved using a 60-minute degradation interval; nevertheless, 20-minute intervals already show predictive performance. The results demonstrate the potential of video-based ML-driven image analysis to monitor protein hydrogel digestion, even with limited data collection, and lay the way for non-invasive in vivo techniques to study digestion.

title: Pathology AI clinical integration: From promise to practice
abstract: Despite substantial advances in digital and computational pathology over the past decade, pragmatic and systematic guidance for translating AI models from research into clinical practice remains limited. Most existing frameworks offer only high-level recommendations on validation, regulatory compliance, and implementation, often lacking pathology-specific roadmaps aligned with laboratory standards. This review first summarizes current progress in digitalization and AI in pathology, with emphasis on key applications in biomarker quantification, molecular status prediction, and multimodality integration. We then outline nine major components essential for pathology AI clinical integration, from defining clinical needs through analytical and clinical validation, workflow interoperability, to health economics, and further summarize and compare eight available frameworks. Next, we introduce the AI Development and Optimization in Pathology for Translation (ADOPT) framework, a practical, phased deployment roadmap specifically designed to align with College of American Pathologists and Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CAP/CLIA) guidelines, to facilitate safe and effective clinical integration of pathology AI tools. We conclude by discussing future perspectives of digital and computational pathology in cancer care, emphasizing widespread clinical adoption of digitized pathology, effective multidisciplinary collaboration, and optimized pathologist-AI synergy to fully realize the promise of pathology AI.

verified_metadata.title: Transforming nanotheranostics with machine learning: From nanostructure design to self-powered sensor and RNA theranostic applications
verified_metadata.abstract: Nanotheranostics, utilizing advanced nanomaterials for improved disease management, overcomes the shortcomings of conventional diagnostics and therapeutics. Notwithstanding significant technological progress, the implementation of nanotheranostic materials encounters impediments, e.g., protracted nanoparticle synthesis, insufficient comprehension of nano–bio interactions, and difficulties in the chemistry, manufacturing, and regulatory frameworks essential for clinical application and commercialization. Machine learning (ML), a crucial subset of artificial intelligence (AI), offers tools that help streamline the labour-intensive processes associated with nanotheranostic materials, potentially enabling its wider adoption. Here, this review surveys machine learning usage in nanoparticle synthesis, nano–bio interactions, diagnostics such as self-powered sensing, therapeutic strategies, and RNA theranostics. It discusses how machine learning enhances the design of biomolecular nanostructures, allowing stable functional platforms for precise assessment and targeted treatments. The review summarizes the challenges in the burgeoning domain of machine learning-assisted nanotheranostics and examines the future directions for creating next-generation nanotheranostics via the utilization of dependable datasets and powerful machine learning models to enhance clinical outcomes for patients.

title: Causal Contrastive Learning for Reliability-oriented Fault Detection in Wastewater Treatment under Process Uncertainty

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。因果对比学习从BSM2及全规模污水处理厂数据中检测过程故障，服务具体环保处理过程。

verified_metadata.abstract: To ensure reliable operations and quality control in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), data-driven fault detection has received wide attention recently, but reliable detection of faults or failures with respect to process variables or quality-related variables remains challenging due to significant process uncertainty. In WWTPs, fault detection is usually affected by data uncertainty, operating-condition uncertainty, and inter-variable relationship uncertainty. These uncertainties are essentially caused by delayed water-quality measurements, wastewater influent loads, or other environmental factors, such as temperature and humidity. In response to these issues, this study proposes causal structure contrastive learning (CSCL) for reliable WWTPs fault detection. In this method, CSCL addresses observation uncertainty by learning window-level representations rather than relying on isolated delayed measurements. Also, it can handle operating-condition uncertainty through causality-preserving augmentation, which retains normal causal structures under admissible influent and process variations. Furthermore, inter-variable relationship uncertainty, by constructing causality-disrupted negative samples that break internal causal dependencies or perturb exogenous-disturbance-driven causal patterns, can be addressed efficiently. By comparing causality-consistent with causality-disrupted samples, CSCL can separate normal process variability from fault-induced causal changes, thereby strengthening the reliability of fault detection. Experiments on BSM2 fault scenarios and full-scale WWTP data demonstrate that CSCL can outperform other fault detection baselines.

title: Neural Scheduling for Carrier Aircraft Recovery with Bolter and Aerial Refueling

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。PPO在燃油、机械完好和着舰约束下优化舰载机回收次序，研究安全关键航空运行。

verified_metadata.abstract: Existing carrier aircraft recovery scheduling studies commonly assume a predetermined aircraft set, limiting their applicability to safety-critical operations involving bolter events, fuel-endurance risk, and online insertion of new-wave tasks. This study formulates dynamic carrier aircraft recovery scheduling as an event-driven sequential decision-making problem that jointly considers bolter recovery, aerial refueling, remaining-fuel evolution, and online task insertion. A Long-Range Dependency-Aware Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm, termed LDA-PPO, is developed by integrating a dynamic recovery pool with a multi-layer masking mechanism. The pool maps time-varying aircraft sets to a stable neural decision interface. The dynamic-recovery-pool and attention masks exclude empty slots from representation learning, while the action-feasibility mask excludes unavailable aircraft from action selection. Each aircraft is encoded as an aircraft token, and multi-head self-attention captures global dependencies in fuel safety, mechanical integrity, mission priority, bolter risk, and new-wave arrivals. In 128 single-wave scenarios with 32 aircraft, LDA-PPO combined higher mean composite objectives and low online computational cost with fewer touchdown fuel-reserve violations and better fuel reliability than most baselines. It handled different task sizes within the dynamic recovery pool capacity and multi-wave missions without parameter updates. The proposed method provides a reliability-oriented online decision-support framework for dynamic carrier aircraft recovery.

title: Pseudo-Anomaly Data Driven Robust and Confidence Information Redundancy Approach in Aircraft Components

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。鲁棒变分推理网络学习航空部件异常输入的概率表征，评估信息冗余与预测置信度。

verified_metadata.abstract: Information redundancy (IR) for flight parameters requires robustness to corrupted auxiliary measurements and confidence assessment of the resulting estimates. This paper proposes a Pseudo-Anomaly data-driven Robust and Confidence IR (PA-RCIR) framework. A Random Anomaly Scenario Generator (RASG) generates pseudo-anomalous auxiliary inputs through complementary signal-level perturbations while preserving their target references. A Dual-phase Robust Variational Inference Network (DRVIN) jointly learns from original and perturbed inputs using a probabilistic latent representation. An Empirical Cumulative Distribution function of prediction Statistical Features (ECDSF) constructs empirical confidence scores from repeated prediction samples and a normal-validation reference distribution. Experiments use real flight records from the Thor and Ibis UAV datasets, with angle-of-attack (AoA) redundancy as a representative task and separate training and evaluation on each dataset. Over ten runs, the mean absolute error (MAE) under normal inputs is 0.0120 on Thor and 0.0007 on Ibis. Under controlled bias and noise corruptions affecting five auxiliary-input channels, the corresponding values are 0.0200 and 0.0012. In both evaluated multichannel mixed-anomaly scenarios, PA-RCIR achieves statistically significant improvements over all six baselines for the three prediction-error metrics after Holm correction. Representative cases and expected calibration error analysis characterize the relationship between confidence scores and prediction quality, with calibration behavior varying across input conditions and prediction-sample statistics. These results support robust information redundancy with empirical confidence assessment under the evaluated input conditions.

title: Context-Aware Prompt Encoding Compression and Sentence-Level Pooling based LLMs for Industrial Equipment Health Status Prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。LLM跨模态融合维护文本和传感器序列，预测实际工业设备健康状态。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate forecasting of industrial equipment health states is crucial for improving system reliability, enabling predictive maintenance, and supporting intelligent manufacturing. Conventional forecasting methods primarily rely on structured sensor data and often fail to leverage reliability-related knowledge contained in unstructured sources such as maintenance reports and failure logs. Although large language models (LLMs) show strong capabilities in textual understanding, their application to industrial prognostics and health management remains limited due to weak integration with quantitative signals and sensitivity to irrelevant textual information. To address these issues, this study proposes a cross-modal forecasting framework, Context-Aware Prompt Encoding Compression and Sentence-Level Pooling–Large Language Model (CASP-LLM). The framework integrates maintenance text with sensor time-series data to improve equipment health-state prediction. Prompts derived from statistical characteristics of sensor signals guide context-aware encoding and sentence-level pooling to extract reliability-relevant semantic features, while a parallel pathway captures temporal degradation patterns from sensor observations. The resulting representations are fused for prediction. Experiments are conducted on public fuel cell datasets and two real industrial heat exchanger datasets. The results demonstrate that CASP-LLM consistently outperforms LSTM, Transformer, TimeLLM, and other comparative models across multiple forecasting horizons.

title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic-static knowledge injection for few-shot electromagnetic interference failure assessment via large language models

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。LLM结合物理静态知识与不确定性感知检索，在少样本条件评估电磁干扰导致的失效。

verified_metadata.abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) can reduce the reliability of electronic systems and lead to functional failures, making EMI immunity assessment essential for reliable system operation. However, such assessment usually requires many experiments, and the resulting data are often costly or unavailable. This makes few-shot EMI failure assessment difficult, especially when model uncertainty must be controlled and physical constraints must be respected. To address the above issues, we propose the Dynamic-Static Knowledge Injection Large Language Model (DSKI-LLM) for few-shot EMI failure assessment. The framework contains a static knowledge injection module and an uncertainty-aware dynamic module. The static module combines Domain-Corrective Alignment Loss with gated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to encourage representations consistent with electromagnetic knowledge. The dynamic module uses predictive entropy to estimate confidence and adjusts retrieval depth during inference. Low-confidence queries retrieve more historical EMI cases, while high-confidence queries avoid unnecessary context expansion. We evaluate DSKI-LLM on PhyEMI, a benchmark dataset built from a controlled EMI experimental platform. Results show that DSKI-LLM improves few-shot prediction over the evaluated baselines and produces more reliable probability estimates. By combining prediction with uncertainty estimation and adaptive evidence retrieval, the proposed method supports more trustworthy EMI failure assessment under limited data.

title: AI-Enabled construction safety management: A paradigm shift from passive compliance to proactive empowerment

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。系统审阅153篇技术研究并构建AI施工危险感知、决策和物理干预分类架构，包含实质安全工程综述。

verified_metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to construction safety through hazard recognition, risk assessment, monitoring, and decision support. Despite rapid advances, existing systems differ substantially in their ability to interpret risk, generate safety-related outputs, and assume intervention authority. This study develops a reliability-oriented maturity framework to classify AI-enabled construction-safety functions. A PRISMA-guided review identified 171 eligible publications, including 153 technical studies and 18 reviews. The technical studies were characterized using two complementary dimensions: Objective Scanning Response (OSR), describing risk-information processing, and Safety State Output (SSO), describing safety-related output. Building on these functional profiles, an L0-L5 maturity framework is developed to characterize functional position, intervention authority, Operational Design Domain, and fallback capability. A Perception-Cognition-Decision-Execution (P-C-D-E) architecture is further developed to represent the functional structure of closed-loop safety intervention, including fast-slow functional separation, state verification, and fallback. Representative scenarios illustrate the framework’s application. The coded evidence indicates a marked asymmetry between risk understanding and physical intervention. The framework remains theoretically derived and has not undergone independent maturity-classification validation. Its contribution is nonetheless substantive: it provides a reproducible classification procedure, an authority-allocation model, and a reliability-oriented evaluation pathway specifying the evidence required before higher levels of autonomous intervention can be justified.

title: HeatVision: Estimating human-centric radiative flux using physics-informed computer vision

ai4s_review.rationale: 全量漏采补录（DOI登记及正式摘要核实）。视觉模型学习光学图像至红外图像映射，再按物理辐射积分估计人体周围辐射通量和平均辐射温度，以790对实测图像验证。

verified_metadata.title: HeatVision: Estimating human-centric radiative flux using physics-informed computer vision
verified_metadata.abstract: Physics-based models to simulate radiative flux in an urban environment, a key driver of human body energy balances and heat stress, are limited by computational load and data availability, while purely “data-driven” AI approaches lack interpretability and robustness. To address this gap, we introduce HeatVision, a physics-informed computer vision framework that leverages widely available street-view imagery and meteorological data to estimate complex radiative fluxes. It employs computer vision algorithms trained on infrared thermography to transform optical images into synthetic infrared imagery, enabling pixel-wise integration of heat losses/gains across a 360°spherical projection. We validated the approach using 790 paired infrared-optical imagery taken in Hong Kong. HeatVision’s estimates of the mean radiant temperature (MRT) agreed reasonably well with measured data from a globe thermometer (with a MAE of 2.31 °C and an RMSE of 3.48 °C), outperforming a physics-based simulation tool (CityComfort+) in both robustness and computational efficiency. By combining physical principles with computer vision, HeatVision demonstrates that the longwave radiation component of urban radiative flux can be estimated from street-view imagery without 3D urban models. However, extending the vision-based approach to shortwave radiation, and validating across more cities and seasons still remains the primary directions for future work.

verified_metadata.title: SHAP-informed and uncertainty-aware urban flood susceptibility mapping for planning support: a CatBoost framework
verified_metadata.abstract: Urban flooding is a major hazard in Iranian cities, and Shiraz is repeatedly affected due to its topography, rapid urban expansion, and drainage limitations. We produced a 10 × 10 m urban flood-susceptibility map for Shiraz and interpreted key controls using machine learning and SHAP. A 2000–2020 inventory included 220 flooded and 220 non-flooded locations. Sixteen predictors were derived from multi-source layers and grouped into climatic, geographic, urban-development, and infrastructure factors (e.g., rainfall, elevation, slope, TWI, drainage density, distance to rivers, land use, and soil texture). Multicollinearity was checked using VIF, tolerance, and Pearson correlation. Six classifiers RF, KNN, GBM, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were evaluated using complementary holdout and geographically grouped spatial-validation protocols. CatBoost achieved a holdout AUC of 0.9089 and an F1-score of 0.8593, while repeated 5-km spatial cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.8588. The final CatBoost map classified 43.60% of the study area as having high or very high flood susceptibility. SHAP analysis identified rainfall, distance to rivers, TWI, and slope as influential predictors. The susceptibility surface achieved a success-rate AUC of 0.874, and full high-susceptibility agreement among all six models covered 32.39% of the study area. The resulting uncertainty-aware planning-priority map provides spatial screening information for field verification, river-corridor assessment, and drainage evaluation, subject to site-specific engineering validation.
