title: Uncertainty-aware graph neural reconstruction of urban temperature fields from sparse sensors under deployment constraints
abstract: Reconstructing spatially continuous daily temperature fields from sparse observations is important for environmental monitoring and heat-risk analysis, yet practical deployments are limited by sensor availability and spacing constraints. This study presents an uncertainty-aware graph neural network framework that combines mean-residual graph-attention reconstruction, deployment-constrained sensor placement, and probabilistic temperature-threshold mapping. The gridded reference field is first evaluated against independent in situ observations to establish its suitability and scale of interpretation. Reconstruction performance is then assessed using separated training, validation, and held-out test periods, supplemented by leave-one-year-out evaluation across alternative sensor budgets and placement strategies. Comparisons include inverse-distance weighting, validation-tuned kriging, a Matérn Gaussian process, residual Proper Orthogonal Decomposition, and a sensor-mean baseline. The proposed model generally achieves the lowest missing-node reconstruction errors at moderate and larger sensor budgets, whereas residual POD remains competitive under the most restrictive sensing configuration. The benefits of additional sensors diminish as the network becomes denser, and the relative performance of placement strategies depends on both the sensor budget and reconstruction method. The ensemble formulation provides spatially varying predictive uncertainty, separates within-member and between-member contributions, and supports calibrated prediction intervals and spatial exceedance-probability mapping. Overall, the framework provides a basis for resource-aware reconstruction of daily grid-scale temperature fields and for evaluating environmental sensor-network designs under practical deployment constraints.

verified_metadata.title: Optimization-guided residual reinforcement learning for real-time low-carbon dispatch of user-side battery–ice hybrid energy storage systems
verified_metadata.abstract: High renewable energy penetration increases the variability and uncertainty of grid carbon emissions, creating a need for user-side energy storage to support low-carbon regulation. Battery–ice hybrid energy storage systems combine rapid power response with intertemporal load shifting. However, dynamic carbon signals do not directly specify the required real-time regulation power or its allocation between battery and ice storage. Day-ahead–real-time signal deviations and heterogeneous operating constraints further complicate coordinated dispatch. This study proposes an optimization-guided residual reinforcement learning method for real-time low-carbon dispatch. A unified equivalent-power model is developed, and a day-ahead mixed-integer linear programming model uses the dynamic carbon emission responsibility factor of electricity (Cr) to generate low-carbon power and state-of-charge reference trajectories. An online feasible baseline is constructed from real-time device states, and a residual soft actor–critic policy incrementally corrects the references according to real-time Cr deviations. A case study at Hangzhou Medicine Port demonstrates robust performance across different Cr-deviation patterns. Compared with day-ahead optimization, the method reduces seven-day cumulative carbon emission responsibility by 8.54% and improves the low-carbon demand matching degree from −0.63 to −0.71. Post-hoc economic evaluation shows a 3.42% increase in operating revenue. Ablation results show that optimization guidance achieved 339.8% and 42.3% greater reductions in carbon emission responsibility relative to the final reductions achieved with rule guidance and no guidance, respectively. The proposed method enables heterogeneous user-side electrical and thermal storage to provide real-time low-carbon grid response.

title: Uncovering universal and system-specific mechanisms of glass formation across covalent, ionic, and metallic networks via SHAP-integrated machine learning
abstract: Establishing a unified yet system-specific physicochemical framework for glass formation across covalent, ionic, and metallic systems remains a fundamental challenge, as existing models are largely confined to a single glass family or heavily biased toward compositions that have been successfully vitrified. Here we bridge this gap using a success-bias-free dataset of 78,889 compositional entries drawn from glass-forming region maps. Encoding each composition as an elemental-property matrix derived from the Magpie database, we train a scalable XGBoost framework that attains 89.6% classification accuracy on the all-glass dataset, and generalizes robustly to extrapolative elemental substitutions and higher-dimensional spaces. Shapley analysis of all-glass and system-specific models shows that the four glass families share the same set of frustration mechanisms whose relative weights redistribute systematically with bonding character. Across all families, governing descriptors exhibit a bounded, non-monotonic dependence that we term frustration inversion, whereby compositional heterogeneity stabilizes the amorphous state only up to a family-specific threshold that narrows as network rigidity decreases, furnishing quantitative bounds on the confusion principle. The analysis further identifies BCC-polymorph-referenced elemental descriptors as compositional-level predictors that encode structural preferences toward vitrification. These results establish a cross-system foundation for amorphous stability and a data-driven route to functional glass design.

title: Impact of the glass transition temperature on Li-ion diffusion in amorphous alloy anodes via machine learning
abstract: Understanding Li diffusion in amorphous alloy anodes is critical for developing fast-charging batteries with improved rate performance and cycling stability. However, the complex structural evolution involving amorphous phases makes the atomic diffusion mechanism unclear. Here, we construct high-precision machine-learning potential for Li–Si/Ge/Sn/Pb systems to investigate Li diffusivity ( D Li ). Our simulations show that D Li increases with Li content and temperature, aligning with experimental trends. Conventional Arrhenius extrapolation from high-temperature data overestimates the D Li obtained from direct room-temperature simulations by 1–2 orders of magnitude, particularly in Li-poor phases. We identify the glass transition temperature ( T g ) as a key descriptor of the change in diffusion behavior. Above T g , the systems exhibit liquid-like dynamics with structural rearrangement and rapid Li motion. Below T g , they exhibit glass-like dynamics with slow structural relaxation and localized Li motion. We employed three dynamical analyses and found that Li-poor phases exhibit stronger Li localization and slower relaxation, whereas Li-rich phases exhibit broader displacements and faster relaxation, supporting a gradual transition from predominantly localized, cage-confined Li motion to more active and extended Li displacements across T g . These results establish a composition–local-structure–diffusion relationship, indicating that optimizing alloy composition to reduce T g may improve Li transport, offering theoretical guidance for developing next-generation battery anodes.

title: Aligning heterogeneous DFT datasets: a graph neural network approach to cross-functional formation energies
abstract: Heterogeneous density functional theory (DFT) calculations, particularly plane-wave implementations, introduce systematic formation energy errors ranging from tens to hundreds of meV/atom, depending on the selection of exchange-correlation functionals, kinetic energy cutoffs, pseudopotentials, and dispersion corrections. As demonstrated by the MatPES dataset, identical structures can exhibit an average energy discrepancy of 107 meV/atom between PBE and r 2 SCAN calculations. Such method-dependent discrepancies hinder the integration of multi-source DFT data, greatly limiting the scale and quality of datasets for training robust materials AI models. Here, we resolve this fundamental data silo barrier via graph-based transfer learning. Leveraging 380,190 structurally paired PBE–r 2 SCAN entries from the MatPES database, we train a structure-aware graph neural network to predict cross-functional energy residuals and align inconsistent DFT energy scales. By adopting GPTFF model architecture, the model converts conventional PBE energies to r 2 SCAN-level accuracy with a mean absolute error of 14.3 meV/atom, compared with 18.2 meV/atom achieved by CHGNet. This versatile approach effectively upgrades massive legacy PBE datasets to high-precision r 2 SCAN standards. It enables reliable predictions of phase stability, battery voltage profiles, and reaction thermodynamics, while allowing the integration of multi-source DFT data to advance the development of high-performance materials foundation models.

title: Generative inverse estimation of 3D atomic coordination from near-edge spectra via equivariant diffusion models
abstract: Abstract Extracting 3D atomic coordinates from spectroscopic data is a longstanding inverse problem. We present an equivariant diffusion model that generates the distribution of site-specific 3D structures directly from near-edge spectra (ELNES/XANES). Trained on Si–O crystals, the model achieves radial accuracy comparable to Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (EXAFS) (bond-distance MAE ~ 0.04 Å) but with superior coordination number precision (errors < 2.0% vs. EXAFS ~ 20%). Crucially, it reconstructs full 3D geometries including bond angles, overcoming the limitations of 1D radial distribution analysis. The model shows encouraging, composition-dependent transferability to amorphous systems despite being trained exclusively on crystalline lattices. Application to experimental O K -edge spectra from α -quartz, cristobalite and stishovite demonstrates feasibility for experimental spectra. This generative approach goes beyond conventional template matching, which retrieves structures from predefined references, by enabling the exploration of candidate 3D structures within a learned structural space and providing a step toward automated, quantitative, 3D local-structure inference from spectroscopic data.

title: MatBind: a shared embedding space for multimodal materials characterization
abstract: Abstract Fully characterizing a crystalline material requires integrating heterogeneous data sources—atomic structures, diffraction patterns, electronic density of states, and natural language—each of which captures a different facet of the same physical object. In practice, however, these modalities are stored and analyzed in isolation, making it difficult to relate or query materials across representational boundaries. We present MatBind , a contrastive learning framework that aligns four material modalities—crystal structure, powder X-ray diffraction (pXRD) simulated from structures, density of states (DOS), and text—into a unified embedding space using crystal structure as the central physical anchor. The framework induces alignment between modalities never explicitly paired during training, enabling emergent zero-shot cross-modal retrieval as a direct consequence of the shared representation. The learned embedding space organizes materials according to physically meaningful properties without explicit supervision, and retrieval performance improves systematically when modalities are combined at query time. These results demonstrate that treating heterogeneous materials data as complementary projections of a single physical reality, rather than as isolated data sources, is not a practical choice but is consistent with the underlying physics.

title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers
abstract: Abstract Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes—fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns—were incorporated into a stacked machine-learning model. Model development and cutoff selection were limited to the training cohort, followed by evaluation in the internal-test and external-test cohorts. The cfDNA model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.930 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.894–0.966) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.891–0.972) in the internal-test and external-test cohorts, respectively. Incorporation of cfDNA with cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) increased AUCs to 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938–0.990) and 0.964 (95% CI, 0.938–0.991). At cutoffs derived from the training cohort, the combined model maintained sensitivities of 88.4% and 89.2% while enhancing specificity from 77.9% to 88.4% and from 78.9% to 91.5%, respectively. The cfDNA model also effectively detected cancers with CA125 and/or HE4 levels below conventional thresholds, and post hoc analyses demonstrated complementary discrimination when cfDNA was added to the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm. These findings advocate for prospective evaluation of integrated cfDNA fragmentomics as an adjunct for preoperative risk stratification of ovarian masses.

title: Predictive performance of lifestyle-informed multimodal brain features for cognition in healthy older adults
abstract: Abstract Identifying neuroimaging markers of cognitive performance in healthy aging is challenging due to heterogeneity in brain and cognitive characteristics. Among the factors relevant to that heterogeneity are lifestyle choices, of which each individual factor explains only a very small amount of variance in brain and cognition. This challenges current approaches for the prediction of cognitive outcomes. We examined whether brain features associated with an overall lifestyle profile (BF-Life multi ) provide predictive information for 13 cognitive outcomes compared with those related to single lifestyle factors (BF-Life single ), in 774 participants from the 1000BRAINS study (age: 67.0 ± 6.7 years), cross-sectionally and longitudinally (4-year follow-up). The BF-Life multi model showed modest domain-specific prediction, with the highest performance for baseline figural memory, primarily involving regions within the salience/ventral attention, default mode, somatomotor, and visual networks. These models did not consistently outperform data-driven models based on general brain features with shared variance alone. Including demographic variables improved prediction, whereas individual lifestyle factors added little benefit. No model reliably predicted longitudinal cognitive outcomes. Overall, lifestyle-related brain differences can contribute domain-specific complementary information for cognitive performance prediction in aging, but are not generalizable across domains and for capturing intraindividual trajectories.

title: Online ecological-prior-guided bitemporal Transformer for mapping potential Spartina alterniflora eradication areas in coastal tidal flats
abstract: Accurate monitoring of Spartina alterniflora eradication is essential for evaluating coastal wetland restoration and supporting invasive-species management. However, vegetation removal and natural surface variation can produce similar spectral changes in heterogeneous tidal flats, complicating image-based detection. To address this issue, we propose COAST ( Coastal Online Adaptive Spatiotemporal Transformer ), an online ecological-prior-guided bitemporal Transformer for mapping potential S. alterniflora eradication areas in the Jiangsu coastal tidal flats, China. The framework uses geographically weighted discriminant analysis (GWDA) posterior probabilities to represent spatially heterogeneous relationships between S. alterniflora pre-eradication spectral features and removal-related change. These probabilities provide soft supervision for a lightweight online prior encoder, whose output modulates bitemporal features through spatial prior gating. Training uses spatial-block out-of-fold GWDA predictions, and inference uses paired images with the prior generated from the pre-eradication image. Under a spatially separated evaluation design, COAST achieved the highest mean F1-score (95.00 %) and IoU (90.48 %) among the evaluated baselines across three random-seed runs. It also achieved a boundary F1-score of 81.25 %, a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 256.04 m, and a changed-area fraction mean absolute error of 0.82 percentage points. Ablation experiments supported the contribution of prior-guided learning relative to the BiT backbone. Evaluation on manually annotated cross-year patches yielded F1-scores of 88.27 % for 2020–2023 and 93.13 % for 2020–2025, supporting temporal transfer within the sampled coastal settings. Local errors included agricultural-background false positives and incomplete target recovery. COAST provides an image-based workflow for repeated regional screening of eradication-related change and the prioritisation of follow-up verification.

title: Tree crown mortality and defoliation assessment in temperate forests using aerial imagery and deep learning
abstract: Forest health is increasingly threatened by global warming and recurrent droughts. However, limited long-term data on tree health and mortality restricts our ability to detect trends and predict forest responses to climate stressors. Traditional methods for assessing tree defoliation are accurate but costly and labor-intensive, highlighting the need for scalable alternatives. This study aims to develop a more automated approach for monitoring tree defoliation and mortality in Germany and Switzerland using deep learning applied to freely available aerial imagery. We assessed crown vitality using three and four defoliation classes derived from field surveys. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained on 48,388 annotated tree crowns from aerial imagery, labeled with forest type and defoliation status. RGB and NDVI-GB inputs were tested using five-fold and spatial-block cross-validation to ensure robustness. The three-class model outperformed the four-class CNN object detection version. RGB and NDVI-GB bands produced similar results in the three-class setup, with F1-scores of 0.74 and 0.73, respectively. Defoliated trees were more challenging to detect (F1-conifer: 0.61, F1-broadleaf: 0.54). Dead trees were detected with high accuracy (F1-score: 0.97), while healthy trees also showed good performance (F1-conifer: 0.78, F1-broadleaf: 0.73). Repeated aerial imagery revealed a 17-fold increase in standing dead trees across a 977-ha protected forest between 2014 (1,062 trees) and 2022 (17,897 trees), with 90 % of the increase after 2018. This study demonstrates that RGB imagery alone is sufficient for operational, tree-level monitoring of both defoliation and mortality over time. As more countries acquire repeated aerial imagery, this study offers broad applicability and supports forest inventories and resilient management strategies.

title: Process-informed deep learning for interpretable forested wetland mapping under dense canopy
abstract: Canopy-obscured hydrologic signals and gradual wetland–upland transitions hinder the delineation of forested wetlands, particularly when heterogeneous Earth-observation evidence is fused as an unstructured feature stack. We developed a process-informed multi-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for mapping forested wetlands on a 10-m modelling grid in the Changbai Mountains, China. The model used 85 covariates derived from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, and Copernicus DEM GLO-30. These covariates were assigned a priori to five predictor streams and processed by separate CNN branches before fusion. Relative to a capacity-matched single-stream baseline, the grouped architecture increased forested-wetland F1 by 3.42 percentage points across five validation folds, whereas the gain on the fixed held-out test set was smaller (+1.03 percentage points). For map production, the probability-averaged five-fold ensemble achieved an overall accuracy of 0.873, a macro-F1 of 0.882, and a forested-wetland F1 of 0.836 on the fixed held-out test set. To interpret correlated predictors, group-aggregated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and k-nearest-neighbor conditional replacement were used to characterize global and conditional model reliance. Among correctly classified forested-wetland samples, global reliance was greatest for temporal features and phenology, whereas conditional replacement indicated the greatest residual model reliance for hydrology, followed by topography. Direct pixel counting yielded a map-derived forested-wetland area of 686.6 km 2 , concentrated mainly in peripheral plains and hills. This framework combines process-informed feature organization with dependence-aware interpretation to support interpretable regional mapping of canopy-obscured forested wetlands.

title: PSGRNet: Multi-scale spectral–frequency representation learning with gated residual fusion for coastal wetland classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery
abstract: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Although UAV hyperspectral imagery provides fine-grained spatial and spectral observations that can help capture such complex and fragmented features, effectively leveraging this information to distinguish spectrally similar and spatially intermixed vegetation types remains an open problem. Therefore, we propose a Progressive Spectral Gated Residual Network (PSGRNet). Specifically, a spectral enhancement and multi-scale sequence modeling strategy is first introduced to strengthen discriminative spectral representations and capture multi-scale spectral dependencies. Building on these enhanced representations, a frequency-aware module further exploits global frequency-domain characteristics to aggregate informative spectral features adaptively. To effectively integrate both spectral and frequency-domain representations, a GRF strategy is developed to improve the robustness of the network in heterogeneous and fragmented coastal wetland scenes. We have collected three UAV-based hyperspectral datasets covering representative coastal wetland scenarios, including reed-dominated natural wetlands (NT-YK), highly fragmented landscapes with dynamic land-cover transitions (YC-YS), and human-influenced estuarine environments (LYG-LH). Experimental results on these three datasets demonstrate that PSGRNet outperforms 9 representative methods, achieving macro F1 scores of 89.25%, 81.99%, and 81.29%, respectively. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for accurate coastal wetland classification and demonstrate the value of the released datasets. The datasets will be publicly available at https://github.com/HAPPYFST/Wetland-HSI-Data .

title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
abstract: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D .

title: MVRNet: A Multi-View Refinement Network for Accurate Recognition of Challenging Intracranial Aneurysms in Enhanced 3D CTA Images
abstract: Intracranial aneurysms are life-threatening and require accurate, timely detection. Traditional manual diagnosis by radiologists can be subjective, leading to misdiagnoses, while existing deep learning approaches struggle with small aneurysms or cases complicated by surrounding tissues. In this paper, we present the Multi-View Refinement Network (MVRNet), a framework that delivers clinically meaningful performance gains on the most challenging intracranial aneurysm cases. It directly addresses real-world diagnostic difficulties, particularly for small, obscured, or ambiguously bounded lesions that conventional methods often miss. In particular, we propose a feature enhancement technique to obtain boundary-clear CTA, an informative supplement to the bone-free CTA, to further reduce the impact of noise and enhance the robustness of IA recognition. Moreover, we develop a multi-view encoder with 2D slicing in different directions to mitigate tissue occlusion effects, coupled with a progressively refined decoder that iteratively corrects uncertain predictions, ensuring precise localization and segmentation. Experimental results indicate that MVRNet improves the F1-score by 24% and the IoU by 16% in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods. Remarkably, previous methods struggled with challenging cases, while our method still achieves satisfactory results, demonstrating a >2× improvement over prior arts on challenging test sets. Our code has been released in https://github.com/TheResearchWorks/MVRNet.

title: Sparse stage path graph Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for bearing remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。孪生KAN及稀疏阶段路径图学习轴承退化状态并预测剩余寿命，两套试验数据验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been utilized to analyze monitoring data for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings. Conventional methods typically aggregate degradation features through GNNs after converting the monitoring data into graphs. However, traditional GNNs face two primary challenges: (1) a single stage of graph data construction is insufficient to capture the complexity of bearing degradation, and (2) the effectiveness of these methods heavily depends on the selection of initial weights, making them susceptible to noise interference. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel sparse stage path graph Kolmogorov-Arnold network (SSPGKAN) model to enhance bearing RUL prediction. First, a siamese KAN model is developed to classify bearing degradation stages, and stage path graphs (SPGs) are constructed to aggregate the degradation features. Subsequently, the SSPGKAN model replaces traditional edges in the graph structure with learnable functions, overcoming the limitations of initial linear weight selection in GNNs and enabling dynamic transmission of graph data. Additionally, a sparse graph optimization method is used to reduce the impact of noise and accurately predict bearing RUL. Verification results from two test bench datasets demonstrate that the SSPGKAN model improves the prediction efficiency and accuracy of bearing RUL.

title: Resilience enhancement study of renewable energy power networks by integrating subnet division and priority enhanced Q-Learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。优先Q-learning优化可再生能源电网级联故障后的恢复，与预防子网划分联合增强韧性。

verified_metadata.abstract: With the acceleration of global energy transition and escalating climate challenges, the large-scale integration of renewable energy into power systems has become inevitable. However, the intermittency of renewable energy output significantly exacerbates the risk of cascading failures in power grids. Traditional critical node protection and post-fault restoration methods struggle to adapt to renewable energy uncertainties, bottlenecking grid resilience assessment and enhancement. This study proposes a dual-phase resilience enhancement framework for renewable energy power systems, addressing pre-failure protection and post-failure restoration challenges. The methodology integrates a Subnet Division-Based Strategy and a Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration to mitigate cascading failures. Subnet Division-Based Strategy partitions networks into functional subnets using breadth-first search and maximum flow algorithms, identifying critical nodes through betweenness centrality optimization. Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration incorporates subnet priority rankings into Q-learning to create a guided exploration mechanism for repair sequence optimization. Experimental validations on IEEE test cases with renewable energy show that: 1) The Subnetwork Division-Based Strategy enables critical node protection, reducing resilience loss by 10%–30% across four attack scenarios; 2) Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration achieves 10% lower resilience loss and a 0.5–1 unit resilience improvement compared to conventional methods; 3) Subnet division prioritization combined with Q-Learning yields a 26.3% performance gain. This dual-phase approach provides grid operators with preventive protection strategies and real-time restoration optimization capabilities, establishes a replicable framework for enhancing network resilience.

title: A GCN-based availability analysis method for mobile network with spatial–temporal effect awareness

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。GCN学习移动网络空间和时间状态关系，评估受动态影响的通信可用性。

verified_metadata.abstract: The spatial–temporal effect induces complex dynamic changes in the states of network, increasing the risk of mobile network unavailability. Current availability analysis methods are difficult to establish the network spatial–temporal dynamic variation pattern. Machine learning methods avoid the weakness of explicitly modeling effect patterns. However, these methods usually neglect spatial topology changes and abrupt temporal dynamics. To address the above problem, we propose a GCN-Based Availability Analysis Method for Networks with Spatial–Temporal Effect Awareness (Gstea). In the spatial domain, the spatial variation is captured by graph adaptation and graph convolution. In the temporal domain, the Ek (ERP-based time-aligned with k-shape integration to preserve shape similarity) fully aligns the temporal sequence to identify abrupt network changes and generates enhanced graph signal propagation. Experimental results show that Gstea outperforms the best-performing baseline methods in various complex network scenarios (average improvement range from 7% to 26%). This demonstrates that Gstea can provide a more accurate evaluation in networks with spatial–temporal effect.

title: An interpretable fault diagnosis framework for nuclear power plant via graph representation and multi-task learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。图网络编码核电厂物理功能关系，多任务同时完成信号重建、故障定位与分类。

verified_metadata.abstract: Neural networks have great potential for enhancing fault diagnosis in nuclear power plants (NPPs). However, current approaches often face challenges such as limited interpretability, data scarcity, and insufficient handling of open-set fault conditions. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel interpretable fault diagnosis framework that integrates graph-based representation with multi-task learning. The framework uses a graph structure to encode the physical and functional relationships within NPPs and integrates it with a hybrid network architecture for spatiotemporal feature extraction. Multi-task learning is then employed to simultaneously perform signal reconstruction, node-level anomaly detection, graph-level fault classification, and prototype learning. Experiments on two reactor systems show that the proposed framework achieves 100% accuracy in closed-set fault classification, even with limited samples, and outperforms baseline models. It also successfully identifies unknown and compound faults in open-set scenarios, providing interpretable insights into fault propagation and affected regions. These results illustrate the framework’s practical potential for improving diagnostic reliability and supporting operators in NPPs.

title: FBSTFnet: A full-band spatiotemporal fusion network for machine remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。GRU和卷积融合多频多传感器退化表征，预测机械剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is central to prognostics and health management (PHM) systems, enabling proactive maintenance and preventing major machinery failures. Current deep learning approaches often employ squeeze-and-excitation mechanisms for multi-sensor signal processing, but mainly capture low-frequency features and neglect important information in other frequency bands. In addition, existing spatiotemporal fusion methods rely on computationally heavy architectures that restrict practical deployment. To address these challenges, a Full-Band Spatiotemporal Fusion Network (FBSTFnet) is proposed, featuring four main innovations: a Full-Band Local Interaction Feature (FBLIF) mechanism that enhances multi-frequency representation through discrete cosine transform (DCT)-based spectral transformation; a hybrid architecture integrating gated recurrent units (GRU) with one-dimensional convolutions for efficient temporal–spatial feature extraction; an Easy-ProbSparse self-attention (EPSA) block that improves spatiotemporal fusion while reducing computational cost; and a Memory-Enhanced Local Feature Compensation (MELFC) block that restores long-term temporal continuity by reinforcing memory and compensating local features. The effectiveness of FBSTFnet is demonstrated on two benchmark datasets. Results show that FBSTFnet achieves a lightweight structure with accurate RUL prediction, providing a promising direction for advancing PHM in mechanical systems.

title: Bayesian adaptive elastic net for early prediction of battery cycle life

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。贝叶斯自适应弹性网处理电池退化特征多重共线性，提前预测循环寿命并量化不确定性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prognosis of battery remaining useful life is essential for evaluating reliability and optimizing the utilization of energy storage systems. To address the challenge of multicollinearity among degradation features, we propose a Bayesian adaptive elastic net method that improves prediction accuracy while providing comprehensive uncertainty quantification. The proposed approach implements adaptive shrinkage, applying separate penalty parameters to each regression coefficient to shrink the non-significant variables while preserving the effects of important predictors. By representing Laplace priors as Gaussian-exponential mixtures through data augmentation techniques and approximating the normalizing constant numerically, we develop an efficient Metropolis-Hastings-within-Gibbs sampling framework for posterior inference. Validation using numerical simulations and battery cycle life data demonstrates that the proposed method delivers superior prediction accuracy and robust uncertainty quantification, even under severe multicollinearity, providing an effective solution for battery lifetime prediction.

title: CSIR-Net: a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network based on structural priors for satellite telemetry data reliability enhancement

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。神经随机微分方程改造LSTM，将不均匀卫星遥测恢复为连续状态轨迹，并校准不确定性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Enhancing satellite telemetry reliability is essential for status assessment and operational management. However, telemetry data have complex spatio-temporal dependencies and diverse missing patterns, making it challenging for traditional methods with discrete modeling, fixed parameters, and static prediction steps to recover. To address these, this paper proposes a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network that transforms degraded discrete data recovery into timestamp-aware continuous-trajectory inference with uncertainty-calibrated selection. Specifically, a long short-term memory network is reconstructed using neural stochastic differential equations to model hidden-state evolution in continuous time, and Ito integrals are incorporated to characterize uneven observation gaps, thereby enabling recovery at arbitrary timestamps. Additionally, time-varying signals and Brownian perturbations are integrated into the model to allow dynamic adjustment of parameters with the input, thereby improving the ability to recover multiple evolving features. Finally, a structure-prior-guided hierarchical graph is constructed to fuse multi-scale dependencies while suppressing redundant error propagation, and multi-head graph attention is used to derive adaptive confidence intervals for selective recovery, thereby improving telemetry reliability without obscuring novel patterns. Experiments on five datasets show the proposed method improves recovery accuracy by 27.7% over the best baseline, achieves 15.2–78.5 ms batch latency, and has strong potential for real-time large-scale telemetry reliability.

title: Topology-constrained U-Net for delamination mapping in ballistic-damaged thin GFRP
abstract: Delamination severely degrades the residual strength of glass-fibre-reinforced plastic (GFRP) laminates impacted by ballistic projectiles. This study introduces TopoPrior-UNet, a U-Net variant named for its novel loss function that embeds Topological Prior knowledge (specifically, a persistent-homology shape-prior loss to enforce the global topological structure of the damage, and a level-set active-contour loss to refine fuzzy boundaries) to segment multi-layer delamination images from a digital single lens reflex camera (DSLR). An initial set of 24 raw panel images was expanded to a 480-image set through three augmentation schemes, enabling learning under extreme data scarcity. Compared with a vanilla U-Net, TopoPrior-UNet improved mean Intersection-over-Union to 0.9832 (+9.9pp) and mean Dice to 0.9915 (+5.3pp), achieving the best scores across six metrics. These gains stem from jointly refining fuzzy boundaries and enforcing global ply topology, as corroborated by an ablation study. The trained model operates in quasi-real-time (i.e., inference in seconds per image) and requires only surface imagery, offering a cost-effective and rapid alternative to traditional NDT methods like X-ray or ultrasonic inspection, which often require minutes to hours for acquisition. Such rapid, non-destructive quantification of delamination extent lays the foundation for on-site residual-strength estimation and timely structural maintenance. • TopoPrior-UNet: level-set contour loss + persistent-homology shape-prior integration. • mIoU 0.9832, mDice 0.9915; +9.9 and +5.3 pts over U-Net on GFRP delamination. • Robust learning from 24 images expanded to 480 via augmentation. • Back-lit DSLR imagery enables near-real-time delamination mapping. • Shows the value of morphology-aware priors for materials engineering tasks.

title: Lifetime Early Prediction for Second-Life Lithium-Ion Battery: A Hierarchical Bayesian Learning Method

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。层次贝叶斯学习融合二次利用电池群组及个体信息，在自采老化数据上提前预测寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: With the rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption, the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries has brought increasing attention to the echelon utilization of second-life batteries (SLBs). These SLBs, typically retired from EVs upon reaching 80% of their rated capacity, possess considerable potential for deployment in stationary energy storage systems. To fully exploit their remaining capacity, accurate lifetime prediction during second-life applications is essential. This study addresses the early lifetime prediction of SLBs by proposing a hierarchical Bayesian model (HBM). Considering the heterogeneity in degradation behavior under varying working conditions, the method initially performs clustering based on operating conditions. Subsequently, a two-level hierarchical Bayesian framework is constructed to model the relationships between battery groups and individual units, enabling more accurate lifetime estimation. Bayesian inference is employed to optimize model parameters using extracted features, thereby reducing predictive uncertainty and enhancing overall accuracy. Validation on a self-collected SLB aging dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms conventional machine learning approaches, especially under data-limited conditions. Quantitatively, the model achieves an average root mean square error (RMSE) of 113.444 cycles (±31.423), mean absolute error (MAE) of 76.616 cycles (±15.516), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 17.188% (±4.073%) on the test set.

title: PAKP: Parallelized Adaptive Kriging method with Partial least squares for high-dimensional reliability analysis

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。并行自适应Kriging与PLS降维共同逼近复杂结构高维极限状态，减少可靠性分析计算。

verified_metadata.abstract: In structural reliability analysis, tackling high-dimensional problems with computational efficiency remains a significant challenge. To address this, the paper proposes a novel active learning method, termed Parallelized Adaptive Kriging with Partial least squares (PAKP), which is designed to enhance both accuracy and efficiency in high-dimensional reliability analysis of complex engineering structures. PAKP combines Kriging-based surrogate modeling with Partial Least Squares (PLS) for dimensionality reduction, effectively mitigating the challenges posed by curse of dimensionality. Another key innovation is the learning function allocation scheme, which adaptively selects the most suitable learning function from a portfolio to identify informative samples for refining the surrogate model. Additionally, a parallelization strategy is introduced to select multiple samples in each iteration, significantly enhancing the computational efficiency. An importance sampling scheme is also incorporated to handle small failure probabilities in high-dimensional settings. The effectiveness of PAKP is validated through five numerical examples, demonstrating its superior performance in balancing accuracy and efficiency. This highlights its potential as a promising solution for high-dimensional reliability analysis.

verified_metadata.abstract: Cavitation in aviation fuel centrifugal pumps can lead to impeller erosion and performance degradation, posing significant reliability risks. To efficiently assess low-probability cavitation failures under multidimensional uncertainty, this study proposes a surrogate-based reliability analysis framework named AK-IEI-SSIS, which integrates Kriging modeling, an Improved Expected Improvement (IEI) learning function, and Subset Simulation Importance Sampling (SSIS). The framework adaptively refines sampling near failure boundaries to enhance accuracy and computational efficiency. Its performance is validated through multiple benchmark cases involving nonlinear and high-dimensional systems. A Python-based parametric platform is also developed to orchestrate parametric modeling, meshing, CFD simulation, and reliability analysis. Applied to an aviation fuel centrifugal pump, the framework accurately quantifies cavitation-induced failure probabilities as low as 5.63 × 10⁻⁴ using only 202 CFD evaluations, achieving a 99 % reduction in computational cost compared to Monte Carlo methods. Although demonstrated on a specific pump, the framework is applicable to reliability assessment of rotating fluid machinery under uncertainty, supporting reliability analysis and maintenance planning for next-generation aerospace propulsion systems.

title: Multi-fidelity Kriging structural reliability analysis with the fusion of non-hierarchical low-fidelity models

verified_metadata.abstract: Adaptive Kriging is a common Bayesian statistical method and has founded wide application in structural reliability analysis. Multi-fidelity (MF) Kriging model can significantly reduce computational cost compared to single-fidelity Kriging model. However, research on MF Kriging reliability analysis remains relatively limited in the literature. Most existing MF Kriging approaches assume that reliability performance functions of varying fidelity levels follow a hierarchical nature, which is not applicable when the performance functions exhibit non-hierarchical fidelity levels across the input space. To handle this challenge, we develop a novel Bayesian adaptive MF Kriging method to integrate high-fidelity (HF) data with non-hierarchical low-fidelity (LF) Kriging models for reliability analysis. We first use the local correlation and variance-weighted fusion approach to fuse all the non-hierarchical LF models. Then, the hierarchical Kriging is employed for the construction of MF model based on HF data and the fused LF model. A new adaptive hierarchical refinement strategy is proposed. This strategy mainly involves a new hierarchical expected feasibility function (HEFF) for identifying the location and fidelity of the optimal sample simultaneously, and a low-fidelity-selection (LFS) algorithm based on Kriging-Believer approach to allocate simulations among non-hierarchical LF models. One numerical example and two engineering examples involving an aircraft tubing and an airfoil stiffener rib, are used to validate the performance of our method.

title: Causal graph inference with adaptive dynamic structure learning for mechanism-oriented fault diagnosis in dynamic industrial systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。多尺度编码及因果图结构学习端到端表征动态工业故障传播，研究具体过程诊断。

verified_metadata.abstract: Complex rotating machinery is essential to safety-critical industrial systems, where undetected faults may trigger cascading failures and pose serious safety risks. Inherent dynamic couplings, multi-source interferences, and time-varying feedback loops lead to complex fault propagation, presenting major challenges for reliable and interpretable diagnostics. Traditional data-driven methods, primarily relying on correlation-based models, often fail to generalize under non-stationary conditions and provide limited understanding of underlying failure mechanisms. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Dynamic Causal Mechanism Learning Diagnostics Framework (DCMLDF), designed to enhance system reliability and mitigate fault risks. The framework incorporates a multi-scale temporal encoder, semantics-aware causal graph inference, a causality-guided predictive decoder, and a unified optimization strategy to enable end-to-end modeling of dynamic fault evolution from high-dimensional sensor data. Evaluated on four benchmark datasets, DCMLDF consistently outperforms five representative baselines in both accuracy and stability. More importantly, it reveals system-level causal dependencies that characterize evolving failure pathways, thereby enabling early warning, root-cause identification, and risk-informed decision-making. These findings highlight the framework’s effectiveness in improving predictive reliability and operational safety, offering a scalable solution for prognostics and health management in complex mechanical systems.

title: Sparse Bayesian learning for joint load-parameter-response identification

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。稀疏贝叶斯学习利用损伤和荷载先验联合反演结构参数、荷载及响应，梁架与实桥验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: The joint identification of the structural loads, parameters, and responses from the sparse measurements is crucial but challenging for assessing the operational conditions of civil infrastructures. Existing joint identification methods typically require the prior information, such as the loading locations and the covariance matrices of the process and observation noise, which are unavailable in practice. To address this limitation, a sparse Bayesian learning technique based on the transmissibility matrix is proposed for the joint load-parameter-response identification. The spatial sparsity of damage indices (defined as the structural parameter change) and loads is adopted as priors in the Bayesian framework. The Expectation-Maximum (EM) algorithm is used to iteratively estimate the most probable values of the damage indices, unknown force time history, measurement noise, and other variance parameters. A modified Metropolis-Hastings (MH) algorithm is developed to jointly generate posterior samples of structural parameters and loads for the expectation calculation in the EM algorithm. Upon convergence, some hyperparameters approach infinity and the associated damage indices and forces become zero, resulting in the sparsity of the identified damage indices and loads. Consequently, the damage indices and input forces are located and quantified simultaneously, and the full-field structural responses are sequentially reconstructed with suppressed uncertainties. The proposed method is verified by a numerical simply-supported beam, a laboratory-tested three-story frame model, and a three-span continuous bridge model. Results demonstrate that the proposed sparse Bayesian technique can accurately identify the damage indices, loads, and responses simultaneously, even when the load position is unknown.

title: A double-loop adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty

verified_metadata.abstract: Robust design optimization under aleatory and epistemic uncertainty still remains several key issues, such as lack of a unified quantitative robustness measure, suffering from huge computational burden and in need for proper searching strategy, etc. To remedy these, a novel adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty is proposed. Based on the unified MC-based simulation technique for both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty, a decision model for robustness measure is built to comprehensively characterize the nominal expectation, the variation due to epistemic uncertainty alone, and the mixed variation due to both epistemic and aleatory uncertainty. To solve the decision model, a double-loop adaptive Kriging-based method is proposed, which can ensure a balance of optimality and robustness with limited calculations of the real deterministic objective. The inner-loop Kriging is locally updated at each training sample of the outer-loop one to ensure accuracy of the minimization and maximization at each focal element of the deterministic objective, while the outer-loop Kriging is deeply coupled into each simulation level of the subset simulation optimization to quickly converge to the optimum without much loss of accuracy. A toy example is used to illustrate the performance of the proposed methodology, engineering applicability of which is further tested by three real engineering examples.

title: Adaptive Kriging‑assisted enhanced sparrow search with augmented‑Lagrangian first-order reliability method for highly efficient structural reliability analysis

verified_metadata.abstract: Uncertainty information exists widely throughout the life cycle of engineering products. Efficient reliability analysis methods are essential to solve complex reliability problems considering multi-source uncertain information. In this study, a hybrid method combining the Active Kriging (AK) model with Enhanced Sparrow Search Optimization (AK-ESSO) is proposed to enhance the performance of classical First-Order Reliability Method (FORM). In the first stage, ESSO’s ability to search for reliability indicators is enhanced through adaptive global search and random local search strategies. In the second stage, the augmented Lagrangian penalty function in FORM is used to enhance the accuracy of the optimization model used to approximate reliability indicators in ESSO. In the third stage, the novel hybrid AK strategy considering global and local accuracy is proposed to enhance the computational efficiency in the limit state assessment process. By combining these three strategies, AK-ESSO enhances the robustness and global performance of FORM in searching for reliability indicators. Using eight numerical and three applicable engineering problems, the AK-ESSO frameworks applied in FORM are compared to the classical FORM algorithm, popular FORM-based metaheuristic algorithms, and hybrid Kriging-based metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that AK - ESSO offers significant advantages in efficiency, and in terms of computational accuracy, the augmented Lagrangian optimization probabilistic model provides significant advantages for AK - ESSO, as well as global convergence in terms of robustness.

title: Variational inference for hierarchical Bayesian learning framework for model updating with non-stationary prediction errors

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。高斯过程误差模型与变分贝叶斯学习联合更新结构动力学参数及预测不确定性。

verified_metadata.abstract: Quantification of model uncertainties are essential for ensuring the credibility of numerical models in robust structural response prediction and reliability assessment. Probabilistic model updating provides an effective way to achieve this purpose. Among these methods, the hierarchical Bayesian modeling (HBM) framework has been widely recognized as a powerful tool for jointly estimating the uncertainty of model parameters and prediction errors, thereby enabling a comprehensive quantification of model uncertainties. Typically, Gaussian white noise (GWN) is used as the probabilistic model for prediction errors, but this assumption fails to capture their non-stationary characteristics. To overcome this limitation, a new HBM framework is developed, which replaces GWN with a Gaussian process (GP) model. An orthogonal expansion is utilized to approximate the GP model as the summation of orthogonal functions with independent Gaussian coefficients for efficient error representation. The use of GP introduces a coupling relationship between the model parameters and the Gaussian coefficients, which makes it impossible to directly infer their joint posterior distribution. To resolve this issue, variational inference is employed. Specifically, the mean field assumption is utilized to decouple the parameters into independent sets, and the variational distributions of each set are sequentially inferred. To ensure consistency across these distributions, an iterative procedure is designed, where the evidence lower bound serves as the convergence index. Through iterative sequential inference, the optimal variational distributions for each parameter set are obtained, and their product approximates the joint posterior distribution. Additionally, the model class selection approach is utilized to determine the optimal number of orthogonal terms for simulating prediction errors, striking a balance of simulation accuracy and complexity. With the estimated uncertainties of model parameters and the GP model of prediction errors, the uncertainty of the output quantity of interest can be predicted. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated using two examples in structural dynamics.

verified_metadata.abstract: The manufacturing quality of the product plays a vital role in the reliability of the complex equipment and the overall system safety. Accurately predicting manufacturing quality helps promptly detect abnormal products and shorten production time. Nevertheless, the multi-source heterogeneous sensor data on the manufacturing systems will unavoidably result in incomplete data, thereby affecting the accuracy of the predictive model. In addition, the imbalanced data in quality labels can deceive conventional models to obtain inexact predictive boundaries, leading to missed detection of abnormal manufacturing products. In this study, an new incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based model is proposed for manufacturing quality prediction. Specifically, an improved probabilistic principal component analysis-based incomplete learning module is first designed to supplement heterogeneous data information. After that, an elaborated cost-sensitive quality predictive model is developed to handle the imbalanced quality labels. Finally, an evolutionary collaborative learning strategy is appended to enhance predictive performance via collaboratively optimizing the incomplete and cost-sensitive learning modules. Application case studies of actual wheel bearing component and valve manufacturing plants demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher accuracy in manufacturing quality abnormal prediction.

verified_metadata.abstract: This paper proposes an ensemble multimodal deep learning approach to identify the geological conditions in shield tunnel engineering. The proposed approach improves the Swin Transformer architecture, building a multimodal model with soil images and tunnel boring machine (TBM) parameters as input. The Dempster Shafer theory is used for information fusion to develop the Ensemble Swin-Transformer-MLP (ESwin-T-M), which accurately identifies geological conditions for tunnel shield projects. In addition, the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-Cam) and the Model-Agnostic Permutation Feature Importance (MAPFI) are used to perform model interpretation analysis. The Circle Line Phase 6 C885 Tunnel Project in Singapore is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results indicate that: (1) The proposed ensemble multimodal fusing network identifies geological conditions with a high F1-Score of 0.9746 in 5-fold cross-validation. (2) The recognition accuracy of the ensemble multimodal fusion network is superior to that of the single modality models and the basic models. (3) The ensemble fusing approach outperforms the approaches utilizing soil images or TBM parameters separately in terms of robustness and anti-interference ability. The novelty of this research lies in the development of an integrated detection method for multimodal information, which overcomes the trustworthy limitations of traditional single-data method and provides technical support for the precise and reliable identification of geological conditions in tunnel engineering.

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of landing risk during extremely windy conditions is vital to ensuring flight safety. However, most existing methods rely on pre-trained single-risk models, which often have poor prediction accuracy under extremely windy conditions such as strong winds. This study proposes an online multi-risk prediction method for airplane landing during extremely windy conditions, leveraging a streaming Bi-LSTM-Transformer (BLT) architecture. First, data preprocessing is performed to ensure the high-quality input for analysis. A comprehensive multi-risk assessment framework is then developed to evaluate the potential landing risks, utilizing the processed data. Subsequently, time-series modeling is conducted using a Bi-LSTM network. To improve the models’ global time-series modeling ability, a Transformer component is integrated into the Bi-LSTM output, forming the BLT model. Finally, stream learning is introduced to maintain predictive performance under extremely windy conditions. Using real-time flight data streams, the Stream BLT model applies eligibility traces and a dynamic learning rate to enable continuous, adaptive learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately predicts airplane landing risks under extremely windy conditions, particularly when wind speeds exceed 33knots. The model achieves an average relative error of approximately 0.01–0.07 and a prediction latency of under 30 ms, offering efficient, reliable real-time airplane landing risk assessment.

It is therefore of paramount significance to develop distinct risk intervention levels following refined degradation evaluations. This study establishes a collaborative self-adaptive optimization problem of routine maintenance and task termination decisions for heterogeneous degrading systems. A Bayesian learning methodology is employed to continuously update the unknown degradation rate utilizing equidistantly sampled data; leveraging such updates constitutes an adaptive multi-level risk control policy employing age-state-dependent thresholds to select between (a) operational continuation, (b) routine maintenance partially restoring degradation at a severity-dependent cost, or (c) terminate the task instantly for overhaul. Implementation on shipboard phased-array radar drivers confirms the framework’s operational viability and demonstrates substantial advantages over conventional strategies in risk loss prevention and task success promotion.

verified_metadata.abstract: Adaptive metamodels using single learning functions fail to consistently maintain the high accuracy or efficiency in calculating failure probabilities of slopes under all scenarios (e.g., natural vs. reservoir slopes) due to the No Free Lunch theorem. It poses a challenge in the adaptive selection of the optimal function under high-dimensional random field domains. To this end, we consider the selection problem as a multi-armed bandit problem, and thus propose a portfolio optimization-based adaptive polynomial-chaos Kriging (POPCK) method that dynamically balances exploration and exploitation of six distinct learning functions, thereby adaptively selecting better functions based on their historical performance. This adaptive selection could be performed under high-dimensional variables by incorporating Karhunen–Loève expansion and sliced inverse regression techniques into POPCK. The feasibility of the proposed method is demonstrated through four classic examples (involving natural, four soil layers, rainfall infiltration, and water level drawdown conditions). Results show that the proposed method exhibits good robustness for all examples, high accuracy (ranking 1st) and computational efficiency (ranking 2nd), whereas the performance of PCKs using the single learning functions fluctuates greatly. This method effectively mitigates the randomness of learning function selection, which is valuable for engineers who lack prior knowledge of optimal learning functions.

title: An efficient reliability assessment framework for complex mechanism wear degradation based on probabilistic space decomposition kriging model

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。概率空间分解Kriging替代磨损退化的高维可靠性模拟，与非线性动力学和Archard模型耦合。

verified_metadata.abstract: Operational wear in complex mechanical systems with joint clearances, driven by nonlinear dynamic behavior, leads to functional degradation and accelerated failure. While critical, the influence of vibration on wear progression is often overlooked in existing studies, and efficiently assessing the reliability of high-fidelity simulation models remains a significant challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability assessment framework for wear degradation (PSDK-WDR). First, we develop a non-uniform wear prediction model that integrates a nonlinear dynamic model with the Archard wear model. This model innovatively updates the wear coefficient using parameters derived from real-time vibration signal energy dissipation. Furthermore, for efficient reliability analysis, we introduce a Monte Carlo simulation method based on a Probability Space Decomposition Kriging model (PSDK-MCS). This method decomposes high-dimensional random variables into subsets via Probabilistic Space Decomposition (PSD) and constructs parallel Kriging sub-models for each subset to accelerate assessments. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed wear model and the PSDK-WDR framework are validated through case studies on crank-slider and flapping-wing mechanisms. This work provides a theoretical basis for understanding wear evolution and efficiently evaluating reliability degradation in complex mechanisms.

title: Nested adaptive Kriging-based reliability analysis and computational resource allocation for complex systems

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。嵌套主动Kriging分解复杂工程系统子问题，并自适应分配可靠性计算资源。

verified_metadata.abstract: Efficient reliability analysis of complex engineering systems faces significant challenges due to the integration of multiple subproblems, multidisciplinary coupling, high-dimensional characteristics, and resource incompatibility. These systems are often decomposed into multiple cascading subsystems, which enables concurrent analysis to manage this complexity. Surrogate-based techniques are widely utilized to alleviate the computational burden associated with time-consuming simulations. This study proposes a nested adaptive Kriging-based method for the reliability analysis of complex systems by integrating system decomposition with adaptive surrogate-based methods. The proposed method operates within a multilayer framework and proceeds in two stages, namely, a sequential updating stage and a resource allocation stage. In the first stage, an efficient nested reliability-oriented acquisition function is developed to guide model updating, and its closed-form expression is derived. In the second stage, a cost-effectiveness strategy that accounts for both simulation costs and modeling costs is introduced to determine which model combinations should be updated at each iteration. Finally, the proposed method is validated to be superior to the benchmark method and strategy through two mathematical examples and two practical applications.

title: Domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。领域知识双流图网络联合编码发动机部件物理拓扑和参数动态退化，C-MAPSS验证寿命预测。

verified_metadata.abstract: Prediction methods integrating domain knowledge with deep learning show great promise for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of aeroengines. Nevertheless, neglecting the decoupling modeling of multi-level domain knowledge such as component-level physical topology and parameter-level essential dependencies has resulted in insufficient and incorrect utilization of valuable degradation information, limiting the further improvement of prediction accuracy and stability. Therefore, a novel domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network (DK-DGJLN) is proposed. First, the physical essential dependencies among components and sensor parameters are extracted through in-depth analysis of aeroengine’s overall structure and working characteristics. Then, a component-level static graph is built to capture physical topology with high fidelity, while a parameter-level dynamic graph is constructed to model dynamic dependencies and degradation evolution. Their decoupling modeling enables faithful embedding of multi-level domain knowledge. Finally, a DGJLN is designed to extract rich and complementary spatial-temporal degradation features from both graphs, with a self-attention-based feature alignment module aggregating them for accurate RUL prediction. Extensive comparative experiments on the C-MAPSS dataset against 19 SOTA methods demonstrate that DK-DGJLN significantly improves prediction performance, especially on FD002 and FD004, where the RMSE values of 12.93 and 13.57 are markedly lower than those of the best comparative methods.

title: Multi-granularity learning-based intelligent decision-making method for equipment operation and maintenance on large-scale knowledge graphs

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。GCN-LSTM在设备运维知识图谱中推理故障关联，新能源车辆工厂数据验证。

verified_metadata.abstract: Effective equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) is crucial for productivity and safety; however, traditional manual decision-making methods are hindered by long cycles and inconsistent accuracy. This paper introduces MulKGR, an intelligent decision-making model designed for large-scale O&M knowledge graphs, addressing challenges such as insufficient multi-level fault association and low decision-making efficiency. The model extracts multi-granularity subgraphs from the O&M knowledge graph, incorporating equipment status, failure modes, and environmental factors to construct relational paths that enhance decision-making. MulKGR then employs a graph convolutional network (GCN) to jointly encode problem text and relational paths, generating word embeddings and calculating similarity scores, thereby optimizing computational efficiency through subgraph pruning. Finally, the pruned subgraphs are processed by a reasoning decision module that integrates GCN with long- and short-term memory networks for dynamic learning, enabling accurate reasoning and answer generation. Experimental results from a new energy vehicle production plant show that MulKGR significantly improves decision-making, achieving an F1 score of 65.88 %, a Hits@1 score of 62.5 %, and reducing decision-making time by 5.69 %. These results demonstrate the model's effectiveness in intelligent decision-making for equipment O&M.

title: Graph learning with variational graph structural information bottleneck for multi-sensor machinery remaining useful life prediction

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。变分图结构信息瓶颈学习多传感器机械退化关系，预测两套设备数据的剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Existing graph learning-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction approaches typically rely on predefined structural priors or fixed constraints to optimize graph topologies. Such priors are often crafted for specific signal modalities and thus exhibit limited generality, restricting their ability to model the complex and heterogeneous interdependencies inherent in multi-sensor signals. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a graph learning framework with a variational graph structural information bottleneck (GL-VGSIB) for multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction. The proposed GL-VGSIB establishes an information-theoretic graph structure learning paradigm that adaptively discovers degradation-relevant graph representations by balancing discriminability and compressibility. In contrast to prior GNN-based RUL frameworks that depend on static structural priors, the variational bottleneck mechanism in GL-VGSIB infers a probabilistic distribution over graph structures, enabling the model to preserve essential task-relevant dependencies while suppressing redundant or spurious connections. The framework integrates a multi-scale convolutional encoder with positional encoding to enhance spatio-temporal feature extraction and employs a reparameterization mechanism to facilitate differentiable stochastic graph sampling. Experimental results on two multi-sensor equipment datasets show that GL-VGSIB achieves a 2.9%-14.8% reduction in prediction error relative to state-of-the-art baselines, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness to multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction.

title: Risk predictive deduction and propagation chain mining for URT emergencies based on interpretable ensemble learning: A new approach to in-time safety management

verified_metadata.abstract: To enhance the emergency response capability of Urban Rail Transit (URT), this paper proposes an in-time safety management approach based on explanatory ensemble learning and key risk chain mining. Firstly, an innovative in-time safety management framework is designed. On this basis, historical incident data from Beijing Metro in recent years is used to identify risk causation and impact range. A dynamic risk assessment and predictive deduction method based on explanatory Stacking ensemble learning model is designed. It incorporates Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) for sample balanced and Optuna for optimal hyperparameter tuning of both base and meta models, achieving superior prediction accuracy for risk impact levels. Then, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) is employed to identify key risk causes and quantify their influence on prediction results. Finally, an improved W-Apriori algorithm is employed to mine the complex associations within key risk propagation chains, thereby providing targeted emergency response strategies. To demonstrate the approach, this paper presents a simulation case based on real operational emergency data and indicate that the proposed model achieves 95.83% accuracy, outperforming traditional machine learning methods across five performance metrics and exhibit superiority to promote a shift in URT safety management from traditional reactive response to proactive prevention and in-time intervention.

title: Physics-constrained causal structure learning for root cause analysis in nuclear system monitoring

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。评分式因果结构学习受核系统物理约束指导，识别事故监测根因并抑制不可能因果边。

verified_metadata.abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is important for identifying the initiating cause of faults and analyzing fault propagation paths in nuclear systems. However, robust RCA in nuclear accident monitoring remains challenging because it depends on reliable identification of causal relationships among monitoring variables, which is difficult under complex system coupling and limited-sample conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-constrained causal structure learning method for RCA in nuclear accident monitoring. First, a simplified physical model of the nuclear system is constructed to extract a priori causal knowledge among key monitoring variables. Second, the causal relationships among different variables are learned by a score-based causal structure learning method under the guidance of the extracted physical constraints. In this process, physically infeasible edges are excluded and the admissible parent sets are restricted before score optimization. Finally, the root cause nodes of faults are identified based on the learned causal graph. The proposed method is validated using two representative accident scenarios generated from a nuclear simulation platform. The results show that the proposed method can improve root-node identification performance, reduce abnormal-edge misidentification, and enhance the robustness of causal structure learning under limited-sample conditions without introducing additional computational burden.

title: Dynamic branch expansion: A hypergraph-augmented adaptive continual learning framework for machine health prognosis under time-varying conditions

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。工况感知超图和动态分支持续学习吸收时变机械退化数据并预测剩余寿命。

verified_metadata.abstract: Industrial data streams with dynamic distributions pose more daunting challenges for data-driven machine health monitoring. Continual learning (CL) method has the ability to adapt to newly-collected data and retain partial memory of previous degradation knowledge, while it still sinks into a dilemma of insufficient accumulation for long-term and diverse degradation patterns under complex operating conditions (OCs). This study proposes an adaptive continuous health prognosis framework with dynamic branch expansion (DBE) for absorbing dynamic data streams to predict the remaining useful life of rotating machines under time-varying OCs. Among it, an OC-aware hypergraph topology network is designed to enhance the hypergraph representation, after which hypergraph topology-memorized knowledge buffer is established for optimal replay sampling. On this basis, an adaptive DBE framework is constructed, which self-recognizes the addition of branches with the continuous influx of new data; and it ingeniously integrates multi-branch predictions via branch discriminator logits at inference stage to enhance CL generalization capability. Case studies of multi-stage continuous prognosis are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results indicate that it can gradually enhance the prediction performance with incremental data, and maintain the predictions of old data while fully learning degraded knowledge at new stages.

title: Risk-oriented degradation modeling and maintenance decision support for computed tomography X-ray tubes using mechanism-informed learning

ai4s_review.rationale: 初筛漏筛补录。门控Transformer融合X射线管灯丝退化物理指标与传感器特征，预测CT部件退化并评估风险。

verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of Computed Tomography (CT) X-ray tubes is essential for maintaining medical service continuity, reducing failure risk, and minimizing unplanned downtime. However, intrinsic degradation patterns are often obscured by heterogeneous operating conditions, such as automatic tube current modulation and voltage optimization. To address this challenge, we propose the Hybrid Affine Gated Fusion Network (HAGF-Net), a deep learning framework tailored for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. HAGF-Net employs a dual-branch parallel architecture that integrates physical priors with data-driven features. One branch processes Mechanism-driven Indicators (MDIs) derived from filament degradation physics, including cathode degradation rate (CDR) and degradation kinetic increment (DKI), using a Conditioned Operating-Gated Transformer (COG-Transformer) that dynamically modulates attention weights based on discrete operational states. Simultaneously, a raw-signal Branch based on CNN-LSTM modules captures local fluctuations and long-term temporal dependencies from multi-dimensional sensor sequences. The framework was validated on a high-resolution IoMT dataset comprising 10 Philips X-ray tubes from multiple clinical sites across China (2017–2024), covering their entire service lives. HAGF-Net demonstrates high global predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.07) and precise final-stage performance (MAE ≈ 3.85 days) and 95% prediction intervals close to the nominal coverage across sites. Ablation and comparison studies indicate that incorporating physical MDIs and condition-aware gating mechanisms enhances model’s robustness and responsiveness to complex degradation dynamics. Under simulated unreliable monitoring conditions, the proposed method evaluates model robustness under reduced sampling frequencies, demonstrating stable performance across different levels of data sparsity.
